raw_text:
24.  CHUPANA      [ to hide something]
SYNONYMS: KATAMA, AWRAA and WARAA, AKANNA, AKHFAA, ASARRA, KHABA’A
24.1  KATAMA (كَتَمَ) :   to consciously hide something in the heart. This word is commonly used for hiding the truth, faith or martyrdom. Its opposite is   اَبَدَ
_______________________________________
Surah Al-Baqarah (The Cow)
2:140
وَمَنْ أَظْلَمُ مِمَّن   كَتَمَ   شَهَادَةً عِندَهُ مِنَ اللّهِ
And who is more unjust than he who   conceals   the testimony he has from Allâh?
______________________________________
Surah Al-Baqarah (The Cow)
2:159
إِنَّ الَّذِينَ   يَكْتُمُونَ   مَا أَنزَلْنَا مِنَ الْبَيِّنَاتِ
Verily, those who   conceal   the clear proofs, evidences and the guidance, which We have sent down.
_______________________________________
Surah Ghafir  (The Forgiver or The Believer)
40:28
وَقَالَ رَجُلٌ مُّؤْمِنٌ مِّنْ آلِ فِرْعَوْنَ   يَكْتُمُ     إِيمَانَهُ
And a believing man of Fir'aun's (Pharaoh) family,   who hid his faith   said.
_______________________________________
24.2  WAARAA   (وَارٰى)   :   the root meaning of     وَارٰى     is used in two ways. 1) to kindle or light a fire. He made the fire come out from pyrites. 2) to hide the truth. Here only the second meaning is relevant.
_______________________________________
Surah Al-A'raf (The Heights)
7:20
فَوَسْوَسَ لَهُمَا الشَّيْطَانُ لِيُبْدِيَ لَهُمَا مَا   وُورِيَ   عَنْهُمَا مِن سَوْءَاتِهِمَا
Then Shaitân (Satan) whispered suggestions to them both in order to uncover that   which was hidden   from them of their private parts.
_______________________________________
And   يُوَارِىْ     وَارٰى   means to remove the truth from the sight of people by hiding it behind a veil.
_______________________________________
Surah Al-Ma'idah (The Table Spread with Food)
5:31
فَبَعَثَ اللّهُ غُرَابًا يَبْحَثُ فِي الأَرْضِ لِيُرِيَهُ كَيْفَ   يُوَارِي   سَوْءةَ أَخِيهِ
Then Allâh sent a crow who scratched the ground to show him to   hide   the dead body of his brother.
_______________________________________
24.3  AKANNA   (اَكَنَّ)   :   according to its root meaning, two things are found: (1) to hide (2) protection, or to place something in a safe place to protect it. To hide something in the heart or to hide it somewhere else.   كنّ   means a small cave in a mountain where refuge can be found, and its plural is   اكنان   . And   اكنّة   is a veil, in the presence of which nothing can come out, or come inside.
_______________________________________
Surah Al-An'am (The Cattle)
6:25
وَجَعَلْنَا عَلَى قُلُوبِهِمْ   أَكِنَّةً   أَن يَفْقَهُوهُ
We have set   veils   on their hearts, so they understand it not.
_______________________________________
The word   اَكَنَّ   is commonly used in the Qur’an in an implied form:
Surah Al-Baqarah (The Cow)
2:235
وَلاَ جُنَاحَ عَلَيْكُمْ فِيمَا عَرَّضْتُم بِهِ مِنْ خِطْبَةِ النِّسَاء أَوْ   أَكْنَنتُمْ   فِي أَنفُسِكُمٌ
And there is no sin on you if you make a hint of betrothal to a woman, or   conceal   it in yourself.
________________________________________
And for this safe place, the words   قلوب صدور نفس   and   نفوس   are used in the Qur’an.
________________________________________
24.4  ASARRA   (اَسَرَّ)   :   سِرّ     means a secret, and its plural is   اسرار   . And   اَسَرَّ   means to hide a secret in the heart, whether it is the truth or not. Instead, it is hidden ******************. Its opposites are   جهر   and   عَلَن  . And   سارَّ   means to whisper or to discuss a secret with each other. In the Qur’an is word is used both in its apparent and implied form.
______________________________________
Surah Yusuf (Prophet Joseph)
12:19

SYNONYMS: KATAMA, AWRAA and WARAA, AKANNA, AKHFAA, ASARRA, KHABA’A

24.1  KATAMA (كَتَمَ) : to consciously hide something in the heart. This word is commonly used for hiding the truth, faith or martyrdom. Its opposite is اَبَدَ

_______________________________________

Surah Al-Baqarah (The Cow)

2:140

وَمَنْ أَظْلَمُ مِمَّن كَتَمَ شَهَادَةً عِندَهُ مِنَ اللّهِ

And who is more unjust than he who conceals the testimony he has from Allâh?

______________________________________

Surah Al-Baqarah (The Cow)

2:159

إِنَّ الَّذِينَ يَكْتُمُونَ مَا أَنزَلْنَا مِنَ الْبَيِّنَاتِ

Verily, those who conceal the clear proofs, evidences and the guidance, which We have sent down.

_______________________________________

Surah Ghafir  (The Forgiver or The Believer)

40:28

وَقَالَ رَجُلٌ مُّؤْمِنٌ مِّنْ آلِ فِرْعَوْنَ يَكْتُمُ إِيمَانَهُ

And a believing man of Fir'aun's (Pharaoh) family, who hid his faith said.

_______________________________________

24.2  WAARAA (وَارٰى) : the root meaning of وَارٰى is used in two ways. 1) to kindle or light a fire. He made the fire come out from pyrites. 2) to hide the truth. Here only the second meaning is relevant.

_______________________________________

Surah Al-A'raf (The Heights)

7:20

فَوَسْوَسَ لَهُمَا الشَّيْطَانُ لِيُبْدِيَ لَهُمَا مَا وُورِيَ عَنْهُمَا مِن سَوْءَاتِهِمَا

Then Shaitân (Satan) whispered suggestions to them both in order to uncover that which was hidden from them of their private parts.

_______________________________________

And يُوَارِىْ وَارٰى means to remove the truth from the sight of people by hiding it behind a veil.

_______________________________________

5:31

_______________________________________

25 CHATT         [ roof ]
SYNONYMS: 3ARSH, SAQAF, and BINA’A
25.1  3ARSH   (عرش)   :   يَعْرِشُ عَرَشَ     means to make a house made of wood, and make a roof on it made of wood, like (??***********************) and to put a grapevine on a fence etc. And   عرش   has two meanings in its root form. (1) throne. (2) the wood used to make a roof. This word is also used for the roof of a room, tent, half house, and (HARWASHA****************) which gives a shade. In the Qur’an this word is used in both meanings.
For the meaning of a roof and its wood, see   2:259.
For the example for throne, see the word “throne”.
_____________________________________
25.2  SAQAF (  سَقْف  ) :   the inside part of a roof which is seen from inside the room. Or (AASMANE KHAANA ****************************).
Refer to 16:26
____________________________________
25.3  BINA’A (  بِنَآء  ) :   means construction, or a constructed building. And it can also refer to every part of a building, whether it is the base, walls, roof, or the whole building. And when this word is used related to the floor, then it still means roof, because   بِنَآء   can refer to the height of a construction.
Refer to 2:23
___________________________________
SUMMARY
3ARSH :   refers to     the whole roof and its wood
SAQAF :   the inside part of a roof
BINA’A :   it means the roof when referring to the floor.

26  CHORNA          [ To leave ]
SYNONYMS: TARAKA, HAJARA, 3ATTALA, KHALLAA, YAZAR, DA3U, and GHAADAR
26.1  TARAKA   (تَرَكَ)   :   this is a common word. It means to leave something, whether it is by purpose or unintentionally, thoughtfully or impulsively. It can be used in any of these cases.
Refer to 2:180 -   this case is unintentional.
Refer to 12:17 -   this case is thoughtful.
____________________________________
26.2  HAJARA   (هَجَرَ)   :   used when one person cuts off his association with another person or people.
Refer to 73:10
Also, another instance of cutting off relations with people is to separate from the place itself. In this context, the meaning of   هجرت   is to leave the country.
Refer to 2:218
____________________________________
26.3 3ATTALA   (عَطَّلَ)   :   to leave something as useless or to make a worker useless.   تعطيل   means the time when one gets free from work. And   مُعَطّل   is that worker who is working now but he is being stopped from working.
Refer to 81:4
And   مُعَطَّلَةٌ بِئْرٌ   refers to well which has been destroyed, is empty or unpopulated.
Refer to 22:45
_____________________________________
26.4  KHALLAA   (خَلّٰى)   :   خَلَا     means to be empty. It can be used in both, (place or tongue**********).   خلوت   means alone.   بعض الٰى خلا     means to meet someone alone.   خَلّٰى   means to separate yourself from someone and leave them alone, ie leaving someone in an empty place. It means to give someone freedom, and not to hold on to them.   سَبِيْلاً خَلّٰى   is a saying which refers not to hold on to someone.
Refer to 9:5
_____________________________________
26.5  YAZAR   (يذر)   :   it is from (Afaal e Naaqsa. It is only used in MUDAARE and AMAR**************). It is used in two ways:
1) to leave something because it is insignificant.
Refer to 6:70
2) doing something and then not allowing anyone to address any problems or interferences in it. In English it is used as the word “let”. For example, “let me do this”.
Refer to 74:11
Here it means that it is between Me and him. You don’t interfere in this matter.
_____________________________________
26.6  DA3U   (دَعُ)   :   this also (Faal Naaqas*********************). It means to leave something peacefully.
Refer to 33:48
And   وَدَّعَ   means to say goodbye to a traveler, or to see someone off happily and with respect. It also includes getting separated yourself and leaving that person.
Refer to 93:31
_____________________________________
26.7 GHAADARA   (غَادَرَ)   :   the word   غَدَر   is used for breaking a promise or unfaithfulness. And   غدار   means an unfaithful person, or a promise breaker. And   غَادَرَ   means to leave something because of some fault in it, or to leave something out.
Refer to 18:47
This means any person, no matter how his deeds are, will not be left out.
Refer to 18:50
_____________________________________
SUMMARY
TARAKA:   is a common word
HAJARA:   to leave your relations or country
3ATTALA:   to leave something useless
KHALLAA:   to leave someone’s way, not hold on to them.
YAZAR:   to leave something because it is insignificant.
DA3U:   means to leave someone peacefully
GHAADAR:   to leave someone because of some fault.

29 CHEENNA or CHEEN LENA
[to snatch]
SYNONYMS: SALABA, GHASABA, NEEL, and KHATAFA
29.1 SALABA   (سَلْب)   :   to take something from someone by force. It means to seize or to pick something, even if the one who is taking is weak.
Refer to 22:73
_______________________________________
29.2 GHASABA   (غَصَبَ)   :   to snatch something with cruelty, oppression, forcefully, or by deception. However, there is a different word for snatching something away by using deception, which is   غبن  . Therefore, for the word   غَصَبَ   the meaning stated by Imam Raghib is correct i.e. a strong person forcefully taking over something from a weak person by cruelty and oppression.
Refer to 18:80
_______________________________________
29.3 NAALA   (ناَلَ)   :   refers to everything that a human can catch with his hand, and he wants it too, or that thing which is within his reach. It refers to taking hold of something or to obtain something.
Refer to 33:25
Then an extension developed in the meaning of this word, and it was also used for a wish being fulfilled, or just fulfillment.
Refer to 2:124
On the other hand another extension developed, because of which this word was also used for the meaning of snatching.
Refer to 9:120
________________________________________
29.4 KHATIFA   (خَطِفَ)   :   fast speed or to fly and swoop down on something in speed, suddenly.
Refer to 2:20
_______________________________________
SUMMARY
SALABA:   to take something forcefully from someone else. common.
GHASABA:   a strong person capturing something of a weak person.
NEEL:   to snatch something which someone wants and it is within his reach.
KHATAFA:   fast speed, and to rapidly grab and take something away.
_______________________________________
For “CHEEKHNA”, see “CHILLANA” and “AAWAAZ”
For “CHEERNA” the words   فَطَّرَ     مَخَرَ   and   قَدَّ   are used. For details, see “PHARHNA”
_______________________________________

29.3 NAALA (ناَلَ) : refers to everything that a human can catch with his hand, and he wants it too, or that thing which is within his reach. It refers to taking hold of something or to obtain something.

Refer to 33:25

 

Then an extension developed in the meaning of this word, and it was also used for a wish being fulfilled, or just fulfillment.

Refer to 2:124

On the other hand another extension developed, because of which this word was also used for the meaning of snatching.

Refer to 9:120

________________________________________

29.4 KHATIFA (خَطِفَ) : fast speed or to fly and swoop down on something in speed, suddenly.

Refer to 2:20

_______________________________________

SUMMARY

SALABA: to take something forcefully from someone else. common.

GHASABA: a strong person capturing something of a weak person.

NEEL: to snatch something which someone wants and it is within his reach.

KHATAFA: fast speed, and to rapidly grab and take something away.

_______________________________________

For “CHEEKHNA”, see “CHILLANA” and “AAWAAZ”

For “CHEERNA” the words فَطَّرَ مَخَرَ and قَدَّ are used. For details, see “PHARHNA”

4 CHAND [Moon]
SYNONYMS: QAMAR(قَمَرَ) AHILLAH(اَهِلَّة)
4.1 / 2 AHILLAH/QAMAR  : AHILLAH plural of HILALهِلاَل. and HILAL meaning new moon and HALLAهَلَّ meaning the manifestation of moon. and AHALLAاَهَلَّ meaning to make some matter famous.like when people sight new moon tell each other by pointing and show each other and spread the word.ALLAH said
Surat Al-Baqarah (The Cow) - سورة البقرة
2:189
يَسْأَلُونَكَ عَنِ الْأَهِلَّةِ ۖ قُلْ هِيَ مَوَاقِيتُ لِلنَّاسِ وَالْحَجِّ ۗ وَلَيْسَ الْبِرُّ بِأَن تَأْتُوا الْبُيُوتَ مِن ظُهُورِهَا وَلَٰكِنَّ الْبِرَّ مَنِ اتَّقَىٰ ۗ وَأْتُوا الْبُيُوتَ مِنْ أَبْوَابِهَا ۚ وَاتَّقُوا اللَّهَ لَعَلَّكُمْ تُفْلِحُونَ
They ask you, [O Muhammad], about the new moons. Say, "They are measurements of time for the people and for Hajj." And it is not righteousness to enter houses from the back, but righteousness is [in] one who fears Allah. And enter houses from their doors. And fear Allah that you may succeed.
People of Arab had divided moon with respect tp shapes in three divisions.HILAL times is 7 days, 3 days after manifest and 4 days before. from 4th till 12 and then 19-26th is QAMAR.13-18th one week is BADRبَدْر. yet its common usage is QAMR . and every shape of moon can be said QAMR.ALLAH said
Surat Yā-Sīn (Ya Sin) - سورة يس
36:39
وَالْقَمَرَ قَدَّرْنَاهُ مَنَازِلَ حَتَّىٰ عَادَ كَالْعُرْجُونِ الْقَدِيمِ
And the moon - We have determined for it phases, until it returns [appearing] like the old date stalk.
SUMMARY  :Every Shape of Moon can be said QAMR.and HILAL is only said for new moon or thin shaped moon.meaning from 26th to 3th of the moon

title: content/ch/ch5.html
raw_text:
5 CHAHNA [To Wish/Long/desire]
SYNONYMS: SHA-A(شَاءَ) AARADA(اَرَادَ) ISHTAHA(اِشْتَهَي) BAGHA IBTIGHA(بَغَي اِبْتَغَي) RAGHIBA(رَغِبَ)
5.1 SHA-A  :It's gerund/verbal nouns is SHAY-شَئْ meaning 'thing' and SHAY- is that which can be known or can be reported(news).plural ASHYA- اشياء. and SHIY-AHشِِيْئَة and MASHIY-AHمَشِيْئَة is Noun meaning 'intention'.actually MASHIY-AH means to invent something or to obtain it.but as creator and manager of every thing is ALLAH.thus MASHIY-AH is only used in the meaning of divine intention(مشيئت الهي).
5.2 AARADA  :there is a difference between MASHI-YAT ILLAHI(مشيئت الهي) and AARADA ILLAHI(اراده الهي). MASHI-YAT is such an intention which is necessary to manifest with regards to the Knowledge of ALLAH and TAQDYR(predestination).on this basis it is said MASHAA-A ALLAHU KANA WA MA LAM YASHAA-U LAM YAKUN(مَاشَآءَ اللّهُ كَانَ وَ مَا لَمْ يَشَآءُ لَمْ يَكُنْ) meaning Whatever ALLAH willed happens and whatever not willed not happen.
whereas AARADA ILLAHI doesn't demand it's final/ultimate manifestation .In the QURAN
Surat Al-Baqarah (The Cow) - سورة البقرة
2:185
شَهْرُ رَمَضَانَ الَّذِي أُنزِلَ فِيهِ الْقُرْآنُ هُدًى لِّلنَّاسِ وَبَيِّنَاتٍ مِّنَ الْهُدَىٰ وَالْفُرْقَانِ ۚ فَمَن شَهِدَ مِنكُمُ الشَّهْرَ فَلْيَصُمْهُ ۖ وَمَن كَانَ مَرِيضًا أَوْ عَلَىٰ سَفَرٍ فَعِدَّةٌ مِّنْ أَيَّامٍ أُخَرَ ۗ يُرِيدُ اللَّهُ بِكُمُ الْيُسْرَ وَلَا يُرِيدُ بِكُمُ الْعُسْرَ وَلِتُكْمِلُوا الْعِدَّةَ وَلِتُكَبِّرُوا اللَّهَ عَلَىٰ مَا هَدَاكُمْ وَلَعَلَّكُمْ تَشْكُرُونَ
The month of Ramadhan [is that] in which was revealed the Qur'an, a guidance for the people and clear proofs of guidance and criterion. So whoever sights [the new moon of] the month, let him fast it; and whoever is ill or on a journey - then an equal number of other days. Allah intends for you ease and does not intend for you hardship and [wants] for you to complete the period and to glorify Allah for that [to] which He has guided you; and perhaps you will be grateful.
and at another place
Surat Ghāfir (The Forgiver) - سورة غافر
40:31
مِثْلَ دَأْبِ قَوْمِ نُوحٍ وَعَادٍ وَثَمُودَ وَالَّذِينَ مِن بَعْدِهِمْ ۚ وَمَا اللَّهُ يُرِيدُ ظُلْمًا لِّلْعِبَادِ
Like the custom of the people of Noah and of 'Aad and Thamud and those after them. And Allah wants no injustice for [His] servants.
even though this matter exists that hardship,difficulty and oppression is found among people.because MASHIYA-AT demands/required of those things.SHA- when relates to human then it refers to such a desire or intention which is subservient to ALLAH's predestination. ALLAH said
Surat At-Takwīr (The Overthrowing) - سورة التكوير
81:29
وَمَا تَشَاءُونَ إِلَّا أَن يَشَاءَ اللَّهُ رَبُّ الْعَالَمِينَ
And you do not will except that Allah wills - Lord of the worlds.
when Human intends to be free from this   restriction.it   can be against the MASHI-YAT of ALLAH. for e.g a human desires that he wouldn't die. yet this is against the MASHI-YAT of ALLAH. therefore it can nnot happen. ALLAH said
Surat Aş-Şaf (The Ranks) - سورة الصف
61:8
يُرِيدُونَ لِيُطْفِئُوا نُورَ اللَّهِ بِأَفْوَاهِهِمْ وَاللَّهُ مُتِمُّ نُورِهِ وَلَوْ كَرِهَ الْكَافِرُونَ
They want to extinguish the light of Allah with their mouths, but Allah will perfect His light, although the disbelievers dislike it.
in addition ,the clear difference between AARADA and MASHI-YAT is that AARADA can be occur early or get delayed.but MASHI-YAT's time does neither occur early or get delayed.
5.3 ISHTAHA  :meaning 'self(one's self) getting attracted to that thing which it like's naturaly.natural disposition for e.g hunger,lust,greed etc. antonym is NAFARAنَفَرَ. and as per Author of MANJAD it means to desire ,desirables things.such desires in which there is not intervention of intention.ALLAH said
Surat Fuşşilat (Explained in Detail) - سورة فصلت
41:31
نَحْنُ أَوْلِيَاؤُكُمْ فِي الْحَيَاةِ الدُّنْيَا وَفِي الْآخِرَةِ ۖ وَلَكُمْ فِيهَا مَا تَشْتَهِي أَنفُسُكُمْ وَلَكُمْ فِيهَا مَا تَدَّعُونَ
We [angels] were your allies in worldly life and [are so] in the Hereafter. And you will have therein whatever your souls desire, and you will have therein whatever you request [or wish]
5.4 BAGHA  :meaning to desire of exceeding moderation in the demand of something.and it can be a commendable attribute as well. as to exceed beyond the duty and it can be deplorable as well. as to exceed beyond the truth to incline towards falsehood. In the QURAN
Surat Yūsuf (Joseph) - سورة يوسف
12:65
وَلَمَّا فَتَحُوا مَتَاعَهُمْ وَجَدُوا بِضَاعَتَهُمْ رُدَّتْ إِلَيْهِمْ ۖ قَالُوا يَا أَبَانَا مَا نَبْغِي ۖ هَٰذِهِ بِضَاعَتُنَا رُدَّتْ إِلَيْنَا ۖ وَنَمِيرُ أَهْلَنَا وَنَحْفَظُ أَخَانَا وَنَزْدَادُ كَيْلَ بَعِيرٍ ۖ ذَٰلِكَ كَيْلٌ يَسِيرٌ
And when they opened their baggage, they found their merchandise returned to them. They said, "O our father, what [more] could we desire? This is our merchandise returned to us. And we will obtain supplies for our family and protect our brother and obtain an increase of a camel's load; that is an easy measurement."
so this money found was not their right which they got
and IBTAGHA meaning to demand by endeavour of something. meaning to strive more than what is required.ALLAH said
Surat Al-Layl (The Night) - سورة الليل
92:20
إِلَّا ابْتِغَاءَ وَجْهِ رَبِّهِ الْأَعْلَىٰ
But only seeking the countenance of his Lord, Most High.
5.5 RAGHIBA  :To like something by heart.and MARGHUWB meaning pleasing to heart.whether this thing is in accordance with natural disposition or not .ALLAH said
Surat Al-Qalam (The Pen) - سورة القلم
68:32
عَسَىٰ رَبُّنَا أَن يُبْدِلَنَا خَيْرًا مِّنْهَا إِنَّا إِلَىٰ رَبِّنَا رَاغِبُونَ
Perhaps our Lord will substitute for us [one] better than it. Indeed, we are toward our Lord desirous."
SUMMARY:
5.1 SHA-A:such a desire or intention which is subject to ALLAH's predestination and this appointed times doesn't get altered/varied
5.2 AARADA: common usage.whether subject to MASHIYA-AT ILLAHI or not.It's time can be varied
5.3 ISHTAHA:desire of pleasing   things.to   desire of natural dispositions
5.4 BAGHA: to exceed moderation for the sake of obtaining something
5.5 RAGHIBA:just desire of something.whether it complies with natural disposition or not

in addition ,the clear difference between AARADA and MASHI-YAT is that AARADA can be occur early or get delayed.but MASHI-YAT's time does neither occur early or get delayed.

5.3 ISHTAHA:meaning 'self(one's self) getting attracted to that thing which it like's naturaly.natural disposition for e.g hunger,lust,greed etc. antonym is NAFARAنَفَرَ. and as per Author of MANJAD it means to desire ,desirables things.such desires in which there is not intervention of intention.ALLAH said

Surat Fuşşilat (Explained in Detail) - سورة فصلت

41:31

نَحْنُ أَوْلِيَاؤُكُمْ فِي الْحَيَاةِ الدُّنْيَا وَفِي الْآخِرَةِ ۖ وَلَكُمْ فِيهَا مَا تَشْتَهِي أَنفُسُكُمْ وَلَكُمْ فِيهَا مَا تَدَّعُونَ

We [angels] were your allies in worldly life and [are so] in the Hereafter. And you will have therein whatever your souls desire, and you will have therein whatever you request [or wish]

5.4 BAGHA:meaning to desire of exceeding moderation in the demand of something.and it can be a commendable attribute as well. as to exceed beyond the duty and it can be deplorable as well. as to exceed beyond the truth to incline towards falsehood. In the QURAN

Surat Yūsuf (Joseph) - سورة يوسف

12:65

وَلَمَّا فَتَحُوا مَتَاعَهُمْ وَجَدُوا بِضَاعَتَهُمْ رُدَّتْ إِلَيْهِمْ ۖ قَالُوا يَا أَبَانَا مَا نَبْغِي ۖ هَٰذِهِ بِضَاعَتُنَا رُدَّتْ إِلَيْنَا ۖ وَنَمِيرُ أَهْلَنَا وَنَحْفَظُ أَخَانَا وَنَزْدَادُ كَيْلَ بَعِيرٍ ۖ ذَٰلِكَ كَيْلٌ يَسِيرٌ

And when they opened their baggage, they found their merchandise returned to them. They said, "O our father, what [more] could we desire? This is our merchandise returned to us. And we will obtain supplies for our family and protect our brother and obtain an increase of a camel's load; that is an easy measurement."

so this money found was not their right which they got

and IBTAGHA meaning to demand by endeavour of something. meaning to strive more than what is required.ALLAH said

Surat Al-Layl (The Night) - سورة الليل

92:20

إِلَّا ابْتِغَاءَ وَجْهِ رَبِّهِ الْأَعْلَىٰ

But only seeking the countenance of his Lord, Most High.

5.5 RAGHIBA:To like something by heart.and MARGHUWB meaning pleasing to heart.whether this thing is in accordance with natural disposition or not .ALLAH said

Surat Al-Qalam (The Pen) - سورة القلم

68:32

عَسَىٰ رَبُّنَا أَن يُبْدِلَنَا خَيْرًا مِّنْهَا إِنَّا إِلَىٰ رَبِّنَا رَاغِبُونَ

Perhaps our Lord will substitute for us [one] better than it. Indeed, we are toward our Lord desirous."

SUMMARY:

5.1 SHA-A:such a desire or intention which is subject to ALLAH's predestination and this appointed times doesn't get altered/varied

5.2 AARADA: common usage.whether subject to MASHIYA-AT ILLAHI or not.It's time can be varied

5.3 ISHTAHA:desire of pleasing things.to desire of natural dispositions

5.4 BAGHA: to exceed moderation for the sake of obtaining something

5.5 RAGHIBA:just desire of something.whether it complies with natural disposition or not

6 CHUP HWNA -REHNA [To be Quiet-To Stay Quiet/Silence]
SYNONYMS:SAKATA(سَكَتَ) SAMATA(صَمَتَ) ANSATA(اَنْصَتَ)
6.1 SAKATA  :to stop suddenly while talking   continuously.to   abate/ let   up.to   silence. opposite of   speech.in   this meaning this word is not used in the QURAN . yet used for the anger abation.ALLAH said
Surat Al-'A`rāf (The Heights) - سورة الأعراف
7:154
وَلَمَّا سَكَتَ عَن مُّوسَى الْغَضَبُ أَخَذَ الْأَلْوَاحَ ۖ وَفِي نُسْخَتِهَا هُدًى وَرَحْمَةٌ لِّلَّذِينَ هُمْ لِرَبِّهِمْ يَرْهَبُونَ
And when the anger subsided in Moses, he took up the tablets; and in their inscription was guidance and mercy for those who are fearful of their Lord.
6.2 SAMATA  :meaning to stay quite.one who talk less,of quiet nature.As per Prophetic Narration MAN SAMATA NAJA(مَنْ صَمَتَ نَجَا) meaning that person who stays silent found salvation.antonym of SAMATA is NATAQAنَطَقَ. MAL-E-SAMAT(urdu) is cash and currency and MAL-E-NATIQ(urdu) to animals.
ALLAH said
Surat Al-'A`rāf (The Heights) - سورة الأعراف
7:193
وَإِن تَدْعُوهُمْ إِلَى الْهُدَىٰ لَا يَتَّبِعُوكُمْ ۚ سَوَاءٌ عَلَيْكُمْ أَدَعَوْتُمُوهُمْ أَمْ أَنتُمْ صَامِتُونَ
And if you [believers] invite them to guidance, they will not follow you. It is all the same for you whether you invite them or you are silent.
6.3 ANSATA  :NASATA(نَصَتَ) and ANSATA meaning to listen to other's discourse quietly.In the QURAN
Surat Al-'A`rāf (The Heights) - سورة الأعراف
7:204
وَإِذَا قُرِئَ الْقُرْآنُ فَاسْتَمِعُوا لَهُ وَأَنصِتُوا لَعَلَّكُمْ تُرْحَمُونَ
So when the Qur'an is recited, then listen to it and pay attention that you may receive mercy.
SUMMARY:
6.1 SAKATA:become quiet, while talking consecutively
6.2 SAMATA:quite ,one who talk less
6.3 ANSATA:to listen to other's discourse quietly

7 CHARAGH [Lamp]
SYNONYMS:MISBAH(مِصْبَاح) SIRAJ(سِرَاج)
7.1 MISBAH  :SABAHAصَبَحَ meaning to be bright and shiny.SABAHA ASSA3R(صَبَحَ الشَّعْر) meaning to have shiny hairs. and SABAHA ALHADIYD(صَبَحَ الْحَدِيْد) meaning shining iron. and SABIYHصَبِِيْح and SABHANصَبْحَان comes in the meaning of beautiful. and Ibn Faris writes that SABAHA is basically indicative of red colour.SUBAH(Morning) is also said so because of its redness. and MISBAH (plural MASABIYHمصابيح)(Lamp) is also said so because of it's redness.In the QURAN
Surat An-Nūr (The Light) - سورة النور
24:35
اللَّهُ نُورُ السَّمَاوَاتِ وَالْأَرْضِ ۚ مَثَلُ نُورِهِ كَمِشْكَاةٍ فِيهَا مِصْبَاحٌ ۖ الْمِصْبَاحُ فِي زُجَاجَةٍ ۖ الزُّجَاجَةُ كَأَنَّهَا كَوْكَبٌ دُرِّيٌّ يُوقَدُ مِن شَجَرَةٍ مُّبَارَكَةٍ زَيْتُونَةٍ لَّا شَرْقِيَّةٍ وَلَا غَرْبِيَّةٍ يَكَادُ زَيْتُهَا يُضِيءُ وَلَوْ لَمْ تَمْسَسْهُ نَارٌ ۚ نُّورٌ عَلَىٰ نُورٍ ۗ يَهْدِي اللَّهُ لِنُورِهِ مَن يَشَاءُ ۚ وَيَضْرِبُ اللَّهُ الْأَمْثَالَ لِلنَّاسِ ۗ وَاللَّهُ بِكُلِّ شَيْءٍ عَلِيمٌ
Allah is the Light of the heavens and the earth. The example of His light is like a niche within which is a lamp, the lamp is within glass, the glass as if it were a pearly [white] star lit from [the oil of] a blessed olive tree, neither of the east nor of the west, whose oil would almost glow even if untouched by fire. Light upon light. Allah guides to His light whom He wills. And Allah presents examples for the people, and Allah is Knowing of all things.
then MISBAH is also used for bright stars in the HOLY QURAN
Surat Al-Mulk (The Sovereignty) - سورة الملك
67:5
وَلَقَدْ زَيَّنَّا السَّمَاءَ الدُّنْيَا بِمَصَابِيحَ وَجَعَلْنَاهَا رُجُومًا لِّلشَّيَاطِينِ ۖ وَأَعْتَدْنَا لَهُمْ عَذَابَ السَّعِيرِ
And We have certainly beautified the nearest heaven with stars and have made [from] them what is thrown at the devils and have prepared for them the punishment of the Blaze.
7.2 SIRAJ  :Ibn Faris said that SARAJAسَرَج is indicative of beauty,adornment and glamour.and SIRAJ(lamp) is said so because of it's light and adornment. horse saddle is said SIRAJسرج as its horse adornment.It is said SARRAJA WAJHAHU(سَرَّجَ وَجْهَهُ) he decorated his face.SARRAJA SHA3RAHU(سَرَّجَ شَعْرَهُ) he breaded or styles his hair. In the QURAN
Surat Al-Furqān (The Criterian) - سورة الفرقان
25:61
تَبَارَكَ الَّذِي جَعَلَ فِي السَّمَاءِ بُرُوجًا وَجَعَلَ فِيهَا سِرَاجًا وَقَمَرًا مُّنِيرًا
Blessed is He who has placed in the sky great stars and placed therein a [burning] lamp and luminous moon.
the aforementioned lexical research of ibn faris and author of Maqa-ys allugha is not confirmed by QURAN. but matter seems to be other way around. QURAN says Sun as SIRAJ
Surat Al-Furqān (The Criterian) - سورة الفرقان
25:61
تَبَارَكَ الَّذِي جَعَلَ فِي السَّمَاءِ بُرُوجًا وَجَعَلَ فِيهَا سِرَاجًا وَقَمَرًا مُّنِيرًا
Blessed is He who has placed in the sky great stars and placed therein a [burning] lamp and luminous moon.
and SIRAJAUN WAHAJAN
Surat An-Naba' (The Tidings) - سورة النبإ
78:13
وَجَعَلْنَا سِرَاجًا وَهَّاجًا
And made [therein] a burning lamp
even thoug its light is reddish not whitish.likewise QURAN says stars as MASABIYH even though their light is Whitish and not reddish.so the real is this
SUMMARY:SIRAJ is that whose light is reddish in nature and MISBAH is that whose light is whitish in nature . and ALLAH knows best.

title: content/ch/ch8.html
raw_text:
8 CHARANA [Grazing]
SYNONYMS:RA3A(رَعَِي) AASAAM(اَسَام)
8.1 RA3A  : meaning to make some cattle graze and it's protection and to upbring. and RA3Iرَاعِي meaning shepherd,herdsman and MAR3Aمَرْعَي meaning fodder as well as   pasture.to   prevent something from getting wasted.and to remove the sources of external threats.antonym is AHMALاهمال meaning herd without shepherd. ALLAH said
Surat Ţāhā (Ta-Ha) - سورة طه
20:54
كُلُوا وَارْعَوْا أَنْعَامَكُمْ ۗ إِنَّ فِي ذَٰلِكَ لَآيَاتٍ لِّأُولِي النُّهَىٰ
Eat [therefrom] and pasture your livestock. Indeed, in that are signs for those of intelligence.
word RA3A basic meaning is training and upbringing therefore it can also be applied to humans. king is RA3Aراعي and public is RA3IYATرعيت
8.2 AASAAM  :SAWMAسَوْم has two basic meanings a) demand b)departure- meaning to depart in demand of something. SAMAT ALIBLسامت الاِبِل meaning Camels went towards the pasture for grazing. and AASAMA meaning to take(cattle) for grazing.ALLAH said
Surat An-Naĥl (The Bee) - سورة النحل
16:10
هُوَ الَّذِي أَنزَلَ مِنَ السَّمَاءِ مَاءً ۖ لَّكُم مِّنْهُ شَرَابٌ وَمِنْهُ شَجَرٌ فِيهِ تُسِيمُونَ
It is He who sends down rain from the sky; from it is drink and from it is foliage in which you pasture [animals].
SUMMARY:
8.1 RA3A:meaning grazing and take care
8.2 AASAAM:to take out for grazing

9- Ascend /Climb(upward)(   چڑھنا  ) - page 414, 415
Note: to watch rising Sun and planets.
Words used are ‘araja’(  عرج  ), ‘Raqiya’(  رقی  ), ‘sa’ada’(  صعد  ), ‘zahara’(  ظہر  ), ‘rahaqa’(  رھق  ) and ‘tasawwara’(  تسور  ).

And [even] if We opened to them a gate from the heaven and they continued therein to ascend,     They would say, "Our eyes have only been dazzled.  أَبْصَارُنَا     سُكِّرَتْ     إِنَّمَا     لَقَالُوا  يَعْرُجُونَ     فِيهِ     فَظَلُّوا     السَّمَاءِ     مِّنَ     بَابًا     عَلَيْهِم     فَتَحْنَا     وَلَوْ   [15:14].
2)-Raqiya’(  رقی  ) means doing magic as well as climbing height. Such that one should do according to his/her power. To climb sedately with slow speed. 5)- ‘rahaqa’(  رھق  )  means one thing getting over another and hiding it or covering it. It has a reflex quality.   رہقہ     الامر   means a matter hides it forcefully or oppressly i.e; covered it. Quran says:
And [other] faces, that Day, will have upon them dust.   Blackness will cover them.  قَتَرَةٌتَرْهَقُهَا      غَبَرَةٌ     عَلَيْهَا     يَوْمَئِذٍ     وَوُجُوهٌ   [80:41]

And has there come to you the news of the adversaries, when they climbed over the wall of [his] prayer chamber -  الْمِحْرَابَ     تَسَوَّرُوا     إِذْ     الْخَصْمِ     نَبَأُ     أَتَاكَ     وَهَلْ   [38:21]
Conclusion:1) ‘araja’(  عرج  ) for climbing with pauses.
2) ‘Raqiya’(  رقی  ) for climbing according to power.
3) ‘sa’ada’(  صعد  ) for climbing upward with problem.
4) ‘zahara’(  ظہر  ) for reaching the height.
5) ‘rahaqa’(  رھق  )   for getting over one thing over another and covering it.
6) ‘tasawwara’(  تسور  ) for climbing wall or crossing over it.

raw_text:
Yadkhuloona, “daakhil hona”, P.473 [any] man
Synonyms:DAKHALA,IDKHIL,WALAJA,AULIJ,SALA,SALLA
SALAKA
1 DAKHALA(دَخَلَ):famous word,  come inside  (opp KHARAJA(خَرَجَ) meaning to go outside and its usage is common
Surat Yūsuf (Joseph)[12:36]
وَ  دَخَلَ   مَعَهُ السِّجْنَ فَتَيَانِ
And there   entered   the prison with him two young men
and IDKHIL(إدخل) is used for "to enter"
Surat Al-'Insān (The Man)[76:31]
يُدْخِلُ   مَن يَشَاءُ فِي رَحْمَتِهِ ۚ
He   admits   whom He wills into His mercy
2 WALAJA(وَلَجَ):ALWALUJ(الوَلوج) meaning   to enter into a narrow place   ,  to enter with difficulty,
Surat Al-'A`rāf (The Heights)[7:40]
وَلَا يَدْخُلُونَ الْجَنَّةَ حَتَّىٰ   يَلِجَ   الْجَمَلُ فِي سَمِّ الْخِيَاطِ ۚ
nor will they enter Paradise until a camel   enters   into the eye of a needle
and   to enter forcefully   is AULAJ(اُولِج)
Surat Al-Ĥaj (The Pilgrimage)[22:61]
يُولِجُ   اللَّيْلَ فِي النَّهَارِ   وَيُولِجُ   النَّهَارَ فِي اللَّيْلِ
causes the night to   enter   the day and causes the day to   enter   the night
3 SALA(صَلي): is particularly used for 'entering into fire'.meaning   to enter into fire and burn
Surat 'Ibrāhīm (Abrahim)[14:29]
جَهَنَّمَ   يَصْلَوْنَهَا   ۖ وَبِئْسَ الْقَرَارُ
[It is] Hell, which they will   [enter to] burn  , and wretched is the settlement.
and to make some one enter into fire or burn SALLA(صلّي) will be used
Surat Al-Ĥāqqah (The Reality)[69:31]
ثُمَّ الْجَحِيمَ   صَلُّوهُ
Then into Hellfire   drive   him.
4 SALAKA(سَلَكَ):has many meanings and can be transitive or intransitive and all of these meaning refers to '  to enter'
A) meaning to thread like beads or pearls on thread
Surat Ash-Shu`arā' (The Poets)[26:200]
كَذَٰلِكَ   سَلَكْنَاهُ   فِي قُلُوبِ الْمُجْرِمِينَ
Thus have We   inserted   disbelief into the hearts of the criminals
B) to put into like putting hand in to shirt
Surat Al-Qaşaş (The Stories)[28:32]
اسْلُكْ   يَدَكَ فِي جَيْبِكَ تَخْرُجْ بَيْضَاءَ مِنْ غَيْرِ سُوء
Insert   your hand into the opening of your garment; it will come out white, without disease
same piece of ayah is used at another place with IDKHIL
Surat An-Naml (The Ant)[27:12]
وَ  أَدْخِلْ   يَدَكَ فِي جَيْبِكَ تَخْرُجْ بَيْضَاءَ مِنْ غَيْرِ سُوءٍ
And   put   your hand into the opening of your garment [at the breast]; it will come out white without disease
C)to follow a path,ALLAH said to the honey bee
Surat An-Naĥl (The Bee)[16:69]
فَاسْلُكِي   سُبُلَ رَبِّكِ ذُلُلًا
and   follow   the ways of your Lord laid down [for you].  "
in the above ayah USLLUKI( اسلَُكَي) has been translated as UDKHULI(اُدخلي)
Surat Al-Muddaththir (The Cloaked One)[74:42]
مَا   سَلَكَكُمْ   فِي سَقَرَ
[And asking them], "What   put   you into Saqar?"
by putting all of these specifications in view sahib muntaha alarib has describe it's summarized meaning as "  to pull one thing to another thing or from another thing  " as per sahib munjad "  to put onething in another thing"   whereas sahib miqyas allugha defines two basic meanings 1)to follow along the path 2)to enter one thing in to other
Summary:
1 DAKHALA:general usage
2 WALAJA: enter into narrow place
3 SALA:enter into fire
4 SALAK:to put or pull one thing into another

10. between, in the middle of, center point   (DARMIYAN)
Synonyms: BAYN, KHILAAL, WAST, SAWAAA, QASD
10.1 BAYN (بَيْن):   Between two points. It defines the connectivity or separation of two different objects. Bana (بَانَ) means to be distant from, so bayn is used to express separation between two objects. According to Ibn Alfaris the word bayn is used to express distinction between two different things
Surat Al-Baqarah (The Cow) - البقرة سورة
2:164
بَيْنَ السَّمَاءِ وَالْأَرْضِ
between the heaven and the earth
Surat Şād (The Letter "Saad") - ص سورة
38:22
فَاحْكُم بَيْنَنَا بِالْحَقِّ
so judge between us with truth
10.2 KHILAAL (خِلٰل):   Point or space between two integrated things. A toothpick is called Alkhilala (اَلْخِلَالَ). Khalal is the act of moving the fingers (of hand) across the beard during ablution. Allah says in the Quran:
Surat Al-Kahf (The Cave) - الكهف سورة
18:33
وَفَجَّرْنَا خِلَالَهُمَا نَهَرًا
And We caused to gush forth within them a river.
This word  is also used to express the space; opening  between the different components of one object as in Quran:
Surat An-Nūr (The Light) - النور سورة
24:43
فَتَرَى الْوَدْقَ يَخْرُجُ مِنْ خِلَالِهِ
then makes them into a heap of layers, and you see the rain comes forth from between them
10.3 WAST (وَسْط):   midway or halfway. To be at the middle of - be in the center of. Allah says in Holy Quran:
Surat Al-Baqarah (The Cow) - البقرة سورة
2:238
حَافِظُوا عَلَى الصَّلَوَاتِ وَالصَّلَاةِ الْوُسْطَىٰ
Maintain with care the [obligatory] prayers and [in particular] the middle prayer
Surat Al-Baqarah (The Cow) - البقرة سورة
2:143
وَكَذَٰلِكَ جَعَلْنَاكُمْ أُمَّةً وَسَطًا
And thus We have made you a medium (just) nation
10.4 SAWAAA (سَوَاۤء):   In the midst of; center point. According to Ibn Alfaris it means “الشَّيْئَينِ بَيْنَ الْاِعْتِدَال وَ  اَلْاِسْتِقَامَة”. In Holy Quran:
Surat Ad-Dukhān (The Smoke) - الدخان سورة
44:47
خُذُوهُ فَاعْتِلُوهُ إِلَىٰ سَوَاءِ الْجَحِيمِ
[It will be commanded], "Seize him and drag him into the midst of the Hellfire
10.5 QASD (قَصْد):   moderation or reasonableness. Just like generosity between extravagance and parsimony and gallantry between derring-do and tameness. Qasada (قَصَدَ) and النفقة   فى   اقتصد means     economization; to spend moderately. Qasad as sabeel (السَّبِيْل     قَصَدَ) means to walk on a path straightly. Allah says in the quran:
Surat Luqmān (Luqman) - لقمان سورة
31:19
وَاقْصِدْ فِي مَشْيِكَ وَاغْضُضْ مِن صَوْتِكَ
And be moderate in your pace and lower your voice
Summary:
10.1 BAYN: In between two different things
10.2 KHILALA: Point or space between two integrated things
10.3 WAST: To be at the middle of (with respect to amount or distance)
10.4 SAWAAA: In the midst of; center point
10.5 QASD: Moderation

فَاحْكُم بَيْنَنَا بِالْحَقِّ

so judge between us with truth

 

10.2 KHILAAL (خِلٰل): Point or space between two integrated things. A toothpick is called Alkhilala (اَلْخِلَالَ). Khalal is the act of moving the fingers (of hand) across the beard during ablution. Allah says in the Quran:

 

Surat Al-Kahf (The Cave) - الكهف سورة

18:33

وَفَجَّرْنَا خِلَالَهُمَا نَهَرًا

And We caused to gush forth within them a river.

 

 

This word  is also used to express the space; opening  between the different components of one object as in Quran:

 

Surat An-Nūr (The Light) - النور سورة

24:43

فَتَرَى الْوَدْقَ يَخْرُجُ مِنْ خِلَالِهِ

then makes them into a heap of layers, and you see the rain comes forth from between them

 

10.3 WAST (وَسْط): midway or halfway. To be at the middle of - be in the center of. Allah says in Holy Quran:

 

Surat Al-Baqarah (The Cow) - البقرة سورة

2:238

حَافِظُوا عَلَى الصَّلَوَاتِ وَالصَّلَاةِ الْوُسْطَىٰ

Maintain with care the [obligatory] prayers and [in particular] the middle prayer

 

Surat Al-Baqarah (The Cow) - البقرة سورة

2:143

وَكَذَٰلِكَ جَعَلْنَاكُمْ أُمَّةً وَسَطًا

And thus We have made you a medium (just) nation

 

10.4 SAWAAA (سَوَاۤء): In the midst of; center point. According to Ibn Alfaris it means “الشَّيْئَينِ بَيْنَ الْاِعْتِدَال وَ  اَلْاِسْتِقَامَة”. In Holy Quran:

 

Surat Ad-Dukhān (The Smoke) - الدخان سورة

44:47

خُذُوهُ فَاعْتِلُوهُ إِلَىٰ سَوَاءِ الْجَحِيمِ

[It will be commanded], "Seize him and drag him into the midst of the Hellfire

 

10.5 QASD (قَصْد): moderation or reasonableness. Just like generosity between extravagance and parsimony and gallantry between derring-do and tameness. Qasada (قَصَدَ) and النفقة فى اقتصد means economization; to spend moderately. Qasad as sabeel (السَّبِيْل قَصَدَ) means to walk on a path straightly. Allah says in the quran:

 

Surat Luqmān (Luqman) - لقمان سورة

31:19

وَاقْصِدْ فِي مَشْيِكَ وَاغْضُضْ مِن صَوْتِكَ

And be moderate in your pace and lower your voice

 

Summary:

10.1 BAYN: In between two different things

10.2 KHILALA: Point or space between two integrated things

 10.3 WAST: To be at the middle of (with respect to amount or distance)

10.4 SAWAAA: In the midst of; center point

10.5 QASD: Moderation

11. Dushmani دشمنی (Rivalry – Enmity)
Also known as ‘aduww’   عدُوّ   and ‘adawah’   عَدَاوَة  , ‘baghdaa’   بَغضَاء   and ‘shana’an’   شَنَان   and ‘shaani’a’   شَانِيءَ
1.          Aduww   عدُوّ  : (aadaa)   اعدَاء   It refers so such a person who is a worse kind of enemy. One who thinks and schemes for evil, harm and loss, and feels joyful at suffering and misery. The antonym is ‘Siddique’   صدّيق   .
Allah Taa’la says:
Surah Al Araaf (The Heights)    سُوۡرَةُ الاٴعرَاف
(7:22)
إِنَّ ٱلشَّيۡطَـٰنَ لَكُمَا عَدُوٌّ۬ مُّبِينٌ۬
“So he made them fall, through deception. And when they tasted of the tree, their private parts became apparent to them, and they began to fasten together over themselves from the leaves of Paradise. And their Lord called to them, "Did I not forbid you from that tree and tell you   that Satan is to you a clear enemy?  ”
Adawah   عَدَاوَة   means enmity and antagonism. It is the first stage of rivalry. It means to be put off by someone’s victory. (Antonym: ‘wilayat’   ولَايت   [guardianship])
2.          Baghdaa   بَغضَاء  : ‘Bughd’   بُغض   (whose antonym is ‘Hubb’   حُبّ  ) means to be disgusted by or be hateful towards something or someone. This is the second stage of enmity. ‘Bughdaah’   بغضة   means to aim to make someone contemptible, worthless and humiliated.
Allah Taa’la says:
Surah Al Maidah (The Table Spread)   سُوۡرَةُ المَائدة
(5:64)
وَأَلۡقَيۡنَا بَيۡنَہُمُ ٱلۡعَدَٲوَةَ وَٱلۡبَغۡضَآءَ إِلَىٰ يَوۡمِ ٱلۡقِيَـٰمَةِ‌ۚ
“And the Jews say, "The hand of Allah is chained." Chained are their hands, and cursed are they for what they say. Rather, both His hands are extended; He spends however He wills. And that which has been revealed to you from your Lord will surely increase many of them in transgression and disbelief.   And We have cast among them animosity and hatred until the Day of Resurrection.   Every time they kindled the fire of war [against you], Allah extinguished it. And they strive throughout the land [causing] corruption, and Allah does not like corrupters.”
3.          Shaani’a   شَانِيءَ  : ‘Shanaa’   شَنَاءَ   means to hold contempt, antagonism and malice. To hate. It is the root for ‘shanaa’an’   شَنَاءَن  .
Allah Taa’la says:
Surah Al Maidah (The Table Spread)   سُوۡرَةُ المَائدة
(5:8)
وَلَا يَجۡرِمَنَّڪُمۡ شَنَـَٔانُ قَوۡمٍ عَلَىٰٓ أَلَّا تَعۡدِلُواْ‌ۚ
“O you who have believed, be persistently standing firm for Allah , witnesses in justice, and do   not let the hatred of a people prevent you from being just.   Be just; that is nearer to righteousness. And fear Allah ; indeed, Allah is Acquainted with what you do.”
‘Shaani’   شَانِيء   is a person who not only holds hatred and antagonism but is also vindictive; which means he holds contempt and malice concurrently. This is the worst kind of enemy. It is the third stage of enmity.
Allah Taa’la says:
Surah Al Kauther (The Abundance)    سُوۡرَةُ الکَوثَر
(108:3)
إِنَّ شَانِئَكَ هُوَ ٱلۡأَبۡتَرُ
“Indeed, your enemy is the one cut off.”

12. Dua kerna – dena دعا کرنا - دینا (To pray – To Pray For)
Also known as ‘da’aa’   دَعَا  , ‘salama’   سَلَّمَ  , ’Hayyaya’   حَيَّيَ   and ‘Salla’   صَلَّ   in the Holy Quran.
1.          Da’aa   دَعَا  : (da’u)   دعو   It means to call out, to call for. This word is used both in the context of praying and cursing. The only difference is that if the suffix is ‘lahu’   لَهُ  , then it refers to the prayer being a blessing and if the suffix is ‘aala’   عَلَى   then it refers to the prayer being a curse. For example ‘da’an lahu’   دَعاً     لَهُ   means ‘someone was prayed for’ and ‘da’a alaeh’   دَعاً     عَلَيه   means ‘someone was cursed at’.  (This word has not been used in the Holy Quran in the context of cursing).
Allah Taa’la says:
Surah Al Baqarah (The Cow)   سُوۡرَةُ     البَقَرَة
(2:61)
وَإِذۡ قُلۡتُمۡ يَـٰمُوسَىٰ لَن نَّصۡبِرَ عَلَىٰ طَعَامٍ۬ وَٲحِدٍ۬ فَٱدۡعُ لَنَا رَبَّكَ يُخۡرِجۡ لَنَا مِمَّا تُنۢبِتُ ٱلۡأَرۡضُ
“  And [recall] when you said, "O Moses, we can never endure one [kind of] food. So call upon your Lord to bring forth for us from the earth its green herbs and its cucumbers and its garlic and its lentils and its onions."   [Moses] said, "Would you exchange what is better for what is less? Go into [any] settlement and indeed, you will have what you have asked." And they were covered with humiliation and poverty and returned with anger from Allah [upon them]. That was because they [repeatedly] disbelieved in the signs of Allah and killed the prophets without right. That was because they disobeyed and were [habitually] transgressing.”
2.          Salama   سَلَّمَ  : To keep healthy, provide security, submission and to pray for someone’s health and wellness. To say ‘Assalam Alaykum’   السلام     علیکم  .
Allah Taa’la says:
Surah Al Noor (The Light)   سُوۡرَةُ النُّور
(24:61)
فَإِذَا دَخَلۡتُم بُيُوتً۬ا فَسَلِّمُواْ عَلَىٰٓ أَنفُسِكُمۡ
“There is not upon the blind [any] constraint nor upon the lame constraint nor upon the ill constraint nor upon yourselves when you eat from your [own] houses or the houses of your fathers or the houses of your mothers or the houses of your brothers or the houses of your sisters or the houses of your father's brothers or the houses of your father's sisters or the houses of your mother's brothers or the houses of your mother's sisters or [from houses] whose keys you possess or [from the house] of your friend. There is no blame upon you whether you eat together or separately.   But when you enter houses, give greetings of peace upon each other - a greeting from Allah ,   blessed and good. Thus does Allah make clear to you the verses [of ordinance] that you may understand.”
3.          Hayyaya   حَيَّيَ  : Hayya   حَيَى   means to stay alive. Hayyaya   حَيَّيَ   (Tahiyyah)   تَحِيَّةً   means to say ‘Hayyak Allah’   حَيَّاك     الّله   to someone, which means ‘May Allah increases you in age’. This is a common word used for the blessing someone I prayer. It also comes in the context of praying for someone’s wellness and well being: ‘Ya sallam’   يا     سَلَّم   or ‘Ya salaam’   يا     سَلَام  . As though ‘sallam’   سَلَّم   is used in particularity and ‘hayya’   حَيَى   is used in a more general meaning.
Allah Taa’la says:
Surah An Nisa (The Women)   سُوۡرَةُ النِّسَاء
(4:86)
وَإِذَا حُيِّيتُم بِتَحِيَّةٍ۬ فَحَيُّواْ بِأَحۡسَنَ مِنۡہَآ أَوۡ رُدُّوهَآ‌ۗ
“  And when you are greeted with a greeting, greet [in return] with one better than it or [at least] return it [in a like manner].   Indeed, Allah is ever, over all things, an Accountant.”
4.          Salla   صَلَّ  : (salw)   صلو   ‘Salaah’   صلَوة   is an Islamic term referring to the five obligatory prayers which is a basic constituent of Islam. However, the real meaning of it refers to blessing or praying for. To show appreciation and declare respect.
Allah Taa’la says:
Surah At Tawbah (The Repentance)   سُوۡرَةُ التّوبَة
(9:103)
وَصَلِّ عَلَيۡهِمۡ‌ۖ إِنَّ صَلَوٰتَكَ سَكَنٌ۬ لَّهُمۡ‌ۗ
“Take, [O, Muhammad], from their wealth a charity by which you purify them and cause them increase,   and invoke [ Allah 's blessings] upon them. Indeed, your invocations are reassurance for them.   And Allah is Hearing and Knowing.”
If the word ‘salla’   صَلّ   is in relation with Allah Taa’la, then it means blessing of mercy. If it is directed towards a person, then it means a prayer for the blessing of mercy.
Allah Taa’la says:
Surah Al Ahzab (The Combined Forces)   سُوۡرَةُ الاٴحزَاب
(33:56)
إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ وَمَلَـٰٓٮِٕڪَتَهُ ۥ يُصَلُّونَ عَلَى ٱلنَّبِىِّۚ يَـٰٓأَيُّہَا ٱلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُواْ صَلُّواْ عَلَيۡهِ وَسَلِّمُواْ تَسۡلِيمًا
“Indeed, Allah confers blessing upon the Prophet, and His angels [ask Him to do so]. O you who have believed, ask [ Allah to confer] blessing upon him and ask [ Allah to grant him] peace.”
Conclusion:
(1)       Duaa   دُعَا  : This is a commonly used word to describe all kinds of prayers.
(2)       Sallama   سَلَّمَ  : To say ‘salam’   سلام  , to bless one for their well being.
(3)       Hayyaya   حَيَّيَ  : To pray for or bless someone a long life.
(4)       Salla   صَلّ  : To pray for blessing for mercy. To recite(send) durood   درود   to the Prophet (s.a.w)

13. Dil دل (heart)
Also known as ‘qalb’   قَلب  , ‘fuwaad’   فُوَأد   (faad)   فاد  , ‘sadr’   صَدر   and ‘nafs’   نَفس   in the Holy Quran.
1.          Qalb   قَلب  : An important organ. A source of life and existence. For thinking, comprehending, wisdom and intellect, Allah Taa’la has addressed the heart. The actions that the modern medicine has associated with the mind, the Holy Quran has associated with the heart.
Allah Taa’la says:
Surah Al Araaf (The Heights)   سُوۡرَةُ الاٴعرَاف
(7:179)

(33:37)

 وَتُخۡفِى فِى نَفۡسِكَ مَا ٱللَّهُ مُبۡدِيهِ

“And [remember, O Muhammad], when you said to the one on whom Allah bestowed favor and you bestowed favor, "Keep your wife and fear Allah ," while you concealed within yourself that which Allah is to disclose. And you feared the people, while Allah has more right that you fear Him. So when Zayd had no longer any need for her, We married her to you in order that there not be upon the believers any discomfort concerning the wives of their adopted sons when they no longer have need of them. And ever is the command of Allah accomplished.”

(2) The association of wishes and desires is with ‘nafs’ نَفس whether the desires are good or evil.

Allah Taa’la says:

Surah An Najm (The Star) سُوۡرَةُ النّجْم

(53:23)

 إِن يَتَّبِعُونَ إِلَّا ٱلظَّنَّ وَمَا تَهۡوَى ٱلۡأَنفُسُ‌ۖ

“They are not but [mere] names you have named them - you and your forefathers - for which Allah has sent down no authority. They follow not except assumption and what [their] souls desire, and there has already come to them from their Lord guidance.”

 

(3) The association of happiness is also related with ‘nafs’ نَفس.

Allah Taa’la says:

Surah An Nisa (The Women) سُوۡرَةُ النِّسَاء

(4:4)

 فَإِن طِبۡنَ لَكُمۡ عَن شَىۡءٍ۬ مِّنۡهُ نَفۡسً۬ا فَكُلُوهُ هَنِيٓـًٔ۬ا مَّرِيٓـًٔ۬ا

“And give the women [upon marriage] their [bridal] gifts graciously. But if they give up willingly to you anything of it, then take it in satisfaction and ease.”

 

Conclusion:

(1)   Qalb قَلب: A source of rationality, Sense of awareness, understanding and wisdom.

(2)   Fuwaad فُوَأد: A center of the intensity of feelings and emotions.

(3)   Sadr صَدر: Locative. Vastness and narrowness. To keep thoughts in secret.

(4)   Nafs نَفس: A center of desires. It is used to refer to being delighted and to keep things secretive.

 

<<Alternate translation>>

 دل – Heart

These words   ) صدر نفس قلب فؤاد (فاد are in Quran.

1.         قلب – a well-known organ of the body, the source of soul and life (قلوب) Allah addresses the heart for thinking, thought, intelligence, understanding.   All the things which modern science and medicine have related to the brain, the Quran has related to the heart.

 

In Surah Al-AAraaf:   (7:179):

 

لَهُمْ قُلُوبٌ لَّا يَفْقَهُونَ بِهَا

 

They have hearts with which they do not understand,

 

2.         فؤاد – some scholars have written that the same difference between ain  عينand basarبصر   or uzun  اذنand samaسمع  , is the same difference in قلب and فؤاد , the proof is in this Ayah below.

 

In Surah Al-Israa:   (17:36):

 

إِنَّ السَّمْعَ وَالْبَصَرَ وَالْفُؤَادَ كُلُّ أُولَٰئِكَ كَانَ عَنْهُ مَسْئُولًا

 

Indeed, the hearing, the sight and the heart - about all those [one] will be questioned.

 

But this is not the fact, because Allah has addressed the heart directly for intelligence, to understand, to think, to comprehend. The real fact is that this part of the body, the heart has many components, just as the brain has different components with different strengths.  In the same way the heart has special components related to special emotions, feelings and actions. According to the science of medicine فؤاد is the upper part of the heart which is above the opening of the stomach, and وجع الفؤاد  means pain of that particular part of the body, فؤاد plural افئدة is derived from فأد.  فأد اللحم means to roast meat on fire, and لحم فئيد  means roasted meat on fire. According to Ibn Faaris الفأد يدل على حمى وشدة الحرارة (ML) – this word indicates heat and severe heat, therefore whenever human’s experience strong emotions and its effects are mentioned then this word would be used.

 

In Surah Al-Qasas: (28:10):

 

وَأَصْبَحَ فُؤَادُ أُمِّ مُوسَىٰ فَارِغًا ۖ

 

And the heart of Moses' mother became empty [of all else].

In Surah Ibrahim ( 14;43)

 

مُهْطِعِينَ مُقْنِعِي رُءُوسِهِمْ لَا يَرْتَدُّ إِلَيْهِمْ طَرْفُهُمْ ۖ وَأَفْئِدَتُهُمْ هَوَاءٌ

 

Racing ahead, their heads raised up, their glance does not come back to them, and their hearts are void.

 

And the mentioning of when Allah will question the فؤاد , it is related to those deeds which have occurred due to strong emotions.

 

3.         صدر – means chest, (plural صدور) and the heart is in the chest.

 

In Surah Haj: (22:46):

 

وَلَٰكِن تَعْمَى الْقُلُوبُ الَّتِي فِي الصُّدُورِ

 

but blinded are the hearts which are within the breasts.

 

Therefore sometimes when the word صدور is used it means hearts, such as:

 

In Surah Yunus: (10:57):

 

وَشِفَاءٌ لِّمَا فِي الصُّدُورِ

 

and healing for what is in the breasts,

Now because the connection of صدر is to adverb of place, therefore whenever there is a need of mentioning the tightness or spaciousness of the heart then the word صدر is used.

 

In Surah Al-Hijr:  (15:97):

 

وَلَقَدْ نَعْلَمُ أَنَّكَ يَضِيقُ صَدْرُكَ بِمَا يَقُولُونَ

 

And We already know that your breast is constrained by what they say

In Surah As-Sarh: (94:1):

 

أَلَمْ نَشْرَحْ لَكَ صَدْرَكَ

 

Did We not expand for you, [O Muhammad], your breast?

 

And شرح صدر  or انشراح صدر is an idiom, when your has  heart has a right feeling about a complicated, difficult matter you call it شرح صدر  .  In order to hide something you need an adverb, therefore to hide a secret, a superstition, a thought, the word  صدر will be used.

 

In Surah Gafir: (40:19):

 

يَعْلَمُ خَائِنَةَ الْأَعْيُنِ وَمَا تُخْفِي الصُّدُورُ

 

He knows that which deceives the eyes and what the breasts conceal.

In Surah Maida: (5:7):

 

إِنَّ اللَّهَ عَلِيمٌ بِذَاتِ الصُّدُورِ

 

Indeed, Allah is Knowing of that within the breasts.

 

In Surah Naas:  (114:5):

 

الَّذِي يُوَسْوِسُ فِي صُدُورِ النَّاسِ

 

Who whispers [evil] into the breasts of mankind.

 

4.         نفس – soul, life, heart, mind , plural نفوس – the source/ origin and refuge of desires. Meaning a heart that desires things and is happy.

 

a.         the connection of concealing thoughts and secrets, this attribute is shared in both  نفوس and صدور.

 

In Surah Ahzaab: (33:37):

 

وَتُخْفِي فِي نَفْسِكَ مَا اللَّهُ مُبْدِيهِ

 

While you concealed within yourself that which Allah is to disclose.

 

b.           the connection of desires is with  نفس either good or bad.

 

In Surah Najm:  (53:23):

 

إِن يَتَّبِعُونَ إِلَّا الظَّنَّ وَمَا تَهْوَى الْأَنفُسُ

 

They follow not except assumption and what [their] souls desire,

c.       the connection of happiness is with    نفس too.

 

In Surah Nisaa: (4:4):

 

فَإِن طِبْنَ لَكُمْ عَن شَيْءٍ مِّنْهُ نَفْسًا فَكُلُوهُ هَنِيئًا مَّرِيئًا

 

But if they give up willingly to you anything of it, then take it in satisfaction and ease.

 

 

Summary:

 

1.     قلب – the source origin of intelligence sense, comprehension.

2.     فؤاد – the centre of strong emotions

3.     صدر – adverb for tightness , spaciousness and to conceal matters

4.     نفس – the centre of desires, it is used for ‘to be happy’ and ‘to hide matters’

14. Dil Mein Baat Daalna دل میں بات ڈالنا (To Drop an Idea/Hint in the Heart)
Also known as ‘Wahi’   وَحىٌ  , ‘Ilhaam’   اِلهَام  , ‘Ilqaa’   اِلقَاء   , ‘Waswaas’   وَسوَاس   and ‘Hamazaat’   هَمَزَات   in the Holy Quran.
1.          Wahi   وَحىٌ  :   The lexical meaning is a strong sign. ‘Aohaa’   اَوحَى   means to give a rapid sign about the unseen; hidden and unknown. There are many types of ‘Wahi’   وحى   ; one of which deals with the inexpugnable and impregnable affairs.
Allah Taa’la says:
Surah Fussilat (Explained in Detail)   سُوۡرَةُ فُصّلَت
(41:12)
وَأَوۡحَىٰ فِى كُلِّ سَمَآءٍ أَمۡرَهَا‌ۚ
“And He completed them as seven heavens within two days   and inspired in each heaven its command.   And We adorned the nearest heaven with lamps and as protection. That is the determination of the Exalted in Might, the Knowing.”
In a different context, ‘wahi’   وحى   has also been explained as an innate or natural guidance/intuition. For example, the instinct of a new born baby to dart towards the mother’s chest.
Allah Taa’la says:
Surah An Nahl (The Bee)   سُوۡرَةُ النّحل
(12:68)
وَأَوۡحَىٰ رَبُّكَ إِلَى ٱلنَّحۡلِ
“  And your Lord inspired to the bee  , "Take for yourself among the mountains, houses, and among the trees and [in] that which they construct.”
As though the guidance and intuition (wahi)   وحى   from Allah Taa’la comes to all creatures; mankind, animals and insects. Such intuition can come towards a non prophet as well.
Allah Taa’la says:
Surah Al Qasas (The Stories)   سُوۡرَةُ القَصَص
(28:7)
وَأَوۡحَيۡنَآ إِلَىٰٓ أُمِّ مُوسَىٰٓ أَنۡ أَرۡضِعِيهِ‌ۖ
“  And We inspired to the mother of Moses,   "Suckle him; but when you fear for him, cast him into the river and do not fear and do not grieve. Indeed, We will return him to you and will make him [one] of the messengers."
In all of the above examples, the meaning of ‘wahi’   وحى   has been used in its lexical context. In a similar connotation, a person also does ‘wahi’   وحى   to another person.
Allah Taa’la says:
Surah Maryam (Mary)   سُوۡرَةُ مَریَم
(19:11)
فَأَوۡحَىٰٓ إِلَيۡہِمۡ أَن سَبِّحُواْ بُكۡرَةً۬ وَعَشِيًّ۬ا
“So he came out to his people from the prayer chamber and   signaled to them to exalt [ Allah ] in the morning and afternoon  .”
Even Satan (shaitaan)   شيطان   does ‘wahi’   وحى   amongst each other.
Allah Taa’la says:
Surah Al Anaam (The Cattle)   سُوۡرَةُ الاٴنعَام
(6:121)
وَإِنَّ ٱلشَّيَـٰطِينَ لَيُوحُونَ إِلَىٰٓ أَوۡلِيَآٮِٕهِمۡ لِيُجَـٰدِلُوكُمۡ‌ۖ
“And do not eat of that upon which the name of Allah has not been mentioned, for indeed, it is grave disobedience  . And indeed do the devils inspire their allies [among men] to dispute with you.   And if you were to obey them, indeed, you would be associators [of others with Him].”
Therefore, ‘wahi’   وحى   can be a guidance, a blessing or even sinister. The ‘wahi’   وحى   that is guidance is always based on wellness, and the ‘wahi’   وحى   that goes against the guidance is definitely the sinister whisperings. In the Islamic term, ‘wahi’   وحى   refers to such knowledge, wisdom and insights of the unseen that Allah Taa’la sends onto his beloved creation (prophet) for the guidance of the mankind. Three of such scenarios have been discussed in the Holy Quran. (1) Allah Taa’la directly puts in the heart. (2) Allah Taa’la sends an angel to his messenger. (3) Communicate behind a veil. (Case in point Musa aleh assalam). Henceforth, the commonly used scenario from these is Allah Taa’la sends the guidance, the ‘wahi’   وحى   through his angel (Gabriel aleh assalam) to his prophets and messengers who then verbalize it.
Allah Taa’la says:
Surah Al Baqarah (the Cow)   سُوۡرَةُ البَقَرَة
(2:97)
قُلۡ مَن كَانَ عَدُوًّ۬ا لِّجِبۡرِيلَ فَإِنَّهُ ۥ نَزَّلَهُ ۥ عَلَىٰ قَلۡبِكَ بِإِذۡنِ ٱللَّهِ
“  Say, "Whoever is an enemy to Gabriel - it is [none but] he who has brought the Qur'an down upon your heart, [O Muhammad], by permission of Allah ,   confirming that which was before it and as guidance and good tidings for the believers."
2.          Ilhaam   اِلهَام  :    It refers to the intuition/guidance that is induced in the heart by Allah taa’la or a wise and knowledgeable person. To provide insight, understanding and strengthen encouragement. Similar to ‘wahi’   وحى  , ‘ilhaam’   اِلهَام   can also come from Shaitaan   شيطان  , especially when it cannot be validated through any ayah or Islamic text. This is why, apart from the Sufi class, none of the scholars consider ‘ilhaam’   اِلهَام   as debatable for evidence. The difference between ‘wahi’   وحى   and ‘ilhaam’   اِلهَام   is that one ‘ilhaam’   اِلهَام   is applicable to the intellectual minded whereas ‘wahi’   وحى   is common. Secondly, ‘ilhaam’   اِلهَام   is associated with the notion of performing or not performing a particular task, whereas ‘wahi’   وحى   constitutes enormity and vastness.
Allah Taa’la says:
Surah Ash Shams (The Sun)   سُوۡرَةُ الشّمس
(91:8)
فَأَلۡهَمَهَا فُجُورَهَا وَتَقۡوَٮٰهَا
“And inspired it [with discernment of] its wickedness and its righteousness”
3.          Ilqaa   اِلقَاء  :   The lexical meaning is ‘to put’. ‘Alqaa aala’   ألقَى     عَلَى   means to educate.
In the Holy Quran,
Surah Al Qamar (The Moon)   سُوۡرَةُ القَمَر
(54:25)
أَءُلۡقِىَ ٱلذِّكۡرُ عَلَيۡهِ مِنۢ بَيۡنِنَا
“  Has the message been sent down upon him from among us?   Rather, he is an insolent liar."
‘Talaqa-ashaee min-hu’   تَلَقَى     الشَئ     مِنهُ   means to learn; to receive education.
Allah Taa’la says:
Surah Al Baqarah (The Cow)   سُوۡرَةُ البَقَرَة
(2:37)
فَتَلَقَّىٰٓ ءَادَمُ مِن رَّبِّهِۦ كَلِمَـٰتٍ۬
“  Then Adam received from his Lord [some] words  , and He accepted his repentance. Indeed, it is He who is the Accepting of repentance, the Merciful.”
As though ‘ilqaa’   اِلقَاء   is the guidance/intuition put in a person’s heart that relates to education and the services of teaching and learning. Like ‘wahi’   وحى   and ‘ilhaam’   اِلهَام  , ‘ilqaa’   اِلقَاء   can also come from Shaitaan.   شيطان
Allah Taa’la says:
Surah Al Haj (The Pilgrimage)   سُوۡرَةُ الحَجّ
(22:52)
فَيَنسَخُ ٱللَّهُ مَا يُلۡقِى ٱلشَّيۡطَـٰنُ
“And We did not send before you any messenger or prophet except that when he spoke [or recited], Satan threw into it [some misunderstanding].   But Allah abolishes that which Satan throws in;   then Allah makes precise His verses. And Allah is Knowing and Wise.”
4.          Waswaas   وَسوَاس  :    From a medical perspective, it is a disease that weakens the mind due to domination or control. As a result, a person starts talking about nonsense things frivolously that were previously not in their heart and neither do these thoughts spring any benefit or wellness for anyone. ‘Wiswaas’   وِسوَاس   refers to the disease of having doubts; unbeneficial or evil that drives its way into the heart. Shaitaan   شيطان  , or the act of Shaitaan   شيطان   to persuade to an evil deed or have evil thoughts set in a person’s heart. It also refers to the early stages of madness, as though ‘waswasa’   وسوسه   places itself in all categories of evil thoughts that may arise in one’s heart or is put in by Shaitaan   شيطان  ; and it is related only to Shaitaan   شيطان  .
Allah Taa’la says:
Surah An Nas (The Mankind)   سُوۡرَةُ النَّاس
(114:4-5)
مِن شَرِّ ٱلۡوَسۡوَاسِ ٱلۡخَنَّاسِ (  ﻿  ٤  ﻿  ) ٱلَّذِى يُوَسۡوِسُ فِى صُدُورِ ٱلنَّاسِ
“From the evil of the retreating whisperer - Who whispers [evil] into the breasts of mankind”
5.          Hamazaat   هَمَزَات  :   ‘Hamaza yadullu Aala Zaghtin-wa Asr-in’   هَمَزَ     يَدُلُّ     عَلَى     ضَغطٍ     وَّ     عَصرٍ   which means to pinch, press, or nip. It refers to the act of poking a sharp object, like a wooden stick, on the back or the hind legs of an animal so that it may run faster. In Punjabi, a common term for this is ‘Chohnbarh Dena’   چونہبڑ     دینا  . It basically means that the Shaitaan   شيطان   not only puts an evil thought in a heart but also provokes and stimulates desire to pursue it. ‘Hamazaat’   هَمَزَات   is also in relation with Shaitaan   شيطان  .
Allah Taa’la says:
Surah Muminun (The Believers)   سُوۡرَةُ المؤمنون
(23:97)
وَقُل رَّبِّ أَعُوذُ بِكَ مِنۡ هَمَزَٲتِ ٱلشَّيَـٰطِينِ
“And say, "My Lord, I seek refuge in You from the incitements of the devils,”
Conclusion:
(1)       Wahi   وحى  : Wahi   وحى  , Ilhaam   اِلهَام   and Ilqaa   اِلقَاء   can come from Allah Taa’la and Shaitaan   شيطان   as well; however waswasa   وَسوَسَه   and hamaz   هَمَزَ   are only in relation with Shaitaan   شيطان  .
(2)       Wahi   وحى   is related to learning, education, beliefs, rules, commands and the unseen. Ilhaam   اِلهَام   is only associated with the decision of performing or not performing a task. Ilqaa   اِلقَاء   is only related to education.
(3)       Waswasa   وَسوَسَه   : It only refers to the influx of evil thoughts in one’s heart, however hamaza   هَمَزَ  , other than the evil thought, also includes the element of persuasion from Shaitaan   شيطان  .
(4)       Every wahi   وحى  , ilhaam   اِلهَام   or ilqaa   اِلقَاء   that is in accordance with the Islamic law is a source of guidance, and if it is not, then it is sinister and coming from Shaitaan   شيطان  .
<<Alternate translation>>
دل میں بات ڈالنا – Inspiration in the heart
These wordsوحى  الهام  القاء وسواس  همزات          are in Quran
1.             وحى   – the lexical meaning is to conceal, and quick indication, and وحى ا means to indicate swiftly about some concealed hidden matter (MF, M L) , then there are  some different types of وحى , one is connected to matters which are directly controlled by Allah:
In Surah Fussilat: (41:12):
وَأَوْحَىٰ فِي كُلِّ سَمَاءٍ أَمْرَهَا
and inspired in each heaven its command.
Secondly the natural instinct is also called وحى, such as the child hastens towards the mother as soon as it is born,
In Surah An-Nahl: (16:68):
وَأَوْحَىٰ رَبُّكَ إِلَى النَّحْلِ
And your Lord inspired to the bee,
Therefore, the inspiration from Allah is to all inanimate objects, animate beings and mankind and this kind of inspiration can be to any, as well as a prophet.
In Surah  Qasas: (28:7):
وَأَوْحَيْنَا إِلَىٰ أُمِّ مُوسَىٰ أَنْ أَرْضِعِيهِ
And We inspired to the mother of Moses, "Suckle him;
In all the above examples the word    وحى has been used in the lexical meaning.  Therefore it can be said that one man can inspire another as:
In Surah Maryam: (19:11):
فَأَوْحَىٰ إِلَيْهِمْ أَن سَبِّحُوا بُكْرَةً وَعَشِيًّا
and signaled to them to exalt [ Allah ] in the morning and afternoon.
The same could be applied to devils inspiring one another:
In Surah An-Aam:   (6:121):
وَإِنَّ الشَّيَاطِينَ لَيُوحُونَ إِلَىٰ أَوْلِيَائِهِمْ لِيُجَادِلُوكُمْ
And indeed do the devils inspire their allies [among men] to dispute with you.
Therefore inspiration can be divine or satanic. Divine inspiration is always based on good, and the inspiration which is against the divine inspiration is satanic. In religious technical terms   وحى is the teachings, rulings and unseen news which Allah sends to his special servants (prophets) for the guidance of common people and its three types have been mentioned in the Quran:
a)             Puts it in the heart directly
b)            Sends his angel to his messenger
c)             Talks behind a screen ( like with prophet Musa)
Although the common way is through Angel Jibraeel Allah sends messages to his prophets which then flows from the Prophet’s mouth.
2.               الهام   – issue/matter which is put in to someone’s heart, by the Almighty or through the great angels (MF) and means to give understanding, comprehension, to give divine help (MJD) same as  وحى, الهام can also be satanic, especially when it cannot be confirmed by any ayah or religious statement, that’s why.  With the exception of Sufi scholars; according to all the scholars الهام  is not sufficient evidence or  proof (M.M). The differences between وحى and  الهام, a) الهام is only used for when referring to intelligent beings, ie mankind, whereas   وحىis can be used for a wider application.    B)    the connection of   الهام is usually referred to either completing an action or refraining from it, whereas وحى has a much wider application.
In Surah As-Shams:  (91:8):
فَأَلْهَمَهَا فُجُورَهَا وَتَقْوَاهَا
And inspired it [with discernment of] its wickedness and its righteousness,
3.                القاء  - lexical meaning to put/pour, and القى على  means to give education (M. M.).
In Surah Qamar: (54:25):
أَأُلْقِيَ الذِّكْرُ عَلَيْهِ مِن بَيْنِنَا
Has the message been sent down upon him from among us?
And تلقى الشئ منه means to learn, to gain knowledge (MJD)
In Surah Baqarah: (2:37):
فَتَلَقَّىٰ آدَمُ مِن رَّبِّهِ كَلِمَاتٍ
Then Adam received from his Lord [some] words
Therefore القاء  means only the thing which is put in the heart which is connected with education, learning and teaching. Both   الهام and وحى it can be satanic.

14. Dil Mein Baat Daalna دل میں بات ڈالنا (To Drop an Idea/Hint in the Heart)

Also known as ‘Wahi’ وَحىٌ, ‘Ilhaam’ اِلهَام, ‘Ilqaa’ اِلقَاء , ‘Waswaas’ وَسوَاس and ‘Hamazaat’ هَمَزَات in the Holy Quran.

1.      Wahi وَحىٌ: The lexical meaning is a strong sign. ‘Aohaa’ اَوحَى means to give a rapid sign about the unseen; hidden and unknown. There are many types of ‘Wahi’ وحى ; one of which deals with the inexpugnable and impregnable affairs.

Allah Taa’la says:

Surah Fussilat (Explained in Detail) سُوۡرَةُ فُصّلَت

(41:12)

 وَأَوۡحَىٰ فِى كُلِّ سَمَآءٍ أَمۡرَهَا‌ۚ

“And He completed them as seven heavens within two days and inspired in each heaven its command. And We adorned the nearest heaven with lamps and as protection. That is the determination of the Exalted in Might, the Knowing.”

In a different context, ‘wahi’ وحى has also been explained as an innate or natural guidance/intuition. For example, the instinct of a new born baby to dart towards the mother’s chest.

Allah Taa’la says:

Surah An Nahl (The Bee) سُوۡرَةُ النّحل

(12:68)

وَأَوۡحَىٰ رَبُّكَ إِلَى ٱلنَّحۡلِ

“And your Lord inspired to the bee, "Take for yourself among the mountains, houses, and among the trees and [in] that which they construct.”

As though the guidance and intuition (wahi) وحى from Allah Taa’la comes to all creatures; mankind, animals and insects. Such intuition can come towards a non prophet as well.

Allah Taa’la says:

Surah Al Qasas (The Stories) سُوۡرَةُ القَصَص

(28:7)

وَأَوۡحَيۡنَآ إِلَىٰٓ أُمِّ مُوسَىٰٓ أَنۡ أَرۡضِعِيهِ‌ۖ

“And We inspired to the mother of Moses, "Suckle him; but when you fear for him, cast him into the river and do not fear and do not grieve. Indeed, We will return him to you and will make him [one] of the messengers."

In all of the above examples, the meaning of ‘wahi’ وحى has been used in its lexical context. In a similar connotation, a person also does ‘wahi’ وحى to another person.

Allah Taa’la says:

Surah Maryam (Mary) سُوۡرَةُ مَریَم

(19:11)

 فَأَوۡحَىٰٓ إِلَيۡہِمۡ أَن سَبِّحُواْ بُكۡرَةً۬ وَعَشِيًّ۬ا

“So he came out to his people from the prayer chamber and signaled to them to exalt [ Allah ] in the morning and afternoon.”

Even Satan (shaitaan) شيطان does ‘wahi’ وحى amongst each other.

Allah Taa’la says:

Surah Al Anaam (The Cattle) سُوۡرَةُ الاٴنعَام

(6:121)

 وَإِنَّ ٱلشَّيَـٰطِينَ لَيُوحُونَ إِلَىٰٓ أَوۡلِيَآٮِٕهِمۡ لِيُجَـٰدِلُوكُمۡ‌ۖ

“And do not eat of that upon which the name of Allah has not been mentioned, for indeed, it is grave disobedience. And indeed do the devils inspire their allies [among men] to dispute with you. And if you were to obey them, indeed, you would be associators [of others with Him].”

Therefore, ‘wahi’ وحى can be a guidance, a blessing or even sinister. The ‘wahi’ وحى that is guidance is always based on wellness, and the ‘wahi’ وحى that goes against the guidance is definitely the sinister whisperings. In the Islamic term, ‘wahi’ وحى refers to such knowledge, wisdom and insights of the unseen that Allah Taa’la sends onto his beloved creation (prophet) for the guidance of the mankind. Three of such scenarios have been discussed in the Holy Quran. (1) Allah Taa’la directly puts in the heart. (2) Allah Taa’la sends an angel to his messenger. (3) Communicate behind a veil. (Case in point Musa aleh assalam). Henceforth, the commonly used scenario from these is Allah Taa’la sends the guidance, the ‘wahi’ وحى through his angel (Gabriel aleh assalam) to his prophets and messengers who then verbalize it.

Allah Taa’la says:

Surah Al Baqarah (the Cow) سُوۡرَةُ البَقَرَة

(2:97)

قُلۡ مَن كَانَ عَدُوًّ۬ا لِّجِبۡرِيلَ فَإِنَّهُ ۥ نَزَّلَهُ ۥ عَلَىٰ قَلۡبِكَ بِإِذۡنِ ٱللَّهِ

“Say, "Whoever is an enemy to Gabriel - it is [none but] he who has brought the Qur'an down upon your heart, [O Muhammad], by permission of Allah , confirming that which was before it and as guidance and good tidings for the believers."

2.      Ilhaam اِلهَام:  It refers to the intuition/guidance that is induced in the heart by Allah taa’la or a wise and knowledgeable person. To provide insight, understanding and strengthen encouragement. Similar to ‘wahi’ وحى, ‘ilhaam’ اِلهَام can also come from Shaitaan شيطان, especially when it cannot be validated through any ayah or Islamic text. This is why, apart from the Sufi class, none of the scholars consider ‘ilhaam’ اِلهَام as debatable for evidence. The difference between ‘wahi’ وحى and ‘ilhaam’ اِلهَام is that one ‘ilhaam’ اِلهَام is applicable to the intellectual minded whereas ‘wahi’ وحى is common. Secondly, ‘ilhaam’ اِلهَام is associated with the notion of performing or not performing a particular task, whereas ‘wahi’ وحى constitutes enormity and vastness.

Allah Taa’la says:

Surah Ash Shams (The Sun) سُوۡرَةُ الشّمس

(91:8)

فَأَلۡهَمَهَا فُجُورَهَا وَتَقۡوَٮٰهَا

“And inspired it [with discernment of] its wickedness and its righteousness”

 

3.      Ilqaa اِلقَاء: The lexical meaning is ‘to put’. ‘Alqaa aala’ ألقَى عَلَى means to educate.

In the Holy Quran,

Surah Al Qamar (The Moon) سُوۡرَةُ القَمَر

(54:25)

أَءُلۡقِىَ ٱلذِّكۡرُ عَلَيۡهِ مِنۢ بَيۡنِنَا

“Has the message been sent down upon him from among us? Rather, he is an insolent liar."

‘Talaqa-ashaee min-hu’ تَلَقَى الشَئ مِنهُ means to learn; to receive education.

Allah Taa’la says:

Surah Al Baqarah (The Cow) سُوۡرَةُ البَقَرَة

(2:37)

فَتَلَقَّىٰٓ ءَادَمُ مِن رَّبِّهِۦ كَلِمَـٰتٍ۬

“Then Adam received from his Lord [some] words, and He accepted his repentance. Indeed, it is He who is the Accepting of repentance, the Merciful.”

As though ‘ilqaa’ اِلقَاء is the guidance/intuition put in a person’s heart that relates to education and the services of teaching and learning. Like ‘wahi’ وحى and ‘ilhaam’ اِلهَام, ‘ilqaa’ اِلقَاء can also come from Shaitaan. شيطان

Allah Taa’la says:

Surah Al Haj (The Pilgrimage) سُوۡرَةُ الحَجّ

(22:52)

 فَيَنسَخُ ٱللَّهُ مَا يُلۡقِى ٱلشَّيۡطَـٰنُ

“And We did not send before you any messenger or prophet except that when he spoke [or recited], Satan threw into it [some misunderstanding]. But Allah abolishes that which Satan throws in; then Allah makes precise His verses. And Allah is Knowing and Wise.”

4.      Waswaas وَسوَاس:  From a medical perspective, it is a disease that weakens the mind due to domination or control. As a result, a person starts talking about nonsense things frivolously that were previously not in their heart and neither do these thoughts spring any benefit or wellness for anyone. ‘Wiswaas’ وِسوَاس refers to the disease of having doubts; unbeneficial or evil that drives its way into the heart. Shaitaan شيطان, or the act of Shaitaan شيطان to persuade to an evil deed or have evil thoughts set in a person’s heart. It also refers to the early stages of madness, as though ‘waswasa’ وسوسه places itself in all categories of evil thoughts that may arise in one’s heart or is put in by Shaitaan شيطان; and it is related only to Shaitaan شيطان.

Allah Taa’la says:

Surah An Nas (The Mankind) سُوۡرَةُ النَّاس

(114:4-5)

مِن شَرِّ ٱلۡوَسۡوَاسِ ٱلۡخَنَّاسِ (﻿٤﻿) ٱلَّذِى يُوَسۡوِسُ فِى صُدُورِ ٱلنَّاسِ

“From the evil of the retreating whisperer - Who whispers [evil] into the breasts of mankind”

 

5.      Hamazaat هَمَزَات: ‘Hamaza yadullu Aala Zaghtin-wa Asr-in’ هَمَزَ يَدُلُّ عَلَى ضَغطٍ وَّ عَصرٍ which means to pinch, press, or nip. It refers to the act of poking a sharp object, like a wooden stick, on the back or the hind legs of an animal so that it may run faster. In Punjabi, a common term for this is ‘Chohnbarh Dena’ چونہبڑ دینا. It basically means that the Shaitaan شيطان not only puts an evil thought in a heart but also provokes and stimulates desire to pursue it. ‘Hamazaat’ هَمَزَات is also in relation with Shaitaan شيطان.

Allah Taa’la says:

Surah Muminun (The Believers) سُوۡرَةُ المؤمنون

(23:97)

وَقُل رَّبِّ أَعُوذُ بِكَ مِنۡ هَمَزَٲتِ ٱلشَّيَـٰطِينِ

“And say, "My Lord, I seek refuge in You from the incitements of the devils,”

 

Conclusion:

(1)   Wahi وحى: Wahi وحى, Ilhaam اِلهَام and Ilqaa اِلقَاء can come from Allah Taa’la and Shaitaan شيطان as well; however waswasa وَسوَسَه and hamaz هَمَزَ are only in relation with Shaitaan شيطان.

(2)   Wahi وحى is related to learning, education, beliefs, rules, commands and the unseen. Ilhaam اِلهَام is only associated with the decision of performing or not performing a task. Ilqaa اِلقَاء is only related to education.

(3)   Waswasa وَسوَسَه : It only refers to the influx of evil thoughts in one’s heart, however hamaza هَمَزَ, other than the evil thought, also includes the element of persuasion from Shaitaan شيطان.

(4)   Every wahi وحى, ilhaam اِلهَام or ilqaa اِلقَاء that is in accordance with the Islamic law is a source of guidance, and if it is not, then it is sinister and coming from Shaitaan شيطان.
