15. Daleel دلیل (Evidence)
Also known as ‘daleel’   دَلِيل  , ‘hujjah’   حُجَّة  , ‘bayinnah’   بَيّنَة   (bayyin)   بيّن  , ‘burhaan’   بُرهَان   (burh wa burhn)   بره     و     برهن   and ‘sultaan’   سُلطَن   in the Holy Quran.
1.          Daleel   دَلِيل  :    ‘Dalalat’   دَلَالَت   and ‘daleel’   دَلِيل   mean such guidance through which cognition of something and knowledge is obtained. Just a person comprehends that a living being is alive through its movement or a scripted/written vocabulary provides evidence of its meaning. Even in a regular conversation, the context in which a vocabulary is used, are evident of its comprehension. ‘Dalla’   دَلَّ   means to express; to mention; to guide; to be a source of knowledge.
Allah Taa’la says:
Surah Al Furqan (The Criterian)   سُوۡرَةُ الفُرقان
(25:45)
أَلَمۡ تَرَ إِلَىٰ رَبِّكَ كَيۡفَ مَدَّ ٱلظِّلَّ وَلَوۡ شَآءَ لَجَعَلَهُ ۥ سَاكِنً۬ا ثُمَّ جَعَلۡنَا ٱلشَّمۡسَ عَلَيۡهِ دَلِيلاً۬
“Have you not considered your Lord - how He extends the shadow, and if He willed, He could have made it stationary? Then We made the sun for it an indication.”
As though the growing of the length of shadows, the setting of the sun and the proportionality between them are evidence over each other; and the ability to assess the precise direction of the sun by the shortening or lengthening of its shadows. A similar determination can be made with timings. Also, the length and direction of a shadow can be determined by observing the direction of the sun.
2.          Hujjah   حُجَّة  : ‘  Haajja’   حَاجَّ   means to argue and to turn out dominant in the argument. ‘Almahajaah’   المحاجة   is having every party reject the proposed argument of the other. ‘Hujjah’   حُجَّة   is an argument having a group of peoples agree unanimously on something, and after coming to a conclusion, one party provides evidence to another. This evidence is called ‘Hujjah’   حُجَّة  . For example, the disbelievers accepted the fact that their creator, master and sustainer is only Allah Taa’la so in relation to that Allah Taa’la says that why can supreme entity, that creates the human being from a drop by getting it through various processes and then brings it to death, not give birth to it again? Such an argument is called ‘Hujjah’.   حُجَّة
Allah Taa’la says:
Surah Al Anaam (The Cattle)   سُوۡرَةُ الاٴنعَام
(6:83)
وَتِلۡكَ حُجَّتُنَآ ءَاتَيۡنَـٰهَآ إِبۡرَٲهِيمَ عَلَىٰ قَوۡمِهِۦ‌ۚ
“  And     that was Our [conclusive] argument which We gave Abraham against his people  . We raise by degrees whom We will. Indeed, your Lord is Wise and Knowing.”
3.          Bayinnah   بَيّنَة  :   It refers to clear and obvious/open dialogue; proof. Some interpretation of ‘Bayinnah’   بَيّنَة   is also elicited through this hadeeth   حديث   of the Prophet (s.a.w). The Prophet (s.a.w) says: “Al-bayinnatu Aala-almudda-I wal-yameenu Aala-almuddaa Alaeh”   اَلبَيّنَةُ     عَلَى     المُدَّعِي     وَاليَميِنُ     عَلَى     المُدَّعَى     عَلَيهِ   (Bukhari). It means that it is the responsibility of the claimant to provide evidence and if he is not able to do so, then it is an adjuration on the defendant.
For example Zaid claims some money from Bakr to which Bakr denies. If Zaid carries a statement from Bakr proving Zaid’s claim or helps in proving Zaid’s claim then this statement is ‘Bayinnah’   بَيّنَة  . Similarly, if Zaid presents a witness to prove his case then it is also called ‘Bayinnah’   بَيّنَة  . ‘Bayinnah’   بَيّنَة   is any strong argument making the opposing party dominated or speechless. The existence of the Holy Quran is ‘Bayinnah’   بَيّنَة   itself, to that the disbelievers could not produce something similar even in a challenge. 15. Daleel دلیل (Evidence)

Also known as ‘daleel’ دَلِيل, ‘hujjah’ حُجَّة, ‘bayinnah’ بَيّنَة (bayyin) بيّن, ‘burhaan’ بُرهَان (burh wa burhn) بره و برهن and ‘sultaan’ سُلطَن in the Holy Quran.

1.      Daleel دَلِيل:  ‘Dalalat’ دَلَالَت and ‘daleel’ دَلِيل mean such guidance through which cognition of something and knowledge is obtained. Just a person comprehends that a living being is alive through its movement or a scripted/written vocabulary provides evidence of its meaning. Even in a regular conversation, the context in which a vocabulary is used, are evident of its comprehension. ‘Dalla’ دَلَّ means to express; to mention; to guide; to be a source of knowledge.

Allah Taa’la says:

“Have you not considered your Lord - how He extends the shadow, and if He willed, He could have made it stationary? Then We made the sun for it an indication.”

As though the growing of the length of shadows, the setting of the sun and the proportionality between them are evidence over each other; and the ability to assess the precise direction of the sun by the shortening or lengthening of its shadows. A similar determination can be made with timings. Also, the length and direction of a shadow can be determined by observing the direction of the sun.

2.      Hujjah حُجَّة: ‘Haajja’ حَاجَّ means to argue and to turn out dominant in the argument. ‘Almahajaah’ المحاجة is having every party reject the proposed argument of the other. ‘Hujjah’ حُجَّة is an argument having a group of peoples agree unanimously on something, and after coming to a conclusion, one party provides evidence to another. This evidence is called ‘Hujjah’ حُجَّة. For example, the disbelievers accepted the fact that their creator, master and sustainer is only Allah Taa’la so in relation to that Allah Taa’la says that why can supreme entity, that creates the human being from a drop by getting it through various processes and then brings it to death, not give birth to it again? Such an argument is called ‘Hujjah’. حُجَّة

World and its different names – 17:
Synonyms are:
1)        دُنْيَا
2)        اَدْنٰى
3)        عاجِلة
4)        اُوْلىٰ
1)dunyaa دُنْيَا   :from danna means sumthing  near. Or close. And this word means to be near according to the time period, location or position or in any other aspect. As per the Islamic beliefs life is for two times. one is the current life which is called as nasha al oolaa .and the second one is the life after death which is called nasaha al okhraa or saniaa and the current life as per the time period is the life near to us so that’s y it is called dunyaa and its antonym is aakhirat (after life/the end).and this word   دُنْيَا dunya   is usually used for the current life as in Quran Allah says:
أُولَٰئِكَ الَّذِينَ اشْتَرَوُا الْحَيَاةَ الدُّنْيَا بِالْآخِرَةِ
2:86 (surah 2 al baqarah,verse 86)
Translation: These are the people who buy the life of this world at the price of the Hereafter.
2)  adnaa اَدْنٰى  :other than the meaning of near as per the time it also portray the meaning of inferiority in position. and adnaa word can be also used in terms of arzaal(WORST)  and pitiful   Mufraddat - مفردات  . فَخَلَفَ مِن بَعْدِهِمْ خَلْفٌ وَرِثُوا الْكِتَابَ يَأْخُذُونَ عَرَضَ هَٰذَا الْأَدْنَىٰ
7:189 (surah al aaraaf 7 verse 189)
Translation: After them succeeded an (evil) generation: They inherited the Book, but they chose (for themselves) the vanities of this world.
3)aajilaah عاجِلة   :antonym is   akrah اَخرة    (hereafter  ). عِجْل iijaal   means quickly or hurriedly. And aajilah عَاجِلة means that comes in haste. it is current time, cash, world and the worldly things.
ALLAH says:
وَتَذَرُونَ الْآخِرَةَ كَلَّا بَلْ تُحِبُّونَ الْعَاجِلَةَ
75:20-21 (surah 75 al-qiyamah,verse 20-21)
Translation: Nay, (ye men!) but ye love the fleeting life, And leave alone the Hereafter.
4  )oolaa اُوْلىٰ  :it is the plural of awaal which means first. It means first or current life (and its opposite is akhraa and aakhiraat which means last or second life) ALLAH says in quran:
وَإِنَّ لَنَا لَلْآخِرَةَ وَالْأُولَىٰ
92:13 (surah 92 al layil verse 13)
Translation: And verily unto Us (belong) the End and the Beginning.

1  )baouda بَعُدَ   : means to be far. Use of this is general. And can be used for all kind of distance. Distance in location, time, and status. To travel or to go at a far place   Fiqhul lughat 11      ALLAH says in Quran:

34:19 (surah 34 saba verse 19)

2)  qassa  قَصَا  (from yaqsoo يَقْصُوَا):  it means getting far and can only be used as adverb of place. and it gives the meaning of  getting far from a specific place and resident of that place.   aqsal madenah اقصَى المدينة   means other brim/edge of the city(other corner of the city). Mosque of Aqsa(proper noun) means the mosque that is far.
ALLAH SAYS in quran:

19:22 (surah 19 maryum verse 22)
Translation: So she conceived him, and she retired with him to a remote place.
3)  naa نَاى   :means to get far.and   naiyaah نَائِيَة   means one who stays away   Maqaayeesul-lughat      and to reach near a far destination   Alfurooqul-lughwiyyah 11  .only used as adverb of time. And according to one phrase of imam raghib “to get away from sumone because of arrogance   Mufraddat – مفردات    .in Quran this word is used in two places and both of its  meanings are justified.
As Allah says in Quran:
وَإِذَا أَنْعَمْنَا عَلَى الْإِنسَانِ أَعْرَضَ وَنَأَىٰ بِجَانِبِهِ
17:83 (surah  17 al israa verse 83)
Translation: Yet when We bestow Our favours on man, he turns away and becomes remote on his side (instead of coming to Us).
And in another place:
وَهُمْ يَنْهَوْنَ عَنْهُ وَيَنْأَوْنَ عَنْهُ ۖ وَإِن يُهْلِكُونَ إِلَّا أَنفُسَهُمْ وَمَا يَشْعُرُونَ
6:26 (surah 6 anaam verse 26)
Translation: Others they keep away from it, and themselves they keep away; but they only destroy their own souls, and they perceive it not.
4)  kafara كفَّرَ  :from kaafaraa which means to hide.and   kufraah كُفرَة    means the darkness of night. and   kafaraah كفارَة   means an act after its performance will  cover up the sins  . And if kafara   كفَّرَ    is attributed to Allah then it means wiping away of sins. And kafara is related to bad deeds as ghafara (forgivness) is to  zanoob(sins).ALLAH SAYS
لَكَفَّرْنَا عَنْهُمْ سَيِّئَاتِهِمْ
5:65 (surah 5 al maidah verse 65)
Translation: We should indeed have blotted out their iniquities
5)  qaDaa  قَضٰى   :its dictionary definition is not to take away but if it is attributed to humans then it means to fulfill a responsibility :
Allah says
فَلَمَّا قَضَىٰ مُوسَى الْأَجَلَ
28:29 (surah 28 al qasas verse 29)
Translation: Now when Moses had fulfilled the term.
However in the following verse as per the Arabic idioms it means to take away. Because, it is also a part of accomplish the task.
ثُمَّ لْيَقْضُوا تَفَثَهُمْ وَلْيُوفُوا نُذُورَهُمْ
22:29 (surah 22 hajj verse 29)
Translation: Then let them end their untidiness and fulfill their vows.
Summary:
1)Bood:it’s a usual word can be used for all kinds of distance.
2)qassa:distance from a specific place citizens
3)naai:its adverb of time and it means to stay away from sum one out of arrogance.
4)kafara: Allah wiping away of sins due to good deeds.
5)qaDaa: after completing  a big task to do something as an additional task (appendage).

raw_text:
Guard:
The words used for guard in Arabic are (i) خَزَنَه and (ii) مُصِيطِر
(i) خَزَنَه
This is the plural of خَازن. It means the treasurer or trustee, or the one who is responsible for collecting money or property. This word is also used for angels who are assigned duties in the Hellfire.   Allah says in the Quran:
كُلَّمَا أُلْقِيَ فِيهَا فَوْجٌ سَأَلَهُمْ خَزَنَتُهَا أَلَمْ يَأْتِكُمْ نَذِيرٌ
Every time a group is cast therein, its keeper will ask: "Did no warner come to you?" (67:8)
(ii) مُصِيطِر
It is also spelled with a س so in Quran, a small س is written over this word to clarify that. Some mention the root as سطر and others mention the root of this word as سطِير.
سطِيرِ على means to overpower someone or become a guardian. سطِير is a custodian.
Allah says in the Quran:
فَذَكِّرْ إِنَّمَا أَنْتَ مُذَكِّرٌ لَسْتَ عَلَيْهِمْ بِمُصَيْطِرٍ
So remind them (O Muhammad (sallellahu alaihi wasallam)), you are only a one who reminds.You are not a dictator over them. (88:21-22)
Meaning that they are in no position to convince you of what they want.
Conclusion:
The same difference lies between خَازن and مُصِيطِر as it is in حفِيظ and رَقِيب.
خَازن is only a caretaker, while مُصِيطِر is a custodian and has responsibilities over the things he is taking care of.

Allah says in Quran
يَوْمَ يَخْرُجُونَ مِنَ الْأَجْدَاثِ سِرَاعًا
70:43 (surah 70 marij verse 43)
translation: The Day whereon they will issue from their sepulchres in sudden haste.

وَجَاءَ مِنْ أَقْصَى الْمَدِينَةِ رَجُلٌ يَسْعَىٰ
36:23 (surah 36 yaseen verse 23)

37:93-94 (surah 37 as safaat verse 93-94)
Translation : Then did he turn upon them, striking (them) with the right hand. Then came (the worshippers) with hurried steps, and faced (him).

Allah says in quran:
فَلَمَّا أَحَسُّوا بَأْسَنَا إِذَا هُم مِّنْهَا يَرْكُضُونَ
21:12 (surah 21 al anbiyaa verse 12)
Translation: Yet, when they felt Our Punishment (coming), behold, they (tried to) flee from it.

Allah says in quran:
لَوْ يَجِدُونَ مَلْجَأً أَوْ مَغَارَاتٍ أَوْ مُدَّخَلًا لَّوَلَّوْا إِلَيْهِ وَهُمْ يَجْمَحُونَ
9:57 (surah 9 at tawbaah verse 57)
Translation: If they could find a place to flee to, or caves, or a place of concealment, they would turn straightaway thereto, with an obstinate rush.
6)  haraa هَرَعَ   :to break forth. to run because of uncontrollable emotions. To run in Shivery manner.   Fiqhul lughat - فقه اللغة    33 To rush or run out of restlessness .to become restless because of rage ,enervation , terror or  cold and run   Miraatul Quraan – مراة القرا  .
Allah says in Quran:
وَجَاءَهُ قَوْمُهُ يُهْرَعُونَ إِلَيْهِ
11:78 (surah 11 hud verse 78)
Translation: And his people came rushing towards him.
7)   nasala   نَسَلَ:   to run from height  toward lowland. As per the author of munjid dictionary it also means to walk fast and plunk. And according to ibn al faris it means to generate one thing from other slowly  Maqaayeesul-lughat - مقائيس اللغة   But in the below verse this meaning cannot be applied.
حَتَّىٰ إِذَا فُتِحَتْ يَأْجُوجُ وَمَأْجُوجُ وَهُم مِّن كُلِّ حَدَبٍ يَنسِلُونَ
21:96 (surah 21 al anbiyaa verse 96)
Translation: Until the Gog and Magog (people) are let through (their barrier), and they swiftly swarm from every hill..

title: Hell and its different names
raw_text:
Hell and its different names
Synonyms are:
1)        النّار
2)        جَهنَّمَ
3)        جَحِيمَ
4)        سَقْر
5)        سَعير
1)annar النّار:   from the word nor. It means fire.its a common word.
When the word naar is preceded  by Al then it will become a proper noun and if this word has no other way to distinguish it than the meaning of   annar النّار   will be always hell.
Allah says:
إِنَّهُمْ صَالُو النَّارِ
38:59 (surah 38 saad verse 59)
Transaltion: they shall burn in the Fire.
2)  jahanum  جَهنَّمَ  : this word is arabicize from the farsi word jehnaam. Means place of penalties. House of punishment or penalties   Mufraddat - مفردات  .   People of lexicon puts it under the   root   of جہم(frown)
Allah says in quran:
جَهَنَّمَ يَصْلَوْنَهَا فَبِئْسَ الْمِهَادُ
38:56 (surah 38 saad verse 56)
Transaltion: Hell!- they will burn therein, - an evil bed (indeed, to lie on)!
3)  jaheem جَحِيمَ:jahama  جَحَمَ   means stare of lion and lion staring with sharp eyes. Jaham جحم means blazing fire and jaheem  جحيم  means fire that blaze sharply    Mufraddat - مفردات   and jaheem means  a sharply ignited fire in a pit. Very hot place
Allah says:
خُذُوهُ فَاعْتِلُوهُ إِلَىٰ سَوَاءِ الْجَحِيمِ
44:47 (surah 44 ad dukhaan verse 47)
Translation:A voice will cry: "Seize ye him and drag him into the midst of the Blazing Fire!
4)saqara سَقْر:   means sun scorching something and   asaqrah اَلسّقرَةُ   means very severe heat of sun. hot winds and   saqar سَقّر   means extremely hot temperature that can scorch the body.
Allah says:
وَمَا أَدْرَاكَ مَا سَقَرُ لَا تُبْقِي وَلَا تَذَرُ لَوَّاحَةٌ لِّلْبَشَرِ
74:27-29 (surah 74 al mudassir verse 27-29)
Transaltion: And what will explain to thee what Hell-Fire is. Naught doth it permit to endure, and naught doth it leave alone!- Darkening and changing the colour of man!
5)  saiieer  سَعير:   meaning to ignite fire and make it severe And because of this attribute hell is also called saieer means all the time blazing fire.
Allah says:
وَسَيَصْلَوْنَ سَعِيرًا
4:10 (surah 4 an nisa verse 10)
Translation: They will soon be enduring a Blazing Fire!
Some level of hells
1)ghaii غَيّ:   ghawaa  غوَىٰ  means to be lost and take a wrong way. this is the next level after   ضلال zalal.  and ghai is  to get astray because of own faults and ghai is also a level  or  valley of hell where misled people will be thrown.
Allah says:
فَخَلَفَ مِن بَعْدِهِمْ خَلْفٌ أَضَاعُوا الصَّلَاةَ وَاتَّبَعُوا الشَّهَوَاتِ ۖ فَسَوْفَ يَلْقَوْنَ غَيًّا
19:59 (surah 19 maryum verse 59)
Translation: But after them there followed a posterity who missed prayers and followed after lusts soon, then, will they face Destruction.
2)hawiaa هَاوِيَه:hawa هوَىٰ  and yahwii يَهْوِىْ   means to fall from a height at ground and   uhwiaa  اُهويَّة    is a deep well and   uhwiaah  اُهويَّة   s deep pit   Munjid - منجد     and hawiaah    هَاوِيَه:   ia a deep pit in hell.
Allah says:
فَأُمُّهُ هَاوِيَةٌ وَمَا أَدْرَاكَ مَا هِيَهْ نَارٌ حَامِيَةٌ
101:9-11 (surah  101 al qariyaah verse 9-11)
Translation: Will have his home in a (bottomless) Pit. And what will explain to thee what this is? (It is) a Fire Blazing fiercely!
3)hutamah الحُطَمَة  : حَطَمَ hatma means trample,to grind.and hatmah is a level in hell.
Allah says in quran:
وَمَا أَدْرَاكَ مَا الْحُطَمَةُ نَارُ اللَّهِ الْمُوقَدَةُ
104:5-6 (surah 104 al humaza verse 5-6)
Translation:   And what can make you know what is the Crusher? It is the fire of Allah, [eternally] fueled.

title: Angels of hell-23
raw_text:
Angels of hell-23
Synonyms are:
1)        خَزْنَة
2)        زبانية (زبن)
3)        مالك

title: Friend-24
raw_text:
Friend-24
Synonyms are:
1)        قَرِيْن
2)        رَفِيْق
3)        وَلِى (مَوَالِى)
4)        صَدِيْق (صِدِّيْق)
5)        خَلِيْل
6)        حَمِيْم
7)        وَلِيْجَة (ولج)
8)        بَطَانَة
9)        خُذُوْل
10)                            اَخْدَان  (خدن)
1)  qareen قَرِيْن:alqaran (الْقَرَن):  a rope through which two camels are tied. And alqaran   (الْقَرَن   ) means peer, opponent. Match in bravery or knowdlege     Munjid - منجد   this word can be applied for living things and non living things   Alfurooqul-lughwiyyah 235  . and   qiraan us sadiin قِرْاٰنُ السَّعْدَيْن   means,two saad stars accumulating in one zodiac. And as per the wordings of imam raghib, qareen Is that person who is same in age to other person or in bravery, power and in other qualities is equal to the other    Mufraddat - مفردات  . This word is usually used in negative sense
Allah says:
حَتَّىٰ إِذَا جَاءَنَا قَالَ يَا لَيْتَ بَيْنِي وَبَيْنَكَ بُعْدَ الْمَشْرِقَيْنِ فَبِئْسَ الْقَرِينُ
43:38  (surah 43 az zukhraf verse 38)
Translation: Until, when he comes to Us [at Judgement], he says [to his companion], "Oh, I wish there was between me and you the distance between the east and west - how wretched a companion."
2)  rafeeq رَفِيْق:arrifq اَلرِّفْق    means soft behavior. a kind way of treating and that thing from which one can take help.   Mirfaqah مِرْفَقَة   means small pillow/cushion    Munjid - منجد   and rafeeq means sympathetic companion. Soft hearted. One who is Compatible or one who stays near   Maqaayeesul-lughat  . And the antonym is    anaff عنف   and it means hardness/harshness  or stone-hearted   Maqaayeesul-lughat  .
Allah says:
فَأُولَٰئِكَ مَعَ الَّذِينَ أَنْعَمَ اللَّهُ عَلَيْهِم مِّنَ النَّبِيِّينَ وَالصِّدِّيقِينَ وَالشُّهَدَاءِ وَالصَّالِحِينَ ۚ وَحَسُنَ أُولَٰئِكَ رَفِيقًا
4:69 (surah 4 An Nisa verse 69)
Translation: those will be with the ones upon whom Allah has bestowed favor of the prophets, the steadfast affirmers of truth, the martyrs and the righteous. And excellent are those as companions.
3  )wali وَلِى:aLwlaa الولاء   means love, friendship, closeness and kinship   Mufraddat - مفردات   and affinity   Maqaayeesul-lughat  .
and   wali وَلِى   means helper, one who share sorrows, one who help at the times of ups and downs.
Allah says in quran:
اللَّهُ وَلِيُّ الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا يُخْرِجُهُم مِّنَ الظُّلُمَاتِ إِلَى النُّورِ
2:257 (surah 2 Al baqara verse 257)
Translation: Allah is the ally of those who believe. He brings them out from darknesses into the light
An alwalaa   لولاء   meaning custody (or sainthood) ,heirship of inheritance and   mawali مَوَالِى
(singular مَولى )   means the inheritor of legacy  .for more explanation check “inheritance”
Allah says
وَلِكُلٍّ جَعَلْنَا مَوَالِيَ مِمَّا تَرَكَ الْوَالِدَانِ وَالْأَقْرَبُونَ
4:33 (surah 4 An nisa verse 33)
Translation:   And for all, We have made heirs to what is left by parents and relatives
4)  Sadiiq صَدِيْق   :true and faithful friend. One who fulfill the ties of friendship. And   sadaqqat صداقت   means hearts to agree on friendship/amity.     Fiqhul lughat - فقه اللغة 98/236
Allah says in Quran:
وَلَا عَلَىٰ أَنفُسِكُمْ أَن تَأْكُلُوا مِن بُيُوتِكُمْ أَوْ بُيُوتِ آبَائِكُمْ أَوْ بُيُوتِ أُمَّهَاتِكُمْ أَوْ بُيُوتِ إِخْوَانِكُمْ أَوْ بُيُوتِ أَخَوَاتِكُمْ أَوْ بُيُوتِ أَعْمَامِكُمْ أَوْ بُيُوتِ عَمَّاتِكُمْ أَوْ بُيُوتِ أَخْوَالِكُمْ أَوْ بُيُوتِ خَالَاتِكُمْ أَوْ مَا مَلَكْتُم مَّفَاتِحَهُ أَوْ صَدِيقِكُمْ
24:61 (surah 24 An nor verse 61)
Translation: nor upon yourselves when you eat from your [own] houses or the houses of your fathers or the houses of your mothers or the houses of your brothers or the houses of your sisters or the houses of your father's brothers or the houses of your father's sisters or the houses of your mother's brothers or the houses of your mother's sisters or [from houses] whose keys you possess or [from the house] of your friend
And   sadeeq صِدِّيْق    It’s a superlative noun it means veracious or true friend.
Allah says:
يُوسُفُ أَيُّهَا الصِّدِّيقُ أَفْتِنَا فِي سَبْعِ بَقَرَاتٍ سِمَانٍ يَأْكُلُهُنَّ سَبْعٌ عِجَافٌ
12:46 (surah 12 yousaf verse 46)
Translation:   [He said], "Joseph, O man of truth, explain to us about seven fat cows eaten by seven [that were] lean.
5  )khaliil خَلِيْل   :khulah  خُلَّةَ  or khilal  خِلال  means heart piercing friendship(heart pervading friendship)     Mufraddat - مفردات  . strong and deep friendship and khaleel means  honest and true friend and its plural is  ikhlaa اَخِلَّاء.
Allah says:
وَاتَّخَذَ اللَّهُ إِبْرَاهِيمَ خَلِيلًا
4:124 (Surah 4 An nisa verse 124)
Tranlstion: And Allah took Abraham as an intimate friend.
6)  hameem حَمِيْم  :basically used for three things a) getting black/dark b)getting hot c)to be close    Maqaayeesul-lughat   and   hama  حمَّ   means  to make hot and ham   azahira حمَّ الظَّهِيْره    means very severe heat at afternoon   Munjid - منجد  . Zealous friend or a very close friend.
Allah says:
وَلَا يَسْأَلُ حَمِيمٌ حَمِيمًا يُبَصَّرُونَهُمْ
70:10-11 (surah 70 al mariaj verse 10-11)
Translation: And no friend will ask [anything of] a friend, They will be shown each other
7)  walijah وَلِيْجَة   :  walaja وَلَجَ    means to enter. A friend who act as a advisor for sumone matters. One who can be trusted /confidential /reliable. Or another meaning is a person who is attach to other nation also   Munjid - منجد  . Both the meanings are almost same.
Allah says:
وَلَمَّا يَعْلَمِ اللَّهُ الَّذِينَ جَاهَدُوا مِنكُمْ وَلَمْ يَتَّخِذُوا مِن دُونِ اللَّهِ وَلَا رَسُولِهِ وَلَا الْمُؤْمِنِينَ وَلِيجَةً
9:16 (surah 9 at tawbah verse 16)
Translation: while Allah has not yet made evident those among you who strive [for His cause] and do not take other than Allah, His Messenger and the believers as intimates?
8)  batanah بَطَانَة   :  batan بطن   means stomach and the inner part of anything. And   batanah بطانة     means secret. Lining under the cloth. a person’s family members relatives  and elites   Munjid - منجد  .. A friend with whom one can share secrets and a friend who is aware of personal matters   Mufraddat - مفردات
Allah says in Quran:
يَا أَيُّهَا الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا لَا تَتَّخِذُوا بِطَانَةً مِّن دُونِكُمْ لَا يَأْلُونَكُمْ خَبَالًا
3:118 (surah 3 Al imraan verse 118)
Translation: O you who have believed, do not take as intimates those other than yourselves, for they will not spare you [any] ruin.
9)  khuzool خُذُوْل  :khazal خَذَل means to not help someone and to leave the partnership. And khuzool   خُذُوْل   is a type of friend who verbally sings praises of friendship but at the  time of need they leave the friends  Munjid - منجد  ..  One who betrays.
Allah says in Quran:
وَكَانَ الشَّيْطَانُ لِلْإِنسَانِ خَذُولًا
25:29 (surah 25 al furqaan verse 29)
Translation: And ever is Satan, to man, a deserter.
10)  akdaan اَخْدَان   :is the plural of khdaan خدن  or khdnaah خدنة   and it means  person who have lots of friends or fellowship, philanderer,mate   ,  intimate friend, adulterer/lewd one who hides his friendship and one who wants to fulfill his sexual desires. Used for both masculine and feminine
Allah says:
مُحْصَنَاتٍ غَيْرَ مُسَافِحَاتٍ وَلَا مُتَّخِذَاتِ أَخْدَانٍ
4:25 (surah  4 An nisa verse 25)
Transaltion: They should be] chaste, neither [of] those who commit unlawful intercourse randomly nor those who take [secret] lovers.
Summary:
1)qareen:peer and same in status and same in age.
2)rafeeq: sympathetic and soft hearted friend
3)sadiqq:the one who fulfill the ties of friendship ,compatible with heart. sadiiq honest friend or the one who fulfill the ties of friendship.
4)wali:helper and the one who share sorrows and defender . mawali the one who is close relative and the inheritor of legacy.
5)khaliil :true and honest friend .whom one  love heartedly.
6)hameem:the one who shows warmth.
7)walijah: advisor, confidential/trustworthy.
8)batanah: with whom one can share secrets. Confidant
9)khuzool:one who betrays at the time of need.
10)akhdaan: intimate friend ,bad friend, or lewd friend.

مُحْصَنَاتٍ غَيْرَ مُسَافِحَاتٍ وَلَا مُتَّخِذَاتِ أَخْدَانٍ

4:25 (surah  4 An nisa verse 25)

Transaltion: They should be] chaste, neither [of] those who commit unlawful intercourse randomly nor those who take [secret] lovers.

Summary:

 

1)qareen:peer and same in status and same in age.

2)rafeeq: sympathetic and soft hearted friend

3)sadiqq:the one who fulfill the ties of friendship ,compatible with heart. sadiiq honest friend or the one who fulfill the ties of friendship.

4)wali:helper and the one who share sorrows and defender . mawali the one who is close relative and the inheritor of legacy.

5)khaliil :true and honest friend .whom one  love heartedly.

6)hameem:the one who shows warmth.

7)walijah: advisor, confidential/trustworthy.

8)batanah: with whom one can share secrets. Confidant

9)khuzool:one who betrays at the time of need.

10)akhdaan: intimate friend ,bad friend, or lewd friend.

25.  DHUTKARA HUA [drive out, revile, reprove]
Synonyms: RAJEEM, DUHOOR, MADHOOR, KHASI
25.1 RAJEEM     (رَجِيْم  ): Rajam ( رَجَم) means to throw stones and Rajeem means cursed, damned. Allah called shaitan in Holy Quran:
Surat An-Naĥl (The Bee) -  النحل سورة
16:98
فَإِذَا قَرَأْتَ الْقُرْآنَ فَاسْتَعِذْ بِاللَّهِ مِنَ الشَّيْطَانِ الرَّجِيمِ
So when you want to recite the Quran, seek refuge with Allah from   Shaitan (Satan), the outcast (the cursed one).
25.2 DUHOOR (دُحُوْر)   : The word Dahara (دَحَرَ) means to reprove; to drive out (force someone to leave). In Quran:
Surat Aş-Şāffāt (Those who set the Ranks) - الصافات سورة
37:9
دُحُورًا ۖ وَلَهُمْ عَذَابٌ وَاصِبٌ
Outcast  , and theirs is a constant (or painful) torment.
Surat Al-'A`rāf (The Heights) - الأعراف سورة
7:18
قَالَ اخْرُجْ مِنْهَا مَذْءُومًا مَّدْحُورًا
(Allah) said (to Iblis) "Get out from this (Paradise)   disgraced and expelled.
25.3 KHASAA (خَسَاَ)   means to revile a dog or a pig. In other words, to reprove someone because he is observed to be contemptible and despicable. Allah says in the Quran:
Surat Al-Mu'minūn (The Believers) - المؤمنون سورة
23:108
قَالَ اخْسَئُوا فِيهَا وَلَا تُكَلِّمُونِ
He will say, "  Remain despised therein   and do not speak to Me.
Summary:
25.1 RAJEEM: cursed
25.2 DUHOOR: to reprove or to drive out
25.3 KHASAA: to reprove someone because he is observed to be contemptible and despicable

raw_text:
26. DHUNDLANA/DHUNDLA NAZAR AANA [blurry, faded, vague]
Synonyms: INKADARA, ABYAZZA, ‘AMAA, GHUMMA
26.1 INKADARA (اِنْكَدَرَ):   Kadarun (كَدَرٌ) means dingy,muddy [opposite of Saffaun (صَفَاءٌ)]. Kudratun (كُدْرَةٌ) means the state of being not bright,vivid, or shining for a colour. Allah says in the Quran:
Surat At-Takwīr (The Overthrowing) - التكوير سورة
81:2
وَإِذَا النُّجُومُ انكَدَرَتْ
When the stars fall,   losing their luster
26.2 ABYAZZA (اَبْيَضَّ)   means whiten - make or become white [opposite of Sawad (سَوَاد) meaning blackness]. Biyaz-ul-‘ain (العين بياض) means eyes becoming white. Ibyazzat Aiyaanuhu (عَيْنُهُ اِبَيَضَّت) means his eyes turned white or he lost his sight as in Quran:
Surat Yūsuf (Joseph) - يوسف  سورة
12:84
وَابْيَضَّتْ عَيْنَاهُ مِنَ الْحُزْنِ فَهُوَ كَظِيمٌ
And he turned away from them and said, "Oh, my sorrow over Joseph," and   his eyes became white from grief  , for he was [of that] a suppressor.
26.3 ‘AMMA (عَمَّى)     : ‘Amia  (عَمِىَ) means blindness - state of being blind and ‘Amiyatil akhbaru an fulaanin  (فُلَانٍ عَنْ عَمِيَتِالْاَخْبَارُ) means the person is lost somewhere and no one knows his location. ‘Amal m’anaa (الْمَعْنٰى عَمَّى is to make vague; to hide. Allah says in the Quran:
Surat Fuşşilat (Explained in Detail) - فصلت سورة
41:44
وَالَّذِينَ لَا يُؤْمِنُونَ فِي آذَانِهِمْ وَقْرٌ وَهُوَ عَلَيْهِمْ عَمًى
And those who do not believe - in their ears is deafness,   and it is upon them blindness  .
26.4 GHUMMA (غُمَّةً)   : To hide something and ghummaa (غُمّٰى) means darkness and dusty. Ghamam (غمام)  means clouds that cover the sunlight of the sun. Ghummatal amr (الْاَمْر غُمَّ)ةَ means complex or obscure matter. Allah says:
Surat Yūnus (Jonah) - يونس سورة
10:71
فَأَجْمِعُوا أَمْرَكُمْ وَشُرَكَاءَكُمْ ثُمَّ لَا يَكُنْ أَمْرُكُمْ عَلَيْكُمْ غُمَّةً ثُمَّ اقْضُوا إِلَيَّ وَلَا تُنظِرُونِ
So resolve upon your plan and [call upon] your associates.   Then let not your plan be obscure to you  . Then carry it out upon me and do not give me respite.
Summary:
26.1 INKADARA: Fading of the color
26.2 AMAL AMAR: Vague or hidden matter
26.3 ABAYAZZA ‘AINUHU: Eyes becoming white
26.4 GHUMMATUL AMR: complex or obscure matter

raw_text:
27. DHUAAN [smoke, copper, coal]
Synonyms: DUKHAAN, NUHAAS, YAHMOOM
27.1 DUKHAAN (دُخَان )  : Smoke. Imam Raghib says it is the smoke from flames of fire.
Surat Fuşşilat (Explained in Detail) - فصلت سورة
41:11
ثُمَّ اسْتَوَىٰ إِلَى السَّمَاءِ وَهِيَ دُخَانٌ
Then He directed Himself to the heaven while it was   smoke
27.2 NUHAAS  ( نُحَاس )    means copper. Also, copper colored fire i.e. smoke wrapped with copper colored fire flames; extremely hot and red smoke. Allah says in the quran:
Surat Ar-Raĥmān (The Beneficent) - الرحمن سورة
55:25
يُرْسَلُ عَلَيْكُمَا شُوَاظٌ مِّن نَّارٍ وَنُحَاسٌ فَلَا تَنتَصِرَانِ
There will be sent upon you   a flame of fire and smoke  , and you will not defend yourselves.
27.3 YAHMOOM (يَحْمُوْم )     Hamma ( حَمَّ ) means to be extremely black. Humma ( حُمَّة )  means coal; ashes and anything burnt from fire. Yahmoom  (يَحْمُوْم ) is the smoke which is hot, black and contaminated.
Allah says in the Quran:
Surat Al-Wāqi`ah (The Inevitable) - الواقعة  سورة
56:43
وَظِلٍّ مِّن يَحْمُومٍ
And a shade of black smoke
Summary:
27.1 DUKHAAN: Smoke
27.2 NUHAAS: Red smoke emerging from copper colored fire
27.3 YAHMOOM: Contaminated black smoke

title: content/d/d28.html
raw_text:
28. DHOOP [sun, heat, hotness]
Synonyms: SHAMS, ZUHAA, HARRA, HAROOR
28.1 SHAMS (شَمْس)   : Sun and also sunlight. Shamsa Yoomuna  (يُوْمَنَا شَمْسَ) means to be sunny (day) and Shammasa means (شَمَّسَ) means to expose to the sun. Shams is used for the sunlight (any time of the day), but it is usually used to signify excessive heat of the sun.
Allah says in the Quran:
Surat Al-'Insān (The Man) -  الانسان سورة
76:13
لَا يَرَوْنَ فِيهَا شَمْسًا وَلَا زَمْهَرِيرًا
Reclining therein on raised thrones, they will see there neither   the excessive heat of the sun
28.2 ZUHAA (ضُحٰى):   Forenoon. It is also used to refer to the sun at the time of Chaasht .
Allah says in the Quran:
Surat An-Nāzi`āt (Those who drag forth) -  النازعات سورة
79:29
وَأَغْطَشَ لَيْلَهَا وَأَخْرَجَ ضُحَاهَا
Its night He covers with darkness,   and its forenoon   He brings out (with light)
28.3 HARRA (حَرَّ)   : Harra and Hararat ( حَرَارَت ) means to be hot, heat. Since the temperature of the sun and sunlight determines the hotness of the atmosphere, so harra is also used to refer sun at the time of noon and hot weather. In Quran:
Surat At-Tawbah (The Repentance) - التوبة سورة
وَقَالُوا لَا تَنفِرُوا فِي الْحَرِّ ۗ
And said, 'Do not go forth in the   heat.
28.4 HAROOR (حَرُوْر ):   to be hot [opposite of zalla ( ظَلّ ) meaning shade]. Extreme heat due to the hot rays of the sun.
Allah says in the Quran:
Surat Fāţir (Originator) -  فاطر سورة
35:20-21
وَلَا الظُّلُمَاتُ وَلَا النُّورُ     وَلَا الظِّلُّ وَلَا الْحَرُورُ
Nor are the darknesses and the light,   Nor are the shade and the heat
Summary:
28.1 SHAMS: Common word used for sun
28.2 ZUHAA: Forenoon
28.3 HARRA: Hotness at the time of noon
28.4 HAROOR: Extreme heat due to the hot rays of the sun

title: content/d/d29.html
raw_text:
29. DHOKA DENA [deceive, betray, cheat]
Synonyms: GHARRA, KHADA’AA, KHAANA, KHAZALA, RAAGHA, KHATARA
29.1 GHARRA (غَرَّ ):   To mislead somebody by the expectation of gaining something. To deceive (with vain hopes); to delude. Ghuroor (رغُرُوْ) and الغرور متاع means Abatil ad duniya (الدنيا اباطيل). Ghuroor means to deceive and deceiving person is called gharoor. Gharoor is also used for any delusion causing pain to a person.
Allah says in Quran:
Surat Al-Ĥadīd (The Iron)  الحديد- سورة
57:14
وَغَرَّتْكُمُ الْأَمَانِيُّ حَتَّىٰ جَاءَ أَمْرُ اللَّهِ وَغَرَّكُم بِاللَّهِ الْغَرُورُ
And wishful thinking deluded you until there came the command of Allah . And the   Deceiver deceived you   concerning Allah .
29.2 KHADA’AA  (خَدَعَ)     : Trick or cheat a person by hiding the truth. To cause someone to believe something that is false; alter or fake a report, etc to appear more favourable. To defraud, swindle, double-cross, rook. Tareek al khud’uh (الخدوع طريق) is a way that appears to visible at times and invisible at varying times. Prophet Muhammad (saw) said “خُدْعَةٌ اَلْحَرْبُ”. Khud’ah here does not mean to deceive or cheat but it is referring to war tactic here. For example: arranging the army in such a way that the quantity appears to be greater than the actual one or shattering of the army so that the enemy can be captured. Such tactics can be used to outwit the enemy. It would not be reckoned as deceitfulness if the intention is good and clear. Allah says in the Quran:
Surat Al-Baqarah (The Cow) -  البقرة سورة
2:9
يُخَادِعُونَ اللَّهَ وَالَّذِينَ آمَنُوا وَمَا يَخْدَعُونَ إِلَّا أَنفُسَهُمْ وَمَا يَشْعُرُونَ
They [think to] deceive Allah and those who believe, but they   deceive   not except themselves and perceive [it] not.
29.3 KHANA (خَانَ)   : Be disloyal or faithless to. Used in particular with subjects like ahad (promises), amanat (loyalty) or nifaaq. Khawwan  (خَوَّان) is a person who is very treacherous or disloyal. Allah says in the Quran:
Surat Al-'Anfāl (The Spoils of War) -  الأنفال سورة
8:58
وَإِمَّا تَخَافَنَّ مِن قَوْمٍ خِيَانَةً فَانبِذْ إِلَيْهِمْ عَلَىٰ سَوَاءٍ ۚ إِنَّ اللَّهَ لَا يُحِبُّ الْخَائِنِينَ
If you [have reason to] fear from a people betrayal, throw [their treaty] back to them, [putting you] on equal terms. Indeed,   Allah does not like the treacherous
29.4 KHAZALA  (خَذَلَ)   : To fail someone (or your friend) when most needed; abandon.
29.5 RAAGHA ILAA (اِلٰى رَاغَ)   :To turn to someone secretly. Raagha 3laa (عَلٰى رَاغَ) means ambuscade . Rawagh (رَوَاغ) means to swindle or plot conspiracy. Rawwagh  (رَوَّاغ) means swindler. Fox is also called rawwagh. Raawaghahuu (رَاوَغَهُ)  - clever trick or pitfall; counterfeit. According to Imam Raghib, it means to turn towards something (with a scheme behind). 37:91

29. DHOKA DENA [deceive, betray, cheat]

Synonyms: GHARRA, KHADA’AA, KHAANA, KHAZALA, RAAGHA, KHATARA

 

29.1 GHARRA (غَرَّ ): To mislead somebody by the expectation of gaining something. To deceive (with vain hopes); to delude. Ghuroor (رغُرُوْ) and الغرور متاع means Abatil ad duniya (الدنيا اباطيل). Ghuroor means to deceive and deceiving person is called gharoor. Gharoor is also used for any delusion causing pain to a person.

Allah says in Quran:

 

Surat Al-Ĥadīd (The Iron)  الحديد- سورة

57:14

وَغَرَّتْكُمُ الْأَمَانِيُّ حَتَّىٰ جَاءَ أَمْرُ اللَّهِ وَغَرَّكُم بِاللَّهِ الْغَرُورُ

And wishful thinking deluded you until there came the command of Allah . And the Deceiver deceived you concerning Allah .

 

29.2 KHADA’AA  (خَدَعَ)   : Trick or cheat a person by hiding the truth. To cause someone to believe something that is false; alter or fake a report, etc to appear more favourable. To defraud, swindle, double-cross, rook. Tareek al khud’uh (الخدوع طريق) is a way that appears to visible at times and invisible at varying times. Prophet Muhammad (saw) said “خُدْعَةٌ اَلْحَرْبُ”. Khud’ah here does not mean to deceive or cheat but it is referring to war tactic here. For example: arranging the army in such a way that the quantity appears to be greater than the actual one or shattering of the army so that the enemy can be captured. Such tactics can be used to outwit the enemy. It would not be reckoned as deceitfulness if the intention is good and clear. Allah says in the Quran:

2:9

يُخَادِعُونَ اللَّهَ وَالَّذِينَ آمَنُوا وَمَا يَخْدَعُونَ إِلَّا أَنفُسَهُمْ وَمَا يَشْعُرُونَ

They [think to] deceive Allah and those who believe, but they deceive not except themselves and perceive [it] not.

If you [have reason to] fear from a people betrayal, throw [their treaty] back to them, [putting you] on equal terms. Indeed, Allah does not like the treacherous

raw_text:
Branding
The words used for branding are (i) وَسَمَ, (ii) كوَى and (iii) شِيَة
(i) وَسَمَ
It means branding on the skin (M.F.) or tattooing, making a mole (M.L.). Dyeing. وسَام and وسمَه are the tools used in branding or dyeing (M.Q.). Allah says in the Quran:
سَنَسِمُهُ عَلَى الْخُرْطُومِ
We shall brand him over the nose! (68:16)
(ii) كَوَى يَكوِِي:
This is the term used for branding with hot iron or any other metal in such a way that the skin is burnt. كَاوِيَة is the tool used. Allah says in the Quran:
يَوْمَ يُحْمَىٰ عَلَيْهَا فِي نَارِ جَهَنَّمَ فَتُكْوَىٰ بِهَا جِبَاهُهُمْ وَجُنُوبُهُمْ وَظُهُورُهُمْ
On the Day when that (  Al-Kanz  : money, gold and silver, etc., the   Zakat   of which has not been paid) will be heated in the Fire of Hell and with it will be branded their foreheads, their flanks, and their backs (9:35)
(iii) شِيَة
وَشَيتُ الشَيُّ وشيََاً meaning to put another contrasting colour on a thing besides its original colour. وَشِيَة or شِيَة mean such a discoloration or branding which is different from that of the colour of the body (M.F.). Allah says in the Quran:
مُسَلَّمَةٌ لَا شِيَةَ فِيهَا
sound, having no other colour except bright yellow. (2:71)
Conclusion:
(i) وَسَمَ: tattooing
(ii) كوَى: branding the skin with a hot metal
(iii) شِيَة: a discolouration different from the colour of the entire body

Ra`ayta, “dekhna”, P.505
Synonyms: RAAA(RAY),NAZARA,BASARA,BASURA,AANASA,ZARA
all these are function of heart meaning they relate not only to eye but also to heart and mind
another catergory of words that refer to the conditon of the act of seeing that are used in the quran are
SHAKHASA(شَخَصَ),LAMAHA(لَمَحَ),HATA3A (هَطَعَ),
EASHAA(عَشَا),AGHMADA(اغْمَضَ),ZAGHA(� �َاغَ)
BARAQA(بَرَقَ)
1 RAAA(رَاَي)RO-YA(رءي):  to be aware of something,to see ,whether by means of eyes or contemplating or pondering or intelligence or wisdom or doubt or imagination .  it is of general usage.
whether awake or dream and meaning last glance,
Quran example(     with eyes  ):Surat Yūsuf (Joseph)[12:4]
إِنِّي   رَأَيْتُ   أَحَدَ عَشَرَ كَوْكَبًا
indeed I have   seen   [in a dream] eleven stars
Quran example(  by pondering  ,):Surat Al-Mā`ūn (The Small Kindesses)[107:1]
أَرَأَيْتَ     الَّذِي يُكَذِّبُ بِالدِّين
Have you   seen   the one who denies the Recompense?
2 NAZARA(نَظَرَ):  to glance,,to seek whether that thing is found or not .  it is also used in both sense i.e by eyes or by pondering
Quran example:Surat At-Tawbah (The Repentance)[9:127]
وَإِذَا مَا أُنزِلَتْ سُورَةٌ     نَّظَرَ   بَعْضُهُمْ إِلَىٰ بَعْضٍ
And whenever a surah is revealed, they   look   at each other
Quran example:
Surat An-Naml (The Ant)[27:33]
فَانظُرِي     مَاذَا تَأْمُرِينَ
so   see   (result of) what you will command
generally it is used to see with eyes
3 BASARA(بَصَرَ)     ,  BASURA(بَصُرَ):BASARA is used for sight and insight. it is rarely used for seeing with eyes
Quran example:
Surat Al-'A`rāf (The Heights)[7:198]
ۖ وَتَرَاهُمْ يَنظُرُونَ إِلَيْكَ وَهُمْ لَا     يُبْصِرُونَ
and you see them looking at you while they do not   see  .
In this ayah RA-YA,NAZARA and BASARA all three synonyms are used.This ayah also clarified the difference between them RA-YA=  imagine,  NAZARA=  see with eyes,  BASARA=  insight
BASURA is more specific/peculiar than BASARA
Quran example:
Surat Ţāhā (Ta-Ha)[20:96]
قَالَ     بَصُرْتُ   بِمَا لَمْ يَبْصُرُوا بِهِ
He said, "I   saw   what they did not see,
here 'saw' something which he figures out but not others.
4 AANASA(اَنَسَ):it means neither see by eyes or insight,but it means   to be acquainted or to know something from its signs  .  perceived
Quran example:
Surat Ţāhā (Ta-Ha)[20:10]
فَقَالَ لِأَهْلِهِ امْكُثُوا إِنِّي   آنَسْتُ   نَارًا
said to his family, "Stay here; indeed, I have   perceived   a fire
Quran example:
Surat An-Nisā' (The Women)[4:6]
فَإِنْ   آنَسْتُم   مِّنْهُمْ رُشْدًا
Then if you   perceive   in them sound judgement
5     ZAR(زَارَ):ZARAH(زَارَه) meaning   to visit someone,and visit to see or meet something,pilgrimage  .ZAWR( زَوْر)meaning   upper part of chest ZAWRT FULANA   means   i put my chest in front of him or i decide for his chest
Quran example:
Surat At-Takāthur (The Rivalry in world increase)[102:1-2]
أَلْهَاكُمُ التَّكَاثُرُ
Competition in [worldly] increase diverts you
حَتَّىٰ   زُرْتُمُ   الْمَقَابِرَ
Until you   visit   the graveyards
Summary:
1 RAAA(RAY):to ponder on a matter
2 NAZARA:generally used for looking
3 BASARA,BASURA:insight
4 AANASA:see, meaning find out.found
5 ZAR: to go for pilgrimage,to visit to see something

Quran example:

وَاقْتَرَبَ الْوَعْدُ الْحَقُّ فَإِذَا هِيَ   شَاخِصَةٌ   أَبْصَارُ الَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا
nd [when] the true promise has approached; then suddenly the eyes of those who disbelieved will be   staring   [in horror]

Surat An-Naĥl (The Bee)[16:77]
ۚ وَمَا أَمْرُ السَّاعَةِ إِلَّا     كَلَمْحِ   الْبَصَرِ أَوْ هُوَ أَقْرَبُ
And the command for the Hour is not but as a   glance   of the eye or even nearer

Surat 'Ibrāhīm (Abrahim)[14:43]
مُهْطِعِينَ مُقْنِعِي رُءُوسِهِمْ لَا يَرْتَدُّ إِلَيْهِمْ طَرْفُهُمْ ۖ
Racing ahead, their heads raised up, their glance does not come back to them,

3ASHI(عشي يعشي عشيَّا عشاوة)meaning invisble at night
3SHWA(عِشوة)meaning blaze that is visible afar at night

وَمَن     يَعْشُ   عَن ذِكْرِ الرَّحْمَٰنِ نُقَيِّضْ لَهُ شَيْطَانًا فَهُوَ لَهُ قَرِينٌ
And whoever is     blinded   from remembrance of the Most Merciful - We appoint for him a devil, and he is to him a companion.

1 SHAKHASA(شَخَصَ):meaning eyes become motionless,to lose ability to see,to stop blinking,

Quran example:

nd [when] the true promise has approached; then suddenly the eyes of those who disbelieved will be staring [in horror]

Racing ahead, their heads raised up, their glance does not come back to them,

وَمَن يَعْشُ عَن ذِكْرِ الرَّحْمَٰنِ نُقَيِّضْ لَهُ شَيْطَانًا فَهُوَ لَهُ قَرِينٌ

DIKHLANA(to make other see)
Synonyms:AARA,REYA,BASSARA,TABBARAJA
1 AARA(اَرَي):from baab(افعال) meaning   to make others see.  this word is used for physical as well conceptual connotation
Surat Al-'Aĥqāf (The Wind-Curved Sandhills)[46:4]
أَرُونِي   مَاذَا خَلَقُوا مِنَ الْأَرْضِ
Show me   what they have created of the earth
Surat An-Nisā' (The Women)[4:105]
لِتَحْكُمَ بَيْنَ النَّاسِ بِمَا   أَرَاكَ   اللَّهُ ۚ
so you may judge between the people by that which Allah has   shown you
(here (     أَرَاكَ  ) means GOD gifted wisdom as well as hidden Revelation).and (اَرَي يُرَاء) from baab (تفاعل) meaning to "  make each other see something"
Surat An-Nisā' (The Women)[4:142]
وَإِذَا قَامُوا إِلَى الصَّلَاةِ قَامُوا كُسَالَىٰ   يُرَاءُونَ   النَّاسَ وَلَا يَذْكُرُونَ اللَّهَ إِلَّا قَلِيلًا
And when they stand for prayer, they stand lazily,   showing   [themselves to] the people and not remembering Allah except a little,
and RIYA-(رِيَاء) meaning to   show off,to exhibit,to do something which is meant to show off
Surat An-Nisā' (The Women)[4:38]
وَالَّذِينَ يُنفِقُونَ أَمْوَالَهُمْ   رِئَاءَ   النَّاسِ
And [also] those who spend of their wealth   to be seen   by the people
2 BASSARA(بَصَّرَ):meaning   to show to others such that what is shown is become known and understood  .to get
acquainted with the conditions and signs of
Surat Al-Ma`ārij (The Ascending Stairways)[70:10-11]
لَا يَسْأَلُ حَمِيمٌ حَمِيمًا   يُبَصَّرُونَهُمْ   ۚ
no friend will ask [anything of] a friend,     They will be shown each other  .
3 TABBARAJA  (تَبَرَّجَ):     BARAJA(بَرَجَ) meaning   to be high,to rise,to be visible.BURJ(بُرج)   is a famous word and TABARJAT AL MIRAH(تَبرجت المراة) meaning   women showing off their beauty and ornament
Surat Al-'Aĥzāb (The Combined Forces)[33:22]
وَقَرْنَ فِي بُيُوتِكُنَّ وَلَا     تَبَرَّجْنَ تَبَرُّجَ   الْجَاهِلِيَّةِ الْأُولَىٰ
And abide in your houses and do not   display yourselves as [was] the display   of the former times of ignorance
Summary
1 AARA:just to make others see
2 BASSARA  : to make other seen such that it will be
known
3 TABBARAJA  :to show off beauty and ornament

raw_text:
33 – Religion
The words دِين, شَرِيعَة and مِلَّة have been used in the Quran
33.1 DEEN (دِين):   this term holds numerous meanings; four of these will be outlined here.  (1) It refers to the whole and complete sovereignty of Allah, (2) the complete enslavement and obedience /devotion of humans, (3) the law of recompense (reward and punishment) and (4) the power of enforcement of the law of recompense.  The term can come in one meaning or more than one, for example
39:3
Surat Az-Zumar (The Troops) - الزمر سورة
أَلَا لِلَّهِ ٱلدِّينُ ٱلۡخَالِصُ‌ (﻿٣﻿)
Unquestionably, for Allah is the pure religion (3)
In this verse, the term holds the essence of all four of the above meanings.  دِين requires that Allah ordains some things for humans and forbids certain things and who ever fails to obey His commands is then recompensed accordingly.  The commands that have been enjoined from Adam (peace be upon him) to the prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) are the real religion.  For example associating partners with the Almighty, stealing, fornication, indecency, etc have always been prohibited while the certainty of the accounting that will take place in the hereafter, etc.  The submission to these commands is called Islam.
Surat 'Āli `Imrān (Family of Imran) - عمران آل سورة
3:19
إِنَّ ٱلدِّينَ عِندَ ٱللَّهِ ٱلۡإِسۡلَـٰمُ‌ۗ (﻿١٩﻿)
Indeed, the religion in the sight of Allah is Islam (19)
33.2 SHARI’AH (شَرِيعَة):   linguistically شَرَعَ refers to specify a clear path.  شَرِيعَة refers to the commands that change according to the time and surrounding conditions.  For example, during the time of Adam (peace be upon him), the marriage of blood siblings was not prohibited, but such a bond was prohibited later on.  Prophet Yaqoob (Jacob, peace be upon him) was married to two blood sisters, this was also forbidden later on.  Similarly, during these times, prostrating to someone other than God because of their greatness was allowed but it was forbidden in the commands that came later on.  Likewise, earlier nations were not allowed anything from war booty while for the Muslims it is lawful to take from it.  The difference between شَرِيعَة and دِين is clarified by the Prophet (peace be upon him) in the following narration:
(متفق عليه) وَاحِدٌ وَدِينُهُم شَتّىٰ اُمَّهَاتُهُم العَلَّاتِ اِخوَةُ اَلاَنبِياءُ
“The prophets are brothers (brothers which have the same father and different mothers), their mothers are different (referring to the شَرِيعَة) while their religion (دِين) is one. (Bukhari & Muslim)
In the Quran, Allah (the exalted) states:
Surat Ash-Shūraá (The Consultation) - الشورى سورة
42:13
شَرَعَ لَكُم مِّنَ ٱلدِّينِ (﻿١٣﻿)
He has ordained for you of religion (13)
33.3 MILLAH (مِلَّة):   Everything that is included in دِين and شَرِيعَة is revealed by Allah.  Along with conveying these commands, the prophet is the first to abide by them.  Gradually, an assembly of followers emerges who also abide by these commands and thus the Islamic society/system forms.  This system/society is called a مِلَّة.  مِلَّة does not refer to the commands but to the system where the prophet is the leader, the followers follow the prophet and the way of life is based on the دِين and شَرِيعَة.  It is compulsory for the followers to obey the leader.  مِلَّة is often translated as ‘religion’ while the religion of all the prophets is the same.  مِلَّة is used to point towards a special prophet.  For example:
Surat 'Āli `Imrān (Family of Imran) - عمران آل سورة
3:95
فَٱتَّبِعُواْ مِلَّةَ إِبۡرَٲهِيمَ حَنِيفً۬ا (﻿٩٥﻿)
So follow the religion of Abraham, inclining toward truth (95)
Summary:
1.          دِين: the commands of Allah that have been the same from Adam (peace be upon him) to Muhammad (peace be upon him) and their obedience
2.          شَرِيعَة: the commands of Allah that change according to the time and conditions
3.          مِلَّة: the system that a prophet, in obedience with the commands of God, establishes amongst his followers

34 – To Give
The words اٰتٰى, اَعطٰى (عطو), اَدَاء (ادو ادى), دِيَة, , اَثَاب (ثوب), وَهَبَ, رَفَدَ, , اِلٰى دَفَعَ, هَدِيَّة and نَحَلَ have been used in the holy Quran
34.1 ATAA (اٰتٰى):   to give; to give something to someone.  Used in common language.
Surat Al-Baqarah (The Cow) - البقرة سورة
2:177
وَءَاتَى ٱلۡمَالَ عَلَىٰ حُبِّهِۦ (﻿١٧٧﻿)
And gives wealth, in spite of love for it (177)
34.2 A’ATAA (اَعطٰى):   used in two meanings: (1) to give something to someone as a favor or to forgive.
Surat Ţāhā (Ta-Ha) - طه سورة
20:50
قَالَ رَبُّنَا ٱلَّذِىٓ أَعۡطَىٰ كُلَّ شَىۡءٍ خَلۡقَهُ ۥ ثُمَّ هَدَىٰ (﻿٥٠﻿)
He said, "Our Lord is He who gave each thing its form and then guided [it]." (50)
(2) اَعطٰى can also mean to obey, to serve.  Thus giving someone more than what one owes them for their obedience and services is also اَعطٰى.  To gift, to reward because of satisfaction with hard work or services are also considered اَعطٰى.
Surat Hūd (Hud) - هود سورة
11:108
وَأَمَّا ٱلَّذِينَ سُعِدُواْ فَفِى ٱلۡجَنَّةِ خَـٰلِدِينَ فِيہَا مَا دَامَتِ ٱلسَّمَـٰوَٲتُ وَٱلۡأَرۡضُ إِلَّا مَا شَآءَ رَبُّكَ‌ۖ عَطَآءً غَيۡرَ مَجۡذُوذٍ۬ (﻿١٠٨﻿)
And as for those who were [destined to be] prosperous, they will be in Paradise, abiding therein as long as the heavens and the earth endure, except what your Lord should will - a bestowal uninterrupted (108).
34.3 ADAA (اَدَاء):   to give someone what is rightfully theirs and to give it all at once.  This term is usually used in situations where one is giving or taking such as in loans, trusts, etc.
Surat Al-Baqarah (The Cow) - البقرة سورة
2:283
فَإِنۡ أَمِنَ بَعۡضُكُم بَعۡضً۬ا فَلۡيُؤَدِّ ٱلَّذِى ٱؤۡتُمِنَ أَمَـٰنَتَهُ ۥ (﻿٢٨٣﻿)
And if one of you entrusts another, then let him who is entrusted discharge his trust [faithfully] (283)
34.4 DIYAH (دِيَة): (ودى) ودٰى – يدى – دِيَةٌ   this term is specifically used for giving blood money; the giving of money in compensation for life.
Surat An-Nisā' (The Women) - النساء سورة
4:92
فَدِيَةٌ۬ مُّسَلَّمَةٌ إِلَىٰٓ أَهۡلِهِۦ (﻿٩٢﻿)
Then a compensation payment presented to his family (92)
34.5 ATHAAB (اَثَاب):   comes for the payment of anything, whether paying back for a good thing or a bad.  Usually used for the reward of good works.  Like اَعطٰى, it includes the meaning of giving what is due or a bit extra.
Surat Al-Mā'idah (The Table Spread) - المائدة سورة
5:85
فَأَثَـٰبَهُمُ ٱللَّهُ بِمَا قَالُواْ جَنَّـٰتٍ۬ تَجۡرِى مِن تَحۡتِهَا ٱلۡأَنۡهَـٰرُ (﻿٨٥﻿)
So Allah rewarded them for what they said with gardens [in Paradise] beneath which rivers flow (85)
34.6 WAHABA (وَهَبَ):   To grant/bestow/endow (without having received any services and without the expectation of getting anything in return).
Surat Ash-Shūraá (The Consultation) - الشورى سورة
42:49
يَہَبُ لِمَن يَشَآءُ إِنَـٰثً۬ا وَيَهَبُ لِمَن يَشَآءُ ٱلذُّكُورَ (﻿٤٩﻿)
He gives to whom He wills female [children], and He gives to whom He wills males (49)
34.7 RADAFA (رَفَدَ):    to bestow and/or to assist.  The term includes two fundamental things: to give to someone needy and poor and to give or allocate a stipend/benefit.  رفاده refers to the fund that the Quraish had created for needy pilgrims.  اَرفَدَ refers to allocating a benefit so that he/she can take from a set amount.  رفد refers to a stipend; assistance.
Surat Hūd (Hud) - هود سورة
11:99

Then if you perceive in them sound judgement, release their property to them (6)

34. Giving - Dena -   (  دينا  )
Synonyms:-
Ata (اٰتٰی), Aata (اَعْطَى), Ada (اَدَاء), Deyatun (دِيَة), Asaaba (اَثَاب), Wahaba (وَهَبَ), Rafada (رَفَدَ), DafaAa (Ila) ((اِلٰی) دَفَعَ), Hadeyyat (هَدِيِّة), Nahala (نَحَلَ)
34.1. Ata (اٰتٰی):   To give someone something.
Quranic Example:-
“…and   gives   wealth, in spite of love for it…” (2:177)
34.2. Aata (اَعْطَى):   Two meanings.
1). To give someone something as a favor to them. To something bestow upon someone   (Mufraddat).
Quranic Example:-
“He said, “Our Lord is He who *gave* each thing its form and then guided
[it].”” (20:50)
2). To be loyal to someone and to serve them   (Munjid)  . And therefore it
also means to give someone a reward greater than their service or hard work.
Quranic Example:-
“And as for those who were [destined to be] prosperous, they will be in
Paradise, abiding therein as long as the heavens and the earth endure,
except what your Lord should will – a   bestowal   uninterrupted.” (11:108)
34.3. Ada (اَدَاء):   To give someone their due right in full. This word is usually used in “give & take” situations such as with a deposit, loan or a tribute.
Quranic Example:-
“And if one of you   entrusts   another, then let him who is entrusted
discharge his trust [faithfully] and let him fear Allah, his Lord.” (2:283)
34.4. Deyatun (دِيَة):   Used to mean blood money but specifically
payment/ransom for someone who was unintentionally killed.
Quranic Example:-
“And whoever kills a believer by mistake – then the freeing of a believing
slave and a   compensation payment   presented to the deceased’s family [is required] unless they give [up their right as] charity.” (4:92)
34.5. Asaaba (اَثَابَ):   A reward or return for any sort of act good or bad, although usually it is used for a return for good acts. Also this word contains some characteristics of 34.1.Aata (اَعْطَى) i.e. to give the return equal to or more than what the act deserves.
Quranic Example:-
“So Allah *rewarded* them for what they said with gardens [in Paradise]
beneath which rivers flow, wherein they abide eternally.” (5:85)
34.6. Wahaba (وَهَبَ):  To give someone something not as a return and
without anything done by them to deserve it, and without any expectation of
receiving anything in return for it.
Quranic Example:-
“He gives to whom He wills female [children], and He   gives   to whom He wills males.” (42:49)
34.7. Rafada (رَفَدَ):   Its meaning is based on two things; ‘to give’ and ‘to help’. It could mean like to give the poor something as a donation, or, the giving of or appointing of allowance to someone. Rafadah (رفادہ)
is the name of that fund that the Quraish used to keep for those hopeful for performing Pilgrimage (hajj) but were too impoverished to do so. And
Arfada (اَرْفَدَ) means to establish an amount of donation for someone
such that they keep taking their desired amount from that appointed amount (Mufraddat). And Rafd (رفد) means donation.
Quranic Example:-
“And they were followed in this [world] with a curse and on the Day of
Resurrection. And wretched is the   gift   which is given.” (11:99)
34.8. DafaAa (Ila) ((اِلٰی) دَفَعَ):   DafaAa (دَفَعَ) means that for the protection of something keeping any external dangers and attacks away (Mufraddat).  And when it is used with Ila (اِلٰی) then that means to hand over someone their possession.
Quranic Example:-
“And test the orphans [in their abilities] until they reach marriageable
age. Then if you perceive in them sound judgement,   release   their property
to them.” (4:6)
34.9. Hadeyyat (هَدِيِّة):   These are those gifts we give each other as a welcome or upon the pleasure of meeting them. And Mehda (مِهْدٰى) is the thing in which this gift is put in to give.
Quranic Example:-
“But what Allah has given me is better than what He has given you. Rather,
it is you who rejoice in your gift.” (27:36)
34.10. Nahala (نَحَلَ):   To give someone something. Nehal Almira (نَحَلَ الْمِرْاة) is giving a bride her promissory gift from her in-laws at the time of marriage. And Nahal (نَحل) is compensation (Munjid). Therefore, Al'nahlat (الْنَّحْلَة) and Al'nihlat (الْنِّحْلَة) are both used for a compensation that is given without the hopes of getting something in return – that is the meaning of Tabran (تَبرعاً).Therefore, both the words are associated with Hiba (ہبہ) which is a gift. And any kind of Hiba or gift can be called Nihlat (نِحْلَة), but any kind of Nihlat cannot be called Hiba, because all compensations are not gifts but, all gifts are compensations, without demanding something in return.
Quranic Example:-
“And give the women [upon marriage] their [bridal]   gifts   graciously. (4:4)
Summary:-
Ata (اٰتٰی):  To give. Used commonly.
Aata (اَعْطَى): A reward for a service or hard work given greater that
what it deserves.
Ada (اَدَاءٌ): To give someone their due right in full.
Deyat (دِيَة): Payment of blood money.
Asaaba (اَثَابَ): Similar to Aata (اَعْطَى). To give a return for a
work more than what it deserves.
Wahab (وَهب): To give something not as a return or reward and without
expectation of receiving a return for it.
Rafada (رَفَدَ): To help the poor or destitute by giving them a donation.
DafaAa (Ila) ((اِلٰی) دَفَعَ): To hand over someone their possession.
Hadeyyat (هَدِيَّة): Those gifts we give each other as a welcome or upon
the pleasure of meeting them.
Nehlatan (نِحْلَةَ): A compensation given without hopes of getting
something in return.

34.1 ATAA (اٰتٰى): to give; to give something to someone.  Used in common language.

 

Surat Al-Baqarah (The Cow) - البقرة سورة

 2:177

وَءَاتَى ٱلۡمَالَ عَلَىٰ حُبِّهِۦ (﻿١٧٧﻿)

And gives wealth, in spite of love for it (177)

 

34.2 A’ATAA (اَعطٰى): used in two meanings: (1) to give something to someone as a favor or to forgive.

 20:50

 قَالَ رَبُّنَا ٱلَّذِىٓ أَعۡطَىٰ كُلَّ شَىۡءٍ خَلۡقَهُ ۥ ثُمَّ هَدَىٰ (﻿٥٠﻿)

He said, "Our Lord is He who gave each thing its form and then guided [it]." (50)

 

(2) اَعطٰى can also mean to obey, to serve.  Thus giving someone more than what one owes them for their obedience and services is also اَعطٰى.  To gift, to reward because of satisfaction with hard work or services are also considered اَعطٰى.

 

Surat Hūd (Hud) - هود سورة

 11:108

 وَأَمَّا ٱلَّذِينَ سُعِدُواْ فَفِى ٱلۡجَنَّةِ خَـٰلِدِينَ فِيہَا مَا دَامَتِ ٱلسَّمَـٰوَٲتُ وَٱلۡأَرۡضُ إِلَّا مَا شَآءَ رَبُّكَ‌ۖ عَطَآءً غَيۡرَ مَجۡذُوذٍ۬ (﻿١٠٨﻿)

And as for those who were [destined to be] prosperous, they will be in Paradise, abiding therein as long as the heavens and the earth endure, except what your Lord should will - a bestowal uninterrupted (108).  

 

34.3 ADAA (اَدَاء): to give someone what is rightfully theirs and to give it all at once.  This term is usually used in situations where one is giving or taking such as in loans, trusts, etc.

 

Surat Al-Baqarah (The Cow) - البقرة سورة

2:283

 فَإِنۡ أَمِنَ بَعۡضُكُم بَعۡضً۬ا فَلۡيُؤَدِّ ٱلَّذِى ٱؤۡتُمِنَ أَمَـٰنَتَهُ ۥ (﻿٢٨٣﻿)

And if one of you entrusts another, then let him who is entrusted discharge his trust [faithfully] (283)

 

34.4 DIYAH (دِيَة): (ودى) ودٰى – يدى – دِيَةٌ this term is specifically used for giving blood money; the giving of money in compensation for life.

 

Surat An-Nisā' (The Women) - النساء سورة

4:92

 فَدِيَةٌ۬ مُّسَلَّمَةٌ إِلَىٰٓ أَهۡلِهِۦ (﻿٩٢﻿)

Then a compensation payment presented to his family (92)

 

34.5 ATHAAB (اَثَاب): comes for the payment of anything, whether paying back for a good thing or a bad.  Usually used for the reward of good works.  Like اَعطٰى, it includes the meaning of giving what is due or a bit extra.

 

Surat Al-Mā'idah (The Table Spread) - المائدة سورة

5:85

 فَأَثَـٰبَهُمُ ٱللَّهُ بِمَا قَالُواْ جَنَّـٰتٍ۬ تَجۡرِى مِن تَحۡتِهَا ٱلۡأَنۡهَـٰرُ (﻿٨٥﻿)

So Allah rewarded them for what they said with gardens [in Paradise] beneath which rivers flow (85)

 

34.6 WAHABA (وَهَبَ): To grant/bestow/endow (without having received any services and without the expectation of getting anything in return).

 

Surat Ash-Shūraá (The Consultation) - الشورى سورة

42:49

يَہَبُ لِمَن يَشَآءُ إِنَـٰثً۬ا وَيَهَبُ لِمَن يَشَآءُ ٱلذُّكُورَ (﻿٤٩﻿)

35 – Wall
The words جِدَار, سَدّ, رَدم, سُور and بُنيان have been used in the holy Quran
35.1 JIDAAR (جِدَار):   [plural جُدُر and جُدران] refers to one of the walls of a house or a fort.  جَدَرَ means to fall from the walls.  According to Ibn Al-Faaris it includes الحاءط هو – the walls of a covered building.
Surat Al-Kahf (The Cave) - الكهف سورة
18:82
وَأَمَّا ٱلۡجِدَارُ فَكَانَ لِغُلَـٰمَيۡنِ يَتِيمَيۡنِ فِى ٱلۡمَدِينَةِ (﻿٨٢﻿)
And as for the wall, it belonged to two orphan boys in the city (82)
35.2 SADD (سَدّ): سدّ   means a barrier, a stop, an enormous wall between two things that works as a barrier and is purposely constructed.   If this wall or barrier is natural, it is called سُدّ.  سَدَّ means to stop a crack (or opening) using a rock.  سِدَاد refers to the cement used to fill a crack or hole.  سُدَّة is used by medical specialists to describe the blockage created by unwanted materials in the intestines.
Surat Al-Kahf (The Cave) - الكهف سورة
18:94
فَهَلۡ نَجۡعَلُ لَكَ خَرۡجًا عَلَىٰٓ أَن تَجۡعَلَ بَيۡنَنَا وَبَيۡنَهُمۡ سَدًّ۬ا (﻿٩٤﻿)
“So may we assign for you an expenditure that you might make between us and them a barrier?" (94)
35.3 RADM (رَدم):   this term is more specific than سَدّ, it refers to a wall or barrier whose cracks and holes are securely covered; a thick wall; a fortified barrier.  رَدَمَ refers to close/fill a crack or hole.  الثوب ردم refers to patch a garment.
Surat Al-Kahf (The Cave) - الكهف سورة
18:95
فَأَعِينُونِى بِقُوَّةٍ أَجۡعَلۡ بَيۡنَكُمۡ وَبَيۡنَہُمۡ رَدۡمًا (﻿٩٥﻿)
But assist me with strength; I will make between you and them a dam (95)
35.4 SOOR (سُور):    according to Ibn Al-Faaris, it refers to وارتفاع علو على يدل – a wall so high that it is impossible enter by crossing or jump over it.  This wall is not of a house but a firewall of a fort or fence/covering.  المدينة سُورَةُ refers to ‘the city of refuge/shelter’.
Surat Al-Ĥadīd (The Iron) - الحديد سورة
57: 13
فَضُرِبَ بَيۡنَہُم بِسُورٍ۬ لَّهُ ۥ بَابُۢ (﻿١٣﻿)
And a wall will be placed between them with a door (13)
35.5 BUNYAAN   (بُنيان):  بَنٰى means to build; any construction that is built in such a way that all of its parts are fixed into each other.  بُنيان refers to every such construction which fulfills this requirement whether it is just the foundation, just a wall or the whole building.
Surat Aş-Şaf (The Ranks) - الصف سورة
61:4
إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ يُحِبُّ ٱلَّذِينَ يُقَـٰتِلُونَ فِى سَبِيلِهِۦ صَفًّ۬ا كَأَنَّهُم بُنۡيَـٰنٌ۬ مَّرۡصُوصٌ۬ (﻿٤﻿)
Indeed, Allah loves those who fight in His cause in a row as though they are a [single] structure joined firmly (4)
Summary:
1.          جِدَار: the wall of a house or fence.
2.          سَدّ: the wall in between two things which works as a barrier
3.          رَدم: a سَدّ whose holes and cracks are carefully filled
4.          سُور: a firewall so high that it cannot be jumped over
5.          بُنيان: a wall or construction whose parts are firmly fixed to each other

36- lunatic, insanity   (DEWANA--DEWANA PAN):-  Page 514
Synonyms:- MAJANONUN (مَجْنُوْنٌ ), KHABT (خَبْط), MAFTOON (مَفْتُوْن), SUOR (سُعُر).
36.1 MAJNONUN (مَجْنُوْنٌ ):   JANNA (جَنَّ) means to spread over something and cover it. senselessness/insensate (in referance to MUNJID). and MAJNUN (مَجْنُوْن ) is a person who is becoming unmindful and insensible. Arabs used the word MAJNUN because they had a view that, Jin enters in a human and makes him crazy. In this way its meaning would be, a man who has been driven crazy by a jin.
Allah SWT states in Qur'an:-
Surat Adh-Dhāriyāt (The Winnowing Winds) - سورة الذاريات
[51:52]
كَذَٰلِكَ مَا أَتَى الَّذِينَ مِن قَبْلِهِم مِّن رَّسُولٍ إِلَّا قَالُوا سَاحِرٌ أَوْ مَجْنُونٌ
Similarly, there came not to those before them any messenger except that they said, "A magician or a madman."
Page 514
and JINNAT (جِنَّة) means jin, it also means madness, In Qur'an,
Surat Al-Mu'minūn (The Believers) - سورة المؤمنون
[23:25]
إِنْ هُوَ إِلَّا رَجُلٌ بِهِ جِنَّةٌ
He is not but a man possessed with madness.
36.2 KHABATA (خَبَطَ)   means to make a man lose his senses by battering (In referance to MAF). And MAKHBUT (مخبوط) means apathetic mind. One whose mind does not work properly. According to Arabs this condition is also related to jin and satans.
Allah SWT states in Qur'an:-
Surat Al-Baqarah (The Cow) - سورة البقرة
[2:275]
الَّذِينَ يَأْكُلُونَ الرِّبَا لَا يَقُومُونَ إِلَّا كَمَا يَقُومُ الَّذِي يَتَخَبَّطُهُ الشَّيْطَانُ مِنَ الْمَسِّ
Those who consume interest cannot stand [on the Day of Resurrection] except as one stands who is being beaten by Satan into insanity.
The difference between KHABAT (خبط) and MAJNUN (جنون) is that, KHABAT is a temporary disease and MAJNUN is a long term permenant disease.
36.3 MAFTOON (مَفْتُوْن):   FATANA (فَطَنَ) to instigate. To fill with adoration, to incline and to amaze. MAFTOON (مفتون ) means mad or insane (in referance to MUNJID). and MAFTOON (مفتون ) refers to such a person who has become apathetic and lost his senses because of tribulations of life.
Allah SWT states in Qur'an,
Surat Al-Qalam (The Pen) - سورة القلم
[68:5-6]
فَسَتُبْصِرُ وَيُبْصِرُونَ
بِأَييِّكُمُ الْمَفْتُونُ
So you will see and they will see
Which of you is the afflicted [by a devil]  .
36.4 SUOR (سُعُر):   SA ARA (سَعَرَ) means blazing of fire and outburst of flame. Often this word is metaphorically used for getting or causing anger.
AS TAR ALSAWS (استعر اللصوص) means robbers have been instigated. AS TAR ALHARB (استعر الحرب) means fight has been boosted. MISAR (مِسْعَرْ) is a log which is used to instensify a fire (in referance to MAF). And SUOR (سُعُر) means madness in which a man easily gets angry over small issues and starts doing wrong things and his intellect does not work well.In Qur'an,
Surat Al-Qamar (The Moon) - سورة القمر
[54:24]
فَقَالُوا أَبَشَرًا مِّنَّا وَاحِدًا نَّتَّبِعُهُ إِنَّا إِذًا لَّفِي ضَلَالٍ وَسُعُرٍ
And said, "Is it one human being among us that we should follow? Indeed, we would then be in error and madness.
Summary:-
1) MAJNUN(مَجْنُوْنٌ ): means mad, crazy. Possesed by jin.
2) KHABATA(خَبَطَ): tepidity of mind and occurance of flaws in it(temporary)
3) MAFTOON(مَفْتُوْن): Madness caused by tribulations of life.
4) SUOR(سُعُر): tepidity produced due to instant lost of temprement .

4.   DUBLA   [Slim, lean]
Synonyms: EJAAF (عِجَاف), ZAAMIR/DAAMIR ( ضَامِر)
4.1   EJAAF   (عِجَاف) (plural of   AEJAF  (اِعْجفْ) )   AAJAFA   (عَجَفَ), to stop eating even when apetite is not fully satisfied. ( Arabic lexicon, meem qaaf),   EJAF   (اعجف) means to reduce fats and get slim.(Arabic lexicon, meem-laam). Therefore,   AEJAF   ( اِعْجفْ ) refers to an animal who has become weak and emaciated due to the shortage of food.
It is stated in Qur'an:-
Surat Yūsuf (Joseph) - سورة يوسف
[12:43]
وَقَالَ الْمَلِكُ إِنِّي أَرَىٰ سَبْعَ بَقَرَاتٍ سِمَانٍ يَأْكُلُهُنَّ سَبْعٌ عِجَافٌ
And [subsequently] the king said, "Indeed, I have seen [in a dream] seven fat cows being eaten by seven [that were] lean  .
4.2   DAMIR/ZAMIR   (ضَامِر) : (  DAMAR   ضمر)   AL-DAMAR   (الاضمار) means horse racing ground, horse training areas and boundries of horse racing ground. The time duration of horse training (In referance to MUNJAD).   DAMIR/ZAMIR   (ضَامِر) refers to such an animals whose body beomes thin and slender due to excessive training and exersice and practice, not due to the lack of food. swift paced,as well as agile so that it can win the competetion. In Arab the word   DEMER/ZEMER   (ضِامِر) is usually used for camels, either male or female.
Allah SWT states in Qur'an:-
Surat Al-Ĥaj (The Pilgrimage) - سورة الحج
[22:27]
وَأَذِّن فِي النَّاسِ بِالْحَجِّ يَأْتُوكَ رِجَالًا وَعَلَىٰ كُلِّ ضَامِرٍ يَأْتِينَ مِن كُلِّ فَجٍّ عَمِيقٍ
And proclaim to the people the Hajj [pilgrimage]; they will come to you on foot and on every lean camel; they will come from every distant pass.
Conclusion:- (1) AJAF(  اعْجف  ):   Thin animal because of food scarcity  . DAMIR/ZAMIR   (  ضَامِر  ) selender and thin animal due to exercising and     training.

5  DARAZ HONA---- KERNA   [EXTENSION----TO EXTEND]
Synonyms: TAALA and TAWAL, MADD and MADAAD, BA ADA.
5.1 TAALA (  طَالَ  ) (TAULAN     طَوْلاً  )   means to increase in length.   TAUL (    طُوْل  )   meaning increase in length/height (Antonym: Broad/wide),   ATAAL (  اَطَال  )   to increase the length.
It is stated in Qur'an:-
Surat Al-'Isrā' (The Night Journey) - سورة الإسراء
[17:37]
وَلَا تَمْشِ فِي الْأَرْضِ مَرَحًا ۖ إِنَّكَ لَن تَخْرِقَ الْأَرْضَ وَلَن تَبْلُغَ الْجِبَالَ طُولًا
And do not walk upon the earth exultantly. Indeed, you will never tear the earth [apart], and you will never reach the mountains in height.
TA-TAWALA ALAYHIL UMR (  تَطَاوَلَ عَلِيْهِ العُمْر   )   means growing of someone's age. Iong age(MANJID).
In Qur'an it is stated:-
Surat Al-Qaşaş (The Stories) - سورة القصص
[28:45]
وَلَٰكِنَّا أَنشَأْنَا قُرُونًا فَتَطَاوَلَ عَلَيْهِمُ الْعُمُرُ
But We produced [many] generations [after Moses], and prolonged was their duration.
5.2 MUDD (  مَدّ   ),   means     to stretch and lengthify. To increase the lenght and widht of a thing in such a manner that it does not break apart.(In referance to MAF)
----------------------------------------------------------------
Page 477
and   MUDDAT   (  مدّت  ) means  Age's(era) length.
In Qur'an it is stated:-
Surat Al-Furqān (The Criterian) - سورة الفرقان
[25:45]
أَلَمْ تَرَ إِلَىٰ رَبِّكَ كَيْفَ مَدَّ الظِّلَّ
Have you not considered your Lord - how He extends the shadow
and   MADDAT (  مدّت  )     meaning duration of period (like 'long time').  It is stated in Qur'an:-

6     DARPAY HONA   [Pursuit/Quest]
Synonyms: TASADDA(  تَصَدّي   ) , HAFA(  حَفَا   ).
6.1 TASADDA (  تَصَدّي   ): SADDA (  صَدي   )   meaning  uproar, the sound which stirkes an object e.g. dome etc then bounces back (echo)  . TASADDA(  تَصَدّي   ) meaning to be incessant after something like echoing voice. To be attentive (in referance to MAF)
Allah SWT stated in Qur'an:-
Surat `Abasa (He Frowned) - سورة عبس
[104: 5-6]
أَمَّا مَنِ اسْتَغْنَىٰ[5]
فَأَنتَ لَهُ تَصَدَّىٰ[6]
As for he who thinks himself without need,
To him you give attention.
6.2     HAFA (حَفَا ) (HAFU حفو )   means insisting to attain something. Tailing and advocation for someone's estimation (in referance to MAF).   Therefore, word   HAFU (  حفو  )   is used for constant pursuance and chasing  of  something .
It is stated in Qur'an:-
Surat Al-'A`rāf (The Heights) - سورة الأعراف
[7:187]
لَا تَأْتِيكُمْ إِلَّا بَغْتَةً ۗ يَسْأَلُونَكَ كَأَنَّكَ حَفِيٌّ عَنْهَا
It will not come upon you except unexpectedly." They ask you as if you are familiar with it
In another versus:-
Surat Maryam (Mary) - سورة مريم
[19:47]
سَأَسْتَغْفِرُ لَكَ رَبِّي ۖ إِنَّهُ كَانَ بِي حَفِيًّا
I will ask forgiveness for you of my Lord. Indeed, He is ever gracious to me.
In this ayah, real meaning of HAFFIYAN   حَفِيًّا   is  to be in pursuit every moment. Shortly it is translated as for kind/compassonate.
Summary:-
(i)   TASADA(  تَصَدّي   )  : temprory pursuits/quests.
(ii)   HAFA  (  حَفَا   ): permenant pursuits/quests.

7-   DARAKTH AUR PODAY   [Trees and plants]
Synonyms  : SHAJARAT (  شَجَرَة  ), SHAJAR(  شجر   ), NAJAM(  نَجْم  ), ATHAL(  اَثْل   ), YAQTEEN(  يَقْطِيْن   ), DAREE (  ضَرِيْع  ), ZAQ QOM.
7.1 SHAJARAT(  شَجَرَة  ), SHAJAR (  شجر   ):   SHAJARAT (  شَجَرَة  )means a tree (Arabic lexicon jeem, Tree) any plant having a woody trunk (in referance to MAF) can be considered as SHAJAR either it grows high or spread on ground. So, word SHAJARAT(  شَجَرَة  ) is common.
Allah SWT states in Qur'an:-
Surat Al-Wāqi`ah (The Inevitable) - سورة الواقعة
[56:71-72]
أَفَرَأَيْتُمُ النَّارَ الَّتِي تُورُونَ
أَأَنتُمْ أَنشَأْتُمْ شَجَرَتَهَا أَمْ نَحْنُ الْمُنشِئُونَ
And have you seen the fire that you ignite?
Is it you who produced its tree, or are We the producer?
7.2   NAJAM(نَجْم )  :   It is also used for 'star' and those plants which do not have woody trunk like herbs etc, (in referance to MAF).
Allah SWT states in Qur'an:-
Surat Ar-Raĥmān (The Beneficent) - سورة الرحمن
[55:6]
وَالنَّجْمُ وَالشَّجَرُ يَسْجُدَانِ
And the stars and trees prostrate.
7.3   ATHAL(اَثْل): ATHALA (اَثَلَ)   is to have a grip in ground. ATHAL(  اَثْل  ) trees which have stong roots. Generally it applies to the tree of tamarisk.
Allah SWT states in Qur'an:
Surat Saba' (Sheba) - سورة سبإ
[34:16]
وَبَدَّلْنَاهُم بِجَنَّتَيْهِمْ جَنَّتَيْنِ ذَوَاتَيْ أُكُلٍ خَمْطٍ وَأَثْلٍ وَشَيْءٍ مِّن سِدْرٍ قَلِيلٍ
We replaced their two [fields of] gardens with gardens of bitter fruit, tamarisks and something of sparse lote trees.
7.4   YAQTEEN (يَقْطِيْن ) :   Such trees which do not have proper (stem or stalk). It includes climbers/ vines for example pumpkin/gourd vines.(meem-qaaf)
Allah SWT states in Qur'an:-
Surat Aş-Şāffāt (Those who set the Ranks) - سورة الصافات
[37:146]
وَأَنبَتْنَا عَلَيْهِ شَجَرَةً مِّن يَقْطِينٍ
And We caused to grow over him a gourd vine.
7.5   DAREE(ضَرِيْع):   means thorny bushes or spiny shrub. (in referance to MAF).
Allah SWT states in Qur'an:-
Surat Al-Ghāshiyah (The Overwhelming) - سورة الغاشية
[88:6]
لَّيْسَ لَهُمْ طَعَامٌ إِلَّا مِن ضَرِيعٍ
For them there will be no food except from a poisonous, thorny plant.
7.6   ZAQ QOM   (زَقُوْم):     means Cereus     tree whose leaves are broad, thick and spiny. It tatses really bitter.
Allah SWT states in Qur'an:-
Surat Ad-Dukhān (The Smoke) - سورة الدخان
[44:43-44]
إِنَّ شَجَرَتَ الزَّقُّومِ
طَعَامُ الْأَثِيمِ
Indeed, the tree of zaqqum.
Is food for the sinful.
Summary:
(i)   SHAJRAT(شَجَرَة)  : It is a common word. It is applicable for all plant types having solid woody trunk.
(ii)   NAJAM (نَجْم )  : Non-woody plants, usually herbs.
(iii)   ATHAL  (اَثْل): Frimly rooted plants and tree of tamarisk.
(iv)     YAQTEEN  (يَقْطِيْن ):     Such plants which do not have solid trunk/wood. Fruiting plants. Specially vines of pumpkin/gourd.
(v)   DAREE   (ضَرِيْع) : Thorny bushes.
(vi)   ZAQ QOM   (زَقُوْم) : Plants that spread over the earth having thick spiny leaves. e.g. Canopy of Cereus.

8.   DARUST/ THEEK.   [Correct/Sound]
Synonyms:-   SAUAAB (صَوَاب ), HAQ (  حَقّ  )  .
8.1   SAUAAB (صَوَاب )   :- means right, correct. applicable (in referance to MANJID). (Antonym: error/mistake) and SUABA WA ASUABA AS SAHM (صَابَ وَ اَصَابَ السَّهْم)  means correct hit of an arrow on target ISTASUAB (اِسْتِصوَاب)  means to find an act or option to be right. To consider it correct. SAUAIB (صَوَيْب)  and MUSAIB (مُصِيْب ) Man of correct opinion. Righteous (In referance to MANJID). and if an arrow strikes at the right place and stays there, it is called MUSIBAH مصيبه  and this word is used for any soleful event (in referance to MAF). Therefore, SAUAAB (صواب) is basically related to opinion and qoute, it is often related to work.
Allah SWT states in Qur'an:
Surat An-Naba' (The Tidings) - سورة النبإ
[78:38]
لَّا يَتَكَلَّمُونَ إِلَّا مَنْ أَذِنَ لَهُ الرَّحْمَٰنُ وَقَالَ صَوَابًا
they will not speak except for one whom the Most Merciful permits, and he will say what is correct.
8.2   HAQ (حَقّ):   Truth, truthfulness and reality. Affirmative (Antonym: superficial). Any thing or talk proved right after experimentation and observation.(in referance to MAF).
Allah SWT states in Qur'an:-
Surat Fuşşilat (Explained in Detail) - سورة فصلت
[41:53]
سَنُرِيهِمْ آيَاتِنَا فِي الْآفَاقِ وَفِي أَنفُسِهِمْ حَتَّىٰ يَتَبَيَّنَ لَهُمْ أَنَّهُ الْحَقُّ
We will show them Our signs in the horizons and within themselves until it becomes clear to them that it is the truth  .
Summary:-
In   SAUAB   (  صواب   )   truthness relates with one's opinion or qoute, whereas   HAQ (  حَقّ  )   involves truthfulness of any thing or dialouge which is proved to be right after observation and experimentation.

9. To correct, rectify   (DURUST KARNA)
Synonyms: ASLAHA, SAWWAA
9.1 ASLAHA (اَصْلَحَ):   The opposite of Islaah is fasaad (incorrectness; the state of decaying, morally corruption) and Aslaha means to correct, repair, or reform the incorrect state.  It also means to reconcile. In Quran:
Surat Hūd (Hud) - هود سورة
11:88
إِنْ أُرِيدُ إِلَّا الْإِصْلَاحَ مَا اسْتَطَعْتُ
I only intend reform as much as I am able
9.2 SAWWAA (سَوّٰى):   Sawaa yaswee (يَسْوِى     سَوٰى) means to level (off), even.  Sawwaa means to put something to a proper, correct, upright position. According to Ibn Alfaris it means ‘ِ الْاِعْتِدَال وَ  اَلْاِسْتِقَامَة’ which gives the same meaning as described earlier. Allah says in the Quran:
Surat Al-'A`lá (The Most High) - الأعلى     سورة
87:2
الَّذِي خَلَقَ فَسَوَّىٰ
Who created and proportioned
Summary:
9.1 ASLAHAA: To correct moral corruption
9.2 SAWWAA: Used for correction of creative disorders
