ڈالنا  - to throw- pour
These words     القى  سلك  نبذ قذف افرغ  اوقع       have been used in the Quran
1.         القى   –   لقى     means two opposing things which come in front of each other, to meet up, but when it is used with baab ifaal then the root meaning changes   القى   –   to throw or put something in such a way that it becomes apparent in front of the other person.
In Surah Al-Aaaraaf, (7;107)
فَأَلْقَىٰ عَصَاهُ فَإِذَا هِيَ ثُعْبَانٌ مُّبِينٌ
So Moses threw his staff, and suddenly it was a serpent, manifest.
And you can also use the word metaphorically as:    In Surah Taha:  (20:39):
وَأَلْقَيْتُ عَلَيْكَ مَحَبَّةً مِّنِّي
And I bestowed upon you love from Me
This word is also used for, to inspire which is called   القاء   (  ilqaa)   refer to   دل میں بات ڈالنا
2.             سلك  -   the discussion has took place under the word   داخل کرنا   , the root meaning is to pull something  to put something in another, therefore according to that sometimes it means to put/to throw.
In Surah Qasas: (28:32):
اسْلُكْ يَدَكَ فِي جَيْبِكَ
Insert your hand into the opening of your garment;
3.          نبذ   –   the root meaning ‘to throw something which is of no interest/value, or to throw something behind your back, (the discussion has took place under the word   پھینکنا   , similar to the word   سلك     it is used also for ‘to put/to throw’).
In Surah Saafaat:   (37:145):
فَنَبَذْنَاهُ بِالْعَرَاءِ وَهُوَ سَقِيمٌ
But We threw him onto the open shore while he was ill
4.       قذف     -    to throw from faraway  ,   but sometimes it is used for,  to put or to throw.
In Surah Hashar:  (59: 2):
وَقَذَفَ فِي قُلُوبِهِمُ الرُّعْبَ
and He cast terror into their hearts.
5.         افرغ  -   فرغ   –   to     finish or complete a job/task   شغل   or to be empty.   افرغ الدلو   – means to pour water from the bucket whilst emptying it (MF) -  to put or pour something slowly.
In Surah Baqarah: (2:250):
رَبَّنَا أَفْرِغْ عَلَيْنَا صَبْرًا وَثَبِّتْ أَقْدَامَنَا
"Our Lord, pour upon us patience and plant firmly our feet
In Surah Kahaf: (18:96):
آتُونِي أُفْرِغْ عَلَيْهِ قِطْرًا
"Bring me, that I may pour over it molten copper."
6.         اوقع  -   وقع     there are two root meanings , to stay firm and to fall down, and   اوقع     means to befall/to make it happen  (MJD) means to place something and then make it firm.
In Surah Maidah: (5:91):
إِنَّمَا يُرِيدُ الشَّيْطَانُ أَن يُوقِعَ بَيْنَكُمُ الْعَدَاوَةَ وَالْبَغْضَاءَ
Satan only wants to cause between you animosity and hatred
Summary:
1.                 القى   – to put/place something with ease which others can see
2.                 سلك  - to put/place something in another
3.                       نبذ  - to throw something away thinking it not worth of attention
4.                 قذف  - to place or to put with intensity and strength
5.                 افرغ    - to place or put in such a manner similar to pouring water slowly from a bucket.
6.                 اوقع  - to place something and then to consolidate it.

raw_text:
ڈبونا  - to drown- dip
These words      اغرق  صبغ      have been used in the Quran
1.              اغرق   -    غرق  -   any non-aquatic creature which drowns and dies   اغرق     to drown someone.
In Surah Baqarah: (2:50):
وَأَغْرَقْنَا آلَ فِرْعَوْنَ وَأَنتُمْ تَنظُرُونَ
and drowned the people of Pharaoh while you were looking on.
2.          صبغ    -   صبغ يده فى الماء    -   to immerse your hands in water, and   اصبغت بالخل   -   I ate chappati dipped in vinegar,   صبغ الثوب    -   to colour material, to immerse material in coloured water,   صبغ     (  sibg  ) means colour and curry, and   صبغة  - means colour and   صابغ   person who colours,   صباغ   (  sabbaag)   means ‘a dyer’(MF, MJD).  This word has been used in the Quran for both meanings.
In Surah Baqarah: (2:138):
صِبْغَةَ اللَّهِ ۖ وَمَنْ أَحْسَنُ مِنَ اللَّهِ صِبْغَةً ۖ
[And say, "Ours is] the religion of Allah . And who is better than Allah in [ordaining] religion?  Not quite happy with this translation doesn’t fit in with the discussion?
And in Surah Muminoon: (23:20):
تَنبُتُ بِالدُّهْنِ وَصِبْغٍ لِّلْآكِلِينَ
which produces oil and food same here? for those who eat.
Summary:
1.              اغرق  - to drown someone in water so that he dies.
2.             صبغ   – to dip a morsel in curry or to immerse cloth in coloured water.

title: content/dd/dd3.html
raw_text:
ڈرنا  - to fear
These words       حذر  راع  اوجس وجف رهب  وجل  رعب  اشفق       خاف   خشي   خشع   اتقى (وقى)       have been used in the Quran
1.         خاف   –   to fear of a forthcoming calamity due to presumptions (MF) the opposite of   خوف   is   امن   – peace, meaning the connection of   خاف     is with the future. The wordings of Abu Hilaal to the meaning of   خوف   is   توقع الضرر المشكوك     - The expectation of a doubtful damage/harm. (I have translated it plz get it checked) (FQ, L 199)
In Surah Hud: (11:70):
قَالُوا لَا تَخَفْ إِنَّا أُرْسِلْنَا إِلَىٰ قَوْمِ لُوطٍ
They said, "Fear not. We have been sent to the people of Lot."
2.        خشي   –   fear which appears in the heart due to the enormity of the matter (MF).
In Surah Al-Israa: (17:31):
وَلَا تَقْتُلُوا أَوْلَادَكُمْ خَشْيَةَ إِمْلَاقٍ
And do not kill your children for fear of poverty.
3.        خشع   –   such a fear which, besides the heart, shows other visible signs, the softening of the heart (MF) that’s why this word has been used for   جوارح   body parts, such as:
In Surah Maa-aarij: (70:44):
خَاشِعَةً أَبْصَارُهُمْ
Their eyes humbled (sahih),  meaning their gaze will be lowered due to fear.
In Surah Gashiyah:  (88:2):
وُجُوهٌ يَوْمَئِذٍ خَاشِعَةٌ
[Some] faces, that Day, will be humbled  (Sahih), Many faces will be lowered cause of fear.
And in Surah Tahaa: (20:108):
وَخَشَعَتِ الْأَصْوَاتُ
and [all] voices will be stilled (Sahih), voices will be surpressed, quelled due to fear.
In Surah Hadid: (57:16):
أَلَمْ يَأْنِ لِلَّذِينَ آمَنُوا أَن تَخْشَعَ قُلُوبُهُمْ لِذِكْرِ اللَّهِ
Has the time not come for those who have believed that their hearts should become humbly submissive at the remembrance of Allah
4.       اتقى (وقى)     -   تقوى    -   to fear from the outcome of deeds, a natural inclination towards good and leaving the bad (MF), to bear in mind the commands and prohibitions of Allah due to His fear (MJD), (opposite of   عدوان  ) and   اتقى     means to try to stay away from sins because of their consequences.   To choose righteousness.
In Surah Baqarah:   (2:187):
كَذَٰلِكَ يُبَيِّنُ اللَّهُ آيَاتِهِ لِلنَّاسِ لَعَلَّهُمْ يَتَّقُونَ
Thus does Allah make clear His ordinances to the people that they may become righteous.
5.        حذر    -   to prevent or stay away from a fearful thing (MF), to be alert of any danger, to prevent (MJD) , In the word   حذر     the danger is     sometimes definite sometimes indefinite, yet by taking precautions you can prevent yourself from that danger, (FQ,L200) like the transmitter of electricity or a frayed electricity wire.
In Surah Baqarah:   (2:19):
يَجْعَلُونَ أَصَابِعَهُمْ فِي آذَانِهِم مِّنَ الصَّوَاعِقِ حَذَرَ الْمَوْتِ
They put their fingers in their ears against the thunderclaps in dread of death.
And   حذر       is also used for safety equipment , as:
In Surah Nisaa: (4:71):
خُذُوا حِذْرَكُمْ
take your precaution (Sahih) take control of your weapons, or consider your safety by any other means.
6.       راع     -   to perplex and to astonish someone (MJD)   روع   – heart ,   رعته   (  raa tuhu)   to frighten , perplex someone and   ناقة روعاء   means cowardly camel (MF), and   الروع   means such a state in which man is amazed by something but also feel frightened due to some imaginary danger.
In Surah Hud: (11:74):
فَلَمَّا ذَهَبَ عَنْ إِبْرَاهِيمَ الرَّوْعُ
And when the fright had left Abraham.
7.        اوجس  -   وجس     to be hidden, to hear the footfall, to fear from something you have heard (MJD), and   اوجس     means to try and hide the fear and not to show the signs/effects of fear on the face.
In Surah Hud: (11:70):
فَلَمَّا رَأَىٰ أَيْدِيَهُمْ لَا تَصِلُ إِلَيْهِ نَكِرَهُمْ وَأَوْجَسَ مِنْهُمْ خِيفَةً ۚ
But when he saw their hands not reaching for it, he distrusted them and felt from them apprehension.
8.       وجف   –   to be agitated, palpitations of the heart  ,   and to fall from fear (MJD), two things are present in   وجف     anxiousness and fear  ,   and with these the heart starts to beat faster.
In Surah An-Naziaat: (79:8):
قُلُوبٌ يَوْمَئِذٍ وَاجِفَةٌ
Hearts, that Day, will tremble.
9.       وجل   –   to fear in the heart (MF), to get goose bumps.  (MQ) to increase in fear, to become old. To fear, due to past mistakes and to be restless (FQ, L 202).
In Surah Anfaal: (8:2):
إِنَّمَا الْمُؤْمِنُونَ الَّذِينَ إِذَا ذُكِرَ اللَّهُ وَجِلَتْ قُلُوبُهُمْ
The believers are only those who, when Allah is mentioned, their hearts become fearful.
10.                          رهب    -   such a fear which comprises of anxiousness and caution (opposite of   رغب   ) and   راهب    means people who fear from Allah, a person who sits in a secluded corner and worshipper, from it the word   رهبانية   is derived, which means to leave behind all the worldly desires(MJD) , and   طول الخوف واستمراره   (FQ, L200) means to be always fearful.
In Surah Al-ambiya: (21:90):
إِنَّهُمْ كَانُوا يُسَارِعُونَ فِي الْخَيْرَاتِ وَيَدْعُونَنَا رَغَبًا وَرَهَبًا ۖ
Indeed, they used to hasten to good deeds and supplicate Us in hope and fear.
11.  رعب    -   the threat,  terror of fear and   رعب   (  ra a ba)   means to fill up with fear (MF) to be overawed by fear, flinch with fear.
In Surah Kahf: (18:18):
لَوِ اطَّلَعْتَ عَلَيْهِمْ لَوَلَّيْتَ مِنْهُمْ فِرَارًا وَلَمُلِئْتَ مِنْهُمْ رُعْبًا
If you had looked at them, you would have turned from them in flight and been filled by them with terror.
12.                           اشفق   –   شفق على    -   to wish someone well, and   اشفق     means thinking  of someone’s good welfare whilst fearing that  no danger befalls them(MF) to be worried about welfare and reform, to have mercy, to be merciful and   شفقة   means mercy compassion, compassion with fear, and   اشفق منه   means to be scared, to be greedy, (MJD).
In Surah  Kahf:  (18:49):
وَوُضِعَ الْكِتَابُ فَتَرَى الْمُجْرِمِينَ مُشْفِقِينَ مِمَّا فِيهِ
And the record [of deeds] will be placed [open], and you will see the criminals fearful of that within it,
Summary:
1.          خاف   – fear of coming danger
2.     خشي   – to fear due to the enormity of the matter
3.      خشع   – fear which has a visible effect on body.
4.   اتقى (وقى)     - to refrain from sins due its consequences
5.     حذر     - to stay away from danger, to be scared, to be alert
6.     راع     - to be amazed whilst fearing an imaginary danger
7.     اوجس   – to be fearful in the heart and try to conceal it
8.   وجف  - the palpitating of the heart with fear and restlessness
9.     وجل   – to be anxious and to fear someone due to previous error
10.   رهب  - fear which combines caution with anxiousness, and it is lengthy
11.   رعب  - terror, overawed by fear
12.   اشفق  - wishing well for someone whilst fearing for them aswell,   mixed feelings of hope and fear.

Page-520
3.11      Ra’aba (رَعَبَ )   means intense fear, terror or to be filled with fear or to lie low because of fear of (being spotted by) someone. It is mentioned in Qur’an
Surat Al-Kahf (The Cave) - سورة الكهف 18:18
للَوِ اطَّلَعْتَ عَلَيْهِمْ لَوَلَّيْتَ مِنْهُمْ فِرَارًا وَّلَمُلِئْتَ مِنْهُمْ رُعْبًا
If you had looked at them, you would have turned from them in flight and been filled by them with terror  .
3.12      Ashfaqa (اَشْفَقَ):    SHAFQA-A’ALA ( شفق أعلى) means to seek after someone's welfare. ASHFAQ (اشفق) means in addition to someone's welfare, to be afraid if trouble comes to him. Moreover, to be worried about welfare and reform. To show mercy, to be kind. And SHAFQATAH (شفقته) means kindness, mercy, kindness with fear. And ASHFAQA MINHU ( اشفق منه ) means to be frightened, greedy. It is mentioned in Qur’an:
Surat Al-Kahf     (The Cave) - سورة الكهف 18:49
وَوُضِـعَ الْكِتٰبُ فَتَرَى الْمُجْرِمِيْنَ مُشْفِقِيْنَ مِمَّا فِيْهِ
And the record [of deeds] will be placed [open], and you will see the criminals fearful of that within it.
Summary:
3.1 KHAFA: The apprehension of danger.
3.2 KHASHIA: Fear because of the greatness/dignity of some Amer.
3.3 KHASHAA:  A fear that affect organs and soul as well.
3.4 ITTAQA: To avoid sins due to the fear of consequences.
3.5 RAAA: To wonder and the fear of imaginative danger.
3.6 HAZERA: To refrain from something dangerous. To be alert.
3.7 AOOJASA: To be frightened in heart and try to hide it.
3.8 WAJAFA: Beating of heart due to fear. Fear and anxiety.
3.9 WAJILA: To be afraid from someone and apprehensive due to personal negligence.
3.10 RAHABA: A fear in which caution and anxiety both are present and it is long.
3.11 RA’ABA: Intensity of fear. Terror.
3.12 ASHFAQA: in addition to someone's welfare, to be afraid if trouble comes to him. Mixed feelings of fear and mercy.

[Some] faces, that Day, will be humbled  (Sahih), Many faces will be lowered cause of fear.

 

And in Surah Tahaa: (20:108):

 

وَخَشَعَتِ الْأَصْوَاتُ 

 

and [all] voices will be stilled (Sahih), voices will be surpressed, quelled due to fear.

 

In Surah Hadid: (57:16):

 

أَلَمْ يَأْنِ لِلَّذِينَ آمَنُوا أَن تَخْشَعَ قُلُوبُهُمْ لِذِكْرِ اللَّهِ

 

Has the time not come for those who have believed that their hearts should become humbly submissive at the remembrance of Allah

 

4.   اتقى (وقى)   - تقوى  - to fear from the outcome of deeds, a natural inclination towards good and leaving the bad (MF), to bear in mind the commands and prohibitions of Allah due to His fear (MJD), (opposite of عدوان) and اتقى means to try to stay away from sins because of their consequences.   To choose righteousness.

 

In Surah Baqarah:   (2:187):

 

كَذَٰلِكَ يُبَيِّنُ اللَّهُ آيَاتِهِ لِلنَّاسِ لَعَلَّهُمْ يَتَّقُونَ

 

Thus does Allah make clear His ordinances to the people that they may become righteous.

 

 

5.    حذر  - to prevent or stay away from a fearful thing (MF), to be alert of any danger, to prevent (MJD) , In the word حذر the danger is sometimes definite sometimes indefinite, yet by taking precautions you can prevent yourself from that danger, (FQ,L200) like the transmitter of electricity or a frayed electricity wire.

 

In Surah Baqarah:   (2:19):

 

يَجْعَلُونَ أَصَابِعَهُمْ فِي آذَانِهِم مِّنَ الصَّوَاعِقِ حَذَرَ الْمَوْتِ

 

They put their fingers in their ears against the thunderclaps in dread of death.

 

And حذر   is also used for safety equipment , as:

 

In Surah Nisaa: (4:71):

 

خُذُوا حِذْرَكُمْ 

 

take your precaution (Sahih) take control of your weapons, or consider your safety by any other means.

 

6.   راع   - to perplex and to astonish someone (MJD) روع – heart , رعته (raa tuhu) to frighten , perplex someone and ناقة روعاء means cowardly camel (MF), and الروع means such a state in which man is amazed by something but also feel frightened due to some imaginary danger.

 

In Surah Hud: (11:74):

 

فَلَمَّا ذَهَبَ عَنْ إِبْرَاهِيمَ الرَّوْعُ 

 

And when the fright had left Abraham.

 

7.    اوجس- وجس to be hidden, to hear the footfall, to fear from something you have heard (MJD), and اوجس means to try and hide the fear and not to show the signs/effects of fear on the face.

 

In Surah Hud: (11:70):

 

فَلَمَّا رَأَىٰ أَيْدِيَهُمْ لَا تَصِلُ إِلَيْهِ نَكِرَهُمْ وَأَوْجَسَ مِنْهُمْ خِيفَةً ۚ 

 

But when he saw their hands not reaching for it, he distrusted them and felt from them apprehension.

 

 

8.   وجف – to be agitated, palpitations of the heart, and to fall from fear (MJD), two things are present in وجف anxiousness and fear, and with these the heart starts to beat faster.

 

In Surah An-Naziaat: (79:8):

 

قُلُوبٌ يَوْمَئِذٍ وَاجِفَةٌ        

 

Hearts, that Day, will tremble.

 

9.   وجل – to fear in the heart (MF), to get goose bumps.  (MQ) to increase in fear, to become old. To fear, due to past mistakes and to be restless (FQ, L 202).

 

In Surah Anfaal: (8:2):

 

إِنَّمَا الْمُؤْمِنُونَ الَّذِينَ إِذَا ذُكِرَ اللَّهُ وَجِلَتْ قُلُوبُهُمْ

 

The believers are only those who, when Allah is mentioned, their hearts become fearful.

 

10.                      رهب  - such a fear which comprises of anxiousness and caution (opposite of رغب ) and راهب  means people who fear from Allah, a person who sits in a secluded corner and worshipper, from it the word رهبانية is derived, which means to leave behind all the worldly desires(MJD) , and طول الخوف واستمراره (FQ, L200) means to be always fearful.

 

In Surah Al-ambiya: (21:90):

 

إِنَّهُمْ كَانُوا يُسَارِعُونَ فِي الْخَيْرَاتِ وَيَدْعُونَنَا رَغَبًا وَرَهَبًا ۖ 

 

Indeed, they used to hasten to good deeds and supplicate Us in hope and fear.

 

11.رعب  - the threat,  terror of fear and رعب (ra a ba) means to fill up with fear (MF) to be overawed by fear, flinch with fear.

 

In Surah Kahf: (18:18):

لَوِ اطَّلَعْتَ عَلَيْهِمْ لَوَلَّيْتَ مِنْهُمْ فِرَارًا وَلَمُلِئْتَ مِنْهُمْ رُعْبًا

 

If you had looked at them, you would have turned from them in flight and been filled by them with terror.

 

12.                       اشفق – شفق على  - to wish someone well, and اشفق means thinking  of someone’s good welfare whilst fearing that  no danger befalls them(MF) to be worried about welfare and reform, to have mercy, to be merciful and شفقة means mercy compassion, compassion with fear, and اشفق منه means to be scared, to be greedy, (MJD).

 

In Surah  Kahf:  (18:49):

 

وَوُضِعَ الْكِتَابُ فَتَرَى الْمُجْرِمِينَ مُشْفِقِينَ مِمَّا فِيهِ 

 

And the record [of deeds] will be placed [open], and you will see the criminals fearful of that within it,

 

Summary:

1.    خاف – fear of coming danger

2. خشي – to fear due to the enormity of the matter

3.  خشع – fear which has a visible effect on body.

4. اتقى (وقى)   - to refrain from sins due its consequences

5. حذر   - to stay away from danger, to be scared, to be alert

6. راع   - to be amazed whilst fearing an imaginary danger

7. اوجس – to be fearful in the heart and try to conceal it

8. وجف- the palpitating of the heart with fear and restlessness

9. وجل – to be anxious and to fear someone due to previous error

10. رهب- fear which combines caution with anxiousness, and it is lengthy

11. رعب- terror, overawed by fear

12. اشفق- wishing well for someone whilst fearing for them aswell,   mixed feelings of hope and fear.    

<<Alternate version:>>

Page-520

 

3.11  Ra’aba (رَعَبَ ) means intense fear, terror or to be filled with fear or to lie low because of fear of (being spotted by) someone. It is mentioned in Qur’an 

Surat Al-Kahf (The Cave) - سورة الكهف 18:18

 

 للَوِ اطَّلَعْتَ عَلَيْهِمْ لَوَلَّيْتَ مِنْهُمْ فِرَارًا وَّلَمُلِئْتَ مِنْهُمْ رُعْبًا        

If you had looked at them, you would have turned from them in flight and been filled by them with terror. 

3.12  Ashfaqa (اَشْفَقَ):  SHAFQA-A’ALA ( شفق أعلى) means to seek after someone's welfare. ASHFAQ (اشفق) means in addition to someone's welfare, to be afraid if trouble comes to him. Moreover, to be worried about welfare and reform. To show mercy, to be kind. And SHAFQATAH (شفقته) means kindness, mercy, kindness with fear. And ASHFAQA MINHU ( اشفق منه ) means to be frightened, greedy. It is mentioned in Qur’an:

 

Surat Al-Kahf (The Cave) - سورة الكهف 18:49

 وَوُضِـعَ الْكِتٰبُ فَتَرَى الْمُجْرِمِيْنَ مُشْفِقِيْنَ مِمَّا فِيْهِ

And the record [of deeds] will be placed [open], and you will see the criminals fearful of that within it.

 

Summary:

 

3.1 KHAFA: The apprehension of danger.

3.2 KHASHIA: Fear because of the greatness/dignity of some Amer.

3.3 KHASHAA:  A fear that affect organs and soul as well.

3.4 ITTAQA: To avoid sins due to the fear of consequences.

3.5 RAAA: To wonder and the fear of imaginative danger.

3.6 HAZERA: To refrain from something dangerous. To be alert.

3.7 AOOJASA: To be frightened in heart and try to hide it.

3.8 WAJAFA: Beating of heart due to fear. Fear and anxiety.

3.9 WAJILA: To be afraid from someone and apprehensive due to personal negligence.

3.10 RAHABA: A fear in which caution and anxiety both are present and it is long.

3.11 RA’ABA: Intensity of fear. Terror.

3.12 ASHFAQA: in addition to someone's welfare, to be afraid if trouble comes to him. Mixed feelings of fear and mercy.

4- DARAANA [To Frighten]
Qur’an has referred to it with words like     KHAWF  (خوف ) , HADHARA (حذرا ), ARHABA (ارھبا ),  ANDHARA ( أنذر ) , AWA’ADA (ا وعدا ). KHAWFA  (خوف ) , HADHARA (حذرا ), ARHABA (ارھبا ) are already discussed above. And it becomes more mutaadi from necessary  .   Take a look at their examples:
Page-521
4.1   Surat Az-Zumar (The Troops) -     سورة الزمر     39:36
اَلَيْسَ اللّٰهُ بِكَافٍ عَبْدَهٗ ۭ وَيُخَوِّفُوْنَكَ بِالَّذِيْنَ مِنْ دُوْنِهٖ ۭ
Is not Allah sufficient for His Servant [Prophet Muhammad]? And [yet], they threaten you with those [they worship] other than Him.
4.2   Surat 'Āli `Imrān (Family of Imran)   -   سورة آل عمران 3:28
وَيُحَذِّرُكُمُ اللّٰهُ نَفْسَهٗ  ۭ
And Allah warns you of Himself.
4.3   Surat Al-'Anfāl (The Spoils of War) -     سورة الأنفال 8:60
وَاَعِدُّوْا لَهُمْ مَّا اسْـتَـطَعْتُمْ مِّنْ قُوَّةٍ وَّمِنْ رِّبَاطِ الْخَيْلِ تُرْهِبُوْنَ بِهٖ عَدُوَّ اللّٰهِ وَعَدُوَّكُمْ
And prepare against them whatever you are able of power and of steeds of war by which you may terrify the enemy of Allah and your enemy  .
And     ISTARHAB (إستر هب):        meaning to try scaring somebody or creating a situation to make him afraid. It is mentioned in Qur’an
Surat Al-'A`rāf (The Heights) -     سورة الأعراف     7:116
فَلَمَّآ اَلْقَوْا سَحَرُوْٓا اَعْيُنَ النَّاسِ وَاسْتَرْهَبُوْهُمْ وَجَاۗءُوْ بِسِحْرٍ عَظِيْمٍ
"Throw," and when they threw, they bewitched the eyes of the people and struck terror into them, and they presented a great [feat of] magic.
4.4 ANDHARA (أنذر):    means to make aware, to inform and to warn of consequences. To be afraid of the resulting judgement of deeds and accountability on the Day of Judgement. And this is only for Allah and his messengers.  NADHEER (نذير ) means one who warns (antonym is one who give good news, to make afraid by specifying information of fear. And INDHAAR (انذار ) actually is a great favour from MUNDHAR (منذر ).
Surat Al-'An`ām (The Cattle) -     سورة الأنعام     6:131
اَلَمْ يَاْتِكُمْ رُسُلٌ مِّنْكُمْ يَقُصُّوْنَ عَلَيْكُمْ اٰيٰتِيْ وَيُنْذِرُوْنَكُمْ  لِقَاۗءَ يَوْمِكُمْ ھٰذَا
Did there not come to you messengers from among you, relating to you My verses and warning you of the meeting of this Day of yours?
4.5 A’AWADAH (ا عودة):     is a common word for promise means to give hope to somebody. But WAEED (وعيد ) denotes the bad result because of a wrong doing, or its punishment, threat. And AOADA (ا وعدا )means to give threat, to intimidate, whether it is verbal or practical, to provide such material. Allah says
Surat Al-'A`rāf (The Heights) -     سورة الأعراف 7:86
وَلَا تَقْعُدُوْا بِكُلِّ صِرَاطٍ تُوْعِدُوْنَ وَتَصُدُّوْنَ عَنْ سَبِيْلِ اللّٰهِ
And do not sit on every path, threatening and averting from the way of Allah those who believe in Him.
Summary:
4.1      KHAWAFA:     To warn somebody of an upcoming danger  .
4.2      HAZARA:     To warn somebody of a dangerous thing, to save or to inform  .
4.3      ARHABA:     To create fear and anxiety  .
4.4      INZAAR:     Warning from prophets and messengers regarding deeds result and accountability  .
4.5      To make afraid, threaten or to give threat.

Page-522
5- DOL [Bucket]
Qur’an     has referred it with the words     DALU (دلو ) ZANUB (ذنوب ).
5.1       DALU (دلو ) :     Pot used to take out water from the well, bucket etc. if it is free of water. It is mentioned in Qur’an:
Surat Yūsuf (Joseph) -     سورة يوسف
12:19
وَجَاۗءَتْ سَيَّارَةٌ فَاَرْسَلُوْا وَارِدَهُمْ فَاَدْلٰى دَلْوَهٗ   ۭ
And there came a company of travellers; then they sent their water drawer, and he let down his bucket.
5.2       ZANUB (ذنوب ):     Pot used to take out water from the well bucket etc. if it is full with water. Allah says:
Surat Adh-Dhāriyāt (The Winnowing Winds) -     سورة الذاريات     51:59
فَاِنَّ لِلَّذِيْنَ ظَلَمُوْا ذَنُوْبًا مِّثْلَ ذَنُوْبِ اَصْحٰبِهِمْ فَلَا يَسْتَعْجِلُوْنِ
And indeed, for those who have wronged their bucket is filled just like their companions.
It means that these wrongdoers have also reached in the doldrums and their survival parameter is filled just like the other wrongdoers similar to them.
Summary:
If the pot is full of water then it is     ZANUB (ذنوب ).     If it is filled with a little bit of water then it is     SIJAL (سجل )     and if it is totally empty then it is     DALU (دلو ).

raw_text:
6- DHAAL [Shield]
Qur’an has included the words     JUNAH (جنة ), and URZA (عرضثہ).
6.1      JUNA (جنة ): DHAAL:     that known weapon which is used to prevent enemy attack, to stop the enemy attack by putting it before his weapon and to rescue yourself. It is used in both physical and spiritual manners.
Surat Al-Mujādila (The Pleading Woman) -     سورة المجادلة     58:16
اِتَّخَذُوْٓا اَيْمَانَهُمْ جُنَّةً فَصَدُّوْا عَنْ سَبِيْلِ اللّٰه
They took their [false] oaths as a cover, so they averted [people] from the way of Allah.
6.2      URZATUN (عر ظة ) :Araza:     means to present and URZA (عرضثہ) Is everything which can save you by putting in front, it can be a shield or any other thing. and URZA (عرضثہ) means target. It is said that and HOWA URZATUN LINAASE (عرضثہ هوا)   means he has been targeted by peoples slandering and defamation. HOWA URZATUN LILKALAAM (للكلام عرضثہ هوا) means he is the target of objections. Hence ARZA (عرضثہ)  is used in deeper concept than JUNAH (جنة ). Allah says:
Surat Al-Baqarah (The Cow) -     سورة البقرة 2:224
وَلَا تَجْعَلُوا اللّٰهَ عُرْضَةً لِّاَيْمَانِكُمٌ
And do not make [your oath by] Allah a target.

6.1  JUNA (جنة ): DHAAL: that known weapon which is used to prevent enemy attack, to stop the enemy attack by putting it before his weapon and to rescue yourself. It is used in both physical and spiritual manners.

Surat Al-Mujādila (The Pleading Woman) - سورة المجادلة 58:16

 اِتَّخَذُوْٓا اَيْمَانَهُمْ جُنَّةً فَصَدُّوْا عَنْ سَبِيْلِ اللّٰه

They took their [false] oaths as a cover, so they averted [people] from the way of Allah.

 

 

6.2  URZATUN (عر ظة ) :Araza: means to present and URZA (عرضثہ) Is everything which can save you by putting in front, it can be a shield or any other thing. and URZA (عرضثہ) means target. It is said that and HOWA URZATUN LINAASE (عرضثہ هوا)   means he has been targeted by peoples slandering and defamation. HOWA URZATUN LILKALAAM (للكلام عرضثہ هوا) means he is the target of objections. Hence ARZA (عرضثہ)  is used in deeper concept than JUNAH (جنة ). Allah says:

Surat Al-Baqarah (The Cow) - سورة البقرة 2:224

 وَلَا تَجْعَلُوا اللّٰهَ عُرْضَةً لِّاَيْمَانِكُمٌ        

And do not make [your oath by] Allah a target.

7- DHANKNA AUR DHAANPNA [Cover and Clothe]
Qur’an has referred them by the words     JANA (جن ), GHASHIA (غشي ) AGHSHA (أغشى ) GHASHA (غشى ) TAGHASHA (تغشى ) and ARHAQA (ارهق ).
7.1        JUNA (جن) :     to hide something by covering it so that it remains hidden from sight. Jin is the creation that remains hidden from sight and JANEEN (جنين ) is the baby inside mother’s womb. It is mentioned in Qur’an:
Surat Al-'An`ām (The Cattle) -     سورة الأنعام     6:77
فَلَمَّا جَنَّ عَلَيْهِ الَّيْلُ رَاٰ كَوْكَبًاَ
So when the night covered him [with darkness], he saw a star.
7.2       GHASHIA (غشي):     to cover one thing from the other in a way that it is not completely hidden. Allah says:
Surat Luqmān (Luqman) -     سورة لقمان     31:32
وَاِذَا غَشِيَهُمْ مَّوْجٌ كَالظُّلَلِ دَعَوُا اللّٰهَ مُخْلِصِيْنَ لَهُ الدِّيْنَ
And when waves come over them like canopies, they supplicate Allah , sincere to Him in religion.
AGHSHA (أغشى ) GHASHA (غشى ) TAGHASHA (تغشى ) are all plurals of GHASHA (غشى ).
Surat Ar-Ra`d (The Thunder) -     سورة الرعد     13:3
يُغْشِي الَّيْلَ النَّهَارَ
He causes the night to cover the day  .
Surat Al-'Anfāl (The Spoils of War) -     سورة الأنفال     8:11
اِذْ يُغَشِّيْكُمُ النُّعَاسَ  ۭ
[Remember] when He overwhelmed you with drowsiness.
Surat Al-'A`rāf (The Heights) -     سورة الأعراف     7:189
فَلَمَّا تَغَشّٰىهَاَ
And when man covers the woman  .
7.3          RAHIQA(رهق ):     Rahaqahu-al-Almr: means some matter chocked him by oppression force and Rahiqa and Arhaqa both has same meanings. And La-Arhaq-Allaho means Allah may not put you in trouble and hardship. Allah says:
Surat Al-Qalam (The Pen)   -   سورة القلم     68:43
اشِعَةً اَبْصَارُهُمْ تَرْهَقُهُمْ ذِلَّةٌ
Their eyes humbled, humiliation will cover them.
Summary:
7.1      JANA: Hide from sight by covering.
7.2      AGHSHA: to cover in a way that it is not completely hidden.
7.3      RAHAQ: by force one thing oppress and covers the other.

8- DHALNA [Descend]
Qur’an has referred them by the words     ZAWAAL (زوال )  and DULUK (دلوك ).
Page-524
8.1           ZAAL (زال ) :      ZOL (زول ) ZAALATISHAMS (زالتيشمش ) downward movement of sun. and ZAWAAL (زوال )means downward movement of sun from the head and the time of downward movement. And ZAWAAL (زوال ) is also used for an object reaching to its extreme height and then coming down slowly. Antonym is UROOJH and ZAWAAL (زوال )also refers to a thing that is drawn to a specific side after leaving its right direction. And ZAALA UNHO MULKOHU (زال عنه ملكه ) means his government has been dissolved/erased. Allah says:
Surat 'Ibrāhīm (Abrahim)   -   سورة ابراهيم     14:44
اَوَلَمْ تَكُوْنُوْٓا اَقْسَمْتُمْ مِّنْ قَبْلُ مَا لَكُمْ مِّنْ زَوَالٍ
Had you not sworn, before, that for you there would be no cessation?
8.2 DULUK (دلو ك ) :     DALKAT ISHAMSO DULUKA (دلکت اشمس دلوکا ) Bend down/bow down of the sun during sunset and ADALKA (ادلک ):means looseness:
(Surat-Bani Israel) سورة بنی اسراءیل     17:78
اَقِمِ الصَّلٰوةَ لِدُلُوْكِ الشَّمْسِ اِلٰى غَسَقِ الَّيْلِ وَقُرْاٰنَ الْفَجْر
Establish prayer at the decline of the sun [from its meridian] until the darkness of the night and [also] the Qur'an of dawn.
Summary:
ZAWAAL (زوال ) :     Is used for coming down from height and     DULUK (دلوك ):     shows a strong notion of strength and looseness  .

raw_text:
9- DHOONDNA [Search]
Qur’an has referred them by the words     TALABA (طلب ) IBTAGHA (ابتغاء ) TAHASAS (تحسس ) TAJASASA (تجسس ) ILTAMASA (التمس ) JAASA (جاس )  BASARA (بعژا ) and TAHERA (تحرى ).
9.1          TALABA (طلب ):   means to desire, want, find and means to search and quest to find and get something. It is used both in physical and spiritual sense.   It is mentioned in Qur’an:
Surat Al-Kahf     (The Cave) - سورة الكهف     18:41
اَوْ يُصْبِحَ مَاۗؤُهَا غَوْرًا فَلَنْ تَسْتَطِيْعَ لَهٗ طَلَبًا
Or its water will become sunken [into the earth], so you would never be able to seek it.
9.2       IBTAGHA (ابتغى ):      BAGHA (بغى ): Ibn-al-faras has told two meanings of BAGHA (بغى ):: TALABASHEE (طلب اشي ) JINS MINAL FASAD (جنس من الفساد ) means desire for a thing and a form of violence i.e. disobedience and rebellion etc. Imam Raghib combines these two terms and define it as “to go over or cross the limit of moderation to get something. And IBTAGHA (ابتغاء )is used in terms of seeking something by trying. Allah says:
Surat Al-'An`ām (The Cattle) -     سورة الأنعام     6:35
فَاِنِ اسْتَطَعْتَ اَنْ تَبْتَغِيَ نَفَقًا فِي الْاَرْضِ اَوْ سُلَّمًا فِي السَّمَاۗءِ
If you are able to seek a tunnel into the earth or a stairway into the sky to bring them a sign.
9.3       TAHASASA  (تحسس ):         AHASA (احس ): means to feel something and TAHASASA (تحسس ): means to make full use of five senses in search of something. Try hard to find a missing thing. This is mehmood attribute. It is mentioned in Qur’an:
Surat Yūsuf (Joseph) -     سورة يوسف     12:87
يٰبَنِيَّ اذْهَبُوْا فَتَحَسَّسُوْا مِنْ يُّوْسُفَ وَاَخِيْهِ
O my sons, go and find out about Youssef and his brother.
Page-525
9.4      TAJASASA (تجسس ):   JASSA (جس )  :     means to know the inner condition of the patient by checking his pulse. It is specific with HASSA (حس ): in HASSA (حس ):, the five senses are utilized to unfold the outside conditions while JASSA (جس )is called as finding inner situations.  And the word JASOOS (جاسوس ) is also related to it. And TAJASASA (تجسس )means to fossick/search something secret, reconnoitre, spying and trying to find someone's faults and weaknesses. Then inform the others. And this attribute is mazmum. Allah says:
Surat Al-Ĥujurāt (The Rooms) -     سورة الحجرات 49:12
وَّلَا تَجَسَّسُوْا وَلَا يَغْتَبْ بَّعْضُكُمْ بَعْضًا
And do not spy or backbite each other.
9.5              ILTAMASA  (التمس ):        LAMASA (لمس ): means to fossick something with hands or fingers and ILTAMASA  (التمس )means to find an object by touching it. Demand an object repeatedly, continuously try to search. Allah says:
Surat Al-Ĥadīd (The Iron) -     سورة الحديد 57:13
قِيْلَ ارْجِعُوْا وَرَاۗءَكُمْ فَالْتَمِسُوْا نُوْرًاۭ
“It will be said, "Go back behind you and seek light.”
9.6      JASA  (جا س ) :     means reaching an extreme in desire of something, greedily find out something:
Surat-Bani Israel ( سورة بنی اسراءیل)     17:5
بَعَثْنَا عَلَيْكُمْ عِبَادًا لَّنَآ اُولِيْ بَاْسٍ شَدِيْدٍ فَجَاسُوْا خِلٰلَ الدِّيَار
We sent against you servants of Ours - those of great military might, and they probed [even] into the homes.
9.7          BASARA  (بعژا ):     means to find out and BASARAL MATTAA ( بعژالمتاع) means to overturn the stuff and BUSIRA (بعژ )word is a mixture of BUESA (بعث )and USERA (عژ )which contain the meanings of both verbs i.e. to raise the dead by overturning them.
Surat Al-Ĥujurāt (The Rooms) -     سورة الحجرات     82:4
وَاِذَا الْقُبُوْرُ بُعْثِرَتْ
And when the [contents of] graves are scattered.
And at another place is
Surat Al-`Ādiyāt (The Courser) -     سورة العاديات     100:9
اَفَلَا يَعْلَمُ اِذَا بُعْثِرَ مَا فِي الْقُبُوْرِ
But does he not know that when the contents of the graves are scattered.
9.8                TAHERA (  تحرى ):     AL-HARA (الأحرى ) means more efficient, more appropriate, more better. And TAHERA (تحرى ) means to use the one which is more appropriate and efficient. To demand  the one which is better between the two things.
Surat Al-Jinn (The Jinn) -     سورة الجن      72:14
وَّاَنَّا مِنَّا الْمُسْلِمُوْنَ وَمِنَّا الْقٰسِطُوْنَ ۭ فَمَنْ اَسْلَمَ فَاُولٰۗىِٕكَ تَحَرَّوْا رَشَدًا
And among us are Muslims [in submission to Allah ], and among us are the unjust. And whoever has become Muslim - those have sought out the right course.
Page-526
Summary:
9.1              TALB:     is a common word. To demand something. To desire, to find  .
9.2              IBTIGHA:     to try hard in seeking something  .
9.3              TAHASAS:     to use five senses in searching something which is related to outside conditions.
9.4              ILTAMASA: repeatedly try to search something  .
9.5              JAASA:     reaching an extreme in desire of something, greedily find out something
9.6              BASARA:     find out something by overturning  .
9.7              TAHARA:     to search for better and most appropriate  .

1-   ZIBAH KERNA   [To Slaughter]
Qur’an has referred them by the words     ZABAHA (ذبح ) ZAKAA (ذكى ) and NAHARA (نحر ).
1.1       ZABAHA (ذبح ):     Running knife at the throat of an animal by following renowned sharia method. And to expel “hararat-e-Gherazi”. It is mentioned in Qur’an:
Surat Al-Baqarah (The Cow) -     سورة البقرة     2:71
فَذَبَحُوْھَا وَمَا كَادُوْا يَفْعَلُوْنَ
So they slaughtered her, but they could hardly do it.
1.2 ZAKAA (زكى ):     to slaughter an animal in a manner that her life comes out quickly and comfortably. And means to read TAKBEER (تكبير ) on hunting animal and leave it. After that, slaughter it by following specific sharia method. Allah says:
Surat Al-Mā'idah (The Table Spread) - سورة المائدة 5:3
وَمَآ اَ كَلَ السَّبُعُ اِلَّا مَا ذَكَّيْتُمْ
And those from which a wild animal has eaten, except what you [are able to] slaughter [before its death].
1.3          NAHAR (نحر ):     means to strike on the chest, to slaughter. And NAHAR (نحر ) means upper part of chest and INTAHARA (انتحر ) means to attempt suicide. And YOUMALNAHR (انحر) means the day of sacrifice i.e. 10th date of ZILHAJ MONTH (ذي الحجة ). And NAHARA (نحر ) means to perform sacrifice or cut the throat or to contest. It means that the real meaning of NAHAR (نحر ) is to cut throat whether it is in the shape of slaughter or sacrifice. Whether it is done by knife or Burcha or the animal is cut in standing or lying.   It is mentioned in Qur’an:
Surat Al-Kawthar (The Abundance) -     سورة الكوثر      108:3
فَصَلِّ لِرَبِّكَ وَانْحَرْ
So pray to your Lord and sacrifice [to Him alone].
Summary:
1.1      ZABAHA:     to slaughter an animal by following renowned Sharia method.
1.2      ZAKAH:  to take care of animals comfort while performing sacrifice.
1.3      NAHARA:     Any way of cutting throat, whether it is sacrifice, slaughter or any other case.

2- ZERIA [Source]
Qur’an has referred them by the words     SABAB and “WASEELA”.
2.1         SABAB (سبب  ):     It is a rope by which we climb and descend from the palm tree: it is due to this association, anything which is used to get to other thing is called as SABAB (سبب  ) Then this word also applies to the path and the path-related equipment as well. Allah says:
Surat Al-Kahf     (The Cave) - سورة الكهف     18:84
فَاَتْبَعَ سَبَبًا وَاٰتَيْنٰهُ مِنْ كُلِّ شَيْءٍ سَبَبًا
And We gave him to everything a way. So he followed a way.
2.2         WASEELA (وسيلة ):     WASALA (وسل )means to reach a thing with allure. And WASAL-ILLALAH (الی اللہ وسل  ) means getting closer to Allah. And AL-WASTA (الواسطه ) and AL-WASEELA (الوسيله ) means source to get closer, status, level. Allah says
Surat Al-Mā'idah (The Table Spread) - سورة المائدة     5:35
وَابْتَغُوْٓا اِلَيْهِ الْوَسِيْلَةَ وَجَاهِدُوْا فِيْ سَبِيْلِهٖ
And seek the means [of nearness] to Him and strive in His cause.
Summary:
The word     SABAB (سبب  )     is common for     Source:     and the source which is opted to draw closer, it is     WASEELA (وسيلة ).

raw_text:
3- ZILLAT [Disgrace]
Qur’an has referred them by the words ZILLA (زلة ) SAGHAR (صغار ) KHIZI (خزي ) and HON (هون )
3.1         ZILLA (زلة ) :     means inferiority (antonym is superiority), weakness, to succumb to power and force. Allah says:
Surat 'Āli `Imrān (Family of Imran)   -   سورة آل عمران     3:112
ضُرِبَتْ عَلَيْهِمُ الذِّلَّةُ اَيْنَ مَا ثُـقِفُوْٓا
They have been put under humiliation [by Allah ] wherever they are overtaken.
3.2         SAGHAR (صغار ):     means the humiliation of becoming inferior after supremacy and its acceptance and acknowledgement. To accept the humiliation of becoming subdued after being ruler or independent.  Allah says
Surat Al-'An`ām (The Cattle) -     سورة الأنعام     6:135
ۭسَيُصِيْبُ الَّذِيْنَ اَجْرَمُوْا صَغَارٌ عِنْدَ اللّٰهِ
There will afflict those who committed crimes debasement before Allah.
3.3       KHIZI  (خزی):     means disgrace and shamefaced. Go down in the eyes of others because of evil deeds and if it is limited to oneself then it is called as Regret. Allah says
Surat Ţāhā (Ta-Ha)   -   سورة طه      20:134
لَقَالُوْا رَبَّنَا لَوْلَآ اَرْسَلْتَ اِلَيْنَا رَسُوْلًا فَنَتَّبِعَ اٰيٰتِكَ مِنْ قَبْلِ اَنْ نَّذِلَّ وَنَخْزٰى
They would have said, "Our Lord, why did You not send to us a messenger so we could have followed Your verses before we were humiliated and disgraced?"
Page-529
3.4         HON (  ھون ):   means insignificance, humiliation and disgrace, insult. It is in Qur’an
Surat An-Naĥl (The Bee) -     سورة النحل     16:59
يَتَوَارٰى مِنَ الْقَوْمِ مِنْ سُوْۗءِ مَا بُشِّرَ بِهٖ  ۭ اَيُمْسِكُهٗ عَلٰي هُوْنٍ اَمْ يَدُسُّهٗ فِي التُّرَابِ  ۭ
He hides himself from the people because of the ill of which he has been informed. Should he keep it in humiliation or bury it in the ground?
If HON (هون ) contains fatah on H then it means softness and this attribute is Mehmood. Just like Allah says while describing the qualities of true believers:
Surat Al-Furqān (The Criterian) -     سورة الفرقان     25:63
وَعِبَادُ الرَّحْمٰنِ الَّذِيْنَ يَمْشُوْنَ عَلَي الْاَرْضِ هَوْنًا ۭ
And the servants of the Most Merciful are those who walk upon the earth easily.
Summary:
3.1              ZILLA:     inferiority and weakness  .
3.2              SAGHAR:     humiliation of becoming inferior after supremacy and its acceptance and acknowledgement.
3.3              KIZI:     Go down in the eyes of people, disgrace.
3.4              HON:     Humiliation because of being inferior.

4- ZALEEL [Inferior]
Qur’an has referred them by the words     AZILLA (أذلة ) MAHEEN (مهين ) SAGHIRUN (صاغر ) DAKHIRUN (دآخر ) ARAZILLUN (أراذل ) ASFALLO (اسفل ) KHASI (خاسی )
4.1         AZILLA  (ازلة ):     Plural of ZALEEL (ذليل )     its antonym is IZAA (عزة ) which is the plural of AZEEZ (عزيز ) here we generally refer ZALEEL (ذليل ) as stingy or mean and we refer AZEEZ (عزيز ) as close relative. Both of these meanings are wrong by dictionary. In reality, ZALEEL (ذليل ) means one who is inferior and AZEEZ (عزيز ) means one who is superior. The concept of  ZALEEL (ذليل ) is literally incomplete without comparing it with the concept of AZEEZ (عزيز ) Qur’an has also used this word in same meaning:
Surat 'Āli `Imrān (Family of Imran)   -   سورة آل عمران     3:123
وَلَقَدْ نَصَرَكُمُ اللّٰهُ بِبَدْرٍ وَّاَنْتُمْ اَذِلَّةٌ
And already had Allah given you victory at [the battle of] Badr while you were few in number.
4.2         MAHEEN  (مهين ):     means been inferior, been weak and MAHEEN (مهين ) means small, not valued, disgraced and friendless. And according to Imam Raghib, MAHEEN (مهين )  is a person on which someone else is imposed and make him disgraced. It is in Qur’an
Surat Az-Zukhruf (The Ornaments of Gold) -     سورة الزخرف     43:52
اَمْ اَنَا خَيْرٌ مِّنْ ھٰذَا الَّذِيْ هُوَ مَهِيْنٌ
Or am I [not] better than this one who is insignificant?
Page-530
4.3         SAGHIR  ( صاغر ):   (it is opposite of KIBR (كبر ) )and SAGHAR (صغار ) means disgrace and SAGHIR SAGHIRUN (صاغر ) means someone with secondary status and the one who is forced to follow orders with derangement of superiority and the one who accept and acknowledge this. It is in Qur’an:
Surat At-Tawbah (The Repentance) -     سورة التوبة     9:29
حَتّٰي يُعْطُوا الْجِزْيَةَ عَنْ يَّدٍ وَّهُمْ صٰغِرُوْنَ
[fight] until they give the jizyah willingly while they are humbled.
4.4         DAKHIR  (داخر ):     DAKHARA (دخر) has three meanings i.e. Humbleness, Humiliation and Disrespectfulness. And DAKHIRA (دخر) means the one who accepts the humiliated obedience due to the lack of wisdom and understanding. It is in Qur’an
(Surat-Momin) (True Believer) -      سورة مومن     40:60
اِنَّ الَّذِيْنَ يَسْتَكْبِرُوْنَ عَنْ عِبَادَتِيْ سَيَدْخُلُوْنَ جَهَنَّمَ دٰخِرِيْنَ
Indeed, those who disdain My worship will enter Hell [rendered] contemptible.
At another occasion it is said:
Surat An-Naml (The Ant) -     سورة النمل     27:87
وَ يَوْمَ يُنْفَخُ فِي الصُّوْرِ فَفَزِعَ مَنْ فِي السَّمٰوٰتِ وَمَنْ فِي الْاَرْضِ اِلَّا مَنْ شَاۗءَ اللّٰهُ  ۭ وَكُلٌّ اَتَوْهُ دٰخِرِيْنَ
And [warn of] the Day the Horn will be blown, and whoever is in the heavens and whoever is on the earth will be terrified except whom Allah wills. And all will come to Him humbled.
4.5         ARAZAL  (ارآزل ):     Plural of ARZAL (ارذل )RAZAL (أراذل ) means able to be disrespectful, evil. And ARAZAL (أراذل ) means crap, faulty and trash. Those low class people to whom other people do not get closer due to their low class.  It is in Qur’an
Surat Hūd (Hud)   -   سورة هود     11:27
وَمَا نَرٰىكَ اتَّبَعَكَ اِلَّا الَّذِيْنَ هُمْ اَرَاذِلُـنَا بَادِيَ الرَّاْيِ
And we do not see you followed except by those who are the lowest of us [and] at first suggestion.
4.6         ASFAL (اسفل ):     ASAFLA (اسفلتہ ) means mean people such as DOON (دون ) and ASFAL (اسفل ) means low and worthless .  It is in Qur’an
(Surat-Ham-m-Sajda) (H-m Sajda)     سورة حم السجدہ     41:29
نَجْعَلْهُمَا تَحْتَ اَقْدَامِنَا لِيَكُوْنَا مِنَ الْاَسْفَلِيْنَ
We may put them under our feet that they will be among the lowest.
4.7         KHASI  (خاسی ):     KHASAA (خسا ) means tiredness and weakness of eye and KHASI MAN-AL KHANAZEER AND ALKALAAB (خاسی من الخنازیروالکلاب )means scolded dogs and pigs who are not allowed to come close to people .  Allah says:
Surat Al-Baqarah (The Cow) -     سورة البقرة     2:65
وَلَقَدْ عَلِمْتُمُ الَّذِيْنَ اعْتَدَوْا مِنْكُمْ فِى السَّبْتِ فَقُلْنَا لَھُمْ كُوْنُوْا قِرَدَةً خٰسِـــِٕيْنَ
And you had already known about those who transgressed among you concerning the sabbath, and We said to them, "Be apes, despised."
Summary:
4.1              ZALEEL:     antonym of AZEEZ (عزيز ) means Great.
4.2              MAHEEN: ZALEEL:      who has fallen from people’s eyes because of his evil deeds .
Page-531
4.3              SAGHIR:     who has fallen from superiority and become subordinate and who accepts it  .
4.4              DAKHIR:     a subordinate due to the lack of wisdom. Disgraced and incapable.
4.5              ARZAL:     disgraced, mean, of low cast, not to be loved, who is low in all aspects.
4.6              ASFAL: low and worthless as compared to superior  .
4.7              KHASI:     Scolded or most disgraced.

  وَ يَوْمَ يُنْفَخُ فِي الصُّوْرِ فَفَزِعَ مَنْ فِي السَّمٰوٰتِ وَمَنْ فِي الْاَرْضِ اِلَّا مَنْ شَاۗءَ اللّٰهُ  ۭ وَكُلٌّ اَتَوْهُ دٰخِرِيْنَ

And [warn of] the Day the Horn will be blown, and whoever is in the heavens and whoever is on the earth will be terrified except whom Allah wills. And all will come to Him humbled.

 

4.5   ARAZAL  (ارآزل ): Plural of ARZAL (ارذل )RAZAL (أراذل ) means able to be disrespectful, evil. And ARAZAL (أراذل ) means crap, faulty and trash. Those low class people to whom other people do not get closer due to their low class.  It is in Qur’an

 

Surat Hūd (Hud) - سورة هود 11:27

 وَمَا نَرٰىكَ اتَّبَعَكَ اِلَّا الَّذِيْنَ هُمْ اَرَاذِلُـنَا بَادِيَ الرَّاْيِ           

 And we do not see you followed except by those who are the lowest of us [and] at first suggestion.

 

4.6   ASFAL (اسفل ): ASAFLA (اسفلتہ ) means mean people such as DOON (دون ) and ASFAL (اسفل ) means low and worthless .  It is in Qur’an

 

(Surat-Ham-m-Sajda) (H-m Sajda) سورة حم السجدہ 41:29

  نَجْعَلْهُمَا تَحْتَ اَقْدَامِنَا لِيَكُوْنَا مِنَ الْاَسْفَلِيْنَ                   

  We may put them under our feet that they will be among the lowest.

4.7   KHASI  (خاسی ): KHASAA (خسا ) means tiredness and weakness of eye and KHASI MAN-AL KHANAZEER AND ALKALAAB (خاسی من الخنازیروالکلاب )means scolded dogs and pigs who are not allowed to come close to people .  Allah says:

 

Surat Al-Baqarah (The Cow) - سورة البقرة 2:65

  وَلَقَدْ عَلِمْتُمُ الَّذِيْنَ اعْتَدَوْا مِنْكُمْ فِى السَّبْتِ فَقُلْنَا لَھُمْ كُوْنُوْا قِرَدَةً خٰسِـــِٕيْنَ                    

 And you had already known about those who transgressed among you concerning the sabbath, and We said to them, "Be apes, despised."

 

 

Summary:

4.1          ZALEEL: antonym of AZEEZ (عزيز ) means Great.

4.2          MAHEEN: ZALEEL:  who has fallen from people’s eyes because of his evil deeds .

 

Page-531

4.3          SAGHIR: who has fallen from superiority and become subordinate and who accepts it.

4.4          DAKHIR: a subordinate due to the lack of wisdom. Disgraced and incapable.

4.5          ARZAL: disgraced, mean, of low cast, not to be loved, who is low in all aspects.

4.6          ASFAL: low and worthless as compared to superior.

4.7          KHASI: Scolded or most disgraced.

raw_text:
5- ZALEEL KERNA [To Humiliate]
Qur’an has referred them by the words     AZALLA (أذل ) AHAANA (أهان ) AKHZA (أخزى ) FAZAHA (فضح ) AZDARAA (اذدری ) and KAYATA (كبت ).
5.1         AZALLA (  أذلة   ): (Opposite of AAZA (اعز)) to make someone superior/Great and there is a strong aspect of being under someone and only a superior can make an insignificant/low, powerless: Allah says
Surat 'Āli `Imrān (Family of Imran)   -   سورة آل عمران     3:26
وَتُعِزُّ مَنْ تَشَاۗءُ وَتُذِلُّ مَنْ تَشَاۗءُ
You honor whom You will and You humble whom You will.
5.2         AAHAANA (اهان ):     consider someone low or weak or make someone low or weak because of hatred and insult him and this can be done by the person of same class or equality and as well as superior. Allah says:
Surat Al-Ĥaj (The Pilgrimage) - سورة الحج     22:18
وَمَنْ يُّهِنِ اللّٰهُ فَمَا لَهٗ مِنْ مُّكْرِمٍ
And he whom Allah humiliates - for him there is no bestower of honour.
5.3         AKHZA  (أخزى ):     to make humiliated and disgraced which is because of man’s own evil deeds and people know them. It is in Qur’an:
Surat 'Āli `Imrān (Family of Imran)   -   سورة آل عمران     3:194
وَلَا تُخْزِنَا يَوْمَ الْقِيٰمَةِ
And do not disgrace us on the Day of Resurrection.
5.4         FATHAHA   (  فظح ):     to describe someone's defects. To make him fall in others eyes. To make him disgraced before others. It is in Qur’an
Surat Al-Ĥijr (The Rocky Tract) -     سورة الحجر     15:68
قَالَ اِنَّ هٰٓؤُلَاۗءِ ضَيْفِيْ فَلَا تَفْضَحُوْنِ
[Lot] said, "Indeed, these are my guests, so do not shame me.
5.5         AZDARAA  (  ازدری ):   to consider someone worthless and contemptible. And AZDARAA (اذدری ) the person who is so much worthless that cannot be counted.   It is in Qur’an
Surat Hūd (Hud)   -   سورة هود     11:31
وَّلَآ اَقُوْلُ لِلَّذِيْنَ تَزْدَرِيْٓ اَعْيُنُكُمْ لَنْ يُّؤْتِيَهُمُ اللّٰهُ خَيْرًا
Nor do I say of those upon whom your eyes look down that Allah will never grant them any good.
Page-532
5.6         KABATA  (  کبت ):     means to return with severity, humiliation, and means to humiliate, to return, to turn, to reject with anger, to kill. This word is used to humiliate and disgrace in the state of anger.  It is in Qur’an
Surat Al-Mujādila (The Pleading Woman) -     سورة المجادلة     58:5
اِنَّ الَّذِيْنَ يُحَاۗدُّوْنَ اللّٰهَ وَرَسُوْلَهٗ كُبِتُوْا كَـمَا كُبِتَ الَّذِيْنَ مِنْ قَبْلِهِمْ
Indeed, those who oppose Allah and His Messenger are abased as those before them were abased.
Summary:
5.1              AZALA:     When superior makes the low one under him or disgrace him.
5.2              AHAAN:      To insult due to hatred, humiliate and disgrace. This can be done by the person of equal class.
5.3              AKHZA:     To humiliate someone because of his apparent defects  .
5.4              FATHAHA:     To make someone fall in others eyes by quoting his evil deeds.
5.5              RADI:     To assume someone very low or cheap.
5.6              KABAT: To humiliate and disgrace someone in the state of anger.

raw_text:
6- ZIMADARI [Responsibility]
Qur’an has referred them by the words     ZIMA (ذمة ) and NAHAB (نحب ).
6.1         ZIMA (  زمة ):     means a form of promise, loyalty commitment, protection, security, responsibility, promise of commitment: such as “You are in refuge of Allah”. They are non-Muslims who, on the basis of promise and commitment lives with safety and protection in Islamic circle by giving capitation to Muslims. Sometimes this word is used for promise and commitment and to fulfil its responsibility. Allah says
Surat At-Tawbah (The Repentance) -     سورة التوبة     9:10
لَا يَرْقُبُوْنَ فِيْ مُؤْمِنٍ اِلًّا وَّلَا ذِمَّةً  ۭ
They do not observe toward a believer any pact of kinship or covenant of protection.
6.2         NAHAB   (نحب ):   it is the nazr that must be completed and as an obligation and  NAHAB –R-RAJUL (نحب ارجل) means man has taken up a thing as obligatory on his life. Hence NAHAB (نحب ) is that responsibility which a person has taken up on his life as essential whether it is a responsibility of nazr or promise.  Allah says:
Surat Al-'Aĥzāb (The Combined Forces) - سورة الأحزاب     23:33
فَمِنْهُمْ مَّنْ قَضٰى نَحْبَهٗ وَمِنْهُمْ مَّنْ يَّنْتَظِرُ ڮ
Among them is he who has fulfilled his vow [to the death], and among them is he who awaits [his chance].
Summary:
6.1              Zima  : The responsibility to fulfil the promise and commitment with the other.
6.2              NAHAB (نحب )   is the fulfilling of responsibility that is taken up on oneself as essential.

raw_text:
1 FAIDA, FAIDA DENA
[Benefit, to benefit someone]
Synonyms: NAFA’(  نفع  ), MATTA’(  مَتَـٰعٌ  ), RABIHAH(  ربح  ), MA’ARIB(  مآرب  )
1.1 nafa’(  نفع  )  : meaning a good thing or to get its part, to benefit. Its antonym is zarar(  ضرر  ) which means difficulty, disadvantage. Its use is common. As Allah states that:
________________
Surat Al-Rad (The thunder) -   سُوۡرَةُ الرّعد
13:16
قُلۡ أَفَٱتَّخَذۡتُم مِّن دُونِهِۦۤ أَوۡلِيَآءَ لَا يَمۡلِكُونَ لِأَنفُسِهِمۡ نَفۡعً۬ا وَلَا ضَرًّ۬ا‌ۚ
Say (O Muhammad): Who is Lord of the heavens and the earth? Say: Allah.   Say: Take ye then (others) beside Him for protectors, which, even for themselves, have neither benefit nor hurt?   Say: Is the blind man equal to the seer, or is darkness equal to light? Or assign they unto Allah partners who created the like of His creation so that the creation (which they made and His creation) seemed alike to them? Say: Allah is the Creator of all things, and He is the One, the Almighty.
________________
1.2 matta’ (  مَتَـٰعٌ  )  : mataa’(  متاع  ) meaning all those things from the items of use that a person or any living being benefits from to keep itself alive. And matta’(  متع  ) means to benefit from any such items. Allah states that:
________________
Surat An-Naziat (Soul-Snatchers) -   سُوۡرَةُ النَّازعَات
79:31-33
أَخۡرَجَ مِنۡہَا مَآءَهَا وَمَرۡعَٮٰهَا وَٱلۡجِبَالَ أَرۡسَٮٰهَا مَتَـٰعً۬ا لَّكُمۡ وَلِأَنۡعَـٰمِكُمۡ
And produced therefrom the water thereof and the pasture thereof, (31) And He made fast the hills, (32) A provision for you and for your cattle.
________________
And matta’(  متع  ) means to give such things to someone so that he may benefit from them, to benefit someone. Allah states that:
________________
Surat Al-Baqarah (The Cow) -   سُوۡرَةُ البَقَرَة
2:236
وَمَتِّعُوهُنَّ عَلَى ٱلۡمُوسِعِ قَدَرُهُ ۥ وَعَلَى ٱلۡمُقۡتِرِ قَدَرُهُ ۥ
It is no sin for you if ye divorce women while yet ye have not touched them, nor appointed unto them a portion.   Provide for them, the rich according to his means, and the straitened according to his means, a fair provision.   (This is) a bounden duty for those who do good.
________________
And tamatta’(  تمتع  ) means to benefit one’s own self, to enjoy. As is stated:
________________
Surat Hud  -   سُوۡرَةُ هُود
11:65
تَمَتَّعُواْ فِى دَارِڪُمۡ ثَلَـٰثَةَ أَيَّامٍ۬‌ۖ
But they hamstrung her, and then he said:   enjoy life in your dwelling-place three days  ! This is a threat that will not be belied.
________________
1.3 rabihah (  ربح  )  : that gain which is achieved from buying and selling, to profit in trade merchandise. And its antonym is khasir(  خسر  ).  Allah states that:
________________
Surat Al-Baqarah (The Cow) -   سُوۡرَةُ البَقَرَة
2:16
فَمَا رَبِحَت تِّجَـٰرَتُهُمۡ وَمَا كَانُواْ مُهۡتَدِينَ
These are they who purchase error at the price of guidance,   so their commerce doth not prosper, neither are they guided.
________________
1.4 ma’arib(  مآرب  )  : arab(  ارب  ) meaning intense requirement without which one cannot manage and you strive to achieve it; meaning requirement, need, extreme, and ma’arib(  مآرب  ), maariba(  مآربة  ), maaraba(  مآربه  ), maaruba(  مآربة  ) meaning requirement and its fulfillment. And its plural is maarib(  مارب  ). And that thing also through which this requirement is fulfilled. Allah states that:
________________
Surat Ta-Ha  -   سُوۡرَةُ طٰه
20:18
قَالَ هِىَ عَصَاىَ أَتَوَڪَّؤُاْ عَلَيۡہَا وَأَهُشُّ بِہَا عَلَىٰ غَنَمِى وَلِىَ فِيہَا مَـَٔارِبُ أُخۡرَىٰ
He said: This is my staff whereon I lean, and wherewith I beat down branches for my sheep, and wherein I find other uses.
________________
Summary:
1.NAFA’(  نفع  ): common word, to receive a part from something beneficial, its antonym is zarar.
2. MATTA’A  (  مَتَـٰعٌ  ):  to benefit from items of use.
3. RABIHAH(  ربح  ): to benefit from trade merchandise.
4. MAARIB(  مآرب  ): needs and ways of its fulfillment.

1.4 ma’arib(مآرب): arab(ارب) meaning intense requirement without which one cannot manage and you strive to achieve it; meaning requirement, need, extreme, and ma’arib(مآرب), maariba(مآربة), maaraba(مآربه), maaruba(مآربة) meaning requirement and its fulfillment. And its plural is maarib(مارب). And that thing also through which this requirement is fulfilled. Allah states that:    

________________

Surat Ta-Ha  - سُوۡرَةُ طٰه

20:18

قَالَ هِىَ عَصَاىَ أَتَوَڪَّؤُاْ عَلَيۡہَا وَأَهُشُّ بِہَا عَلَىٰ غَنَمِى وَلِىَ فِيہَا مَـَٔارِبُ أُخۡرَىٰ

He said: This is my staff whereon I lean, and wherewith I beat down branches for my sheep, and wherein I find other uses.

________________

Summary:

1.NAFA’(نفع): common word, to receive a part from something beneficial, its antonym is zarar.

2. MATTA’A(مَتَـٰعٌ):  to benefit from items of use.

3. RABIHAH(ربح): to benefit from trade merchandise.

4. MAARIB(مآرب): needs and ways of its fulfillment.

title: content/f/f10.html
raw_text:
10- FASAAD KARNA - DALNA [Causing corruption - Making Violence]
The Qur’an has referred to it by the words     AFSADA (أفسد) ‘ATHA or ‘AATH (عثایاعاث) and NAZA’ (نزع).
10.1        AFSADA (أفسد):     FASADA (فسد ) means the deterioration of something, decaying and AFSADA (أفسد) means to deteriorate something and decay it. FASAAD (فساد ) is the antonym of ISLAH (اصلاح ). The word FASAAD (فساد ) is used in both physical and spiritual sense. Allah Said:
Surat Al-'A`rāf (The Heights) - سورة الأعراف     7:56
وَلَا تُفْسِدُوْا فِي الْاَرْضِ بَعْدَ اِصْلَاحِهَا
And cause not corruption upon the earth after its reformation.
Page-667
10.2  ASA or AAS (عثایاعاث):     It is in Quran:
Surat Al-Baqarah (The Cow) - سورة البقرة 2:60
وَلَا تَعْثَوْا فِى الْاَرْضِ مُفْسِدِيْنَ
And do not commit abuse on the earth, spreading corruption.
TA’THAWA (تعثوا ) substance is written as (ع ث ی ) by some glossaries, and means ATHA, YA’THA, ‘ATHIYA (عثی یعثی عثیا ) and it denotes mental and intellectual deterioration. For example, the promotion of wrong beliefs and ideologies by using literature or speeches. And some have written its substance as ع ی ث. ‘AATHA, YA’EETHA, ‘ATHYA (عاث یعیث عثیا) that advocates deterioration of sensory or material things, such as abusing or doing injustice to someone. The note section in both cases is always LA TA’THAWA (لاتعثوا ).
10.3           NAZA’ (نزع):     means to cast violence between two things, to create a dispute, to persuade in favour of violence, to create disorder, to make a quarrel, to create rivalry and means to deteriorate work and interfere in, or create violence. It is mentioned in the Qur’an:
Surat Yūsuf (Joseph) - سورة يوسف      12:100
مِّنَ الْبَدْوِ مِنْۢ بَعْدِ اَنْ نَّزَغَ الشَّيْطٰنُ بَيْنِيْ وَبَيْنَ اِخْوَتِيْ
After Satan had induced [estrangement] between me and my brothers.
Summary:
10.1ANSADA can be applied for creating estrangement, and once violence takes the form of habit then ‘AATHA or ATHAA will be used. And the reality of NAZAGHA is to interfere whether it is in one or more thing. Then cast estrangement among them.

raw_text:
11- FAZOOL BATAIN KARNA [Involved in idle talk]
Qur’an has referred to it the words     ALGHA (الغی) KHAAD (خاض) FIQA (فکہ) SAMARA (سمر) AND HAJR (ھجر).
11.1        ALGHA (الغی):     LAGHA (لغا ) means to talk without thinking, malicious talk, and means the chirping of birds and similarly, anything mentioned repeatedly. And ALGHA (الغی) means to blabber or babble in such a way that the voice of the addressed person is drowned from its noise so that other people also cannot hear it. It is in Qur’an:
(Surat-Ham-m-Sajda) (H-m Sajda) سورة حم السجدہ     41:26
وَقَالَ الَّذِيْنَ كَفَرُوْا لَا تَسْمَعُوْا لِھٰذَا الْقُرْاٰنِ وَالْـغَوْا فِيْهِ لَعَلَّكُمْ تَغْلِبُوْنَ
And those who disbelieve say, "Do not listen to this Qur'an and speak noisily during [the recitation of] it that perhaps you will overcome."
11.2        KHAAD (خاض):     means to impact. KHAADA FI AL-MAA’ (خاض فی الماء) means to impact water. KHAAD FIL-HADEETH (خاض فی الحدیث ) to engage in talks and interfere in the middle of something. Means to be fully involved in talking or working. It is mostly used in the Qur’an for doing idle work or talk. Allah says:
Surat Al-'An`ām (The Cattle) - سورة الأنعام     6:68
وَاِذَا رَاَيْتَ الَّذِيْنَ يَخُوْضُوْنَ فِيْٓ اٰيٰتِنَا فَاَعْرِضْ عَنْهُمْ حَتّٰي يَخُوْضُوْا فِيْ حَدِيْثٍ غَيْرِهٖ
And when you see those who engage in [offensive] discourse concerning Our verses, then turn away from them until they enter into another conversion.
Page-668
11.3        FIQA (فکہ):     means to engage in laughter, laugh or to make laugh. And FIQAHA (فکاھ ) means jesting and TAFKAHA BA’RAD FULAAN (تفکھ بعرض فلان) means to enjoy backbiting someone. To get pleasure from talking. It is in the Qur’an:
Surat Al-Muţaffifīn (The Defrauding) - سورة المطففين     83:31
وَاِذَا انْقَلَبُوْٓا اِلٰٓى اَهْلِهِمُ انْقَلَبُوْا فَكِهِيْنَ
And when they returned to their people, they would return jesting.
11.4        SAMARA (سمر):     To describe tales and stories before going to sleep at night. The talks before going to sleep. The story telling.
11.5     HAJAR (ھجر):     YAHJARA (یهجر ) to do malicious talks, to talk rubbish. HAJAR (ھجر ) means inappropriate talk, bad conversation, talking nonsense, rave in sleep or due to disease. Allah Said:
Surat Al-Mu'minūn (The Believers) - سورة المؤمنون 23:67
مُسْتَكْبِرِيْنَ ڰ بِهٖ سٰمِرًا تَهْجُرُوْنَ
In arrogance regarding it, conversing by night, speaking evil.
Summary:
11.1 ALGHA: To blabber in such a way that the voice of others cannot be heard.
11.2 KHAADA: To be engaged in some malicious talk.
11.3 FIQA: Such type of laughter and jesting that gives pleasure. Jesting.
11.4 SAMARA: To describe tales and stories before going to sleep at night.
11.5 HAJAR: To rave in sleep or in disease. To talk rubbish.

title: content/f/f12.html
raw_text:
12- FAZOOL KHARCHI KARNA [Spending extravagantly]
Qur’an has referred to it by the words ASRAFA (اسرف) and BADHARA (بذر).
12.1     ASRAFA (اسرف):     SARAFA (سرف) and ASRAFA (اسرف) means to go beyond moderate limits and its use is common for spending more than required in wealth or material things. And moderation limit is only for those things that are permitted and AMR MUBAH (امر مباح). Hence the meaning of extravagance is spending more than needed in permitted things. Allah Said:
Surat Al-'A`rāf (The Heights) - سورة الأعراف     7:31
وَّكُلُوْا وَاشْرَبُوْا وَلَا تُسْرِفُوْا
Eat and drink, but be not excessive.
12.2     BADHARA (بذر):      BADHARA (بذر) and BAZAR (بزر) means seed and BADHARA (بذر) means to spread seeds, so the way seeds are spread on the ground, if wealth is also spread like this then it is called TABZEER (تبزیر). Hence whether the need is permitted or not, excessive spending of wealth is called TABZEER (تبزیر) and it is a worse action than ASRAFA (اسرف).
Page-669
Allah Said:
(Surat-Bani Isra’eel) (Children of Israel) سورة بنی اسراءیل     17:26-27
اِنَّ الْمُبَذِّرِيْنَ كَانُوْٓا اِخْوَانَ الشَّيٰطِيْنِ وَلَا تُبَذِّرْ تَبْذِيْرًا
And do not spend wastefully. Indeed, the wasteful are brothers of the devils.
Summary:
ASRAAF is used for excessive spending on permitted things and TABZEER is used for excessive spending of wealth on both, permitted and  non-permitted things (nut commonly for non-permitted things).

raw_text:
13- FAZEELAT DENA - (BUZURGI DENA) [To Give Preference ()]
The Qur’an has referred to it by the words     FADALA (فضل) and KARAMA (کرم).
13.1     FADALA (فضل):     FADAL (فضل ) means according/financing some good works beyond moderate means. And FADALA (فضل) means for the sake of giving favour, endowing someone with goodness more than he is privileged to. Allah Said:
Surat Al-Baqarah (The Cow) - سورة البقرة     2:122
يٰبَنِىْٓ اِسْرَاۗءِيْلَ اذْكُرُوْا نِعْمَتِىَ الَّتِىْٓ اَنْعَمْتُ عَلَيْكُمْ وَاَنِّىْ فَضَّلْتُكُمْ عَلَي الْعٰلَمِيْنَ
O Children of Israel, remember My favor which I have bestowed upon you and that I preferred you over the worlds.
13.2     KARAMA (کرم):     KARAM (کرم) is a type of honour that is present in oneself due to his (good) conduct. And KARAMA (کرم) means to install the attributes of honour in someone. Allah Said:
(Surat-BaniIsrael) (Children of Israel) سورة بنی اسراءیل     17:70
وَلَقَدْ كَرَّمْنَا بَنِيْٓ اٰدَمَ وَحَمَلْنٰهُمْ فِي الْبَرِّ وَالْبَحْرِ
And We have certainly honoured the children of Adam and carried them on the land and sea.

title: content/f/f14.html
raw_text:
14- FAISLA KERNA [To Decide]
The Qur’an has to it by the words FATAHA (فتح) FASALA (فصل) HAKAMA (حکم) QADA (قضی) HATAMA (حتم).
14.1     FATAHA (فتح)  : means to remove the closure or complication from something. Antonym is IGHLAAQ (اغلاق) meaning to give victory and to decide. Those decision that differentiates between right and wrong and where the complication is removed and no party has any doubts. Allah Said:
Surat Al-'A`rāf (The Heights) - سورة الأعراف     7:89
رَبَّنَا افْتَحْ بَيْنَنَا وَبَيْنَ قَوْمِنَا بِالْحَقِّ
Our Lord, decide between us and our people in truth.
14.2     FASALA (فصل):     means to differentiate one thing from the other and the act of moving away from it. Hence FASAL (فصل) is AKHAS (اخص ) in comparison with FATAHA (فتح). Only distinction is found in FATAHA (فتح) but ‘distinction’ and ‘separation’ are both found (in FASALA).This distinction and separation can be found in the same thing as well, such as a book. Similarly at times, FATAHA (فتح) is related to one thing and sometimes, with many things.
Page-670
Allah Said:
Surat Al-Mursalāt (The Emissaries) - سورة المرسلات     77:38
هٰذَا يَوْمُ الْفَصْلِ ۚ جَمَعْنٰكُمْ وَالْاَوَّلِيْنَ
This is the Day of Judgement; We will have assembled you and the former peoples.
14.3     HAKAMA (حکم):     means MANA’ ‘AN-ADHLAM( منع عن اظلم), a decision in which injustice is prevented. And means a command to stop fighting and quarrelling.  It is in Qur’an:
Surat Al-'Anbyā' (The Prophets) - سورة الأنبياء     21:78
وَدَاوٗدَ وَسُلَيْمٰنَ اِذْ يَحْكُمٰنِ فِي الْحَرْثِ
And [mention] David and Solomon, when they judged concerning the field.
14.4     QADA (قضی):     YAQDI (یقضی) QADYA (قضیا) WAQADAA (وقضا) and WAQADI’ (وقضئ) means to: 1) do and complete some work, and: 2) give a final (lasting) ruling among parties, and QADA (قضی) is be used in judgement when power is available to impose that ruling. QADHI (قاضی) is a renowned word. Allah Said:
Surat An-Nisā' (The Women) - سورة النساء     4:65
فَلَا وَرَبِّكَ لَا يُؤْمِنُوْنَ حَتّٰي يُحَكِّمُوْكَ فِيْمَا شَجَــرَ بَيْنَھُمْ ثُمَّ لَا يَجِدُوْا فِيْٓ اَنْفُسِهِمْ حَرَجًا مِّمَّا قَضَيْتَ
But no, by your Lord, they will not [truly] believe until they make you, [O Muhammad], judge concerning that over which they dispute among themselves and then find within themselves no discomfort from what you have judged.
14.5     HATAMA (حتم):   means to decide, to make strong, to give ruling about something, to make obligatory. And HAATIM (حاتم) means ruler. It is said HATAM AL-HAATIM KADHA (حتم الحاتم کذا) i.e. the ruler has given a ruling for this. And HADHA WALAD HATAM (ھاذا ولد حتم) means this is a boy and there is no doubt of his origin (i.e. lineage). AND HATAMA (حتم) means QADHAA WA QADR (قضا و قدر). Surat Maryam (Mary) - سورة مريم     19:71
وَاِنْ مِّنْكُمْ اِلَّا وَارِدُهَا  ۚ كَانَ عَلٰي رَبِّكَ حَتْمًا مَّقْضِيًّا
And there is none of you except he will come to it. This is upon your Lord an inevitability decreed.
Summary:
14.1           FATAH:     To make AGHLAAQ away and give a clear decision about a thing.
14.2           FASAL:  (Making) distinction and separation.
14.3           HAKAM:     Such a ruling that prevents oppression  .
14.4               QADAA:     A final ruling given from a person who has the power to impose it.

14- FAISLA KERNA [To Decide]

 

The Qur’an has to it by the words FATAHA (فتح) FASALA (فصل) HAKAMA (حکم) QADA (قضی) HATAMA (حتم).

 

 

14.1 FATAHA (فتح): means to remove the closure or complication from something. Antonym is IGHLAAQ (اغلاق) meaning to give victory and to decide. Those decision that differentiates between right and wrong and where the complication is removed and no party has any doubts. Allah Said:

Surat Al-'A`rāf (The Heights) - سورة الأعراف 7:89

 رَبَّنَا افْتَحْ بَيْنَنَا وَبَيْنَ قَوْمِنَا بِالْحَقِّ  

 Our Lord, decide between us and our people in truth.

14.2 FASALA (فصل): means to differentiate one thing from the other and the act of moving away from it. Hence FASAL (فصل) is AKHAS (اخص ) in comparison with FATAHA (فتح). Only distinction is found in FATAHA (فتح) but ‘distinction’ and ‘separation’ are both found (in FASALA).This distinction and separation can be found in the same thing as well, such as a book. Similarly at times, FATAHA (فتح) is related to one thing and sometimes, with many things.

           Page-670

 

  Allah Said:

Surat Al-Mursalāt (The Emissaries) - سورة المرسلات 77:38

 هٰذَا يَوْمُ الْفَصْلِ ۚ جَمَعْنٰكُمْ وَالْاَوَّلِيْنَ

This is the Day of Judgement; We will have assembled you and the former peoples.

14.3 HAKAMA (حکم): means MANA’ ‘AN-ADHLAM( منع عن اظلم), a decision in which injustice is prevented. And means a command to stop fighting and quarrelling.  It is in Qur’an:

Surat Al-'Anbyā' (The Prophets) - سورة الأنبياء 21:78

   وَدَاوٗدَ وَسُلَيْمٰنَ اِذْ يَحْكُمٰنِ فِي الْحَرْثِ

 And [mention] David and Solomon, when they judged concerning the field.

14.4 QADA (قضی): YAQDI (یقضی) QADYA (قضیا) WAQADAA (وقضا) and WAQADI’ (وقضئ) means to: 1) do and complete some work, and: 2) give a final (lasting) ruling among parties, and QADA (قضی) is be used in judgement when power is available to impose that ruling. QADHI (قاضی) is a renowned word. Allah Said:

 

Surat An-Nisā' (The Women) - سورة النساء 4:65

فَلَا وَرَبِّكَ لَا يُؤْمِنُوْنَ حَتّٰي يُحَكِّمُوْكَ فِيْمَا شَجَــرَ بَيْنَھُمْ ثُمَّ لَا يَجِدُوْا فِيْٓ اَنْفُسِهِمْ حَرَجًا مِّمَّا قَضَيْتَ           

But no, by your Lord, they will not [truly] believe until they make you, [O Muhammad], judge concerning that over which they dispute among themselves and then find within themselves no discomfort from what you have judged.

14.5 HATAMA (حتم): means to decide, to make strong, to give ruling about something, to make obligatory. And HAATIM (حاتم) means ruler. It is said HATAM AL-HAATIM KADHA (حتم الحاتم کذا) i.e. the ruler has given a ruling for this. And HADHA WALAD HATAM (ھاذا ولد حتم) means this is a boy and there is no doubt of his origin (i.e. lineage). AND HATAMA (حتم) means QADHAA WA QADR (قضا و قدر). Hence HATAM (حتم) is a decision that is lasting and irrevocable. It is in Qur’an:

Surat Maryam (Mary) - سورة مريم 19:71

  وَاِنْ مِّنْكُمْ اِلَّا وَارِدُهَا  ۚ كَانَ عَلٰي رَبِّكَ حَتْمًا مَّقْضِيًّا    

And there is none of you except he will come to it. This is upon your Lord an inevitability decreed.

 

Summary:

14.1       FATAH: To make AGHLAAQ away and give a clear decision about a thing.

14.2       FASAL:  (Making) distinction and separation.

14.3       HAKAM: Such a ruling that prevents oppression.

14.4           QADAA: A final ruling given from a person who has the power to impose it.

14.5           HATAM: Absolute and irrevocable ruling. The decision by Allah.

2 FATAH HONA, DENA
[to succeed, to let someone succeed]
Synonyms: FATAH(  فتح  ), AZFARA(  اظفر  )
2.1 fatah(  فتح  )  : meaning to remove complication and restraint from something. This word is used in meanings of opening, deciding and giving success (antonym: ighlaaq(  إغلاق  )). And when this word is used for being successful after competition with the enemy, then its meaning will be such an obvious and clear decision after which the enemy can have no doubts about its defeat. Allah states that:
________________
Surat An-Nasar (The Help) -   سُوۡرَةُ النّصر
110:1-2
إِذَا جَآءَ نَصۡرُ ٱللَّهِ وَٱلۡفَتۡحُ وَرَأَيۡتَ ٱلنَّاسَ يَدۡخُلُونَ فِى دِينِ ٱللَّهِ أَفۡوَاجً۬ا
When Allah's succour and the triumph cometh (1) And thou seest mankind entering the religion of Allah in troops
________________
2.2 azfara (  اظفر  )  : zafar(  ظفر  ) meaning the nails of humans or animals. And zafar falaan(  ظفرفلان  ) meaning that someone shoved their nails into something or succeeded. And azfara(  اظفر  ) means to achieve such success, that the enemy gets thrusted in the chest with nails meaning success and then dominating the enemy. As is said in the words of Ibn-alFaris:   يدل علي القهر و الفوز و الغلبة   Allah states that:
________________
Surat Al-Fath (Victory) -   سُوۡرَةُ الفَتْح
48:24
وَهُوَ ٱلَّذِى كَفَّ أَيۡدِيَهُمۡ عَنكُمۡ وَأَيۡدِيَكُمۡ عَنۡہُم بِبَطۡنِ مَكَّةَ مِنۢ بَعۡدِ أَنۡ أَظۡفَرَكُمۡ عَلَيۡهِمۡ‌ۚ
And He it is Who hath withheld men's hands from you, and hath withheld your hands from them, in the valley of Mecca, after He had made you victors over them  . Allah is Seer of what ye do.
________________
Summary:
The word fatah(  فتح  ) is used only for prevalence whereas azfara(  اظفر  ) includes dominance over enemy after success.
‘FAKHAR KERNA’ – see ‘itrana’

3 FRAKHI, ASOODAGI
[ampleness, complacence]
Synonyms: MAISRA(  ميسرة  ), TAUL(  طول  ), BASTA(  بسطة  ), SA’ATA(  سعتة  )
3.1 maisra(  ميسرة  )  : yusr(  يسر  ) meaning ease(antonym usr(  عسر  ) meaning difficuly) and maisra(  ميسرة  ) means times of ease, those times when a person can easily manage his daily activities financially. Allah states that:
________________
Surat Al-Baqarah (The Cow) -   سُوۡرَةُ البَقَرَة
2:280
وَإِن كَانَ ذُو عُسۡرَةٍ۬ فَنَظِرَةٌ إِلَىٰ مَيۡسَرَةٍ۬‌ۚ
And if the debtor is in straitened circumstances, then (let there be) postponement to (the time of) ease  ; and that ye remit the debt as almsgiving would be better for you if ye did not know.
________________
3.2 taul (  طول  )  : tool(  طول  ) meaning length, long and long periods of time. And the word taul(  طول  ) is used in the meaning of favor and kindness which is not temporary. And taul(  طول  ) also means expenditure of daily living, favor, kindness, generosity. As Allah states that:
________________
Surat Al-Nisa (Women) -   سُوۡرَةُ النِّسَاء
4:25
وَمَن لَّمۡ يَسۡتَطِعۡ مِنكُمۡ طَوۡلاً أَن يَنڪِحَ ٱلۡمُحۡصَنَـٰتِ ٱلۡمُؤۡمِنَـٰتِ
And whoso is not able to afford to marry free, believing women  , let them marry from the believing maids whom your right hands possess. Allah knoweth best (concerning) your faith. Ye (proceed) one from another; so wed them by permission of their folk, and give unto them their portions in kindness, they being honest, not debauched nor of loose conduct. And if when they are honourably married they commit lewdness they shall incur the half of the punishment (prescribed) for free women (in that case). This is for him among you who feareth to commit sin. But to have patience would be better for you. Allah is Forgiving, Merciful.
________________
And   اولوالطول   means those people who can easily manage their living.
________________
3.3 basta (  بسطة  )  : basat(  بسط  ) meaning to open and spread. And its antonym is qabaz(  قبض  ) and qadar(  قدر  ). Basata(  بسطة  ) means vastness (of space), ampleness and abundance although this ampleness may be in terms of money or anything else. This word is used in the literal and semantic meanings. Allah states that:
________________
Surat Al-Baqarah (The Cow) -   سُوۡرَةُ البَقَرَة
2:247
وَزَادَهُ ۥ بَسۡطَةً۬ فِى ٱلۡعِلۡمِ وَٱلۡجِسۡمِ‌ۖ
Their Prophet said unto them: Lo! Allah hath raised up Saul to be a king for you. They said: How can he have kingdom over us when we are more deserving of the kingdom than he is, since he hath not been given wealth enough? He said: Lo!   Allah hath chosen him above you, and hath increased him abundantly in wisdom and stature  . Allah bestoweth His Sovereignty on whom He will. Allah is All-Embracing, All-Knowing.
________________
at another place, it is stated:
________________
Surat Al-Ankaboot (The Spider) -   سُوۡرَةُ العَنکبوت
29:62
ٱللَّهُ يَبۡسُطُ ٱلرِّزۡقَ لِمَن يَشَآءُ مِنۡ عِبَادِهِۦ وَيَقۡدِرُ لَهُ ۥۤ‌ۚ
Allah maketh the provision wide for whom He will of His bondmen, and straiteneth it for whom (He will).   Lo! Allah is Aware of all things.
________________
3.4 sa’ata (  سعتة  )  : wasia’(  وسع  ) meaning to have some space and gap in something. And alwusu’(  الوسع  ) meaning abundance of sustenance. And the antonym of wusa’h(  وسع  ) is zeeq(  ضيق  ) and usr(  عسر  ). Sa’ata(  سعتة  ) is used for depicting abundance in sustenance. And   اولوالسعة   meaning those people who can not only manage their living easily and save some but are also in a position to give charity and donations. Allah states that:
________________
Surat Al-Noor (The Light) -   سُوۡرَةُ النُّور
24:22
وَلَا يَأۡتَلِ أُوْلُواْ ٱلۡفَضۡلِ مِنكُمۡ وَٱلسَّعَةِ أَن يُؤۡتُوٓاْ أُوْلِى ٱلۡقُرۡبَىٰ وَٱلۡمَسَـٰكِينَ
And let not those who possess dignity and ease among you swear not to give to the near of kin and to the needy  , and to fugitives for the cause of Allah. Let them forgive and show indulgence. Yearn ye not that Allah may forgive you? Allah is Forgiving, Merciful.
________________
Summary:
1.MAISRA(  ميسرة  ): to live easily after some difficulty
2. TAUL(  طول  ): self sustained of living
3. BASTA(  بسطة  ): abundance and ampleness in whatever thing they might be.
4. OOL-US-SA’A(  اولوالسعة  ): complacent people; those who can save some for themselves.

raw_text:
4- FARAAKH KARNA- HONA [To Open, be Opened]
Quran has referred to them with the words like     RAHABA (رحب) , WASI’ (وسع), TAFSUHU (تفسح).
4.1 RAHIBA (رحب) and RAHABA  (رحب):    mean wideness of space. It is only used for wideness of the space. The wideness of space or (of a) house, and its antonym is DHAAQA (ضاق). Allah Said:
Surat At-Tawbah (The Repentance) - سورة التوبة     9:25
وَّضَاقَتْ عَلَيْكُمُ الْاَرْضُ بِمَا رَحُبَتْ
And the earth was confining for you with its vastness.
And MARHAB (مرحب) word is used for pray. MARHABA (مرحبا) means welcome. And LA MARHABA (لامرحبا) is used as a curse (i.e. there is no capacity or space for you).
It is in Qur’an:
Surat Şād (The Letter "Saad") - سورة ص 38:59
لَا مَرْحَبًۢا بِهِمْ ۭ اِنَّهُمْ صَالُوا النَّارِ
No welcome for them. Indeed, they will burn in the Fire.
4.2 WASI’ (وسع)   is used for both space and condition. It means wideness, holding, capacity Allah Said:
Surat Al-Baqarah (The Cow) - سورة البقرة 2:255
وَسِعَ كُرْسِـيُّهُ السَّمٰوٰتِ وَالْاَرْضَ
His Kursi extends over the heavens and the earth.
And Allah Said:
Surat Al-Baqarah (The Cow) - سورة البقرة 2:286
لَا يُكَلِّفُ اللّٰهُ نَفْسًا اِلَّا وُسْعَهَا
Allah does not burden a soul except [what is within] its capacity.
And AWSA’ (اوسع) means to have much wealth. And AWSA’ AL-MAWDI’ (اوسع الموضع) means to make a space wide.
Allah Said:
Surat Adh-Dhāriyāt (The Winnowing Winds) - سورة الذاريات 51:47
وَالسَّمَاۗءَ بَنَيْنٰهَا بِاَيْىدٍ وَّاِنَّا لَمُوْسِعُوْنَ
And the heaven We constructed with strength, and indeed, We are [its] expander.
4.3 TAFSUHU (تفسح) in relation to FASAHA  (فسح):    means to take a wide step and FASAHA  (فسح) and TAFASAHA FAL-MAJLEES ( تفسح فلمجليس ) means to give space in gatherings, meaning to sit openly in a manner so that space is created for others. Allah Said:
Page-662
Surat Al-Mujādila (The Pleading Woman) - سورة المجادلة   58  :11
اِذَا قِيْلَ لَكُمْ تَفَسَّحُوْا فِي الْمَجٰلِسِ فَافْسَحُوْا يَفْسَحِ اللّٰهُ لَكُمْ
When you are told, "Space yourselves" in gatherings, then make space; Allah will make space for you.
Summary:
4.1      RAHIBA:     only for the openness of space.
4.2      WASI’: holding or capacity  .
AWSA’:     To make widening space  .
