4- FARAAKH KARNA- HONA [To Open, be Opened]

Quran has referred to them with the words like RAHABA (رحب) , WASI’ (وسع), TAFSUHU (تفسح).

 

4.1 RAHIBA (رحب) and RAHABA  (رحب):  mean wideness of space. It is only used for wideness of the space. The wideness of space or (of a) house, and its antonym is DHAAQA (ضاق). Allah Said:

 

Surat At-Tawbah (The Repentance) - سورة التوبة 9:25

وَّضَاقَتْ عَلَيْكُمُ الْاَرْضُ بِمَا رَحُبَتْ

And the earth was confining for you with its vastness.

And MARHAB (مرحب) word is used for pray. MARHABA (مرحبا) means welcome. And LA MARHABA (لامرحبا) is used as a curse (i.e. there is no capacity or space for you).

 

It is in Qur’an:

 

Surat Şād (The Letter "Saad") - سورة ص 38:59

لَا مَرْحَبًۢا بِهِمْ ۭ اِنَّهُمْ صَالُوا النَّارِ

No welcome for them. Indeed, they will burn in the Fire.

 

4.2 WASI’ (وسع) is used for both space and condition. It means wideness, holding, capacity Allah Said:

 

Surat Al-Baqarah (The Cow) - سورة البقرة 2:255

وَسِعَ كُرْسِـيُّهُ السَّمٰوٰتِ وَالْاَرْضَ

His Kursi extends over the heavens and the earth.

 

And Allah Said:

Surat Al-Baqarah (The Cow) - سورة البقرة 2:286

لَا يُكَلِّفُ اللّٰهُ نَفْسًا اِلَّا وُسْعَهَا

 

Allah does not burden a soul except [what is within] its capacity.

 

And AWSA’ (اوسع) means to have much wealth. And AWSA’ AL-MAWDI’ (اوسع الموضع) means to make a space wide.

 

Allah Said:

 

Surat Adh-Dhāriyāt (The Winnowing Winds) - سورة الذاريات 51:47

وَالسَّمَاۗءَ بَنَيْنٰهَا بِاَيْىدٍ وَّاِنَّا لَمُوْسِعُوْنَ

 

And the heaven We constructed with strength, and indeed, We are [its] expander.

 

4.3 TAFSUHU (تفسح) in relation to FASAHA  (فسح):  means to take a wide step and FASAHA  (فسح) and TAFASAHA FAL-MAJLEES ( تفسح فلمجليس ) means to give space in gatherings, meaning to sit openly in a manner so that space is created for others. Allah Said:

 

Page-662

Surat Al-Mujādila (The Pleading Woman) - سورة المجادلة 58:11

اِذَا قِيْلَ لَكُمْ تَفَسَّحُوْا فِي الْمَجٰلِسِ فَافْسَحُوْا يَفْسَحِ اللّٰهُ لَكُمْ  

When you are told, "Space yourselves" in gatherings, then make space; Allah will make space for you.

 

 

Summary:

4.1  RAHIBA: only for the openness of space.

4.2  WASI’: holding or capacity.

AWSA’: To make widening space.

4.3 TAFSUHU: Open to make space for others.

title: content/f/f5.html
raw_text:
5- FARISHTA [ANGEL]
Quran     has referred it with the words     MALAK (ملك) MALAIKAH (ملائكة) and ROOH (روح )
5.1       MALAK (ملك) MALAIKAH (ملائكة) :     Feminine is LAIK ( لايك  ). Its meaning is to deliver a message. AL AKAT ALA-FULAAN ( الاکت الی فلان ) means to deliver a message to somebody; and AL-KUNA ( الکنی ) means to deliver him my message. And MALAK (ملك) MALAIKAH (ملائكة) means a messenger Angel and MALAK (ملك) means Angel used in Shari’ terms. There is no difference in that (the Angel) must be a messenger. Allah has appointed the Angels for universal duties. The Angel of cloud, the Angel of death, the angels of Hell and Paradise, MALAK (ملك) MALAIKAH (ملائكة) is used for all of them, although they are not messengers. Whenever an unseen sound or hidden sound is delivered from Allah, then instead of MALAK (ملك), MALAIKAT (ملائكة) plural term is used. Allah Said:
Surat 'Āli `Imrān (Family of Imran) - سورة آل عمران     3:45
اِذْ قَالَتِ الْمَلٰۗىِٕكَةُ يٰمَرْيَمُ اِنَّ اللّٰهَ يُبَشِّرُكِ بِكَلِمَةٍ مِّنْهُ اسْمُهُ الْمَسِيْحُ عِيْسَى ابْنُ مَرْيَمَ
[And mention] when the Angels said, "O Mary, indeed Allah gives you good tidings of a word from Him, whose name will be the Messiah, Jesus, the son of Mary
On this occasion or in similar occasions, why MALAIKAT (ملائكة) plural term is used instead of MALAK (ملك) is beyond the scope of human wisdom.
5.2       ROOH (روح ):     Man is given very small knowledge about the reality of the soul, to understand the true meaning of ROOH (روح ) is beyond the capabilities of man. ROOH (روح ) is also used in terms of blessing (رحمت ) in the Qur’an, and in terms of WAHI ( وحی ) and QUR’AN (قران ) and in terms of Angel (فرشتہ ) also. The Angel who is specifically appointed from Allah to deliver His Message to the Prophets is JIBREEL (جبریل ). ALLAH has called him with the titles of ROOH (روح ) and ROOH AL-AMEEN (روح الامین ) and RASOOLI-KAREEM (رسول کریم ). The Angel who came to MARYAM and delivered the message of Allah after transforming in human form, he is called ROOH (روح ) in Surat- Maryam.  And instead of MALAK (ملك), he is called MALAIKAH (ملائكة) in Surat AAL-Imraan. Commentators opine that this ROOH (روح ) was JIBREEL. Maryam was not a Prophet, even if Jibreel or some other Angel came to her, delivered the Message of Allah and
Page-663
talked to her. This message was also related to the personality of Hazrat Maryam. Aside from delivering it to others, there was no connection with this message which is essentially for Prophethood and prophecy. Allah Said:
Surat Maryam (Mary) - سورة مريم     19:17
فَاَرْسَلْنَآ اِلَيْهَا رُوْحَنَا فَتَمَثَّلَ لَهَا بَشَرًا سَوِيًّا
Then We sent to her Our Angel, and he represented himself to her as a well-proportioned man.

raw_text:
6- FARQ [Difference]
Quran has included the words     BA’D (بعد), and TAFAWUTA (تفاوت).
6.1      BUAD (بعد)     BAED (بعد) and BAUD (بعد)   means to get away and the real meaning of BUAD (بعد) is also (to do) away but this word is used in terms of getting away due to a curse or being rebuked. When this word is used for (mental) migration then it gives the meaning of (being) different or distant. Like Allah Said:
Surat Az-Zukhruf (The Ornaments of Gold) - سورة الزخرف     43:38
قَالَ يٰلَيْتَ بَيْنِيْ وَبَيْنَكَ بُعْدَ الْمَشْرِقَيْنِ
He says [to his companion], "Oh, I wish there was between me and you the distance between the east and west.
6.2      TAFAWUTA (تفاوت) antonym of ISTAWA (  استوا )   FAAT AL-AMR (فات الامر ) means going out of timings to do some task and termed as non-returnable. And TAFAWUT-ISHA’EEN (تفاوت اشعین) means unsettling of two things between each other and non-appropriateness. This word is always used negatively and FAAT (فات ) means when something goes so far away from a person that it becomes difficult for him to get it. And TAFAWUT (تفاوت ) means difference in the attributes of two things. Hence the attribute of each one kills the other. Allah says:
Surat Al-Mulk (The Sovereignty) - سورة الملك 67:3
مَا تَرٰى فِيْ خَلْقِ الرَّحْمٰنِ مِنْ تَفٰوُتٍ
You do not see in the creation of the Most Merciful any inconsistency.
It means that there is a complete relevance and consistency in all things in universe.
Summary:
6.1      BU’AD:     The measurement of distance and difference  .
6.2      TAFAWUT  :   The difference between two things due to the difference in their attributes. Inconsistency.

raw_text:
7- FIRQA------GAROOH [Sect - Group]
Quran has referred them by the words     FIRQAH (فرقة), FAREEQ (فريق) TA’IFAH (طائفة) ZAMURA (زمر) SHEE’AH (شيعه) and UNAAS (اناس).
7.1       FIRQAH (فرقة) :   FARAQA (فرق ) means to separate, tearing and FIRQ (فرق ) means separated part and FIRQAH (فرقة) means separated (smaller group of) people apart from a (bigger) community. The group of like-minded people in big numbers separated from some nation or community. Allah says:
Page-664
Surat At-Tawbah (The Repentance) - سورة التوبة     9:122
فَلَوْلَا نَفَرَ مِنْ كُلِّ فِرْقَــةٍ مِّنْھُمْ طَاۗىِٕفَةٌ لِّيَتَفَقَّهُوْا فِي الدِّيْنِ
For there should separate from every division of them a group [remaining] to obtain understanding in the religion.
7.2      FAREEQ (فريق):     FIRQAH (فرقة) and FAREEQ (فريق) have approximately similar meanings. FAREEQ (فريق) is used when some other party is also present or goes against it. Like Allah Said:
Surat Ash-Shūraá (The Consultation) - سورة الشورى     42:7
فَرِيْقٌ فِي الْجَنَّةِ وَفَرِيْقٌ فِي السَّعِيْرِ
A party will be in Paradise and a party in the Blaze.
At another occasion, it is said:
Surat Maryam (Mary) - سورة مريم     19:73
اَيُّ الْفَرِيْقَيْنِ خَيْرٌ مَّقَامًا وَّاَحْسَنُ نَدِيًّا
"Which of [our] two parties is best in position and best in association?"
7.3         TA’IFAH (طائفة):   The people of one point-of-view and religion. This word can be applied to the smallest (group) and even to a single person as well. just like some commentators says about this verse: Allah says:
Surat Al-Ĥujurāt (The Rooms) - سورة الحجرات     49:9
وَاِنْ طَاۗىِٕفَتٰنِ مِنَ الْمُؤْمِنِيْنَ اقْتَتَلُوْا فَاَصْلِحُوْا بَيْنَهُمَا
And if two factions among the believers should fight, then make settlement between the two. That the word TAIFA (طائفة) is applied to a single person in this verse.
7.4         ZAMURA (زمر):   The plural of ZUMARAH (زمرہ ) means Group. When a big group moves after being divided into small units or groups then these groups are called as ZUMAR (زمر) (See the explanation in JAMAAT (جماعت )) Allah says:
Surat Az-Zumar (The Troops) - سورة الزمر     39:73
وَسِيْقَ الَّذِيْنَ اتَّقَوْا رَبَّهُمْ اِلَى الْجَنَّةِ زُمَرًا
But those who feared their Lord will be driven to Paradise in groups.
7.5         SHEE’AH (شيعه):   means party, faction, political group. The people from whom man gets power and they are scattered around him. Someone's helper or follower. The base of such party is normally due to difference of beliefs. Allah says:
Surat Al-Qaşaş (The Stories) - سورة القصص     28:15
فَوَجَدَ فِيْهَا رَجُلَيْنِ يَـقْتَتِلٰنِ ڭ هٰذَا مِنْ شِيْعَتِهٖ وَهٰذَا مِنْ عَدُوِّه
And found therein two men fighting: one from his faction and one from among his enemy.
And the plural of SHEE’AH (شيعه) is SHAI’YA (شعیا) as well and also ASHYAA’ (اشیاع). ASHIYAA’ (اشیاع) meaning the people who possess similar habits and manners whether they had passed before or present. Same gender. Allah Said:
Surat Saba' (Sheba) - سورة سبإ     34:54
وَحِيْلَ بَيْنَهُمْ وَبَيْنَ مَا يَشْتَهُوْنَ كَمَا فُعِلَ بِاَشْيَاعِهِمْ مِّنْ قَبْلُ
And prevention will be placed between them and what they desire, as was done with their kind before.
Page-665
7.6         UNAAS (اناس):   Groups that are present or made according to the division, or separate groups related to different tribes. (According to some, there is no difference between UNAAS (اناس) and NAAS (ناس ). It is in the Qur’an:
Surat Al-Baqarah (The Cow) - سورة البقرة     2:60
قَدْ عَلِمَ كُلُّ اُنَاسٍ مَّشْرَبَھُمْ
And every people knew its watering place.
Summary:
7.1      FIRQAH: The separated part of many people from a big group.
7.2      FAREEQ: That group to whom there is an opposite group present or listed.
7.3      TA’IFAH: The small community of people with same views and religion.
7.4      ZUMAR: Small groups and units.
7.5      SHEE’AH: The party or faction with opposite beliefs.
7.6      UNAAS: Sects made because of tribes or distribution.
For Obedience, look at “To Obey”.

7.6   UNAAS (اناس): Groups that are present or made according to the division, or separate groups related to different tribes. (According to some, there is no difference between UNAAS (اناس) and NAAS (ناس ). It is in the Qur’an:

Surat Al-Baqarah (The Cow) - سورة البقرة 2:60

قَدْ عَلِمَ كُلُّ اُنَاسٍ مَّشْرَبَھُمْ

And every people knew its watering place.

 

Summary:

7.1  FIRQAH: The separated part of many people from a big group.

7.2  FAREEQ: That group to whom there is an opposite group present or listed.

7.3  TA’IFAH: The small community of people with same views and religion.

7.4  ZUMAR: Small groups and units.

7.5  SHEE’AH: The party or faction with opposite beliefs.

7.6  UNAAS: Sects made because of tribes or distribution.

For Obedience, look at “To Obey”.

raw_text:
8- FARYAAD RASI [To Complaint]
Qur’an has referred to it by the words     ISTIJAAB (استجاب), JOOB (جوب) and ASRAKHA (اصرخ).
8.1      ISTIJAAB (استجاب):      JAABA (جاب) means stone-cutting. And ‘AJAABA (أجاب ) means MARAJA’T AL-KALAAM (مراجعتہ الکلام ) means to answer question. And SALA (سل ) also comes with two meanings: 1) To inquire about a thing, and: 2) To ask for a thing or to demand. Hence ‘AJAABA (أجاب ) also comes with those two meanings, to respond to someone's query. Like Allah Said:
Surat Al-Mā'idah (The Table Spread) - سورة المائدة     5:109
يَوْمَ يَجْمَعُ اللّٰهُ الرُّسُلَ فَيَقُوْلُ مَاذَآ اُجِبْتُمْ
[Be warned of] the Day when Allah will assemble the messengers and say, "What was the response you received?".
And to accept its meaning in response to a demand for something. Like it is Said:
Surat An-Naml (The Ant) - سورة النمل 27:62
اَمَّنْ يُّجِيْبُ الْمُضْطَرَّ اِذَا دَعَاهُ
Is He [not best] who responds to the desperate one when he calls upon Him.
And ISTIJAAB (استجاب) means accepting the prayer, or to honour or accept the demands of a caller especially when call is exercised. Allah Said:
Surat Al-'Anbyā' (The Prophets) - سورة الأنبياء 21:76
وَنُوْحًا اِذْ نَادٰي مِنْ قَبْلُ فَاسْتَجَبْنَا لَهٗ فَنَجَّيْنٰهُ وَاَهْلَهٗ مِنَ الْكَرْبِ الْعَظِيْمِ
And [mention] Noah, when he called [to Allah ] before [that time], so We responded to him and saved him and his family from the great flood.
8.2 ASRAKHA (اصرخ):     SARAKHA (صراخ ) means to howl or scream so that someone comes (to help). And SAREEKH (صريخ ) means to come to the aid and the meaning of ASRAKHA (اصرخ) is same. It is in the Qur’an:
Page-666
Surat 'Ibrāhīm (Abrahim) - سورة ابراهيم     14:22
فَلَا تَلُوْمُوْنِيْ وَلُوْمُوْٓا اَنْفُسَكُمْ ۭ مَآ اَنَا بِمُصْرِخِكُمْ وَمَآ اَنْتُمْ بِمُصْرِخِيَّ
So do not blame me; but blame yourselves. I cannot be called to your aid, nor can you be called to my aid.
Summary:
8.1       If a prayer or call is offered to Allah for aid and He accept it then it is called ISTIHAAB (استحاب ) while in case of ASRAKHA (اصرخ), anybody who listens to the shouting can come to the aid.

title: content/f/f9.html
raw_text:
9- FARYAAD KARNA [To Call For Aid]
Quran has referred to it by the words     ISTIGHAATH (استغاث) and ISTISRAKH (استصرخ).
9.1          ISTIGHAATHA (استغاث):    GHATHA (غاث ) means to help or support somebody in harsh times and GHAYTH (غيث ) is the rain which is on-time and according to the needs as well. ISTIGHAATH (استغاث ) means to call Allah for aid as well as call a ruler for help and to seek assistance in hard times. ISTIGHAATHAH (استغاثة ) is a well-known word meaning to call for  aid from a ruler or court (regarding a problem affecting him). Allah says:
Surat Al-'Anfāl (The Spoils of War) - سورة الأنفال     8:9
اِذْ تَسْتَغِيْثُوْنَ رَبَّكُمْ فَاسْتَجَابَ لَكُمْ
[Remember] when you asked help of your Lord, and He answered you.
9.2       ISTISRAKH (استصرخ):      means to gain people’s attention by screaming and shouting for help. (Description is explained above). It is in Qur’an:
Surat Al-Qaşaş (The Stories) - سورة القصص     28:18
فَاِذَا الَّذِي اسْتَـنْصَرَهٗ بِالْاَمْسِ يَسْتَــصْرِخُهٗ
When suddenly the one who sought his help the previous day cried out to him [once again].
Summary:
If help is asked before Allah or authorised ruler then the word ISTIGHAATH (استغاث) will be used and if the people are called by howling and screaming then  ISTISRAKH (استصرخ) will be used.

Page 726--
گ   (GAAF)
1. GAR-NA (To Pitch)
Synonyms: NASABA, ARSA (RASU), DASSA, WAADA
1.1 NASABA(نَصَبَ):   Means to pitch or install something such that some part of it is under the ground and most of it is outside in some other direction like pitching in a flagpole or a spear or to erect a building or a stone and it is also used for an idol which is fixed in someplace. In the Quran:
1.   Surat Al-Ghāshiyah (The Overwhelming) - سورة الغاشية 88:19
وَإِلَى الْجِبَالِ كَيْفَ نُصِبَتْ
And at the mountains - how they are erected?
2.   Surat Al-Mā'idah (The Table Spread) - سورة المائدة 5:3
وَمَا ذُبِحَ عَلَى النُّصُبِ
And [those animals] killed by strangling
1.2 ARSA(اَرسَى)  : RASU(رسو) means to establish or erect and ARSA(اَرسَى) means to pitch something in the ground so that most part of it is inside the ground and less is outside. RASAL-WAT-DA-FIL-ARDI(رَسَا الوَتدَ فِى الْاَرضِ) means to pitch a rivet in the ground and RASIYA(راسيه) means mountain and its plural is RAWASI(رَوَاسِى). RASIYA(راسية) are those mountains which are spread far away on the ground and their major portion is underground and RAWASI(رَوَاسِى) means mountain range. Both NASABA(نصب) and RASU(رسو) are used for fixing mountains. In the Quran:
1  . Surat An-Nāzi`āt (Those who drag forth) - سورة النازعات 79:32
وَالْجِبَالَ أَرْسَاهَا
And the mountains He set firmly.
2  . Surat Ar-Ra`d (The Thunder) - سورة الرعد 13:3
هُوَ الَّذِي مَدَّ الْأَرْضَ وَجَعَلَ فِيهَا رَوَاسِيَ وَأَنْهَارًا ۖ
And it is He who spread the earth and placed therein firmly set mountains and rivers
1.3 DASSA  (دَسَّ): Means to conceal something by burying it in the ground or to enter one thing into another forcefully or to hide something by burying it or sinking down in the soil and DASSA ALAEH(دَسَّ عَلَيه) means to conspire or to plot secretly. In the Quran:
Page 727--
1. Surat Ash-Shams (The Sun) - سورة الشمس 91:10
وَقَدْ خَابَ مَن دَسَّاهَا
And he has failed who instills it [with corruption].
2. Surat An-Naĥl (The Bee) - سورة النحل 16:59
أَيُمْسِكُهُ عَلَىٰ هُونٍ أَمْ يَدُسُّهُ فِي التُّرَابِ ۗ
Should he keep it in humiliation or bury it in the ground
1.4 WA’ADA(  وَأَدَ  ):   Burying someone alive under the weight of the earth. To bury alive. It is most particular to DASSA(دَسَّ). In the Quran:
Surat At-Takwīr (The Overthrowing) - سورة التكوير 81:8
بِأَيِّ ذَنبٍ قُتِلَتْ وَإِذَا الْمَوْءُودَةُ سُئِلَتْ
And when the girl [who was] buried alive is asked. For what sin she was killed?
Summary:
1. NASABA: To wedge like a flagpole.  A small portion buried in the soil while the rest is erect above the surface.
2. ADSA: Like burying a peg in the ground with most of the part buried in the ground.
3. DASSA: To bury or thrust something under the ground
4. WA’ADA: To bury a living being in the ground.
For GARD-O-GHUBAR, refer to “GHUBAR”.

title: content/gg/gg10.html
raw_text:
10 GUZARNA [to pass]
Synonyms: SABAQA, KHALA, SALAFA, MARRA, MADAA, INSALAKH
10.1 SABAQA (سَبَقَ):   To leave behind others and move ahead. To advance. Thus one who passes ahead,  and always wanted be ahead of those who were behind. Allah says in the Quran
Surah Al Hashr (The exile): سورۃ الحَشر 59:10
رَبَّنَا ٱغۡفِرۡ لَنَا وَلِإِخۡوَٲنِنَا ٱلَّذِينَ سَبَقُونَا بِٱلۡإِيمَـٰنِ
Our Lord, forgive us, and our brethren who preceded us in faith
When it is used for ‘passing’ then it means ‘passed earlier’ or  after passing this place a person  also went pass other things, or is still passing by some other things. Allah says in the Quran
Surah Ta-Ha (Ta-ha): سورۃ طٰھٰ  20:99
كَذَٲلِكَ نَقُصُّ عَلَيۡكَ مِنۡ أَنۢبَآءِ مَا قَدۡ سَبَقَ‌ۚ
Thus We narrate to you reports of times gone by;
10.2 KHALA  (خَلَا)  :   Means empty. To separate one thing from other. To pass by something so that no one resists it. Used for both time and place. KHALAA   (خَلّٰی)   means to vacate, In the Quran
Surah Al Tawbah (The repentance): سورۃ التوبھ 9:5
فَخَلُّواْ سَبِيلَهُمۡ‌ۚ
then open the way for them
Means to give way, to get out of way and let someone pass through or leave the way and do not resist. KHALA’ (خَلَاء) is also an empty house and also the ‘space’ between the sky and earth. Thus KHALA (خلا) apart from passing someone also refers to empty space or moments. Allah says in the Quran
Surah Al-Baqarah (The cow): سورۃ البَقَرَۃ  2:141
تِلۡكَ أُمَّةٌ۬ قَدۡ خَلَتۡ‌ۖ لَهَا مَا كَسَبَتۡ
That was a community that has passed. To them is what they have earned,
10.3 SALAFA (سَلَفَ):   Means to move ahead, and SALAF-AL-QAWM (سَلَفَ الْقَوْم) means to be ahead of a nation or group (dictionary al Manjad). SALF (سَلْف) means an ancient, someone who has passed away (opposite KHALF(خَلْف)) and (plural ASLAAF(اَسْلاَف)) and ASLAAF (اَسْلاَف) means those pious elders who have passed away. SALAFI (سَلَفی) is a person who likes to connect with them. KHALAF means a loser or an unfit or unworthy successor.  Thus when SALAF (سَلَفَ) is referred to passing then it  depicts the forthcoming generations or similar events. Allah says in the Quran
Surah An-Nisa (The women): سورۃ النِّسا 4:23
وَأَن تَجۡمَعُواْ بَيۡنَ ٱلۡأُخۡتَيۡنِ إِلَّا مَا قَدۡ سَلَفَ‌ۗ
And the wives of your genetic sons, and marrying two sisters simultaneously. Except what is past
10.4 MARRA (مَرَّ):   To go past something, to walk past something. In the Quran
Surah Al-Baqarah (The cow): سورۃ البَقَرَۃ  2:259
أَوۡ كَٱلَّذِى مَرَّ عَلَىٰ قَرۡيَةٍ۬
Or like him who passed by a town
And ISRAMARR   (اِسْتَمَرّ)   means to keep on passing by, to be in a state of continuously passing by something   (dictionary al Manjad). MAROOR-E-AYYAM (مَرُوْرِ اَیَّام) means passing of days. MARR (مَرّ) is also used in same meaning in Quran as ISTAMARR (اِسْتَمَرّ).  For instance
Surah Al-Araf (The heights): سورۃ الأعرَاف 7:189
حَمَلَتۡ حَمۡلاً خَفِيفً۬ا فَمَرَّتۡ بِهِ
she carries a light burden and continues therein.
In another place
Surah Al-Qamar (The moon): سورۃ القَمَر 54:2
وَإِن يَرَوۡاْ ءَايَةً۬ يُعۡرِضُواْ وَيَقُولُواْ سِحۡرٌ۬ مُّسۡتَمِرٌّ۬
And if they see a miracle, they turn away and say, "Passing magic."
Surah Yusuf (Joseph): سورۃ یُوسُف 12:105
يَمُرُّونَ عَلَيۡہَا
the earth do they pass by
Thus MARR (مَرّ) refers to passing by and also to ISTAMRAR (استمرار).
10.5 MAZAA (  مَضٰی  ):   Means to walk past, to leave. Opposite of MAZAA (مَضٰی) is ISTAQBALA (اِسْتَقْبَلَ) means to come from front, to approach from front. And MAZAA (مَضٰی) means to leave or move away from front. And MAAZI (ماضی) means past whose opposite is MUSTAQBIL (مستقبل) meaning future. Used for both novelty and grandee, for any kind or events. MAZAA-ALA-AL-AMAR (مَضٰی عَلیَ الْاَمْر) means continuity in work (dictionary al Manjad). In the Quran
Surah Al-Anfal (The Spoils of War): سُوۡرَةُ الاٴنفَال 8:38
وَإِن يَعُودُواْ فَقَدۡ مَضَتۡ سُنَّتُ ٱلۡأَوَّلِينَ
But if they persist—the practice of the ancients has passed away.
In another place
Surah Al-Kahf (The Cave): سورۃ الکھف 18:60
حَتَّىٰٓ أَبۡلُغَ مَجۡمَعَ ٱلۡبَحۡرَيۡنِ أَوۡ أَمۡضِىَ حُقُبً۬ا
until I reach the junction of the two seas, or I will pass epochs away."
10.6 INSALAKHA (  اِنْسَلَخَ  ):   SALAKHA (سَلَخَ) means to pull off sin or hide. And SALAKHA (سَلَخَ) and INSALAKH-ASH-SHAHAR (اِنْسَلَخَ الشَّھْر) means last dates of lunar month. Allah says in the Quran
Surah Al Tawbah (The repentance): سورۃ التوبھ 9:5
فَإِذَا ٱنسَلَخَ ٱلۡأَشۡہُرُ ٱلۡحُرُمُ
When the Sacred Months have passed,
Summary:
10.1 SABAQA: To take over, also likes those whom left behind.
10.2 KHALA: Passing of something with account of empty space or time, and something coming in the place.
10.3 SALAFA: Passing of something with connection to the later one.
10.4 MARRA: Passing also with ISTAMARR or continuity, to go past something.
10.5 MADAA: To do something in the past time.
10.6 INSALAKH: Passing of a lunar month.

10 GUZARNA [to pass]

Synonyms: SABAQA, KHALA, SALAFA, MARRA, MADAA, INSALAKH

10.1 SABAQA (سَبَقَ): To leave behind others and move ahead. To advance. Thus one who passes ahead,  and always wanted be ahead of those who were behind. Allah says in the Quran

Surah Al Hashr (The exile): سورۃ الحَشر 59:10

 رَبَّنَا ٱغۡفِرۡ لَنَا وَلِإِخۡوَٲنِنَا ٱلَّذِينَ سَبَقُونَا بِٱلۡإِيمَـٰنِ

Our Lord, forgive us, and our brethren who preceded us in faith

When it is used for ‘passing’ then it means ‘passed earlier’ or  after passing this place a person  also went pass other things, or is still passing by some other things. Allah says in the Quran

Surah Ta-Ha (Ta-ha): سورۃ طٰھٰ  20:99

كَذَٲلِكَ نَقُصُّ عَلَيۡكَ مِنۡ أَنۢبَآءِ مَا قَدۡ سَبَقَ‌ۚ

Thus We narrate to you reports of times gone by;

10.2 KHALA(خَلَا): Means empty. To separate one thing from other. To pass by something so that no one resists it. Used for both time and place. KHALAA (خَلّٰی) means to vacate, In the Quran

Surah Al Tawbah (The repentance): سورۃ التوبھ 9:5

 فَخَلُّواْ سَبِيلَهُمۡ‌ۚ

then open the way for them

Means to give way, to get out of way and let someone pass through or leave the way and do not resist. KHALA’ (خَلَاء) is also an empty house and also the ‘space’ between the sky and earth. Thus KHALA (خلا) apart from passing someone also refers to empty space or moments. Allah says in the Quran

Surah Al-Baqarah (The cow): سورۃ البَقَرَۃ  2:141

 تِلۡكَ أُمَّةٌ۬ قَدۡ خَلَتۡ‌ۖ لَهَا مَا كَسَبَتۡ

That was a community that has passed. To them is what they have earned, 

10.3 SALAFA (سَلَفَ): Means to move ahead, and SALAF-AL-QAWM (سَلَفَ الْقَوْم) means to be ahead of a nation or group (dictionary al Manjad). SALF (سَلْف) means an ancient, someone who has passed away (opposite KHALF(خَلْف)) and (plural ASLAAF(اَسْلاَف)) and ASLAAF (اَسْلاَف) means those pious elders who have passed away. SALAFI (سَلَفی) is a person who likes to connect with them. KHALAF means a loser or an unfit or unworthy successor.  Thus when SALAF (سَلَفَ) is referred to passing then it  depicts the forthcoming generations or similar events. Allah says in the Quran

Surah An-Nisa (The women): سورۃ النِّسا 4:23

وَأَن تَجۡمَعُواْ بَيۡنَ ٱلۡأُخۡتَيۡنِ إِلَّا مَا قَدۡ سَلَفَ‌ۗ

 And the wives of your genetic sons, and marrying two sisters simultaneously. Except what is past

10.4 MARRA (مَرَّ): To go past something, to walk past something. In the Quran

Surah Al-Baqarah (The cow): سورۃ البَقَرَۃ  2:259

أَوۡ كَٱلَّذِى مَرَّ عَلَىٰ قَرۡيَةٍ۬

 Or like him who passed by a town

And ISRAMARR (اِسْتَمَرّ) means to keep on passing by, to be in a state of continuously passing by something (dictionary al Manjad). MAROOR-E-AYYAM (مَرُوْرِ اَیَّام) means passing of days. MARR (مَرّ) is also used in same meaning in Quran as ISTAMARR (اِسْتَمَرّ).  For instance

Surah Al-Araf (The heights): سورۃ الأعرَاف 7:189

 حَمَلَتۡ حَمۡلاً خَفِيفً۬ا فَمَرَّتۡ بِهِ

 she carries a light burden and continues therein.

In another place

Surah Al-Qamar (The moon): سورۃ القَمَر 54:2

 وَإِن يَرَوۡاْ ءَايَةً۬ يُعۡرِضُواْ وَيَقُولُواْ سِحۡرٌ۬ مُّسۡتَمِرٌّ۬

And if they see a miracle, they turn away and say, "Passing magic."

Surah Yusuf (Joseph): سورۃ یُوسُف 12:105

 يَمُرُّونَ عَلَيۡہَا

the earth do they pass by

Thus MARR (مَرّ) refers to passing by and also to ISTAMRAR (استمرار).

10.5 MAZAA (مَضٰی): Means to walk past, to leave. Opposite of MAZAA (مَضٰی) is ISTAQBALA (اِسْتَقْبَلَ) means to come from front, to approach from front. And MAZAA (مَضٰی) means to leave or move away from front. And MAAZI (ماضی) means past whose opposite is MUSTAQBIL (مستقبل) meaning future. Used for both novelty and grandee, for any kind or events. MAZAA-ALA-AL-AMAR (مَضٰی عَلیَ الْاَمْر) means continuity in work (dictionary al Manjad). In the Quran

Surah Al-Anfal (The Spoils of War): سُوۡرَةُ الاٴنفَال 8:38

 وَإِن يَعُودُواْ فَقَدۡ مَضَتۡ سُنَّتُ ٱلۡأَوَّلِينَ

 But if they persist—the practice of the ancients has passed away.

In another place

Surah Al-Kahf (The Cave): سورۃ الکھف 18:60

 حَتَّىٰٓ أَبۡلُغَ مَجۡمَعَ ٱلۡبَحۡرَيۡنِ أَوۡ أَمۡضِىَ حُقُبً۬ا

until I reach the junction of the two seas, or I will pass epochs away."

10.6 INSALAKHA (اِنْسَلَخَ): SALAKHA (سَلَخَ) means to pull off sin or hide. And SALAKHA (سَلَخَ) and INSALAKH-ASH-SHAHAR (اِنْسَلَخَ الشَّھْر) means last dates of lunar month. Allah says in the Quran

فَإِذَا ٱنسَلَخَ ٱلۡأَشۡہُرُ ٱلۡحُرُمُ

When the Sacred Months have passed,

Summary:

10.1 SABAQA: To take over, also likes those whom left behind.

10.2 KHALA: Passing of something with account of empty space or time, and something coming in the place.

10.3 SALAFA: Passing of something with connection to the later one.

11. GALA [throat, neck]
Synonyms: HULQOOM, HANAJIR
11.1 HULQOOM (حُلْقُوْم):   Means throat or neck, the place of a body of animal from where he is slaughtered. A very famous body part. HULQOOM (حُلْقُوْم) and HALAQ (حلق) means the same. In the Quran
Surah Al-Waqiah (The Inevitable): سُوۡرَةُ الواقِعَة 56:83
فَلَوۡلَآ إِذَا بَلَغَتِ ٱلۡحُلۡقُومَ
So when it has reached the throat.
11.2 HANAJIR (حَنَاجِر):   (Singular HANJRAH (حنجرہ)) larynx, wind pipe (dictionary al Manjad). In the Quran
Suran Al-Ahzaab (The clans): سورۃ الأحزَاب 33:10
وَبَلَغَتِ ٱلۡقُلُوبُ ٱلۡحَنَاجِرَ وَتَظُنُّونَ بِٱللَّهِ ٱلظُّنُونَا۟
and the hearts reached the throats, and you harbored doubts about God.
Summary
11.1 HULQOOM : HALAQ means neck. Including the outer skin and everything.
11.2 HANAJIR: Means the internal windpipe, or larynx.

raw_text:
12 GUM HONA – HATH NA LAGNA [to lose, to miss ]
Synonyms: FATA, FAQADA, ZALLA
12.1 FATA (فَاتَ):   Something getting out of hand, FAAT-AL-AMR (فَاتَ الاَمْر) means time to do a task that is lost and would not come back. Allah says in the Quran
Surat Al-Hadeed (The Iron): سورة الحديد 57:23
لِّكَيۡلَا تَأۡسَوۡاْ عَلَىٰ مَا فَاتَكُمۡ وَلَا تَفۡرَحُواْ بِمَآ ءَاتَٮٰڪُمۡ‌ۗ
You may not be sad over matters that you fail to get, nor rejoice because of that which has been given to you.
12.2 FAQADA (فَقَدَ):   To not get something. Not available. Even if is attained later on or to lose something despite of its availability. This word is derived from ADM (عَدَم) ۔In the Quran
Surah Yusuf (Joseph): سورۃ یُوسُف 12:71
قَالُواْ وَأَقۡبَلُواْ عَلَيۡهِم مَّاذَا تَفۡقِدُونَ
They said, as they came towards them, “What are you missing?”
And TAFAQQADA (تَفَقَّدَ) means to verify or review if something is missing. According to Imam Raghib to know if something is missing. To find something missing or lost. In the Quran
Surah An-Naml (The ant): سورۃ النَّمل 27:20
وَتَفَقَّدَ ٱلطَّيۡرَ فَقَالَ مَا لِىَ لَآ أَرَى ٱلۡهُدۡهُدَ
And he reviewed the birds; then he said, "what is it with me that I do not see the hoopoe?
12.3 ZALLA (ضَلَّ):   Actually means to forget the way and get lost. But it also means to lose one existence and find another in return. In the Quran
Surah As-Sajda (The prostration ): سُوۡرَةُ السَّجدَة 32:10
وَقَالُوٓاْ أَءِذَا ضَلَلۡنَا فِى ٱلۡأَرۡضِ أَءِنَّا لَفِى خَلۡقٍ۬ جَدِيدِۭ‌ۚ
And they say, “When we are lost into the earth, shall we be in a new creation?”
Summary:
12.1 FATA: To lose an opportunity, to lose hope of getting something.
12.2 FAQADA: For some time, not able to get something in spite of its availability.
12.3 ZALLA: To convert a thing’s existence into another thing and losing it.

title: content/gg/gg13.html
raw_text:
13 GUMAN KERNA – KHIAL KERNA [to think, to suppose]
SYNONYMS: ZANNA, ZA’AMA, HASIBA
13.1 ZANNA (ظَنَّ):   The signs which lead to some results are called ZANN (ظَنّ). If the signs and suppositions are strong then ZANN (ظَنّ) refers to certainty and surety. In this case this word is preceded by ANNA (اَنَّ), AN (اَنْ). Allah says in the Quran
Surah Al-Baqarah (The cow): سورۃ البَقَرَۃ 2:46
ٱلَّذِينَ يَظُنُّونَ أَنَّہُم مُّلَـٰقُواْ رَبِّہِمۡ وَأَنَّهُمۡ إِلَيۡهِ رَٲجِعُونَ
Who are certain that they will meet their Lord and that they will return to Him.
Surah Al-Qiyammah (the resurrection): سورۃ القِیَِامَھ 75:28
وَظَنَّ أَنَّهُ ٱلۡفِرَاقُ
And the dying one is certain that it is the [time of] separation
Surah Al-Fath (The victory): سورۃ الفَتْح  48:12
بَلۡ ظَنَنتُمۡ أَن لَّن يَنقَلِبَ ٱلرَّسُولُ
But you thought that the Messenger and the believers would never return to their families,
And when refers to some suspicious or doubt then ZANN (ظَنّ) is preceded by INN (اِنّ) and IN (اِنْ). And the second indication is that the word ZANN (ظَنّ) is accompanied by a context which changes its meaning to assumption or doubt. For instance
Surah An-Najm (the star): سورۃ النَّجم 53:28
إِن يَتَّبِعُونَ إِلَّا ٱلظَّنَّ‌ۖ وَإِنَّ ٱلظَّنَّ لَا يُغۡنِى مِنَ ٱلۡحَقِّ شَيۡـًٔ۬ا
They follow not except assumption, and indeed, assumption avails not against the truth at all.
In this example INNA (اِنَّ)and the word HAQ (حق) (truth), change the meaning of ZANN (ظَنّ) to supposition and doubt.
Surah Al-Jathiya (Crouching): سُوۡرَةُ الجَاثیَة 45:32
إِن نَّظُنُّ إِلَّا ظَنًّ۬ا وَمَا نَحۡنُ بِمُسۡتَيۡقِنِينَ
We assume only assumption, and we are not convinced.' "
In this example INN (اِنّ) and the word YAQEEN (یقین) (‘believe’) change ZANN (ظَنّ) into suspicion or superstition.
Surah Al-Fath (The victory): سورۃ الفَتْح  48:6
ٱلظَّآنِّينَ بِٱللَّهِ ظَنَّ ٱلسَّوۡءِ‌ۚ
Those who harbor evil thoughts about God.
In this example the word ZANN-AS-SU’ (ظَنَّ ٱلسَّوۡءِ‌) particularizes the meaning of ZANN (ظَنّ) to doubt and supposition. Then there are stages of supposition and doubts between belief and suspicion, and ZANN (ظَنّ) is used for every such stage.
13.2 ZA’AMA (زَعَمَ):   False supposition; According to Ibn-Al-Faris ‘اَلْقَوْلُ مِنْ غَیْرِ صِحَّةٍ وَّلَا یَقِیْنٍ’ meaning a statement that is untrue and unauthentic. In Quran where ever this word is used, the one who is suspects is derogated or belittled. Allah says in the Quran
Surah At-Taghābun (The Mutual Disillusion): سورة التغابن 64:7
زَعَمَ ٱلَّذِينَ كَفَرُوٓاْ أَن لَّن يُبۡعَثُواْ‌ۚ
Those who disbelieve think that they shall never be raised
13.3 HASIBA (حَسِبَ):   HASAB (حَسَب) means to count or to calculate, HASUBA (حَسُبَ) means a noble or honorable. HASIBA (حَسِبَ) means to suppose or think. This word is for that degree or supposition in which a person only secretly knows or wishes for it but does not consider it a truth. A most likely supposition. Allah says in the Quran
Surah Al-Baqarah (The cow): سورۃ البَقَرَۃ  2:214
أَمۡ حَسِبۡتُمۡ أَن تَدۡخُلُواْ ٱلۡجَنَّةَ وَلَمَّا يَأۡتِكُم مَّثَلُ ٱلَّذِينَ خَلَوۡاْ مِن قَبۡلِكُم‌ۖ
Or do you think that you will enter Paradise while such [trial] has not yet come to you as came to those who passed on before you?
Summary:
13.1 ZANNA: ZANN (ظَنّ) Refers to larger set of meanings. And all stages of supposition or doubts are covered by it, suspicion,
13.2 ZA’AMA: False supposition
13.3 HASIBA: A most likely supposition.

In this example the word ZANN-AS-SU’ (ظَنَّ ٱلسَّوۡءِ‌) particularizes the meaning of ZANN (ظَنّ) to doubt and supposition. Then there are stages of supposition and doubts between belief and suspicion, and ZANN (ظَنّ) is used for every such stage.

13.2 ZA’AMA (زَعَمَ): False supposition; According to Ibn-Al-Faris ‘اَلْقَوْلُ مِنْ غَیْرِ صِحَّةٍ وَّلَا یَقِیْنٍ’ meaning a statement that is untrue and unauthentic. In Quran where ever this word is used, the one who is suspects is derogated or belittled. Allah says in the Quran

Surah At-Taghābun (The Mutual Disillusion): سورة التغابن 64:7

 زَعَمَ ٱلَّذِينَ كَفَرُوٓاْ أَن لَّن يُبۡعَثُواْ‌ۚ

Those who disbelieve think that they shall never be raised

13.3 HASIBA (حَسِبَ): HASAB (حَسَب) means to count or to calculate, HASUBA (حَسُبَ) means a noble or honorable. HASIBA (حَسِبَ) means to suppose or think. This word is for that degree or supposition in which a person only secretly knows or wishes for it but does not consider it a truth. A most likely supposition. Allah says in the Quran

Surah Al-Baqarah (The cow): سورۃ البَقَرَۃ  2:214

 أَمۡ حَسِبۡتُمۡ أَن تَدۡخُلُواْ ٱلۡجَنَّةَ وَلَمَّا يَأۡتِكُم مَّثَلُ ٱلَّذِينَ خَلَوۡاْ مِن قَبۡلِكُم‌ۖ

Or do you think that you will enter Paradise while such [trial] has not yet come to you as came to those who passed on before you?

Summary:

13.1 ZANNA: ZANN (ظَنّ) Refers to larger set of meanings. And all stages of supposition or doubts are covered by it, suspicion,

13.2 ZA’AMA: False supposition

13.3 HASIBA: A most likely supposition.

14 GUNNAH [sin]
Synonyms: ZAMB, KHATA, HUUB, HINTH, ITHM, IJRAAM,JUNAH, LAMAM
14.1ZAMB (ذَنْۢب):   Any act whose outcome is bad, and MA-YATBA’-ZAMM (ما یتبع الذم) and its usage is so common that it can be used for small mistakes to bigger sins. (Plural ZUNOOB (ذنوب))
Surah Al-Fath (The victory): سورۃ الفَتْح  48:1
إِنَّا فَتَحۡنَا لَكَ فَتۡحً۬ا مُّبِينً۬ا لِّيَغۡفِرَ لَكَ ٱللَّهُ مَا تَقَدَّمَ مِن ذَنۢبِكَ وَمَا تَأَخَّرَ
We have granted you a conspicuous victory. That God may forgive you your sin, past and to come,
These sins can only be some very small mistakes on part of Prophet Mohammed (S.A.A.W) because no Muslim can even think of Prophet Mohammed (S.A.A.W) doing even of the smallest sins. For instance in another place in the Quran
Surah Al Tawbah (The repentance): سورۃ التوبھ 9:43
عَفَا ٱللَّهُ عَنكَ لِمَ أَذِنتَ لَهُمۡ
May God pardon you! Why did you give them permission
And one of the biggest sins is an unjust murder. And even for that the word ZAMB   (ذَنْۢب)   is used. In the Quran
Surah Ash-Shura’ (The Poets): صورۃ الشُّعْراء 26:14
وَلَهُمۡ عَلَىَّ ذَنۢبٌ۬ فَأَخَافُ أَن يَقۡتُلُونِ
And they have upon me a [claim due to] sin, so I fear that they will kill me."
14.2 KHATA (خَطَا):   A sin that is not done intentionally by any human and it happens accidently. For instance a hunter while hunting a prey kills a human. And if this mistake can be rectified by some offering then its punishment can be reduced and it is called KHITA’ (خِطْأ) KHAT’A (خَطْأ).     And if of some other kind of sin, Allah can forgive it if begged for mercy and for good deeds, and this is known as KHATAA’ (خَطَأ) (Plural KHATAAYA (خطایا)). And KHATIA (خَطِئَ) (Plural KHATIA’AT (خطئات)) also comes in the same meaning. Allah says in the Quran
Surah An-Nisa (The women): سورۃ النِّسا 4:92
وَمَن قَتَلَ مُؤۡمِنًا خَطَـًٔ۬ا فَتَحۡرِيرُ رَقَبَةٍ۬ مُّؤۡمِنَةٍ۬ وَدِيَةٌ۬ مُّسَلَّمَةٌ إِلَىٰٓ أَهۡلِهِۦۤ إِلَّآ أَن يَصَّدَّقُواْ‌ۚ
Anyone who kills a believer by error must set free a believing slave, and pay compensation to the victim’s family, unless they remit it as charity.
In another place in the Quran
Surah Al-Baqarah (The cow): سورۃ البَقَرَۃ  2:58
وَقُولُواْ حِطَّةٌ۬ نَّغۡفِرۡ لَكُمۡ خَطَـٰيَـٰكُمۡ‌ۚ
Say, 'Pardon.' We will forgive your sins,
14.3 HUUB (حُوْب):   ALHUUBAH (اَلْحُوْبَة) refers to parents, sister or daughter, the phrase ‘اِنَّ لِیْ حُوْبَةٌ اَعْوَلُھَا’ means my family who are under my guardianship (  dictionary al Manjad). HAUB   (حَوْب)   means to disobey parents or parents delinquency in upbringing their child. According to Imam Raghib those act that are strictly forbidden, their perpetration is called HUUB   (حُوْب)  .  HUUB   (حُوْب)   basically means scolding or castigation. HUUB   (حُوْب)   is any such sin which when performed must be punished by castigation.
Surah An-Nisa (The women): سورۃ النِّسا 4:2
وَلَا تَأۡكُلُوٓاْ أَمۡوَٲلَهُمۡ إِلَىٰٓ أَمۡوَٲلِكُمۡ‌ۚ إِنَّهُ ۥ كَانَ حُوبً۬ا كَبِيرً۬ا
And do not consume their properties by combining them with yours, for that would be a serious sin.
14.4 HINTH (حِنْث):    Means a false or fake oath, sin or disobedience. HANATH-FIL-YAMEEN (حَنَثَ فِی الْیَمِیْن) means to disregard an oath. And HANITHA (حَنِثَ) means to sway towards lie and sins, to get involved in them   (  dictionary al Manjad). Thus HINTH   (حِنْث)   is a type of sin related to breaking of an oath or pledge. Allah says in the Quran
Surah Al-Waqiah (The Inevitable): سُوۡرَةُ الواقِعَة 56:46
وَكَانُواْ يُصِرُّونَ عَلَى ٱلۡحِنثِ ٱلۡعَظِيمِ
And were persisting in great sin
14.5 ITHM (اِثْم):   Any such act that stops from good deeds, (Plural ATHAAM (اٰثام)) (Opposite BIRR (بِرّ) ). ITHM (اِثْم) means culpability according to dictionary. According to Prophet Mohammed (S.A.A.W) “ ‏اَلْبِرُّ مَا اطْمَأَنَّتْ إِلَيْهِ النَّفْسُ وَالْإِثْمُ مَا ‏ ‏حَاكَ فِی صَدْرِكَ”  A virtue is something which brings content to your heart, and vice is that which brings discontent.
Thus ITHM (اِثْم) is that condition of heart that stops from good deeds and encourages vice and sinful activities and when time comes a person cannot resist from sin. ITHM (اِثْم) is related more to heart than to act and such a person is called ATHEEM (اِثِیْم) (Opposite SALEEM (سَلِیْم)). Allah says in the Quran
Surah Al-Maeda (The table spread): سورۃ المَائدہ 5:2
وَتَعَاوَنُواْ عَلَى ٱلۡبِرِّ وَٱلتَّقۡوَىٰ‌ۖ وَلَا تَعَاوَنُواْ عَلَى ٱلۡإِثۡمِ وَٱلۡعُدۡوَٲنِ‌ۚ
And cooperate with one another in virtuous conduct and conscience, and do not cooperate with one another in sin and hostility.
In another place in the Quran
Surah Al-Baqarah (The cow): سورۃ البَقَرَۃ  2:283
وَلَا تَكۡتُمُواْ ٱلشَّهَـٰدَةَ‌ۚ وَمَن يَڪۡتُمۡهَا فَإِنَّهُ ۥۤ ءَاثِمٌ۬ قَلۡبُهُ ۥ‌ۗ
And do not conceal testimony. Whoever conceals it is sinner at heart.
14.6 IJRAAM (اِجْرَام):   JURM (جُرْم) is an action that is punishable by law. But that type of action is not right by both Quran and dictionary as well. JURM (جُرْم) and JAREEMAH (جَرِیْمَۃ) means someone who commits huge sins. AJRAMA (اَجْرَمَ) means the misfortune that comes from a sin (  dictionary al Manjad)  . JURM (جُرْم) is every such act which is not legal and not as a result of some obligatory or worthy action. Allah says in the Quran
Surah Hud (Hud): سورۃ ھود 11:35
قُلۡ إِنِ ٱفۡتَرَيۡتُهُ ۥ فَعَلَىَّ إِجۡرَامِى وَأَنَا۟ بَرِىٓءٌ۬ مِّمَّا تُجۡرِمُونَ
Say, “If I made it up, upon me falls my crime, and I am innocent of the crimes you commit.”
14.7 JUNAH (جَنَاح):   Doesn’t actually mean sin but to sway towards a sin, to incline to sinful activities, JANAHA (جَنَحَ) means to incline or lean towards (  dictionary al Manjad)  . In the Quran it’s a common phrase “لَا جُنَاحَ عَلَیْکُمْ” or “لَیْسَ عَلَیْکُمْ جُنَاحٌ” meaning there is no encumbrance, or not a punishable or convictable thing. Like in the Quran
Surah Al-Baqarah (The cow): سورۃ البَقَرَۃ  2:236
لَّا جُنَاحَ عَلَيۡكُمۡ إِن طَلَّقۡتُمُ ٱلنِّسَآءَ مَا لَمۡ تَمَسُّوهُنَّ
There is no sin on you, if you divorce women while yet you have not touched
And JANAHA   (جَنَحَ)   (Plural MAFTUHA   (مفتوحہ)   means arm, wing or side ) is used for inclination towards virtue. Like in the Quran
Surah Al-Isra (The Night Journey): سُوۡرَةُ الإسرَاء 17:24
وَٱخۡفِضۡ لَهُمَا جَنَاحَ ٱلذُّلِّ مِنَ ٱلرَّحۡمَةِ
And lower to them the wing of humility, out of mercy
In another place in the Quran
Surah Ash-Shura’ (The Poets): صورۃ الشُّعْراء 26:215
وَٱخۡفِضۡ جَنَاحَكَ لِمَنِ ٱتَّبَعَكَ مِنَ ٱلۡمُؤۡمِنِينَ
And lower your wing to those of the believers who follow you.
14.8 LAMAM (لَمَمْ):   Those tiny mistakes and sins that lead to committing bigger sins. And ALAMA (اَلَمَ) means to commit small vices or sins (  dictionary al Manjad)  . For instance before adultery visiting a stranger woman, to talk freely with her. Or opinions and advices related to theft before actually committing a theft. Allah says in the Quran
Surah An-Najm (the star): سورۃ النَّجم 53:32
ٱلَّذِينَ يَجۡتَنِبُونَ كَبَـٰٓٮِٕرَ ٱلۡإِثۡمِ وَٱلۡفَوَٲحِشَ إِلَّا ٱللَّمَمَ‌ۚ إِنَّ رَبَّكَ وَٲسِعُ ٱلۡمَغۡفِرَةِ‌ۚ
Those who avoid gross sins and indecencies—except for minor lapses—your Lord is of Vast Forgiveness.
Summary:
14.1 ZAMB: Common word for any level or kind of sin
14.2 KHATA: A sin committed unintentionally
14.3 HUUB: The bigger sins that are related to family, Sin for which castigation should be opted.
14.4 HINTH: To break an oath or vow, sins related to oaths and vows
14.5 ITHM: Constant inclination towards sin, and not refraining from committing a sin
14.6 IJRAAM: The crime or burden or greater sins,
14.7 JUNAH: Inclination towards sins,
14.8 LAMAM: The small sins that lead to bigger sins.

 ٱلَّذِينَ يَجۡتَنِبُونَ كَبَـٰٓٮِٕرَ ٱلۡإِثۡمِ وَٱلۡفَوَٲحِشَ إِلَّا ٱللَّمَمَ‌ۚ إِنَّ رَبَّكَ وَٲسِعُ ٱلۡمَغۡفِرَةِ‌ۚ

Those who avoid gross sins and indecencies—except for minor lapses—your Lord is of Vast Forgiveness.

Summary:

14.1 ZAMB: Common word for any level or kind of sin

14.2 KHATA: A sin committed unintentionally

14.3 HUUB: The bigger sins that are related to family, Sin for which castigation should be opted.

14.4 HINTH: To break an oath or vow, sins related to oaths and vows

14.5 ITHM: Constant inclination towards sin, and not refraining from committing a sin

14.6 IJRAAM: The crime or burden or greater sins,

14.7 JUNAH: Inclination towards sins,

14.8 LAMAM: The small sins that lead to bigger sins.

title: content/gg/gg15.html
raw_text:
15 GUNEHGAR [sinner]
Synonyms: AATHM, AETHM, KHATI’, MUJRIM, FAASIQ, FAAJIR
AATHM (اٰثِم), AETHM (اَیثَم), KHATI’ (خَطِئ), MUJRIM (مُجْرِم), have been discussed before in GUNAH (sin).
15.4 FAASIQ (فَاسِق):   FASAQA (فَسَقَ) someone who deviates from the path of virtue, vicious (  dictionary al Manjad). To break out of the circle of submission. To be careless on part of licit orders. FASIQ   (فَاسِق)   word is used for a habitual disobedient. An Immoral person. But a FAASIQ   (فَاسِق)   does distinguish a sinful act as sin and disobedience. Allah says in the Quran
Surah Al-Hujraat (The Inner Apartments): سُوۡرَةُ الحُجرَات 49:6
يَـٰٓأَيُّہَا ٱلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُوٓاْ إِن جَآءَكُمۡ فَاسِقُۢ بِنَبَإٍ۬ فَتَبَيَّنُوٓاْ
O you who have believed, if there comes to you a disobedient one with information, investigate,
15.5 FAAJIR (فَاجِر):   (Plural FUJJAR (فُجَّار), Opposite ABRAAR (ابرار)) FAJARA (فَجَرَ) to tear apart something on a wide scale. FAAJIR (فَاجِر) is someone who disobeys religion or betrays religion’s rules. An immoral and vice person who keeps on committing sins and doesn’t repent. FAJOOR (فجور) is someone who is engrossed in committing sins. A debauched person (  dictionary al Manjad)  . FAJARA (فَجَرَ) means to be obstinate or stubborn, display stubbornness. FAAJIR (فاجر) is one who doesn’t consider a sin as bad. A bully or thug. Allah says in the Quran
Surah Al-Muţaffifīn (The Defrauding): سورة المطففين 83:7
كَلَّآ إِنَّ كِتَـٰبَ ٱلۡفُجَّارِ لَفِى سِجِّينٍ۬
Nay! Truly, the Record (writing of the deeds) of the Fujjar (disbelievers, sinners, evil-doers and wicked) is (preserved) in Sijjin.
Summary:
15.1 AATHM: One who sins sometimes, ATHEEM: Who has a vicious nature and is ready to do vice anytime.
15.2 KHATI’: Unintentional sinner
15.3 MUJRIM: He who commits a big or deadly sin.
15.4 FASIQ: Those sinners who consider a sin as bad

title: content/gg/gg16.html
raw_text:
16 GANADAGI – NAJASAT [filth,   uncleanness  ]
Synonyms: TAFATHA, RIJZ, RUJZ, RIJS
16.1 TAFATHA (تَفَثَ):   TAFATHA (تَفَثَ)     means something getting   unclean   or filthy; QADAA TAFITH (قَضٰی تَفِثَ) is to remove this kind of filth (  dictionary al Manjad)  . According to Abu- A’bedah it means to clip the nails, trimming the moustache, to put on a fragrance. And all the things that are forbidden for mehram except nikkah and the use of them like cleaning the body up, to clip the nails, to cut off the outgrown hair, to take a bath and wearing tidy clothes, putting on a fragrance. QADAA TAFITH (قَضٰی تَفِثَ) refers to all such things. Allah said in the Quran
Surah Al-Hajj (The Pilgrimage): سُوۡرَةُ الحَجّ 22:29
ثُمَّ لۡيَقۡضُواْ تَفَثَهُمۡ وَلۡيُوفُواْ نُذُورَهُمۡ وَلۡيَطَّوَّفُواْ بِٱلۡبَيۡتِ ٱلۡعَتِيقِ
Then let them end their untidiness and fulfill their vows and perform Tawaf around the ancient House."
16.2 RIJZ (رِجْز):   RAJAZA (رَجَزَ) means to spread anguish, RAJAZA FULLAN (رَجَزَ فُلَانٌ)     he read ‘agitated poems’. RIJZIA ASHAAR “ رجزیہ اشعار” are those poems that were sung or narrated during the war to motivate for the battle. In this phrase “عَزَابٌ مِّنْ رِجْزٍ اَلِیْم” RIJZ (رِجْز) means something that is causing agitation. And RIJZ (رِجْز)     are those evil thoughts that come from devil, motivating and influence heart for evil or wicked stuff. Allah says in the Quran
Surah Al-Anfal (The Spoils of War): سُوۡرَةُ الاٴنفَال 8:11
إِذۡ يُغَشِّيكُمُ ٱلنُّعَاسَ أَمَنَةً۬ مِّنۡهُ وَيُنَزِّلُ عَلَيۡكُم مِّنَ ٱلسَّمَآءِ مَآءً۬ لِّيُطَهِّرَكُم بِهِۦ وَيُذۡهِبَ عَنكُمۡ رِجۡزَ ٱلشَّيۡطَـٰنِ
When He caused calm to fall on you as a security from Him and sent down upon you water from the cloud that He might thereby purify you, and take away from you the uncleanness of the Shaitan,
Here ‘رِجۡزَ ٱلشَّيۡطَـٰنِ ’ refers to those thoughts from devil that could have brooded as a result of failure in the battle of badar.
RUJZ   (رُجْز)   and RIJZ   (رِجْز)   are actually same   (  dictionary al Manjad). And have the difference between them is same as the difference between HAMAL   (حَمْل)   and HIMAL   (حِمْل)   or WAQR    (وَقْر)   and WIQR   (وِقْر)    (See BAUJH [burden] for details). And it refers to all the evil thoughts that reside in heart. They can be related to   the sin of polytheism or some wicked thought. Allah says in the Quran
Surah Al-Muddaththir (The Cloaked One): سورۃ المدَّثّر 74:4
وَثِيَابَكَ فَطَهِّرۡ وَٱلرُّجۡزَ فَٱهۡجُرۡ
And your clothing purify. And uncleanliness avoid.
16.3 RIJS (رِجْس):   That filth or grim that is rendered impure by licit or Shairah laws (  dictionary al Manjad). This word can be used to depict filth both in material form and semantically. Allah says in the Quran
Surah Al-Ana’am (The cattle): سورۃ الانعام 6:145
إِلَّآ أَن يَكُونَ مَيۡتَةً أَوۡ دَمً۬ا مَّسۡفُوحًا أَوۡ لَحۡمَ خِنزِيرٍ۬ فَإِنَّهُ ۥ رِجۡسٌ
except carrion, or spilled blood, or the flesh of swine—because it is impure—
Another place in the Quran
Surah Al Tawbah (The repentance): سورۃ التوبھ 9:125
وَأَمَّا ٱلَّذِينَ فِى قُلُوبِهِم مَّرَضٌ۬ فَزَادَتۡہُمۡ رِجۡسًا إِلَىٰ رِجۡسِهِمۡ
And as for those in whose hearts is a disease, it adds uncleanness to their uncleanness
Here RIJS   (رِجْس)   means the filth or uncleanness of infidelity and polytheism. And here the words depicts its semantic meaning. (Also see ‘impure’)
Summary:
16.1 TAFATHA: Filth of body.
16.2 RIJZ: Thoughts of agitation from devil
16.3 RIJS: Filth of sordid and forbidden things.

title: content/gg/gg17.html
raw_text:
17 GIN-NA [to count]
Synonyms: ADDA, HASABA, AHSAA
17.1 ADDA (عَدََّ):   Means to count, to add up, to include. A very famous word. And ADDAD (عدد) means numeral or count. In the Quran
Surah Al-Kahf (The Cave): سورۃ الکھف 18:11
فَضَرَبۡنَا عَلَىٰٓ ءَاذَانِهِمۡ فِى ٱلۡكَهۡفِ سِنِينَ عَدَدً۬ا
So We cast [a cover of sleep] over their ears within the cave for a number of years.
17.2 HASABA (حَسَبَ):   YAHSABU (یَحْسَبُ), HISAABAN WA HUSBAANAN (حِسَابًا وَ حُسْبَانًا) means to count and to keep the count. Count systematically so that there is no difference in the calculation.
Surah Al-Ana’am (The cattle): سورۃ الانعام 6:96
وَجَعَلَ ٱلَّيۡلَ سَكَنً۬ا وَٱلشَّمۡسَ وَٱلۡقَمَرَ حُسۡبَانً۬ا‌ۚ
And He made the night for rest, and the sun and the moon for calculation.
17.3 AHSAA (اَحْصٰی):   HASAA (حَصٰی) means a pebble and HASAA YAHSI (حصی یحصی) means to pelt pebbles. The people of Arab use to count on pebbles due to unavailability of a chronologer. Thus this word also refers to counting. HASAA (حَصٰی) refers to two things 1. To count, 2. To keep a record of it or to remember it. It is related to ADDA (عَدََّ). Allah says in the Quran
Surah Ibraheem (Abraham): سورۃ ابراھیم 14:34
وَإِن تَعُدُّواْ نِعۡمَتَ ٱللَّهِ لَا تُحۡصُوهَآ‌ۗ
And if you count the Blessings of Allah, never will you be able to count them.
And sometimes it is used to refer to having the ability to count. Like in the Quran
Surah Al-Muzammil (The enshrouded one): سورۃ المُزمّل 73:20
عَلِمَ أَن لَّن تُحۡصُوهُ فَتَابَ عَلَيۡكُمۡ‌ۖ
He knows that you are unable to keep count thereof. So He has turned to you (in mercy):
Summary:
17.1 ADDA: To count
17.2 HASABA: To count systematically so no errors occur.
17.3 AHSAA: To count and keep a record of it.

title: content/gg/gg18.html
raw_text:
18 GAUD [cradle]
Synonyms: MAHD, HUJOOR
18.1 MAHD     (  مَھْد  ):   Rocker or provenience or the mother’s lap for an infant. Until an infant is lactating his mother lap becomes his cradle. This word is also for brought up or the ways of brought up. (Also see ‘BICHONA’ [Bed]). Allah says in the Quran
Surah Ale- Imran (The family of Imran): سورۃ آل عِمْرن 3:46
وَيُڪَلِّمُ ٱلنَّاسَ فِى ٱلۡمَهۡدِ وَڪَهۡلاً۬
He will speak to the people in the cradle and in maturity and will be of the righteous."
18.2 HUJOOR (  حُجُور  ):   (singular HIJR (حِجْر)) HUJR (حُجْر) means a cradle. The phrase “فُلاَنٌ فِیْ حِجْرِ فُلاَنٌ” means so and so  brought in so and so’s cradle or guardianship (  dictionary al Manjad) or under the charge of so and so or he is under limitation of financial and control by so and so. In the Quran
Surah An-Nisa (The women): سورۃ النِّسا 4:23
وَرَبَـٰٓٮِٕبُڪُمُ ٱلَّـٰتِى فِى حُجُورِڪُم
And your stepdaughters in your guardianship
Summary:
18.1 MAHD: Mother’s lap for an infant.
18.2:   HUJOOR: In case of older children their cradle refers to their guardian who can put limitations to their control, or who nurture them

And your stepdaughters in your guardianship

Summary:

18.1 MAHD: Mother’s lap for an infant.

18.2: HUJOOR: In case of older children their cradle refers to their guardian who can put limitations to their control, or who nurture them

19 GEHRA – GEHRAEE [Deep, Depth]
Synonyms: LUJJAHTAN, GAURAN, AMEEQ
19.1 LUJJAHTAN (  لُجَّةً  ):   LUJJ (لجّ) means the depth of water, that area of where water reaches its maximum depth. LUJJ-UL-BAHR (لُجُّ الْبَحر) means the utmost depth of a sea.  بَحۡرٍ۬ لُّجِّىٍّ۬  (24:20) means “ vast deep sea” LUJJAH (لُجَّة) means deep waters. Allah says in the Quran
Surah An-Naml (The ant): سورۃ النَّمل 27:44
فَلَمَّا رَأَتۡهُ حَسِبَتۡهُ لُجَّةً۬ وَكَشَفَتۡ عَن سَاقَيۡهَا‌ۚ
It was said to her, “Go inside the palace.” And when she saw it, she thought it was a deep pond, and she bared her legs.
19.2 GAURAN     (  غَوْر  ):   GHAARA (غَارَ) means to move to lower grounds. GHAR (غَار) Meaning cave is a famous word. GHAUR (غَوْر) means a declivity or a low ground, and underground depth. Thus this word refers to depth as well as some place. Allah says in the Quran
Surah Al-Mulk (The Sovereignty): سُوۡرَةُ المُلک67:30
قُلۡ أَرَءَيۡتُمۡ إِنۡ أَصۡبَحَ مَآؤُكُمۡ غَوۡرً۬ا فَمَن يَأۡتِيكُم بِمَآءٍ۬ مَّعِينِۭ
Say, "Have you considered: if your water was to become sunken [into the earth], then who could bring you flowing water?"
19.3 AMEEQ (  عَمِیْق  ):   UMQ (عُمْق) means a depth of something (Opposite IRTAFA’ (ارتفع) (loftiness)) If a distance is towards the horizon then it refers to distance or length, and if the distance is above the ground then the distance will be called IRTAFA’ (ارتفع) or loftiness lastly of distance goes below the level of ground, or is lower than the position where one stands than this distance will be UMQ (عُمْق) or depth. And AMEEQ (عَمِیْق) means deep. In the Quran
Surah Al-Hajj (The Pilgrimage): سُوۡرَةُ الحَجّ 22:27
يَأۡتِينَ مِن كُلِّ فَجٍّ عَمِيقٍ۬
Coming from every remote path,
In the above ayah AMEEQ (عَمِیْق) refers to far off because of FAJH (فَجّ). FAJH (فَجّ) refers to path between two mountains which is a contoured path containing elevations and depressions.
Summary:
19.1 LUJJAHTAN: Deep water, LUJJ means depth of water
19.2 GAURAN: Underground depth, lower ground
19.3 AMEEQ: Depth. Common word.

2. GARDISH (Circulation/Rotation)
Synonyms: RAIB(ALMANOON), DAIRA(DUR), DOOLATAN, DAWAL.
2.1 RAIB-(Al-MANOON)( (المنون)     رَيب):   Means suspicion and paranoia.        Conjecture    (for details, refer to SHAK-O-SHUBA). And MANAI(مَنَى) means to test. To involve. Also MANIYAT(مَنِيَّة) which means death. The will of God. And plurals of MANIYAT(مَنِيَّة) are MANAYA(مَنَايَا) and MANOON(مَنُون). And RAIB-AL-MANON(رَيب المنون) is used idiomatically when one person is in wait for the ruin or demise of another. And it is often translated from the circulation/passing of time (misfortunes). In the Quran:
Surat Aţ-Ţūr (The Mount) - سورة الطور 52:30
أَمْ يَقُولُونَ شَاعِرٌ نَّتَرَبَّصُ بِهِ رَيْبَ الْمَنُونِ
Or do they say [of you], "A poet for whom we await a misfortune of time?"
2.2 DAIRA  (دَائِرَة): DARA(دَارَ) Means to spin. Go in circles. And the word DAIRA(دَائِرَة) also has a negative connotation. In geometry it’s defined as a boundary (the circumference) consisting of points equidistant from a fixed center. Revolving around a centre. The hardships and fatalities of time. Hence the word is used in the negative sense. Which means to wait for a calamity or misfortune to befall someone.(Plural DAWAER دوائر). In the Quran:
Surat At-Tawbah (The Repentance) - سورة التوبة 9:98
وَمِنَ الْأَعْرَابِ مَن يَتَّخِذُ مَا يُنفِقُ مَغْرَمًا وَيَتَرَبَّصُ بِكُمُ الدَّوَائِرَ ۚ عَلَيْهِمْ دَائِرَةُ السَّوْءِ ۗ
And among the bedouins are some who consider what they spend as a loss and await for you turns of misfortune. Upon them will be a misfortune of evil.
Page 728--
2.3. DOOLATAN  (دُولَةً) and DAULATAN(دَولَةً), unlike DAIRA(دَائِرَة), are used in a good sense. DAL-AL-ZAMAAN(دال الزمان) means the turning of time from one situation/circumstances to another. It is used for the circulation of money, the times of happiness and their await. In the Quran:
1.  Surat Al-Ĥashr (The Exile) - سورة الحشر 59:7
كَيْ لَا يَكُونَ دُولَةً بَيْنَ الْأَغْنِيَاءِ مِنكُمْ ۚ
So that it will not be a perpetual distribution among the rich from among you.
2.   Surat 'Āli `Imrān (Family of Imran) - سورة آل عمران 3:140
وَتِلْكَ الْأَيَّامُ نُدَاوِلُهَا بَيْنَ النَّاسِ
And these days [of varying conditions] We alternate among the people.
Summary:
The difference in RAIB-UL-MANOON and DAIRAH is that RAIB-UL-MANOON is used for the death or acute severeness of a person whereas this severity is not found in DAIRAH and DOOLAT is used for the circulation towards pleasant times/periods.

20 GHAAT [Drinking place]
Synonyms: MASHRAB, WIRD
20.1 MASHRAB (مَشْرَبْ):   A place to drink or fetch water from. Drinking place. A common word
Surah Al-Baqarah (The cow): سورۃ البَقَرَۃ 2:60
قَدۡ عَلِمَ ڪُلُّ أُنَاسٍ۬ مَّشۡرَبَهُمۡ‌ۖ
And each tribe recognized its drinking-place.
20.2 WIRD (وِرْد):   WARADA (وَرَدَ) means to reach a place to drink water (Opposite SADAR (صَدَر) means to return from a place after drinking water). And WIRD (وِرْد) is place made for drinking water, like tanks are made for animals to drink water from. A thirsty is also known as WIRD   وِرۡدً۬ا (19:89). Allah says in the Quran
Surah Hud (Hud): سورۃ ھود 11:98
يَقۡدُمُ قَوۡمَهُ ۥ يَوۡمَ ٱلۡقِيَـٰمَةِ فَأَوۡرَدَهُمُ ٱلنَّارَ‌ۖ وَبِئۡسَ ٱلۡوِرۡدُ ٱلۡمَوۡرُودُ
He will go before his people on the Day of Resurrection and will lead them to the Fire for watering-place. Ah, hapless is the watering-place (whither they are) led.

title: content/gg/gg21.html
raw_text:
21 GHAATI [pass, way]
Synonyms: NAJAD, AQABAH
21.1 NAJAD (نَجَد):   Means a pass or a raised ground. Clear ground between trees. An elevated path   (  dictionary al Manjad). And NAJADA   (نَجَدَ)   means to be lofty and prominent   (  dictionary al Manjad) and an elevated and hard ground. NAJAD   (نَجَد)   refers to pass and also those paths which connect to the pass. Allah says in the Quran
Surah Al-Balad (The City): سورة البلد 90:10
وَهَدَيۡنَـٰهُ ٱلنَّجۡدَيۡنِ
And have shown him the two ways?
21.2 AQABAH   (عَقَبَةَ)  :   A mountain pass; or a perilous path to climb a mountain. Thus AQABAH   (عَقَبَةَ)   refers only to that path that leads to a pass or used for climbing a mountain, hence in the ayah below.
Surah Al-Balad (The City): سورة البلد 90:11
فَلَا ٱقۡتَحَمَ ٱلۡعَقَبَةَ وَمَآ أَدۡرَٮٰكَ مَا ٱلۡعَقَبَةُ
But he has not broken through the difficult pass. And what can make you know what is [breaking through] the difficult pass?
But According to dictionary al Manjad AQABAH (عَقَبَةَ) means a difficult pass, and a perilous path that is used to get on it
Summary:
21.1 NAJAD: Pass
21.2 AQABAH: A perilous pass
For GHABRANA and GHABRAHAT [Upset, Perturbation] see BEQARAR HONA [Upset, perturbation]

22 GHAR [Home]
Synonyms: BAIT, MASKAN, DAR, DIYAAR, AHL
22.1 BAIT (بَیْت):   BAATA (بَاتَ) means to spend a night. To sleep out. BAIT (بَیْت) is the place where one sleeps. Conventionally BAIT (بَیْت) refers to that place where a person and his family lives with him and spend their nights and that is their place of dwelling (Plural BUYOOT (بیوت)). Allah says in the Quran
Surah Al-Ahzaab (The clans): سورۃ الأحزَاب 33:33
وَقَرۡنَ فِى بُيُوتِكُنَّ وَلَا تَبَرَّجۡنَ تَبَرُّجَ ٱلۡجَـٰهِلِيَّةِ ٱلۡأُولَىٰۖ
And settle in your homes; and do not display yourselves, as in the former days of ignorance.
Allah has used the word BAIT (بَیْت) and ALBAIT (اَلْبَیْت) for KAABA too, and it also refers to same thing. Prophet Muhammad (S.A.W.W) said ‘الخلق عيال الله’ ‘All creatures are the dependents of Allah’. Though Kaaba is not a place to sleep but it is a place of dwelling
-------------
22 GHAR
[Home]
Synonyms: BAIT(  بيت  ), MASKAN(  مسكن  ), DAAR, DAYAR(  دار, ديار  ), AHAL(  أهل  )
22.1 bait(  بيت  )  : baat(  بات  ) meaning to spend night, and bait means that place where you spend night. Literally, bait(  بيت)   means that place where a person and his family living with him can spend the night and that is their abode. Allah states that:
________________
Surat Al-Ahzab (The Clans) -   سُوۡرَةُ الاٴحزَاب
33:33
وَقَرۡنَ فِى بُيُوتِكُنَّ وَلَا تَبَرَّجۡنَ تَبَرُّجَ ٱلۡجَـٰهِلِيَّةِ ٱلۡأُولَىٰۖ
And stay in your houses. Bedizen not yourselves with the bedizenment of the Time of Ignorance.   Be regular in prayer, and pay the poor-due, and obey Allah and His messenger. Allah's wish is but to remove uncleanness far from you, O Folk of the Household, and cleanse you with a thorough cleansing.
________________
And for Kaaba as well, Allah has used the words bait(  بيت  ) and al-bait(  البيت  ). This also constitutes the mentioned relationship. The Prophet PBUH said that   الخلق عيال الله   And although Kaaba is not a place to spend the night but is definitely an abode.
________________
22.2 maskan (  مسكن  ):   sakan(  سكن  ) meaning to inhabit. Also it means to rest after some work. And maskan(  مسكن  ) is that place where a person lives and to let a person live somewhere without taking rent is called sukni(  سكني  ). People living in a home are called sukn(  سكن  ) which is the plural of saakin(  ساكن  ). The word maskan(  مسكن  ) has been derived from the word bait(  بيت  ) because bait(  بيت  ) is used for living and night spending whereas maskan(  مسكن  ) only refers to the place of stay. Thus every bait(  بيت  ) is maskan(  مسكن  ) but every maskan(  مسكن  ) is not bait(  بيت  ). Allah states that:
________________
Surat Al-Qasas(The Story) -   سُوۡرَةُ القَصَص
28:58
فَتِلۡكَ مَسَـٰكِنُهُمۡ لَمۡ تُسۡكَن مِّنۢ بَعۡدِهِمۡ إِلَّا قَلِيلاً۬‌ۖ
And how many a community have We destroyed that was thankless for its means of livelihood!   And yonder are their dwellings, which have not been inhabited after them save a little.   And We, even We, were the inheritors.
________________
22.3 daar(  دار  )(pl: door   دور   and dayar   ديار  )  : meaning home, house. Daar(  دار  ) has been used in wide senses which constitutes home, mansion, village, city, country, all world and hereafter (for details, see ‘sheher’).  And when daar(  دار)   is used for residence, then it means house whereas bait(  بيت  ) means a home. Furthermore, when daar(  دار  ) is used in terms of a house, then its plural will also be daar(  دار  ). It is stated in the Quran:
________________
Surat Hud -   سُوۡرَةُ هُود
11:65
فَقَالَ تَمَتَّعُواْ فِى دَارِڪُمۡ ثَلَـٰثَةَ أَيَّامٍ۬‌ۖ
But they hamstrung her,   and then he said: enjoy life in your dwelling-place three days!   This is a threat that will not be belied.
________________
22.4 ahal (  أهل  )  : ahal(  أهل  ) is also used in wide definitions (For details and difference between ahal(  أهل)   and aal(  أل)  , see ‘aulad’(  اولاد)  ). In common terms, ahal-arrijaal(  اهل الرجال  ) means man of the house and ahal-o-ayal(  اهل و عيال  ) means wife and children whom he supports. As the word qarya(  قرية  ) is used for village as well as people living in the village, similarly, ahal(  أهل  ) is used for people living in the house as well as the house itself. Allah states that:
________________
Surat Al-E-Imran(Family of Imran) -   سُوۡرَةُ آل عِمرَان
3:121

22 GHAR [Home]

Synonyms: BAIT, MASKAN, DAR, DIYAAR, AHL

22.1 BAIT (بَیْت): BAATA (بَاتَ) means to spend a night. To sleep out. BAIT (بَیْت) is the place where one sleeps. Conventionally BAIT (بَیْت) refers to that place where a person and his family lives with him and spend their nights and that is their place of dwelling (Plural BUYOOT (بیوت)). Allah says in the Quran

Surah Al-Ahzaab (The clans): سورۃ الأحزَاب 33:33

وَقَرۡنَ فِى بُيُوتِكُنَّ وَلَا تَبَرَّجۡنَ تَبَرُّجَ ٱلۡجَـٰهِلِيَّةِ ٱلۡأُولَىٰۖ

 And settle in your homes; and do not display yourselves, as in the former days of ignorance. 

Allah has used the word BAIT (بَیْت) and ALBAIT (اَلْبَیْت) for KAABA too, and it also refers to same thing. Prophet Muhammad (S.A.W.W) said ‘الخلق عيال الله’ ‘All creatures are the dependents of Allah’. Though Kaaba is not a place to sleep but it is a place of dwelling

 

-------------

22 GHAR

[Home]

Synonyms: BAIT(بيت), MASKAN(مسكن), DAAR, DAYAR(دار, ديار), AHAL(أهل)

22.1 bait(بيت): baat(بات) meaning to spend night, and bait means that place where you spend night. Literally, bait(بيت) means that place where a person and his family living with him can spend the night and that is their abode. Allah states that:

________________

Surat Al-Ahzab (The Clans) - سُوۡرَةُ الاٴحزَاب

33:33

وَقَرۡنَ فِى بُيُوتِكُنَّ وَلَا تَبَرَّجۡنَ تَبَرُّجَ ٱلۡجَـٰهِلِيَّةِ ٱلۡأُولَىٰۖ

And stay in your houses. Bedizen not yourselves with the bedizenment of the Time of Ignorance. Be regular in prayer, and pay the poor-due, and obey Allah and His messenger. Allah's wish is but to remove uncleanness far from you, O Folk of the Household, and cleanse you with a thorough cleansing.

________________

And for Kaaba as well, Allah has used the words bait(بيت) and al-bait(البيت). This also constitutes the mentioned relationship. The Prophet PBUH said that الخلق عيال الله And although Kaaba is not a place to spend the night but is definitely an abode.

________________

22.2 maskan (مسكن): sakan(سكن) meaning to inhabit. Also it means to rest after some work. And maskan(مسكن) is that place where a person lives and to let a person live somewhere without taking rent is called sukni(سكني). People living in a home are called sukn(سكن) which is the plural of saakin(ساكن). The word maskan(مسكن) has been derived from the word bait(بيت) because bait(بيت) is used for living and night spending whereas maskan(مسكن) only refers to the place of stay. Thus every bait(بيت) is maskan(مسكن) but every maskan(مسكن) is not bait(بيت). Allah states that:

________________

Surat Al-Qasas(The Story) - سُوۡرَةُ القَصَص

28:58

فَتِلۡكَ مَسَـٰكِنُهُمۡ لَمۡ تُسۡكَن مِّنۢ بَعۡدِهِمۡ إِلَّا قَلِيلاً۬‌ۖ

And how many a community have We destroyed that was thankless for its means of livelihood! And yonder are their dwellings, which have not been inhabited after them save a little. And We, even We, were the inheritors.

________________

22.3 daar(دار)(pl: door دور and dayar ديار): meaning home, house. Daar(دار) has been used in wide senses which constitutes home, mansion, village, city, country, all world and hereafter (for details, see ‘sheher’).  And when daar(دار) is used for residence, then it means house whereas bait(بيت) means a home. Furthermore, when daar(دار) is used in terms of a house, then its plural will also be daar(دار). It is stated in the Quran:

________________

Surat Hud - سُوۡرَةُ هُود

11:65

فَقَالَ تَمَتَّعُواْ فِى دَارِڪُمۡ ثَلَـٰثَةَ أَيَّامٍ۬‌ۖ

But they hamstrung her, and then he said: enjoy life in your dwelling-place three days! This is a threat that will not be belied.

________________

22.4 ahal (أهل): ahal(أهل) is also used in wide definitions (For details and difference between ahal(أهل) and aal(أل), see ‘aulad’(اولاد)). In common terms, ahal-arrijaal(اهل الرجال) means man of the house and ahal-o-ayal(اهل و عيال) means wife and children whom he supports. As the word qarya(قرية) is used for village as well as people living in the village, similarly, ahal(أهل) is used for people living in the house as well as the house itself. Allah states that:

________________

Surat Al-E-Imran(Family of Imran) - سُوۡرَةُ آل عِمرَان

3:121

وَإِذۡ غَدَوۡتَ مِنۡ أَهۡلِكَ تُبَوِّئُ ٱلۡمُؤۡمِنِينَ مَقَـٰعِدَ لِلۡقِتَالِ‌ۗ

And remember when thou settedst forth at daybreak from thy housefolk to assign to the believers their positions for the battle, Allah was Hearer, Knower.

________________

2. MASKAN(مسكن): meaning just to live there, even not having a place to spend night.

3. DAAR(دار): its use is very common. If used in terms of house, it refers to the exit status of the house i.e. there could be many bait in one daar.

4. AHAL(أهل): house, people living in the house, family; all these come under its meaning.

raw_text:
23 GHARI
[Clock, time, period]
Synonyms: SA’A(  ساعة  ), AANA(  أناء  ), ZULF(  زلف  )
23.1 sa’a(  ساعة  )  : a specified period of time, instant (pl. saa’at(  ساعات  )). The people of Arab had divided the day and night into periods of 12 hours each and given them specific names whose details can be found in ‘din’ and ‘raat’. Nowadays as well, the complete period of day and night is divided into 24 hours. Thus, sa’a(  ساعة)   can also be used to depict one hour as Allah states that:
________________
Surat Al-Ahqaf (The Dunes) -   سُوۡرَةُ الاٴحقاف
46:35
لۡمۡ يَلۡبَثُوٓاْ إِلَّا سَاعَةً۬ مِّن نَّہَارِۭ‌ۚ
Then have patience (O Muhammad) even as the stout of heart among the messengers (of old) had patience, and seek not to hasten on the doom for them. On the day when they see that which they are promised (it will seem to them)   as though they had tarried but an hour of daylight.   A clear message. Shall any be destroyed save evil-living folk?
________________
And sa’a(  ساعة)   can also refer to a watch. And sa’ati(  ساعاتى  ) means a person who owns a shop of watches. Sometimes, sa’a(  ساعة)   also refers to a period or times which can comprise not only a complete day but even many days, months or years. Allah states that:
________________
Surat Tawba (Repentance) -   سُوۡرَةُ التّوبَة
9:117
لَّقَد تَّابَ ٱللَّهُ عَلَى ٱلنَّبِىِّ وَٱلۡمُهَـٰجِرِينَ وَٱلۡأَنصَارِ ٱلَّذِينَ ٱتَّبَعُوهُ فِى سَاعَةِ ٱلۡعُسۡرَةِ
Allah hath turned in mercy to the Prophet, and to the Muhajirin and the Ansar who followed him in the hour of hardship.   After the hearts of a party of them had almost swerved aside, then turned He unto them in mercy. Lo! He is Full of Pity, Merciful for them.
________________
And as-sa’a(  الساعة  ) refers to the day of judgment. As is stated:
________________
Surat Al-Anaam (Cattle) -   سُوۡرَةُ الاٴنعَام
6:31
حَتَّىٰٓ إِذَا جَآءَتۡہُمُ ٱلسَّاعَةُ بَغۡتَةً۬
They indeed are losers who deny their meeting with Allah   until, when the Hour cometh on them suddenly  , they cry: Alas for us, that we neglected it! They bear upon their backs their burdens. Ah, evil is that which they bear!
________________
23.2 aana (  أناء  )  : aan(  آن  ) meaning a period of time (pl. aana(  أناء  )) and anaa yaani(  أني ياني  ) meaning the time of something has reached and it has reached its limit. Furthermore, anaa(  أني  ) meaning a complete day or some part of it but in the Quran, the word aana(  أناء  ) has been used thrice at 3:113, 20:13, 39:9 and in all these places, the word lail(  ليل  )(night) has been used with aana(  أناء  ). It has never been used with day. Thus it can be understood that the word aana(  أناء)   is associated with the hours of night. Allah states that:
________________
Surat Al-E-Imran (Family of Imran) -   سُوۡرَةُ آل عِمرَان
3:113
يَتۡلُونَ ءَايَـٰتِ ٱللَّهِ ءَانَآءَ ٱلَّيۡلِ وَهُمۡ يَسۡجُدُونَ
They are not all alike. Of the People of the Scripture there is a staunch community   who recite the revelations of Allah in the night season, falling prostrate (before Him).
________________
23.3 zulf(  زلف  )  : meaning the initial part of night or first hours. The basic meanings of zulf(  زلف  ) are of status and closeness. The first part of night is called zulf(  زلف  ) because it is the nearest and close part of the complete night. Allah states that:
________________
Surat Hud  -   سُوۡرَةُ هُود
11:114
أَقِمِ ٱلصَّلَوٰةَ طَرَفَىِ ٱلنَّہَارِ وَزُلَفً۬ا مِّنَ ٱلَّيۡلِ‌ۚ
Establish worship at the two ends of the day and in some watches of the night.   Lo! good deeds annul ill-deeds. This is reminder for the mindful.
________________
Summary:
1.SA’A(  ساعة  ): a particular time of day or night, era, day of judgment.
2. AANA(  أناء  ): hours of night.
3. ZULF(  زلف  ): initial hours or part of night.

24 GHUSNA
[To enter]
Synonyms: WALAJA(  ولج  ), JASA(  جاس  )(JAUS   جوس  )
24.1 walaja(  ولج  )  : to enter a narrow place, go inside. It is stated in the Quran:
________________
Surat Al-Araf (The Heights) -   سُوۡرَةُ الاٴعرَاف
7:40
وَلَا يَدۡخُلُونَ ٱلۡجَنَّةَ حَتَّىٰ يَلِجَ ٱلۡجَمَلُ فِى سَمِّ ٱلۡخِيَاطِ‌ۚ
Lo! they who deny Our revelations and scorn them, for them the gates of heaven will nor be   opened not will they enter the Garden until the camel goeth through the needle's eye.   Thus do We requite the guilty.
________________
24.2 jasa (  جاس  )  : meaning to reach the middle of something and meaning to reach the limits in desire of something. And jasa fi-lbait(  جاس في البيت  ) meaning that he entered the house for burglary and crime. And jawwas(  جواس  ) meaning to create chaos in a nation. It is stated in the Quran:
________________
Surat Al-Isra (Children of Israel) -   سُوۡرَةُ بنیٓ اسرآئیل / الإسرَاء
17:5
بَعَثۡنَا عَلَيۡڪُمۡ عِبَادً۬ا لَّنَآ أُوْلِى بَأۡسٍ۬ شَدِيدٍ۬ فَجَاسُواْ خِلَـٰلَ ٱلدِّيَارِ‌ۚ
So when the time for the first of the two came,   We roused against you slaves of Ours of great might who ravaged (your) country  , and it was a threat performed.
________________
Summary:
1.WALAJA(  ولج  ): used to show entering in a narrow space.
2. JASA(  جاس  ): to enter to create chaos and destruction.

title: content/gg/gg25.html
raw_text:
25 GHASEETNA
[To drag]
Synonyms: JARRA(  جر  ), SAHABA (  سحب  ), A’TALA(  عتل  )
25.1 jarra(  جر  )  : the aspect of pulling is more evident in jarra(  جر  ) as compared to dragging. To pull in the upward direction or to pull something stationary such that it is no longer stable and it starts to drag is called jarr(  جر  ). It is stated in the Quran:
________________
Surat Al-Araf(The Heights) -   سُوۡرَةُ الاٴعرَاف
7:150
وَأَخَذَ بِرَأۡسِ أَخِيهِ يَجُرُّهُ ۥۤ إِلَيۡهِ‌ۚ
And when Moses returned unto his people, angry and grieved, he said: Evil is that (course) which ye took after I had left you. Would ye hasten on the judgment of your Lord? And he cast down the tablets,   and he seized his brother by the head, dragging him toward him  . He said: Son of my mother! Lo! the folk did judge me weak and almost killed me. Oh, make not mine enemies to triumph over me and place me not among the evil-doers.
________________
And jaishun-jarrarun(  جيش جرار  ) is used for such a big group of people which advances and covers a vast area as if it is advancing through pulling and dragging.
________________
25.2 sahaba (  سحب  )  : the aspect of dragging is more prominent in sahaba(  سحب)   and less of pulling. According to Imam Raghib, it means to drag someone upon his face, when something is lying down instead of being upright or is in a horizontal position as compared to vertical and it is then dragged, then it will be sahaba(  سحب  ). And sahaab(  سحاب  ) meaning clouds. Sahaab(  سحاب)   is used for clouds because (i)wind drags them (ii) and it itself advances as if it is being dragged. It is stated in the Quran:
________________
Surat Al-Qamar (The Moon) -   سُوۡرَةُ القَمَر
54:48
يَوۡمَ يُسۡحَبُونَ فِى ٱلنَّارِ عَلَىٰ وُجُوهِهِمۡ
On the day when they are dragged into the Fire upon their faces   (it is said unto them): Feel the touch of hell
________________
25.3 a’tala(  عتل  )  : a’tala(  عتل)   includes the aspect of roughness and toughness as compared to jarra(  جر)  . According to the people of lexical jurisprudence, it means to put something in the neck and use it to drag someone roughly. It is stated in the Quran:
________________
Surat Ad-Dukhan (Smoke) -   سُوۡرَةُ الدّخان
44:47
خُذُوهُ فَٱعۡتِلُوهُ إِلَىٰ سَوَآءِ ٱلۡجَحِيمِ
(And it will be said):   Take him and drag him to the midst of hell
________________
Summary:
JARRA(  جر  ): To pull a stationary object in such a way that it starts to drag. And when this jarra(  جر  ) include roughness and brutality, it becomes a’atala(  عتل)  . And when you drag something that is lying around, it is sahaba(  سحب  ).

يَوۡمَ يُسۡحَبُونَ فِى ٱلنَّارِ عَلَىٰ وُجُوهِهِمۡ

On the day when they are dragged into the Fire upon their faces (it is said unto them): Feel the touch of hell

________________

25.3 a’tala(عتل): a’tala(عتل) includes the aspect of roughness and toughness as compared to jarra(جر). According to the people of lexical jurisprudence, it means to put something in the neck and use it to drag someone roughly. It is stated in the Quran:

________________

Surat Ad-Dukhan (Smoke) - سُوۡرَةُ الدّخان

44:47

خُذُوهُ فَٱعۡتِلُوهُ إِلَىٰ سَوَآءِ ٱلۡجَحِيمِ

(And it will be said): Take him and drag him to the midst of hell

________________

Summary:

JARRA(جر): To pull a stationary object in such a way that it starts to drag. And when this jarra(جر) include roughness and brutality, it becomes a’atala(عتل). And when you drag something that is lying around, it is sahaba(سحب).

26 GHORRA
[Horse]
Synonyms: KHAIL(  خيل  ), SAFINAAT(  صفنت  ), JIYAD(  جياد  ) JAUD(  جود)  , A’ADIYAT(  عاديات  ) ADAD(  عدد)
26.1 khail(  خيل  )  : Khail(  خيل   )is unisex i.e. it can be used for any kind of horse either it is male or female. It is also used to refer to a group or herd of horses as ghanam(  غنم  ) is used for a herd of goats. It is also used to refer to a horse rider. Allah states that:
________________
Surat An-Nahl(The Bee) -   سُوۡرَةُ النّحل
16:8
وَٱلۡخَيۡلَ وَٱلۡبِغَالَ وَٱلۡحَمِيرَ لِتَرۡڪَبُوهَا وَزِينَةً۬‌ۚ
And horses and mules and asses (hath He created) that ye may ride them, and for ornament  . And He createth that which ye know not.
________________
In this ayat, khail(  خيل  ) is used as a unisex and in the following ayats, khail(  خيل  ) is used for a horse rider or collectively for horse rider and his horse. Allah states that:
________________
Surat Al-Isra(Children of Israel) -   سُوۡرَةُ بنیٓ اسرآئیل / الإسرَاء
17:64
وَأَجۡلِبۡ عَلَيۡہِم بِخَيۡلِكَ وَرَجِلِكَ
And excite any of them whom thou canst with thy voice, and urge thy horse and foot against them  , and be a partner in their wealth and children, and promise them. Satan promiseth them only to deceive
________________
The basic meaning of khail(  خيل)   is having different kinds of thoughts in mind, and the word khayal(  خيال  ) is derived from it. And alkhaila(  الخيلاء  ) is used for such a sense of superiority which a horse rider feels as compared to a man on foot. Similarly, the word takhayyul(  تخيل  ) is derived from it meaning to know about something from wisdom, to fly high.
26.2 saafinaat (  صفنت  )  : plural of saafin(  صافن  ). Safana(  صفن)   meaning a horse standing on three legs in such a way that only the edge of the fourth foot is on the ground. And it refers to an active and energetic horse.
________________
26.3 jiyad (  جياد  )  : plural of jayyad(  جيد  ). Jood(  جود  ) means to have ampleness in something. And jawad(  جواد)   is used for a generous man or woman. Jaad al faras(  جاد الفرس  ) means a lively and fast horse. The word jayyad(  جيد  ) is also used to depict the finery of something. According to the people of lexical jurisprudence, jiyad(  جياد  ) means a fast and fine horse. It is stated in the Quran:
________________
Surat Sad -   سُوۡرَةُ صٓ
38:31
إِذۡ عُرِضَ عَلَيۡهِ بِٱلۡعَشِىِّ ٱلصَّـٰفِنَـٰتُ ٱلۡجِيَادُ
When there were shown to him at eventide lightfooted coursers
________________
26.4 a’adiyat (  عاديات  )  : plural of a’adiya(  عادية  ) and a’adiya(  عادية  ) is the feminine of a’adi(  عادي  ) and a’adi(  عادي  ) means that party which is ready for murder, chaos creating horses. A’d-al-fars(  عد الفرس  ) meaning that the horse took a leap. Ta’ad-al-qaum(  تعادي القوم  ) meaning people took part in a race. Thus a’adiyat(  عاديات  ) means those horses going to war which take part in races. Allah states that:
________________
Surat Adiyat (The Chargers) -   سُوۡرَةُ العَادیَات
100:1
وَٱلۡعَـٰدِيَـٰتِ ضَبۡحً۬ا
By the snorting coursers
________________
Summary:
1.KHAIL(  خيل  ): unisex, its use is common. Used for horse, horse rider or collectively for both.
2. SAFINAT(  صفنت  ): an active and energetic horse standing on three legs.
3. JIYAD(  جياد  ): fast and fine type of horses.
4. A’ADIYAT(  عاديات  ): those horses which take part in races and are trained for war.
For ‘ghoomna’, see ‘phirna’
