27 GHAIRNA
[To surround]
Synonyms: HAFFA(  حف  ), AHATA(  أحأط   )(HAUT)(   حوط  ), HASAR(  حصر  ), HAAQA(  حاق   )(HAIQ)(   حيق  )
27.1 haffa(  حف  )  : means to surround something from both sides and haffah bakza(  حفه بكذا  ) meaning to enclose and mahiffah(  محفة  ) meaning carriage, a moving cart which is covered from shades from all sides. It is stated in the Quran:
________________
Surat Al-Kahf (The Cave) -   سُوۡرَةُ الکهف
18:32
وَحَفَفۡنَـٰهُمَا بِنَخۡلٍ۬ وَجَعَلۡنَا بَيۡنَہُمَا زَرۡعً۬ا
Coin for them a similitude: Two men, unto one of whom   We had assigned two gardens of grapes, and We had surrounded both with date-palms   and had put between them tillage.
________________
At another place it is stated:
________________
Surat Az-Zumar (The Troops) -   سُوۡرَةُ الزُّمَر
39:75
وَتَرَى ٱلۡمَلَـٰٓٮِٕڪَةَ حَآفِّينَ مِنۡ حَوۡلِ ٱلۡعَرۡشِ
And thou (O Muhammad) seest the angels thronging round the Throne,   hymning the praises of their Lord. And they are judged aright. And it is said: Praise be to Allah, the Lord of the Worlds!
________________
27.2 ahata (  أحأط  )  : meaning to enclose, to build four sided walls, to surround something in such a way that it is kept safe in such a way that it cannot get out by itself nor can someone else take something out of it. Just like a house is enclosed in four sided walls. Allah states that:
________________
Surat Yunus  -   سُوۡرَةُ یُونس
10:22
وَجَآءَهُمُ ٱلۡمَوۡجُ مِن كُلِّ مَكَانٍ۬ وَظَنُّوٓاْ أَنَّہُمۡ أُحِيطَ بِهِمۡ‌ۙ
He it is Who maketh you to go on the land and the sea till, when ye are in the ships and they sail with them with a fair breeze and they are glad therein, a storm-wind reacheth them   and the wave cometh unto them from every side and they deem that they are overwhelmed therein  ; (then) they cry unto Allah, making their faith pure for Him only: If Thou deliver us from this, we truly will be of the thankful.
________________
This word is also used in the literal meaning. Allah states that:
________________
Surat Al-Baqarah (The Cow) -   سُوۡرَةُ البَقَرَة
2:81
بَلَىٰ مَن كَسَبَ سَيِّئَةً۬ وَأَحَـٰطَتۡ بِهِۦ خَطِيٓـَٔتُهُ ۥ فَأُوْلَـٰٓٮِٕكَ أَصۡحَـٰبُ ٱلنَّارِ‌ۖ
Nay, but whosoever hath done evil and his sin surroundeth him; such are rightful owners of the Fire  ; they will abide therein.
________________
27.3 ahsara(  احصر  )  : meaning to encircle, to surround something in such a way that it remains locked inside and cannot come outside, to detain someone and not let any kind of information, message or help to be passed inside. Allah states that:
________________
Surat Al-Tawba (Repentence) -   سُوۡرَةُ التّوبَة
9:5
وَٱحۡصُرُوهُمۡ وَٱقۡعُدُواْ لَهُمۡ ڪُلَّ مَرۡصَدٍ۬‌ۚ
Then, when the sacred months have passed, slay the idolaters wherever ye find them, and take them (captive),   and besiege them, and prepare for them each ambush  . But if they repent and establish worship and pay the poor-due, then leave their way free. Lo! Allah is Forgiving, Merciful.
________________
27.4 haaqa(  حاق  )  : meaning something to befall on something and meaning that something befallen on something and surround it. Thus any type of enclosure which a person being enclosed feels on himself; some kind of difficulty, problem or calamity to befall on someone. And haiq(  حيق  ) means reward or punishment for one’s actions; bad consequence of bad deeds thus this word is used in the negative sense. It is stated in the Quran:
________________
Surat Az-Zumar(The Troops) -   سُوۡرَةُ الزُّمَر
39:48
وَحَاقَ بِهِم مَّا كَانُواْ بِهِۦ يَسۡتَہۡزِءُونَ
And the evils that they earned will appear unto them, and that whereat they used to scoff will surround them.
________________
At another location, it is stated:
________________
Surat Fatir(The Angels) -   سُوۡرَةُ فَاطِر
35:43
وَلَا يَحِيقُ ٱلۡمَكۡرُ ٱلسَّيِّئُ إِلَّا بِأَهۡلِهِۚۦ
(Shown in their) behaving arrogantly in the land and plotting evil  ; and the evil plot encloseth but the men who make it  . Then, can they expect aught save the treatment of the folk of old? Thou wilt not find for Allah's way of treatment any substitute, nor wilt thou find for Allah's way of treatment aught of power to change.
________________
This part of the above mentioned ayat is also used as a proverb.
Summary:
1.HAFFA(  حف  ):means only to surround.
2. AHATA(  أحأط  ): means to surround in such a way as to protect.
3. AHSARA(  احصر  ): to enclose and detain.
4. HAAQA(  حاق  ): means some calamity to befall on someone.

3. GARDAN (Neck)
Synonyms: UNUQ, JEED, RAQBAT, WATEEN.
3.1 UNUQ(عُنُق):   Neck or Throat. Famous/Known part of a human body. It is commonly used. (Plural A’NAAQ اَعنَاق). In the Quran:
Surat Al-'Isrā' (The Night Journey) - سورة الإسراء 17:13
وَكُلَّ إِنسَانٍ أَلْزَمْنَاهُ طَائِرَهُ فِي عُنُقِهِ ۖ
And [for] every person We have imposed his fate upon his neck.
3.2 JEED(جِيد):   Thin and long neck. A beautiful neck like that of a deer. In the Quran:
Surat Al-Masad (The Palm Fiber, Flame) - سورة المسد 111:4
وَامْرَأَتُهُ حَمَّالَةَ الْحَطَبِْفِي جِيدِهَا حَبْلٌ مِّن مَّسَدٍْ
And his wife [as well] - the carrier of firewood. Around her neck is a rope of [twisted] fiber.
3.3 RAQABAT(رَقَبَة):   Means neck or the back part of it(nape). And RAQABA(رَقَبَ) means to put a rope or noose around a person’s neck. To guard or supervise. And generally, the Arabs say JAZ’-ASHARAF(جزء اشرف) and refer it as a total. Likewise, RAQBA(رقبة) is referred to a slave because he has a noose of slavery around his neck (Plural RIQAB رقاب).  And TEHREER-RAQBA(تحرير رقبة)  means to free the neck from this loop. Which means to free a slave. In the Quran:
Surat Al-Balad (The City) - سورة البلد 90:13
ْفَكُّ رَقَبَةٍْ وَمَا أَدْرَاكَ مَا الْعَقَبَةُ
And what can make you know what is [breaking through] the difficult pass?.It is the freeing of a slave
3.4 WATEEN (وَتِين):   Means the vein of the neck(aorta). The jugular vein which goes from heart to the brain. That side of neck where the jugular vein lies. In the Quran:
Surat Al-Ĥāqqah (The Reality) - سورة الحاقة 69: 45-46
لَأَخَذْنَا مِنْهُ بِالْيَمِينِْثُمَّ لَقَطَعْنَا مِنْهُ الْوَتِينَْ
We would have seized him by the right hand; Then We would have cut from him the aorta.
Summary:
1. UNQ: A common word for neck.
2. JEED: Long and beautiful neck
3. RAQABAT: The neck itself and its back part(Nape). Noose of slavery.
4. WATEEN: The front portion of the neck where the jugular vein lies.

3.3 RAQABAT(رَقَبَة): Means neck or the back part of it(nape). And RAQABA(رَقَبَ) means to put a rope or noose around a person’s neck. To guard or supervise. And generally, the Arabs say JAZ’-ASHARAF(جزء اشرف) and refer it as a total. Likewise, RAQBA(رقبة) is referred to a slave because he has a noose of slavery around his neck (Plural RIQAB رقاب).  And TEHREER-RAQBA(تحرير رقبة)  means to free the neck from this loop. Which means to free a slave. In the Quran:

Surat Al-Balad (The City) - سورة البلد 90:13

ْفَكُّ رَقَبَةٍْ وَمَا أَدْرَاكَ مَا الْعَقَبَةُ

And what can make you know what is [breaking through] the difficult pass?.It is the freeing of a slave

3.4 WATEEN (وَتِين): Means the vein of the neck(aorta). The jugular vein which goes from heart to the brain. That side of neck where the jugular vein lies. In the Quran:

Surat Al-Ĥāqqah (The Reality) - سورة الحاقة 69: 45-46

لَأَخَذْنَا مِنْهُ بِالْيَمِينِْثُمَّ لَقَطَعْنَا مِنْهُ الْوَتِينَْ

We would have seized him by the right hand; Then We would have cut from him the aorta.

 

Summary:

1. UNQ: A common word for neck.

2. JEED: Long and beautiful neck

3. RAQABAT: The neck itself and its back part(Nape). Noose of slavery.

4. WATEEN: The front portion of the neck where the jugular vein lies.

raw_text:
Page 729--
4. GIRIFT KARNA (To Grip)
Synonyms: AAKHAZA, SARRABA, LAMA.
4.1. AAKAHAZA(آخَزَ)  : Akhaza(اَخَزَ) means to catch/hold something, to achieve, to bring something in enclosure, and Aakhaza(آخَزَ) means to impeach or find fault, whether this impeachment is by words or by performance/behavior.  In the Quran:
Surat Al-Baqarah (The Cow) - سورة البقرة 2:286
رَبَّنَا لَا تُؤَاخِذْنَا إِن نَّسِينَا أَوْ أَخْطَأْنَا ۚ
"Our Lord, do not impose blame upon us if we have forgotten or erred.
4.2 SARRABA(ثَرَّبَ):   SARABA(ثَرَبَ) and SARRABA(ثَرَّبَ) means to declare someone’s work as bad and shameful. To punish or reprimand/scold on a mistake. In the Quran:
Surat Yūsuf (Joseph) - سورة يوسف 12:94
قَالَ لَا تَثْرِيبَ عَلَيْكُمُ الْيَوْمَ ۖ يَغْفِرُ اللَّهُ لَكُمْ ۖ
He said, "No blame will there be upon you today. Allah will forgive you.
4.3 LAAMA(لَام):   Means to insult someone for committing a bad deed. To blame/criticize and to warn someone for his/her deeds. And LAUM(لَوم) means criticize and fear. Therefore, LAAMA(لَام) is used when a doer, while doing an action, has a fear that he will be insulted whether this action is good or bad for a person. In the Quran:
Surat Al-Mā'idah (The Table Spread) - سورة المائدة 5:54
يُجَاهِدُونَ فِي سَبِيلِ اللَّهِ وَلَا يَخَافُونَ لَوْمَةَ لَائِمٍ ۚ
They strive in the cause of Allah and do not fear the blame of a critic.
Summary:
1. AAKHAZA: To impeach or find fault in some undesirable action.
2. TASREEB: Means scolding. Reproof. Is more hard than insult.
3. LAUMA: To insult, whether the action is bad or not. It does not has the intensity as of TASREEB.

5. GARMI-GARAM KARNA-HONA (Hotness/Heat, To Heat- Be Heated)
Synonyms: SUAIF, HARR, HAMM, HAMI, SAQAR, SAMOOM.
5.1 SUAIF(صَيف):   Summer season. And SUAI’IF(صَيِّف) means the rainfall of summer and the grass grown due to it. SUAF(صَاف) and SUAI’AF(صَيَّف) means to spend summer season somewhere. In the Quran:
Surat Quraysh (Quraysh) - سورة قريش 106:2
إِيلَافِهِمْ رِحْلَةَ الشِّتَاءِ وَالصَّيْفِ
Their accustomed security [in] the caravan of winter and summer -
5.2 HARR(حَرّ):   Means temperature or heat. Whether it’s caused by fire or Sun(Sunlight). Like when heat is produced when rubbing two things together. However, this word is usually applied to the virulence of the sun. And HAROOR(حَرُوْر) means radiance/heat. Hot wind(Also look DHOOP).
Page 730--
In the Quran:
Surat At-Tawbah (The Repentance) - سورة التوبة 9:81
وَقَالُوا لَا تَنفِرُوا فِي الْحَرِّ ۗ قُلْ نَارُ جَهَنَّمَ أَشَدُّ حَرًّا ۚ
And they said, 'Do not go forth in the heat." Say, "The fire of Hell is more intensive in heat"
5.3. HAMMA(  حَمّ  )
5.4. HAMIA(حمى):   These two words are so close/similar in meaning that it is difficult  to distinguish between them. That is why Philologists take both their derivatives according to both these root words. There are four means to obtain heat; Fire and sunlight are materialistic means, and heat of emotions/desires and natural heat(of a body). In all these four resources, these two roots are used. If there’s any difference, it’s that HAMMA(حَمّ) is used as a transitive(verb) and HAMIA(حَمِىَ) as intransitive(verb). But when passive voice is used, then they become synonyms. For instance, HAMMAL-MA’(حَمَّ الْمَاء) means to heat-up water. And HUMMA-RRAJUL(حَمَّ الرَّجُل) means a person has got fever. And HUMMA(حُمَّى) means fever. The Philologists have written in subjection to both roots. HAMMAT-TANOOR(حَمَّ التَّنُور) means heated a stove. And HAMIAN-NAAR(حمى النار) means that fire flared up. And HAMEEM(حميم) means hot water and also cold water( LUGHAT AZDAAD لغت اضداد i.e. it has opposite meanings). And it also means a zealous friend or relative. This belongs to emotions/feelings. And HAMMAZ-ZAHIRAT(حَمَّ الظَّهِيرَة) refers to the extreme hotness during midday. And HAMMAT(حَمَّة) means a fountain of hot water. And HUMMAT(حُمَّة) means coal. Everything burned up in fire or ashes. And HAMAAM(حمام) means a place for bath/ablution with hot water. Now inspect their following examples. In the Quran:
1.   Surat Al-'An`ām (The Cattle) - سورة الأنعام 6:70
لَهُمْ شَرَابٌ مِّنْ حَمِيمٍ وَعَذَابٌ أَلِيمٌ بِمَا كَانُوا يَكْفُرُونَ
For them will be a drink of scalding water and a painful punishment because they used to disbelieve.
2.   Surat Al-Ma`ārij (The Ascending Stairways) - سورة المعارج 70:10
وَلَا يَسْأَلُ حَمِيمٌ حَمِيمًا
And no friend will ask [anything of] a friend.
3.   Surat Al-Qāri`ah (The Calamity) - سورة القارعة 101: 10-11
نَارٌ حَامِيَةٌ وَمَا أَدْرَاكَ مَا هِيَهْ
And what can make you know what that is? It is a Fire, intensely hot.
4.   Surat Al-Fatĥ (The Victory) - سورة الفتح 48:26
إِذْ جَعَلَ الَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا فِي قُلُوبِهِمُ الْحَمِيَّةَ حَمِيَّةَ الْجَاهِلِيَّةِ
When those who disbelieved had put into their hearts chauvinism - the chauvinism of the time of ignorance.
5.5. SAQARA(سَقَرَ):   Means the scorching of fire or sunlight. SAQARAT-HUSH-SHAMS(سَقَرَتهُ الشَّمْس) means the fire burned/scorched him/her. Then this word has become notorious for hell. In the Quran:
Surat Al-Qamar (The Moon) - سورة القمر 54:48
ذُوقُوا مَسَّ سَقَرَ
Taste the touch of Saqar(Fire).
5.6 SAMOOM(سَمُوم):   SAMMA(سَمّ) means a narrow hole like the eye of a needle or the hole of nose(nostrils) and ear. Also, SAMMA(سَمّ) means deadly poison. And SAMOOM(سَمُوم) means hot wind which can penetrate through the body from inside like a poison. In the Quran:
Surat Aţ-Ţūr (The Mount) - سورة الطور 52:27
فَمَنَّ اللَّهُ عَلَيْنَا وَوَقَانَا عَذَابَ السَّمُومِ
So Allah conferred favor upon us and protected us from the punishment of the Scorching Fire.
Surah At-Tur (The Mount): سورۃ الطُّور 52:27
فَمَنَّ ٱللَّهُ عَلَيۡنَا وَوَقَٮٰنَا عَذَابَ ٱلسَّمُومِ
So Allah conferred favor upon us and protected us from the punishment of the Scorching Fire.
Summary:
5.1 SAIF: Summer season
5.2 HARR: Heat, heat of sunshine.
5.3 HAMM: Similar to HAMI, used for both heat and cordiality.
5.4 HAMI: Similar to HAMM, used for both heat and cordiality.
5.5 SAQR: Hell, Burning of body due to heat.
5.6 SAMOOM: Hot breeze that penetrates a body.

6 GARMI HASIL KERNA [to feel heat, to get warmth]
Synonyms: DIFF’UN, ISTALAA
6.1 DIF’UN (دَفْءٌ): DAFIA’-MINAL-BARD (دَفِئَ مِنَ الْبَرْد) means to warm up, to get warm, or feel the heat. To protect oneself from cold and get warm. DAFFA’A (دَفَّاَ) means to warm; ADFA’A (اَدْفَاَ) means to wear warm clothes. DIF’UN (دَفْءٌ) means extreme heat and also equipment to get warm or get heat. ADDIFA’U (اَلدِّفَاءُ) means warm clothes or equipment to get warm (dictionary al Manjad).
Surat An-Nahl (The Bee): سورۃ النّحل16:5
وَٱلۡأَنۡعَـٰمَ خَلَقَهَا‌ۗ لَڪُمۡ فِيهَا دِفۡءٌ۬ وَمَنَـٰفِعُ وَمِنۡهَا تَأۡڪُلُونَ
And the livestock—He created them for you. In them are warmth and benefits for you, and of them you eat.
6.2 ISTALAA (اِصْطَلٰی):   SALA (صَلَی) means to enter fire. ASLAA (اَصْلٰی) and SALLA (صَلّٰی) means to put into fire. And ISTALAA (اِصْطَلٰی) means to get warmth from fire or to warm oneself on fire. To warm oneself to protect from cold. In the Quran
Surah An-Naml (The ant): سورۃ النَّمل 27:7
أَوۡ ءَاتِيكُم بِشِہَابٍ۬ قَبَسٍ۬ لَّعَلَّكُمۡ تَصۡطَلُونَ
or bring you a firebrand, that you may warm yourselves.”
Summary:
6.1 DIFF’UN: DAFA’A’ to get warmth by wearing warm clothes
6.2 ISTALAA: Get warmth from Fire

title: content/gg/gg7.html
raw_text:
7 GIRNA – GIRANA [to fall, to cause to fall]
Synonyms: SAKATA, KHARRA, HADAMA, HADDA, INQADDA, HABATA, WAQA’A, HARA, HAWAA, KHAWA, WAJABA, RADAA, SARA’A, TALL, TA’ASA, IDDAARAKA, INHAMARA, SABBA, SAKABA
7.1 SAKATA (سَقَطَ):   To throw something down from height. This word is used commonly but it has indirectly contempt in it. For instance “رَجُلٌ سَاقِط” means an ignoble person (dictionary al Manjad). In the Quran
Surah Al-Ana’am (The Cattle): سورۃ الانعام 6:59
وَمَا تَسۡقُطُ مِن وَرَقَةٍ إِلَّا يَعۡلَمُهَا
Not a leaf falls but He knows it;
The way this word is used materially, in the same manner it is used semantically. Allah says in the Quran
Surah Al Tawbah (The repentance): سورۃ التوبھ 9:49
أَلَا فِى ٱلۡفِتۡنَةِ سَقَطُواْ‌ۗ
Unquestionably, into trial they have fallen
And SUQITA-FI-YADIHI  (سُقِطَ فِیْ یدِہِ)is used as an idiom, which means to be ashamed and sorry. And only changes due to conscience. Allah says in the Quran
Surah Al-Araf (The heights): سورۃ الأعرَاف 7:149
وَلَمَّا سُقِطَ فِىٓ أَيۡدِيهِمۡ وَرَأَوۡاْ أَنَّهُمۡ قَدۡ ضَلُّواْ
Then, when they regretted, and realized that they had erred,
And for causing to fall ASQATA  (اَسْقَطَ)is used. In the Quran
Surah Ash-Shura’ (The Poets): صورۃ الشُّعْراء 26:187

So cause to fall upon us fragments of the sky, if you should be of the truthful
7.2 KHARRA (خَرَّ):   Falling with perturbation and sound. To be upset or fluster and also creating sound while falling. KHAREER (خریر) means the sound of water falling or dripping. Allah says in the Quran.

Then, when he fell down, it became clear to the sprites that, had they known the unseen, they would not have remained in the demeaning torment.
7.3 HADAM (ھَدَم):   To destroy a building or a construction. HADDAMA (ھَدَّم) means to destroy, level or cause a building to fall. INHIDAAM (اِنْھِدَام) is a famous word, which gives the same meaning as HADAM (ھَدَم) . Allah says in the Quran

وَلَوۡلَا دَفۡعُ ٱللَّهِ ٱلنَّاسَ بَعۡضَہُم بِبَعۡضٍ۬ لَّهُدِّمَتۡ صَوَٲمِعُ وَبِيَعٌ۬
Were it not that God repels people by means of others: monasteries, churches, synagogues, and mosques—where the name of God is mentioned much—would have been demolished.
7.4 HADDA (ھَدَّ):   Breaking and falling of a building making sound and noise. Allah says in the Quran.
Surah Maryam (Mary): سُوۡرَةُ مَریَم 19:90
تَڪَادُ ٱلسَّمَـٰوَٲتُ يَتَفَطَّرۡنَ مِنۡهُ وَتَنشَقُّ ٱلۡأَرۡضُ وَتَخِرُّ ٱلۡجِبَالُ هَدًّا
At which the heavens almost rupture, and the earth splits, and the mountains fall and crumble.
7.5 INQADDA (اِنْقَضَّ):   Cracking of a building or wall, nearing to fall, QADD-AL-HAAIT (قَضَّ الْحَائِط) means to break down a wall, and INQADD-AL-HAAIT (اِنْقَضَّ الحَائِط) means “the wall cracked open and fell”. Allah says in the Quran

فَوَجَدَا فِيہَا جِدَارً۬ا يُرِيدُ أَن يَنقَضَّ فَأَقَامَهُ ۥ‌ۖ
There they found a wall about to collapse, and he repaired it.

وَإِنَّ مِنۡہَا لَمَا يَہۡبِطُ مِنۡ خَشۡيَةِ ٱللَّهِ‌ۗ
there are some of them that fall down for fear of Allah .

قُلۡنَا ٱهۡبِطُواْ مِنۡہَا جَمِيعً۬ا‌ۖ
We said, "Go down from it, all of you.
In the following ayah
Surah Hud (Hud): سورۃ ھود 11:48
قِيلَ يَـٰنُوحُ ٱهۡبِطۡ بِسَلَـٰمٍ۬ مِّنَّا
It was said, “O Noah, disembark with peace from Us;
In the ayah above the word BISALAMIN (بِسَلَـٰمٍ۬) is eliminating the aspects of scorn and constrain making it a divine will.
7.7 WAQA’A (وَقَعَ):   To fall, to prove, to occur, this word usually represents hate, extremity and turmoil. WAQIA (واقعہ) means an event that is accompanied by hardship. Allah says in the Quran
Surah Al-Araf (The heights): سورۃ الأعرَاف 7:171
وَإِذۡ نَتَقۡنَا ٱلۡجَبَلَ فَوۡقَهُمۡ كَأَنَّهُ ۥ ظُلَّةٌ۬ وَظَنُّوٓاْ أَنَّهُ ۥ وَاقِعُۢ بِہِمۡ
And when We suspended the mountain over them, as if it was an umbrella, and they thought it would fall on them:
7.8 HARA (ھَارَ):   HAWR (ھور) means falling of something in a way that a portion of it falls on the other objects too.  The word INHAAR (اِنْھَارَ) and INHIDAAM (اِنْھِدَام) are similar in meaning. INHIDAAM (اِنْھِدَام) means falling of a building, construction or wall but INHAAR (اِنْھَارَ) covers a wider range of meaning. Allah says in the Quran
Surah Al Tawbah (The repentance): سورۃ التوبھ 9:109
خَيۡرٌ أَم مَّنۡ أَسَّسَ بُنۡيَـٰنَهُ ۥ عَلَىٰ شَفَا جُرُفٍ هَارٍ۬ فَٱنۡہَارَ بِهِۦ فِى نَارِ جَهَنَّمَ‌ۗ
one who laid the foundation of his building on the edge of a bank about to collapse, so it collapsed with him into the fire of Hell?
7.9 HAWAA (ھوٰی):   HAWA (ھَوَا) is a famous word which means the air between the sky and earth, HAWAA (ھوٰی) means to fall from a height on the ground. Used also for a falling or shooting star. Allah says in the Quran
Surah An-Najm (the star): سورۃ النَّجم 53:1
وَٱلنَّجۡمِ إِذَا هَوَىٰ
By the star as it goes down.
In another place in Quran
Surah Al-Hajj  (The Pilgrimage): سُوۡرَةُ الحَجّ 22:31
فَكَأَنَّمَا خَرَّ مِنَ ٱلسَّمَآءِ فَتَخۡطَفُهُ ٱلطَّيۡرُ أَوۡ تَهۡوِى بِهِ ٱلرِّيحُ فِى مَكَانٍ۬ سَحِيقٍ۬
it is as though he has fallen from the sky, and is snatched by the birds, or is swept away by the wind to a distant abyss.
7.10 KHAWAA (خوی):   KHAWAA (خوی) and HAWAA (ھوٰی) are similar in meaning, HAWAA (ھوٰی) means the air filled empty space between the sky and earth, and KHAWA (خَوٰی) is empty space between any two objects. Like HAW-AN-NAJAM (ھَوَی النَّجْم) is used similarly KHAW-AN-NAJAM (خوی النجم) is used. TAKHWIYAH (تخویة) means to leave space between two things, KHAW-AD-DAAR (خوی الدار) means to demolish or break down a house that is depopulated and deserted. Allah says in the Quran
Surah Al-Baqarah (The cow): سورۃ البَقَرَۃ  2:259
أَوۡ كَٱلَّذِى مَرَّ عَلَىٰ قَرۡيَةٍ۬ وَهِىَ خَاوِيَةٌ عَلَىٰ عُرُوشِهَا
Or [consider such an example] as the one who passed by a township which had fallen into ruin.
7.11 WAJABA (وَجَبَ):   ALWAJABAH (اَلْوَجَبَة) is to make something fall by a blast (dictionary al Manjad), this word has also the aspect of death in it, like DARABAHU-FAWAJABA (ضَرَبَهُ فَوَجَبَ) means he hit him and he fell down and died. Allah says in the Quran
Surah Al-Hajj  (The Pilgrimage): سُوۡرَةُ الحَجّ 22:36
فَٱذۡكُرُواْ ٱسۡمَ ٱللَّهِ عَلَيۡہَا صَوَآفَّ‌ۖ فَإِذَا وَجَبَتۡ جُنُوبُہَا فَكُلُواْ مِنۡہَا وَأَطۡعِمُواْ ٱلۡقَانِعَ وَٱلۡمُعۡتَرَّ‌ۚ
So pronounce God’s name upon them as they line up. Then, when they have fallen on their sides, eat of them and feed the contented and the beggar.
7.12 RADAA (ردی):   Means to throw some living thing from a height or dash someone in a pit from ground which fatally injures him. In the Quran
Surah Ta-Ha (Ta-ha): سورۃ طٰھٰ  20:16
وَٱتَّبَعَ هَوَٮٰهُ فَتَرۡدَىٰ
follows his desire turn you away from it, lest you fall.
ARD-AR-RUJAL (اَرْدَی الرَّجُل) means to throw someone into a well. RADD-AR-RAJUL (رَدَّی الرَّجُل) means to cause a man to fall, to kill. Allah says in the Quran
Surah As-Saaffat (The Aligners) : سُوۡرَةُ الصَّافات37:56
قَالَ تَٱللَّهِ إِن كِدتَّ لَتُرۡدِينِ
He says, "By Allah decidedly you were almost about to topple me down indeed.
TARADDA (تَرَدّٰی) means to fall into a well, MUTARADDIYAH وَٱلۡمُتَرَدِّيَةُ (5:3) is an animal that falls in a well or pit and dies. Allah says in the Quran
Surat Al-Layl (The Night): سورة الليل 92:11
وَمَا يُغۡنِى عَنۡهُ مَالُهُ ۥۤ إِذَا تَرَدَّىٰٓ
Nor will his wealth profit him when he falls headlong (into the Pit).
7.13 SARA’A (صَرَعَ):   Means to fall on ground due to perturbation and anxiety, or fall and roll on ground due to a seizure (dictionary al Manjad), SARA’ (صَرَع) refers to epilepsy which causes the patient to fall to ground helpless. SARA’A (صَرَعَ) means to dash an opponent to ground in a brawl and to overcome him. Allah says in the Quran
Surah Al-Haqqah (The reality): سورۃ الحَاقَّۃ 69:7
فَتَرَى ٱلۡقَوۡمَ فِيہَا صَرۡعَىٰ كَأَنَّہُمۡ أَعۡجَازُ نَخۡلٍ خَاوِيَةٍ۬
You could see the people tossed around, as though they were stumps of hollow palm-trees.
7.14 TALL (تلّ):   Means to throw someone upon forehead, Allah says in the Quran
Surah As-Saaffat (The Aligners) : سُوۡرَةُ الصَّافات37:103
فَلَمَّآ أَسۡلَمَا وَتَلَّهُ ۥ لِلۡجَبِينِ
So when they both submitted and he threw him down upon his forehead,
7.15 TA’ASA (تَعَسَ):   To stumble and fall, and not recover and stand. Fall down and break, He fell down pronely and died. TA’ASA (تَعَسَ) means to slip and fall head on. AT-TA’SAH (التَّعَسَہ) means fatality (dictionary al Manjad). Allah says in the Quran

وَٱلَّذِينَ كَفَرُواْ فَتَعۡسً۬ا لَّهُمۡ
But as for those who disbelieve, for them is perdition,
7.16 IDDAARAKA (اِدّٰرَك):   DARK (دَرْك) means mixing of a thing with another, and then becoming one. DARK (دَرْك) is also the seabed, and also that rope which is combined with another rope to get to the seabed. To achieve an aim through some medium is called ADRAKA (اَدْرَكَ), Like about FIRA’OUN (فرعون) in Quran حَتَّىٰٓ إِذَآ أَدۡرَڪَهُ ٱلۡغَرَقُ (when the (fate of) drowning overtook him) (11:90) means the final destination was that he was drowned. So a chain of causation lead to his drowning. IDDAARAKA (اِدّٰرَك) also gives the same picture. Allah says in the Quran
Surah An-Naml (The ant): سورۃ النَّمل 27:66
بَلِ ٱدَّٲرَكَ عِلۡمُهُمۡ فِى ٱلۡأَخِرَةِ‌ۚ

Every time a crowd enters, it will curse its sister-crowd. Until, when they are all in it,
Means the final destination is hell and due to close relationship and connection bringing along one group after another and fall into hell.

So We opened the floodgates of heaven with water pouring down.

Surah Abasa (He frowned): سورۃعَبَسَ 80:24
فَلۡيَنظُرِ ٱلۡإِنسَـٰنُ إِلَىٰ طَعَامِهِۦۤ أَنَّا صَبَبۡنَا ٱلۡمَآءَ صَبًّ۬ا
Let man consider his food. We pour down water in abundance.
7.19 SAKABA (سَکَبَ):   SAKAB-AL-MAA’ (سکب الماء) means falling and spilling of water. ASKAB (اسکب) means a continuous rain fall. AL-ASKUB (الاسکوب) means continuous shower. And MAA’IM-MASKOOB (مَاءٍمَّسْکُوْبٍ) means JAARIN-DAAIMAN (جَارٍ دَائِمًا) “continuously flowing water”. Thus SAKABA refers to three things falling of water from a height, flowing of water and continuity. Allah says in the Quran
Surah Al-Waqiah (The Inevitable): سُوۡرَةُ الواقِعَة 56:30
وَظِلٍّ۬ مَّمۡدُودٍ۬  وَمَآءٍ۬ مَّسۡكُوبٍ۬
And extended shade. And outpouring water.
Summary:
7.1 SAKATA: Falling from height, a very common word.
7.2 KHARRA: Falling with noise and perturbation.
7.3 HADAMA: Falling of a construction, wall or building.
7.4 HADDA: Sudden falling and collapsing of a building, construction or wall.
7.5 INQADDA: Cracking of a construction, building or wall, about to fall.
7.6 HABATA: To fall due to pain or perturbation, to come out, or get down.
7.7 WAQA’A: Fall accompanied by difficulty,
7.8 HARA: Falling of something on another thing,
7.9 HAWAA: To fall from sky or a great height,
7.10 KHAWA: To fall from space between two things
7.11 WAJABA: to collapse and die, or collapse while dying.
7.12 RADAA: To fall into a pit and die.
7.13 SARA’A: To dash to ground like in brawl or due to death or sickness,
7.14 TALL: To fall head-on, pronely,
7.15 TA’ASA: Stumble and fall head-on,
7.16 IDDAARAKA: To fall after failing and giving up,
7.17 INHAMARA: Falling and flowing of water
7.18 SABBA: Falling, spilling and flowing of water,
7.19 SAKABA: Continuous falling and flowing of water.

In the following ayah

Surah Hud (Hud): سورۃ ھود 11:48

 قِيلَ يَـٰنُوحُ ٱهۡبِطۡ بِسَلَـٰمٍ۬ مِّنَّا

 It was said, “O Noah, disembark with peace from Us;

In the ayah above the word BISALAMIN (بِسَلَـٰمٍ۬) is eliminating the aspects of scorn and constrain making it a divine will.

 

7.7 WAQA’A (وَقَعَ): To fall, to prove, to occur, this word usually represents hate, extremity and turmoil. WAQIA (واقعہ) means an event that is accompanied by hardship. Allah says in the Quran

Surah Al-Araf (The heights): سورۃ الأعرَاف 7:171

 وَإِذۡ نَتَقۡنَا ٱلۡجَبَلَ فَوۡقَهُمۡ كَأَنَّهُ ۥ ظُلَّةٌ۬ وَظَنُّوٓاْ أَنَّهُ ۥ وَاقِعُۢ بِہِمۡ

 And when We suspended the mountain over them, as if it was an umbrella, and they thought it would fall on them:

7.8 HARA (ھَارَ): HAWR (ھور) means falling of something in a way that a portion of it falls on the other objects too.  The word INHAAR (اِنْھَارَ) and INHIDAAM (اِنْھِدَام) are similar in meaning. INHIDAAM (اِنْھِدَام) means falling of a building, construction or wall but INHAAR (اِنْھَارَ) covers a wider range of meaning. Allah says in the Quran

Surah Al Tawbah (The repentance): سورۃ التوبھ 9:109

 خَيۡرٌ أَم مَّنۡ أَسَّسَ بُنۡيَـٰنَهُ ۥ عَلَىٰ شَفَا جُرُفٍ هَارٍ۬ فَٱنۡہَارَ بِهِۦ فِى نَارِ جَهَنَّمَ‌ۗ

 one who laid the foundation of his building on the edge of a bank about to collapse, so it collapsed with him into the fire of Hell?

7.9 HAWAA (ھوٰی): HAWA (ھَوَا) is a famous word which means the air between the sky and earth, HAWAA (ھوٰی) means to fall from a height on the ground. Used also for a falling or shooting star. Allah says in the Quran

Surah An-Najm (the star): سورۃ النَّجم 53:1

وَٱلنَّجۡمِ إِذَا هَوَىٰ

By the star as it goes down.

In another place in Quran

Surah Al-Hajj  (The Pilgrimage): سُوۡرَةُ الحَجّ 22:31

فَكَأَنَّمَا خَرَّ مِنَ ٱلسَّمَآءِ فَتَخۡطَفُهُ ٱلطَّيۡرُ أَوۡ تَهۡوِى بِهِ ٱلرِّيحُ فِى مَكَانٍ۬ سَحِيقٍ۬

it is as though he has fallen from the sky, and is snatched by the birds, or is swept away by the wind to a distant abyss.

7.10 KHAWAA (خوی): KHAWAA (خوی) and HAWAA (ھوٰی) are similar in meaning, HAWAA (ھوٰی) means the air filled empty space between the sky and earth, and KHAWA (خَوٰی) is empty space between any two objects. Like HAW-AN-NAJAM (ھَوَی النَّجْم) is used similarly KHAW-AN-NAJAM (خوی النجم) is used. TAKHWIYAH (تخویة) means to leave space between two things, KHAW-AD-DAAR (خوی الدار) means to demolish or break down a house that is depopulated and deserted. Allah says in the Quran

Surah Al-Baqarah (The cow): سورۃ البَقَرَۃ  2:259

 أَوۡ كَٱلَّذِى مَرَّ عَلَىٰ قَرۡيَةٍ۬ وَهِىَ خَاوِيَةٌ عَلَىٰ عُرُوشِهَا

Or [consider such an example] as the one who passed by a township which had fallen into ruin.

7.11 WAJABA (وَجَبَ): ALWAJABAH (اَلْوَجَبَة) is to make something fall by a blast (dictionary al Manjad), this word has also the aspect of death in it, like DARABAHU-FAWAJABA (ضَرَبَهُ فَوَجَبَ) means he hit him and he fell down and died. Allah says in the Quran

Surah Al-Hajj  (The Pilgrimage): سُوۡرَةُ الحَجّ 22:36

فَٱذۡكُرُواْ ٱسۡمَ ٱللَّهِ عَلَيۡہَا صَوَآفَّ‌ۖ فَإِذَا وَجَبَتۡ جُنُوبُہَا فَكُلُواْ مِنۡہَا وَأَطۡعِمُواْ ٱلۡقَانِعَ وَٱلۡمُعۡتَرَّ‌ۚ

 So pronounce God’s name upon them as they line up. Then, when they have fallen on their sides, eat of them and feed the contented and the beggar.

7.12 RADAA (ردی): Means to throw some living thing from a height or dash someone in a pit from ground which fatally injures him. In the Quran

Surah Ta-Ha (Ta-ha): سورۃ طٰھٰ  20:16            

 وَٱتَّبَعَ هَوَٮٰهُ فَتَرۡدَىٰ

follows his desire turn you away from it, lest you fall.

ARD-AR-RUJAL (اَرْدَی الرَّجُل) means to throw someone into a well. RADD-AR-RAJUL (رَدَّی الرَّجُل) means to cause a man to fall, to kill. Allah says in the Quran

Surah As-Saaffat (The Aligners) : سُوۡرَةُ الصَّافات37:56

قَالَ تَٱللَّهِ إِن كِدتَّ لَتُرۡدِينِ

He says, "By Allah decidedly you were almost about to topple me down indeed.

TARADDA (تَرَدّٰی) means to fall into a well, MUTARADDIYAH وَٱلۡمُتَرَدِّيَةُ (5:3) is an animal that falls in a well or pit and dies. Allah says in the Quran

Surat Al-Layl (The Night): سورة الليل 92:11

وَمَا يُغۡنِى عَنۡهُ مَالُهُ ۥۤ إِذَا تَرَدَّىٰٓ

Nor will his wealth profit him when he falls headlong (into the Pit).

7.13 SARA’A (صَرَعَ): Means to fall on ground due to perturbation and anxiety, or fall and roll on ground due to a seizure (dictionary al Manjad), SARA’ (صَرَع) refers to epilepsy which causes the patient to fall to ground helpless. SARA’A (صَرَعَ) means to dash an opponent to ground in a brawl and to overcome him. Allah says in the Quran

Surah Al-Haqqah (The reality): سورۃ الحَاقَّۃ 69:7

 فَتَرَى ٱلۡقَوۡمَ فِيہَا صَرۡعَىٰ كَأَنَّہُمۡ أَعۡجَازُ نَخۡلٍ خَاوِيَةٍ۬

You could see the people tossed around, as though they were stumps of hollow palm-trees.

7.14 TALL (تلّ): Means to throw someone upon forehead, Allah says in the Quran

Surah As-Saaffat (The Aligners) : سُوۡرَةُ الصَّافات37:103

فَلَمَّآ أَسۡلَمَا وَتَلَّهُ ۥ لِلۡجَبِينِ

So when they both submitted and he threw him down upon his forehead,

7.15 TA’ASA (تَعَسَ): To stumble and fall, and not recover and stand. Fall down and break, He fell down pronely and died. TA’ASA (تَعَسَ) means to slip and fall head on. AT-TA’SAH (التَّعَسَہ) means fatality (dictionary al Manjad). Allah says in the Quran

Surah Muhammad (Muhammad): سُوۡرَةُ محَمَّد 47:9

وَٱلَّذِينَ كَفَرُواْ فَتَعۡسً۬ا لَّهُمۡ

But as for those who disbelieve, for them is perdition,

7.16 IDDAARAKA (اِدّٰرَك): DARK (دَرْك) means mixing of a thing with another, and then becoming one. DARK (دَرْك) is also the seabed, and also that rope which is combined with another rope to get to the seabed. To achieve an aim through some medium is called ADRAKA (اَدْرَكَ), Like about FIRA’OUN (فرعون) in Quran حَتَّىٰٓ إِذَآ أَدۡرَڪَهُ ٱلۡغَرَقُ (when the (fate of) drowning overtook him) (11:90) means the final destination was that he was drowned. So a chain of causation lead to his drowning. IDDAARAKA (اِدّٰرَك) also gives the same picture. Allah says in the Quran

Surah An-Naml (The ant): سورۃ النَّمل 27:66

 بَلِ ٱدَّٲرَكَ عِلۡمُهُمۡ فِى ٱلۡأَخِرَةِ‌ۚ

In fact, their knowledge of the Hereafter is confused.

Thus even after gathering and composing all knowledge they will fail hopelessly. In another place in the Quran

Surah Al-Araf (The heights): سورۃ الأعرَاف 7:38

 كُلَّمَا دَخَلَتۡ أُمَّةٌ۬ لَّعَنَتۡ أُخۡتَہَا‌ۖ حَتَّىٰٓ إِذَا ٱدَّارَڪُواْ فِيہَا جَمِيعً۬ا

Every time a crowd enters, it will curse its sister-crowd. Until, when they are all in it,

Means the final destination is hell and due to close relationship and connection bringing along one group after another and fall into hell.

7.17 INHAMARA (اِنْھَمَرَ):  HAMAR-AL-MAA’ (ھَمَرَ الْمَاء) means he spilled the water, INHARAM-AL-MAA’ (اِنْھَمَرَ الْمَاء) means the water fell and flowed. Or falling of tears, Allah says in the Quran

Surah Al-Qamar (The moon): سورۃ القَمَر 54:11

 فَفَتَحۡنَآ أَبۡوَٲبَ ٱلسَّمَآءِ بِمَآءٍ۬ مُّنۡہَمِرٍ۬

 So We opened the floodgates of heaven with water pouring down.

 

7.18 SABBA (صَبَّ): SABB-AL-MAA’ (صَبَّ الماء) means to throw or spill water on someone all at once, SABBA-ALAEH-IL-BALA’ (صَبَّ عَلَیْهِ الْبَلَاء) means to throw someone in trouble (dictionary al Manjad). Allah says in the Quran

Surah Abasa (He frowned): سورۃعَبَسَ 80:24

 فَلۡيَنظُرِ ٱلۡإِنسَـٰنُ إِلَىٰ طَعَامِهِۦۤ أَنَّا صَبَبۡنَا ٱلۡمَآءَ صَبًّ۬ا

Let man consider his food. We pour down water in abundance.

 

7.19 SAKABA (سَکَبَ): SAKAB-AL-MAA’ (سکب الماء) means falling and spilling of water. ASKAB (اسکب) means a continuous rain fall. AL-ASKUB (الاسکوب) means continuous shower. And MAA’IM-MASKOOB (مَاءٍمَّسْکُوْبٍ) means JAARIN-DAAIMAN (جَارٍ دَائِمًا) “continuously flowing water”. Thus SAKABA refers to three things falling of water from a height, flowing of water and continuity. Allah says in the Quran

Surah Al-Waqiah (The Inevitable): سُوۡرَةُ الواقِعَة 56:30

وَظِلٍّ۬ مَّمۡدُودٍ۬  وَمَآءٍ۬ مَّسۡكُوبٍ۬

And extended shade. And outpouring water.

 

Summary:

7.1 SAKATA: Falling from height, a very common word.

7.2 KHARRA: Falling with noise and perturbation.

7.3 HADAMA: Falling of a construction, wall or building.

7.4 HADDA: Sudden falling and collapsing of a building, construction or wall.

7.5 INQADDA: Cracking of a construction, building or wall, about to fall.

7.6 HABATA: To fall due to pain or perturbation, to come out, or get down.

7.7 WAQA’A: Fall accompanied by difficulty,

7.8 HARA: Falling of something on another thing,

7.9 HAWAA: To fall from sky or a great height,

7.10 KHAWA: To fall from space between two things

7.11 WAJABA: to collapse and die, or collapse while dying.

7.12 RADAA: To fall into a pit and die.

7.13 SARA’A: To dash to ground like in brawl or due to death or sickness,

7.14 TALL: To fall head-on, pronely,

7.15 TA’ASA: Stumble and fall head-on,

7.16 IDDAARAKA: To fall after failing and giving up,

7.17 INHAMARA: Falling and flowing of water

7.18 SABBA: Falling, spilling and flowing of water,

7.19 SAKABA: Continuous falling and flowing of water.

8 GIRWI RAKHNA [pawn, pledge]
Synonyms:  RAHANA, ABSALA
8.1 RAHANA (رَھَنَ):   Means to leave something as a guarantee in return for a loan to the creditor. To pledge. RAHN (رَھْن) is the thing that is pawned. A common word. The object can be a living or a non-living thing.  RIHANUN (رِھَانٌ) is the thing that is set aside as a bet during a competition. The object left as a security for loans. Allah says in the Quran
Surah Al-Baqarah (The cow): سورۃ البَقَرَۃ  2:283
وَإِن كُنتُمۡ عَلَىٰ سَفَرٍ۬ وَلَمۡ تَجِدُواْ كَاتِبً۬ا فَرِهَـٰنٌ۬ مَّقۡبُوضَةٌ۬‌ۖ
This word is used materially and also semantically. Allah says in the Quran
Surah Al-Muddaththir (The Cloaked One): سورۃ المدَّثّر 74:38
كُلُّ نَفۡسِۭ بِمَا كَسَبَتۡ رَهِينَةٌ
Every soul is hostage to what it has earned
8.2 ABSALA (اَبْسَلَ):   To give someone to pangs of death, to pledge (dictionary al Manjad). To keep as a hostage. When the object pawned is a living thing then this word is used, otherwise RAHN (رہن) is more common. Allah says in the Quran
Surah Al-Ana’am (The cattle): سورۃ الانعام 6:70
وَذَڪِّرۡ بِهِۦۤ أَن تُبۡسَلَ نَفۡسُۢ بِمَا كَسَبَتۡ
But remind with it, lest a soul becomes damned on account of what it has earned.
Summary:
8.1 RAHANA: Leave something as a guarantee in return for a loan.
8.2 ABSALA: To give oneself or any living thing for arrest or for death (hostage).

9. GARHA [pit, hole]
Synonyms:  HUFRAH, JUROOF, UKHDOOD, GHAIT
9.1 HUFRAH (حُفْرَۃ):   HUFRAH (حُفْرَۃ) and HAFEERAH (حَفِیرَۃ) means a pit. HAFARA (حَفْرَ) means to dig a pit. HAFR (حَفْر) means earth from the pit. MIHFAR (مِحْفَر) is the tool used to dig the pit (dictionary al Manjad).  A famous proverb “مردود فی الحافرۃ” means “dirt landed into where it belonged”. Allah says in the Quran
Surah Ale- Imran (The family of Imran): سورۃ آل عِمْرن 3:103
وَكُنتُمۡ عَلَىٰ شَفَا حُفۡرَةٍ۬ مِّنَ ٱلنَّارِ فَأَنقَذَكُم مِّنۡہَا‌ۗ
And you were on the brink of a pit of fire, and He saved you from it.
9.2 JUROOF (جُرُف):   The coast or a stream or river that is hollowed by the flow of river, wave-cut notch (dictionary al Manjad).  Allah says in the Quran
Surah Al Tawbah (The repentance): سورۃ التوبھ 9:109
أَم مَّنۡ أَسَّسَ بُنۡيَـٰنَهُ ۥ عَلَىٰ شَفَا جُرُفٍ هَارٍ۬
he who lays his foundation on the edge of a cracking hollowed bank,
9.3 UKHDOOD (اخدود):   AL-KADD-WALA-KHADOOD ( الخدّوالاخدود) means a deep and rectangular pit,(plural AKHADEED(اخدید))  AL-KHADD (اَلْخَدّ) means a stream of water, a long pit. AL-KHADDAH-WAL-UKHDOOD ( اَلْخَدَّۃ والْاُخْدُوْد) means a pit (dictionary al Manjad).  UKHDOOD (اخدود) is that deep and long hole that is dug in rectangular shape. Ditch or pit. ALLAH says in the Quran
Surat Al-Burūj (The Mansions of the Stars): سورة البروج 85:4
قُتِلَ أَصۡحَـٰبُ ٱلۡأُخۡدُودِ
Cursed be the makers of the pit,
9.4 GHAIT (غَائِط):   GHOAUT (غَوْط) means a depression in ground. GHAAT-AL-HUFRAH (غَاط الْحُفْرَة) means to dig a hole. GHAWWAT-AL-BI’R (غَوَّطَ الْبِئْر) means to dig deeper into a well. AL-GHAIT (الغَائِط) means a low land, a place for defecation, toilet (dictionary al Manjad).  It’s a metaphor that a noble and a shy person would try to find an isolated and deep place for urination. Allah says in the Quran
Surah An-Nisa (The women): سورۃ النِّسا 4:43 and
Surah Al-Maeda (The table spread): سورۃ المَائدہ 5:6
أَوۡ جَآءَ أَحَدٌ۬ مِّنكُم مِّنَ ٱلۡغَآٮِٕطِ
or one of you comes from the toilet,
Summary :
9.1 HUFRAH: Pit, a common word.
9.2 JUROOF: Wave-cut notch at the bank of river or stream.
9.3 UKHDOOD: Ditch or trench, a self dug deep rectangular pit.
9.4 GHAIT: Depressed ground, metaphorically a place for defecation.

1 GHAAR [Cave]
Synonyms:GHAR غَار MAGHARAT مَغَارَات KAHF كَهْف
1.1 GHAR  :GHAWR غَوْر is said for low ground as well as depth.GHAR ARRAJUL(غَارَ الرَّجُل) meaning man descend down to low ground. and GHAR ALMA-U غَارَ الْمَاءُ meaning water(level) lowers to underground.GHAWR meaning deep- deep thought. and GHAR meaning such a low place or depth where human can take refuge/shelter.common to that it is in some mountain or underground.ALLAH said
Surat At-Tawbah (The Repentance) - سورة التوبة
9:40
إِلَّا تَنصُرُوهُ فَقَدْ نَصَرَهُ اللَّهُ إِذْ أَخْرَجَهُ الَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا ثَانِيَ اثْنَيْنِ إِذْ هُمَا فِي الْغَارِ إِذْ يَقُولُ لِصَاحِبِهِ لَا تَحْزَنْ إِنَّ اللَّهَ مَعَنَا ۖ فَأَنزَلَ اللَّهُ سَكِينَتَهُ عَلَيْهِ وَأَيَّدَهُ بِجُنُودٍ لَّمْ تَرَوْهَا وَجَعَلَ كَلِمَةَ الَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا السُّفْلَىٰ ۗ وَكَلِمَةُ اللَّهِ هِيَ الْعُلْيَا ۗ وَاللَّهُ عَزِيزٌ حَكِيمٌ
If you do not aid the Prophet - Allah has already aided him when those who disbelieved had driven him out [of Makkah] as one of two, when they were in the cave and he said to his companion, "Do not grieve; indeed Allah is with us." And Allah sent down his tranquillity upon him and supported him with angels you did not see and made the word of those who disbelieved the lowest, while the word of Allah - that is the highest. And Allah is Exalted in Might and Wise.
and MAGHARA مَغَار is adverb (of place) from GHAWR which also comes in the meaning of cave.and it's plural is MAGHARAT.ALLAH said
Surat At-Tawbah (The Repentance) - سورة التوبة
9:57
لَوْ يَجِدُونَ مَلْجَأً أَوْ مَغَارَاتٍ أَوْ مُدَّخَلًا لَّوَلَّوْا إِلَيْهِ وَهُمْ يَجْمَحُونَ
If they could find a refuge or some caves or any place to enter [and hide], they would turn to it while they run heedlessly.
1.2 KAHF  :(plural KAHUWF كَهُوْف)KAHF is specific than cave.KAHF is such a cave or cavern which is in mountain- and is large.when it is small then it is called cave.ALLAH said.
Surat Al-Kahf (The Cave) - سورة الكهف
18:9
أَمْ حَسِبْتَ أَنَّ أَصْحَابَ الْكَهْفِ وَالرَّقِيمِ كَانُوا مِنْ آيَاتِنَا عَجَبًا
Or have you thought that the companions of the cave and the inscription were, among Our signs, a wonder?
for GHARAT HUWNA-KARNA [To be Plundered/Ravaged-To plunder/Ravage] please see BARBAD HUWNA [To be Destroyed] and HALAK KARNA [To Kill]

title: content/gh/gh2.html
raw_text:
2 GHAGIL HUWNA-KARNA [To be Negligent-To make negligent]
Synonyms:GHAFALA غَفَلَ AGHFALA اَغْفَلَ SAHA سَهَي SAMADA سَمَدَ ALHA اَلْهَي
2.1 GHAFALA  :meaning to leave some deed.whether intentional or   unintentional.to   be uninformed of knowing of facts .to not do some deed that needs to be done owing to laziness or forgetfulness.and a person can be negligent of one's own work or one's self and of others as well as ALLAH said
Surat Al-Baqarah (The Cow) - سورة البقرة
2:140
أَمْ تَقُولُونَ إِنَّ إِبْرَاهِيمَ وَإِسْمَاعِيلَ وَإِسْحَاقَ وَيَعْقُوبَ وَالْأَسْبَاطَ كَانُوا هُودًا أَوْ نَصَارَىٰ ۗ قُلْ أَأَنتُمْ أَعْلَمُ أَمِ اللَّهُ ۗ وَمَنْ أَظْلَمُ مِمَّن كَتَمَ شَهَادَةً عِندَهُ مِنَ اللَّهِ ۗ وَمَا اللَّهُ بِغَافِلٍ عَمَّا تَعْمَلُونَ
Or do you say that Abraham and Ishmael and Isaac and Jacob and the Descendants were Jews or Christians? Say, "Are you more knowing or is Allah ?" And who is more unjust than one who conceals a testimony he has from Allah ? And Allah is not unaware of what you do.
also said
Surat An-Nisā' (The Women) - سورة النساء
4:102
وَإِذَا كُنتَ فِيهِمْ فَأَقَمْتَ لَهُمُ الصَّلَاةَ فَلْتَقُمْ طَائِفَةٌ مِّنْهُم مَّعَكَ وَلْيَأْخُذُوا أَسْلِحَتَهُمْ فَإِذَا سَجَدُوا فَلْيَكُونُوا مِن وَرَائِكُمْ وَلْتَأْتِ طَائِفَةٌ أُخْرَىٰ لَمْ يُصَلُّوا فَلْيُصَلُّوا مَعَكَ وَلْيَأْخُذُوا حِذْرَهُمْ وَأَسْلِحَتَهُمْ ۗ وَدَّ الَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا لَوْ تَغْفُلُونَ عَنْ أَسْلِحَتِكُمْ وَأَمْتِعَتِكُمْ فَيَمِيلُونَ عَلَيْكُم مَّيْلَةً وَاحِدَةً ۚ وَلَا جُنَاحَ عَلَيْكُمْ إِن كَانَ بِكُمْ أَذًى مِّن مَّطَرٍ أَوْ كُنتُم مَّرْضَىٰ أَن تَضَعُوا أَسْلِحَتَكُمْ ۖ وَخُذُوا حِذْرَكُمْ ۗ إِنَّ اللَّهَ أَعَدَّ لِلْكَافِرِينَ عَذَابًا مُّهِينًا
And when you are among them and lead them in prayer, let a group of them stand [in prayer] with you and let them carry their arms. And when they have prostrated, let them be [in position] behind you and have the other group come forward which has not [yet] prayed and let them pray with you, taking precaution and carrying their arms. Those who disbelieve wish that you would neglect your weapons and your baggage so they could come down upon you in one [single] attack. But there is no blame upon you, if you are troubled by rain or are ill, for putting down your arms, but take precaution. Indeed, Allah has prepared for the disbelievers a humiliating punishment.
and AGHFALA meaning to make some one negligent of something by diverting one's attention.or to stop.ALLAH said
Surat Al-Kahf (The Cave) - سورة الكهف
18:28
وَاصْبِرْ نَفْسَكَ مَعَ الَّذِينَ يَدْعُونَ رَبَّهُم بِالْغَدَاةِ وَالْعَشِيِّ يُرِيدُونَ وَجْهَهُ ۖ وَلَا تَعْدُ عَيْنَاكَ عَنْهُمْ تُرِيدُ زِينَةَ الْحَيَاةِ الدُّنْيَا ۖ وَلَا تُطِعْ مَنْ أَغْفَلْنَا قَلْبَهُ عَن ذِكْرِنَا وَاتَّبَعَ هَوَاهُ وَكَانَ أَمْرُهُ فُرُطًا
And keep yourself patient [by being] with those who call upon their Lord in the morning and the evening, seeking His countenance. And let not your eyes pass beyond them, desiring adornments of the worldly life, and do not obey one whose heart We have made heedless of Our remembrance and who follows his desire and whose affair is ever [in] neglect.
2.2 SAHA  :meaning to forget.heart turn to other side.and SAHW سَهْو meaning soft-peace.SAHW is actually this action which gets done owing to negligence.if it is not intentional then it can be pardoned.like some madman calling names.and if intentional then it's accountable.SAJDA SAHW سجده سهو is a famous word.meaning the prostration that is performed for compensating any short comings in the offering of prayer owing to diversion of one's attention. and this word doesn't relate to the action of others (only for one's own action).ALLAH said
Surat Al-Mā`ūn (The Small Kindesses) - سورة الماعون
107:5
الَّذِينَ هُمْ عَن صَلَاتِهِمْ سَاهُونَ
[But] who are heedless of their prayer -
2.3 SAMADA  :meaning to be amazed- to be stunned.and SAMADA FIY AL3AML(سَمَدَ فِي الْعَمْل) meaning to be engaged in some matter.and SAMMADA سَمَّدَ meaning to be engaged in some sporting activity.so SAMADA is used for sporting rather than performing actual matter owing to negligence.ALLAH said
Surat An-Najm (The Star) - سورة النجم
53:60
وَتَضْحَكُونَ وَلَا تَبْكُونَ
And you laugh and do not weep
Surat An-Najm (The Star) - سورة النجم
53:61
وَأَنتُمْ سَامِدُونَ
While you are proudly sporting?
Surat An-Najm (The Star) - سورة النجم
53:62
فَاسْجُدُوا لِلَّهِ وَاعْبُدُوا
So prostrate to Allah and worship [Him].
2.4 ALHA  :LAHW لَهْو is every that thing which keeps turning away/diverting human from actual objective.and LAHA YALHUW لَهَا يَلْهُو meaning to play-to be fond of- and LAHA and ALHA لَهَي الْهَي meaning to be   engaged.to   divert attention.so in ALHA,diversion is not owing to negligence but owing to other useless activities.ALLAH said
Surat At-Takāthur (The Rivalry in world increase) - سورة التكاثر
102:1
أَلْهَاكُمُ التَّكَاثُرُ
Competition in [worldly] increase diverts you
Summary:
2.1 GHAFALA:to not perform some action owing to forgetfulness(unintentional) or laziness(intentional).or to be negligent of some other's work[(that needs to be done by one)]
2.2 SAHA:owing to forgetfulness, to do some other thing other than actual thing or to do it improperly. it doesn't relate to others.
2.3 SAMADA:to engage in sporting activities rather than performing actual deed owing to negligence
2.4 ALHA:when the cause of diversion of attention from actual deed is leisurely and sporting activities or other things rather than forgetfulness

title: content/gh/gh3.html
raw_text:
3 GHALIB ANA, HONA, KERNA
[To dominate, to prevail]
Synonyms: ZAHARA(  ظَهَر  ), AZZA(  عَزّ  ), GHALABA(  غلب  ), ISTA’LA(  استقلي  ), QAHARA(  قهر  )
3.1 zahara(  ظَهَر  )  : There are two main points in the meaning of zahara (i) to become visible, to come in front, to become noticeable and (ii)strength. Then this word is also used in the material and semantic sense. It is stated:
________________
Surat Room (The Romans) -   سُوۡرَةُ الرُّوم
30:41
ظَهَرَ ٱلۡفَسَادُ فِى ٱلۡبَرِّ وَٱلۡبَحۡرِ
Corruption doth appear on land and sea   because of (the evil) which men's hands have done, that He may make them taste a part of that which they have done, in order that they may return.
________________
Also stated:
________________
Surat Tauba (Repentance) -   سُوۡرَةُ التّوبَة
9:48
حَتَّىٰ جَآءَ ٱلۡحَقُّ وَظَهَرَ أَمۡرُ ٱللَّهِ
Aforetime they sought to cause sedition and raised difficulties for thee   till the Truth came and the decree of Allah was made manifest  , though they were loth.
________________
Thus the word zahara means the appearance of something with strength and power. And the word azhar(  أظهر   )has been used to give the meaning of ‘to prevail’, as is stated:
________________
Surat Tauba (Repentance) -   سُوۡرَةُ التّوبَة
9:33
هُوَ ٱلَّذِىٓ أَرۡسَلَ رَسُولَهُ ۥ بِٱلۡهُدَىٰ وَدِينِ ٱلۡحَقِّ لِيُظۡهِرَهُ ۥ عَلَى ٱلدِّينِ ڪُلِّهِ
He it is Who hath sent His messenger with the guidance and the Religion of Truth, that He may cause it to prevail over all religion  , however much the idolaters may be averse.
________________
3.2 azza (  عَزّ  ) (antonym: zalla) (     ذل  ):   meaning to control and zalla(  ذل   ) meaning to be controlled. This is evident in the rural atmosphere where the landowners control the peasants and laborers. These are the meanings of aziz(  عزيز   ) and zaleel(  ذليل)  . It is stated in the Quran:
________________
Surat Sad -   سُوۡرَةُ صٓ
38:23
فَقَالَ أَكۡفِلۡنِيہَا وَعَزَّنِى فِى ٱلۡخِطَابِ
Lo! this my brother hath ninety and nine ewes while I had one ewe;   and he said: Entrust it to me, and he conquered me in speech  .
________________
3.3 ghalaba(  غلب  )  : includes the meanings of force, wrath and intensity i.e. to gain domination and preferment by force ad maghloob(  مغلوب  ) is that one who is forced to submit. Allah states that:
________________
Surat Al-Baqarah (The Cow) -   سورة البقرة
2:249
ڪَم مِّن فِئَةٍ۬ قَلِيلَةٍ غَلَبَتۡ فِئَةً۬ ڪَثِيرَةَۢ بِإِذۡنِ ٱللَّهِ‌ۗ
And when Saul set out with the army, he said: Lo! Allah will try you by (the ordeal of) a river. Whosoever therefore drinketh thereof he is not of me, and whosoever tasteth it not he is of me, save him who taketh (thereof) in the hollow of his hand. But they drank thereof, all save a few of them. And after he had crossed (the river), he and those who believed with him, they said: We have no power this day against Goliath and his hosts. But those who knew that they would meet Allah exclaimed  : How many a little company hath overcome a mighty host by Allah's leave  ! Allah is with the steadfast.
________________
3.4 ista’la (  استعلي  )  : ala ya’lo(  على يعلو  ) means to elevate. And ista’la(  استعلي  ) means wanting to be elevated, the desire to become dominant and prevailing. Ta’alli(  تعلي  ) means to boast. The words ta’alli(  تعلي)   and ista’la(  استعلي  ) are usually used in the negative sense. And ala(  علا  ) and ya’lo(  يعلو  ) used in positive as well as negative sense. And aliya(  علي  ) and ya’la(  يعلي  ) are used in positive sense. Allah states that:
________________
Surat Ta-Ha -   سُوۡرَةُ طٰه
20:64
فَأَجۡمِعُواْ ڪَيۡدَكُمۡ ثُمَّ ٱئۡتُواْ صَفًّ۬ا‌ۚ وَقَدۡ أَفۡلَحَ ٱلۡيَوۡمَ مَنِ ٱسۡتَعۡلَىٰ ۖ
So arrange your plan, and come in battle line. Whoso is uppermost this day will be indeed successful.
________________
3.5 qahara (  قهر  )  : There are two main points: (i)to prevail (ii)to ridicule the submissive, to repress him. Then this word is also used separately for these meanings. It is stated in the Quran:
________________
Surat Al-Araf (The Heights) -   سُوۡرَةُ الاٴعرَاف
7:127
قَالَ سَنُقَتِّلُ أَبۡنَآءَهُمۡ وَنَسۡتَحۡىِۦ نِسَآءَهُمۡ وَإِنَّا فَوۡقَهُمۡ قَـٰهِرُونَ
The chiefs of Pharaoh's people said: (O King), wilt thou suffer Moses and his people to make mischief in the land, and flout thee and thy gods?   He said: We will slay their sons and spare their women, for lo! we are in power over them.
________________
In this ayat, the word qahar(  قهر  ) is giving both the meanings. And in the following ayat, it is only giving the meaning of repressing. Allah states that:
________________
Surat Ad-Dhuha (The Morning Hours) -   سُوۡرَةُ الِضُّحىٰ
93:9-10
فَأَمَّا ٱلۡيَتِيمَ فَلَا تَقۡهَرۡۖ وَأَمَّا ٱلسَّآٮِٕلَ فَلَا تَنۡہَرۡ
Therefore the orphan oppress not. Therefor the beggar drive not away.
________________
Summary:
1. ZAHARA(  ظَهَر  ): meaning to come forward with force, to become evident, an upcoming force.
2. AZZA(  عَزّ  ): meaning to be dominant
3. GHALABA(  غلب  ): to become dominant by force.
4. ISTA’LA(  استعلي  ): to have the hungry desire of becoming dominant.
5. QAHAR(  قهر  ): to become dominant and ridicule, to repress the weak.

Therefore the orphan oppress not. Therefor the beggar drive not away.

________________

Summary:

1. ZAHARA(ظَهَر): meaning to come forward with force, to become evident, an upcoming force.

2. AZZA(عَزّ): meaning to be dominant

3. GHALABA(غلب): to become dominant by force.

4. ISTA’LA(استعلي): to have the hungry desire of becoming dominant.

5. QAHAR(قهر): to become dominant and ridicule, to repress the weak.

4 GHUBAAR
[Dust]
Synonyms: GHABARA(  غبرة  ), NAQA’A(  نقعا  ), HABA’A(  هباء  )
4.1 ghabara(  غبرة  )  : meaning haze/mist. The small particles that float in the air after a dust storm. Allah states that:
________________
Surat Abasa (He Frowned) -   سُوۡرَةُ عَبَسَ
80:40-41
وَوُجُوهٌ۬ يَوۡمَٮِٕذٍ عَلَيۡہَا غَبَرَةٌۖتَرۡهَقُهَا قَتَرَةٌ
And other faces, on that day, with dust upon them. Veiled in darkness.
________________
4.2 naqa’a (  نقعا  )  : meaning dust of the pathway, that dust which is left behind when a fast moving vehicle passes through some place. These dust particles then settle to the ground slowly because of being heavier than air. It is stated in the Quran:
________________
Surat Al-Adiyat (The Chargers) -   سُوۡرَةُ العَادیَات
100:4-5
فَوَسَطۡنَ بِهِۦ جَمۡعًا ۖ فَأَثَرۡنَ بِهِۦ نَقۡعً۬ا
Then, therewith, with their trail of dust. Cleaving, as one, the centre (of the foe).
________________
4.3 haba’a(  هباء  )  : habwa(  هبوة  ) meaning the thin particles of dust, those thin dust particles that always remain in air and are not even seen. Allah states that:
________________
Surat Al-Furqan (The Standard) -   سُوۡرَةُ الفُرقان
25:23
وَقَدِمۡنَآ إِلَىٰ مَا عَمِلُواْ مِنۡ عَمَلٍ۬ فَجَعَلۡنَـٰهُ هَبَآءً۬ مَّنثُورًا
And We shall turn unto the work they did and make it scattered motes.
________________
Summary:
1.GHABARA(  غبرة  ): dust particles that can be seen.
2. NAQA’A(  نقعا  ): those heavier dust particles that a fast moving vehicle leaves behind
3. HABA’A(  هباء  ): those thing dust particles that are always scattered in the air and cannot be seen.
For gharoob, see gharaba, aqala, and waqaba. To become proud/arrogant, see ‘itraana’.

raw_text:
5 GHUSSA
[Anger]
Synonyms: SAKHATA(  سخط  ), GHAIZ(  غيظ  ), GHAZABA(  غضب  ), HARD(  حرد  )
5.1 sakhata(  سخط  )  : meaning to do something unwillingly and sakht(  سخط  ) means dislike. This is the first level of anger and this is always associated with elders towards younger ones. One can say   سخط الأمير علي الحاجب   but not   سخط الحاجب علي الأمير  . Allah states that:
________________
Surat Ai-E-Imran (Family of Imran) -   سُوۡرَةُ آل عِمرَان
3:162
أَفَمَنِ ٱتَّبَعَ رِضۡوَٲنَ ٱللَّهِ كَمَنۢ بَآءَ بِسَخَطٍ۬ مِّنَ ٱللَّهِ
Is one who followeth the pleasure of Allah as one who hath earned condemnation from Allah  , whose habitation is the Fire, a hapless journey's end?
________________
5.2 ghaiz (  غيظ  )  : such type of displeasure which increases a man’s blood circulation and this is the second level of anger.  But in this case, there is no act of revenge. And ghaiz(  غيظ  ) can also be associated with a person’s own self. Allah states that:
________________
Surat Al-E-Imran (Family of Imran) -   سُوۡرَةُ آل عِمرَان
3:134
وَٱلۡڪَـٰظِمِينَ ٱلۡغَيۡظَ وَٱلۡعَافِينَ عَنِ ٱلنَّاسِ‌ۗ
Those who spend (of that which Allah hath given them) in ease and in adversity,   those who control their wrath and are forgiving toward mankind  ; Allah loveth the good.
________________
5.3 ghazaba(  غضب  )  : this word is common to the people of lexical jurisprudence which is used for all types of anger. But this definition does not appear to be correct. Our beloved Prophet PBUH has defined ghazaba(  غضب  ) as:
________________
اتقوا من الغضب فانه جمرة توقدفى قلب ابن أدم ألم تروا الى انتفاخ اوداجه و جمرة عينىىه
save yourself from ghazaba() as it is that flame of fire which lights in the hearts of the sons of Adam. Don’t you see that such a person’s veins swell and his eyes become red?
________________
And obviously, this situation arises when a person becomes so full of anger that he wants to take revenge. And Ibn-alFaris has defined its meaning as severe displeasure. And others have defined ghazaba(  غضب  ) as to hold grudge and be furious and ghazaba(  غضب  ) always arises for some other person meaning  that it could be of young towards elders or elders towards young. Allah states that:
________________
Surat Ta-Ha -   سُوۡرَةُ طٰه
20:81
وَمَن يَحۡلِلۡ عَلَيۡهِ غَضَبِى فَقَدۡ هَوَىٰ
Eat of the good things wherewith We have provided you, and transgress not in respect thereof lest My wrath come upon you:   and he on whom My wrath cometh, he is lost indeed  .
________________
5.4 hard(  حرد  )  : harid(  حرد  ) means to be angry on someone and harada(  حرد  ) means to forbid. Hard(  حرد  ) means to attack someone or investigate after being overwhelmed with anger. Harad(  حرد  ) actually is not the name of a situation of anger but that of such acts of revenge and vengeance which a person does after being overwhelmed with anger. And according to Abu-Halal, harad(  حرد  ) means to payback in insanity in a state of anger. Allah states that:
________________
Surat Al-Qalam (The Pen) -   سُوۡرَةُ القَلَم
68:25
وَغَدَوۡاْ عَلَىٰ حَرۡدٍ۬ قَـٰدِرِينَ
They went betimes, strong in (this) purpose
________________
Summary:
1.SAKHT(  سخط  ): Just displeasure, dislike. First level, of elders towards young.
2. GHAIZ(  غيظ  ): when blood circulation increases. Second level; and ghaiz can also come at one’s own self.
3. GHAZABA(  غضب  ): when a person takes revenge, overwhelmed with anger regardless of young or old. This is not associated with one’s self but towards others.
4. HARAD(  حرد  ): The state of revenge because of severe anger, to approach quickly and to do something in an altered state of mind.

6 GHUSSA DILANA
[To infuriate]
Synonyms: ASKHATA(  أسخط  ), GHAZA(GHAIZ) (  غاظ  ), ASAFA(  أسف  )
6.1 askhata(  أسخط  )  : details have been stated above meaning to displease someone. Allah states that:
________________
Surat Muhammad -   سُوۡرَةُ محَمَّد
47:28
ذَٲلِكَ بِأَنَّهُمُ ٱتَّبَعُواْ مَآ أَسۡخَطَ ٱللَّهَ وَڪَرِهُواْ رِضۡوَٲنَهُ
That will be because they followed that which angereth Allah, and hated that which pleaseth Him.   Therefore He hath made their actions vain.
________________
6.2 ghaza (  غاظ  )  : meaning to anger someone. Details have been stated above. It is stated in the Quran:
________________
Surat Al-Tawba (Repentance) -   سُوۡرَةُ التّوبَة
9:120
وَلَا يَطَـُٔونَ مَوۡطِئً۬ا يَغِيظُ ٱلۡڪُفَّارَ
It is not for the townsfolk of Al-Madinah and for those around them of the wandering Arabs to stay behind the messenger of Allah and prefer their lives to his life. That is because neither thirst nor toil nor hunger afflicteth them in the way of Allah,   nor step they any step that angereth the disbelievers  , nor gain they from the enemy a gain, but a good deed is recorded for them therefor. Lo! Allah loseth not the wages of the good.
________________
6.3 asafa(  أسف  ), alasaf(  الأسف  )  : that kind of anger which is based on grief and sorrow. If the anger is directed towards the weak, it takes the form of fury and wrath. And if it is towards the strong, then it takes the form of grief because of helplessness. And asafa(  أسف  ) means to lose something and ten to grieve over it. Moreover asafa(  أسف  ) means to anger someone, to make someone sorrowful. Allah states that:
________________
Surat Az-Zukhruf (Ornaments of Gold) -   سُوۡرَةُ الزّخرُف
43:55
فَلَمَّآ ءَاسَفُونَا ٱنتَقَمۡنَا مِنۡهُمۡ
So, when they angered Us, We punished them   and drowned them every one.
________________
Summary:
1.ASKHT(  أسخط  ): Just to displeasure.
2. GHAZA(  غاظ  ): to anger.
3. ASAFA(  أسف  ): that kind of anger which creates fury in the strong and leaves the weak in grief and sorrow.

title: content/gh/gh7.html
raw_text:
7 GHAM
[sorrow]
Synonyms: GHAM(  غم  ), HUZN(  حزن  ), BASSA(  بت  )
7.1 gham(  غم  )  : The literal meaning of gham(  غم  ) is to conceal and hide. Ghumma(  غمي  ) meaning dust and darkness and ghumaam(  غمام  ) meaning those clouds that conceal sunlight. And gham(  غم  ) means distress and suffering.  Allah states that:
________________
Surat Al-E-Imran(Family of Imran) -   سُوۡرَةُ آل عِمرَان
3:154
ثُمَّ أَنزَلَ عَلَيۡكُم مِّنۢ بَعۡدِ ٱلۡغَمِّ أَمَنَةً۬ نُّعَاسً۬ا يَغۡشَىٰ طَآٮِٕفَةً۬ مِّنكُمۡ‌ۖ
Then, after grief, He sent down security for you. As slumber did it overcome a party of you  , while (the other) party, who were anxious on their own account, thought wrongly of Allah, the thought of ignorance. They said: Have we any part in the cause? Say (O Muhammad): The cause belongeth wholly to Allah. They hide within themselves (a thought) which they reveal not unto thee, saying: Had we had any part in the cause we should not have been slain here. Say: Even though ye had been in your houses, those appointed to be slain would have gone forth to the places where they were to lie. (All this hath been) in order that Allah might try what is in your breasts and prove what is in your hearts. Allah is Aware of what is hidden in the breasts (of men)
________________
7.2 huzn (  حزن  )  : means sadness. To feels distressed with regard to something and this depicts the restless nature of human beings. When nothing can be done about distress, it takes the form of sadness. And huzn(  حزن  ) is also used for difficulties. Therefore, that kind of sadness which is because of some difficulty is called huzn(  حزن  ).  Allah states that:
________________
Surat Yusuf -   سُوۡرَةُ یُوسُف
12:84
وَٱبۡيَضَّتۡ عَيۡنَاهُ مِنَ ٱلۡحُزۡنِ
And he turned away from them and said: Alas, my grief for Joseph!   And his eyes were whitened with the sorrow that he was suppressing.
________________
7.3 bassa (  بت  )  : means extreme sadness (  شدت الحزن  ) that kind of sorrow which eats a man from within, a long period of grief and sorrow. It is stated in the Quran:
________________
Surat Yusuf -   سُوۡرَةُ یُوسُف
12:86
إِنَّمَآ أَشۡكُواْ بَثِّى وَحُزۡنِىٓ إِلَى ٱللَّهِ
He said:   I expose my distress and anguish only unto Allah  , and I know from Allah that which ye know not.
________________
Summary:
1.GHAM(  غم  ): a common word used for distress and sorrow.
2. HUZN(  حزن  ): that kind of sadness whose source is some kind of difficulty.
3. BASSA(  بت  ): extreme sorrow.

9 GHAUR KERNA
[To ponder] [RA’A, NAZARA and BASARA are also used for this meaning. Its details will be found in ‘DEKHNA’. When they are used in the literal meaning, then that means to think and ponder. However, this thought and contemplation are temporary.]
Synonyms: TAFAKKUR(  تَفَكَّر  ), TADABBUR(  تدبر  ), TAFAQQUH(  تفقه  ), IDDAKAR(  ادكَّر  ), ISTANBATA(  استنبط  )
9.1 tafakkur(  تَفَكَّر  )  : alfikarah(  الفَكَّره  ) means that force which translates knowledge into knowing.  And tafakkur(  تفَكَّر  ) means to to think, to contemplate, to ponder over the different aspects of a matter. Fikr(  فَكَّر  ), afkar(  افَكَّر  ), fakkar(  فَكَّر  ), and tafakkur(  تفَكَّر  ) are close to each other in meaning. Fikr meaning thought (pl afkar) and meaning to contemplate over a matter’s arguments. Allah states that:
________________
Surat Al-Baqarah(The Cow) -   سُوۡرَةُ البَقَرَة
2:219
كَذَٲلِكَ يُبَيِّنُ ٱللَّهُ لَكُمُ ٱلۡأَيَـٰتِ لَعَلَّڪُمۡ تَتَفَكَّرُونَ
They question thee about strong drink and games of chance. Say: In both is great sin, and (some) utility for men; but the sin of them is greater than their usefulness. And they ask thee what they ought to spend. Say: that which is superfluous.   Thus Allah maketh plain to you (His) revelations, that haply ye may reflect.
________________
9.2 tadabbur (  تدبر  )  : Dubar(  دبر  ) means the backside or rear of something. And adbar(  ادبر  ) means to turn your back towards someone. And tadabbur(  تدبر  ) means to think over the outcome of something, to ponder and contemplate over its results then to create a plan accordingly. And this is called tadbeer(  تدبير  ). Allah states that:
________________
Surat Al-Mumenoon (The Believers) -   سُوۡرَةُ المؤمنون
23:68
أَفَلَمۡ يَدَّبَّرُواْ ٱلۡقَوۡلَ أَمۡ جَآءَهُم مَّا لَمۡ يَأۡتِ ءَابَآءَهُمُ ٱلۡأَوَّلِينَ
Have they not pondered the Word, or hath that come unto them which came not unto their fathers of old?
________________
9.3 tafaqquh (  تفقه  )  : alfaqah(  الفقه  ) means to reach the knowledge of unknown from known, to achieve something and gain knowledge about it. Then this was associated with the knowledge of Shariah. Every person who has knowledge of permissible and prohibited things is faqeeh(  فقيه  ) and tafaqquh(  تفقه  ) means to ponder over known things and orders and reach a solution over a problem for which there was no specific order, to create understanding. Allah states that:
________________
Surat Al-Tawba (Repentance) -   سُوۡرَةُ التّوبَة
9:122
فَلَوۡلَا نَفَرَ مِن كُلِّ فِرۡقَةٍ۬ مِّنۡہُمۡ طَآٮِٕفَةٌ۬ لِّيَتَفَقَّهُواْ فِى ٱلدِّينِ
And the believers should not all go out to fight.   Of every troop of them, a party only should go forth, that they (who are left behind) may gain sound knowledge in religion  , and that they may warn their folk when they return to them, so that they may beware.
________________
9.4 iddakar(  ادكَّر  )  : zakara(  ذكَّر  ) means to remember something. And zakkar(  ذكَّر  ) means to make someone remember something in such a way that he takes advice from it. And iddakar(  ادكَّر  ) means to remember something yourself, bring to mind, then think over it and ponder over it to take advice from it. Allah states that:
________________
Surat Al-Qamar (The Moon) -   سُوۡرَةُ القَمَر
54:17
وَلَقَدۡ يَسَّرۡنَا ٱلۡقُرۡءَانَ لِلذِّكۡرِ فَهَلۡ مِن مُّدَّكِرٍ۬
And in truth We have made the Qur'an easy to remember; but is there any that remembereth?
________________
9.5 istanbata(  استنبط  )  : nabat(  نبط  ) means the water that is taken out for the first time after digging a well. And nabata(  نبط  ) means to take out water from the base of a well. And istanbaat(  استنباط  ) has the meaning of elicitation and istanbata(  استنبط  ) means to reveal something from hiding, to take out of control, to invent. Istanbaat(  استنباط  ) is actually a form of interpretation in which you contemplate over the knowledge of known things and reach its core and deduce results and solutions to other problems. Allah states that:
________________
Surat Al-Nisa (Women) -   سُوۡرَةُ النِّسَاء
4:83
وَلَوۡ رَدُّوهُ إِلَى ٱلرَّسُولِ وَإِلَىٰٓ أُوْلِى ٱلۡأَمۡرِ مِنۡہُمۡ لَعَلِمَهُ ٱلَّذِينَ يَسۡتَنۢبِطُونَهُ ۥ مِنۡہُمۡ‌ۗ
And if any tidings, whether of safety or fear, come unto them, they noise it abroad, whereas   if they had referred it to the messenger and to such of them as are in authority, those among them who are able to think out the matter would have known it  . If it had not been for the grace of Allah upon you and His mercy ye would have followed Satan, save a few (of you).
________________
Summary:
1.TAFAKKUR(  تَفَكَّر  ):to ponder over various aspects of a matter.
2. TADABBUR(  تدبر  ): to keep an eye on the outcome of a matter and then plan accordingly.
3. TAFAQQUH(  تفقه  ): to ponder over known things and create an understanding and try to find solutions to similar problems.
4. IDDAKAR(  ادكَّر  ): to bring a matter to remembrance and taking advice from it.
5. ISTANBATA(  استنبط  ): to ponder wonder the knowledge of the known and find solutions and results of incidental problems.

Page 878
ہ
1 HATH [Hand]
Synonyms: YADD, YAMEEN, SHIMAAL, DIRAA’
1.1YADD (ید):   Means a hand. The actually word is YADDI (یدی), but the ‘ی’ was dropped. The double of it is YADAAN (یَدَان) and YADAIN (یَدَیْن), and plural is AIEDI (اَیْدِی). Allah says in the Quran
Surah Al-Baqarah (The cow): سورۃ البَقَرَۃ  2:79
فَوَيْلٌ لَّهُم مِّمَّا كَتَبَتْ أَيْدِيهِمْ وَوَيْلٌ لَّهُم مِّمَّا يَكْسِبُونَ
Woe to them for what their hands have written and woe to them for what they earn.
And because hand is the most vital part of body when it comes to work and strength, this word also symbolizes strength, possession and ownership. Allah says in the Quran
Surah Al-Baqarah (The cow): سورۃ البَقَرَۃ  2:237
أَن يَعْفُونَ أَوْ يَعْفُوَ الَّذِي بِيَدِهِ عُقْدَةُ النِّكَاحِ
unless they forego the right, or the one in whose hand is the marriage contract foregoes it۔
And BAIEN-YADEE (بین یدی) and BAIEN-AIDEE (بین ایدی) is used for previous and front or present metaphorically. Allah says in the Quran
Surah Al-Mujadila (The Pleading Women) سُوۡرَةُ المجَادلة 58:12
يَا أَيُّهَا الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا إِذَا نَاجَيْتُمُ الرَّسُولَ فَقَدِّمُوا بَيْنَ يَدَيْ نَجْوَاكُمْ صَدَقَةً
O you who have believed, when you [wish to] privately consult the Messenger, present before your consultation a charity.
In another place in Holy Quran
Surah Yaseen (Yaseen): سورۃ ٰیٰس 36:9
وَجَعَلْنَا مِن بَيْنِ أَيْدِيهِمْ سَدًّا وَمِنْ خَلْفِهِمْ سَدًّا
And We have put a bar in front of them and a bar behind them,
Also in Quran
Surah Al-Baqarah (The cow): سورۃ البَقَرَۃ  2:65
فَقُلْنَا لَهُمْ كُونُوا قِرَدَةً خَاسِئِينَ فَجَعَلْنَاهَا نَكَالًا لِّمَا بَيْنَ يَدَيْهَا وَمَا خَلْفَهَا
We said to them: "Be you monkeys, despised and rejected." So We made this punishment an example to their own and to succeeding generations
Page 879
1.2 YAMEEN (یَمِیْن):   (Plural AIEMAAN (اَیْمَان)) means the right hand. For instance in Quran
Surah Ta-Ha (Ta-ha):سورۃ طٰھٰ  20:17
وَمَا تِلْكَ بِيَمِينِكَ يَا مُوسَىٰ
And what is that in your right hand, O Moses?"
And also the right side (Opposite SHIMAAL (شمال) (left)). For instance in the Quran
Surah Saba' (Sheba) - سورة سبإ 34:15
لَقَدْ كَانَ لِسَبَإٍ فِي مَسْكَنِهِمْ آيَةٌ ۖ جَنَّتَانِ عَن يَمِينٍ وَشِمَالٍ ۖ
There was for [the tribe of] Saba' in their dwelling place a sign: two [fields of] gardens on the right and on the left.
The way YADD (ید) is used for strength and possession, YAMEEN (یَمِیْن) is used for a wider range of meanings because in power and skill right hand is better than left hand. MULK-YAMEEN (ملک یمین) refers to that thing which is under complete ownership and authority. Metaphorically it refers to a male or female slave. For instance in the Quran
Surah An-Nisa (The women): سورۃ النِّسا 4:24
وَالْمُحْصَنَاتُ مِنَ النِّسَاءِ إِلَّا مَا مَلَكَتْ أَيْمَانُكُمْ
Also (forbidden are) women already married, except those (captives and slaves) whom your right hands possess.
Apart from this, Arab used to put or strike their right hand on the hand of the addressed person to strengthen an oath, thus this word started to be used for a vow or oath. YAMEEN (یَمِیْن) is that swearing that is done to strengthen a vow. Allah says in the Quran
Surah Al Tawbah (The repentance): سورۃ التوبھ 9:13
أَلَا تُقَاتِلُونَ قَوْمًا نَّكَثُوا أَيْمَانَهُمْ
Would you not fight a people who broke their oaths
1.3 SHIMAAL (شِمَال):   Means left, left hand, or left side (Opposite YAMEEN (یَمِیْن)). The way YAMEEN (یَمِیْن) refers to fortune and good luck, in the same way SHIMAAL (شِمَال) refers to bad luck   (dictionary al Manjad)  . (Plural SHMAAIL (شمائل)). In the Quran
Surah Al-Haqqah (The reality): سورۃ الحَاقَّۃ 69:25
وَأَمَّا مَنْ أُوتِيَ كِتَابَهُ بِشِمَالِهِ فَيَقُولُ يَا لَيْتَنِي لَمْ أُوتَ كِتَابِيَهْ
But as for he who is given his record in his left hand, he will say, "Oh, I wish I had not been given my record
Another place in the Quran
Surah Al-Araf (The heights): سورۃ الأعرَاف 7:17
ثُمَّ لَآتِيَنَّهُم مِّن بَيْنِ أَيْدِيهِمْ وَمِنْ خَلْفِهِمْ وَعَنْ أَيْمَانِهِمْ وَعَن شَمَائِلِهِمْ
Then I will come to them from before them and from behind them and on their right and on their left,
Page 880
1.4 DIRAA’ (ذِرَاع):   Means hand. Span between elbow till the middle finger. DARAA’-ATH-THAUB (ذَرَعَ الثَوَبَ) means to measure a cloth with DIRAA’ (ذراع) and DARUHU-KADA (ذَرْعُہُ کَذَا) means this is the length or measurement. And DIRAA’ (ذراع) is a tool for measurement whose length is between fifty (50) to seventy (70) centimeters   (dictionary al Manjad)  . Almost twenty (20) to twenty-seven (27) inches. The reason for the difference in measurement is that in the earlier ages the heights of humans used to be tall which have reduced now. Certain translators take DIRAA’ (ذِرَاع) as a yard.
Surah Al-Haqqah (The reality): سورۃ الحَاقَّۃ 69:32
ثُمَّ فِي سِلْسِلَةٍ ذَرْعُهَا سَبْعُونَ ذِرَاعًا فَاسْلُكُوهُ
Then into a chain whose length is seventy cubits insert him."
Summary:
1.1YADD: Hand, power or possession.
1.2 YAMEEN: Right hand, complete ownership and authority.
1.3 SHIMAAL: Left hand, left side.
1.4 DIRAA’: Hand and a tool for measuring cubits.

10 HUM AAHANGI HONA
[to have mutual understanding]
Synonyms: QAREEN(  قرين  ), ATRAAB(  أتراب  ), SAMMI(  سمي  ), KUFWA(  كفو  ), SAFFA(  صف  ), DAHAA(  ضاهى  )
10.1 qareen(  قرين  )  : qarn(  قرن  )(pl:qaroon(  قرون  )) meaning era, period (for details, see zamana). In this way, qareen(  قرين  ) means of same age and qarn(  قرن  ) means that one rope with which you tie two camels. Qaran-as-saurain(  قرن الثورين  ) meaning to tie two cows together, thus qareen(  قرين  ) means companion, such a companion who is very close and it is usually used in  a negative sense. Allah states that:
________________
Surat An-Nisa (Women) -   سُوۡرَةُ النِّسَاء
4:38
وَمَن يَكُنِ ٱلشَّيۡطَـٰنُ لَهُ ۥ قَرِينً۬ا فَسَآءَ قَرِينً۬ا
And (also) those who spend their wealth in order to be seen of men, and believe not in Allah nor the Last Day. Whoso taketh Satan for a comrade, a bad comrade hath he
________________
10.2 atraab (  أتراب  )  : turaab(  تراب  ) means sand, dirt. Tariba(  ترب  ) means to be covered in dust as well as being poor. And atraba(  اترب  ) means to be rich as well as to be healthy. And taarab(  تارب  ) means to lay together in sand, be of same age, be a friend. (pl: atraab(  أتراب  )) The feminine of tariba(  ترب  ) is taribata(  تربة  ) meaning woman of same  age. Atraab(  أتراب  ) is used for women thus atraab(  أتراب  ) means those friends and women among which there is mutual understanding. It is stated in the Quran:
________________
Surat Al-Waqia (The Event)  -   سُوۡرَةُ الواقِعَة
56: 36-37
عُرُبًا أَتۡرَابً۬ا فَجَعَلۡنَـٰهُنَّ أَبۡكَارًا
And made them virgins, (36) Lovers, friends,
________________
10.3 sammi(  سمي  )  : ism(  اسم  ) means name and sammi(  سمي  ) means of same name, such two or more people who have the same name. Allah states that:
________________
Surat Maryam -   سُوۡرَةُ مَریَم
19:7
ٱسۡمُهُ ۥ يَحۡيَىٰ لَمۡ نَجۡعَل لَّهُ ۥ مِن قَبۡلُ سَمِيًّ۬ا
(It was said unto him): O Zachariah! Lo! We bring thee tidings of a son whose name is John; we have given the same name to none before (him).
________________
10.4 kufwa(  كفو  )  : kafa(  كفا  ), kafoo(  كفو  ) and kafa(  كفى  ) meaning of same standard and stature, equal and meaning example, unison, and meaning to be of same standard as the other. Kifaa(  كفاء  ) is used for such a piece of cloth which is put on the backside of a tent with a similar cloth piece. The word kufwa(  كفو  ) is usually used at the time of a wedding or fight. Fulan kufwun liflaan(  فلان كفو لفلان  ) meaning those two people are of same standard. Allah states that:
________________
Surat Al-Ikhlas (The Unity) -   سُوۡرَةُ الإخلاص
112:4
وَلَمۡ يَكُن لَّهُ ۥ ڪُفُوًا أَحَدٌ
And there is none comparable unto Him.
________________
10.5 saffa(  صف  )  : meaning to make a queue, to make straight queue. Saffafa(  صفف  ) means to keep a queue straight. Saffa(  صف  ) means a straight line of everything, class, disciplined nation. Allah states that:
________________
Surat Al-Fajr (The Dawn) -   سُوۡرَةُ الفَجر
89:22
وَجَآءَ رَبُّكَ وَٱلۡمَلَكُ صَفًّ۬ا صَفًّ۬ا
And thy Lord shall come with angels, rank on rank,
________________
Asaafatu min alibl(  الصافة من الابل  ) (pl: safaat(  صافات  ) and sawwaaf(  صواف  )) camel standing in a queue and saaf(  صف  ) meaning camels who have kept their legs in a queue. Saffa-at-tair(  صف الطير  ) means the birds kept their wings straight in a line during flight and the birds spread their wings in the air and not moving them and all of them doing this. Allah states that:
________________
Surat Al-Mulk (The Kingdom) -   سُوۡرَةُ المُلک
67:19
أَوَلَمۡ يَرَوۡاْ إِلَى ٱلطَّيۡرِ فَوۡقَهُمۡ صَـٰٓفَّـٰتٍ۬ وَيَقۡبِضۡنَ‌ۚ مَا يُمۡسِكُهُنَّ إِلَّا ٱلرَّحۡمَـٰنُ‌ۚ
Have they not seen the birds above them spreading out their wings and closing them? Naught upholdeth them save the Beneficent. Lo! He is Seer of all things.
________________
10.6 daaha(  ضاهى  )  : daaha-rajul(  ضاهى الرجل  ) meaning one person resembling the other or to have similar habits. Dahiyyun(  ضهى  ) meaning identical person. Allah states that:
________________
Surat Al-Tawba (Repentance) -   سُوۡرَةُ التّوبَة
9:30
يُضَـٰهِـُٔونَ قَوۡلَ ٱلَّذِينَ ڪَفَرُواْ
And the Jews say: Ezra is the son of Allah, and the Christians say: The Messiah is the son of Allah. That is their saying with their mouths. They imitate the saying of those who disbelieved of old. Allah (Himself) fighteth against them. How perverse are they!
________________
Summary:
1. QAREEN(  قرين  ): same age companion.
2. ATRAAB(  أتراب  ): of same age and similar interests, friends, companions.
3. SAMMI(  سمي  ): of same name.
4. KUFWA(  كفو  ): of same standard and stature.
5. SAFFA(  صف  ): straight queue and line.
6. DAAHI(  ضاهى  ): similar habits and facial features.

raw_text:
11 HIMMAT HAARNA
[To become hopeless]
Synonyms: FASHILA(  فشل  ), ISTAKAAN(  استكان  )
11.1 fashila(  فشل  )  : meaning showing of cowardice at the time of fight, to become hopeless, to become coward, showing fear. It is stated in the Quran:
________________
Surat Al-E-Imran (Family of Imran) -   سُوۡرَةُ آل عِمرَان
3: 152
حَتَّىٰٓ إِذَا فَشِلۡتُمۡ وَتَنَـٰزَعۡتُمۡ فِى ٱلۡأَمۡرِ
Allah verily made good His promise unto you when ye routed them by His leave, until (the moment) when your courage failed you, and ye disagreed about the order and ye disobeyed, after He had shown you that for which ye long. Some of you desired the world, and some of you desired the Hereafter. Therefore He made you flee from them, that He might try you. Yet now He hath forgiven you. Allah is a Lord of Kindness to believers.
________________
11.2 istakaan(  استكان  )  : meaning to lose heart and become hopeless after becoming weak and tired of hard work, to become exhausted and helpless. Allah states that:
________________
Surat Al-E-Imran (Family of Imran)  -   سُوۡرَةُ آل عِمرَان
3:146
فَمَا وَهَنُواْ لِمَآ أَصَابَہُمۡ فِى سَبِيلِ ٱللَّهِ وَمَا ضَعُفُواْ وَمَا ٱسۡتَكَانُواْ‌ۗ
And with how many a prophet have there been a number of devoted men who fought (beside him). They quailed not for aught that befell them in the way of Allah, nor did they weaken, nor were they brought low. Allah loveth the steadfast.
________________
Summary:
FASHILA(  فشل  ) is used to depict being weak and hopeless at the start and ISTAKAN(  استكان  ) for being hopeless after complete hard work and effort.
