SYNONYMS:JALA (JLW)جلا جلو,NAFA(نفي)
9.1 JALA-  :JALA(جلا) meaning to clear some command-to make apparent or visible-JALA ARRAJL(3N BALADIHI)[جلا الرجل (عن بلدهِ)]to make someone leave one's city or    country.to    exile.JALA ANNAKHL( جَلَا النَّحْل) meaning to extract honey by steaming away honey bees.and ALJALIY(الجالي) meaning those traveller who left behind their country. In the QURAN
Surat Al-Ĥashr (The Exile) - سورة الحشر
59:3
وَلَوْلَا أَن كَتَبَ اللَّهُ عَلَيْهِمُ الْجَلَاءَ لَعَذَّبَهُمْ فِي الدُّنْيَا ۖ وَلَهُمْ فِي الْآخِرَةِ عَذَابُ النَّارِ
And if not that Allah had decreed for them evacuation, He would have punished them in [this] world, and for them in the Hereafter is the punishment of the Fire.
9.2 NAFA  :meaning to not remain,and its antonym is CABATA(ثَبَتَ) and MANFIYمنفي meaning annihilated/destroyed.being moved away and NAFA ARRAJL MIN BALADIHI(نفي الرجل من بلدهِ) meaning to exile some one of city. and NAFA YANFU(نَفَي ينفوا) meaning to imprison in prison.and to chuck something out side as well like mill,to flour-or vessel to boil or flood to garbage.ANNIFAYAH(اَلنِّفَايَة) is that useless thing which is thrown aside.so NAFA YANFUW includes the elements of helplessness and insult. ALLAH said
Surat Al-Mā'idah (The Table Spread) - سورة المائدة
5:33
إِنَّمَا جَزَاءُ الَّذِينَ يُحَارِبُونَ اللَّهَ وَرَسُولَهُ وَيَسْعَوْنَ فِي الْأَرْضِ فَسَادًا أَن يُقَتَّلُوا أَوْ يُصَلَّبُوا أَوْ تُقَطَّعَ أَيْدِيهِمْ وَأَرْجُلُهُم مِّنْ خِلَافٍ أَوْ يُنفَوْا مِنَ الْأَرْضِ ۚ ذَٰلِكَ لَهُمْ خِزْيٌ فِي الدُّنْيَا ۖ وَلَهُمْ فِي الْآخِرَةِ عَذَابٌ عَظِيمٌ
Indeed, the penalty for those who wage war against Allah and His Messenger and strive upon earth [to cause] corruption is none but that they be killed or crucified or that their hands and feet be cut off from opposite sides or that they be exiled from the land. That is for them a disgrace in this world; and for them in the Hereafter is a great punishment,
SUMMARY:
9.1 JALA-:meaning to exile some one
9.2 NAFA YANFUW meaning to expel someone with insult and humiliation

1. KATNA [to cut]
Synonyms:  HASADA, SARAMA, QATA’A, QATTA’A, BATARA, BATAKA, ADDA, KHASADA, JAZZA, AQARA
1.1 HASADA (حَصَدَ):   To cut or harvest a fully ready crop. HASEED (حَصِیْد) means harvested crop. MAHSAD (محصد) means a sickle and HASEEDAH (حصیدۃ) is the portion of crop left after harvest, which cannot be reached by the sickle. Thus the word HASADA (حَصَدَ) is used for cutting a crop with a sickle. In the Quran
Surah Yusuf (Joseph): سورۃ یُوسُف 12:47
فَمَا حَصَدتُّمۡ فَذَرُوهُ فِى سُنۢبُلِهِۦۤ
But whatever you harvest, leave it in its spikes,
1.2 SARAMA (صَرَمَ):   To cut down a tree with a sharp tool. SAARIM (صَارِم) means a sword and SARUMA (صَرُمَ) means to cut with a sword. And SAROOM (صَرُوُم) a cutting sword   (dictionary Al   Manjad  )  . Allah says in the Quran
Surah Al-Qalam (The Pen):سورۃ القلم  68:17
إِنَّا بَلَوۡنَـٰهُمۡ كَمَا بَلَوۡنَآ أَصۡحَـٰبَ ٱلۡجَنَّةِ إِذۡ أَقۡسَمُواْ لَيَصۡرِمُنَّہَا مُصۡبِحِينَ
We tested them, as We tested the owners of the garden, when they vowed to harvest it in the morning.
1.3 QATA’A (قَطَعَ):   To slice of a part of something. Allah says in the Holy Quran
Surah Al Hashr (The exile): سورۃ الحَشر 59:5
مَا قَطَعۡتُم مِّن لِّينَةٍ أَوۡ تَرَڪۡتُمُوهَا قَآٮِٕمَةً عَلَىٰٓ أُصُولِهَا فَبِإِذۡنِ ٱللَّهِ
Whether you cut down a tree, or leave it standing on its trunk, it is by God’s will.
1.4 QATTA’A (قَطَّعَ):   To cut something into pieces. To chop into small pieces. Allah says in the Holy Quran
Surah Muhammad (Muhammad): سُوۡرَةُ محَمَّد 47:15
وَسُقُواْ مَآءً حَمِيمً۬ا فَقَطَّعَ أَمۡعَآءَهُمۡ
and are given to drink boiling water, that cuts-up their bowels?
1.5 BATARA (بَتَرَ):   This word is used to refer to cutting the tail of an animal. It also means to clip off generations, childless or someone who won’t be remembered in good terms. Allah says in the Quran
Surah Al-Kauther (Abundance): سُوۡرَةُ الکَوثَر108:3
إِنَّ شَانِئَكَ هُوَ ٱلۡأَبۡتَرُ
For he who hated you, he will be cut off (from Future Hope).
1.6 BATAKA (بتك):   According to Khalil this word means to cut the ear of. According to Imam Raghib this word means to slice the ears or other organ or hair of an animal. During the times of ignorance people used to do these things as an offering or sacrifice. In the Quran
Surah An-Nisa (The women): سورۃ النِّسا 4:119
وَلَأُضِلَّنَّهُمۡ وَلَأُمَنِّيَنَّهُمۡ وَلَأَمُرَنَّهُمۡ فَلَيُبَتِّڪُنَّ ءَاذَانَ ٱلۡأَنۡعَـٰمِ
“And I will mislead them, and I will entice them, and I will prompt them to slit the ears of cattle, and I will prompt them to alter the creation of God.”
1.7 ADDA (عَضَّ):   To bite an animal with teeth, to bite. Allah says in the Quran
Surah Al-Furqaan (The criterion): سورۃ الفُرْقان 25:27
وَيَوۡمَ يَعَضُّ ٱلظَّالِمُ عَلَىٰ يَدَيۡهِ يَقُولُ يَـٰلَيۡتَنِى ٱتَّخَذۡتُ مَعَ ٱلرَّسُولِ سَبِيلاً۬
On that Day, the wrongdoer will bite his hands, and say, “If only I had followed the way with the Messenger.
1.8 KHADADA (خَضَدَ):   To cut or remove the thorns of a tree. To make thorn-less   (dictionary Al   Manjad  )  . In the Quran
Surah Al-Waqiah (The Inevitable): سُوۡرَةُ الواقِعَة 56:28
فِى سِدۡرٍ۬ مَّخۡضُودٍ۬
(They will be) among Lote-trees without thorns,
1.9 JAZZA (جَزَّ):   The word actually means to cut or grind into tiny pieces. AL-JIZZ (الجِزّ) means a small piece of a chopped up thing, JUZAD (جُزاد) or JUZAZ (جُزاز) means a slice or a piece of gold, JAAZAT (جَازات) means  small bits and pieces of a chopped up thing   (dictionary Al   Manjad  )  . In Quran this word is used for the same meanings.  فَجَعَلَهُمۡ جُذَٲذًا (21:58)  ( So he reduced them into pieces) and this word was started to mean cutting and breaking. In the Quran
Surah Hud (Hud): سورۃ ھود 11:108
عَطَآءً غَيۡرَ مَجۡذُوذٍ۬
a gift without break.
1.10 AQARA (عَقَرَ):   Has the meaning of wounding in it. AL-KALB-AQOOR (الکلب العقور) means a biting dog. AQAR-AN-NAKHLA (عَقَرَالنَّخْلَۃ) means to uproot a date palm, cut it from its roots   (dictionary Al   Manjad  )  . In the Quran
Surah Ash-Shams (The Sun): سُوۡرَةُ الشّمس 91:14
فَكَذَّبُوهُ فَعَقَرُوهَا
Then they rejected him (as a false prophet), and they hamstrung her.
Summary:
1.1      HASADA: To Cut a ripe crop with sickle
1.2 SARAMA: To cut bunch of fruits with a sharp tool.
1.3 QATA’A: To slice of something.
1.4 QATTA’A: To cut into pieces
1.5 BATARA: To cut an animal’s tail, to be childless
1.6 BATAKA: To slice or cut an ear
1.7 ADDA: To bite
PAGE 691
1.8 KHADADA: Clear of thorns of a tree.
1.9 JAZZA: To cut a hard thing into small pieces.
1.10 AQARA: To cut to wound gravely.

وَيَوۡمَ يَعَضُّ ٱلظَّالِمُ عَلَىٰ يَدَيۡهِ يَقُولُ يَـٰلَيۡتَنِى ٱتَّخَذۡتُ مَعَ ٱلرَّسُولِ سَبِيلاً۬

On that Day, the wrongdoer will bite his hands, and say, “If only I had followed the way with the Messenger.

1.8 KHADADA (خَضَدَ): To cut or remove the thorns of a tree. To make thorn-less (dictionary Al Manjad). In the Quran

Surah Al-Waqiah (The Inevitable): سُوۡرَةُ الواقِعَة 56:28

فِى سِدۡرٍ۬ مَّخۡضُودٍ۬

 (They will be) among Lote-trees without thorns,

 

1.9 JAZZA (جَزَّ): The word actually means to cut or grind into tiny pieces. AL-JIZZ (الجِزّ) means a small piece of a chopped up thing, JUZAD (جُزاد) or JUZAZ (جُزاز) means a slice or a piece of gold, JAAZAT (جَازات) means  small bits and pieces of a chopped up thing (dictionary Al Manjad). In Quran this word is used for the same meanings.  فَجَعَلَهُمۡ جُذَٲذًا (21:58)  ( So he reduced them into pieces) and this word was started to mean cutting and breaking. In the Quran

Surah Hud (Hud): سورۃ ھود 11:108

 عَطَآءً غَيۡرَ مَجۡذُوذٍ۬

 a gift without break.

 

1.10 AQARA (عَقَرَ): Has the meaning of wounding in it. AL-KALB-AQOOR (الکلب العقور) means a biting dog. AQAR-AN-NAKHLA (عَقَرَالنَّخْلَۃ) means to uproot a date palm, cut it from its roots (dictionary Al Manjad). In the Quran

Surah Ash-Shams (The Sun): سُوۡرَةُ الشّمس 91:14

فَكَذَّبُوهُ فَعَقَرُوهَا

Then they rejected him (as a false prophet), and they hamstrung her.

Summary:

1.1  HASADA: To Cut a ripe crop with sickle

1.2 SARAMA: To cut bunch of fruits with a sharp tool.

1.3 QATA’A: To slice of something.

1.4 QATTA’A: To cut into pieces

1.5 BATARA: To cut an animal’s tail, to be childless

1.6 BATAKA: To slice or cut an ear

1.7 ADDA: To bite

PAGE 691

1.8 KHADADA: Clear of thorns of a tree.

1.9 JAZZA: To cut a hard thing into small pieces.

1.10 AQARA: To cut to wound gravely.

10. KITAAB [Book]
Synonyms: KITAB, ASFAAR, SIJIL, NUSKHAH, ZUBUR, SUHUF
10.1 KITAB (کِتَاب):   Means a written object, letter, manuscript of deed, renowned word for book (plural KUTUB (کتب) ). In the Quran
Surah An-Naml (The ant): سورۃ النَّمل 27:28
ٱذۡهَب بِّكِتَـٰبِى هَـٰذَا
Go with this letter of mine
10.2 ASFAAR (اَسْفَار):   (singular SIFR (سَفْر)) SIFR (سِفْر) means a big book. One of the volumes of Torah (  dictionary Al   Manjad  )  . SUFR (سُفْر) means to declare or reveal something. SIFR (سِفْر) is a book that reveals the truth. A large scholia or explanation of Torah. Allah says in the Quran
Surah Al-Jumua (Friday): سُوۡرَةُ الجُمُعَة 62:5
مَثَلُ ٱلَّذِينَ حُمِّلُواْ ٱلتَّوۡرَٮٰةَ ثُمَّ لَمۡ يَحۡمِلُوهَا كَمَثَلِ ٱلۡحِمَارِ يَحۡمِلُ أَسۡفَارَۢا‌ۚ
The example of those who were entrusted with the Torah, but then failed to uphold it, is like the donkey carrying works of literature
10.3 SIJIL(سِجِل):   Means a register of instructions, a register of laws and claims which are kept by a judge. A judicial register. Allah says in the Quran
Surah Al-Anbiya (the prophets): سورۃ الانَبیاء 21:104
يَوۡمَ نَطۡوِى ٱلسَّمَآءَ ڪَطَىِّ ٱلسِّجِلِّ لِلۡڪُتُبِ‌ۚ
On the Day when We fold the heaven, like the folding of a book.
10.4 NUSKHAH (نُسْخَة):   NASAKH (نَسَخَ) means to erase or reject. NASAKH-AL-KITAAB (نسخ الکتاب) means to copy a book word-by-word. NUSKHAH (نُسْخَة) means anything that can be copied from and which is also copied. Every NUSKHAH (نُسْخَة) is a book but every book is not a NUSKHAH. Allah says in the Quran
Surah Al-Araf (The heights): سورۃ الأعرَاف 7:154
وَفِى نُسۡخَتِہَا هُدً۬ى وَرَحۡمَةٌ۬ لِّلَّذِينَ هُمۡ لِرَبِّہِمۡ يَرۡهَبُونَ
In their transcript is guidance and mercy for those in awe of their Lord.
10.5 ZUBUR (زُبُر):   ZUBRAH (زِبْرۃ) means a large sheet of iron (plural ZUBAR (زُبَر) ), ZABAR-AL-KITAB (زَبَرالکِتَاب) means to write a book in large font. ZIBR (زِبْر) is actually a verbal noun but is also used as a noun and gives the meaning of a noun and means a book (plural ZUBUR (زُبُر)). ZABOOR (زَبُور) is the Holy Book sent on DAVID (Hazrat Daood A.S). MIZBAR (مِزْبر) means a pen (  dictionary Al   Manjad  ). ZUBARA   (زُبَرَ)   means to write on a stone and basically refers to thickness and grossness. Allah says in the Quran
Surah Ash-Shura’ (The Poets): صورۃ الشُّعْراء 26:196
وَإِنَّهُ ۥ لَفِى زُبُرِ ٱلۡأَوَّلِينَ
And it is in the scriptures of the ancients.
10.6   SUHUF (صُحُف):   (singular SAHEEFAH(صَحِیْفَۃ)) SAHEEFA (صَحِیْفَۃ) means outspread thing that can write or  be written on. SAHEEFA (صَحِیْفَۃ) also means a written paper or leaf. SIHAFA (صِحَافَة) means journalism and ISHAAF (اَصْحَفَ) means to compile written papers into a book. MUSHAF (مُصْحَف) means a book. A bound scripture. Allah says in the Quran
Surah Al-Ala (The Most High): سُوۡرَةُ الاٴعلی 87:18-19
إِنَّ هَـٰذَا لَفِى ٱلصُّحُفِ ٱلۡأُولَىٰ صُحُفِ إِبۡرَٲهِيمَ وَمُوسَىٰ
This is in the former scriptures. The Scriptures of Abraham and Moses.
Summary
10.1 KITAAB: A written object. Famous word for book.
10.2 ASFAAR: Scholia and explanation of large books (Torah)
10.3 SIJIL: Written notes or books that can be kept as a record.
10.4 NUSKHAH: A copied book or one that can be copied from
10.5 ZUBUR: A book written in large font
10.6 SUHUF: Written leaves of paper that can be compiled into a book.

raw_text:
11. KATRA JANA – BACH KAY NIKAL JANA [to clip, to escape safely]
Synonyms: ZAAWARA, QARADA, HAADA
11.1ZAAWARA (زَاوَرَ):   QAWL-AZ-ZAAWAR (قول الزاور) means a wrong or twisted statement, AZWAR (اَزْوَر) means a person who has an obstructive nature (  dictionary Al   Manjad  )  . BI’RUN-ZAWRAA’ (بِئْرٌزَوْرَاءَ) means a well that is dug up distortedly, ZAWARA (زَاوَرَ) means to bend or escape by bending.
11.3 QARADA (قَرَضَ):   Means to clip and escape by clipping, QARAD-AL-MAAKAN (قَرَضَ المَکَان) means he evaded from the place by moving away. QARADA-FIS-SAEER (قَرَضَ فیِ السَّیْر ) means to bend around while walking. Allah says in the Quran
Surah Al-Kahf (The Cave): سورۃ الکھف 18:17
وَتَرَى ٱلشَّمۡسَ إِذَا طَلَعَت تَّزَٲوَرُ عَن كَهۡفِهِمۡ ذَاتَ ٱلۡيَمِينِ وَإِذَا غَرَبَت تَّقۡرِضُہُمۡ ذَاتَ ٱلشِّمَالِ
You would have seen the sun, when it rose, veering away from their cave towards the right, and when it sets, moving away from them to the left,
11.4 HAADA (حَادَ):   Means to turn away from proper path and evade. To change direction. Allah says in the Quran
Surah Qaf (Qaf): سُوۡرَةُ قٓ 50:19
وَجَآءَتۡ سَكۡرَةُ ٱلۡمَوۡتِ بِٱلۡحَقِّ‌ۖ ذَٲلِكَ مَا كُنتَ مِنۡهُ تَحِيدُ
The daze of death has come in truth: “This is what you tried to evade.”
Synonyms:
11.1 ZAAWARA: To twist and escape
11.2 QARADA: To lop and leave a place and then follow a proper path.
11.3 HAADA: To lop and runaway and not return to a proper path

raw_text:
12. KITNAY? [How much?]
Synonyms: KAM, KA’AYYIN
12.1 KAM (کَمْ):   To inquire for an amount, meaning how much or how many, and is used as a question. In the Quran
Surah Al-Baqarah (The cow): سورۃ البَقَرَۃ  2:259
قَالَ ڪَمۡ لَبِثۡتَ‌ۖ
He said, “For how long have you tarried?”
12.1 KA’AYYIN (کَاَیٍّ):   KAM (کَمْ) and KA’YYIN (کَاَیٍّ) almost means the same. The difference is only that KA’AYYIN (کَاَیِّنْ) has excess in it too. A lot or number of or how many and not taken as a question. Allah says in the Quran
Surah Yusuf (Joseph): سورۃ یُوسُف 12:105
وَڪَأَيِّن مِّنۡ ءَايَةٍ۬ فِى ٱلسَّمَـٰوَٲتِ وَٱلۡأَرۡضِ يَمُرُّونَ عَلَيۡہَا
How many a sign in the heavens and the earth do they pass by,
For KAJI see TAIRHA HONA
For KARWAT see PEHLU

raw_text:
---PAGE 700
13 KURAIDNA [to scrape, to dig]
Synonyms: BAHATHA, BA’THARA
13.1 BAHATHA (بَحَثَ):   To dig up, to scrape, to find explore in under the earth. Allah says in the Quran
Surah Al-Maeda (The table spread): سورۃ المَائدہ 5:31
فَبَعَثَ ٱللَّهُ غُرَابً۬ا يَبۡحَثُ فِى ٱلۡأَرۡضِ لِيُرِيَهُ ۥ كَيۡفَ يُوَٲرِى سَوۡءَةَ أَخِيهِ‌ۚ
Then God sent a raven digging the ground, to show him how to cover his brother's corpse.
13.2 BA’THARA (بَعْثَرَ):   According to Imam Raghib BU’THARA (بَعْثَرَ) is made from two words BU’ITH (بُعِثَ) and UTHEER (اُثِیْر) means to dig up a grave or exhume a body. BA’THAR-AL-MATA’ (بَعْثَرَ المَتَاع) means to turn over or scatter luggage (  dictionary Al   Manjad  ).   BA’THARA (بَعْثَرَ) to dig up, bring up, or investigate. Allah says in the Quran
Surah Al-Adiyat (The Chargers): سُوۡرَةُ العَادیَات 100:9
أَفَلَا يَعۡلَمُ إِذَا بُعۡثِرَ مَا فِى ٱلۡقُبُورِ
Does he not know? When the contents of the graves are scattered around.
13.2BAHATHA: To dig up beneath the earth
13.2 BA’THARA: Scrape and bring up or reveal.

14. KARWA [bitter, painful]
Synonyms: AMARRA, UJAAJ, KHAMT
14.1 AMARRA(اَمَرَّ) :   MARRA (مَرَّ) (MARARAH(مَرَارَۃ)) means bitter or painful, MURRUN (مُرٌ) means bitter. AMARRA (اَمَرَّ) means extremely bitter or intolerable (  dictionary Al   Manjad  )  . Allah says in the Quran
Surah Al-Qamar (The moon): سورۃ القَمَر 54:46
بَلِ ٱلسَّاعَةُ مَوۡعِدُهُمۡ وَٱلسَّاعَةُ أَدۡهَىٰ وَأَمَرُّ
The Hour is their appointed time—the Hour is more disastrous, and most bitter.
14.2UJAAJ (اَجَاج):   Means bitter or saline water. AJJ-AL-MAA’ (اَجَّ الْمَاءَ) means to make water bitter or saline. Allah says in the Quran
Surah Al-Waqiah (The Inevitable): سُوۡرَةُ الواقِعَة 56:70
لَوۡ نَشَآءُ جَعَلۡنَـٰهُ أُجَاجً۬ا فَلَوۡلَا تَشۡكُرُونَ
If We will, We can make it salty. Will you not be thankful?

وَبَدَّلۡنَـٰهُم بِجَنَّتَيۡہِمۡ جَنَّتَيۡنِ ذَوَاتَىۡ أُڪُلٍ خَمۡطٍ۬
We substituted their two gardens with two gardens of bitter fruits
Synonyms:
14.1 AMARRU: Purely bitter or extremely bitter.
14.2 UJAAJ: Saline or bitter water
14.3 KHAMT: Bitter or sour, unsavory

raw_text:
Page 701--
15. KISAN [Farmer]
Synonyms: ZURRA'A, KUFFARA
15.1 ZURRA'A  (زُّرَّاعَ):  (Plural Of ZAAR'E     زَارِعْ) means a farmer, an agriculturist or a sower. It is commonly used. In the Quran
Surah Al-Fatĥ (The Victory) - سورة الفتح 48:29
كَزَرْعٍ أَخْرَجَ شَطْأَهُ فَآزَرَهُ فَاسْتَغْلَظَ فَاسْتَوَىٰ عَلَىٰ سُوقِهِ يُعْجِبُ الزُّرَّاعَ
Which produces its offshoots and strengthens them so they grow firm and stand upon their stalks, delighting the sowers .
15.2 KUFFARA  (  كُفَّار  ): (Plural of KAAFIR   كَافِرْ  ) KUFR(كُفْرِ) means to hide something. And KAAFIR(  كَافِرْ  ) refers to many things.
1. Denier of ALLAH.
2. Denier of the blessings of ALLAH or one who is Ungrateful.
3. Concealer of the truth or the one who lives in secrecy. Land or plants away from the people.
And ALKAFRU (الْكَفْرُ) refers to a land that is far away from people or Village. In the Quran:
Surat Al-Ĥadīd (The Iron) - سورة الحديد 57:20
كَمَثَلِ غَيْثٍ أَعْجَبَ الْكُفَّارَ نَبَاتُهُ
Like the example of a rain whose [resulting] plant growth pleases the tillers.
Summary  : Farmer is  KAFIR while planting a seed in the land and is ZAAR'E while maintaining it.

16. KASHTI- JAHAAZ  (Boat or Ship)
SYNONYMS: JAARIA"H, SAFINA'H, FULK
16.1 JAARIA'H   (جَارِيَة): JARA YAJRI (جَرى يَجْرِى) refers to moving or flowing. It refers to things which move like water and wind. With same consistency, a boat is referred as JAARIA'H(جَارِيَة). JAWAAR(جوار) refers to a sailing boat which moves in accordance with the flow and direction of the wind and water.
Surah Ar-Raĥmān (The Beneficent) - سورة الرحمن 55:24
وَلَهُ الْجَوَارِ الْمُنشَآتُ فِي الْبَحْرِ كَالْأَعْلَام
“And to Him belong the ships [with sails] elevated in the sea like mountains.”
16.2 SAFINA'HT  (سَفِينَة): SAFANA (سَفَنَ) means to peel off or make soft. SAFAN(سَفَن) refers to a wood cutting tool. SAFEEN (سَفِينْ) refers to a nail used to split wood and MISFAN (مِسفَن) means tools for wood cutting. And SAFANA'HT (سَفِينَة) means profession of ship-building. SAFEENA'HT refers to ship or boat. In a way SAFINA’HT (سَفِينَة) refers to a ship that is designed and made smooth and comfortable. In the Quran:
Surah Al-Kahf (The Cave) - سورة الكهف 18:79
أَمَّا السَّفِينَةُ فَكَانَتْ لِمَسَاكِينَ يَعْمَلُونَ فِي الْبَحْرِ
As for the ship, it belonged to poor people working  at sea.
Page 702--
16.3 FULK (فُلْك):     The word FULK(فُلْك) points out something moving in a circle or rotating. FALK-UM-MINAL-BAHRI (فَلْكٌ مِّنَ الْبَحْرِى) means a whirlpool, where water from all four sides gathers and rotates rapidly. And FALAK (فَلَك) means orbit. The path for rotation of all planets. AASMAN(آسمان) and ALFALKA’H(اَلفَلكَة) refers to all those things which are elevated, bulging or round. In a way, compared to rotating, a ship is called as FULK(  فُلْك  ). (It has no plural) And the word Mash’hoon(مَشحُوْن) often comes with FULK (  فُلْك  ) in Quran. And SHAHAN (شَحَنَ) means boarding a ship and filling it. ASH’SHAHNA (اَلشَّحنَة) refers to the thing which is boarded in the ship. In a way, FULK refers to a ship, which works as a freight and also for carrying passengers. In the Quran:
Surah Aş-Şāffāt (Those who set the Ranks) - سورة الصافات 37:140
وَإِنَّ يُونُسَ لَمِنَ الْمُرْسَلِين إِذْ أَبَقَ إِلَى الْفُلْكِ الْمَشْحُونَِ
And indeed, Jonah was among the messengers. [Mention] when he ran away to the laden ship.
Summary:
1. A ship is JAARIAH in terms of moving, Safinah in terms of smoothness and comfort and FULK in terms of resembling a ship.

17. Different Names Of Kaabah
Synonyms: KAABAH, AL-BAEET, BAEET-UL-ANEEQ, HARAM, BAEET-UL-HARAAM, BAEET-UL-MUHARRAM, MASJID-UL-HARAAM.
17.1 KAABAH(كَعبَة):   It refers to all cubical shaped things. With same correspondence, the KAABAH (کعبہ) is called KAABAH. Whose altitudes and dimensions are equal or almost equal. A square or constructed in resemblance with a square. In the Quran:
Surah Al-Mā'idah (The Table Spread) - سورة المائدة 5:95
يَحْكُمُ بِهِ ذَوَا عَدْلٍ مِّنكُمْ هَدْيًا بَالِغَ الْكَعْبَةِ
As judged by just two men among you as an offering [to Allah ] delivered to the Ka'bah.
17.2 AL_BAEET (اَلبَيْت):   A specific house. Bait-Ullah Shareef (House of ALLAH). In the Quran:
Surat Al-Baqarah (The Cow) - سورة البقرة 2:125
وَإِذْ جَعَلْنَا الْبَيْتَ مَثَابَةً لِّلنَّاسِ وَأَمْنًا
And [mention] when We made the House, a place of return for the people and [a place of] security
17.3 BAEET-UL-ATEEQ(بَيتُ الْعَتِيق):   Means ancient house. ATEEQ (عَتِيق) refers to such a thing which, together with being old, features nobility  and doesn’t shows any decrease at all. In the Quran:
Surah Al-Ĥaj (The Pilgrimage) - سورة الحج 22:29
وَلْيَطَّوَّفُوا بِالْبَيْتِ الْعَتِيقِ
And perform Tawaf around the ancient House.
17.4 HARAM (حَرَم):   Means Strong Prohibition (اَلمنع الشديد)
1. HARAAM(حَرَام) are those things whose use is strongly prohibited by the Sharia and its inverse is HALAAL(حَلآل) which refers to those things, on the use of which there is no restriction.
2. HARAM (  حَرَم  ) and HARAAM (حَرَام) means respectful. One who deserves respect and courtesy. In the Quran:
Surat Al-Qaşaş (The Stories) - سورة القصص 28:57
أَوَلَمْ نُمَكِّن لَّهُمْ حَرَمًا آمِنًا
Have we not established for them a safe sanctuary.
Page 703--
17.5 BAEET-UL-HARAAM(بَيتُ الحَرَام)
17.6 BAEET-UL-MUHARRAM(بَيتُ المُحَرَّم):   Both have the same meaning i.e.a respectful and sacred house. In the Quran:
Surat Al-Mā'idah (The Table Spread) - سورة المائدة 5:2
وَلَا آمِّينَ الْبَيْتَ الْحَرَامَ
And nor the people resorting to the sacred house.
Surat 'Ibrāhīm (Abrahim) - سورة ابراهيم 14:37
17.7 MASJID-UL-HARAAM(مَسجِدُ الحَرَام):   Honourable and respectful Masjid (Mosque).Bait-Ullah Shareef (House of ALLAH). In the Quran:
Surat Al-'Isrā' (The Night Journey) - سورة الإسراء 17:1
سُبْحَانَ الَّذِي أَسْرَىٰ بِعَبْدِهِ لَيْلًا مِّنَ الْمَسْجِدِ الْحَرَامِ إِلَى الْمَسْجِدِ الْأَقْصَى
Exalted is He who took His Servant by night from al-Masjid al-Haram to al-Masjid al- Aqsa

title: content/k/k18.html
raw_text:
18. KAL (Yesterday)
Synonyms: AMS, GHAD.
18.1 AMS(اَمْس):   One day past  today. Deroz(ديروز) (Yesterday) or if it occurs in vowel points, then AL’AMS(اَلاَمْس) means any day from the past periods. Also, the word AMS(اَمْس) idiomatically refers to the time that is passed recently. In the Quran:
Surat Al-Qaşaş (The Stories) - سورة القصص 28:18
فَإِذَا الَّذِي اسْتَنصَرَهُ بِالْأَمْسِ يَسْتَصْرِخُهُ
When suddenly the one who sought his (Musa A.S) help the previous day cried out to him [once again].
In this Aayah, AMS( اَمْس) refers to yesterday. While in the following Aayah, it refers to the time that has passed recently. In the Quran:
Surat Yūnus (Jonah) - سورة يونس 10:24
فَجَعَلْنَاهَا حَصِيدًا كَأَن لَّمْ تَغْنَ بِالْأَمْسِ
We make it (town) as a harvest, as if it had not flourished yesterday.
18.2 GHAD(غَد):   Means the following day. FARDA(فردا) (Tomorrow). Like AMS(اَمْس), this word also gives the meaning of both, the coming day and the near future. For instance, in the following  Aayah it refers to the coming day.
Surat Yūsuf (Joseph) - سورة يوسف 12:12
أَرْسِلْهُ مَعَنَا غَدًا يَرْتَعْ وَيَلْعَبْ وَإِنَّا لَهُ لَحَافِظُونَ
Send him with us tomorrow that he may eat well and play.
And in the below mentioned Aayah, the word GHAD(غَد) is not only referring to near future, but is also giving the meaning of the life hereafter which is close to the accordance of Quran.
Page 704--
Surat Al-Ĥashr (The Exile) - سورة الحشر 59:18
وَلْتَنظُرْ نَفْسٌ مَّا قَدَّمَتْ لِغَدٍ
And let every soul look to what it has put forth for tomorrow.

أَرْسِلْهُ مَعَنَا غَدًا يَرْتَعْ وَيَلْعَبْ وَإِنَّا لَهُ لَحَافِظُونَ

Send him with us tomorrow that he may eat well and play.

 

And in the below mentioned Aayah, the word GHAD(غَد) is not only referring to near future, but is also giving the meaning of the life hereafter which is close to the accordance of Quran.

 

Page 704--

Surat Al-Ĥashr (The Exile) - سورة الحشر 59:18

وَلْتَنظُرْ نَفْسٌ مَّا قَدَّمَتْ لِغَدٍ

And let every soul look to what it has put forth for tomorrow.

title: content/k/k19.html
raw_text:
19. KAM KARNA- KAMI KARNA- GHATANA ( To decrease, Reduce, To diminish)
Synonyms: ZALAM, ALA, QASARA, ALATA, HAZHAMA, FATARA, QALLA, TAFFAFA, KHASIRA, NAQASA, BAKHASA, FARRATA, WATARA.
19.1 ZALAMA(ظَلَمَ):   Means to place something other than it’s actual location. And it’s opposite is A’DL(عَدْل). Therefore, anything  against the justice will be cruelty. In a way, the word ZALAMA(ظَلَمَ) is widely used. In anything, whether there’s any deficiency or excess and no matter how much less or greater this variation may be, ZULM(ظلم) applies to everyone. In addition to this, this word is used as both, materialistically and meaningfully. In the Quran:
Surat Al-Kahf (The Cave) - سورة الكهف 18:33
كِلْتَا الْجَنَّتَيْنِ آتَتْ أُكُلَهَا وَلَمْ تَظْلِم مِّنْهُ شَيْئًا ۚ
Each of the two gardens produced its fruit and did not fall short thereof in anything.
19.2 ALA  (اَلَا): Means to show negligence. Not to do any work the way it should be done. To spare. In the Quran:
Surat 'Āli `Imrān (Family of Imran) - سورة آل عمران 3:118
يَا أَيُّهَا الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا لَا تَتَّخِذُوا بِطَانَةً مِّن دُونِكُمْ لَا يَأْلُونَكُمْ خَبَالًا
O you who have believed, do not take as intimates those other than yourselves, for they will not spare you [any] ruin.
19.3 QASARA(  قَصَرَ  ):   Not to do the amount of work as required. And according to Imam Raghib, not to reach the height or peak of something. Not fulfilling the fixed quantity or number. To lessen or shorten. In the Quran:
Surat An-Nisā' (The Women) - سورة النساء 4:101
وَإِذَا ضَرَبْتُمْ فِي الْأَرْضِ فَلَيْسَ عَلَيْكُمْ جُنَاحٌ أَن تَقْصُرُوا مِنَ الصَّلَاةِ
And when you travel throughout the land, there is no blame upon you for shortening the prayer.
19.4 ALATA(  اَلَتَ  ):   Means to diminish from one’s right. Diminish from one’s labour. Not to reward fully or delay for one’s work. ALQASR WA IBTA’(اَلقَصر وَ اِبطَاء). In the Quran:
Surat Aţ-Ţūr (The Mount) - سورة الطور 52:21
مَا أَلَتْنَاهُم مِّنْ عَمَلِهِم مِّن شَيْءٍ
We will not deprive them of anything of their deeds.
19.5 HAZHAMA (  هَضَمَ  ):   Means to crush, squeeze or squash something that is soft, and reduce it. To deprive a weak person from his/her right. To extort. HAZEEM (هَضِيم) means both, soft and fragile, also quick digestible. In the Quran:
Page 705--
Surat Ţāhā (Ta-Ha) - سورة طه 20:112
وَمَن يَعْمَلْ مِنَ الصَّالِحَاتِ وَهُوَ مُؤْمِنٌ فَلَا يَخَافُ ظُلْمًا وَلَا هَضْمًا
But he who does of righteous deeds while he is a believer - he will neither fear injustice nor deprivation.
19.6 FATARA(  فَتَرَ  ):   The occurrence of  weakness in anything. The decrease or subsidy in pace due to constant working or exhaustion. In the Quran:
Surat Az-Zukhruf (The Ornaments of Gold) - سورة الزخرف 43:75
إِنَّ الْمُجْرِمِينَ فِي عَذَابِ جَهَنَّمَ خَالِدُونَ ْ لَا يُفَتَّرُ عَنْهُمْ وَهُمْ فِيهِ مُبْلِسُونَ ْ
Indeed, the criminals will be in the punishment of Hell, abiding eternally. It will not be allowed to subside for them, and they, therein, are in despair.
19.7 QALLA(  قَلَّ  ):   Basically it has two meanings.
1. To be elevated.
2. To be less.
Here the second one is discussed. Means to be less in quantity or numbers. (Opposite KASURA كَثُرَ). In the Quran:
Surat Al-Kahf (The Cave) - سورة الكهف 18:39
إِن تَرَنِ أَنَا أَقَلَّ مِنكَ مَالًا وَوَلَدً ْ
Although you see me less than you in wealth and children.
19.8 TAFFAFA (  طَفَّفَ  ):   TAFEEF(طَفِيف) means an ordinary and worthless thing. And TAFFAFA(طَفَّفَ) means to fill a measurement scale a little less from the mark or even taking a small scale or parameter. In the Quran:
Surat Al-Muţaffifīn (The Defrauding) - سورة المطففين 83:1
وَيْلٌ لِّلْمُطَفِّفِينَْ
Woe to those who give less [than due].
19.9 KHASIRA(  خَسِرَ  ):   Means the decrease in capital or stock. Generally, this word is specific for trade(Opposite of RABIHA رَبِحَ). To suffer a loss. And KHASR-UL-MEEZAAN(خسرالميزان) means to bring a decrease in weight after seizing someone’s right . Like it’s said in the following Aayah,
Surat Al-Muţaffifīn (The Defrauding) - سورة المطففين 83:3
وَإِذَا كَالُوهُمْ أَو وَّزَنُوهُمْ يُخْسِرُونَ ْ
But if they give by measure or by weight to them, they cause loss.
19.10 NAQASA(  نَقَصَ  ):   To decrease or reduce.( opposite of ZADA زَادَ and ZIYADAH زِيَادَة is the opposite of NUQSAAN نُقصَان). This word is most common to KHASIRA (خَسِرَ). Every damage is a loss but every loss is not a damage. In the Quran:
Surat Al-Muzzammil (The Enshrouded One) - سورة المزمل 73:3
نِّصْفَهُ أَوِ انقُصْ مِنْهُ قَلِيلًا ْ أَوْ زِدْ عَلَيْهِ وَرَتِّلِ الْقُرْآنَ تَرْتِيلًا ْ
Half of it - or subtract from it a little. Or add to it, and recite the Qur'an with measured recitation.
19.11 BAKHASA(  بَخَسَ  ):   BAKHS (بَخس) means defective, cheap or inferior. And BAKHASA(بَخَسَ) means to give something defective or inferior in return or to give in a reduced quantity. In the Quran:
Surat Yūsuf (Joseph) - سورة يوسف 12:20
وَشَرَوْهُ بِثَمَنٍ بَخْسٍ دَرَاهِمَ مَعْدُودَةٍ
And they sold him (Hazrat Yusuf A.S) for a reduced price - a few dirhams.
PAGE 706
Surah Al-Araf (The heights): سورۃ الأعرَاف 7:85
وَلَا تَبۡخَسُواْ ٱلنَّاسَ أَشۡيَآءَهُمۡ
do not cheat people out of their rights
19.12 FARRATA (فَرَّطَ):   Means to neglect. To lag in the limits of moderation or to decrement in it. (for details see HADD SE BARHNA) FARRATA (فَرَّطَ) is from the dictionary of antonyms. Allah says in the Quran
Surah Al-Ana’am (The Cattle): سورۃ الانعام 6:31
حَتَّىٰٓ إِذَا جَآءَتۡہُمُ ٱلسَّاعَةُ بَغۡتَةً۬ قَالُواْ يَـٰحَسۡرَتَنَا عَلَىٰ مَا فَرَّطۡنَا فِيہَا
Then, when the Hour comes upon them suddenly, they will say, “Alas for us, how we have neglected it.”
19.13 WATARA (وَتَرَ):   Means to mock or tease, to hurt. To decrement in money or rights. ALWATR (اَلْوَتْر) or ALWITR (اَلْوِتْر) means to take revenge, or to do injustice while taking revenge.
Surah Muhammad (Muhammad): سُوۡرَةُ محَمَّد 47:35
وَٱللَّهُ مَعَكُمۡ وَلَن يَتِرَكُمۡ أَعۡمَـٰلَكُمۡ
for Allah is with you, and will never put you in loss for your (good) deeds.
Summary:
19.1 ZALAMA: Used for a wide range of meanings. For all types of fluctuations.
19.2 ALA: To do an unsatisfactory work.
19.3 QASARA: To fall short in some work.
19.4 ALAT: To pay less or delay a payment to a return or job.
19.5 HADHAM: To oppress a weak, to crush soft
19.6 FATARA: To fall short due to weakness
19.7 QALLA: To fall short in quantity
19.8 TAFFAFA: To measure inadequately
19.9 KHASIRA: To make a loss in business
19.10 NAQASA: More common, used for any kind of loss.
19.11 BAKHASA: To give a substandard thing or give less in exchange for a good one,
19.12 FARRATA: To err or t  o lag in the limits of moderation.
19.13 WATARA: To lag while repaying.

raw_text:
2 KATNA [to get cut]
Synonyms: TAQATTA’, MINN
2.1 TAQATTA’ (تَقَطَّعَ):   Means something getting cut or sliced off. Allah Says in the Holy Quran
Surah Al-Baqarah (The cow): سورۃ البَقَرَۃ  2:166
إِذۡ تَبَرَّأَ ٱلَّذِينَ ٱتُّبِعُواْ مِنَ ٱلَّذِينَ ٱتَّبَعُواْ وَرَأَوُاْ ٱلۡعَذَابَ وَتَقَطَّعَتۡ بِهِمُ ٱلۡأَسۡبَابُ
Then would those who are followed clear themselves of those who follow (them): They would see the penalty, and all relations between them would be cut off.
2.2 MINN (مِنَّ):   Refers to many things. 1. To be virtuous to someone. 2. Show somebody your appreciation. 3. Cut   (dictionary Al   Manjad  ),   meaning cut or get cut. The third meaning will be under the discussion. MINN-AR-RUJAL (مِنَّ الرَّجُلَ) means to exhaust someone or weaken. MINN-AL-JABL (مِنَّ الجَبْل) means to cut a rope and MINN-ASH-SHAI (مِنَّ الشَّئ) means the scarcity of something. Thus MINN (مِنَّ) can be referred to gradual decrease in something leading to its eradication or cut-off from its sequence. Allah says in the Holy Quran
Surah Fussilat (Explained in Detail): سورۃ فُصّلَت 41:8
إِنَّ ٱلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُواْ وَعَمِلُواْ ٱلصَّـٰلِحَـٰتِ لَهُمۡ أَجۡرٌ غَيۡرُ مَمۡنُونٍ۬
As for those who believe and do righteous deeds—for them is a reward uninterrupted
Summary:
2.1 TAQATTA’: Getting cut or sliced off
2.2 MINN: Gradual decrease in something leading to its cut-off from its sequence.

raw_text:
20 KAMANA – KAMAI KERNA [to earn, to work]
Synonyms: AMILA, KASABA, IKTASABA, IKTARAFA
20.1 A’MILA   (عَمِلَ)  :   Anything that a man does intentionally is his act. And because earning/working is also an act thus it also refers to earning. Allah says in the Quran.
Surah Al-Kahf (The Cave): سورۃ الکھف 18:79
أَمَّا ٱلسَّفِينَةُ فَكَانَتۡ لِمَسَـٰكِينَ يَعۡمَلُونَ فِى ٱلۡبَحۡرِ
As for the boat, it belonged to paupers working at sea.
20.2 KASABA (کَسَبَ):   For earning, to earn or reap this word is related to AMILA   (عَمِلَ)  . To work in order to get benefit or success. Regardless of whom it is done for and regardless of the nature of profession i.e. it may be good or bad, forbidden or legal. KAASIB (کَاسِبَ) is a laborer or employee. Allah says in the Quran
Surah Al-Maeda (The table spread): سورۃ المَائدہ 5:38
وَٱلسَّارِقُ وَٱلسَّارِقَةُ فَٱقۡطَعُوٓاْ أَيۡدِيَهُمَا جَزَآءَۢ بِمَا كَسَبَا
As for the thief, whether male or female, cut their hands as a penalty for what they have reaped
PAGE 707
20.3 IKTASAB (اِکْتَسَب):   AKATASAB (اَکَتَسَب) is anything done keeping in account ones’ personal benefit or gain. Allah says in the Holy Quran
Surah An-Nisa (The women): سورۃ النِّسا 4:32
لِّلرِّجَالِ نَصِيبٌ۬ مِّمَّا ٱڪۡتَسَبُواْ‌ۖ وَلِلنِّسَآءِ نَصِيبٌ۬ مِّمَّا ٱكۡتَسَبۡنَ‌ۚ
For men is a share of what they have earned, and for women is a share of what they have earned.
20.4 IKTARAFA (اِقْتَرَفَ):   KARAFA (قَرَفَ) means to peel of the crust of the wound.  IKTARFA (اِقْتَرَفَ) means to maledict work. To work or earn using illegal ways. The idiom “اَلْاِعِتَرَافُ یَزِیْلُ الْاِقْتِرَاف” means admitting an offense, vanishes an offense. This IKTARAAF (اِقْتَرَفَ) refers to sin and malign activities. Allah says in the Holy Quran.
Surah Al-Ana’am (The Cattle): سورۃ الانعام 6:120
إِنَّ ٱلَّذِينَ يَكۡسِبُونَ ٱلۡإِثۡمَ سَيُجۡزَوۡنَ بِمَا كَانُواْ يَقۡتَرِفُونَ
those who earn sin will get due recompense for their "earnings."
Summary:
20.1 A’MILA: Common word for an act or work. Also used for earning.
20.2 KASABA: Do some work for benefit regardless of whom it is done for.
20.3 IKTASABA: To do something for personal gain.
20.4 IKTARFA: To do an illegal work. Earn through illegal works.

title: content/k/k21.html
raw_text:
21 KAMRAH [room, chamber]
Synonyms: HUJRAH, GHURFAH
21.1 HUJRAH(حُجْرَۃ):   Means a room or grave (dictionary al Manjad). (Plural HUJRAAT (حُجْرات)).  Means a place to live. Thus HUJRAH (حُجْرَۃ) refers to that simple room which is used as a house. Allah says in the Holy Quran
Surah Al-Hujraat  (The Inner Apartments): سُوۡرَةُ الحُجرَات 49:4
نَّ ٱلَّذِينَ يُنَادُونَكَ مِن وَرَآءِ ٱلۡحُجُرَٲتِ
Those who call you from behind the chambers
21.1 GHURFAH (غُرْفَة):   Means a room or chamber on the upper floor (dictionary al Manjad). GHURAF (غُرَف) and GHURAFAT (غُرَفَات) are stages and positions in paradise. Thus GHURFAH (غُرْفَة) means a well built and lofty room. Allah says in the Holy Quran.
Surah Al-Furqaan (The criterion): سورۃ الفُرْقان 25:75
أُوْلَـٰٓٮِٕكَ يُجۡزَوۡنَ ٱلۡغُرۡفَةَ بِمَا صَبَرُواْ
Those will be awarded the Chamber for their patience

title: content/k/k22.html
raw_text:
22 KAMZOR [weak]
Synonyms:  ZAEEF, WAAHIYAH, AWHAN, AZILLAH
PAGE 708
22.1 ZAEEF (ضَعِیْف):   (opposite QAWI (قوی)) Means inferior in strength and power. Weak. A famous word. And ZAE’F (ضَعْف) and ZU’UF(ضِعْف) mean weakness. (plural ZUA’FAA’ (ضُعَفَاء) and ZI’AAF (ضِعَاف)). In the Quran
Surah Al-Baqarah (The cow): سورۃ البَقَرَۃ  2:282
كَانَ ٱلَّذِى عَلَيۡهِ ٱلۡحَقُّ سَفِيهًا أَوۡ ضَعِيفًا
But if the debtor is mentally deficient, or weak,
22.2 WAAHIYAH (وَاھِیَة):    WAHIA (وَاھِی) means weakness due to old age for instance a worn out cloth. WAHIA (وَاھِیَ) mean loosening of something for instance these connections have gone loose. This word is used mostly for clothes and ropes. ALWAHI (اَلْوَاھْی) means a puncture in leather. Thus it means frailness, wearing out, weakness or dilapidation of something due to old age. Allah says in the Holy Quran
Surah Al-Haqqah (The reality): سورۃ الحَاقَّۃ 69:16
وَٱنشَقَّتِ ٱلسَّمَآءُ فَهِىَ يَوۡمَٮِٕذٍ۬ وَاهِيَةٌ۬
And the heaven will crack; so on that Day it will be frail.
22.3 AWHAN (اَوْھَن):   WAHANA (وَھَنَ) means weak, if used material things then it refers to weakening of a bone or strong object. And if used semantically then it refers to weakness in action or moral weakness. WAHANA (وَھَنَ) means to falter, to become lethargic and weak due to lack of strength, fragile. Allah says in the Quran
Surah Al-Ankaboot  (The Spider): سُوۡرَةُ العَنکبوت 29:41
ا‌ۖ وَإِنَّ أَوۡهَنَ ٱلۡبُيُوتِ لَبَيۡتُ ٱلۡعَنڪَبُوتِ‌ۖ
But the most fragile of houses is the spider’s house
In another place in Quran
Surah An-Nisa (The women): سورۃ النِّسا 4:104
وَلَا تَهِنُواْ فِى ٱبۡتِغَآءِ ٱلۡقَوۡمِ‌ۖ
And do not falter in the pursuit of the enemy
22.4 AZILLAH (اَذِلَّة):   (singular ZALEEL (َذلیل), opposite AZEEZ(عزیز)) Means inferior. Inferior in honor or respect. A low grade citizen. Allah says in the Quran
Surah Ale- Imran (The family of Imran): سورۃ آل عِمْرن 3:123
وَلَقَدۡ نَصَرَكُمُ ٱللَّهُ بِبَدۡرٍ۬ وَأَنتُمۡ أَذِلَّةٌ۬‌ۖ
God had given you victory at Badr, when you were weak
Summary:
22.1 ZAEEF: Lesser in strength or power
22.2 WAAHIYAH: Weak due to wearing out
22.3 WAHAN: Weak or lethargic due to lack of strength
22.3 AZILLAH: Inferior people
KAMZOR KARNA [to weaken]:
ISTADAFA (اِسْتَضْعَفَ) for making and keeping weak and AWHANA (اَوْھَن) for making weak and slow. In the Quran
Surah Al-Anfal (The Spoils of War): سُوۡرَةُ الاٴنفَال 8:18
ذَٲلِكُمۡ وَأَنَّ ٱللَّهَ مُوهِنُ كَيۡدِ ٱلۡكَـٰفِرِينَ
Such is the case. God will weaken the strategy of the disbelievers.

title: content/k/k23.html
raw_text:
PAGE 709
23 KINARA [brim, edge, coast]
Synonyms: TARF, HADD, HARF, UFQ, AQTAAR, ARJAA’, SHAFA, MA’ZAL, SHATEE’, SAHIL, AQSA, UDWAH, SADAF
23.1 TARF (طَرْف):    Means end limit, brim, corners of a cubical object, sharp edges, sight or direction (dictionary al Manjad). (Plural ATRAAF (اَطْرَاف)) Allah says in the Holy Quran
Surah Hud (Hud): سورۃ ھود 11:114
وَأَقِمِ ٱلصَّلَوٰةَ طَرَفَىِ ٱلنَّہَارِ
Perform the prayer at the borders of the day,
23.2 HADD (حَدّ):   HADDA-ASAKEEN (حَدَّٓالسکین) means to sharpen a knife. HADD-US-SAIF (حَدُّالسَّیْف) means edge of a sword. HADD (حَدّ) means the limit between two things. HADD-UL-MAKAN (حَدُّالمَکَان) means the marking the boundaries of a house. HADDUD ARBA’ (حدود اربعہ) is also from this word which means the four boundaries. Therefore HADD (حَدّ) are the boundaries and limits of something that separates it from other. And HUDDUD ALLAH (حُدُوْدُ الله) means restrictive ordinance of Allah which is a sin to be transgressed. Allah says in the Holy Quran
Surah Al-Baqarah (The cow): سورۃ البَقَرَۃ  2:229
وَمَن يَتَعَدَّ حُدُودَ ٱللَّهِ فَأُوْلَـٰٓٮِٕكَ هُمُ ٱلظَّـٰلِمُونَ
Those who transgress God’s limits are the unjust.
23.3 HARF (حَرْف):   HARF-UL-JABAL (حَرْفُ الجَبَل) means a sharp end of a mountain. A loftiest mountain. It is said FULANUN-ALA’-HARFIM-MIN-AMRIHI “فُلَانٌ عَلٰی حَرْفٍ مِّنْ امرہ” means the person is as the brink of the matter. Meaning if anything is done against his will he will break away (dictionary al Manjad). Limit of agitation. Allah says in the Quran.
Surah Al-Hajj  (The Pilgrimage): سُوۡرَةُ الحَجّ 22:11
وَمِنَ ٱلنَّاسِ مَن يَعۡبُدُ ٱللَّهَ عَلَىٰ حَرۡفٍ۬‌ۖ فَإِنۡ أَصَابَهُ ۥ خَيۡرٌ ٱطۡمَأَنَّ بِهِۦ‌ۖ وَإِنۡ أَصَابَتۡهُ فِتۡنَةٌ ٱنقَلَبَ عَلَىٰ وَجۡهِهِۦ
And among the people is he who worships God on edge. When something good comes his way, he is content with it. But when an ordeal strikes him, he makes a turnaround.
23.4 UFQ (اُفْق):   AFAQ (اَفَقَ) Two things that are wide apart and meet together at the edge or seem like they meet, horizon. The place where they meet is called UFAQ (اُفْق) for instance the sky and earth are far apart. At the far end of sight where they seem like meeting each other is called UFAQ (اُفْق). (Plural AFAAQ (اٰفاق)). AFAAQ (اٰفاق) means the expanse of universe which covers a huge area. Allah says in the Holy Quran
Surah An-Najm (the star): سورۃ النَّجم 53:7
وَهُوَ بِٱلۡأُفُقِ ٱلۡأَعۡلَىٰ
While he was at the highest horizon
In another place in the Holy Quran
Surah Fussilat (Explained in Detail): سورۃ فُصّلَت 41:53
سَنُرِيهِمۡ ءَايَـٰتِنَا فِى ٱلۡأَفَاقِ وَفِىٓ أَنفُسِہِمۡ
We will show them Our proofs on the horizons, and in their very souls
Page 710
23.5 AQTAAR (اَقْطَار):   QATARA (قَطَرَ) means to stand in a line or row. QATAR-AL-BAEERU-ILAL-BAEER (قَطَرَ ٓالْبَعِیْرُ اِلٰی الْبَعِیْر) means to line up all the camels in a row. AQTAR-UD-DUNIYA (اقطار الدنیا) means the 4 corners of earth. In Geometry it is the line passing through the middle that divides the earth into two equal parts i.e. the equator (dictionary al Manjad). Thus QATAR (قطر) refers to a straight line and also to a circular object. And there can be multiple such lines in every direction. Allah says in the Quran
Suran Al-Ahzaab (The clans): سورۃ الأحزَاب 33:14
وَلَوۡ دُخِلَتۡ عَلَيۡہِم مِّنۡ أَقۡطَارِهَا ثُمَّ سُٮِٕلُواْ ٱلۡفِتۡنَةَ لَأَتَوۡهَا وَمَا تَلَبَّثُواْ بِہَآ إِلَّا يَسِيرً۬ا
Had it been invaded from its sides, and they were asked to dissent, they would have done so with little hesitation.
In another place in the Holy Quran
Surah Ar-Rahman (The Beneficent): سُوۡرَةُ الرَّحمٰن 55:33
يَـٰمَعۡشَرَ ٱلۡجِنِّ وَٱلۡإِنسِ إِنِ ٱسۡتَطَعۡتُمۡ أَن تَنفُذُواْ مِنۡ أَقۡطَارِ ٱلسَّمَـٰوَٲتِ وَٱلۡأَرۡضِ فَٱنفُذُواْ‌ۚ
O society of jinn and humans! If you can pass through the bounds of the heavens and the earth, go ahead and pass
23.6 ARJAA’ (اَرْجَاء):   (singular RAJA (رَجَا)) Means an end of a circular object. RAJA-AL-BIR’ (رَجَا الْبِئْر) means edge of a well. RAJA-AL-SAMAA’ (رَجَاالسَّمَاء) means edge of the sky. In the Quran
Surah Al-Haqqah (The reality): سورۃ الحَاقَّۃ 69:17
وَٱلۡمَلَكُ عَلَىٰٓ أَرۡجَآٮِٕهَا‌ۚ وَيَحۡمِلُ عَرۡشَ رَبِّكَ فَوۡقَهُمۡ يَوۡمَٮِٕذٍ۬ ثَمَـٰنِيَةٌ۬
And the angels will be ranged around its borders, while eight will be carrying the Throne of your Lord above them that Day.
23.7 SHAFA (شَفَا):   This word is commonly used for near death state. SHAFA (شَفَا) refers to edge or brink of something that is hollow or empty and standing on which causes a fear of falling in and death. Allah says in the Quran
Surah Ale- Imran (The family of Imran): سورۃ آل عِمْرن 3:103
وَكُنتُمۡ عَلَىٰ شَفَا حُفۡرَةٍ۬ مِّنَ ٱلنَّارِ فَأَنقَذَكُم مِّنۡہَا‌ۗ
And you were on the brink of a pit of fire, and He saved you from it.
In another place in Holy Quran Allah says
Surah Al Tawbah (The repentance): سورۃ التوبھ 9:109
أَم مَّنۡ أَسَّسَ بُنۡيَـٰنَهُ ۥ عَلَىٰ شَفَا جُرُفٍ هَارٍ۬
or he who founds his structure on the brink of a cliff that is about to tumble
23.8 MA’ZAL(مَعْزل):   AZAL (مَعْزل) means avoidance or withdrawal, to separate. To turn aside and get saved.  According to Ibn Al Faras “تدُلُّ علی تنخیة وامالة وابعاد” means MA’ZAL is that edge or side turning to which a man is saved from a peril. Allah says in the Holy Quran
Surah Hud (Hud): سورۃ ھود 11:42
وَنَادَىٰ نُوحٌ ٱبۡنَهُ ۥ وَڪَانَ فِى مَعۡزِلٍ۬ يَـٰبُنَىَّ ٱرۡڪَب مَّعَنَا
and Noah called out to his son, who had separated himself (from the rest): "O my son! embark with us,
Page 711
23.9 SHATEE’ (شاطئ):   Means one of the two edges of something. One of the side or coast of a river or a valley. Allah says in the Quran
Surah Al Qasas (The stories): سورۃ القَصَص 28:30
فَلَمَّآ أَتَٮٰهَا نُودِىَ مِن شَـٰطِىِٕ ٱلۡوَادِ ٱلۡأَيۡمَنِ
When he reached it, he was called from the right side of the valley,
23.10 SAHIL (سَاحِل):   This word is used particularly for a coast or shore of a river or sea (dictionary al Manjad). In the Quran
Surah Ta-Ha (Ta-ha): سورۃ طٰھٰ  20:39
فَلۡيُلۡقِهِ ٱلۡيَمُّ بِٱلسَّاحِلِ
The river will wash him to shore,
23.11 AQSA (اَقْصَا):   QSW (قصو) has the perception of being far or living far. And AQSA (اَقْصٰی) means a far end or the other side. Allah says in the Quran
Surah Yaseen (Yaseen): سورۃ ٰیٰس 36:20
وَجَآءَ مِنۡ أَقۡصَا ٱلۡمَدِينَةِ رَجُلٌ۬ يَسۡعَىٰ
Then there came running, from the farthest part of the City
23.12   UDWAH (عُدْوَۃ):   A’DA (عَدَا) means a traveler going far away and also edge of a valley. UDWAH (عُدْوَۃ) means a high place on the edge of a valley (dictionary al Manjad). Thus UDWAH (عُدْوَۃ) refers to that edge of a valley that is not just far but higher in altitude. Allah says in the Quran
Surah Al-Anfal (The Spoils of War): سُوۡرَةُ الاٴنفَال 8:42
إِذۡ أَنتُم بِٱلۡعُدۡوَةِ ٱلدُّنۡيَا وَهُم بِٱلۡعُدۡوَةِ ٱلۡقُصۡوَىٰ
Remember you were on the hither side of the valley, and they on the farther side
23.13 SADAF (صَدَف):   An open field in the middle of mountains is called a valley. And the edge or boundary of that valley is known as SADAF (صَدَف). So SADAF (صَدَف) can be translated as an “edge of a valley” but “edge of mountain” is a better translation. Thus Imam Raghib also refers to it as “edge of mountain”. Allah says in the Quran
Surah Al-Kahf (The Cave): سورۃ الکھف 18:96
حَتَّىٰٓ إِذَا سَاوَىٰ بَيۡنَ ٱلصَّدَفَيۡنِ
At length, when he had filled up the space between the two steep mountain-sides
Summary:
23.1 TARF: Extreme edge or limit of anything
23.2 HADD:  Boundaries and limits of something that separates it from other
23.3 HARF: Sharp edge, Limit of agitation
23.4 UFQ: The edge where two separate things meet.
23.5 AQTAAR: Side or edge of a circular thing.
23.6 ARJAA’: Edge of a circular object i.e. a well or sky
23.7 SHAFA: Edge of something a that hollow, and falling into it can cause death.
23.8 MA’ZAL: A edge of side which serves as a shelter or protection
23.9 SHATEE’: One of the edge of a river or field
23.10 SAHIL: River or sea coast
23.11 AQSA: The other edge or side
12.12 UDWAH: A far away lofty edge or side.
12.13 SADAF: Edge of a mountain.

raw_text:
Page 712
24: KUNWAN [well]
Synonyms: BI’R, JUBB, RASS
24.1 BI’R (بِئر):   Means a well, it’s a common word regardless that it is deserted or inhibited. Also a dried well can be called BI’R (بِئر) too. In the Holy Quran
Surah Al-Hajj  (The Pilgrimage): سُوۡرَةُ الحَجّ 22:45
وَبِئۡرٍ۬ مُّعَطَّلَةٍ۬ وَقَصۡرٍ۬ مَّشِيدٍ
They lie in ruins; with stilled wells, and lofty mansions.
24.2 JUBB (جُبّ):   A well that is only dug up and its walls are not stoned or bricked. A mud well. In the Quran
Surah Yusuf (Joseph): سورۃ یُوسُف 12:15
فَلَمَّا ذَهَبُواْ بِهِۦ وَأَجۡمَعُوٓاْ أَن يَجۡعَلُوهُ فِى غَيَـٰبَتِ ٱلۡجُبِّ‌ۚ
So they went away with him, and agreed to put him at the bottom of the well
24.3 RASS (رَسّ):   A very large well. Which has ample of water in it. In the Quran
Surah Qaf (Qaf): سُوۡرَةُ قٓ 50:12
كَذَّبَتۡ قَبۡلَهُمۡ قَوۡمُ نُوحٍ۬ وَأَصۡحَـٰبُ ٱلرَّسِّ وَثَمُودُ
The people of Noah denied before them, and the companions of the well and Thamud.

25 KAWRA [whip, lash]
Synonyms: SAUWT, JALDAH
25.1 SAUWT (سَوْط):   Means a separated leather, whip or lash, scourge SAATA (سَاطَ) means to whip, and SAWAT (سَوَّاط) means a guard with a whip or lash. MISWAAT (مِسْوَاط) is that horse that doesn’t move without being whipped.
Surah Al-Fajr (The Dawn): سُوۡرَةُ الفَجر 89:13
فَصَبَّ عَلَيۡهِمۡ رَبُّكَ سَوۡطَ عَذَابٍ
So your Lord poured down upon them a scourge of punishment.
25.2 JALDAH (جَلْدَۃ):   JILD (جلد) the skin of a living is called JILD (جِلد). JALADA (جَلَدَ) means to beat someone on skin so that the injury does not go beyond the skin. raw_text:
26 KOSHISH KERNA [to try, to strive, to struggle]
Synonyms: SAA’, JAHADA, KADAHA
26.1 SAA’ (سعٰی):   To pace or walk briskly, to jog. To make efforts for the completion of a good or bad matter to strive. In the Quran
Surah An-Najm (the star): سورۃ النَّجم 53:39
وَأَن لَّيۡسَ لِلۡإِنسَـٰنِ إِلَّا مَا سَعَىٰ
And that the human being attains only what he strives for.
26.2 JAHADA (جَھَدَ):   To put in the best effort to complete a task. Extreme effort. According to ibn al Faris “اَصْلُهُ الْمُشَقَّۃ وَمَا یُقَارِبُهُ”. Allah says in the Quran
Surah Al-Ankaboot  (The Spider): سُوۡرَةُ العَنکبوت 29:69
وَٱلَّذِينَ جَـٰهَدُواْ فِينَا لَنَہۡدِيَنَّہُمۡ سُبُلَنَا‌ۚ
As for those who strive for Us —We will guide them in Our ways
26.3 KADAHA (کَدَحَ):   AL-KADAH (اَلْکَدْح) means a scratch. KADAHA (کَدَحَ) means to work very hard. Or bear pain and peril while doing work. In the Quran
Surah Al-Inshiqaq (The Splitting Open):  سُوۡرَةُ الانشقاق84:6
يَـٰٓأَيُّهَا ٱلۡإِنسَـٰنُ إِنَّكَ كَادِحٌ إِلَىٰ رَبِّكَ كَدۡحً۬ا فَمُلَـٰقِيهِ
O man! You are laboring towards your Lord, and you will meet Him.
Summary:
26.1 SAA’: To make efforts for a work.
26.2 JAHADA: To put in all the efforts for a task
26.3 KADAHA: To work while bearing pain

raw_text:
27 KON [who, which]
Synonyms: MAN, AYYU
27.1 MAN (مَنْ):   For anyone capable of intelligence, this word is used for singular or plural, feminine or masculine everyone. Means ‘who’ For instance “مَنْ رَّبُّكَ” who is your God?   (dictionary al Manjad). Allah says in the Quran
Surah Al-Baqarah (The cow): سورۃ البَقَرَۃ  2:255
مَن ذَا ٱلَّذِى يَشۡفَعُ عِندَهُ ۥۤ إِلَّا بِإِذۡنِهِۦ‌ۚ
Who is he that can intercede with Him except with His permission?
27.2 AYYU (اَیُّ):   When used in questions, this word becomes a pronoun and gives the meaning of ‘who’, it usually is prefixed by something else (which gives a meaning of challenge) like who amongst the following? Or which of you. This word is also used for everyone. Allah says in the Quran
Page 714
Surah Al-Mulk (The Sovereignty ): سُوۡرَةُ المُلک67:2
لِيَبۡلُوَكُمۡ أَيُّكُمۡ أَحۡسَنُ عَمَلاً۬‌ۚ
He who created death and life—to test you—as to which of you is better in conduct.
In another place in the Quran
Surah An-Nisa (The women): سورۃ النِّسا 4:11
لَا تَدۡرُونَ أَيُّهُمۡ أَقۡرَبُ لَكُمۡ نَفۡعً۬ا‌ۚ
you do not know which are closer to you in welfare

title: content/k/k28.html
raw_text:
28 KOI [any, anyone, one]
Synonyms:  AHAD, MAN and MIN
28.1 AHAD (اَحَد):   Means incomparable, extraordinary, one and peerless like قُلۡ هُوَ ٱللَّهُ أَحَدٌ (Say, “He is God, the One.) (112:1) and in numeric system it means one ‘1’. Like AHADA-ASHARA (اَحَدَعَشَرَ), (feminine IHDAA (اِحْدٰی)). And the third use of this word is to represent one element in a group, both in positive and negative means. And used for everything usually. For instance
Surah Yusuf (Joseph): سورۃ یُوسُف 12:78
فَخُذۡ أَحَدَنَا مَڪَانَهُ ۥۤ‌ۖ
so take one of us
And when used in a negative sense it will give the meaning of ‘anyone’. For instance
Surah Al-Haqqah (The reality): سورۃ الحَاقَّۃ 69:47
فَمَا مِنكُم مِّنۡ أَحَدٍ عَنۡهُ حَـٰجِزِينَ
Nor could any of you withhold him (from Our wrath).
28.2 MAN (مَنْ) MIN (مِنْ):   These two words sometime represent unknown units of a group. The only difference in that MAN (مَنْ) is used for any intelligent being and gives the meaning of ‘anyone’ or ‘any person’. Like
Surah Al-Baqarah (The cow): سورۃ البَقَرَۃ  2:8
وَمِنَ ٱلنَّاسِ مَن يَقُولُ ءَامَنَّا بِٱللَّهِ
Among the people are those who say, “We believe in God and in the Last Day,”
And MIN   (مِنْ)   is usually used for creations without intelligence. For example in the Quran
Surah Al-Isra (The Night Journey): سُوۡرَةُ الإسرَاء 17:44
وَإِن مِّن شَىۡءٍ إِلَّا يُسَبِّحُ بِحَمۡدِهِۦ
There is not a thing that does not glorify Him with praise,
Summary:
28.1 AHAD:   Means one of the groups. Usually used for all intelligent beings
28.2 MAN, MIN:   MAN is used for one or many units of a group, usually used for intelligent beings. MIN is used for dumb creations.

29. KEH, GOYA KEH [to, as if]
Synonyms: AN, KANA, KANNA, KA’ANAMA, ALLA
Page 715
29.1 AN (اَنْ):   ANNA MUKAFAFAH (اَنَّ مخففة) when this word comes in sentence it gives a meaning of ‘to’ and ‘as if’. In the Quran
Surah Al-Baqarah (The cow): سورۃ البَقَرَۃ  2:26
إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ لَا يَسۡتَحۡىِۦۤ أَن يَضۡرِبَ مَثَلاً۬
Indeed, Allah is not timid to present an example
29.2 KANA (کَاَنَ), KANNA (کَاَنَّ), KA’ANAMA (کَاَنَّمَا):   These words are composed of simile ‘ك’ and AN (اَنْ), ANNA (اَنَّ). And give the meaning of ‘as if’. Allah says in the Holy Quran
Surah Luqman (Luqman): سُوۡرَةُ لقمَان 31:7
كَأَن لَّمۡ يَسۡمَعۡهَا كَأَنَّ فِىٓ أُذُنَيۡهِ وَقۡرً۬ا‌ۖ
as if he heard them not, as if there was deafness in both his ears:
AN (اَنْ) and KA’N (کَاَنْ), are verbs and ANNA (اَنَّ) and KA’ANNA (کَاَنَّ) are nouns as shown in the ayah above.
Surah Al-Anfal (The Spoils of War): سُوۡرَةُ الاٴنفَال 8:6
كَأَنَّمَا يُسَاقُونَ إِلَى ٱلۡمَوۡتِ
as if they were being driven to death
29.3 ALLA (اَلَّا):   ALLA (اَلَّا) is actually AN (اَنْ) and LA (لَا) and means ‘as if not’ when it comes in a sentence. Allah says in the Quran
Surah Fussilat (Explained in Detail): سورۃ فُصّلَت 41:30
تَتَنَزَّلُ عَلَيۡهِمُ ٱلۡمَلَـٰٓٮِٕڪَةُ أَلَّا تَخَافُواْ وَلَا تَحۡزَنُواْ
the angels will descend upon them: “Do not fear, and do not grieve,

title: content/k/k3.html
raw_text:
3 KAGHAZ [paper]
Synonyms: RAQQ, QIRTAAS
3.1 RAQQ (رَقّ):   RAQQA (رَقَّ) means to be thin and soft. RIQQAT (رَقَّت) means to be soft hearted/ kind hearted (opposite QASAAWAT (قساوت)). RAQQ (رَقّ) is anything that is thin and soft, for instance a leaf, a membrane, or a thin piece of leather or paper scroll. Thus this word has a very ordinary use. Allah says in the Quran
Surah At-Tur (The Mount): سورۃ الطُّور 52:2
وَكِتَـٰبٍ۬ مَّسۡطُورٍ۬ فِى رَقٍّ۬ مَّنشُورٍ۬
And a Book inscribed. In a published scroll.
3.2 QIRTAAS (قِرْطَاس):   Means a handwritten letter   (dictionary Al   Manjad  )  , regardless of how many pages. QIRTAAS ABYAD (قرطاس ابیض) is a famous word which means a complete and published report on some important matter. QIRTAAS (قِرْطَاس) actually refers to that initial form of paper invented by Egyptians, during the time of revelation of Quran this paper was available but was very scarce. Allah says in the Holy Quran
Surah Al-Ana’am (The Cattle): سورۃ الانعام 6:7
وَلَوۡ نَزَّلۡنَا عَلَيۡكَ كِتَـٰبً۬ا فِى قِرۡطَاسٍ۬ فَلَمَسُوهُ بِأَيۡدِيہِمۡ
Had We sent down upon you a book on paper, and they had touched it with their hands,
PAGE 692
Synonyms:
3.1 RAQQ: Any thin or soft thing that can be written on.
3.2 QIRTAAS: Means a written paper or papers, the initial raw form of paper.

title: content/k/k30.html
raw_text:
30 KAHAN [where]
Synonyms: AYNA, AYNAMA, ANNA
30.1 AYNA (اَیْنَ), AYNAMA (اَیْنَمَا):   AYNA (اَیْنَ) is an adverb of place. Used to inquire about a place. For instance
Surat An-Nahl (The Bee): سورۃ النّحل16:27
أَيۡنَ شُرَڪَآءِىَ ٱلَّذِينَ
“Where are My associates
MA (مَا) after AYNA (اَیْنَ) gives the meaning of ‘where ever’. Thus the sentence becomes a challenge and requires recompense. For instance
Surah An-Nisa (The women): سورۃ النِّسا 4:78
أَيۡنَمَا تَكُونُواْ يُدۡرِككُّمُ ٱلۡمَوۡتُ
Wherever you may be, death will catch up with you
And
Surah Al-Baqarah (The cow): سورۃ البَقَرَۃ  2:115
فَأَيۡنَمَا تُوَلُّواْ فَثَمَّ وَجۡهُ ٱللَّهِ‌ۚ
So wherever you [might] turn, there is the Face of Allah
THUMMA (ثُمَّ) is actually reply to AYNA (اَیْنَ) - AYNA (اَیْنَ) means ‘where’ and THUMMA (ثُمَّ) mean ‘there’ or ‘that place’.
30.2 ANNA (اَنّٰی):   Used to inquire about place and circumstances or conditions. In the Quran
Surah Ale- Imran (The family of Imran): سورۃ آل عِمْرن 3:37
قَالَ يَـٰمَرۡيَمُ أَنَّىٰ لَكِ هَـٰذَا‌ۖ
He said, “O Mary, where did you get this from?”
And when representing an adverb then it gives the meaning of ‘where’. For instance in the Quran

قَـٰتَلَهُمُ ٱللَّهُ‌ۚ أَنَّىٰ يُؤۡفَڪُونَ
May God assail them! How (Where) deceived they are!
Summary:
30.1 AYNA: To inquire about a place
30.1 ANNA: To inquire about place as well as circumstances and condition

raw_text:
Page 716
31. KAHANIAN – WAQIYAT [stories, accounts]
Synonyms: ASATEER, AHADEES, QASAS
31.1 ASATEER (اَسَاطِیْر):   ASTURAH (اَسْطُورَہ), ASAYTARAH (اَسَیْطَرَۃ), and ISTAAR (اِسْطَار) all are singular of ASATEER (اَسَاطِیْر). And ISTAAR (اِسْطَار) is also derived from SATR (سَطَر) meaning anything written in a straight line or has been written down but actually represents nothing, unreal and baseless speech, myth (dictionary al Manjad). Stories or accounts that are based on fiction.
Surah Al-Ana’am (The cattle): سورۃ الانعام 6:25
يَقُولُ ٱلَّذِينَ كَفَرُوٓاْ إِنۡ هَـٰذَآ إِلَّآ أَسَـٰطِيرُ ٱلۡأَوَّلِينَ
those who disbelieve will say, “These are nothing but myths of the ancients.”
31.2 AHADEES (اَحَادِیْث):   (singular HADEES (حَدِیْث)) any address that comes in to being and did not existed before. This word is applied to those events that people have forgotten due to passage of time. Informative or exemplary stories. Allah says in the Quran
Surah Al-Mumenoon (The believers): سُوۡرَةُ المؤمنون 23:44
كُلَّ مَا جَآءَ أُمَّةً۬ رَّسُولُهَا كَذَّبُوهُ‌ۚ فَأَتۡبَعۡنَا بَعۡضَہُم بَعۡضً۬ا وَجَعَلۡنَـٰهُمۡ أَحَادِيثَ‌ۚ
every time there came to a people their messenger, they accused him of falsehood: so We made them follow each other (in punishment): We made them as a tale (that is told):
31.3 QASAS (قَصَص):   (singular QISSAH (قِصَّه)) QASSA (قَصَّ) means to walk on footsteps. QASSA (قَصَّ) also means to narrate an event. And QASAS (قَصَص) are those events that are passed through generation and people through recount and narration. A Narrated event. Allah says in the Quran
Surah Yusuf (Joseph): سورۃ یُوسُف 12:3
نَحۡنُ نَقُصُّ عَلَيۡكَ أَحۡسَنَ ٱلۡقَصَصِ
We do relate unto you the most beautiful of stories,
Summary:
31.1 ASATEER: Baseless account.
31.2 AHADEES: Forgotten but Exemplary accounts.
31.3 QASAS: Narrated stories.

32 KHAAL [skin, hide]
Synonyms: JILD, SHAWAA
32.1 JILD (جِلْد):   Skin or hide of an animal, upper layer of body that is skin or hide. A very common word. Allah says in the Quran
Surah An-Nisa (The women): سورۃ النِّسا 4:56
كُلَّمَا نَضِجَتۡ جُلُودُهُم بَدَّلۡنَـٰهُمۡ جُلُودًا غَيۡرَهَا
Every time their skins are cooked, We will replace them with other skins,
Page 717
32.2 SHAWAA(شَوٰی):   Corners or sides of body, hands, feet and those parts of body which when injured are not life threatening. The idiom “رَمَاہُ فَاَشْوَاہُ” means the arrow struck him on a side or didn’t strike on an organ that would fatally injure the person. Allah says in the Quran
Surah Al-Maarij (The Ascending Stairs): سُوۡرَةُ المعَارج 70:15
كَلَّآ‌ۖ إِنَّہَا لَظَىٰ نَزَّاعَةً۬ لِّلشَّوَىٰ
By no means! It is a Raging Fire. It strips away the scalps.

title: content/k/k33.html
raw_text:
33 KHAAL UTARNA [to strip, skinning, to peel]
Synonyms: SALAKHA, KASHATA
33.1 SALAKHA (سَلَخَ):   SALAKH-AL-HAYYATUH (سَلَخَ الْحَیَّةُ) means a snake shredding its skin. SALAKH-UL-HAYYAH  (سَلَخَ الحیَّة) means ecdysis of snake. SALAKH-UL-MIRAH (سَلَخَ الْمِرَاۃ) means a woman removing her shirt. SALAKH-UL-KHAROOF (سَلَخَ الْخَرُوْف) means to skin a goat kid   (dictionary al Manjad). Thus SALAKHA   (سَلَخَ)   means a raw skin, raw hide, or temporary remove or strip a membrane. Allah says in the Quran
Surah Yaseen (Yaseen): سورۃ ٰیٰس 36:37
وَءَايَةٌ۬ لَّهُمُ ٱلَّيۡلُ نَسۡلَخُ مِنۡهُ ٱلنَّہَارَ
Another sign for them is the night: We strip the day out of it
33.2 KASHATA (کَشَطَ):   KASHATA AL BAEER (کَشَطَ البعیر) means to skin a camel. KISHAT (کِشَاط) means a loose or removed skin.  KASH-SHAT (کَشَّاط) means slaughterer   (dictionary al Manjad)  .  Allah says in the Holy Quran
Surah At-Takwir (The Overthrowing): سُوۡرَةُ التّکویر 81:11
وَإِذَا ٱلسَّمَآءُ كُشِطَتۡ
When the sky is peeled away.
Summary:
33.1 SALAKHA: To remove skin or membrane temporarily.
33.2 KASHATA: To remove a firm skin or membrane.

title: content/k/k34.html
raw_text:
34 KHANA [eat]
Synonyms:  AKALA, TA’AMA, RATTAA’
34.1 AKALA (اَکَلَ):   A very common word and is used for any type of eatable, food, fruits, sweets, bread etc. Used for both human and other non human beings. The idiom “اَکَلَتِ النَّارُ الْحَطَبَ” means the fire ate the wood. In the Quran
Surah Al-Maeda (The table spread): سورۃ المَائدہ 5:3
وَمَآ أَكَلَ ٱلسَّبُعُ إِلَّا مَا ذَكَّيۡتُمۡ
that which have been (partly) eaten by a wild animal; unless you are able to slaughter it (in due form);
34.2 TA’AMA (طَعَمَ):   Has a very limited use then AKALA (اَکَلَ), means to eat food, to eat bread, and anything that is eaten as nutrition. This word is applied to humans mostly. TA’AMMI (طَعَامِّی) means a person who sells bread. MAT’AM (مطْعَم) means a hotel. Allah says in the Quran
Page 718
Suran Al-Ahzaab (The clans): سورۃ الأحزَاب 33:53
فَإِذَا طَعِمۡتُمۡ فَٱنتَشِرُواْ وَلَا مُسۡتَـٔۡنِسِينَ لِحَدِيثٍۚ
And when you have eaten, disperse, without lingering for conversation.
34.3 RATTAA’ (رَتَعَ):   Usually means grazing and eating of animals. When used for humans metaphorically it refers to a person eat to his fill. Or eating too much like animals. In the Quran
Surah Yusuf (Joseph): سورۃ یُوسُف 12:12
أَرۡسِلۡهُ مَعَنَا غَدً۬ا يَرۡتَعۡ وَيَلۡعَبۡ
Send him with us tomorrow that he may eat well and play.
Summary:
34.1 AKALA: Anything eating anything, used for a wide range of meanings.
34.2 TA’AMA: Humans eating food.
34.3 RATTAA’: Eating to fill. Animals grazing and eating.

raw_text:
36 KHAJOOR [date (fruit)]
Synonyms:  NAKHILAH, NAKHAL, NAKHEEL, LEENAH, RUTAB
36.1 NAKHILAH (نَخْلَة):   Means a date palm. Allah says in the Quran
Surah Maryam (Mary): سُوۡرَةُ مَریَم 19:25
وَهُزِّىٓ إِلَيۡكِ بِجِذۡعِ ٱلنَّخۡلَةِ
And shake the trunk of the palm-tree towards you
NAKHAL (نَخْل) is the plural of NAKILAH (نَخْلَة), date palms and its fruit. Dates or date plum. Allah says in the Quran
Surah Al-Kahf (The Cave): سورۃ الکھف 18:32
جَعَلۡنَا لِأَحَدِهِمَا جَنَّتَيۡنِ مِنۡ أَعۡنَـٰبٍ۬ وَحَفَفۡنَـٰهُمَا بِنَخۡلٍ۬
To one of them We gave two gardens of vine, and We surrounded them with palms-trees,
NAKHEEL (نَخِیْل) is that orchard or plantation which contains a large number of date palms. Allah says on the Quran
Surah Al-Baqarah (The cow): سورۃ البَقَرَۃ  2:266
أَيَوَدُّ أَحَدُڪُمۡ أَن تَكُونَ لَهُ ۥ جَنَّةٌ۬ مِّن نَّخِيلٍ۬ وَأَعۡنَابٍ۬
Would anyone of you like to have a garden of palms and vines,
Page 719
36.2 LEENAH (لِیْنَة):   All types of date palms and its fruits except AJWAH (عجوہ) (A very exquisite type of date). Allah says in the Quran
Surah Al Hashr (The exile): سورۃ الحَشر 59:5
مَا قَطَعۡتُم مِّن لِّينَةٍ أَوۡ تَرَڪۡتُمُوهَا قَآٮِٕمَةً عَلَىٰٓ أُصُولِهَا فَبِإِذۡنِ ٱللَّهِ
Whether you cut down a tree, or leave it standing on its trunk, it is by God’s will.
36.3 RUTAB (رُطَب):   A fresh date. Allah says in the Quran
Surah Maryam (Mary): سُوۡرَةُ مَریَم 19:25
تُسَـٰقِطۡ عَلَيۡكِ رُطَبً۬ا جَنِيًّ۬ا
and it will drop ripe dates by you.”

جَعَلۡنَا لِأَحَدِهِمَا جَنَّتَيۡنِ مِنۡ أَعۡنَـٰبٍ۬ وَحَفَفۡنَـٰهُمَا بِنَخۡلٍ۬

To one of them We gave two gardens of vine, and We surrounded them with palms-trees,

 NAKHEEL (نَخِیْل) is that orchard or plantation which contains a large number of date palms. Allah says on the Quran

Surah Al-Baqarah (The cow): سورۃ البَقَرَۃ  2:266

 أَيَوَدُّ أَحَدُڪُمۡ أَن تَكُونَ لَهُ ۥ جَنَّةٌ۬ مِّن نَّخِيلٍ۬ وَأَعۡنَابٍ۬

Would anyone of you like to have a garden of palms and vines,

Page 719

36.2 LEENAH (لِیْنَة): All types of date palms and its fruits except AJWAH (عجوہ) (A very exquisite type of date). Allah says in the Quran

Surah Al Hashr (The exile): سورۃ الحَشر 59:5

مَا قَطَعۡتُم مِّن لِّينَةٍ أَوۡ تَرَڪۡتُمُوهَا قَآٮِٕمَةً عَلَىٰٓ أُصُولِهَا فَبِإِذۡنِ ٱللَّهِ

Whether you cut down a tree, or leave it standing on its trunk, it is by God’s will.

36.3 RUTAB (رُطَب): A fresh date. Allah says in the Quran

Surah Maryam (Mary): سُوۡرَةُ مَریَم 19:25

تُسَـٰقِطۡ عَلَيۡكِ رُطَبً۬ا جَنِيًّ۬ا

and it will drop ripe dates by you.”

title: content/k/k37.html
raw_text:
37 KHARA KERNA – HONA [to stand up]
Synonyms: QAAMA, AQAAMA, WAQAFA, NATAQA, NASHAZA
37.1QAAMA (قَامَ):   Means stood up (Opposite JALASA (جَلَسَ) and QA’ADA (قَعَدَ)). A very famous word. Allah says in the Quran.
Surah An-Nisa (The women): سورۃ النِّسا 4:142
وَإِذَا قَامُوٓاْ إِلَى ٱلصَّلَوٰةِ قَامُواْ كُسَالَىٰ
And when they stand for prayer, they stand lazily,
And AQAMA   (اَقَامَ)   Means to make someone stand, to raise someone or something, to make stand upright. To arrange a thing vertically. Allah says in the Quran
Surah Al-Kahf (The Cave): سورۃ الکھف 18:77
فَوَجَدَا فِيہَا جِدَارً۬ا يُرِيدُ أَن يَنقَضَّ فَأَقَامَهُ
They found there a wall on the point of falling down, but he set it up straight.
37.2 WAQAFA (وَقَفَ):   Means to stop while walking or doing something. To stand without moving. To halt or halt someone.  Used as both transitive and intransitive verb. Allah says in the Quran
(As intransitive verb)
Surah Al-Ana’am (The Cattle): سورۃ الانعام 6:30
وَلَوۡ تَرَىٰٓ إِذۡ وُقِفُواْ عَلَىٰ رَبِّہِمۡ‌ۚ
If you could but see when they will be made to stand before their Lord.
(As transitive verb)
Surah As-Saaffat (The Aligners) : سُوۡرَةُ الصَّافات37:24
وَقِفُوهُمۡ‌ۖ إِنَّہُم مَّسۡـُٔولُونَ
And stop them. They are to be questioned.”
37.3 NATAQA (نَتَقَ):   To move or raise or spread something   (dictionary al Manjad). Also to stretch something and make it lose. Or to move or shake something so forcefully that it leans to a side without breaking from its roots. Allah says in the Quran
Surah Al-Araf (The heights): سورۃ الأعرَاف 7:171
وَإِذۡ نَتَقۡنَا ٱلۡجَبَلَ فَوۡقَهُمۡ كَأَنَّهُ ۥ ظُلَّةٌ۬ وَظَنُّوٓاْ أَنَّهُ ۥ وَاقِعُۢ بِہِمۡ
And when We suspended the mountain over them, as if it was an umbrella, and they thought it would fall on them
37.4 NASHAZA (نَشَزَ):   To get on feet, to stand up. NASHAZ-AR-RUJAL (نشز الرجل) means the man who was sitting got up on his feet. NASHAZ-AN-MAKANA (نشز عن مکانہ) means he got up and started to move. Allah says in the Quran
Page 720
Surah Al-Mujadila (The Pleading Women) سُوۡرَةُ المجَادلة 58:11
وَإِذَا قِيلَ ٱنشُزُواْ فَٱنشُزُواْ
And when you are told to rise up, rise up
Summary:
37.1 QAAMA: (Opposite JALASA and QA’ADA) a popular word for standing up., AQAAMA to make something upright,
37.2 WAQAFA: To stand up without moving. To stop for a moment while walking, to halt
37.3 NATAQA: To cause something to bend.
37.4 NASHAZA: To get up on feet and move. Stand up

raw_text:
38 KAWLNA [to boil]
Synonyms: ANAA, GHALAA
38.1 ANAA (اَنٰی), YANEE (یَانْیِ):   Means boiling of water etc. after reaching an extreme temperature. Boiling of a liquid thing due to extreme temperature. In the Quran
Surah Al-Ghashiya (The overwhelming): سُوۡرَةُ الغَاشِیَة 88:5
تُسۡقَىٰ مِنۡ عَيۡنٍ ءَانِيَةٍ۬
The while they are given, to drink, of a boiling hot spring,
38.2 GHALAA (غَلٰی):   Boiling and rising of water due to extreme temperature. To boil. GHAL-AL-QADAR (غلی القدر) means boiling pot. Rising of items in a pot. Allah says in the Quran
Surah Ad-Dukhan (The Smoke): سُوۡرَةُ الدّخان44:45
يَغۡلِى فِى ٱلۡبُطُونِ كَغَلۡىِ ٱلۡحَمِيمِ
boiling inside the bellies. Like the boiling of seething water.

title: content/k/k39.html
raw_text:
39 KHOLNA [to open, to spread]
Synonyms: BASATA, FATAHA, HALLA, SHARAHA, KASHAFA, NASHATA, FARAJA
39.1 BASATA (بَسَطَ):   To open or spread something (opposite QABAZA (قبض), QADAR (قدر)). To spread or extend something. To unfold. Allah says in the Quran
Surah Al-Rad (The Thunder): سُوۡرَةُ الرّعد13:26
ٱللَّهُ يَبۡسُطُ ٱلرِّزۡقَ لِمَن يَشَآءُ وَيَقۡدِرُ‌ۚ
Allah extends provision for whom He wills and restricts [it].
39.2 FATAHA (فَتَحَ):   To remove the complexity of a complicated matter (Opposite AGHLAAQ (اغلاق)). To open a tied up luggage. Allah says in the Quran
Surah Yusuf (Joseph): سورۃ یُوسُف 12:65
وَلَمَّا فَتَحُواْ مَتَـٰعَهُمۡ وَجَدُواْ بِضَـٰعَتَهُمۡ رُدَّتۡ إِلَيۡہِمۡ‌ۖ
And when they opened their baggage, they found that their goods were returned to them.
39.3 HALLA (حَلَّ):   HAL-AL-AQDAH (حلّ العقدہ) means to open a knot. To detangle. To solve a problem  (dictionary al Manjad). ARBAAB-HAL-O-AQAD (اربابِ حلّ وعقد) (administrative authority) is a famous word.
Page 721--
In the Quran:
Surat Ţāhā (Ta-Ha) - سورة طه 20:27
يَفْقَهُوا قَوْلِي وَاحْلُلْ عُقْدَةً مِّن لِّسَانِي
And untie the knot from my tongue. That they may understand my speech.
39.4 SHARAHA(شَرَحَ):   Means to open the meanings of difficult speech/conversations  and according to Ibn-un-Faris, there are basically two things in SHARAH(شرح).
1. To open victory
2. Statement (Wazahat) or explanation and SHARAH SADAR(شرح صدر) means to expand the chest. Means to understand a difficult or complicated matter. In the Quran:
Surat Ţāhā (Ta-Ha) - سورة طه 20:25
وَيَسِّرْ لِي أَمْرِي رَبِّ اشْرَحْ لِي صَدْرِي
My Lord, expand for me my breast [with assurance]. And ease for me my task.
39.5 KASHAFA(كَشَفَ):   To expand and move off. To unveil. To remove one thing from another and revealing and expressing the first one. In the Quran:
Surat An-Naml (The Ant) - سورة النمل 27:44
فَلَمَّا رَأَتْهُ حَسِبَتْهُ لُجَّةً وَكَشَفَتْ عَن سَاقَيْهَا ۚ
But when she(Princess SABA) saw it, she thought it was a body of water and uncovered her shins [to wade through].
39.6 NASHATA (  نَشَطَ  ):   This word belongs to the Lughat Azdad لغت اضداد. Which means that it has opposing meanings  .   NASHAT-AL-HABLA(نَشَطَ الحَبلَ) means tied a knot. And NASHAT-AL-UQDAT(نَشَطَ العُقدَة) means tightening/tightened the knot. And ALNASHOOT(النشوط) means a knot which can be easily opened/undone. And NASHATA(  نَشَطَ  )   means to undo/open a knot. In that context, this word is in particular to HALLA(حَلَّ). Which means that HALL-AL-UQDAT(حل العقدة) and NASHATA(  نَشَطَ  ), both have the same meanings. Means opening a knot. To loosen a close linkage or constraint. To loosen a knot etc. In the Quran:
Surat An-Nāzi`āt (Those who drag forth) - سورة النازعات 79:2
ۚ وَالنَّاشِطَاتِ نَشْطًا وَالنَّازِعَاتِ غَرْقًا
By those [angels] who extract with violence. And [by] those who remove with ease.
39.7 FARAJA(فَرَجَ):    A concept of openness is found in FARJ (فَرْج). FARAJA(فَرَجَ) means to open, to widen, expand etc. (Refer to SHAGAAF for further details). In the Quran:
Surat Al-Mursalāt (The Emissaries) - سورة المرسلات 77:9
وَإِذَا السَّمَاءُ فُرِجَتْ
And when the heaven is opened.
Summary:
1. BAST: To open and spread.
2. FATAH: To open a complicated matter or a closed stuff/equipment.
3. HALLA: (ALUQDAT) To open/undo a knot.
4. SHARAHA: To open the meanings of a difficult talk/speech.
5. KASHAFA: To remove one thing and then unveil another.
6. NASHATA: To loosen a knot, constraint or linkage.
7. FARAJA: To open and expand. To widen.

title: content/k/k4.html
raw_text:
4. KAAFI HONA [ample, enough]
Synonyms: KAFAA, HASB
4.1 KAFAA (کفٰی):   Ample, to be satisfied with something and to be indifferent about others. The subjective form of KAFAA (کفٰی) is usually followed by the word BA, for instance KAFA BILLAHI SHAHEEDA (کفٰی بِاللہِ شھیدا) that the testimony of Allah in ample and complete and all the other testimonies bear no importance before it   (dictionary Al   Manjad  )  . KAFAYAH (کفایۃ) is anything that is sufficient and makes every other thing unattractive. MUKAFAAT (مکافات) means to return a favor with equal or greater favor   (dictionary Al   Manjad  )  . KAFAA (کفٰی) actually means to requite evenly for something. And also to repay a little greater. Allah says in the Quran
Suran Al-Ahzaab (The clans): سورۃ الأحزَاب 33:25
وَكَفَى ٱللَّهُ ٱلۡمُؤۡمِنِينَ ٱلۡقِتَالَ‌ۚ وَكَانَ ٱللَّهُ قَوِيًّا عَزِيزً۬ا
enough is Allah for the believers in their fight. And Allah is full of Strength, able to enforce His Will.
4.2 HASB (حَسْب):   HASABA (حَسَبَ) mean to do estimation, to count, to keep an account of it. HASB is an agent noun thus while keeping one thing in account and estimating for it. There is no specific word for it so is translated as simply ‘(ample/enough)’. HASB (حَسْب) is also prolific to KAFAA (کفٰی). Allah says in the Quran
Surah Ale- Imran (The family of Imran): سورۃ آل عِمْرن 3:173
حَسۡبُنَا ٱللَّهُ وَنِعۡمَ ٱلۡوَڪِيلُ
“God is enough for us; He is the Excellent Protector.”
Summary:
Both these words are quite similar to one another and can be used interchangeably for example  وَكَفَىٰ بِجَهَنَّمَ (enough is Hell) 4:55 and  فَحَسۡبُهُ ۥ جَهَنَّمُ‌ۚ  (Hell is enough) 2:206 . The only difference is that KAFAA gives a collective approach and HASB is used when looking into every aspect individually like وَكَفَىٰ بِٱللَّهِ حَسِيبً۬ا (God suffices as a Reckoner.)4:6.

 وَكَفَى ٱللَّهُ ٱلۡمُؤۡمِنِينَ ٱلۡقِتَالَ‌ۚ وَكَانَ ٱللَّهُ قَوِيًّا عَزِيزً۬ا

enough is Allah for the believers in their fight. And Allah is full of Strength, able to enforce His Will.

4.2 HASB (حَسْب): HASABA (حَسَبَ) mean to do estimation, to count, to keep an account of it. HASB is an agent noun thus while keeping one thing in account and estimating for it. There is no specific word for it so is translated as simply ‘(ample/enough)’. HASB (حَسْب) is also prolific to KAFAA (کفٰی). Allah says in the Quran

Surah Ale- Imran (The family of Imran): سورۃ آل عِمْرن 3:173

 حَسۡبُنَا ٱللَّهُ وَنِعۡمَ ٱلۡوَڪِيلُ

“God is enough for us; He is the Excellent Protector.”

Summary:

 

Both these words are quite similar to one another and can be used interchangeably for example  وَكَفَىٰ بِجَهَنَّمَ (enough is Hell) 4:55 and  فَحَسۡبُهُ ۥ جَهَنَّمُ‌ۚ  (Hell is enough) 2:206 . The only difference is that KAFAA gives a collective approach and HASB is used when looking into every aspect individually like وَكَفَىٰ بِٱللَّهِ حَسِيبً۬ا (God suffices as a Reckoner.)4:6.

40. KHETI BAARI KARNA (To cultivate/To Farm)
Synonyms: HARASA, ZARA’A
Page 722--
40.1 HARASA(حَرَثَ):    Means to plow the land and sow seeds in it and to prepare it for cultivation. And MEHRAS (مِحرَث) (plural MAHARIS محارث) means the tools for plowing land/plowing tools etc. But sometimes the cultivation/harvest is also referred as HARS(حَرْث). In the Quran:
Surat Al-Qalam (The Pen) - سورة القلم 68:22
أَنِ اغْدُوا عَلَىٰ حَرْثِكُمْ إِن كُنتُمْ صَارِمِينَ
Go early to your crop if you would cut the fruit.
40.2 ZARA’A(زَرَعَ):    Its real meaning is INBAAT (اِنبَات) (germination) or to grow. And to sow seeds and irrigate it (land) with water, and to take care of it appropriately. It’s growth is virtually linked to a human being because he is the one who fulfills the duty for taking care of it otherwise, the fact is that it is Allah’s job to grow the farm. In the Quran:
Surat Al-Wāqi`ah (The Inevitable) - سورة الواقعة 56: 63-64
أَأَنتُمْ تَزْرَعُونَهُ أَمْ نَحْنُ الزَّارِعُونَ أَفَرَأَيْتُم مَّا تَحْرُثُونَ
And have you seen that [seed] which you sow? Is it you who makes it grow, or are We the grower?
Summary:
1. HARASA means to plow a land and sow seeds.
2. ZARA’A to sow seed and irrigate it afterwards and to take appropriate care of it.

title: content/k/k41.html
raw_text:
41. KHENCHNA (To pull / To stretch)
Synonyms: MADDA, JARRA, IZTARRA, SALAKHA, NAZA’A, SAFA’A.
41.1 MADDA(مَدَّ):   Means to make something tall/long by stretching it and to spread it. In a way that the connection/linkage remains established. MUDDAT(مدّت) means the stretches of time. In the Quran:
Surat Al-'A`rāf (The Heights) - سورة الأعراف 7:202
وَإِخْوَانُهُمْ يَمُدُّونَهُمْ فِي الْغَيِّ ثُمَّ لَا يُقْصِرُونَ
But their brothers - the devils increase them in error; then they do not stop short.
And MADDADA(مَدَّدَ) is used as more emphasis. In the Quran:
Surat Al-Humazah (The Traducer) - سورة الهمزة 104:9
فِي عَمَدٍ مُّمَدَّدَةٍ
In extended columns.
41.2 JARRA(جَرَّ):   Means to pull/stretch and drag. To drag on the floor. And JAISHUN-JARRARUN(جَيشٌ جَرَّارٌ) refers to a big army spread in a vast area and advances forward like as if it’s stretching in numbers. In the Quran:
Surat Al-'A`rāf (The Heights) - سورة الأعراف 7:150
وَأَخَذَ بِرَأْسِ أَخِيهِ يَجُرُّهُ إِلَيْهِ ۚ
And he (Musa A.S) seized his brother by [the hair of] his head, pulling him toward him.
41.3 IZTARRA(اِضطَرَّ):   To forcibly pull someone to work. To make someone work by turning him helpless and powerless. In the Quran:
Surat Al-Baqarah (The Cow) - سورة البقرة 2:126
وَمَن كَفَرَ فَأُمَتِّعُهُ قَلِيلًا ثُمَّ أَضْطَرُّهُ إِلَىٰ عَذَابِ النَّارِ ۖ
And whoever disbelieves - I will grant him enjoyment for a little; then I will force him to the punishment of the Fire, and wretched is the destination.
Page 723--
41.4 SALAKHA(سَلَخَ):   To remove the skin of a living being by pulling it. Casting-off of a snake’s exuviae. And according to Ibn-ul-Faris, it means to remove something from the skin. And SALAKHATISHAHR(سَلَخَتِ الشَّهْر) means the passing of the last day of a month. In the Quran:
Surat Yā-Sīn (Ya Sin) - سورة يس 36:37
وَآيَةٌ لَّهُمُ اللَّيْلُ نَسْلَخُ مِنْهُ النَّهَارَ فَإِذَا هُم مُّظْلِمُونَ
And a sign for them is the night. We remove from it [the light of] day, so they are [left] in darkness.
41.5 NAZA’A(نَزَعَ):   Means to draw out/extort something from its place/habitat. Like drawing out a soul from a body, to draw out something by pulling it. In the Quran:
Surat Al-'A`rāf (The Heights) - سورة الأعراف 7:43
وَنَزَعْنَا مَا فِي صُدُورِهِم مِّنْ غِلٍّ
And We will have removed whatever is within their breasts of resentment
41.6 SAFA’A(سَفَعَ):   Means to hold and pull the forelock of a horse. In the Quran:
Surat Al-`Alaq (The Clot) - سورة العلق 96:15
لَئِن لَّمْ يَنتَهِ لَنَسْفَعًا بِالنَّاصِيَةِ
If he does not desist, We will surely drag him by the forelock.
Summary:
1. MADDA: Means to stretch and spread. To elongate such that the substance remains intact/linked.
2. JARRA: To pull or drag someone on the ground.
3. IZTARRA: To pull someone to work, forcibly and violently.
4. SALAKHA: To pull skin from the body.
5. NAZA’A: To extort something from its place or habitat.
6. SAFA’A: To pull by the forelocks.

raw_text:
42. KHELNA (To play)
Synonyms: LA’AB, LAHAA(LAHW), ABASA.
42.1 LA’ABA(لَعَبَ):   Means to play. To do something for sake of enjoyment. To do something which has no benefit in it. And LU’BA(لُعبَة) means game/activity, turns in a game or with which the game is played. LA’IB(لاعب) and LA’IBA(لَعِبَ) means a player. And MULA’IB means a partner/player in a game. In the Quran:
Surat Az-Zukhruf (The Ornaments of Gold) - سورة الزخرف  43:83
فَذَرْهُمْ يَخُوضُوا وَيَلْعَبُوا حَتَّىٰ يُلَاقُوا يَوْمَهُمُ الَّذِي يُوعَدُونَ
So leave them to converse vainly and amuse themselves until they meet their Day which they are promised.
42.2 LAHAA(لَهى):   Means a show/performance or any other activity which is done for fun and entertainment. And it is most common to LA’ABA(لَعَبَ). LAHW(لَهْو) also includes playing. And to witness a game or to jest, all are included. Meaning all those activities which keep us diverted from purposeful ones and are the cause of amusement are LAHW(لَهْو). And ALHA(ا لَهى   )   refers to the unawareness from the objects of true purpose caused by these sources of entertainment. In the Quran:
Surat Al-'An`ām (The Cattle) - سورة الأنعام 6:32
وَمَا الْحَيَاةُ الدُّنْيَا إِلَّا لَعِبٌ وَلَهْوٌ ۖ
And the worldly life is not but amusement and diversion.
Page 724--
42.3 ABASA(عَبَثَ)     :    This is more important than LAHW(لَهْو). Meaning to do a purposeful work, but carrying it out as if it’s frolic. And to turn this work unintended and resultless through this incorporation. And ABASA(عَبَثَ) means both i.e To play as well as mixing one thing into another. ABASA-SHAI’A-BISHAI(عَبَثَ الشَّئ بِالشَّئ) means to mix/introduce one thing into another. And ABAS(عَبَث) means to joke or play around. In the Quran:
Surat Al-Mu'minūn (The Believers) - سورة المؤمنون
أَفَحَسِبْتُمْ أَنَّمَا خَلَقْنَاكُمْ عَبَثًا
Then did you think that We created you uselessly.
Summary:
1. LA’IBA: Means to play.
2. LAHA: Is most common to LA’AB. All those activities which cause inattention from the real purpose.
3. ABASA: To do something unintended or to make a purposeful work useless by incorporating it with fun.
