raw_text:
17 NASEEHAT, NASEEHAT KERNA, HASIL KERNA
[Advice, to advise, to take advice]
Synonyms: NASAHA(  نصح  ), ZAKKAR(  ضد  ), WA’Z(  وعظ  ), WASSA(  وصى  ), I’BRAH(  عبرة  ), I’TABAR(  اعتبر  )
17.1 nasaha(  نصح  )  : to think good about someone. Naseeha(  نصيحة  ) is all those sayings and acts which includes well wishing for others. Allah states that:
________________
Surat Hud  -   سُوۡرَةُ هُود
11:34
وَلَا يَنفَعُكُمۡ نُصۡحِىٓ إِنۡ أَرَدتُّ أَنۡ أَنصَحَ لَكُمۡ إِن كَانَ ٱللَّهُ يُرِيدُ أَن يُغۡوِيَكُمۡ‌ۚ
My counsel will not profit you if I were minded to advise you, if Allah's will is to keep you astray. He is your Lord and unto Him ye will be brought back.
________________
17.2 zakkara (  ذكر  )  : zakara(  ذكر  ) meaning to remember and miss someone (ant: nasiya(  نسي  )) and zikr(  ذكر  ) means to bring something in heart or on tongue. Tazkara(  تذكره  ) means all those things through which you remember some of your needs, certificate, passport, tickets etc. The Holy Quran is also called zikr(  ذكر  ) and tazkara(  تذكره  ) because it also reminds one of the natural preaching and holding of witness for goodness in humans. Zikr(  ذكر  ) also means all those advices which make you remember Allah and whatever reminds you of Allah, is zikr(  ذكر  ). Zakkara(  ذكر  ) means to advise and bring to attention. Zakkar-al-qaum(  ذكرالقوم  ) means that he gave advice to his nation. Allah states that:
________________
Surat Adh-Dhariyat (The Scatterers)  -   سُوۡرَةُ الذّاریَات
51:55
وَذَكِّرۡ فَإِنَّ ٱلذِّكۡرَىٰ تَنفَعُ ٱلۡمُؤۡمِنِينَ
And warn, for warning profiteth believers.
________________
And the word tazakkar(  تذكر  ) is used to accept or take advice as is stated:
________________
Surat Al-Baqarah (The Cow)  -   سُوۡرَةُ البَقَرَة
2:221
وَيُبَيِّنُ ءَايَـٰتِهِۦ لِلنَّاسِ لَعَلَّهُمۡ يَتَذَكَّرُونَ
Wed not idolatresses till they believe; for lo! a believing bondwoman is better than an idolatress though she please you; and give not your daughters in marriage to idolaters till they believe, for lo! a believing slave is better than an idolater though he please you. These invite unto the Fire, and Allah inviteth unto the Garden, and unto forgiveness by His grace, and expoundeth His revelations to mankind that haply they may remember.
________________
17.3 wa’za(  وعظ  )  : meaning to say such good things which touch the heart, to incline someone towards piousness through intimidation and persuasion, to dress down or scold which includes the aspect of fear, to entice someone towards good deeds through fear. Allah states that:
________________
Surat Yunus  -   سُوۡرَةُ یُونس
10:57
يَـٰٓأَيُّہَا ٱلنَّاسُ قَدۡ جَآءَتۡكُم مَّوۡعِظَةٌ۬ مِّن رَّبِّڪُمۡ وَشِفَآءٌ۬ لِّمَا فِى ٱلصُّدُورِ
O mankind! There hath come unto you an exhortation from your Lord, a balm for that which is in the breasts, a guidance and a mercy for believers.
________________
17.4 wassa(  وصى  )  : alwasiyyah(  الوصية  ) means to direct someone through advice before an event has occurred. It is stated in the Quran:
________________
Surat An-Nisa (Women) -   سُوۡرَةُ النِّسَاء
4:12
مِنۢ بَعۡدِ وَصِيَّةٍ۬ يُوصِينَ بِهَآ أَوۡ دَيۡنٍ۬‌ۚ
And unto you belongeth a half of that which your wives leave, if they have no child; but if they have a child then unto you the fourth of that which they leave, after any legacy they may have bequeathed, or debt (they may have contracted, hath been paid). And unto them belongeth the fourth of that which ye leave if ye have no child, but if ye have a child then the eighth of that which ye leave, after any legacy ye may have bequeathed, or debt (ye may have contracted, hath been paid). And if a man or a woman have a distant heir (having left neither parent nor child), and he (or she) have a brother or a sister (only on the mother's side) then to each of them twain (the brother and the sister) the sixth, and if they be more than two, then they shall be sharers in the third, after any legacy that may have been bequeathed or debt (contracted) not injuring (the heirs by willing away more than a third of the heritage) hath been paid. A commandment from Allah. Allah is Knower, Indulgent.
________________
And when it is associated towards Allah then it means to instruct and order as is stated:
________________
Surat An-Nisa (Women) -   سُوۡرَةُ النِّسَاء
4:11
يُوصِيكُمُ ٱللَّهُ فِىٓ أَوۡلَـٰدِڪُمۡ‌ۖ
Allah chargeth you concerning (the provision for) your children: to the male the equivalent of the portion of two females, and if there be women more than two, then theirs is two-thirds of the inheritance, and if there be one (only) then the half. And to of his parents a sixth of the inheritance, if he have a son; and if he have no son and his parents are his heirs, then to his mother appertaineth the third; and if he have brethren, then to his mother appertaineth the sixth, after any legacy he may have bequeathed, or debt (hath been paid). Your parents or your children: Ye know not which of them is nearer unto you in usefulness. It is an injunction from Allah. Lo! Allah is Knower, Wise.
________________
17.5 I’bra and I’tabar(  عبرة, اعتبر  )  : a’boor(  عبور  ) is basically used to depict how the water is crossed whether it is through swimming or boat, animal or through a bridge. And a’br-un-nahr(  عبرالنهر  ) is that place where you go inside the water and cross it. Similarly, a’br-ul-ain(  عبرالعين  ) means the flowing of tears through the eyes and a’bra(  عبر  ) meaning tears and a’bara(  عبر  ) means to be sad, to cry. A’br-al-ain(  عبرالعين  ) means filling of eyes with tears. A’brata(  عبرة  ) means to receive advice on some matter through consideration and pondering. It is said
لك بفلان عبرة   Which means to consider the situation of the person to find out about the actual cause of the event. Allah states that:
________________
Surat Al-Noor (The Light) -   سُوۡرَةُ النُّور
24:44
يُقَلِّبُ ٱللَّهُ ٱلَّيۡلَ وَٱلنَّهَارَ‌ۚ إِنَّ فِى ذَٲلِكَ لَعِبۡرَةً۬ لِّأُوْلِى ٱلۡأَبۡصَـٰرِ
Allah causeth the revolution of the day and the night. Lo! herein is indeed a lesson for those who see.
________________
And I’tabar(  اعتبر  ) means to ponder over a sad and grieving event and take advice from it. Allah states that:
________________
Surat Al-Hashr (Exile) -   سُوۡرَةُ الحَشر
59: 2
وَقَذَفَ فِى قُلُوبِہِمُ ٱلرُّعۡبَ‌ۚ يُخۡرِبُونَ بُيُوتَہُم بِأَيۡدِيہِمۡ وَأَيۡدِى ٱلۡمُؤۡمِنِينَ فَٱعۡتَبِرُواْ يَـٰٓأُوْلِى ٱلۡأَبۡصَـٰرِ
He it is Who hath caused those of the People of the Scripture who disbelieved to go forth from their homes unto the first exile. Ye deemed not that they would go forth, while they deemed that their strongholds would protect them from Allah. But Allah reached them from a place whereof they recked not, and cast terror in their hearts so that they ruined their houses with their own hands and the hands of the believers. So learn a lesson, O ye who have eyes!
________________
Summary:
1. NASAHA(  نصح  ): to talk or act as well wishing for someone.
2. ZAKKARA(  ذكر  ): that advice which reminds you of God
3.  WA’ZA(  وعظ  ): to advise through intimidation and persuasion.
4. WASSA(  وصى  ): to instruct someone and give advice before an event has taken place.
5. I’TABAR(  اعتبر  ): to think about the causes of a distressing event and take advice from it .

raw_text:
18 NI’MAT
[Blessing]
Synonyms: NI’MAH(  نعمة  ), NA’MAH (  نعمة  ), AALAA(  ألاء  )(   ألي  )
18.1 ni’mah(  نعمة  )  : meaning graciousness, bestowal, kindliness, favor; such a favor which you bestow on someone (pl: ni’am(  نعم  ) and ana’m(  أنعم  )). Ni’mah(  نعمة  ) is unisex and it is used for all kinds of blessings whether small or big, less or more. Allah states that:
________________
Surat Al-E-Imran (Family of Imran) -   سُوۡرَةُ آل عِمرَان
3:171
يَسۡتَبۡشِرُونَ بِنِعۡمَةٍ۬ مِّنَ ٱللَّهِ وَفَضۡلٍ۬
They rejoice because of favour from Allah and kindness, and that Allah wasteth not the wage of the believers.
________________
18.2 na’mah (  نعمة  )  : meaning all those things which are a basis for rectification and betterment in economy. Goods of luxury and its accessories. Allah states that:
________________
Surat Ad-Dukhan (The Smoke) -   سُوۡرَةُ الدّخان
44:27
وَنَعۡمَةٍ۬ كَانُواْ فِيہَا فَـٰكِهِينَ
And pleasant things wherein they took delight!
________________
18.3 aalaa(  ألاء  )  : (plural of ila(  ألي  )) meaning blessing. Ra’la yaaloo(  رالى يالو  ) meaning to lessen, to leave margin, to make mistake as is stated:
________________
Surat Al-E-Imran (Family of Imran) -   سُوۡرَةُ آل عِمرَان
3:118
لَا يَأۡلُونَكُمۡ خَبَالاً۬
O ye who believe! Take not for intimates others than your own folk, who would spare no pains to ruin you; they love to hamper you. Hatred is revealed by (the utterance of) their mouths, but that which their breasts hide is greater. We have made plain for you the revelations if ye will understand.
________________
And ala(  ألاء  ) means all those blessings which cater for the needs of people and come continuously and he does not feel the lack of something to spend his life and usually it is used in the plural sense because there is not just one such blessing. Hence aalaai(  ألاءي  ) is used. Allah states that:
________________
Surat Ar-Rahman (The Merciful) -   سُوۡرَةُ الرَّحمٰن
55:10-13
فَبِأَىِّ ءَالَآءِ رَبِّكُمَا تُكَذِّبَانِ وَٱلۡحَبُّ ذُو ٱلۡعَصۡفِ وَٱلرَّيۡحَانُ فِيہَا فَـٰكِهَةٌ۬ وَٱلنَّخۡلُ ذَاتُ ٱلۡأَكۡمَامِ وَٱلۡأَرۡضَ وَضَعَهَا لِلۡأَنَامِ
And the earth hath He appointed for (His) creatures, Wherein are fruit and sheathed palm-trees, Husked grain and scented herb. Which is it, of the favours of your Lord, that ye deny?
________________
Summary:
1. NAI’MAH(  نعمة  ): bestowal, favor that is done on someone.
2.NA’MAH(  نعمة  ): goods and accessories of luxury
3. AALA(  ألاء  ): basic needs of life.

And the earth hath He appointed for (His) creatures, Wherein are fruit and sheathed palm-trees, Husked grain and scented herb. Which is it, of the favours of your Lord, that ye deny?

________________

Summary:

1. NAI’MAH(نعمة): bestowal, favor that is done on someone.

2.NA’MAH(نعمة): goods and accessories of luxury

3. AALA(ألاء): basic needs of life.

raw_text:
19 NI’MAT ATA KERNA
[To provide blessing]
Synonyms: ANA’MA(  أنعم  ), NA’AM(  نعم  ), KHAWWALA(  خول  ), ATRAFA(  اترف  )  , AGHNA(  اغنى  ), AQNA(  أقنى  )
19.1 ana’ma(  أنعم  )  : meaning to bestow, to reward. This word is not used for an unknown person. This will never come:   أنعم على فرسه   and will never be used for one’s own self. Allah states that:
________________
Surat Al- Fatiha (The Opening) -   سُوۡرَةُ الفَاتِحَة
1:6-7
صِرَٲطَ ٱلَّذِينَ أَنۡعَمۡتَ عَلَيۡهِمۡ ٱهۡدِنَا ٱلصِّرَٲطَ ٱلۡمُسۡتَقِيمَ
Show us the straight path, The path of those whom Thou hast favoured. Not (the path) of those who earn Thine anger nor of those who go astray.
________________
and na’mma(  نعم  ) means to bless someone with a blessing. As is stated:
________________
Surat Al-Fajr(The Dawn) -   سُوۡرَةُ الفَجر
89:15
فَأَمَّا ٱلۡإِنسَـٰنُ إِذَا مَا ٱبۡتَلَٮٰهُ رَبُّهُ ۥ فَأَكۡرَمَهُ ۥ وَنَعَّمَهُ ۥ
As for man, whenever his Lord trieth him by honouring him, and is gracious unto him, he saith: My Lord honoureth me.
________________
19.2 khawwala (  خول  )  : meaning to bestow, to confer, to grant. Allah states that:
________________
Surat Al-Anaam (Cattle) -   سُوۡرَةُ الاٴنعَام
6:94
وَتَرَكۡتُم مَّا خَوَّلۡنَـٰكُمۡ وَرَآءَ ظُهُورِڪُمۡ‌ۖ
Now have ye come unto Us solitary as We did create you at the first, and ye have left behind you all that We bestowed upon you, and We behold not with you those your intercessors, of whom ye claimed that they possessed a share in you. Now is the bond between you severed, and that which ye presumed hath failed you.
________________
19.3 atrafa (  اترف  )  : attaraffu(  الترفة  ) means abundance of luxury, abundance of blessings which can falter a human being. Mutrif(  مترف  ) means those affluent people who have gone astray because of abundance of wealth.
________________
Surat Hud  -   سُوۡرَةُ هُود
11:116
وَٱتَّبَعَ ٱلَّذِينَ ظَلَمُواْ مَآ أُتۡرِفُواْ فِيهِ وَكَانُواْ مُجۡرِمِينَ
If only there had been among the generations before you men possessing a remnant (of good sense) to warn (their people) from corruption in the earth, as did a few of those whom We saved from them! The wrong-doers followed that by which they were made sapless, and were guilty.
________________
19.4 aghna (  اغنى  )  : meaning blessing someone by Allah with so much wealth and riches that he does not need anything from anyone. It is a common word.
________________
19.5 aqna (  أقنى  )  : means to make generous and to make happy I,e, to give so much wealth that apart from fulfilling his needs, he also become happy .It also means to give generously, then increase the wealth even more, to bestow a treasure and according to some, aqna(  أقنى  ) is the antonym of aghna(  اغنى  ) meaning to make poor, aqna(  أقنى  ) is the opposite. Allah states that:
________________
Surat An-Najm (The Star) -   سُوۡرَةُ النّجْم
53:48
وَأَنَّهُ ۥ هُوَ أَغۡنَىٰ وَأَقۡنَىٰ
And that He it is Who enricheth and contenteth;
________________
Summary:
1.ANA’M(  أنعم  ): to grant and give favor, it is common.
2. KHAWWALA(  خول  ): to confer or grant (only used for people)
3. ITRAFA(  اترف  ): to become astray because of affluence.
4. AGHNA(  اغنى  ): giving so much wealth that the person doesn’t need anything else.
5. AQNA(  أقنى  ): to give generously and satisfy, to give treasure and according to some, to make poor.

2 NA-PAAK [Profane]
Synonyms: RIJS, KHABEETH, NAJAS
2.1 RIJS (رِجْس):   Refers to filth or grime (see GANDAGI [filth]) and also to profanity. And it refers to filth or those things that are rendered unlawful or impure by Shariah regardless of bacterial nature or by meaning. Allah says in the Quran
Surah Al Tawbah (The repentance): سورۃ التوبھ 9:95
فَأَعْرِضُوا عَنْهُمْ ۖ إِنَّهُمْ رِجْسٌ ۖ وَمَأْوَاهُمْ جَهَنَّمُ
So turn away from them. Surely, they are Rijsun [i.e. Najasun (impure) because of their evil deeds], and Hell is their dwelling place,
2.2 KHABEETH (خبیث):   Means impure or filthy (Opposite TAYYAB (طیّب)). This word is used both materially and figuratively. Materially it refers to a waste and value less thing. KHABEES-AL-HADEED (خبیث الحدید) means the iron rust, or grime of iron. This word also refers to rotting, smelly and filthy things. Allah says in the Quran
Surah Al-Baqarah (The cow): سورۃ البَقَرَۃ  2:267
وَلَا تَيَمَّمُوا الْخَبِيثَ مِنْهُ تُنفِقُونَ وَلَسْتُم بِآخِذِيهِ إِلَّا أَن تُغْمِضُوا فِيهِ
and do not even aim at getting anything which is bad, in order that out of it ye may give away something, when ye yourselves would not receive it except with closed eyes
When used figuratively, it refers to a person indulged in obscenity or has a mischievous nature. Allah says in the Quran
Surah Al-Noor (The light): سورۃ النور 24:26
الْخَبِيثَاتُ لِلْخَبِيثِينَ وَالْخَبِيثُونَ لِلْخَبِيثَاتِ
Women impure are for men impure, and men impure for women impure
2.3 NAJAS (نَجَسٌ):   This word is also used for exoteric and esoteric sort of filthiness. DAAUN-NAJISUN-WA-NAAJISUN (دَاءٌ نَجَسٌ وَّ نَاجِسٌ) means an incurable disease. NAJJASAS-SABI (نَجَّسَ الصَّبِی) means in order to save a child from evil put a charm around his neck. NUJUS (نُجُس) are those who make these charms and spells of protection (dictionary al Manjad). This word is never used in material meaning in Quran (Opposite TAHIR (طاھر), TUHOOR (طھور)). When used figuratively then it refers to the filth of polytheism and infidelity that turns into an incurable disease. Allah says in the Quran
Surah Al Tawbah (The repentance): سورۃ التوبھ 9:28
يَا أَيُّهَا الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا إِنَّمَا الْمُشْرِكُونَ نَجَسٌ فَلَا يَقْرَبُوا الْمَسْجِدَ الْحَرَامَ بَعْدَ عَامِهِمْ هَٰذَا
O you who believe (in Allah's Oneness and in His Messenger (Muhammad SAW)! Verily, the Mushrikun (polytheists, pagans, idolaters, disbelievers in the Oneness of Allah, and in the Message of Muhammad SAW) are Najasun (impure). So let them not come near Al-Masjid-al-Haram (at Makkah) after this year,
Page 836
Summary:
2.1 RIJS: Things rendered impure by Sharia Laws.
2.2 KHABEETH: Waste and filthy things. People who are indulged in obscenity.
2.3 NAJAS: People who are indulged in the ideas of infidelity and polytheism to the level of being incurable. Things that are completely rendered filthy by Shariah.

raw_text:
20 NUKSAN, NUKSAN HONA
[Damage, loss]
Synonyms: DARRA(  ضر  ), DAIR(  ضير  ), KHASARA(  خسارا  ), KASAAD(  كساد  ), BAKHS(  بخس  ), BAWAAR(  بوار  ), MAGHRAM(  مغرم  )
20.1 darra(  ضر  )  : meaning difficulty, loss (ant: nafa(  نفع  )). It is a common word. Allah states that:
________________
Surat Al-Araf (The Heights) -   سُوۡرَةُ الاٴعرَاف
7:188
قُل لَّآ أَمۡلِكُ لِنَفۡسِى نَفۡعً۬ا وَلَا ضَرًّا إِلَّا مَا شَآءَ ٱللَّهُ‌ۚ
Say: For myself I have no power to benefit, nor power to hurt, save that which Allah willeth. Had I knowledge of the Unseen, I should have abundance of wealth, and adversity would not touch me. I am but a warner, and a bearer of good tidings unto folk who believe.
________________
And dair(  ضير  ) also means damage, disadvantage, loss. According to Imam Raghib, daarah(  ضاره  ) and darra(  ضره  ) have the same meaning. It is stated in the Quran:
________________
Surat Al-Shuara (The Poets) -   سُوۡرَةُ الشُّعَرَاء
26:50
قَالُواْ لَا ضَيۡرَ‌ۖ إِنَّآ إِلَىٰ رَبِّنَا مُنقَلِبُونَ
They said: It is no hurt, for lo! unto our Lord we shall return.
________________
20.2 khasara (  خسارا  )  : meaning the decrease in the selling of goods, to have loss in something instead of profit, failure. Allah states that:
________________
Surat Fatir (The Angels)  -   سُوۡرَةُ فَاطِر
35: 39
وَلَا يَزِيدُ ٱلۡكَـٰفِرِينَ كُفۡرُهُمۡ إِلَّا خَسَارً۬ا
He it is Who hath made you regents in the earth; so he who disbelieveth, his disbelief be on his own head. Their disbelief increaseth for the disbelievers, in their Lord's sight, naught save abhorrence. Their disbelief increaseth for the disbelievers naught save loss.
________________
20.3 kasaad(  كساد  )  : meaning not wanting to buy anything, to bear loss, trade merchandise not being sold.
كساد بازارى   is famous which means bearish behavior in the market. It is stated in the Quran:
________________
Surat Al-Tawba (Repentence) -   سُوۡرَةُ التّوبَة
9:24
وَتِجَـٰرَةٌ۬ تَخۡشَوۡنَ كَسَادَهَا
Say: If your fathers, and your sons, and your brethren, and your wives, and your tribe, and the wealth ye have acquired, and merchandise for which ye fear that there will be no sale, and dwellings ye desire are dearer to you than Allah and His messenger and striving in His way: then wait till Allah bringeth His command to pass. Allah guideth not wrongdoing folk.
________________
20.4 bakhs(  بخس  )  : meaning worthless and useless thing. Yabkhas(  يبخس  ) means to decrease something through cruelty. Allah states that:
________________
Surat Al-Jinn (The Jinn) -   سُوۡرَةُ الجنّ
72:13
فَمَن يُؤۡمِنۢ بِرَبِّهِۦ فَلَا يَخَافُ بَخۡسً۬ا وَلَا رَهَقً۬ا
And when we heard the guidance, we believed therein, and whoso believeth in his Lord, he feareth neither loss nor oppression.
________________
20.5 bawaar(  بوار  )  : boor(  بور  ) and bawaar(  بوار  ) meaning extreme devaluation of something and reaching near the limit of death, to keep bearing loss gradually finally resulting in the end of trade merchandise and destruction. Allah states that:
________________
Surat Fatir (The Angels) -   سُوۡرَةُ فَاطِر
35:29
وَأَنفَقُواْ مِمَّا رَزَقۡنَـٰهُمۡ سِرًّ۬ا وَعَلَانِيَةً۬ يَرۡجُونَ تِجَـٰرَةً۬ لَّن تَبُورَ
Lo! those who read the Scripture of Allah, and establish worship, and spend of that which We have bestowed on them secretly and openly, they look forward to imperishable gain
________________
20.6 maghram(  مغرم  )  : alghurm(  الغرم  ): that type of financial loss which a person has to bear without anyone’s breach of trust or fraud, ransom, and gharim (  غرم  ) means to pay off one’s loan.  Ghareem(  غريم  ) means the one who gives loan as well as the one who takes loan. Allah states that:
________________
Surat Al-Tawba (Repentance) -   سُوۡرَةُ التّوبَة
9:60
وَفِى ٱلرِّقَابِ وَٱلۡغَـٰرِمِينَ وَفِى سَبِيلِ ٱللَّهِ وَٱبۡنِ ٱلسَّبِيلِ‌ۖ
The alms are only for the poor and the needy, and those who collect them, and those whose hearts are to be reconciled, and to free the captives and the debtors, and for the cause of Allah, and (for) the wayfarer; a duty imposed by Allah. Allah is Knower, Wise.
________________
And maghram(  مغرم  ) and ghurm(  غرم  ) both have the same meaning. Mughram(  مغرم  ) is that person who has to pay ransom. Allah states that:
________________
Surat Hud -   سُوۡرَةُ هُود
56:65-66
إِنَّا لَمُغۡرَمُونَ لَوۡ نَشَآءُ لَجَعَلۡنَـٰهُ حُطَـٰمً۬ا فَظَلۡتُمۡ تَفَكَّهُونَ
If We willed, We verily could make it chaff, then would ye cease not to exclaim: Lo! we are laden with debt!
________________
Summary:
1. DARRA(  ضر  ): loss, it is common.
2. KHASARA(  خسارا  ): loss in trade, decrease in goods of merchandise.
3. KASAAD(  كساد  ): decrease or end in demand of sales goods.
4. BAKHS(  بخس  ): to get worthless or useless thing instead of good quality thing.
5. BAWAAR(  بوار  ): to get ruined after continuous losses.
6. MAGHRAM(  مغرم  ): ransom, the amount which one has to pay without any reason.

Say: For myself I have no power to benefit, nor power to hurt, save that which Allah willeth. Had I knowledge of the Unseen, I should have abundance of wealth, and adversity would not touch me. I am but a warner, and a bearer of good tidings unto folk who believe.

________________

And dair(ضير) also means damage, disadvantage, loss. According to Imam Raghib, daarah(ضاره) and darra(ضره) have the same meaning. It is stated in the Quran:

________________

Surat Al-Shuara (The Poets) - سُوۡرَةُ الشُّعَرَاء

26:50

قَالُواْ لَا ضَيۡرَ‌ۖ إِنَّآ إِلَىٰ رَبِّنَا مُنقَلِبُونَ

They said: It is no hurt, for lo! unto our Lord we shall return.

________________

20.2 khasara (خسارا): meaning the decrease in the selling of goods, to have loss in something instead of profit, failure. Allah states that:

________________

Surat Fatir (The Angels)  - سُوۡرَةُ فَاطِر

35: 39

وَلَا يَزِيدُ ٱلۡكَـٰفِرِينَ كُفۡرُهُمۡ إِلَّا خَسَارً۬ا

He it is Who hath made you regents in the earth; so he who disbelieveth, his disbelief be on his own head. Their disbelief increaseth for the disbelievers, in their Lord's sight, naught save abhorrence. Their disbelief increaseth for the disbelievers naught save loss.

________________

20.3 kasaad(كساد): meaning not wanting to buy anything, to bear loss, trade merchandise not being sold.

كساد بازارى is famous which means bearish behavior in the market. It is stated in the Quran:

________________

Surat Al-Tawba (Repentence) - سُوۡرَةُ التّوبَة

9:24

وَتِجَـٰرَةٌ۬ تَخۡشَوۡنَ كَسَادَهَا

Say: If your fathers, and your sons, and your brethren, and your wives, and your tribe, and the wealth ye have acquired, and merchandise for which ye fear that there will be no sale, and dwellings ye desire are dearer to you than Allah and His messenger and striving in His way: then wait till Allah bringeth His command to pass. Allah guideth not wrongdoing folk.

________________

20.4 bakhs(بخس): meaning worthless and useless thing. Yabkhas(يبخس) means to decrease something through cruelty. Allah states that:  

________________

Surat Al-Jinn (The Jinn) - سُوۡرَةُ الجنّ

72:13

فَمَن يُؤۡمِنۢ بِرَبِّهِۦ فَلَا يَخَافُ بَخۡسً۬ا وَلَا رَهَقً۬ا

And when we heard the guidance, we believed therein, and whoso believeth in his Lord, he feareth neither loss nor oppression.

________________

20.5 bawaar(بوار): boor(بور) and bawaar(بوار) meaning extreme devaluation of something and reaching near the limit of death, to keep bearing loss gradually finally resulting in the end of trade merchandise and destruction. Allah states that:

________________

Surat Fatir (The Angels) - سُوۡرَةُ فَاطِر

35:29

وَأَنفَقُواْ مِمَّا رَزَقۡنَـٰهُمۡ سِرًّ۬ا وَعَلَانِيَةً۬ يَرۡجُونَ تِجَـٰرَةً۬ لَّن تَبُورَ

Lo! those who read the Scripture of Allah, and establish worship, and spend of that which We have bestowed on them secretly and openly, they look forward to imperishable gain

________________

20.6 maghram(مغرم): alghurm(الغرم): that type of financial loss which a person has to bear without anyone’s breach of trust or fraud, ransom, and gharim (غرم) means to pay off one’s loan.  Ghareem(غريم) means the one who gives loan as well as the one who takes loan. Allah states that:  

________________

Surat Al-Tawba (Repentance) - سُوۡرَةُ التّوبَة

9:60

وَفِى ٱلرِّقَابِ وَٱلۡغَـٰرِمِينَ وَفِى سَبِيلِ ٱللَّهِ وَٱبۡنِ ٱلسَّبِيلِ‌ۖ

The alms are only for the poor and the needy, and those who collect them, and those whose hearts are to be reconciled, and to free the captives and the debtors, and for the cause of Allah, and (for) the wayfarer; a duty imposed by Allah. Allah is Knower, Wise.

________________

And maghram(مغرم) and ghurm(غرم) both have the same meaning. Mughram(مغرم) is that person who has to pay ransom. Allah states that:

________________

Surat Hud - سُوۡرَةُ هُود

56:65-66

إِنَّا لَمُغۡرَمُونَ لَوۡ نَشَآءُ لَجَعَلۡنَـٰهُ حُطَـٰمً۬ا فَظَلۡتُمۡ تَفَكَّهُونَ

If We willed, We verily could make it chaff, then would ye cease not to exclaim: Lo! we are laden with debt!

________________

Summary:

1. DARRA(ضر): loss, it is common.

2. KHASARA(خسارا): loss in trade, decrease in goods of merchandise.

3. KASAAD(كساد): decrease or end in demand of sales goods.

4. BAKHS(بخس): to get worthless or useless thing instead of good quality thing.

5. BAWAAR(بوار): to get ruined after continuous losses.  

6. MAGHRAM(مغرم): ransom, the amount which one has to pay without any reason.

21 NIKAH KERNA, KARANA
[To get married, to marry someone]
Synonyms: NAKAHA(  نكح  ), ANKAHA(  أنكح  ), ZAWWAJ(  زوج  )
21.1 nakaha(  نكح  )  : alnikah(  النكاح  ) is that pact which is made between spouses and it is associated only with the living creations i.e. human beings and jinns. And nakaha(  نكح  ) means to make the pact of your own marriage. Allah states that:
________________
Surat An-Nisa (Women) -   سُوۡرَةُ النِّسَاء
4: 3
فَٱنكِحُواْ مَا طَابَ لَكُم مِّنَ ٱلنِّسَآءِ
And if ye fear that ye will not deal fairly by the orphans, marry of the women, who seem good to you, two or three or four; and if ye fear that ye cannot do justice (to so many) then one (only) or (the captives) that your right hands possess. Thus it is more likely that ye will not do injustice.
________________
and ankaha(  أنكح  ) means to make the pact of someone else’s marriage. Or to give someone else in marriage. Allah states that:
________________
Surat Al-Baqarah (The Cow) -   سُوۡرَةُ البَقَرَة
2:221
وَلَا تَنكِحُواْ ٱلۡمُشۡرِكَـٰتِ حَتَّىٰ يُؤۡمِنَّ‌ۚ
Wed not idolatresses till they believe; for lo! a believing bondwoman is better than an idolatress though she please you; and give not your daughters in marriage to idolaters till they believe, for lo! a believing slave is better than an idolater though he please you. These invite unto the Fire, and Allah inviteth unto the Garden, and unto forgiveness by His grace, and expoundeth His revelations to mankind that haply they may remember.
________________
21.2 zawwaj (  زوج  )  : zauj(  زوج  ) meaning coupl, husaband, wife, companion. And zawwaj(  زوج  ) means to create a couple. Whenever there are males and females in animals, they are called zauj(  زوج  ) of each other. Apart from animals, in other things, even things are called zauj(  زوج  ). The second aspect of this is that after the pact of marriage, the husband wife don’t live together, then also zawwaj(  زوج  ) will not be used. Hence, the correct meaning of zawwaj(  زوج  ) will be marriage pact and living together as well as to wed and create couple. And its meaning will not be to marry oneself but to give someone else in marriage. Allah states that:
________________
Surat Al-Ahzab (The Clans)  -   سُوۡرَةُ الاٴحزَاب
33:37
فَلَمَّا قَضَىٰ زَيۡدٌ۬ مِّنۡہَا وَطَرً۬ا زَوَّجۡنَـٰكَهَا لِكَىۡ لَا يَكُونَ عَلَى ٱلۡمُؤۡمِنِينَ حَرَجٌ۬ فِىٓ أَزۡوَٲجِ أَدۡعِيَآٮِٕهِمۡ
And when thou saidst unto him on whom Allah hath conferred favour and thou hast conferred favour: Keep thy wife to thyself, and fear Allah. And thou didst hide in thy mind that which Allah was to bring to light, and thou didst fear mankind whereas Allah hath a better right that thou shouldst fear Him. So when Zeyd had performed that necessary formality (of divorce) from her, We gave her unto thee in marriage, so that (henceforth) there may be no sin for believers in respect of wives of their adopted sons, when the latter have performed the necessary formality (of release) from them. The commandment of Allah must be fulfilled.
________________
Summary:
1. NAKAHA(  نكح  ): only used for living creations and marriage agreement.
2. ZAWWAJ(  زوج  ): to make couple, it is common. Also, it includes the aspect of living together after marriage.
According to Imam Raghib, if zawwaj(  زوج  ) ends in ‘  ب   ‘, then it only means to create a couple, not the consummation of marriage. And zawwajnahum bihoorin ainin(  زوجناهم بحور عين  ) just includes this that they are just companion and friends, else in the Quran it would have been zawwajnahum hooran(  زوجنهم حورا  ) instead of zawwajnahum bihoorin(  زوجنهم بحور  ). As zawwajtuhu imra’tan(  زوجته امراءة  ) is a proverb. And Allah knows best!

22 NIKALNA
[To exit]
Synonyms: KHARAJA(  خرج  ), BARAZA(  برز  ), NAFARA(  نفر  ), GHA’ZA(  غزى  ), ZAHAQA(  زهق  ), NAFAZA(  نفذ  ), SALLALA(  سلل  ), LAWAZA(  لوازا  ), DAFAQA(  دفق  ), SHARAQA(  شرق  ), TALAA’(  طلع  )
22.1 kharaja(  خرج  )  : to exit, to come outside (ant:dakhala(  دخل  )), it is a famous word and its use is also common. It is stated in the Quran:
________________
Surat Al-Hashr(Exile) -   سُوۡرَةُ الحَشر
59:11
لَٮِٕنۡ أُخۡرِجۡتُمۡ لَنَخۡرُجَنَّ مَعَكُمۡ
Hast thou not observed those who are hypocrites, (how) they tell their brethren who disbelieve among the People of the Scripture: If ye are driven out, we surely will go out with you, and we will never obey anyone against you, and if ye are attacked we verily will help you. And Allah beareth witness that they verily are liars.
________________
22.2 baraza (  برز  )  : meaning to come outside in the open ground, to come in the front, to emerge after hiding. Barz(  برز  ) meaning atmosphere and vast ground. And dawat-e-mubarzat(  دعوت مبازرت  ) means in a battlefield, a person coming forward and challenging someone from the enemy’s side to fight. It is stated in the Quran:
________________
Surat Al-Baqarah (The Cow) -   سُوۡرَةُ البَقَرَة
2:250
وَلَمَّا بَرَزُواْ لِجَالُوتَ وَجُنُودِهِۦ
And when they went into the field against Goliath and his hosts they said: Our Lord! Bestow on us endurance, make our foothold sure, and give us help against the disbelieving folk.
________________
22.3 nafara (  نفر  )  : means to set off on a mission or war. An-nafar(  النفر  ) means a group of fighters, a party of three to ten people and nafeer(  نفير  ) meaning the people setting off for a fight. Nafeer-ul-aam(  نفيرالعام  ) means the rising of masses against the enemy. Allah states that:
________________
Surat An-Nisa (Women) -   سُوۡرَةُ النِّسَاء
4:71
فَٱنفِرُواْ ثُبَاتٍ أَوِ ٱنفِرُواْ جَمِيعً۬ا
O ye who believe! Take your precautions, then advance the proven ones, or advance all together.
________________
22.4 ghaza (  غزى  )  : ghazu(  غزو  ) meaning to set off with the intent of fighting with the enemy and meaning to set off for fight, to attack for the loot. Ghazza(  غزى  ) means to prepare to send for a fight. Ghazza(  غزى  ) and aghza(  اغزى  ) both mean to send for fight and give ammunition. Allah states that:
________________
Surat Al-E-Imran (Family of Imran) -   سُوۡرَةُ آل عِمرَان
3:156
أَوۡ كَانُواْ غُزًّ۬ى لَّوۡ كَانُواْ عِندَنَا مَا مَاتُواْ
O ye who believe! Be not as those who disbelieved and said of their brethren who went abroad in the land or were fighting in the field: If they had been (here) with us they would not have died or been killed: that Allah may make it anguish in their hearts. Allah giveth life and causeth death; and Allah is Seer of what ye do.
________________
22.5 zahaqa (  زهق  )  : to run off, zahaq-an-nafs(  زهق  النفس  ) meaning the exiting of soul from the body. Zahaq-al-batil(  زهق الباطل  ) means the escaping of evil and zahiq(  زاهق  ) meaning disheartened, discouraged, the one coming for a battle and running after failing. Also, zahaq(  زهق  ) is a part of the set of opposites. Zahiq(  زاهق  ) means a fat animal as well as a very weak and thin animal. Hence, zahaq(  زهق  ) means to make some run off after defeating them as well as making them run off after weakening them. Allah states that:
________________
Surat Al-Isra (Children of Israel) -   سُوۡرَةُ بنیٓ اسرآئیل / الإسرَاء
17: 81
وَقُلۡ جَآءَ ٱلۡحَقُّ وَزَهَقَ ٱلۡبَـٰطِلُ‌ۚ إِنَّ ٱلۡبَـٰطِلَ كَانَ زَهُوقً۬ا
And say: Truth hath come and falsehood hath vanished away. Lo! falsehood is ever bound to vanish.
________________
22.6 nafaza (  نفذ  )  : meaning to pass through something and nafaaz(  نفاذ  ) meaning the initiation of something with force, the detonation of something and passing through something completely. Allah states that:
________________
Surat Ar-Rahman (The Merciful) -   سُوۡرَةُ الرَّحمٰن
55:33
يَـٰمَعۡشَرَ ٱلۡجِنِّ وَٱلۡإِنسِ إِنِ ٱسۡتَطَعۡتُمۡ أَن تَنفُذُواْ مِنۡ أَقۡطَارِ ٱلسَّمَـٰوَٲتِ وَٱلۡأَرۡضِ فَٱنفُذُواْ‌ۚ
O company of jinn and men, if ye have power to penetrate (all) regions of the heavens and the earth, then penetrate (them)! Ye will never penetrate them save with (Our) sanction.
________________
22.7 sallala (  سلل  )  : to exit quietly, to sneak.
________________
22.8 liwaza (  لوازا  )  : laaza-bil-jabal(  لاذ بالجبل  ) meaning to conceal behind a mountain, hide. Lauz(  لوز  ) means the corner of a mountain, and malaaz(  ملاذ  ) means a place of hiding or fort. Liwaza(  لوازا  ) means to set off to find some kind of concealment. Allah states that:
________________
Surat Al-Noor (The Light) -   سُوۡرَةُ النُّور
24:63
قَدۡ يَعۡلَمُ ٱللَّهُ ٱلَّذِينَ يَتَسَلَّلُونَ مِنكُمۡ لِوَاذً۬ا‌ۚ
Make not the calling of the messenger among you as your calling one of another. Allah knoweth those of you who steal away, hiding themselves. And let those who conspire to evade orders beware lest grief or painful punishment befall them.
________________
22.9 dafaqa (  دفق  )  : meaning the coming forward of something through force and strength, to set off with a jump. Allah states that:
________________
Surat At-Tariq (The Morning Star) -   سُوۡرَةُ الطّارق
86:5-6
خُلِقَ مِن مَّآءٍ۬ دَافِقٍ۬ فَلۡيَنظُرِ ٱلۡإِنسَـٰنُ مِمَّ خُلِقَ
So let man consider from what he is created. He is created from a gushing fluid
________________
22.10 sharaqa (  شرق  )  : sharq(  شرق  ) means sun, the place where the sun rises, and shirq(  شرق  ) means the ray of coming coming through a creak of the door. Sharaqat-i-shams(  شرقت الشمس  ) meaning the rising of sun, and mashriq(  مشرق  ) meaning the place of rising of sun. Thus the word sharaqa(  شرق  ) is specific to the rising of the sun or to any thing that is much more bright and shining than other planets. As Allah has stated:
________________
Surat Az-Zumar (The Troops) -   سُوۡرَةُ الزُّمَر
39:69
وَأَشۡرَقَتِ ٱلۡأَرۡضُ بِنُورِ رَبِّہَا
And the earth shineth with the light of her Lord, and the Book is set up, and the prophets and the witnesses are brought, and it is judged between them with truth, and they are not wronged.
________________
And ashraqa(  اشرق  ) is also used to depict the doing of some work at sunrise. Allah states that:
________________
Surat Al-Shuara (The Poets) -   سُوۡرَةُ الشُّعَرَاء
26:60
فَأَتۡبَعُوهُم مُّشۡرِقِينَ
And they overtook them at sunrise.
________________
22.11 talaa’ (  طلع  )  : the rising of ordinary planets and it also includes the sun. Thus, the word talaa’(  طلع  ) is common whereas sharaqa(  شرق  ) is only used with the rising of the sun. The girls of Bani Najaar used to sing a song when the Prophet PBUH would come, its first line was tala-al-badru-a’laina(  طلع البدر علينا  ). In the Quran, the word talaa’(  طلع)   has not been used for the rising of planets, although it has been associated with fajr(dusk) (or with the sun) and the light of fajr is much less than the sun. Allah states that:
________________
Surat Al-Qadr (Fate) -   سُوۡرَةُ القَدر
97:5
سَلَـٰمٌ هِىَ حَتَّىٰ مَطۡلَعِ ٱلۡفَجۡرِ
(The night is) Peace until the rising of the dawn.
________________
Summary:
1. KHARAJA(  خرج  ): to exit, use is common.
2. BARAZA(  برز  ): to exit to the ground, to come in front.
3. NAFARA(  نفر  ): to set off on war or mission.
4. GHAZA(  غزى  ): this word is specific to setting off on jihad.
5. ZAHAQA(  زهق  ): to run off after getting disheartened and discouraged.
6. NAFAZA(  نفذ  ): to pass through.
7. SALLALA(  سلل  ): to slip off.
8. LAAZ(  لاذ  ): to set off in search of concealment.
9. DAFAQA(  دفق  ): to move forward with force and strength, to set off with a jump.
10. SHARAQA(  شرق  ): rising of sun.
11. TALAA’(  طلع  ): rising of planets and stars(including the sun). It is common.

Surat Al-Hashr(Exile) - سُوۡرَةُ الحَشر

59:11

لَٮِٕنۡ أُخۡرِجۡتُمۡ لَنَخۡرُجَنَّ مَعَكُمۡ

Hast thou not observed those who are hypocrites, (how) they tell their brethren who disbelieve among the People of the Scripture: If ye are driven out, we surely will go out with you, and we will never obey anyone against you, and if ye are attacked we verily will help you. And Allah beareth witness that they verily are liars.

________________

22.2 baraza (برز): meaning to come outside in the open ground, to come in the front, to emerge after hiding. Barz(برز) meaning atmosphere and vast ground. And dawat-e-mubarzat(دعوت مبازرت) means in a battlefield, a person coming forward and challenging someone from the enemy’s side to fight. It is stated in the Quran:  

________________

Surat Al-Baqarah (The Cow) - سُوۡرَةُ البَقَرَة

2:250

وَلَمَّا بَرَزُواْ لِجَالُوتَ وَجُنُودِهِۦ

And when they went into the field against Goliath and his hosts they said: Our Lord! Bestow on us endurance, make our foothold sure, and give us help against the disbelieving folk.

________________

22.3 nafara (نفر): means to set off on a mission or war. An-nafar(النفر) means a group of fighters, a party of three to ten people and nafeer(نفير) meaning the people setting off for a fight. Nafeer-ul-aam(نفيرالعام) means the rising of masses against the enemy. Allah states that:

________________

Surat An-Nisa (Women) - سُوۡرَةُ النِّسَاء

4:71

فَٱنفِرُواْ ثُبَاتٍ أَوِ ٱنفِرُواْ جَمِيعً۬ا

O ye who believe! Take your precautions, then advance the proven ones, or advance all together.

________________

22.4 ghaza (غزى): ghazu(غزو) meaning to set off with the intent of fighting with the enemy and meaning to set off for fight, to attack for the loot. Ghazza(غزى) means to prepare to send for a fight. Ghazza(غزى) and aghza(اغزى) both mean to send for fight and give ammunition. Allah states that:

________________

Surat Al-E-Imran (Family of Imran) - سُوۡرَةُ آل عِمرَان

3:156

أَوۡ كَانُواْ غُزًّ۬ى لَّوۡ كَانُواْ عِندَنَا مَا مَاتُواْ

O ye who believe! Be not as those who disbelieved and said of their brethren who went abroad in the land or were fighting in the field: If they had been (here) with us they would not have died or been killed: that Allah may make it anguish in their hearts. Allah giveth life and causeth death; and Allah is Seer of what ye do.

________________

22.5 zahaqa (زهق): to run off, zahaq-an-nafs(زهق  النفس) meaning the exiting of soul from the body. Zahaq-al-batil(زهق الباطل) means the escaping of evil and zahiq(زاهق) meaning disheartened, discouraged, the one coming for a battle and running after failing. Also, zahaq(زهق) is a part of the set of opposites. Zahiq(زاهق) means a fat animal as well as a very weak and thin animal. Hence, zahaq(زهق) means to make some run off after defeating them as well as making them run off after weakening them. Allah states that:

________________

Surat Al-Isra (Children of Israel) - سُوۡرَةُ بنیٓ اسرآئیل / الإسرَاء

17: 81

وَقُلۡ جَآءَ ٱلۡحَقُّ وَزَهَقَ ٱلۡبَـٰطِلُ‌ۚ إِنَّ ٱلۡبَـٰطِلَ كَانَ زَهُوقً۬ا

And say: Truth hath come and falsehood hath vanished away. Lo! falsehood is ever bound to vanish.

________________

22.6 nafaza (نفذ): meaning to pass through something and nafaaz(نفاذ) meaning the initiation of something with force, the detonation of something and passing through something completely. Allah states that:

________________

Surat Ar-Rahman (The Merciful) - سُوۡرَةُ الرَّحمٰن

55:33

يَـٰمَعۡشَرَ ٱلۡجِنِّ وَٱلۡإِنسِ إِنِ ٱسۡتَطَعۡتُمۡ أَن تَنفُذُواْ مِنۡ أَقۡطَارِ ٱلسَّمَـٰوَٲتِ وَٱلۡأَرۡضِ فَٱنفُذُواْ‌ۚ

O company of jinn and men, if ye have power to penetrate (all) regions of the heavens and the earth, then penetrate (them)! Ye will never penetrate them save with (Our) sanction.

________________

22.7 sallala (سلل): to exit quietly, to sneak.

________________

22.8 liwaza (لوازا): laaza-bil-jabal(لاذ بالجبل) meaning to conceal behind a mountain, hide. Lauz(لوز) means the corner of a mountain, and malaaz(ملاذ) means a place of hiding or fort. Liwaza(لوازا) means to set off to find some kind of concealment. Allah states that:

________________

Surat Al-Noor (The Light) - سُوۡرَةُ النُّور

24:63

قَدۡ يَعۡلَمُ ٱللَّهُ ٱلَّذِينَ يَتَسَلَّلُونَ مِنكُمۡ لِوَاذً۬ا‌ۚ

Make not the calling of the messenger among you as your calling one of another. Allah knoweth those of you who steal away, hiding themselves. And let those who conspire to evade orders beware lest grief or painful punishment befall them.

________________

22.9 dafaqa (دفق): meaning the coming forward of something through force and strength, to set off with a jump. Allah states that:

________________

Surat At-Tariq (The Morning Star) - سُوۡرَةُ الطّارق

86:5-6

خُلِقَ مِن مَّآءٍ۬ دَافِقٍ۬ فَلۡيَنظُرِ ٱلۡإِنسَـٰنُ مِمَّ خُلِقَ

So let man consider from what he is created. He is created from a gushing fluid

________________

22.10 sharaqa (شرق): sharq(شرق) means sun, the place where the sun rises, and shirq(شرق) means the ray of coming coming through a creak of the door. Sharaqat-i-shams(شرقت الشمس) meaning the rising of sun, and mashriq(مشرق) meaning the place of rising of sun. Thus the word sharaqa(شرق) is specific to the rising of the sun or to any thing that is much more bright and shining than other planets. As Allah has stated:

________________

Surat Az-Zumar (The Troops) - سُوۡرَةُ الزُّمَر

39:69

وَأَشۡرَقَتِ ٱلۡأَرۡضُ بِنُورِ رَبِّہَا

And the earth shineth with the light of her Lord, and the Book is set up, and the prophets and the witnesses are brought, and it is judged between them with truth, and they are not wronged.

________________

And ashraqa(اشرق) is also used to depict the doing of some work at sunrise. Allah states that:

________________

Surat Al-Shuara (The Poets) - سُوۡرَةُ الشُّعَرَاء

26:60

فَأَتۡبَعُوهُم مُّشۡرِقِينَ

And they overtook them at sunrise.

________________

22.11 talaa’ (طلع): the rising of ordinary planets and it also includes the sun. Thus, the word talaa’(طلع) is common whereas sharaqa(شرق) is only used with the rising of the sun. The girls of Bani Najaar used to sing a song when the Prophet PBUH would come, its first line was tala-al-badru-a’laina(طلع البدر علينا). In the Quran, the word talaa’(طلع) has not been used for the rising of planets, although it has been associated with fajr(dusk) (or with the sun) and the light of fajr is much less than the sun. Allah states that:

________________

Surat Al-Qadr (Fate) - سُوۡرَةُ القَدر

97:5

سَلَـٰمٌ هِىَ حَتَّىٰ مَطۡلَعِ ٱلۡفَجۡرِ

(The night is) Peace until the rising of the dawn.

________________

Summary:

1. KHARAJA(خرج): to exit, use is common.

2. BARAZA(برز): to exit to the ground, to come in front.

3. NAFARA(نفر): to set off on war or mission.

4. GHAZA(غزى): this word is specific to setting off on jihad.

5. ZAHAQA(زهق): to run off after getting disheartened and discouraged.

6. NAFAZA(نفذ): to pass through.

7. SALLALA(سلل): to slip off.

8. LAAZ(لاذ): to set off in search of concealment.

9. DAFAQA(دفق): to move forward with force and strength, to set off with a jump.

10. SHARAQA(شرق): rising of sun.

11. TALAA’(طلع): rising of planets and stars(including the sun). It is common.

title: content/n/n23.html
raw_text:
23 NIKAALNA
[to take out]
Synonyms: AKHRAJA(  اخرج  ), BARRAZA(  برز  ), TARADA(  طرد  )
23.1 akhraja(  اخرج  )  : to take out, its use is common.
________________
Surat Al-Tawba (Repentance) -   سُوۡرَةُ التّوبَة
9:40
إِلَّا تَنصُرُوهُ فَقَدۡ نَصَرَهُ ٱللَّهُ إِذۡ أَخۡرَجَهُ ٱلَّذِينَ ڪَفَرُواْ
If ye help him not, still Allah helped him when those who disbelieve drove him forth, the second of two; when they two were in the cave, when he said unto his comrade: Grieve not. Lo! Allah is with us. Then Allah caused His peace of reassurance to descend upon him and supported him with hosts ye cannot see, and made the word of those who disbelieved the nethermost, while Allah's Word it was that became the uppermost. Allah is Mighty, Wise.
________________
23.2 barraza (  برز  )  : meaning to bring forward (for details, see above). It is stated in the Quran:
________________
Surat An-Naziat (Soul-Snatchers)) -   سُوۡرَةُ النَّازعَات
79:36
وَبُرِّزَتِ ٱلۡجَحِيمُ لِمَن يَرَىٰ
And hell will stand forth visible to him who seeth,
________________
23.3 tarada(  طرد  ):   to distant someone by thinking of him as being inferior or low-grade, to move them, to scold off. Allah states that:
________________
Surat Al-Anaam (Cattle) -   سُوۡرَةُ الاٴنعَام
6:52
وَلَا تَطۡرُدِ ٱلَّذِينَ يَدۡعُونَ رَبَّهُم بِٱلۡغَدَوٰةِ وَٱلۡعَشِىِّ يُرِيدُونَ وَجۡهَهُ ۥ‌ۖ
Repel not those who call upon their Lord at morn and evening, seeking His Countenance. Thou art not accountable for them in aught, nor are they accountable for thee in aught, that thou shouldst repel them and be of the wrong-doers.
________________
Summary:
1. AKHRAJA(  اخرج  ): common for taking out something.
2. BARRAZA(  برز  ): to bring out something in an open space.
3. TARADA(  طرد  ): to throw off someone as being inferior and low-grade.

title: content/n/n24.html
raw_text:
24 NIGAH
[sight]
Synonyms: BASAR(  بصر  ), TARAF(  طرف  )
24.1 basar(  بصر  )  : meaning eye as well as the function of the eye i.e. sight, vision and viewing. And the process of viewing is made clear through this word. Allah states that:
________________
Surat Qaf  -   سُوۡرَةُ قٓ
50:22
فَبَصَرُكَ ٱلۡيَوۡمَ حَدِيدٌ۬
(And unto the evil-doer it is said): Thou wast in heedlessness of this. Now We have removed from thee thy covering, and piercing is thy sight this day.
________________
24.2 taraf (  طرف  )  : its real meaning is the edge or limit of something. Tarf-ul-ain(  طرف العين  ) meaning blink of an eye and tarfatu a’in(  طرفة عين  ) meaning that time or duration which occurs during the blink of an eye. Thus in taraf(  طرف  ), the aspect of viewing is not evident but points towards a very less period of time. Allah states that:
________________
Surat Al-Naml (The Ants) -   سُوۡرَةُ النَّمل
27:40
أَنَا۟ ءَاتِيكَ بِهِۦ قَبۡلَ أَن يَرۡتَدَّ إِلَيۡكَ طَرۡفُكَ‌ۚ
One with whom was knowledge of the Scripture said: I will bring it thee before thy gaze returneth unto thee. And when he saw it set in his presence, (Solomon) said: This is of the bounty of my Lord, that He may try me whether I give thanks or am ungrateful. Whosoever giveth thanks he only giveth thanks for (the good of) his own soul; and whosoever is ungrateful (is ungrateful only to his own soul's hurt). For lo! my Lord is Absolute in independence, Bountiful.
________________
then this word became a same-meaning word with basar(  بصر  ) because of its excessive usage as tarfun khafiyun(  طرف خفي  ) means angry look and qadiratu-taraf(  قصرت طرف  ) (37:48) meaning the women with lowered gazes.
________________
Summary:
The word BASARA(  بصر  )is used to depict sight or vision whereas the word TARAF(  طرف  ) points towards the small amount of time taken in the blink of an eye.
(for ‘nigah, nigah daalna’, see ‘daikhna’)

title: content/n/n25.html
raw_text:
25 NIGEHBAAN
[guardian]
Synonyms: HAAFIZ(  حافظ  ), HAFEEZ(  حفيظ  ), RAQEEB(  رقيب  ), MUQEET(  مقيت  )(   قوة  ), HARAS(  حرس  ), MUHAIMIN(  مهيمن  )
25.1 haafiz(  حافظ  )  : ahfaz(  احفظ  ) (ant:azaa’(  اضاع  )) meaning to save something from wastage and destruction, to protect. To protect something from outside dangers. Haafiz(  حافظ  ) is a pronoun meaning the protector and hafeez(  حفيظ  ) has the aspect of addition i.e. the protect who protects at all times. Allah states that:
________________
Surat Yusuf -   سُوۡرَةُ یُوسُف
12:64
فَٱللَّهُ خَيۡرٌ حَـٰفِظً۬ا‌ۖ
He said: Can I entrust him to you save as I entrusted his brother to you aforetime? Allah is better at guarding, and He is the Most Merciful of those who show mercy.
________________
Surat Hud  -   سُوۡرَةُ هُود
11:86
وَمَآ أَنَا۟ عَلَيۡكُم بِحَفِيظٍ۬
That which Allah leaveth with you is better for you if ye are believers; and I am not a keeper over you.
________________
25.2 raqeeb (  رقيب  )  : raqba(  رقبة  ) meaning neck and raqaba(  رقب  ) meaning to keep a watch on someone’s neck or to watch over or guard someone. Raqba(  رقبة  ) means care, guard, savior and fear. Hence, raqeeb(  رقيب  ) is that kind of protector who is cautious himself at all times, and whoever has a raqeeb(  رقيب  ), there is nothing hidden between them. It is stated in the Quran:
________________
Surat Al-Maeda (The Table) -   سُوۡرَةُ المَائدة
5:117
فَلَمَّا تَوَفَّيۡتَنِى كُنتَ أَنتَ ٱلرَّقِيبَ عَلَيۡہِمۡ‌ۚ
I spake unto them only that which Thou commandedst me, (saying): Worship Allah, my Lord and your Lord. I was a witness of them while I dwelt among them, and when Thou tookest me Thou wast the Watcher over them. Thou art Witness over all things.
________________
25.3 muqeet(  مقيت  ):   quwwa(  قوة  ) qaata(  قات  ) meaning to provide sustenance, provision, to be a custodian, and aaqat(  اقات  ) meaning to have power, to protect, to provide provision and muqeet(  مقيت  ) means the people of power, guardian and custodian. Thus muqeet(  مقيت  ) is such a guardian who is self sufficient. According to Ibn-al-Faris, three things are included in muqeet: (i) to have power on something (ii) protection (iii) generous thus muqeet(  مقيت  ) is that powerful being who has the complete power to protect you. Allah states that:
________________
Surat An-Nisa (Women) -   سُوۡرَةُ النِّسَاء
4: 85
وَكَانَ ٱللَّهُ عَلَىٰ كُلِّ شَىۡءٍ۬ مُّقِيتً۬ا
Whoso interveneth in a good cause will have the reward thereof, and whoso interveneth in an evil cause will bear the consequence thereof. Allah overseeth all things.
________________
25.4 harasa(  سول  ):   haras(  حرس  ) meaning to take in protection, to arrest, to keep watch, to keep watch on a convict. According to Ibn-al-Faris, haras(  حرس  ) includes two things: (i) protection (ii) era. Thus to protect for some duration of time and haras-al-Malik(  حرس الملك  ) meaning royal guards, bodyguards. It is stated in the Quran:
________________
Surat Al-Jinn (The Jinn) -   سُوۡرَةُ الجنّ
72: 8
وَأَنَّا لَمَسۡنَا ٱلسَّمَآءَ فَوَجَدۡنَـٰهَا مُلِئَتۡ حَرَسً۬ا شَدِيدً۬ا وَشُہُبً۬ا
And (the Jinn who had listened to the Qur'an said): We had sought the heaven but had found it filled with strong warders and meteors.
________________
25.5 muhaimin(  مهيمن  ):   according to Ibn-al-Faris and some other scholars, define this as the one who provides peace and haiman-at-tairu a’la farakhihi(  هيمن الطائر على فراخه  ) means the bird spread it feathers on her child. Muhaimin(  مهيمن  ) is that one who (i) gives peace to someone from fear (ii) doesn’t let the rights of someone be neglected. This word has been used in the Quran twice and came in both these meanings. Allah states that:
________________
(i) in the meaning of bringing peace:
Surat Al-Hashr (Exile) -   سُوۡرَةُ الحَشر
59:23
ٱلۡمَلِكُ ٱلۡقُدُّوسُ ٱلسَّلَـٰمُ ٱلۡمُؤۡمِنُ ٱلۡمُهَيۡمِنُ
He is Allah, than Whom there is no other God, the Sovereign Lord, the Holy One, Peace, the Keeper of Faith, the Guardian, the Majestic, the Compeller, the Superb. Glorified be Allah from all that they ascribe as partner (unto Him).
________________
(ii) in the meaning of not getting the rights of someone being neglected::
Surat Al-Maeda (The Table) -   سُوۡرَةُ المَائدة
5:48
وَأَنزَلۡنَآ إِلَيۡكَ ٱلۡكِتَـٰبَ بِٱلۡحَقِّ مُصَدِّقً۬ا لِّمَا بَيۡنَ يَدَيۡهِ مِنَ ٱلۡڪِتَـٰبِ وَمُهَيۡمِنًا عَلَيۡهِ‌ۖ
And unto thee have We revealed the Scripture with the truth, confirming whatever Scripture was before it, and a watcher over it. So judge between them by that which Allah hath revealed, and follow not their desires away from the truth which hath come unto thee. For each We have appointed a divine law and a traced-out way. Had Allah willed He could have made you one community. But that He may try you by that which He hath given you (He hath made you as ye are). So vie one with another in good works. Unto Allah ye will all return, and He will then inform you of that wherein ye differ.
________________
Summary:
1. HAAFIZ(  حافظ  ): the one who saves something from destruction.
2. RAQEEB(  رقيب  ): that protector who himself remain cautious as well as keeps an eye on all activities of the other thing.

25 NIGEHBAAN

[guardian]

Synonyms: HAAFIZ(حافظ), HAFEEZ(حفيظ), RAQEEB(رقيب), MUQEET(مقيت)( قوة), HARAS(حرس), MUHAIMIN(مهيمن)

25.1 haafiz(حافظ): ahfaz(احفظ) (ant:azaa’(اضاع)) meaning to save something from wastage and destruction, to protect. To protect something from outside dangers. Haafiz(حافظ) is a pronoun meaning the protector and hafeez(حفيظ) has the aspect of addition i.e. the protect who protects at all times. Allah states that:

________________

Surat Yusuf - سُوۡرَةُ یُوسُف

12:64

فَٱللَّهُ خَيۡرٌ حَـٰفِظً۬ا‌ۖ

He said: Can I entrust him to you save as I entrusted his brother to you aforetime? Allah is better at guarding, and He is the Most Merciful of those who show mercy.

________________

Surat Hud  - سُوۡرَةُ هُود

11:86

وَمَآ أَنَا۟ عَلَيۡكُم بِحَفِيظٍ۬

That which Allah leaveth with you is better for you if ye are believers; and I am not a keeper over you.

________________

25.2 raqeeb (رقيب): raqba(رقبة) meaning neck and raqaba(رقب) meaning to keep a watch on someone’s neck or to watch over or guard someone. Raqba(رقبة) means care, guard, savior and fear. Hence, raqeeb(رقيب) is that kind of protector who is cautious himself at all times, and whoever has a raqeeb(رقيب), there is nothing hidden between them. It is stated in the Quran:

________________

Surat Al-Maeda (The Table) - سُوۡرَةُ المَائدة

5:117

فَلَمَّا تَوَفَّيۡتَنِى كُنتَ أَنتَ ٱلرَّقِيبَ عَلَيۡہِمۡ‌ۚ

I spake unto them only that which Thou commandedst me, (saying): Worship Allah, my Lord and your Lord. I was a witness of them while I dwelt among them, and when Thou tookest me Thou wast the Watcher over them. Thou art Witness over all things.

________________

25.3 muqeet(مقيت): quwwa(قوة) qaata(قات) meaning to provide sustenance, provision, to be a custodian, and aaqat(اقات) meaning to have power, to protect, to provide provision and muqeet(مقيت) means the people of power, guardian and custodian. Thus muqeet(مقيت) is such a guardian who is self sufficient. According to Ibn-al-Faris, three things are included in muqeet: (i) to have power on something (ii) protection (iii) generous thus muqeet(مقيت) is that powerful being who has the complete power to protect you. Allah states that:

________________

Surat An-Nisa (Women) - سُوۡرَةُ النِّسَاء

4: 85

وَكَانَ ٱللَّهُ عَلَىٰ كُلِّ شَىۡءٍ۬ مُّقِيتً۬ا

Whoso interveneth in a good cause will have the reward thereof, and whoso interveneth in an evil cause will bear the consequence thereof. Allah overseeth all things.

________________

25.4 harasa(سول): haras(حرس) meaning to take in protection, to arrest, to keep watch, to keep watch on a convict. According to Ibn-al-Faris, haras(حرس) includes two things: (i) protection (ii) era. Thus to protect for some duration of time and haras-al-Malik(حرس الملك) meaning royal guards, bodyguards. It is stated in the Quran:

________________

Surat Al-Jinn (The Jinn) - سُوۡرَةُ الجنّ                

72: 8

وَأَنَّا لَمَسۡنَا ٱلسَّمَآءَ فَوَجَدۡنَـٰهَا مُلِئَتۡ حَرَسً۬ا شَدِيدً۬ا وَشُہُبً۬ا

And (the Jinn who had listened to the Qur'an said): We had sought the heaven but had found it filled with strong warders and meteors.

________________

25.5 muhaimin(مهيمن): according to Ibn-al-Faris and some other scholars, define this as the one who provides peace and haiman-at-tairu a’la farakhihi(هيمن الطائر على فراخه) means the bird spread it feathers on her child. Muhaimin(مهيمن) is that one who (i) gives peace to someone from fear (ii) doesn’t let the rights of someone be neglected. This word has been used in the Quran twice and came in both these meanings. Allah states that:

________________

(i) in the meaning of bringing peace:

Surat Al-Hashr (Exile) - سُوۡرَةُ الحَشر

59:23

ٱلۡمَلِكُ ٱلۡقُدُّوسُ ٱلسَّلَـٰمُ ٱلۡمُؤۡمِنُ ٱلۡمُهَيۡمِنُ

He is Allah, than Whom there is no other God, the Sovereign Lord, the Holy One, Peace, the Keeper of Faith, the Guardian, the Majestic, the Compeller, the Superb. Glorified be Allah from all that they ascribe as partner (unto Him).

________________

(ii) in the meaning of not getting the rights of someone being neglected::

Surat Al-Maeda (The Table) - سُوۡرَةُ المَائدة

5:48

وَأَنزَلۡنَآ إِلَيۡكَ ٱلۡكِتَـٰبَ بِٱلۡحَقِّ مُصَدِّقً۬ا لِّمَا بَيۡنَ يَدَيۡهِ مِنَ ٱلۡڪِتَـٰبِ وَمُهَيۡمِنًا عَلَيۡهِ‌ۖ

And unto thee have We revealed the Scripture with the truth, confirming whatever Scripture was before it, and a watcher over it. So judge between them by that which Allah hath revealed, and follow not their desires away from the truth which hath come unto thee. For each We have appointed a divine law and a traced-out way. Had Allah willed He could have made you one community. But that He may try you by that which He hath given you (He hath made you as ye are). So vie one with another in good works. Unto Allah ye will all return, and He will then inform you of that wherein ye differ.

________________

Summary:

1. HAAFIZ(حافظ): the one who saves something from destruction.

2. RAQEEB(رقيب): that protector who himself remain cautious as well as keeps an eye on all activities of the other thing.

3. MUQEET(مقيت): that protector who has complete power on protection;

4. HARAS(حرس): guard, watchman, the one who arrests, protection, era.

5. MUHAIMIN(مهيمن): the one who protects after offering refuge.

(Also see ‘hifazat kerna’)

26 NIGALNA
[to swallow]
Synonyms: BALAA’(  بلع  ), MARAA’(  مرء  ), SAGHA(  ساغ  ), GHASSA(  غص  ), LAQIFA(  لقف  ), ILTAQAM(  التقم  )
26.1 balaa’(  بلع  )  : bala’m(  بلعم  ) or bulu’om(  بلعوم  ) meaning throat, the esophagus, and balaa’(  بلع  ) means to swallow, to swallow down the throat. Allah states that:
________________
Surat Hud  -   سُوۡرَةُ هُود
11:44
وَقِيلَ يَـٰٓأَرۡضُ ٱبۡلَعِى مَآءَكِ
And it was said: O earth! Swallow thy water and, O sky! be cleared of clouds! And the water was made to subside. And the commandment was fulfilled. And it (the ship) came to rest upon (the mount) Al-Judi and it was said: A far removal for wrongdoing folk!
________________
26.2 maraa’(  مرء  ):   almariu’(  المري  ) is that track which goes from the throat to the stomach through which food reaches the stomach. And maraa’(  مرء  ) means the food reached through this track to the stomach easily and mariaa’(  مرء  ) means that food which easily reaches the stomach. Allah states that:
________________
Surat An-Nisa (Women) -   سُوۡرَةُ النِّسَاء
4:4
فَإِن طِبۡنَ لَكُمۡ عَن شَىۡءٍ۬ مِّنۡهُ نَفۡسً۬ا فَكُلُوهُ هَنِيٓـًٔ۬ا مَّرِيٓـًٔ۬ا
And give unto the women (whom ye marry) free gift of their marriage portions; but if they of their own accord remit unto you a part thereof, then ye are welcome to absorb it (in your wealth).
________________
26.3 sagha (  ساغ  )  : meaning the swallowing of food or water easily and being pleasant. It is stated in the Quran:
________________
Surat An-Nahl (The Bee) -   سُوۡرَةُ النّحل
16:66
لَّبَنًا خَالِصً۬ا سَآٮِٕغً۬ا لِّلشَّـٰرِبِينَ
And lo! in the cattle there is a lesson for you. We give you to drink of that which is in their bellies, from betwixt the refuse and the blood, pure milk palatable to the drinkers.
________________
and asaagha(  اساغ  ) means the swallowing of food or water through the throat. Allah states that:
________________
Surat Ibrahim -   سُوۡرَةُ إبراهیم
14:16-17
يَتَجَرَّعُهُ ۥ وَلَا يَڪَادُ يُسِيغُهُ  وَيُسۡقَىٰ مِن مَّآءٍ۬ صَدِيدٍ۬
Hell is before him, and he is made to drink a festering water, (16) Which he sippeth but can hardly swallow, and death cometh unto him from every side while yet he cannot die, and before him is a harsh doom.
________________
26.4 ghassa (  غص  )  : meaning to choke by eating or drinking, food getting stuck in the throat and not being swallowed. Allah states that:
________________
Surat Al-Muzammil (The Enshrouded One) -   سُوۡرَةُ المُزمّل
73:12-13
وَطَعَامً۬ا ذَا غُصَّةٍ۬  إِنَّ لَدَيۡنَآ أَنكَالاً۬ وَجَحِيمً۬ا
Lo! with Us are heavy fetters and a raging fire, (12) And food which choketh (the partaker), and a painful doom
________________
26.5 laqifa (  لقف  )  : meaning to take something quickly, laqif-at-taa’m(  لقف الطعام  ) meaning to eat quickly, to take something with craftiness and cunningly and this word is used to take something in hand or mouth meaning to eat and swallow in a hurry. Allah states that:
________________
Surat Ta-Ha  -   سُوۡرَةُ طٰه
20:69
وَأَلۡقِ مَا فِى يَمِينِكَ تَلۡقَفۡ مَا صَنَعُوٓاْ‌ۖ
Throw that which is in thy right hand! It will eat up that which they have made. Lo! that which they have made is but a wizard's artifice, and a wizard shall not be successful to whatever point (of skill) he may attain.
________________
26.6 iltaqam (  التقم  )  : laqama(  لقم  ) meaning to make a bite, the amount of food that can be taken at one time in the mouth, to put in mouth with hand, and iltaqam(  التقم  ) means to take in quickly, to eat quickly by taking big bites. Allah states that:
________________
Surat As-Saafat (The Rangers) -   سُوۡرَةُ الصَّافات
37:142
فَٱلۡتَقَمَهُ ٱلۡحُوتُ وَهُوَ مُلِيمٌ۬
And the fish swallowed him while he was blameworthy;
________________
Summary:
1. BALAA’(  بلع  ): to swallow, its use is common.
2. MARAA’(  مرء  ): the reaching of something easily to the stomach.
3. SAGHA(  ساغ  ): the reaching of something easily to the stomach because of it being pleasant.
4. GHASSA(  غص  ): to choke on food.
5. LAQIFA(  لقف  ): to eat quickly, to swallow without chewing.
5. ILTAQAM(  التقم  ): to eat quickly, to swallow at once with big bites.

27 NAHANA-DHAWNA [To Take a Bath, To Wash]   pg 862
Synonyms:GHASALA غَسَلَ IGHTASALA اِغْتَسَلَ TAHHARA طَهَّرَ ITTAHARA اِطَّهَرَ
27.1 GHASALA  :meaning to wash something and remove it's dirt and stain/uncleanliness. said in the QURAN
Surat Al-Mā'idah (The Table Spread) - سورة المائدة
5:6
يَا أَيُّهَا الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا إِذَا قُمْتُمْ إِلَى الصَّلَاةِ فَاغْسِلُوا وُجُوهَكُمْ وَأَيْدِيَكُمْ إِلَى الْمَرَافِقِ وَامْسَحُوا بِرُءُوسِكُمْ وَأَرْجُلَكُمْ إِلَى الْكَعْبَيْنِ ۚ وَإِن كُنتُمْ جُنُبًا فَاطَّهَّرُوا ۚ وَإِن كُنتُم مَّرْضَىٰ أَوْ عَلَىٰ سَفَرٍ أَوْ جَاءَ أَحَدٌ مِّنكُم مِّنَ الْغَائِطِ أَوْ لَامَسْتُمُ النِّسَاءَ فَلَمْ تَجِدُوا مَاءً فَتَيَمَّمُوا صَعِيدًا طَيِّبًا فَامْسَحُوا بِوُجُوهِكُمْ وَأَيْدِيكُم مِّنْهُ ۚ مَا يُرِيدُ اللَّهُ لِيَجْعَلَ عَلَيْكُم مِّنْ حَرَجٍ وَلَٰكِن يُرِيدُ لِيُطَهِّرَكُمْ وَلِيُتِمَّ نِعْمَتَهُ عَلَيْكُمْ لَعَلَّكُمْ تَشْكُرُونَ
O you who have believed, when you rise to [perform] prayer, wash your faces and your forearms to the elbows and wipe over your heads and wash your feet to the ankles. And if you are in a state of janabah, then purify yourselves. But if you are ill or on a journey or one of you comes from the place of relieving himself or you have contacted women and do not find water, then seek clean earth and wipe over your faces and hands with it. Allah does not intend to make difficulty for you, but He intends to purify you and complete His favor upon you that you may be grateful.
and IGHTASALA meaning to clean entire body of dirt and uncleanliness or to bath. said in the QURAN
Surat An-Nisā' (The Women) - سورة النساء
4:43
يَا أَيُّهَا الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا لَا تَقْرَبُوا الصَّلَاةَ وَأَنتُمْ سُكَارَىٰ حَتَّىٰ تَعْلَمُوا مَا تَقُولُونَ وَلَا جُنُبًا إِلَّا عَابِرِي سَبِيلٍ حَتَّىٰ تَغْتَسِلُوا ۚ وَإِن كُنتُم مَّرْضَىٰ أَوْ عَلَىٰ سَفَرٍ أَوْ جَاءَ أَحَدٌ مِّنكُم مِّنَ الْغَائِطِ أَوْ لَامَسْتُمُ النِّسَاءَ فَلَمْ تَجِدُوا مَاءً فَتَيَمَّمُوا صَعِيدًا طَيِّبًا فَامْسَحُوا بِوُجُوهِكُمْ وَأَيْدِيكُمْ ۗ إِنَّ اللَّهَ كَانَ عَفُوًّا غَفُورًا
O you who have believed, do not approach prayer while you are intoxicated until you know what you are saying or in a state of janabah, except those passing through [a place of prayer], until you have washed [your whole body]. And if you are ill or on a journey or one of you comes from the place of relieving himself or you have contacted women and find no water, then seek clean earth and wipe over your faces and your hands [with it]. Indeed, Allah is ever Pardoning and Forgiving.
27.2 TAHHARA  :TAHARAT's طَهَرَتْ antonym is TAMACAT طَمَثَتْ meaning women having menstruation.and TAHARAT meaning after menstruation to purify by bathing.and word TAHHARA is of wider context in usage than GHASALA .TAHARAT is on three methods.TAHARAT ZAHIRY,HUKMIY and QALBI[Physical Purity,Commanded Purity and Purity of Heart].take it's example as that if there occurs slight droplet of urine on a cloth then it doesn't become dirty but does become impure. said in the QURAN
Surat Al-Muddaththir (The Cloaked One) - سورة المدثر
74:4
وَثِيَابَكَ فَطَهِّرْ
And your clothing purify
so TAHHARA refers to cleaning clothes from dirth and uncleanliness as well to purify of it impurities. and this is also the difference between ITTAHARA(bathing) and IGHTASALA(bathing). as well.
Summary:
GHASALA and IGHTASALA used for removing dirt and stain or cleanliness only whereas TAHHARA and ITTAHARA is used in addition to removing dirt and stain or uncleanliness also to remove impurities

title: content/n/n28.html
raw_text:
La - Not
Various words have been used in the Quran for this.
1- Laesa
It is used in a similar way as “not” is used in English.
2- La, Lum, Lun
'La', whenever used with a verb makes it negative as in 'La Yaddrib', translated as 'he does not hit' or 'he will not hit'. If, however, 'Lum' is used, it depicts past tense as well as making it negative, for example, 'Lum yaddrib' means 'he did not hit'. 'Lun', however, changes it to future and is furthur used to strengthen the negation, for example, 'Lun yaddriba' means, 'he (definitely) won't hit'.
3- Inna, Maa, Hul
These are 3 words that have different meanings of their own but if 'Illa' follows any of these, it changes their meanings to 'no' or 'not'. For example, 'In antum illa takzibun' translated as, 'You are not but liars', meaning you like to tell lies. Similarly, 'Ma min ilaahin il Allah' meaning, there is no diety except Allah. 'Hal kuntu illa basharan rasoolan' meaning, I am not but a messenger.
For 'no' or 'not', the following are regularly used, La, Lamma, Bala, Kalla, Innama, Ma and Laat.
a- La
La is used frequently to change an affirmative statement to negative and to joing statements together.
“  And the disbeliever had not believed, nor had he prayed  ” 75:31
b- Kama
Kama is commonly used to negate an incident in the past. It carries the meaning of 'yet' in English.
“  Do you think that you will be left [as you are] while Allah has not yet made evident those among you who strive” 9:16
c- Bala
When the question is in negative and the answer is in affirmative but it rectifies the negation in the question, then Bala is used as in 'why not'.
“  Am I not your Lord?" They said, "Yes, why not [we have testified]” 7:172
d- Kalla
It means never or something that is ever impossible. It is used to serve caution and to negate the last statement.
“  About what are they asking one another? About the great news - That over which they are in disagreement. No! They are going to know. Then, no! They are going to know” 78:1-5
e- Inni
Inni means 'other than', for example
“  Say, "I am only a man like you [other than], to whom has been revealed ” 18:110
f- Ma
It is used in various ways. When there is a claim in a statement, it negates it and so is called Ma of negation.
“  Perfect is Allah ! This is not a man; this is none but a noble angel ” 12:31
g- Lat
It is used in the same meaning as Laesa and is of Yemini origin.
“  And they [then] called out; but it was not a time for escape” 38:3
It means that they started calling out for forgiveness when it was not the time for forgiveness.

La - Not

Various words have been used in the Quran for this.

1- Laesa

It is used in a similar way as “not” is used in English.

2- La, Lum, Lun

'La', whenever used with a verb makes it negative as in 'La Yaddrib', translated as 'he does not hit' or 'he will not hit'. If, however, 'Lum' is used, it depicts past tense as well as making it negative, for example, 'Lum yaddrib' means 'he did not hit'. 'Lun', however, changes it to future and is furthur used to strengthen the negation, for example, 'Lun yaddriba' means, 'he (definitely) won't hit'.

3- Inna, Maa, Hul

These are 3 words that have different meanings of their own but if 'Illa' follows any of these, it changes their meanings to 'no' or 'not'. For example, 'In antum illa takzibun' translated as, 'You are not but liars', meaning you like to tell lies. Similarly, 'Ma min ilaahin il Allah' meaning, there is no diety except Allah. <<PARTIAL ENTRY>>
Page 865
29.2 JADD (جَدّ):   JADEED (جدید) means a new thing. The word JADDA (جَدَّ)  refers to many meanings. 1. To be a dignified man. 2. To be fortunate or lucky. 3. New. When it refers to something being new then it means something that has a counterpart and the thing is useable. And after the use it becomes old, ragged and useless. For instance a new dress. Allah says in the Quran
Surah Qaf (Qaf): سُوۡرَةُ قٓ 50:15
بَلْ هُمْ فِي لَبْسٍ مِّنْ خَلْقٍ جَدِيدٍ
But they are in confusion over a new creation.
29.3: BADAA’ (بَدَعَ):   Means 1. To initiate something or use it for the first time 2. Something that has no example or counterpart before it. Due to this aspect the name of Allah is BADEE’ (بَدِیع) which means the originator. And BID’AN (بِدْعًا) means someone who introduces  a process of thing. Allah says in the Quran
Surah Al-Ahqaf (The Dunes) - سورة الأحقاف 46:9
قُلْ مَا كُنتُ بِدْعًا مِّنَ الرُّسُلِ
Say (O Muhammad SAW):"I am not a new thing among the Messengers (of Allah)
Summary:
29.1 HADATHA: A new thing coming in existence which is previously non-existent. All creations can be called HAADITH.
29.2 JADEED: Something that is new and has a counterpart.
29.3 BID’AN: The very first item of its counterparts.

3 NA-PASANDEEDA [Disliked, Undesirable]
Synonyms: MAKRUH, IDD, MUNKIR, IMR, MAZMOOM, UFF
3.1 MAKRUH (مَکْرُوْہ):   KARIHA (کَرِہَ) means to dislike something; MAKRUH (مَکْرُوْہ) is anything that is displeasing to temperament. And one gets offended by it. Allah says in the Quran
Surah Al-Hujraat (The Inner Apartments): سُوۡرَةُ الحُجرَات 49:12
أَيُحِبُّ أَحَدُكُمْ أَن يَأْكُلَ لَحْمَ أَخِيهِ مَيْتًا فَكَرِهْتُمُوهُ
Would one of you like to eat the flesh of his brother when dead? You would detest it.
Also there are some things that seem displeasing but actually they are due to some cause. These things are also stated in Shariah. For instance
Surah Al-Baqarah (The cow): سورۃ البَقَرَۃ  2:216
كُتِبَ عَلَيْكُمُ الْقِتَالُ وَهُوَ كُرْهٌ لَّكُمْ ۖ وَعَسَىٰ أَن تَكْرَهُوا شَيْئًا وَهُوَ خَيْرٌ لَّكُمْ
Fighting is ordained for you, even though you dislike it. But it may be that you dislike something while it is good for you,
Thus MAKRUH (مَکْرُوْہ) is something that is undesirable both to mind and Shariah. In the Quran
Surah Al-Isra (The Night Journey): سُوۡرَةُ الإسرَاء 17:38
كُلُّ ذَٰلِكَ كَانَ سَيِّئُهُ عِندَ رَبِّكَ مَكْرُوهًا
The evil of all these is disliked by your Lord.
3.2 IDD (اِدَّ):   Means an extremely displeasing thing that raises uproar. ADEED (اَدِیْد) means racket, turbulence. And ADD-ALAMAR (اَدّ الامر) means a task being strenuous and difficult. ADEED means racket. IDD (اِدّ) means a difficulty, a horrific event. A difficult task (dictionary al Manjad). A displeasing thing that causes a turbulence or upheaval. Allah says in the Quran
Surah Maryam (Mary): سُوۡرَةُ مَریَم 19:88-89
وَقَالُوا اتَّخَذَ الرَّحْمَٰنُ وَلَدًا لَّقَدْ جِئْتُمْ شَيْئًا إِدًّا
And they say, “The Most Merciful has begotten a son.”  You have come up with something monstrous.
3.3 MUNKIR (منکر):   Any uncommon or surprising thing. (Opposite of INKAAR [denial] is ARFAAN (عرفان); opposite of MUNKIR (منکر) is MAROOF (معروف)) Thus MUNKIR (منکر) is that thing that is rendered nefarious by society. Allah says in the Quran
Surah Ale- Imran (The family of Imran): سورۃ آل عِمْرن 3:104
وَلْتَكُن مِّنكُمْ أُمَّةٌ يَدْعُونَ إِلَى الْخَيْرِ وَيَأْمُرُونَ بِالْمَعْرُوفِ وَيَنْهَوْنَ عَنِ الْمُنكَرِ
And let there be [arising] from you a nation inviting to [all that is] good, enjoining what is right and forbidding what is wrong, and those will be the successful.
Page 837
But Shairah has not limited the MUNKIRAT (منکرات) to social dislikes but also if something obscene is famous in a society and is not considered wicked by the society, such things are also corrected by the Shariah. Allah says in the Quran
Surah Al-Ankaboot  (The Spider): سُوۡرَةُ العَنکبوت 29:29
وَتَأْتُونَ فِي نَادِيكُمُ الْمُنكَرَ
And practise Al-Munkar (disbelief and polytheism and every kind of evil wicked deed) in your meetings.
3.4 IMR (اِمْر):   Anything that is against the mind and the Shariah (dictionary al Manjad). Meaning MUNKIRAN-AZEEMA. AMIR-AL-AMR (اِمِرَ الْاَمْر) means to break all the limits in a matter. Extremely irrational thing. Allah says in the Quran
Surah Al-Kahf (The Cave): سورۃ الکھف 18:71
قَالَ أَخَرَقْتَهَا لِتُغْرِقَ أَهْلَهَا لَقَدْ جِئْتَ شَيْئًا إِمْرًا
[Moses] said, "Have you torn it open to drown its people? You have certainly done a grave thing."
3.5 MADMOOM (مَذْمُوْم) and MAD’OOM (مَذْءُوْم):   DAMMA (ذَمَّ), and DA’AMA (ذَءَمَ) both means to refer to something as little or disdain it. DA’AMA (ذَءَمَ) has two basic things 1. Repulsion 2. Flaw. Means to put a flaw, to disdain, to defame. DAMMA (ذَمَّ)  (Opposite HAMADA (حَمَدَ), MADAHA (مَدَحَ)) means to report someone’s flaws regardless of them being deliberate or based on reflexes (dictionary al Manjad). Allah says in the Quran
Surah Al-Araf (The heights): سورۃ الأعرَاف 7:18
قَالَ اخْرُجْ مِنْهَا مَذْءُومًا مَّدْحُورًا
(Allah) said (to Iblis) "Get out from this (Paradise) disgraced and expelled.
3.6 UFF (اُفّ):   All the filthy and disliked things like grime, scraps of nails etc. But metaphorically it refers to expressing dislike for a bad thing. In the Quran
Surah Al-Anbiya (the prophets): سورۃ الانَبیاء 21:67
أُفٍّ لَّكُمْ وَلِمَا تَعْبُدُونَ مِن دُونِ اللَّهِ
Uff to you and to what you worship instead of Allah . Then will you not use reason?"
Summary:
3.1 MAKRUH: Things that are disliked by nature.
3.2 IDD: An extremely displeasing thing that causes uproar.
3.3 MUNKIR: Anything rendered nefarious by society.
3.4 IMR: Extremely irrational thing.
3.5 MAZMOOM: To dislike due to some flaw.
3.6 UFF: Word to express dislike.

30 NEECHAY [Below, lower]
Synonyms: THAT, ASFAL
30.1 THAT (تَحْت):   THAT (تَحْت) is a noun of place and its opposite is FAUQ (فوق) which means up. Both used materially and figuratively. Allah says in the Quran
Surah Al-Maeda (The table spread): سورۃ المَائدہ 5:66
وَلَوْ أَنَّهُمْ أَقَامُوا التَّوْرَاةَ وَالْإِنجِيلَ وَمَا أُنزِلَ إِلَيْهِم مِّن رَّبِّهِمْ لَأَكَلُوا مِن فَوْقِهِمْ وَمِن تَحْتِ أَرْجُلِهِم
And if only they upheld [the law of] the Torah, the Gospel, and what has been revealed to them from their Lord, they would have consumed [provision] from above them and from beneath their feet.
30.2 ASFAL (اَسْفَل):   Means the lower one (Opposite A’LAA (اعلٰی)). This word is used in two ways 1. The upper part of a thing is called A’LAA (اعلٰی) and its lower part is called ASFAL (اَسْفَل). For instance ASFALAHU-AGHLAZU-MIN-AA’LAHU (اَسْفَلہُ اَغْلَظُ مِنْ اَعْلَاُہ) means the lower part is harder than the upper part.
For highness in status and honor the word A’LAA (اَعْلٰی) is used and for dishonor and inferiority the word ASFALA (اَسْفَل)  (Feminine SUFLA (سُفُلٰی)). Prophet Muhammad (S.A.A.W) said “الْيَدُ الْعُلْيَا خَيْرٌ مِنَ الْيَدِ السُّفْلَى” means ‘The upper hand is better than the lower hand’. In this Hadeeth the word ULIA (عُلْيَا) and SUFLA (سُفْلَى) are used figuratively which means the one who gives charity and the ones who receive it. In the Quran
Surah Al Tawbah (The repentance): سورۃ التوبھ 9:40
وَجَعَلَ كَلِمَةَ الَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا السُّفْلَىٰ ۗ وَكَلِمَةُ اللَّهِ هِيَ الْعُلْيَا
and made the word of those who disbelieved the lowest, while the Word of God is the Highest.
SAFIL (سَافِل) means to be inferior in honor and status. ASSIFLAH (اَسِفْلَۃ) means scurvy people. Allah says in Quran
Page 866
Surah At-Teen (The Fig) - سورة التين 95:4-5
لَقَدْ خَلَقْنَا الْإِنسَانَ فِي أَحْسَنِ تَقْوِيمٍ  ثُمَّ رَدَدْنَاهُ أَسْفَلَ سَافِلِينَ
We created man in the best design. Then reduced him to the lowest of the low.
Summary:
30.1 THAT: Below. Noun of place.
30.2 ASFAL: The lower part of something. To be low in honor. Lower; Inferior.

Prophet Muhammad (S.A.A.W) said “الْيَدُ الْعُلْيَا خَيْرٌ مِنَ الْيَدِ السُّفْلَى” means ‘The upper hand is better than the lower hand’. In this Hadeeth the word ULIA (عُلْيَا) and SUFLA (سُفْلَى) are used figuratively which means the one who gives charity and the ones who receive it. In the Quran

Surah Al Tawbah (The repentance): سورۃ التوبھ 9:40

وَجَعَلَ كَلِمَةَ الَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا السُّفْلَىٰ ۗ وَكَلِمَةُ اللَّهِ هِيَ الْعُلْيَا

and made the word of those who disbelieved the lowest, while the Word of God is the Highest.

SAFIL (سَافِل) means to be inferior in honor and status. ASSIFLAH (اَسِفْلَۃ) means scurvy people. Allah says in Quran

Page 866

Surah At-Teen (The Fig) - سورة التين 95:4-5

لَقَدْ خَلَقْنَا الْإِنسَانَ فِي أَحْسَنِ تَقْوِيمٍ  ثُمَّ رَدَدْنَاهُ أَسْفَلَ سَافِلِينَ

We created man in the best design. Then reduced him to the lowest of the low.

Summary:

30.1 THAT: Below. Noun of place.

30.2 ASFAL: The lower part of something. To be low in honor. Lower; Inferior.
