raw_text:
31. NEECHAY KERNA – RAKHNA, PAST KERNA [to lower]
Synonyms: KHAFADA, GHADDA, QASARA, KHASHAA’
31.1 KHAFADA (خَفَضَ):   Means to lower, to kneel (Opposite RAFAA’ (رفع)). KHAFID (خافِض) and RAFIAA’ (رافِع) both are the names of Allah. KHAFID (خافِض) means the lowerer and RAFIAA (رافِع) means the exalter. KHAFADA-AS-SAUT (خَفَضَ الصَّوت) means he lowered the voice.  KHAFAD-AL-JANAH (خَفَضَ الجناج) means to lower the arm. Allah says in the Quran
Surah Al-Isra (The Night Journey): سُوۡرَةُ الإسرَاء 17:24
وَاخْفِضْ لَهُمَا جَنَاحَ الذُّلِّ مِنَ الرَّحْمَةِ
And lower to them the wing of humility out of mercy
31.2 GHADDA (غَضَّ):   Means to lower gaze or voice, GHADDA-SAUTA (غَضَ الصَوْتُہُ) means he lowered the voice. GHADDA-BASARA (غَضَّ بَصَرُہُ) means he lowered his gaze or removed his gaze from an illicit thing. Allah says in the Quran
Surah Al-Noor (The light): سورۃ النور 24:31
وَقُل لِّلْمُؤْمِنَاتِ يَغْضُضْنَ مِنْ أَبْصَارِهِنَّ
And tell the believing women to lower their gaze (from looking at forbidden things),
In another place in Quran
Surah Luqman (Luqman): سُوۡرَةُ لقمَان 31:19
وَاقْصِدْ فِي مَشْيِكَ وَاغْضُضْ مِن صَوْتِكَ
And be moderate in your pace and lower your voice
31.3 QASARA (قَصَر):   To be unable to reach the length and end of something, to lessen, to shorten, to perform lesser than the required task. Like SALATUL-QASAR (الصَلٰوۃُ القَصْر), QASUR-RUT-TARF (قَصَرُ الطَّرْف) means to restrain the gaze and not use it to the total extent of sight. In this meaning it is specific for sight. In the Quran
Surah As-Saaffat (The Aligners): سُوۡرَةُ الصَّافات37:48
وَعِندَهُمْ قَاصِرَاتُ الطَّرْفِ عِينٌ
And with them will be women limiting [their] glances, with large, [beautiful] eyes,
Page 867
31.4  KHASHAA’ (خَشَعَ):   KHASHAA’ (خَشَعَ) is a fear which affects emotions. Such effects can also be visible in eyes, voice and expressions. Thus for lowering them in fear this word is used. For lowering voice and eyes the word GHADDA (غَضَّ) is also used but the difference is that when the reason is due to fear then KHASHAA’ (خَشَعَ). Allah says in the Quran
For sight:
Surah Al-Maarij (The Ascending Stairs): سُوۡرَةُ المعَارج 70:44
خَاشِعَةً أَبْصَارُهُمْ تَرْهَقُهُمْ ذِلَّةٌ
Their eyes cast down; overwhelmed by humiliation.
For voice:
Surah Ta-Ha (Ta-ha): سورۃ طٰھٰ  20:108
وَخَشَعَتِ الْأَصْوَاتُ لِلرَّحْمَٰنِ
Voices will be hushed before the Merciful,
For face:
Surah Al-Ghashiya (The overwhelming): سُوۡرَةُ الغَاشِیَة 88:2
وُجُوهٌ يَوْمَئِذٍ خَاشِعَةٌ
(Some) faces on that day shall be downcast,
Summary:
31.1 KHAFADA: To get pressed or press. To lower gaze.
31.2 GHADDA: Lowering of sight and voice.
31.3 QASARA: To limit ones’ gaze. To not use full sight.
31.4 KHASHAA’:  To lower eyes, voice or face due to fear.

32 NAIK – NAIK BAKHT [Pious, Fortunate]
Synonyms: SALEH, ABRAR, BARARAH, RASHEED, SAEED, MUTTAQEEN, RABBANI.
32.1 SALEH (صَالِح):   SALAH (صَلَح) means to rectify a problem; its opposite is FASADA (فَسَدَ) ۔SALEH (صالح) means one who polishes himself. One who rectifies his soul. One who takes up virtue and leaves the vice and is working in rectifying himself. In the Quran
Surah Al-Kahf (The Cave): سورۃ الکھف 18:82
وَكَانَ أَبُوهُمَا صَالِحًا
and their father had been righteous.
In another place in the Quran
Surah Al-Araf (The heights): سورۃ الأعرَاف 7:56
وَلَا تُفْسِدُوا فِي الْأَرْضِ بَعْدَ إِصْلَاحِهَا
And cause not corruption upon the earth after its reformation
32.2 ABRAR (ابْرَار):   (Singular BAR (بار)) BIRR (بِرّ) means to do good deeds on a large scale, BIRR (بِرّ) is not Virtue but quality to always be indulged in doing virtuous acts. (Opposite ITHM) Allah says in the Quran
Surah Ale- Imran (The family of Imran): سورۃ آل عِمْرن 3:92
لَن تَنَالُوا الْبِرَّ حَتَّىٰ تُنفِقُوا مِمَّا تُحِبُّونَ
You will not attain virtuous conduct until you give of what you cherish.
Page 868
BIRRA (بِرَّ) and BARR (بَارّ) is that person who is always ready to do good deeds. And when given a chance he does it. HAJJ-E-MABROORAS (حج مبروراس) is that Hajj which is done correctly according to the sunnah of Prophet Muhammad (S.A.A.W). And no mistake is made while doing it. In the Quran
Surah Maryam (Mary): سُوۡرَةُ مَریَم 19:14
وَبَرًّا بِوَالِدَيْهِ وَلَمْ يَكُن جَبَّارًا عَصِيًّا
And dutiful towards his parents, and he was neither an arrogant nor disobedient (to Allah or to his parents).
32.3 BARARA (بَرَرَةٌ): Plural of BARRA (بَرَّ) and is more prolific then BAARR (بَارّ), and has more exaggeration in it. In the Quran
Surah Abasa (He frowned): سورۃعَبَسَ 80:15-16
بِأَيْدِي سَفَرَةٍكِرَامٍ بَرَرَةٍ
(Written) by the hands of scribes- Honourable and Pious and Just.
32.4 RASHEED (رَشِیْد):   RUSHD (رُشْد) means a straight path. To walk on the right path or keep following a straight road. And its opposite is GHAEE (غَیّ). Means to take up a wrong path. Allah says in the Quran
Surah Al-Baqarah (The cow): سورۃ البَقَرَۃ  2:256
قَد تَّبَيَّنَ الرُّشْدُ مِنَ الْغَيِّ
Verily, the Right Path has become distinct from the wrong path.
And RASHEED (رَشِیْد) means one who is virtuous who has good habits and ways. A pious and reasonable person. In the Quran
Surah Hud (Hud): سورۃ ھود 11:78
فَاتَّقُوا اللَّهَ وَلَا تُخْزُونِ فِي ضَيْفِي ۖ أَلَيْسَ مِنكُمْ رَجُلٌ رَّشِيدٌ
So fear God, and do not embarrass me before my guests. Is there not one reasonable man among you?”
32.5 SAEED (سَعِیْد):   A person who is pious by nature. A prosperous person and its opposite is SHAQEE (شَقِیّ) which means an unfortunate person. SA’ADA (سَعَدَ) means good luck. And God’s help by creating appropriate conditions for doing virtue. Allah says in the Quran
Surah Hud (Hud): سورۃ ھود 11:105
يَوْمَ يَأْتِ لَا تَكَلَّمُ نَفْسٌ إِلَّا بِإِذْنِهِ ۚ فَمِنْهُمْ شَقِيٌّ وَسَعِيدٌ
The Day it comes no soul will speak except by His permission. And among them will be the wretched and the prosperous.
32.6 MUTTAQEEN (مُتَّقِیْنَ) or MUTTAQOON (مُتَّقُونَ):   (Singular MUTTAQI (متقی)) WAQQA (وَقٰی) means to save something from a dangerous thing and ITTAQAA (اِتَّقٰی) - TAQWAA (تقوٰی) (Opposite UDWAAN (عدوان)) means to abstain from evil deeds due to fear of God and his wrath. MUTAAQI (مُتَّقِیْ) means a God fearing and continent person, who restrains from forbidden things because of the fear of Allah   (dictionary al Manjad)  . In the Quran
Surah Al-Baqarah (The cow): سورۃ البَقَرَۃ  2:177
ۗ أُولَٰئِكَ الَّذِينَ صَدَقُوا ۖ وَأُولَٰئِكَ هُمُ الْمُتَّقُونَ
These are the sincere; these are the pious.
Page 869
32.7  RABBANI (رَبَّانِی):   This word is heavily debated by Imam Raghib. According to some scholars it means those who nurtures of knowledge.  Some relate it to the word RABB (رَبّ) as JISMANI (جِسْمَانِیٌّ) is related to JISM (جِسْمٌ) similarly RABBANI is related to RABB means a person devoted to Allah only. A Muslim monk.  According to manjad it means both a great scholar and a person devoted to Allah or a pious person. The second meaning seems more correct because in the Quran the word AHBAAR أَحْبَار     (Scholar) comes separately with RABBANIYOON وَالرَّبَّانِيُّونَ  (5:44). And also the word RIBBIYYOON رِبِّيُّونَ is also used in Quran with same meaning (3:146). Allah says in the Quran
Surah Al-Maeda (The table spread): سورۃ المَائدہ 5:63
لَوْلَا يَنْهَاهُمُ الرَّبَّانِيُّونَ وَالْأَحْبَارُ عَن قَوْلِهِمُ الْإِثْمَ وَأَكْلِهِمُ السُّحْتَ
Why do the rabbis and religious scholars not forbid them from saying what is sinful and devouring what is unlawful
Summary:
32.1 SALEH: One who rectifies himself. And also every kind of vice.
32.2 ABRAR: (BAR) One who is always ready to do good deeds. One who does a lot of good deeds.
32.3 BARARAH: (BARR) more exaggerated then BAR.
32.4 RASHEED: One with good habits and ways, pious.
32.5 SAEED: Pious by nature. Fortunate.
32.6 MUTTAQEEN: One who abstains from bad deeds due to fear of God, continent person.
32.7 RABBANI: A person devoted to Allah. A saint.

32.6 MUTTAQEEN: One who abstains from bad deeds due to fear of God, continent person.

32.7 RABBANI: A person devoted to Allah. A saint.

raw_text:
33 NAIKI-NAIK KAM [piety, Good deeds]
Synonyms: URF, MAAROOF, HASANAH, KHAIR, BIRR
33.1 URF (عُرف) and MAAROOF (مَعْرُوْف):   ARAFA (عَرَفَ) (Opposite NAKARA (نَکَرََ) something being surprising) means to recognize something. MAAROOF (معروف) and URF (عرف) are those things that are considered good in a society. And is a good custom of a society. Ways of good people. National custom that is liked. For instance to sit politely and respectfully in front of the elders and address them politely. Allah says in the Quran
Surah Al-Araf (The heights): سورۃ الأعرَاف 7:199
خُذِ الْعَفْوَ وَأْمُرْ بِالْعُرْفِ وَأَعْرِضْ عَنِ الْجَاهِلِينَ
In another place in Holy Quran
Surah Ale- Imran (The family of Imran): سورۃ آل عِمْرن 3:1  04
وَلْتَكُن مِّنكُمْ أُمَّةٌ يَدْعُونَ إِلَى الْخَيْرِ وَيَأْمُرُونَ بِالْمَعْرُوفِ وَيَنْهَوْنَ عَنِ الْمُنكَرِ
And let there be among you a community calling to virtue, and advocating righteousness, and deterring from evil.
Page 870
33.3 HASANAH (حَسَنَةٌ):   (Plural HASNAAT (حَسَنَات)) Any pleasing and liked thing that is in accordance with the mind and Shariah (Opposite SAYYIAH (سَیِّئَةً) (Plural SAYYIAT (سیّئات))).  Allah says in the Quran
Surah Hud (Hud): سورۃ ھود 11:114
إِنَّ الْحَسَنَاتِ يُذْهِبْنَ السَّيِّئَاتِ
The good deeds take away the bad deeds.
33.4 KHAIR (خَیْر):   (Plural KHAIRAAT (خیرات)) (Opposite SHARR (شرّ)) Means a virtue at its best. A thing from which everyone can benefit from. Greater virtues. Good deeds done at a larger scale. KHAIR (خَیْر) also refers to those things with which everyone is pleased. For instance arranging drinking water for travelers. Allah says in the Quran
Surah Ale- Imran (The family of Imran): سورۃ آل عِمْرن 3:1  14
وَيَأْمُرُونَ بِالْمَعْرُوفِ وَيَنْهَوْنَ عَنِ الْمُنكَرِ وَيُسَارِعُونَ فِي الْخَيْرَاتِ
and advocate righteousness and forbid evil, and are quick to do good deeds.
33.5 BIRR (بِرّ):   Always having a temperament to do piety and when given a chance do it (Opposite ITHM (اثم)). For Detail see NAIK BAKHT [fortunate] above. Allah says in the Quran
Surah Al-Maeda (The table spread): سورۃ المَائدہ 5:2
وَتَعَاوَنُوا عَلَى الْبِرِّ وَالتَّقْوَىٰ ۖ وَلَا تَعَاوَنُوا عَلَى الْإِثْمِ وَالْعُدْوَانِ
And cooperate in righteousness and piety, but do not cooperate in sin and aggression.
Summary:
33.1 URF and MAAROOF: Good customs of society. Good deeds.
33.2 HASANAH: An action in accordance  with mind and Shariah rules.
33.3 KHAIR: Any work that is liked by all. Everyone benefits from it.
33.4 BIRR: Always having a temperament for a virtue.
For AHSANA, ANAMA see IHSAAN KERNA [to do a favour]

raw_text:
4 NAADAN [foolish, unintelligent]
Synonyms: JAHIL, SUFAHAA’
Page 838
4.1JAHIL (جَاھِل):   (Opposite AALIM (عالم)) lacking knowledge, unknown. JAHALA (جَاھِل) means a mind of a person being empty of knowledge regardless of the reason. A very common word. In the Quran
Surah Al-Baqarah (The cow): سورۃ البَقَرَۃ  2:273
يَحْسَبُهُمُ الْجَاهِلُ أَغْنِيَاءَ مِنَ التَّعَفُّفِ
An ignorant [person] would think them self-sufficient because of their restraint,
4.2 SUFAHAA’ (سُفَھَاء):   (Singular SAFEEHA (سَفِیْھَه)) (Opposite of SAFAH (سفھ) is HILM (حِلم)) means 1. Half witted and 2. A person with low morals. And SAFEEHA (سَفِیْھَه) refers to an unintelligent person who cannot attain any skill or knowledge due to his dumbness and also has low moral values. And argues without knowing or understanding anything. Foolish. Allah says in the Quran
Surah Al-Baqarah (The cow): سورۃ البَقَرَۃ  2:142
سَيَقُولُ السُّفَهَاءُ مِنَ النَّاسِ مَا وَلَّاهُمْ عَن قِبْلَتِهِمُ الَّتِي كَانُوا عَلَيْهَا
The foolish among the people will say, "What has turned them away from their qiblah, which they used to face
For NARAZ KERNA [To Annoy] See GHUSSA DILANA [to cause anger]

title: content/n/n5.html
raw_text:
5 NARAZGI [umbrage, resentfulness]
Synonyms: SAKHATA, DIGHAN, GHILL
5.1 SAKHATA (سَخَط):   Means displeasure, Unwillingness. (Opposite RIZWAN (رضوان) meaning willingness and SAKHATA (سَخَط) means to be displeased about something done against ones will. To be offended. Allah says in the Quran
Surah Al Tawbah (The repentance): سورۃ التوبھ 9:58
فَإِنْ أُعْطُوا مِنْهَا رَضُوا وَإِن لَّمْ يُعْطَوْا مِنْهَا إِذَا هُمْ يَسْخَطُونَ
If they are given some of it, they become pleased; but if they are not given any, they grow resentful.
5.2 DIGHAN (ضِغْن):   Means despise and malice. Resentfulness that stays in heart. Allah says in the Quran
Surah Muhammad (Muhammad): سُوۡرَةُ محَمَّد 47:29
أَمْ حَسِبَ الَّذِينَ فِي قُلُوبِهِم مَّرَضٌ أَن لَّن يُخْرِجَ اللَّهُ أَضْغَانَهُمْ
Do those in whose hearts is sickness think that God will not expose their malice?
5.3 GHILL (غِلّ):   Means vindictiveness, hidden enmity. And GHALLA (غَلَّ) means to steal, and defalcation. To secretly put something in one’s own things. GHILL (غِلّ) is despise and defaced (dictionary al Manjad). Allah says in the Quran.
Surah Al-Araf (The heights): سورۃ الأعرَاف 7:43
وَنَزَعْنَا مَا فِي صُدُورِهِم مِّنْ غِلٍّ
And We will have removed whatever is within their breasts of resentment,
Summary:
5.1 SAKHATA: Resentfulness.
5.2 DIGHAN: Resentfulness that is hidden in heart.
5.3 GHILL: Resentfulness to the extent of enmity and is hidden in heart.

title: content/n/n6.html
raw_text:
Page 839
6 NASHUKRA [ungrateful]
Synonyms: KAFOOR, KANOOD
6.1 KAFOOR (کَفُوْر):   KAFARA (کَفَرَ) means 1. Someone who does not acknowledge Allah. 2. Someone who denies the gifts of Allah. To be thankless. For the one who denies Allah is the word KAAFIR (کَافِر) and for the one who denies his bounties the word KAFOOR (کَفُوْر) or KAFFAR (کَفَّار) word is used. (Opposite SHAAKIR (شاکِر), SHAKOOR (شَکُوْر)). Allah says in the Quran
Surah Al-Insan (The Man) - سورة الانسان 76:3
إِنَّا هَدَيْنَاهُ السَّبِيلَ إِمَّا شَاكِرًا وَإِمَّا كَفُورًا
Indeed, We guided him to the way, be he grateful or be he ungrateful.
6.2 KANOOD (کَنُوْد):   KANADA (کَنَدَ) means to be thankless. KANOOD (کَنُوْد) refers to that ungrateful person who is always mentioning the problems and troubles but has no regard for the bounties of Allah. Ungrateful; Renegade. Allah says in the Quran
Surah Al-Adiyat (The Chargers): سُوۡرَةُ العَادیَات 100:6
إِنَّ الْإِنسَانَ لِرَبِّهِ لَكَنُودٌ
Indeed mankind, to his Lord, is ungrateful.
Summary:
6.1 KAFOOR: Ungrateful.
6.2 KANOOD: Ungrateful and querulous.

title: content/n/n7.html
raw_text:
7 NA FARMANI [Disobedience]
Synonyms: A’SAA, FASAQA, FAJARA
7.1 A’SAA (عَصٰی):   Means to disobey an order, to disobey (dictionary al Manjad). To not execute a virtuous task. This can be deliberate or accidental. وَالْعِصْيَانَ  (49:7) means rebellion .  AASI (عَاصِی) means one who disobeys. ESIYYAN (16:44) means extremely disobedient. In the Quran
Surah Ta-Ha (Ta-ha): سورۃ طٰھٰ  20:121
وَعَصَىٰ آدَمُ رَبَّهُ فَغَوَىٰ
Thus Adam disobeyed his Lord, and fell.
7.2  FASAQA (فَسَقَ):   Means to abandon the path of righteous and virtue. Vicious; (dictionary al Manjad). FASIQ (فَاسِق) is a habitual disobeyer. And FISQ (فسق) refers to indulging in all little and bigger sinful activities. To not take care of religious bounds. But this sort of person renders sinful activities as bad. Allah says in the Quran
Surah As-Sajda (The prostration): سُوۡرَةُ السَّجدَة 32:18
أَفَمَن كَانَ مُؤْمِنًا كَمَن كَانَ فَاسِقًا
Then is one who was a believer like one who was defiantly disobedient? They are not equal.
Page 840
7.3 FAJARA (فَجَرَ):   Means to tear apart something widely. FAAJIR (فَاجِر) is a person who betrays and disobeys religion. A vicious person. A person who keeps on committing sins and does not repent. An evildoer. FAJOOR (فجور) is a person engrossed in sins or fornicator. FAJARA (فَجَرَ)     means to be stubborn. FAJIR (فاجر) is that sinner who does not consider  committing sin as bad. Allah says in the Quran
Surah Nooh (Noah) - سورة نوح 71:27
إِنَّكَ إِن تَذَرْهُمْ يُضِلُّوا عِبَادَكَ وَلَا يَلِدُوا إِلَّا فَاجِرًا كَفَّارًا
Indeed, if You leave them, they will mislead Your servants and not beget except [every] wicked one and [confirmed] disbeliever.
Summary:
7.1 A’SAA: On who disobeys sometimes, deliberately or accidently.
7.2 FASAQA: One who is habitual in committing sin and does not ask for forgiveness but considers a sin as bad.
7.3 FAJARA: One who is habitual in committing sin and does not ask for forgiveness does not consider a sin as bad.
For NAQIS [defective] see RADDI [waste]

title: content/n/n8.html
raw_text:
8 NAAK [Nose]
Synonyms: ANF, KHURTOOM
8.1 ANF (اَنْف):   Means a nose, a famous body part. Nose is protruding body part so any part of something that is protruding is also called ANF (اَنْف), for instance ANF-AL-JABAL (انف الجبل) means the protruding part of mountain. In the Quran
Surah Al-Maeda (The table spread): سورۃ المَائدہ 5:45
وَالْعَيْنَ بِالْعَيْنِ وَالْأَنفَ بِالْأَنفِ
an eye for an eye, a nose for a nose,

raw_text:
9 NAAM – NAAM RAKHNA [name, to name]
Synonyms: ISM, SAMMA, LAQAB, NABAZA, FULAN
Page 841
9.1 ISM (اِسْم):   Means a name of something, SAMW (سمو) means loftiness. A noun is called ISM (اسم) because it is used to introduce something and it comes under discussion (Plural ISMAA (اسمإ)). Allah says in the Quran
Surah Al-Baqarah (The cow): سورۃ البَقَرَۃ  2:31
وَعَلَّمَ آدَمَ الْأَسْمَاءَ كُلَّهَا
And He taught Adam the names, all of them;
And SAMMA (سَمَّی) means to name someone or something. And while naming, taking in account the qualities of that person or thing is not necessary. In the Quran
Surah Al-Araf (The heights): سورۃ الأعرَاف 7:71
أَتُجَادِلُونَنِي فِي أَسْمَاءٍ سَمَّيْتُمُوهَا أَنتُمْ وَآبَاؤُكُم
Are you arguing with me over names, which you and your ancestors invented,
And SAMIYAN (سَمِیًّا) means a namesake. Allah says in the Quran
Surah Maryam (Mary): سُوۡرَةُ مَریَم 19:7
اسْمُهُ يَحْيَىٰ لَمْ نَجْعَل لَّهُ مِن قَبْلُ سَمِيًّا
His name will be Yahya (John). We have given that name to none before (him)."
9.2 LAQAB (لقب):   Apart from real name, this sort of name takes in account  the qualities of the named person. For instance MASEEH is the title of HAZRAT EESA (A.S) (Jesus) who spent his whole life in journey and travelling and never settled down into a married life. Allah says in the Quran
Surah Ale- Imran (The family of Imran): سورۃ آل عِمْرن 3:45
إِذْ قَالَتِ الْمَلَائِكَةُ يَا مَرْيَمُ إِنَّ اللَّهَ يُبَشِّرُكِ بِكَلِمَةٍ مِّنْهُ اسْمُهُ الْمَسِيحُ عِيسَى ابْنُ مَرْيَمَ
The Angels said, “O Mary, God gives you good news of a Word from Him. His name is the Messiah, Jesus, son of Mary,
In this Ayah, MASEEH (مسيح) is a LAQAB (لقب) and IBN-MARYAM (ابن مريم) (Son of Mary) is the lineage, which Allah has used with name of mother because he had no father.
9.3 NABAZA (نَبَزَ):   AN-NABZ (اَلنَّبْز) is also a type of LAQAB (لقب) (title), but it is used to represent the bad qualities of a person regardless of a person having them or not and these qualities can be related to bloodline or morals. NABAZA (نَبَزَ) means to name someone in offensive words or name calling (dictionary al Manjad). Allah says in the Quran
Surah Al-Hujraat (The Inner Apartments): سُوۡرَةُ الحُجرَات 49:11
وَلَا تَنَابَزُوا بِالْأَلْقَابِ
nor shall you insult one another with names.
9.4 FULAN (فُلَانٌ):   (Feminine FULANATUN (فُلَانَةٌ)) is a replacement to ISM (اسم). When used for all the intelligent things then this word can be preceded by  ‘AL’ (ال). For instance RAKABTU-FULANA‘رَکَبْتُ فُلَانَ’ means he rode so and so animal (male) and HALABTU-FULANATA ‘حَلَبْتُ فُلَانَةَ’ means he milked so and so animal (female). In the Quran
Surah Al-Furqaan (The criterion): سورۃ الفُرْقان 25:28
يَا وَيْلَتَىٰ لَيْتَنِي لَمْ أَتَّخِذْ فُلَانًا خَلِيلًا
Oh, woe to me; I wish I never took so-and-so for a friend.
Summary:
9.1 ISM: A name that is used to introduce anything.
9.2 LAQAB: Name based on a quality.
9.3 NABAZA: To call names.
9.4 FULAN: Instead of naming something call it ‘so and so’ or ‘such a one’.

title: Allah says in the Quran: 16:96 : Surat An-Naĥl (The Bee) -   سورة النحل
raw_text:
1.            Near /Close by:
1.               Ind     عِند   : means near . its used both in terms of space & distance.   عندالمكان   means close/near  to some place or home &    عندالليل    means close/near to night ( a little before or after sunset)
Allah says in the Quran: 16:96 : Surat An-Naĥl (The Bee) -   سورة النحل
مَا عِندَكُمْ يَنفَدُ   ۖ   وَمَا عِندَ اللَّهِ بَاقٍ   ۗ   وَلَنَجْزِيَنَّ الَّذِينَ صَبَرُوا أَجْرَهُم بِأَحْسَنِ مَا كَانُوا يَعْمَلُونَ
Whatever you have will end, but what Allah has is lasting. And We will surely give those who were patient their reward according to the best of what they used to do.
Sometimes,   مِن   comes before   عِند   which further stresses the point.    مِن عِند   meaning from near , from the side of..
Allah says in the Quran: 3:165: Surat 'Āli `Imrān (Family of Imran) -   سورة آل عمران
أَوَلَمَّا أَصَابَتْكُم مُّصِيبَةٌ قَدْ أَصَبْتُم مِّثْلَيْهَا قُلْتُمْ أَنَّىٰ هَٰذَا ۖ قُلْ هُوَ مِنْ عِندِ أَنفُسِكُمْ ۗ إِنَّ اللَّهَ عَلَىٰ كُلِّ شَيْءٍ قَدِيرٌ
Why [is it that] when a [single] disaster struck you [on the day of Uhud], although you had struck [the enemy in the battle of Badr] with one twice as great, you said, "From where is this?" Say, "It is from yourselves." Indeed, Allah is over all things competent.
2.            Lada    لَدَى   & ladun   لَدُن    : both these words are the same . when minn    مِن   is before lada    لَدَى     ,then it changes from ladun. Like for example,   مِن لَّدُنكَ    &    مِن لَّدُنَّا  . If it comes without   مِن   , then it is    لَدَى   . like for example :    بِما لَديهِم    or    لَدَالباب    . this word is derived from          عِند    & shows more closeness or nearness.    نيز تمكّن كو مقتضى هى       . couldn’t translate. For example if i have wealth with me (present ) ,then  its called   لدنِّى مالٌ   . But, we can say    عِندى مالٌ   , when the ownership of wealth is there but its not with the person.
As Allah says in the Quran: 12:25 Surat Yūsuf (Joseph) -   سورة يوسف
وَاسْتَبَقَا الْبَابَ وَقَدَّتْ قَمِيصَهُ مِن دُبُرٍ وَأَلْفَيَا سَيِّدَهَا لَدَى الْبَابِ   ۚ   قَالَتْ مَا جَزَاءُ مَنْ أَرَادَ بِأَهْلِكَ سُوءًا إِلَّا أَن يُسْجَنَ أَوْ عَذَابٌ أَلِيمٌ
And they both raced to the door, and she tore his shirt from the back, and they found her husband at the door. She said, "What is the recompense of one who intended evil for your wife but that he be imprisoned or a painful punishment?"
In another verse, 4:67: Surat An-Nisā' (The Women) -   سورة النساء
وَإِذًا لَّآتَيْنَاهُم مِّن لَّدُنَّا أَجْرًا عَظِيمًا
And then We would have given them from Us a great reward.
لَقِىَ يَلقِي لَقاءً
3.            Tilqaa    تِلقاء  , laqee    لَقِىَ  ,yalqee    يَلقِي   ,liqaa’ann    لَقاءً   :  These words means things coming closer to each other.  To meet. Tilqaa    تِلقاء   is noun of liqaa   لَقاء   . & is used  in terms of  coming opposite to each other. So when they say   جَلَسَ تَلقَاءِى   ,then it means he sat opposite to the other person.
As per the Quran: 28:23 : Surat Al-Qaşaş (The Stories) -   سورة القصص
وَلَمَّا وَرَدَ مَاءَ مَدْيَنَ وَجَدَ عَلَيْهِ أُمَّةً مِّنَ النَّاسِ يَسْقُونَ وَوَجَدَ مِن دُونِهِمُ امْرَأَتَيْنِ تَذُودَانِ ۖ قَالَ مَا خَطْبُكُمَا ۖ قَالَتَا لَا نَسْقِي حَتَّىٰ يُصْدِرَ الرِّعَاءُ ۖ وَأَبُونَا شَيْخٌ كَبِيرٌ
And when he came to the well of Madyan, he found there a crowd of people watering [their flocks], and he found aside from them two women driving back [their flocks]. He said, "What is your circumstance?" They said, "We do not water until the shepherds dispatch [their flocks]; and our father is an old man."
تَلقاء نفس   means automatically.   فَعَلَ الامر من تلقاءِ نفسه   . he did his work all by himself. (without anyone forcing him to do it or helping him)
As per the Quran:  10:15 : Surat Yūnus (Jonah) -   سورة يونس
وَإِذَا تُتْلَىٰ عَلَيْهِمْ آيَاتُنَا بَيِّنَاتٍ   ۙ   قَالَ الَّذِينَ لَا يَرْجُونَ لِقَاءَنَا ائْتِ بِقُرْآنٍ غَيْرِ هَٰذَا أَوْ بَدِّلْهُ   ۚ   قُلْ مَا يَكُونُ لِي أَنْ أُبَدِّلَهُ مِن تِلْقَاءِ نَفْسِي   ۖ   إِنْ أَتَّبِعُ إِلَّا مَا يُوحَىٰ إِلَيَّ   ۖ   إِنِّي أَخَافُ إِنْ عَصَيْتُ رَبِّي عَذَابَ يَوْمٍ عَظِيمٍ
And when Our verses are recited to them as clear evidences, those who do not expect the meeting with Us say, "Bring us a Qur'an other than this or change it." Say, [O Muhammad], "It is not for me to change it on my own accord. I only follow what is revealed to me. Indeed I fear, if I should disobey my Lord, the punishment of a tremendous Day."
4.            Haul    حَول  : The basic meaning of     حَال    is a change in state & death.   حول الشىء   means such a side/angle of a thing where it is possible to turn it. Afterwards this word was used for ‘around something’ or ‘near something’.
Allah says in the Quran: 2:17:  Surat Al-Baqarah (The Cow) -   سورة البقرة
مَثَلُهُمْ كَمَثَلِ الَّذِي اسْتَوْقَدَ نَارًا فَلَمَّا أَضَاءَتْ مَا حَوْلَهُ ذَهَبَ اللَّهُ بِنُورِهِمْ وَتَرَكَهُمْ فِي ظُلُمَاتٍ لَّا يُبْصِرُونَ
Their example is that of one who kindled a fire, but when it illuminated what was around him, Allah took away their light and left them in darkness [so] they could not see.
Summary:
1.            Ind    عِند    :used for nearness in distance & time. When minn   مِن   is used , then it means its stressing the fact.
2.            Ladun    لَدُن    : it is derived from   عِند   & always comes with    مِن   . referes to more closeness. Similar to its meaning is lada,   لَدَى    which comes without   مِن    .
3.            Tilqaa’e   تَلقَاءِى    : it gives the meaning of automatic,something happening by itself. In relation to   عندانفسكم   ,it has closeness as well as stressing the fact. It also determines the direction of the opposite.
4.            Haul    حَول   : around or near something.

title: content/p/p10.html
raw_text:
Previous
اخر, خلف are the two words that Quran uses for previous/back/passed.
1.اخر is antonym of first and means that comes after. It’ used for adjectives of time. Ref (56:40)
Page274
2.خلف: is the two back to back or following nations or to be descendent of someone. خلف also comes in negative or bad context i.e. Illegible or incapable descendent. Ref (19:59). And the opposite of خلف is بِين يدِي and both of them come as adjectives of time and place. If it is used as adjective of time then obviously it’s used for ancestors. Ref (2:66). But if خلفhas been brought as compare to بِين يدِي then it gives meaning of being at back. Ref ( 13:11)
Summary:
اخر just comes as adjective of time and it’s general. خلف can be used in both cases i.e. adjective of time or place. As adjective of time it shows previous but there should be an ancestral/ patrimonial relationship between the prior and former.

title: content/p/p11.html
raw_text:
To regret
ندم, حسِرَ, سُقِطَ فِي يَدِيه are the words which mean to regret/ contrite about.
1.ندم to regret/rue over your bad deeds and its usage is general. Ref (5:52)
2.حسِرَ :Author of فِقه إللُغة says that its شدّ الندَامة means the severity in ruefulness/regret. But author of المُنجِد opines حسِرَ and حسرة is to regret. Ref (6:31)
Page 275
3.سُقِطَ فِي يَدِيه is an idiom means to be embarrassed after being amiss or after being erroneous. (7:149)
Summary:
ندم to regret over one’s own bad deed. حسِرَ to be severely regretful and then express regret. سُقِطَ فِي يَدِيه to be ashamed/ embarrassed over being erroneous.

title: content/p/p12.html
raw_text:
To get old
بَلِيَ, قَدِيم, عَتِيق vocabulary for getting old.
1.بَلِيَOldness/deterioration of any usable thing after long usage. بَلِيَ الثوب means ragged/worn out clothes. Ref (20:120)
2.قَدِيم means to be of old times or to be ancient. Its antonym is جَدِيد. قَدمto move forward and قَدُم is to get old. Ref (12:95)
3.عَتِيقis from العتق means thoroughbred/pureblooded. عَتِيقis a thing which is despite of being old and ancient still has dignity and purity in it. That’s why بيت الله is also called as بيت العتِيق. Ref (22:29)
Page 276
Summary:   بَلِيَ to become old/worn out because of long use. قَدِيم ancient. عَتِيق old but still dignified and honored.

To get old

بَلِيَ, قَدِيم, عَتِيق vocabulary for getting old.

1.بَلِيَOldness/deterioration of any usable thing after long usage. بَلِيَ الثوب means ragged/worn out clothes. Ref (20:120)

2.قَدِيم means to be of old times or to be ancient. Its antonym is جَدِيد. قَدمto move forward and قَدُم is to get old. Ref (12:95)

3.عَتِيقis from العتق means thoroughbred/pureblooded. عَتِيقis a thing which is despite of being old and ancient still has dignity and purity in it. That’s why بيت الله is also called as بيت العتِيق. Ref (22:29)

Page 276

Summary: بَلِيَ to become old/worn out because of long use. قَدِيم ancient. عَتِيق old but still dignified and honored.

Veil/Cover (noun)
غِطَاء غِشَاوة غُلف اكمَام اكِنّة ستر حِجَاب عَورة سُرَادِق are the formulates which have been told in Quran to interpret the word cover or veil indifferent contexts.
1.غِطَاء means the lid/top/wrapper or the cover that gives full coverage. Like the lid of a pan or ink pot. Lid to cover the object that has one sided opening. That lid should be heavy/ dense and adjoining so that it may provide full coverage and hiding. Ref (50:22).
2.غِشَاوة to cover the object with something thin and tenuous so that it may allow light peak. غشِي is a disease in which one’s senses stop working. And this veil or cover could be of fabric or metaphorically of dark too. Ref (2:7)
3.غُلف to cover something amply. غلقت السِيف to put the sword in scabbard. غلاَف is a thing in which one conceals the object. غُلف is the plural of this word. Ref (2:88)
Page 277
4.اكمَام is derived from كمّ means to conceal or to veil. كمّ البَعِير to muzzle the camel. كمّ also means the covering or outer layer of spikes/fruits. Ref (55:11)
5.اكِنّة To hide something at secure place and to protect from the sun. كنّ فِي نفسِهto keep something in heart. كنّ is that safe place or shelter/sanctuary. إكنَان اكِنّة are the plurals for كنّ. Mean this word can narrate both literal and metaphorical meanings. In literal mean ref (16:81). Metaphorical mean (41:5)
6.ستر to hide or to cover it also means shield. Or anything that serves the purpose of covering or veiling. سُتره is any hindrance that one places in front before performing salah. ستر السطح means the wall that covers the roof. ستر does not gives meaning of full coverage still one can sneak a peek. Ref (18:90).
7.حِجَاب means the hindrance/barrier or the obstruction that renders making advance. حَاجب means doorkeeper. حجب to put something in cover/veil or hidden and obstructed to block any contact or advance. Ayahs that are related to rulings over women’s dress code called آية حجَاب. And حجَابmeans a cover that flows over her eyes and allow her to see the passage/way but not any irrelevant by passer and a man also may not see her. It’s an obstacle between two things that prohibits view. Ref (33:53)
Page 278
8.عَورة , العوَار means a hole/slits in a cloth or house. Ref (33:13). Anything that one conceals out of shame. Ref (24:31) this word also comes in background of covering merely. (24:58)
9.سُرَادِق this is from Persian means the thick walls of fabric/curtains. Or tents/camps without ceiling/tops. Ref (18:29)
Summary:
غِطَاء lid that covers one sided open thing (glass or a cooking pan) and provides full coverage. غِشَاوة tenuous or thin cover that doesn’t suffice the coverage can be used both in literal and metaphorical meaning. غُلف ample/copious cover. اكمَامcover or sheath over the fruits.اكِنّة protective covering or sheltered places. ستر is partial covering/veil or hindrance. حِجَاب that renders the sight of object or thing that prohibits easy access . عَورة is hole or places need to be covered up. سُرَادِق curtains of thick fabric or tents without tops/caps.

raw_text:
To up bring/ nurture
رَبَّا،رَبّئ(ربؤ)، انبت، انشَا، ربَّ، كَفّلَ are the terms which applies on the context of upbringing/nurturing/ raising etc.
1.رَبَّا and رَبّئ means upbringing of a baby/infant. رَبّئ exclusively means to up bring or to foster a kid or to civilize. Ref (26:18), (17:24)
2.انبت: نبت (noun)growth of grass or foliation. انبت (verb) to cultivate/grow something. But if the child is being fostered/nurtured in such a careful way that he out stands among others then Allah has used انبت for that kind of brought up. Ref (3:27)
3.انشَا: نشَا to be born, to come to life, to reach youth (مُنجِد). انشَاto give someone existence and then to up bring. نَاشِيyoung/fully grown/adult.نشَا ة= growth. Ref (56:62), (56:76), (13:12) نشَاء ،يُنشِئُ only means to up bring or to raise. Ref (43:18).
Page 280
4.ربَّ it’s the noun which means to gradually raise someone and make them reach the perfection and completeness and to slack all of one’s necessities. Commonly stated as sustainer. This word is common for subject noun. Ref (1:2). This attribute exclusively belongs to Allah SWT and HE is the ربَّ. But this word can also be taken in the means of master or owner. But in this scenario the noun of this verb would be ربَابيت not ربُوبِية. Ref (12:41). Generally we don’t find plural for ربَّ but as disbelievers had taken many of them so Quran has takenاربَاب as plural. Ref (12:39)
5.كَفّلَ : to up bring someone and to spend on that person. Or to financially support anybody and to look after. Ref (3:44).
Summary:
رَبَّا & تربية to rear and up bring. انبت to up bring meticulously and to take care of one’s diet. انشَا to give someone existence and to up bring.ربَّ to give someone existence and gradually make them reach the wholeness. كَفّلَ to be responsible or to be the guarantor of someone’s rearing.
<<Alternate translation>>
Rabb, Parwarish Kurna, P.279
{
Synonyms: RABA,RABBI,RABU,ANBAT,ANSHA,RABBA,KAFFALA
1 RABA(رَبي),RABBI(رَبّي):RABA ALWALAD(رَبَا الولد) meaning growing up of child,and RABBI meaning to upbring child,to teach him manners
FIRAUN said to MUSA(AS)
Surat Ash-Shu`ara' [26:18] - The Noble Qur'an
أَلَمْ   نُرَبِّكَ   فِينَا وَلِيدًا
Did we not   raise   you among us as a child
Surat Al-'Isra' [17:24] - The Noble Qur'an
وَقُل رَّبِّ ارْحَمْهُمَا كَمَا   رَبَّيَانِي   صَغِيرًا
say, "My Lord, have mercy upon them as they   brought me up   [when I was] small."
2 ANBATA(انْبَتَ):NABATA(نَبَتَ) meaning growing up of grass or vegetables etc. and ANBATA meaning grow up.but if a child is brought up in an extraordinary manner such that the growth and development of child is accelerated then for that ANBATA is used in Quran
Surat 'Ali `Imran [3:37] - The Noble Qur'an
فَتَقَبَّلَهَا رَبُّهَا بِقَبُولٍ حَسَنٍ   وَأَنبَتَهَا نَبَاتًا   حَسَنًا
So her Lord accepted her with good acceptance and caused her to   grow   in a good manner
3 INSHAA(انْشَاَ),:NASHAA(نَشَاَ) meaning to born,to become alive and to reach youth and INSHAA meaning to give birth to someone and then to up bring . NASHI(
نَاشِي) means young man. and NISHAT(نشاة) meaning elevation
Surat Al-Waqi`ah [56:71-72] - The Noble Qur'an
أَفَرَأَيْتُمُ النَّارَ الَّتِي تُورُونَ أَأَنتُمْ   أَنشَأْتُمْ   شَجَرَتَهَا أَمْ نَحْنُ   الْمُنشِئُونَ
And have you seen the fire that you ignite?
Is it you who   produced   its tree, or are We the   producer  ?
Surat Ar-Ra`d [13:12] - The Noble Qur'an
وَ  يُنشِئُ   السَّحَابَ الثِّقَالَ
and   generates   the heavy clouds
and NASHSHAA(نَشّا) YUNASHSHIU(يُنَشِّيُ) from baabb taf3eel meaning only to upbring and nurture
Surat Az-Zukhruf [43:18] - The Noble Qur'an
أَوَمَن   يُنَشَّأُ   فِي الْحِلْيَةِ وَهُوَ فِي الْخِصَامِ غَيْرُ مُبِينٍ
So is one   brought up   in ornaments while being during conflict unevident [attributed to Allah ]?
4 RABB(ربّ):RABBUN(ربّ) is a gerund meaning to upbring someone gradually to perfection and to cater for all the needs.This word is normally used as verbal noun
Surat Al-Fatihah [1:2] - The Noble Qur'an
الْحَمْدُ لِلَّهِ   رَبِّ   الْعَالَمِينَ
[All] praise is [due] to Allah ,   Lord   of the worlds
This attribute of RABOBIYAT(ربوبيت) is only for ALLAH and ARRABB(الربّ) is only ALLAH.yet RABB can refer to master and owner in that case the gerund is not RABOBIYAH(ربوبية) but RABABIYAT(ربابيت)
Surat Yusuf [12:41] - The Noble Qur'an
يَا صَاحِبَيِ السِّجْنِ أَمَّا أَحَدُكُمَا فَيَسْقِي   رَبَّهُ   خَمْرًا ۖ
O two companions of prison, as for one of you, he will give drink to his   master   of wine;
likewise there is no sense of plural of RABB but as disbeliever had made many RABB therefore Quran has used for that plural ARBABUN(ارباب)
Surat Yusuf [12:39] - The Noble Qur'an
يَا صَاحِبَيِ السِّجْنِ أَ  أَرْبَابٌ   مُّتَفَرِّقُونَ خَيْرٌ أَمِ اللَّهُ الْوَاحِدُ الْقَهَّارُ
O [my] two companions of prison, are separate   lords   better or Allah , the One, the Prevailing?
5 KAFFALA(كفّل):meaning to upbring and spent on someone.meaning to be responsible for someone boarding and lodging and wellbeing
Surat 'Ali `Imran [3:44] - The Noble Qur'an
وَمَا كُنتَ لَدَيْهِمْ إِذْ يُلْقُونَ أَقْلَامَهُمْ أَيُّهُمْ   يَكْفُلُ   مَرْيَمَ
And you were not with them when they cast their pens as to which of them should be   responsible   for Mary
Summary:
1 RABBA: only for upbringing and educatingg
2 ANBATA: careful upbringing and nurturing in excellence
3 NASHAA: meaning to give birth and to upbring for growth
4 RABB: to give birth and then to upbring gradually to perfection and take care of all necessities
5 KAFFALA: to be reponsible for upbringing and education

raw_text:
Page 281
To read and to make someone read
قرأ، اَقرء، تلئ، رتل، درس، درَاسة، اَملئ (ملئ lexicons that have been used in Quran.
1.قرأ is normally used for verb to read or to study either to read a entire piece of writing or to read a word or two. Quran is called as قرآنbecause it’s repeatedly or frequently read book and its hyperbolized noun. Like from غفرhyperbolized noun would be غُفرَان. Ref (29:19). اَقرءto make someone else read. Ref (87:6).
2.تلئ يتلُوَا to follow again and again. Ref (91:2). It also means to read any book or to read Quran. تِلََاوة is reading/reciting particular torevealed and sacred books. This word can’t be used if one reads a word or two from the revealed book verses should be recited. Ref (29:45) but it seems the specification of this word to the recitation/reading of revealed book is invention of latter Islamic period. Because Quran has used this word in the context of reading or reciting the magic spells. Ref (2:102)
Page 282:
3.رتل: رتَلattribute or beauty, decoration, goodness of anything. رتّل means to read with elocution and ترتِيل means to recite with voice beautified (مُنجِد). To read slowly/bit by bit. Ref (73:4)
4.درس to get worn out/ragged. درس الثوب ragged or frayed clothes. درس العلمmeans to be attentive in order to learn (مُنجِد). إمَام رَاغِبsays that this word implies when one learns, organizes and get influenced by knowledge. And one can meet this stage if he/she works continuously.درسhence it means to read punctually and continuously. Ref (3:79.) دَرَسَ & دِرَاسة to read and to make someone read. دَارَس to read unto each other. Ref (5:152)
5.اَملئ: الاِملاءit’s been used in duo matters املّ يمِلّ املاَء ملل and املئ،يُملِي، إملَاء in both cases إملاَء means the same i.e. To dictate. According to thisتُملئ means to read unto somebody near some scholars. Ref (25:5).

To call out to
دعا ،نادئ، اذّن، إبتهل، جهر reflect the above mentioned phrase.
1.دعا and نِداء are near in meaning. But دعا is more precise and particular than نِداء. Subtle differences are: دعا means just call نِداءmeans to call out loudly because word نِدئ also comes in the context of long distances. منادئ(فاعل) means the caller, herald. The content of دعا must be meaningful. نِداء can be meaningful or it can be meaningless. A cry/shout or a callout could be نِداء but not دعا like if one calls out somebody’s name it would be نِداءnot دعا. In دعا one should address somebody but in نِداءit’s not necessary to name the منادئ (مفعول. Ref (2:171). نعقto caw or the croak of crow. And the in the cited verse نِداء just means to shout/yell. دعا means to call out to someone. Ref (19:3). In the cited verse word خفِيا is excepting the scenario. نِداءhas also some been found in Quran in the context of اذان.
Page 285:
Ref (62:9) and in this case also the (مفعول) منادئ is not specified and the condition of loud voice and long distance is also here.
2.اذّن to draw attention by calling out loudly. So that the voice may access their ears. اذان& تاذِين is more precise and specific than نِداء. Ref (12:70).
3.إبتهل: بهل means specific kind of separation and invocation or دعا. إبتهال، مباهلة is that in a decision both parties freely implore anathemas for each other if they would lie. Ref (3:61).
4.جهر to make one’s voice audible/hearable to others. And antonym of this word is اسرّ to lower the volume so that your acquainted people cannot hear. Like in the congregational prayer the follower or مُقتدِي recite. Ref (20:7).
Summary:   دعاmeaningful talk or to address the specific being in a suppressed voice. نِداء just implies on shout out or yelling out meaningfulness of content is not necessary or specification of منادئ is also not needed. اذان to draw attention by addressing/ calling in loud voice. إبتهالtype of anathemas. جهر to make one’s voice audible or too clear to be understood.

raw_text:
Page 286:
To hold
اخذ، بطش، تناوش، قبض ،خطف، سطا (سطو)، إعتصم، إستمسك (مسك)، درك all these terms come under the canopy of holding or catching something.
1.اخذ it’s common for holding or taking something. Mean to get something and to surround/encompass it. This word can be used in both metaphorically and literally. Ref literal meaning (20:94). Ref metaphorical meaning (2:93).
2.بطشto hold something with strength and upper handedly. Or to hold powerfully/clench, to take something forcefully. Means tough and strong grip. To hold with scaring toughness. Like اخذ this word can also be used in dual meanings. Ref (26:130).
3.تناوش ناش to hold something on an arm stretch length. To ask for something/ to quest for something. تناوشto get access to the required object. Ref (34:52).
4.قبض to hold something in fist. قبضة implies on fist. Ref (20:96).
5.خطف to get something and leave quickly/wrench away/snatch. Ref (22:31).
Page 287:
6.سطا to attack somebody and take over him/ usurp. إمام راغب says سطا means to hold someone powerfully while attacking. سطوةis البطش بر فع اليدto takeover someone by beating. Sway/controlling influence. Ref (22:72).
7.إعتصم (عصم) to save something. إعتصم to hold tightly with palms/clutch/cling and to claw. Ref (3:103).
8.إستمسك to cling to/ to adhere to. To seize/halt and to stick to. تمسّك , إستمسكto hold on to or to grasp powerfully and not let it go. (مُنجد). Ref (2:265).
9.دركto take over from the back. Rock bottom can also be called so. (36:40).
Summary:   اخذ general for, to hold. بطش firm and tough grip. تناوش to hold something placed far. قبض to hold/grab in fist. خطف to grasp and leave hastily/ wrench away. سطاto hold like attacking. إعتصمto clutch. إستمسك to cling to/ to hold on to. درك to take over from the back.

Subhan   (p.261)
According to Ibn-e-Faaris, two types of meanings may originate from the word 'Sabaha'.
i) Asort of Ibadah
ii)A sort of Running   (meem-laam)
And Imam Raaghib wrote 'floating' or 'gliding' or 'quick passing of an object through water or air' as the meanings of 'Sabaha'.  (muff)
'Sabbaah' means a Natator or a Glider. and 'Farasun Sabooh' refers to a horse which does not move to either side due it's fast speed.  (munjad)
Allah(swt) says:
وَهُوَ الَّذِي خَلَقَ اللَّيْلَ وَالنَّهَارَ وَالشَّمْسَ وَالْقَمَرَ ۖ كُلٌّ فِي فَلَكٍ يَسْبَحُونَ
"And He it is Who has created the night and the day, and the sun and the moon, each in an orbit floating." [21:33]
In another Verse:
وَالسَّابِحَاتِ سَبْحًا
"And by those(angels) that swim along." [79:3]
And later on, they started using this word in the meaning of doing something quickly. As Allah(swt) says:
إِنَّ لَكَ فِي النَّهَارِ سَبْحًا طَوِيلًا
"Verily, there is for you by day prolonged occupation with ordinary duties." [73:7]
Subhan   is a verbal noun which stems from 'Sabaha' like 'Ghufran' from 'ghafara'.
There are millionsand billions of planets in the space revolving in their orbits and the never palpitate or swing neither do the bump or collide with one another. So, it is obvious that their Controlling Entity could only be the One who is sound and deviceful in His contrivance and management, free of any miscue or imperfection and that is exactly what Subhan means.
And furthermore; such a wise planner who is contriving the affairs of this universe with His excellent contrivance must be the Only Super Power free of any partners. Because the interference of any second party may infest and thus embroil the discipline of this Universe. Hence 'Subhan' refers to that Being who is free of any imperfections having absolute authority over all the matters and is montioring the movements of all the objects that comprise this universe.
Allah(swt) says:
وَقَالُوا اتَّخَذَ اللَّهُ وَلَدًا ۗ سُبْحَانَهُ ۖ بَلْ لَهُ مَا فِي السَّمَاوَاتِ وَالْأَرْضِ ۖ كُلٌّ لَهُ قَانِتُونَ
"And they (Jews, Christians and pagans) say: Allâh has begotten a son (children or offspring). Glory be to Him (Exalted be He above all that they associate with Him). Nay, to Him belongs all that is in the heavens and on earth, and all surrender with obedience (in worship) to Him."[2:116]
And these movements or actions of these objects as in accordance with the laws prescribed by their Wise Contriver are named as 'Their Tasbeeh (Proclaimation of the perfection and glorification of ALLAH(SWT) in the way He taught), or Obedience(Submission) or Worship.
So, all the things ,this universe contains, confirm silently through their actions that the Entity Who is contriving them is free of any imperfections and having any partneres.
Allah(swt) says:
سَبَّحَ لِلَّهِ مَا فِي السَّمَاوَاتِ وَمَا فِي الْأَرْضِ ۖ وَهُوَ الْعَزِيزُ الْحَكِيمُ
"Whatsoever is in the heavens and whatsoever is on the earth glorifies Allâh. And He is the All-Mighty, the All-Wise."[61:1]
Another aspect of this universal management system is that man gets deeply surprised to see it's perfect discipline in which there is not even a moment's delays neither it's get stuck nor clash. So, his tongue cannot help proclaiming the greatness and glorification of the One managing this universe. So, the word 'Subhan' can also be used in those moments of amazement when one is taken aback by the outstanding,artistic pieces of work by The Creator of the universe. Therefore; it is a word which can be used to express amazement as well as the transcedence.
Allah(swt) says:
سُبْحَانَ الَّذِي أَسْرَىٰ بِعَبْدِهِ لَيْلًا مِنَ الْمَسْجِدِ الْحَرَامِ إِلَى الْمَسْجِدِ الْأَقْصَى
"Glorified (and Exalted) is He (Allâh) [above all that (evil) they associate with Him]. Who took His slave (Muhammad SAW) for a journey by night from Al-Masjid-al-Harâm (at Makkah) to Al-Masjid-al-Aqsa (in Jerusalem)." [17:1]
Here, the usage of word 'Subhan' marks the fact that this journey was physical and not a spiritual one.

According to Ibn-e-Faaris, two types of meanings may originate from the word 'Sabaha'.

i) Asort of Ibadah

ii)A sort of Running (meem-laam)

And Imam Raaghib wrote 'floating' or 'gliding' or 'quick passing of an object through water or air' as the meanings of 'Sabaha'.(muff)

'Sabbaah' means a Natator or a Glider. and 'Farasun Sabooh' refers to a horse which does not move to either side due it's fast speed.(munjad)

Allah(swt) says:

وَهُوَ الَّذِي خَلَقَ اللَّيْلَ وَالنَّهَارَ وَالشَّمْسَ وَالْقَمَرَ ۖ كُلٌّ فِي فَلَكٍ يَسْبَحُونَ

"And He it is Who has created the night and the day, and the sun and the moon, each in an orbit floating." [21:33]

In another Verse:

وَالسَّابِحَاتِ سَبْحًا

"And by those(angels) that swim along." [79:3]

And later on, they started using this word in the meaning of doing something quickly. As Allah(swt) says:

إِنَّ لَكَ فِي النَّهَارِ سَبْحًا طَوِيلًا

"Verily, there is for you by day prolonged occupation with ordinary duties." [73:7]

Subhan is a verbal noun which stems from 'Sabaha' like 'Ghufran' from 'ghafara'.

There are millionsand billions of planets in the space revolving in their orbits and the never palpitate or swing neither do the bump or collide with one another. So, it is obvious that their Controlling Entity could only be the One who is sound and deviceful in His contrivance and management, free of any miscue or imperfection and that is exactly what Subhan means.

And furthermore; such a wise planner who is contriving the affairs of this universe with His excellent contrivance must be the Only Super Power free of any partners. Because the interference of any second party may infest and thus embroil the discipline of this Universe. Hence 'Subhan' refers to that Being who is free of any imperfections having absolute authority over all the matters and is montioring the movements of all the objects that comprise this universe.

Allah(swt) says:

وَقَالُوا اتَّخَذَ اللَّهُ وَلَدًا ۗ سُبْحَانَهُ ۖ بَلْ لَهُ مَا فِي السَّمَاوَاتِ وَالْأَرْضِ ۖ كُلٌّ لَهُ قَانِتُونَ

"And they (Jews, Christians and pagans) say: Allâh has begotten a son (children or offspring). Glory be to Him (Exalted be He above all that they associate with Him). Nay, to Him belongs all that is in the heavens and on earth, and all surrender with obedience (in worship) to Him."[2:116]

And these movements or actions of these objects as in accordance with the laws prescribed by their Wise Contriver are named as 'Their Tasbeeh (Proclaimation of the perfection and glorification of ALLAH(SWT) in the way He taught), or Obedience(Submission) or Worship.

So, all the things ,this universe contains, confirm silently through their actions that the Entity Who is contriving them is free of any imperfections and having any partneres.

Allah(swt) says:

سَبَّحَ لِلَّهِ مَا فِي السَّمَاوَاتِ وَمَا فِي الْأَرْضِ ۖ وَهُوَ الْعَزِيزُ الْحَكِيمُ

"Whatsoever is in the heavens and whatsoever is on the earth glorifies Allâh. And He is the All-Mighty, the All-Wise."[61:1] 

Another aspect of this universal management system is that man gets deeply surprised to see it's perfect discipline in which there is not even a moment's delays neither it's get stuck nor clash. So, his tongue cannot help proclaiming the greatness and glorification of the One managing this universe. So, the word 'Subhan' can also be used in those moments of amazement when one is taken aback by the outstanding,artistic pieces of work by The Creator of the universe. Therefore; it is a word which can be used to express amazement as well as the transcedence.

Allah(swt) says:

سُبْحَانَ الَّذِي أَسْرَىٰ بِعَبْدِهِ لَيْلًا مِنَ الْمَسْجِدِ الْحَرَامِ إِلَى الْمَسْجِدِ الْأَقْصَى

"Glorified (and Exalted) is He (Allâh) [above all that (evil) they associate with Him]. Who took His slave (Muhammad SAW) for a journey by night from Al-Masjid-al-Harâm (at Makkah) to Al-Masjid-al-Aqsa (in Jerusalem)." [17:1]

Here, the usage of word 'Subhan' marks the fact that this journey was physical and not a spiritual one.

meaning to follow along with the flow of crowd,meaning with this flooding crowd you swim along as well. as per sahib munjad AFAD AL QAUM MIN MAKAN(افاض القوم من مكان) meaning to disperse and disband and AFAD FIL HADITH (افاض في الحديث) meaning engross in talk for long time.

Surat Yunus [10:61] - The Noble Qur'an

وَلَا تَعْمَلُونَ مِنْ عَمَلٍ إِلَّا كُنَّا عَلَيْكُمْ شُهُودًا إِذْ تُفِيضُونَ فِيهِ ۚ

and you [people] do not do any deed except that We are witness over you when you are involved in it

as per Ibn ul Faris (تفيضون فيه) is (إِندفعوا فيه) meaning you are so engross that you forget everything else

START OF QATADA POST

4 .Sabaha (p.808) 

To float; According to Imam Raaghib, this word refers to something floating or gliding or it's quick passing through water or air. (muff)

Allah(swt) says:

وَكُلٌّ فِي فَلَكٍ يَسْبَحُونَ

"They all float, each in an orbit." [36:40]

And then later on, they started using this word in the meaning of 'quickly doing something'.

ALLAH(SWT) says in Qura'n:

إِنَّ لَكَ فِي النَّهَارِ سَبْحًا طَوِيلًا

"Verily, there is for you by day prolonged occupation with ordinary duties." [73:7] 

Subhaan: such a state of busyness in which speediness is dominent due to heavy work load.

END OF QATADA POST

Summary:

1 SHUGL: general,meaning to get occupied in some work

2 KHADA: to be involved with full attention,used in bad meaning

3 AFADA:such an involvment in some work which makes one forgetful of oneself

4 SABHAN:such an occupation/engagement in which swiftness is prominent owing to work load

To ask for or to give Refuge  (Panah dena or lena # 21) page 289
Synonyms:
Ajaar/istejaar:     اجارَ
a'azaa:  أَعُوذُ
1. Ajaara/istejaar
jaar is a neighbor or a  personal assistant
istejaar   is to   ask for   asylum and protection from the enemy
ajaara   is   to give   someone refuge or asylum from an enemy
وَإِنْ أَحَدٌ مِّنَ ٱلْمُشْرِكِينَ   ٱسْتَجَارَكَ     فَأَجِرْهُ   حَتَّىٰ يَسْمَعَ كَلَـٰمَ ٱللَّـهِ ثُمَّ أَبْلِغْهُ مَأْمَنَهُۥ ۚ ذَٰلِكَ بِأَنَّهُمْ قَوْمٌ لَّا يَعْلَمُونَ ﴿   ٦   ﴾
[9:6]  And if one of the idolaters seek protection from you, grant him protection till he hears the word of Allah, then make him attain his place of safety; this is because they are a people who do not know.
2. a'azoo/isteaaz
auz is one who gives refuge
ma'aaz is a place of refuge
taawuz is the 'chantings' or 'mantras' written on a piece of paper/fabric  and hung around the neck or the house to ward off evil
isteaaz is   to seek refuge   from invisible lurkings and the evils of the devil, jinn or magic and magicians
a'azaa/a'auzoo   (a)   is to come under someone's refuge and remain close   (b)   hold on tight and not let go of the One who is providing the protection from the danger (c) enter a safe-haven already and be given respite immediately (d) cling to the anchor
وَإِذْ قَالَ مُوسَىٰ لِقَوْمِهِۦٓ إِنَّ ٱللَّـهَ يَأْمُرُكُمْ أَن تَذْبَحُوا۟ بَقَرَةً ۖ قَالُوٓا۟ أَتَتَّخِذُنَا هُزُوًا ۖ قَالَ   أَعُوذُ   بِٱللَّـهِ أَنْ أَكُونَ مِنَ ٱلْجَـٰهِلِينَ ﴿   ٦٧   ﴾
[2:67]  And when Musa said to his people: Surely Allah commands you that you should sacrifice a cow; they said: Do you ridicule us? He said: I   seek the protection   of Allah from being one of the ignorant.
وَإِمَّا يَنزَغَنَّكَ مِنَ ٱلشَّيْطَـٰنِ نَزْغٌ   فَٱسْتَعِذْ   بِٱللَّـهِ ۚ إِنَّهُۥ سَمِيعٌ عَلِيمٌ ﴿   ٢٠٠   ﴾
[7:200] And if a false imputation from the Shaitan afflict you, seek refuge in Allah; surely He is Hearing, Knowing.
Summary:
Ajaar/istejaar:[     اجارَ ]   refuge from an enemy
a'azaa:[  أَعُوذُ ]    refuge from all evil spirits

Page 290
22- POOCHNA (To Ask)
Synonyms: Sa’ala, Istifta’a, Istanba’a
22.1 SA’ALA   has two basic meanings.   1)   istisfar to ask (question) for getting answer for something   2)   to ask for something and to want it in return. Here the first meaning is being discussed. It is commonly used under the meaning of Istisfar. Allah SWT Said:
Surat Al-Mulk (The Sovereignty)
67:8
كُلَّمَا أُلْقِيَ فِيهَا فَوْجٌ سَأَلَهُمْ خَزَنَتُهَا أَلَمْ يَأْتِكُمْ نَذِيرٌ
Every time a group is cast therein, its keeper will ask: "Did no warner come to you?"
22.2 ISTIFTA’A   : FATWA and FUTYA is the answer (opinion) for any difficult matter. Istafta meaning to ask fatwa (juristic ruling concerning Islamic law issued by an Islamic scholar) to ask juristic rulings from any scholar regarding any difficult matter. To discover opinion / decision about any difficult matter. Allah SWT said:
Surat An-Nisā' (The Women)
4:176
يَسْتَفْتُونَكَ قُلِ اللَّهُ يُفْتِيكُمْ فِي الْكَلَالَةِ
They ask you for a legal verdict
22.3 ISTANBA’A  :  Nab’a is such news which is important and has link with questioner and answerer too .whether some incident has happened or will happen, word Nabuwwat ( Prophet hood)and Nabi (Prophet)  is derived from it. Nabi ( Prophet) is the one who receives news ( messages) from Allah (SWT) through revelation  and conveys  it to the people, whether they are linked to past, or  supernatural,and to future. Istanba’a means to discover the news. To verify     the news  Allah SWT said:
Surat Yūnus (Jonah)
10:53
وَيَسْتَنْبِئُونَكَ أَحَقٌّ هُوَ ۖ قُلْ إِي وَرَبِّي إِنَّهُ لَحَقٌّ
And they ask you (O Muhammad SAW) to inform them (saying): "Is it true (i.e. the torment and the establishment of the Hour;
And according to Imam Raghib Nabah is that new in which there is no possibility of lying but this does not seem to be correct because Allah (SWT) said:
Surat Al-Ĥujurāt (The Rooms)
49:06

22- POOCHNA (To Ask)

 

Synonyms: Sa’ala, Istifta’a, Istanba’a

 

22.1 SA’ALA has two basic meanings. 1) istisfar to ask (question) for getting answer for something 2) to ask for something and to want it in return. Here the first meaning is being discussed. It is commonly used under the meaning of Istisfar. Allah SWT Said:

 

Surat Al-Mulk (The Sovereignty)

 67:8

كُلَّمَا أُلْقِيَ فِيهَا فَوْجٌ سَأَلَهُمْ خَزَنَتُهَا أَلَمْ يَأْتِكُمْ نَذِيرٌ

Every time a group is cast therein, its keeper will ask: "Did no warner come to you?"

 

 

22.2 ISTIFTA’A : FATWA and FUTYA is the answer (opinion) for any difficult matter. Istafta meaning to ask fatwa (juristic ruling concerning Islamic law issued by an Islamic scholar) to ask juristic rulings from any scholar regarding any difficult matter. To discover opinion / decision about any difficult matter. Allah SWT said:

 

Surat An-Nisā' (The Women)

4:176

يَسْتَفْتُونَكَ قُلِ اللَّهُ يُفْتِيكُمْ فِي الْكَلَالَةِ

They ask you for a legal verdict

 

22.3 ISTANBA’A:  Nab’a is such news which is important and has link with questioner and answerer too .whether some incident has happened or will happen, word Nabuwwat ( Prophet hood)and Nabi (Prophet)  is derived from it. Nabi ( Prophet) is the one who receives news ( messages) from Allah (SWT) through revelation  and conveys  it to the people, whether they are linked to past, or  supernatural,and to future. Istanba’a means to discover the news. To verify the news  Allah SWT said:

 

Surat Yūnus (Jonah)

10:53

 

وَيَسْتَنْبِئُونَكَ أَحَقٌّ هُوَ ۖ قُلْ إِي وَرَبِّي إِنَّهُ لَحَقٌّ

 

And they ask you (O Muhammad SAW) to inform them (saying): "Is it true (i.e. the torment and the establishment of the Hour;

 

And according to Imam Raghib Nabah is that new in which there is no possibility of lying but this does not seem to be correct because Allah (SWT) said:

 

Surat Al-Ĥujurāt (The Rooms)

49:06

 

يَا أَيُّهَا الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا إِنْ جَاءَكُمْ فَاسِقٌ بِنَبَإٍ فَتَبَيَّنُوا

 

O you who believe! If a Fasiq (liar — evil person) comes to you with any news, verify it,

 

Like this, The Nabaa which hoopoe bird brought to prophet solmon (a). So you thought of verification mandatory due to the possibility of lying.

 

Summary:

1 SA’ALA: to ask (generally)

2 ISTIFTA’A: to ask for Islamic Rulings (legal verdict) in any difficult issue

3.ISTANBA’A: to ask about some important news.

Topic: 23
POORA (COMPLETE) - SARA -SAB (The Whole -ALL)
Synonyms: Kullun, Kamilun, Ka’affatun and Salamun
23.1:   Kullun  : meaning all, the whole, (its opposite is a part) means which has all parts, and Kullun is also used to encircle (enclose) all parts of it. So it means each one, every individual and everything. Let’s see the example. Allah (SWT) said:
Surat-al-Ambiya (The Prophets)
21:35
كُلُّ نَفْسٍ ذَائِقَةُ الْمَوْتِ
Everyone is going to taste death
Surat Al-'Anfāl (The Spoils of War)
39:8
وَقَاتِلُوهُمْ حَتَّىٰ لَا تَكُونَ فِتْنَةٌ وَيَكُونَ الدِّينُ كُلُّهُ لِلَّهِ
And fight them until there is no more Fitnah (disbelief and polytheism: i.e. worshipping others besides Allâh) and the religion (worship) will all be for Allâh Alone [in the whole of the world.
23.2   Kamil  : The complete (its opposite is inexact) means that thing which has complete parts and complete qualities, means which fulfills the Purpose (need).
Surat-Al-Baqarah (The Cow)
2- 233
وَالْوَالِدَاتُ يُرْضِعْنَ أَوْلَادَهُنَّ حَوْلَيْنِ كَامِلَيْنِ
The mothers shall give suck to their children for two whole years,
23.3   Kaffatun  : Al-Kifaf: is complete Periphery of any thing, and   Kaaf   is nominative (subject), and its feminine is   Kaffatun.  it is said (Ja an-nase Kaffatun) means every one came. This word is   ublug   from   Kamil,   because it does not only encircle (encompass) parts but also (jumlae pehloo) Now have a look at the examples:
Surat-Al-Baqarah (The Cow)
2- 208
يَا أَيُّهَا الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا ادْخُلُوا فِي السِّلْمِ كَافَّةً وَلَا تَتَّبِعُوا خُطُوَاتِ الشَّيْطَانِ ۚ إِنَّهُ لَكُمْ عَدُوٌّ مُبِينٌ
O you who believe! Enter perfectly in Islâm (by obeying all the rules and regulations of the Islâmic religion) and follow not the footsteps of Shaitân (Satan). Verily! He is to you a plain enemy  .
Surat-ul-Saba
34-28
وَمَا أَرْسَلْنَاكَ إِلَّا كَافَّةً لِلنَّاسِ بَشِيرًا وَنَذِيرًا وَلَٰكِنَّ أَكْثَرَ النَّاسِ لَا يَعْلَمُونَ
And We have not sent you (O Muhammad SAW) except as a giver of glad tidings and a warner to all mankind, but most of men know not.
Lets see now   SARAY-SAB (The Whole –ALL)
Salamun:   means be guzand and correct healthy and sound As-salam means to be saved and pure from external and internal calamities. And SALAMUN means which is correct in its nature and no one else has right on it.Allah (SWT) said:
Surat-az-Zumar:
39:29
رَجُلًا فِيهِ شُرَكَاءُ مُتَشَاكِسُونَ وَرَجُلًا سَلَمًا لِرَجُلٍ هَلْ يَسْتَوِيَانِ مَثَلًا
a man belonging to many partners at variance with each other, and a man belonging entirely to one master: are those two equal in comparison?
Summary:
Kul:   it comes in the opposite of Juz (part) and it is also used to encompasses the all parts (complete, whole, each one)
Kamil:   It comes in the opposite of Naqis (inexact) which has no shortcoming and fulfill the purpose.
Kaffatun:  every individual from a group or jumlae pehloo of some matter all of all .in theses meanings it is ublugh from  Kul (all)
Salamun:  be guzun and correct, means on which no one else has any kinds of right.

Topic: 24
POORA KARNA – HONA
To complete-To be completed
Synonyms: Tamma , Atamma,Akmal,Aoufa,Qada, and Asbaga
24.1: Atamma: tama   or   tama us-shai   means     that some thing reaches to that level where is no need of any external factor and its opposite is   Naqasa (-----)   Allah (SWT)     said:
Surat Al-'An`ām (The Cattle)
6:115
وَتَمَّتْ كَلِمَتُ رَبِّكَ صِدْقًا وَعَدْلًا
And the Word of your Lord has been fulfilled in truth and in justice
And   Atamma   means to make any inexact or incomplete thing to reach at the level of complete, and it is usually used for counting, quantity or to complete the duration. Allah (SWT) said:
Surat Al-Qaşaş (The Stories):
28:27
فَإِنْ أَتْمَمْتَ عَشْرًا فَمِنْ عِنْدِكَ
but if you complete ten years, it will be (a favour) from you
a  )  For counting:
Surat Al-Mā'idah (The Table Spread)
5:3
وَأَتْمَمْتُ عَلَيْكُمْ نِعْمَتِي
Completed My Favour upon you
b): For quantity:
Surat-Al-Baqarah (The Cow)
2:187
ثُمَّ أَتِمُّوا الصِّيَامَ إِلَى اللَّيْلِ
then complete your fast till the night appears
24.2: Akmala  : (kamil its opposite is also naqis) means to complete a started work. means to achieve the purpose for which it came into existence. Allah (SWT) said:
Surat Al-Mā'idah (The Table Spread)
5:3
الْيَوْمَ أَكْمَلْتُ لَكُمْ دِينَكُمْ وَأَتْمَمْتُ عَلَيْكُمْ نِعْمَتِي
This day, I have perfected your religion for you, completed My Favour upon you
Lets see the second example to differentiate between   Tamamm  (all) and   Kamal   (complete).
Surat-Al-Baqarah (The Cow)
2:233
وَالْوَالِدَاتُ يُرْضِعْنَ أَوْلَادَهُنَّ حَوْلَيْنِ كَامِلَيْنِ ۖ لِمَنْ أَرَادَ أَنْ يُتِمَّ الرَّضَاعَة
َThe mothers shall give suck to their children for two whole years, (that is) for those (parents) who desire to complete the term of suckling,
In this verse word Tamam is used to complete the term (duration) of suckling and Kamil is used to complete the need of term of suckling.
24.3: Awufa  : wafa this word is used for fulfilling the promise, measurement, life or conditions and the reward, and its opposite is (Gadar) to betrayal. Let’s have look on the examples:
a  ) For Promise:
Surat-Al-Baqarah (The Cow)
2:40
وَأَوْفُوا بِعَهْدِي أُوفِ بِعَهْدِكُمْ
and fulfill (your obligations to) My Covenant (with you) so that I fulfill (My Obligations to) your covenant (with Me),
b) For measurement  :
Surat Al-'A`rāf (The Heights)
7:85
فَأَوْفُوا الْكَيْلَ وَالْمِيزَانَ وَلَا تَبْخَسُوا النَّاسَ أَشْيَاءَهُمْ
so give full measure and full weight and wrong not men in their things,
For vows:
c) Surat Al-Ĥaj (The Pilgrimage)
22:29
وَلْيُوفُوا نُذُورَهُمْ
and perform their vows
d) For reward or for Paying rewards and it will come from waffa:
Allah (SWT) said:
Surat 'Āli `Imrān (Family of Imran)
3:57
وَأَمَّا الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا وَعَمِلُوا الصَّالِحَاتِ فَيُوَفِّيهِمْ أُجُورَهُمْ ۗ
And as for those who believe (in the Oneness of Allâh) and do righteous good deeds, Allâh will pay them their reward in full.
24.4: Qada:   When it is related to human being then it means to fulfill the responsibility and to free from it. Allah (SWT) said:
Surat-Al-Baqarah (The Cow)
2:200
فَإِذَا قَضَيْتُمْ مَنَاسِكَكُمْ فَاذْكُرُوا اللَّهَ كَذِكْرِكُمْ آبَاءَكُمْ
So when you have accomplished your Manasik remember Allâh as you remember your forefathers
Like this it comes to another place:
Surat Al-'Aĥzāb (The Combined Forces)
33:23
فَمِنْهُمْ مَنْ قَضَىٰ نَحْبَهُ وَمِنْهُمْ مَنْ يَنْتَظِرُ
of them some have completed their vow (to the extreme) and some (still) wait
24.5: Asbagh:-----------   -------  ,and according to Imam Raghib its meaning is wide and can be easily understood. Sabigh is wide (zirrah) and   Asbagh   means to complete the work in such way that there is no shortcoming and purpose is also fulfilled. Usually this word is used for ablution and to fulfill the blessings. Allah (SWT) said:
Surat Luqmān (Luqman
31:20
وَأَسْبَغَ عَلَيْكُمْ نِعَمَهُ ظَاهِرَةً وَبَاطِنَةً
and has made His bounties flow to you in exceeding measure, (both) seen and unseen?
Summary:
Atamma:   To complete some thing in such way that there is not remaining any fault.
Akmala:   To complete some thing in such way that the purpose is gained.
Aw’fa  : it is used for, Promise, measurement, reward, value and life.
Qada:   when it related to mankind it means to fulfill the responsibility and to free from it.
Asbagha:   To complete some thing in such way that there is not remaining any fault and need is also fulfilled in its best way.
For Hidden see   Chupna.

Asbagha: To complete some thing in such way that there is not remaining any fault and need is also fulfilled in its best way.

For Hidden see Chupna.

Then God said, "Take four birds, and train them to come back to you. Then place them separately on each   hilltop  , and call them: they will come flying to you. Know that God is almighty and wise."
وَإِذْ قَالَ إِبْرَٰهِـۧمُ رَبِّ أَرِنِى كَيْفَ تُحْىِ ٱلْمَوْتَىٰ   ۖ   قَالَ أَوَلَمْ تُؤْمِن   ۖ   قَالَ بَلَىٰ وَلَـٰكِن لِّيَطْمَئِنَّ قَلْبِى   ۖ   قَالَ فَخُذْ أَرْبَعَةً مِّنَ ٱلطَّيْرِ فَصُرْهُنَّ إِلَيْكَ ثُمَّ ٱجْعَلْ عَلَىٰ كُلِّ  جَبَلٍ   مِّنْهُنَّ جُزْءًا ثُمَّ ٱدْعُهُنَّ يَأْتِينَكَ سَعْيًا   ۚ   وَٱعْلَمْ أَنَّ ٱللَّـهَ عَزِيزٌ حَكِيمٌ   ﴿   ٢٦٠

Singular:Raasi
Rasoo means 'to be anchored'
'Rasaa Safinah' means 'the anchored ship'
'Marsaa' means Port , harbor
'Rasi' also means a big pot dug in place
Rasiya is a strong , solid mountain
Rawasi   is a chain of mountains
[21:31]We set firm   mountains   upon the earth lest it should sway under them, and We placed therein passages for paths so that they might find their way.
وَجَعَلْنَا فِى ٱلْأَرْضِ   رَوَٰسِىَ   أَن تَمِيدَ بِهِمْ وَجَعَلْنَا فِيهَا فِجَاجًا سُبُلًا لَّعَلَّهُمْ يَهْتَدُونَ   ﴿   ٣١

A very big mountain
Wide and huge mountain
[26:63] Then We bade Moses strike the sea with his staff. And it parted, and each part was like a   huge   mountain  .
فَأَوْحَيْنَآ إِلَىٰ مُوسَىٰٓ أَنِ ٱضْرِب بِّعَصَاكَ ٱلْبَحْرَ   ۖ   فَٱنفَلَقَ فَكَانَ كُلُّ فِرْقٍ   كَٱلطَّوْدِ   ٱلْعَظِيمِ   ﴿   ٦٣
4.  Sawkhratun: ٱلصَّخْرَ
Rocky Hill
Boulder Mountain
a Big Boulder
According to Ibn FAris its a 'Hijr azeem'
[89:9] and with the Thamud, who cut out   [huge] rocks   in the valley,
وَثَمُودَ ٱلَّذِينَ جَابُوا۟   ٱلصَّخْرَ   بِٱلْوَادِ   ﴿   ٩
5.  Aa'laam: ٱلْأَعْلَـٰمِ
Singular: Alama
'Alama' means a SignPost, Flag, LightHouse or a Mountain
Aa'laam are those things or people that stand out amongnst the rest.
[55:24] And His are the Ships sailing smoothly through the seas, lofty as   mountains  :
وَلَهُ ٱلْجَوَارِ ٱلْمُنشَـَٔاتُ فِى ٱلْبَحْرِ   كَٱلْأَعْلَـٰمِ     ﴿   ٢٤

30.6 WASL (وَصَل) :
[to reach, unite or join]
WASL can be used with these three meanings separately. For example:
a.           Meaning to reach:
Surah Hud 11:81
قَالُوا يَا لُوطُ إِنَّا رُسُلُ رَبِّكَ لَن يَصِلُوا إِلَيْكَ
The angels said, "O Lot, indeed we are messengers of your Lord; [therefore], they will never reach you.
b.          Meaning to unite or join:
Surah Al-Baqarah (The Cow) 2:27
وَيَقْطَعُونَ مَا أَمَرَ اللَّهُ بِهِ أَن يُوصَلَ
“and sever that which Allah has ordered to be joined (or held together)”
30.7 AFDAA (اَفْضي):   FADA means the vast and empty space between the earth and sky. Afdaa is used figuratively for intimate relations with one’s woman or to tell a secret. For example:
Surah An-Nisa (The Women) 4:21
وَكَيْفَ تَأْخُذُونَهُ وَقَدْ أَفْضَىٰ بَعْضُكُمْ إِلَىٰ بَعْضٍ
“And how could you take it while you have gone in unto each other”
30.8 MASSA (مَسَّ  ): Massa literally means to touch physically but can also be used figuratively to refer to an experience. For example, the Quran says:
Surah Al-Araf 7:95
ثُمَّ بَدَّلْنَا مَكَانَ السَّيِّئَةِ الْحَسَنَةَ حَتَّىٰ عَفَوا وَّقَالُوا قَدْ مَسَّ آبَاءَنَا الضَّرَّاءُ وَالسَّرَّاءُ
“Then We exchanged in place of the bad [condition], good, until they increased [and prospered] and said, ‘Our fathers [also] were touched with hardship and ease.’ So We seized them suddenly while they did not perceive.”
30.9 WARADA (وَرَدَ):   means finding a well after searching for water. Its antonym is SADARA (صَدَرَ) which means to return after collecting or drinking water from a well.
Surah Al-Qasas 28:23
وَلَمَّا وَرَدَ مَاءَ مَدْيَنَ وَجَدَ عَلَيْهِ أُمَّةً مِّنَ النَّاسِ يَسْقُونَ
“And when he came to the well of Madyan, he found there a crowd of people watering [their flocks] “
Summary:
30.1BALAGHA: To reach the last stage of an objective.
30.2ASAABA:
30.3NAALA: To reach and obtain something one desires
30.4NAWASHA: To reach out and grab something. Can be used instead of Naala in a more general sense
30.5 TA’ATWAA: To gain something one has no right upon
30.6WASALA: To reach something and join it
30.7AFDAA: Figuratively refers to intimate relations between man and wife
30.8MASSA: Literal meaning is to touch but can be used to mean something gained from an experience.
30.9WARADA: To reach a well

Aasawba[ اَصابَ   ]: to befall; to be afflicted; something good or bad from Allah
Nawish[ناوش   ] : to reach out and get hold of something; Nawush is more generally used than Nala
Na'al (Neel)  [نالَ   ]: to reach and obtain one's desireed object
Wa  saw  la  [وَصَلَ  ]: to reach something and get connected
Afdha   [افضَي  ] : to reach one's spouse for intimacy
Ta'ata:[ تَعاطَي  ] to reach out and grab something that doesnt belong to you
Massa[مَسّ   ]: to reach out and touch
Warada [ وَرَدَ   ]: to reach a  water fountain or a well or a lake;

وَكَيْفَ تَأْخُذُونَهُ وَقَدْ أَفْضَىٰ بَعْضُكُمْ إِلَىٰ بَعْضٍ

“And how could you take it while you have gone in unto each other”

30.8 MASSA (مَسَّ): Massa literally means to touch physically but can also be used figuratively to refer to an experience. For example, the Quran says:

Surah Al-Araf 7:95

ثُمَّ بَدَّلْنَا مَكَانَ السَّيِّئَةِ الْحَسَنَةَ حَتَّىٰ عَفَوا وَّقَالُوا قَدْ مَسَّ آبَاءَنَا الضَّرَّاءُ وَالسَّرَّاءُ

“Then We exchanged in place of the bad [condition], good, until they increased [and prospered] and said, ‘Our fathers [also] were touched with hardship and ease.’ So We seized them suddenly while they did not perceive.”

30.9 WARADA (وَرَدَ): means finding a well after searching for water. Its antonym is SADARA (صَدَرَ) which means to return after collecting or drinking water from a well.

Surah Al-Qasas 28:23

وَلَمَّا وَرَدَ مَاءَ مَدْيَنَ وَجَدَ عَلَيْهِ أُمَّةً مِّنَ النَّاسِ يَسْقُونَ

“And when he came to the well of Madyan, he found there a crowd of people watering [their flocks] “

30.1BALAGHA: To reach the last stage of an objective.

30.2ASAABA:

30.3NAALA: To reach and obtain something one desires

30.4NAWASHA: To reach out and grab something. Can be used instead of Naala in a more general sense

30.5 TA’ATWAA: To gain something one has no right upon

30.6WASALA: To reach something and join it

30.7AFDAA: Figuratively refers to intimate relations between man and wife

30.8MASSA: Literal meaning is to touch but can be used to mean something gained from an experience.

30.9WARADA: To reach a well

  1. Balagha [ بلغ  ]: to reach the zenith of something
  2. Aasawba[ اَصابَ   ]: to befall; to be afflicted; something good or bad from Allah
  3. Nawish[ناوش   ] : to reach out and get hold of something; Nawush is more generally used than Nala
  4. Na'al (Neel)  [نالَ   ]: to reach and obtain one's desireed object
  5. Wasawla  [وَصَلَ  ]: to reach something and get connected
  6. Afdha   [افضَي  ] : to reach one's spouse for intimacy
  7. Ta'ata:[ تَعاطَي  ] to reach out and grab something that doesnt belong to you
  8. Massa[مَسّ   ]: to reach out and touch
  9. Warada [ وَرَدَ   ]: to reach a  water fountain or a well or a lake;

31: POHANCHANA [TO DELIVER]
Synonyms: ABLAGHA or BALLAGHA, AWRADA, JABAA, ADLAA
31.1 ABLAGHA or BALLAGHA ( بَلَّغَ ,اَبْلَغ):   Both can be used to describe the delivery of a thing or a message to its final destination. For example
Surah At-Taubah 9:6
وَإِنْ أَحَدٌ مِّنَ الْمُشْرِكِينَ اسْتَجَارَكَ فَأَجِرْهُ حَتَّىٰ يَسْمَعَ كَلَامَ اللَّهِ ثُمَّ أَبْلِغْهُ مَأْمَنَهُ ذَٰلِكَ بِأَنَّهُمْ قَوْمٌ لَّا يَعْلَمُونَ
“And if any one of the polytheists seeks your protection, then grant him protection so that he may hear the words of Allah. Then deliver him to his place of safety. That is because they are a people who do not know.”
In Surah Al-Ma’idah 5:67
يَا أَيُّهَا الرَّسُولُ بَلِّغْ مَا أُنزِلَ إِلَيْكَ مِن رَّبِّكَ
“O Messenger, announce that which has been revealed to you from your Lord”
31.2 AWRADA (اَوْرَدَ):   To lead someone to a destination. For example
Surah Al-Huud 11:98
يَقْدُمُ قَوْمَهُ يَوْمَ الْقِيَامَةِ فَأَوْرَدَهُمُ النَّارَ   ۖ   وَبِئْسَ الْوِرْدُ الْمَوْرُودُ
“He (Pharoah) will precede his people on the Day of Resurrection and lead them into the Fire; and wretched is the place to which they are led.”
31.3 JABAA (جَبَا):   The basic meaning refers to two steps a. to gather something and then b. to deliver it to some other place. For example
Surah Al-Qasas 28:57
أَوَلَمْ نُمَكِّن لَّهُمْ حَرَمًا آمِنًا يُجْبَىٰ إِلَيْهِ ثَمَرَاتُ كُلِّ شَيْءٍ أَوَلَمْ نُمَكِّن لَّهُمْ حَرَمًا آمِنًا يُجْبَىٰ إِلَيْهِ ثَمَرَاتُ كُلِّ شَيْءٍ
“Have we not established for them a safe sanctuary to which are brought the fruits of all things as provision from Us?”
31.3 ADLAA (اَدْلى):   Dalw (دَلْو) refers to an empty water bucket. Adlaa then means to gradually lower an empty bucket into a well. Adlaa ilaa falaan (فلان ادلى ادلى) means to take one’s dispute to another person for resolution and then trying to use family connections or bribery for unfair advantage.  For example:
Surah Al-Baqarah 2:188
وَلَا تَأْكُلُوا أَمْوَالَكُم بَيْنَكُم بِالْبَاطِلِ وَتُدْلُوا بِهَا إِلَى الْحُكَّامِ لِتَأْكُلُوا فَرِيقًا مِّنْ أَمْوَالِ النَّاسِ بِالْإِثْمِ وَأَنتُمْ تَعْلَمُونَ
“And do not consume one another's wealth unjustly or send it [in bribery] to the rulers in order that [they might aid] you [to] consume a portion of the wealth of the people in sin, while you know [it is unlawful].”
Summary:
31.1 ABLAGHA or BALLAGHA: To deliver a thing or a message to its final destination. Ballagha is used specifically for a message while Ablagha is more generic.
31.2 AWRADA: To lead someone to a place
31.3 JABAA: To gather something and then deliver it to another place
31.4 ADLAA ILAA FALAN: To take one’s dispute to another person for resolution and use nepotism and bribery to gain unfair advantage
