32: PHAARNA [TO RIP]
Synonyms: KHARAQA, QADDA, FATARA, FAJARA, MAKHARA, SHAQQA, FALAQA, FARAQA, MAZZAQA
32.1 KHARAQA (خَرَقَ):   To rip something and ruin it. To break something in order to destroy it. Kharaqah (خَرَقَه) refers to a piece of tattered cloth and khariq (خارق) means something non-typical. For example
Surah Al-Kahf 18:71
فَانطَلَقَا حَتَّىٰ إِذَا رَكِبَا فِي السَّفِينَةِ خَرَقَهَا   ۖ   قَالَ أَخَرَقْتَهَا لِتُغْرِقَ أَهْلَهَا لَقَدْ جِئْتَ شَيْئًا إِمْرًا
So they set out, until when they had embarked on the ship, al-Khidhr tore it open. [Moses] said, "Have you torn it open to drown its people? You have certainly done a grave thing."
32.2 QADDA (قَدَّ):   To rip something lengthwise. Also refers to a person’s height. Qadeed (قديد) refers to long slices of dried meat. For example
Surah Yusuf 12:25
وَاسْتَبَقَا الْبَابَ وَقَدَّتْ قَمِيصَهُ مِن دُبُرٍ
“And they both raced to the door, and she tore his shirt from the back”
32.3 FATARA (فَطَرَ):   To rip something lengthwise in order to crack or break it. To scratch. In this way, it can also mean to create or to give birth to. Futoor (فُطُوْر)  refers to a crack. The Quran says:
Surah Al-Mulk 27:3
فَارْجِعِ الْبَصَرَ هَلْ تَرَىٰ مِن فُطُورٍ
“So return [your] vision [to the sky]; do you see any breaks?”
At another place, it says
Surah Ar-Rum 30:30
فِطْرَتَ اللَّهِ الَّتِي فَطَرَ النَّاسَ عَلَيْهَا
“[Adhere to] the fitrah of Allah upon which He has created [all] people”
32.4 FAJARA (فَجَرَ):   To break or rip something on a vast scale. Hence the time of breaking dawn is called Fajr (فَجَر) as it appears on the vast horizon. Fajoor (فجور) refers to blatant disregard for religious tenets. Fajir (فاجر) and Fajjar (فجّار) also rise from the same root. Fajara (فَجَرَ) and fajjara (فَجَّرَ) both refer to making water flow over a vast area. For example
Surah Al-Isra’ 17:90
وَقَالُوا لَن نُّؤْمِنَ لَكَ حَتَّىٰ تَفْجُرَ لَنَا مِنَ الْأَرْضِ يَنبُوعًا
‘And they say, "We will not believe you until you break open for us from the ground a spring.’
Fajjara (فَجَّرَ ) specifically refers to opening up a long waterway. For example
Surah Al-Kahf 18:33
وَفَجَّرْنَا خِلَالَهُمَا نَهَرًا
“And We caused to gush forth within them a river.”
32.5 MAKHARA (مَخَرَ):   Refers to erosion caused by water. Makhar-ul-maa-ul-arda (مَخَرُالْمَاءُالْاَرْضَ) refers to water eroding the earth and swirling in it. Makhar us safeena (مخرالسفينه) refers to a boat plowing through the water and making noise. Makhir (ماخِر) [plural: Mawakhir (مَوَاخِر)] is a boat which plows through the water and makes noise.
Surah An-Nahl 16:14
وَتَرَى الْفُلْكَ مَوَاخِرَ فِيهِ
“And you see the ships plowing through it”
32.6 SHAQQA (شَقَّ):   To cause something hard to burst or break. The Quran uses it to describe the cracking or bursting of such hard things like the sky, earth, moon and rocks. For example
Surah ‘Abasa 80:26
ثُمَّ شَقَقْنَا الْأَرْضَ شَقًّا
“Then We broke open the earth, splitting it”
32.7 FALAQA and FARAQA (فَلَقَ, فَرَقَ):   Both words are very similar in meaning and both contain two basic steps:  a. to burst or crack and then b. to separate. Parting the hair is referred to by using either  farq (فَرق) or filq (فِلْق). Therefore, the Quran uses both these words for the same meaning. For example
Surah Al-Baqarah 2:50
وَإِذْ فَرَقْنَا بِكُمُ الْبَحْرَ فَأَنجَيْنَاكُمْ وَأَغْرَقْنَا آلَ فِرْعَوْنَ وَأَنتُمْ تَنظُرُونَ
“And [recall] when We parted the sea for you and saved you and drowned the people of Pharaoh while you were looking on.”
At another point, the Quran says
Surah Ah-Shu’ara 26:63
فَأَوْحَيْنَا إِلَىٰ مُوسَىٰ أَنِ اضْرِب بِّعَصَاكَ الْبَحْرَ   ۖ   فَانفَلَقَ فَكَانَ كُلُّ فِرْقٍ كَالطَّوْدِ الْعَظِيم
‘Then We inspired to Moses, "Strike with your staff the sea," and it parted, and each portion was like a great towering mountain.’
However, there is a slight difference in the meaning. Falaqa is often used when something breaks into two approximately equal parts. Falaqa or filq refer to a broken part of the original thing. Faraqa is more generic in its use and can refer to two or more than two parts.  The second difference is that falaqa is usually used for non-living things whereas faraqa can be used for both non-living and living thing especially humans. A separated part of a class is called firq and if this separated part is big enough, it is called faraqah. In a dispute, one side is called fareeq (فريق). For example
Surah Al-An’am 6:95
إِنَّ اللَّهَ فَالِقُ الْحَبِّ وَالنَّوَىٰ
“Indeed, Allah is the cleaver of grain and date seeds”
Similarly, in Surah Al-An’am 6:96, falaqa is used because the sunlight breaks the sky in a clear line.
فَالِقُ الْإِصْبَاحِ
“[He is] the cleaver of daybreak”
32.9 MAZZAQA (مَزَّقَ):   To rip, to disperse, to destroy. Includes the intensity if action. For example
Surah Saba’ 34:19
فَجَعَلْنَاهُمْ أَحَادِيثَ وَمَزَّقْنَاهُمْ كُلَّ مُمَزَّقٍ
“so We made them narrations and dispersed them in total dispersion”
Summary:
32.1 KHARAQA: To rip something and ruin it
32.2 QADDA: To rip something lengthwise
32.3 FATARA: To rip, to scratch
32.4 FAJARA: To break something on a vast scale
32.5 MAKHARA: A boat ripping through the water and making noise
32.6 SHAQQA: To rip or break something hard
32.7 FALAQA: To break a non-living thing into two separate parts
32.8 FARAQA: To break something into two or more separate pieces
32.9 MAZZAQA: To destroy by breaking into small scattered pieces

To Burst, Break, Explode (Phatna # 33) Page 304
Synonyms:
Infatawr, Tafattawr
Shaqqa, Inshaqqa
Infalaq
Tasawdda'a
Tamayyez
1. Infatawr     انفَطَرَ
cleave
rift, flaw
drill a hole to break
perforate
[82:1] Sahih International
When the sky   breaks apart
إِذَا السَّمَاءُ   انفَطَرَ  تْ     ﴿   ١
(19:90)
2. Shaqqaqu/Inshaqqa      شَّقَّق
burst with intensity
Split into two
[2:74] Sahih International
Then your hearts became hardened after that, being like stones or even harder. For indeed, there are stones from which rivers burst forth, and there are some of them that   split open   and water comes out, and there are some of them that fall down for fear of Allah. And Allah is not unaware of what you do.
ثُمَّ قَسَتْ قُلُوبُكُم مِّن بَعْدِ ذَٰلِكَ فَهِيَ كَالْحِجَارَةِ أَوْ أَشَدُّ قَسْوَةً   ۚ   وَإِنَّ مِنَ الْحِجَارَةِ لَمَا يَتَفَجَّرُ مِنْهُ الْأَنْهَارُ   ۚ   وَإِنَّ مِنْهَا لَمَا   يَشَّقَّقُ   فَيَخْرُجُ مِنْهُ الْمَاءُ   ۚ   وَإِنَّ مِنْهَا لَمَا يَهْبِطُ مِنْ خَشْيَةِ اللَّـهِ   ۗ  وَمَا اللَّـهُ بِغَافِلٍ عَمَّا تَعْمَلُونَ   ﴿   ٧٤
3. Infalaqa
to split a small or a softer thing
dissect
rip
4. Tasawdda'a
to fissure
bifurcate
crack but doesn't seperate into pieces
example: earthquakes, headaches
[86:12] Yusuf Ali
And by the Earth which opens out (for the gushing of springs or the sprouting of vegetation),-
وَالْأَرْضِ ذَاتِ   الصَّدْعِ   ﴿   ١٢
[56:19] Yusuf Ali
No after-ache will they receive therefrom, nor will they suffer intoxication:
لَّا   يُصَدَّعُونَ   عَنْهَا وَلَا يُنزِفُونَ   ﴿   ١٩

33:19] Yusuf Ali
Covetous over you. Then when fear comes, thou wilt see them looking to thee, their eyes revolving, like (those of) one over whom hovers death: but when the fear is past, they will smite you with sharp tongues, covetous of goods. Such men have no faith, and so Allah has made their deeds of none effect: and that is easy for Allah.
أَشِحَّةً عَلَيْكُمْ   ۖ   فَإِذَا جَاءَ الْخَوْفُ رَأَيْتَهُمْ يَنظُرُونَ إِلَيْكَ   تَدُورُ   أَعْيُنُهُمْ كَالَّذِي يُغْشَىٰ عَلَيْهِ مِنَ الْمَوْتِ   ۖ   فَإِذَا ذَهَبَ الْخَوْفُ سَلَقُوكُم بِأَلْسِنَةٍ حِدَادٍ أَشِحَّةً عَلَى الْخَيْرِ   ۚ   أُولَـٰئِكَ لَمْ يُؤْمِنُوا فَأَحْبَطَ اللَّـهُ أَعْمَالَهُمْ   ۚ   وَكَانَ ذَٰلِكَ عَلَى اللَّـهِ يَسِيرًا   ﴿   ١٩
2.   Taw  fa    طُوفُ
to go around
to circulate

There will circulate among them young boys made eternal
يَطُوفُ   عَلَيْهِمْ وِلْدَانٌ مُّخَلَّدُونَ   ﴿   ١٧
3. Haar    يَحُورَ
to go through the circuit and return to the starting point
[84:14] Sahih International
Indeed, he had thought he would never return [to Allah].
إِنَّهُ ظَنَّ أَن لَّن   يَحُورَ   ﴿   ١٤
4. Taqallaba/Inqalaba      انقَلَبَ
to turn oneself around
to change inside out
360 degrees turn
revolution
roll back
roll over
(2:144)
(67:4)
(3:144)

And of the people is he who worships Allah on an edge. If he is touched by good, he is reassured by it; but if he is struck by trial, heturns on his face [to the other direction]. He has lost [this] world and the Hereafter. That is what is the manifest loss.
وَمِنَ النَّاسِ مَن يَعْبُدُ اللَّـهَ عَلَىٰ حَرْفٍ   ۖ   فَإِنْ أَصَابَهُ خَيْرٌ اطْمَأَنَّ بِهِ   ۖ   وَإِنْ أَصَابَتْهُ فِتْنَةٌ   انقَلَبَ   عَلَىٰ وَجْهِهِ خَسِرَ الدُّنْيَا وَالْآخِرَةَ   ۚ   ذَٰلِكَ هُوَ الْخُسْرَانُ الْمُبِينُ  ﴿   ١١

to turn back and flee

My verses had already been recited to you, but you were turning back on your heels.

6. In  saw  rafa    انصَرَفُوا
turn one's/someone's direction a little or completely away from something
[9:127] Shakir
And whenever a chapter is revealed, they cast glances at one another: Does any one see you? Then they turn away: Allah has turned away their hearts because they are a people who do not understand.
وَإِذَا مَا أُنزِلَتْ سُورَةٌ نَّظَرَ بَعْضُهُمْ إِلَىٰ بَعْضٍ هَلْ يَرَاكُم مِّنْ أَحَدٍ ثُمَّ   انصَرَفُوا   ۚ   صَرَفَ اللَّـهُ قُلُوبَهُم بِأَنَّهُمْ قَوْمٌ لَّا يَفْقَهُونَ   ﴿   ١٢٧   ﴾
7. Walla (Tawalla)    وَلَّىٰ
to turn one's back
to turn away
to divert
[  27:10] Shakir
And cast down your staff. So when he saw it in motion as if it were a serpent, he turned back retreating and did not return: O Musa! fear not; surely the apostles shall not fear in My presence;
وَأَلْقِ عَصَاكَ   ۚ   فَلَمَّا رَآهَا تَهْتَزُّ كَأَنَّهَا جَانٌّ   وَلَّىٰ   مُدْبِرًا وَلَمْ يُعَقِّبْ   ۚ   يَا مُوسَىٰ لَا تَخَفْ إِنِّي لَا يَخَافُ لَدَيَّ الْمُرْسَلُونَ   ﴿   ١٠   ﴾

to turn down
to repel
to reject
to dump

يَسْأَلُونَكَ عَنِ الشَّهْرِ الْحَرَامِ قِتَالٍ فِيهِ   ۖ   قُلْ قِتَالٌ فِيهِ كَبِيرٌ   ۖ   وَصَدٌّ عَن سَبِيلِ اللَّـهِ وَكُفْرٌ بِهِ وَالْمَسْجِدِ الْحَرَامِ وَإِخْرَاجُ أَهْلِهِ مِنْهُ أَكْبَرُ عِندَ اللَّـهِ   ۚ   وَالْفِتْنَةُ أَكْبَرُ مِنَ الْقَتْلِ   ۗ   وَلَا يَزَالُونَ يُقَاتِلُونَكُمْ حَتَّىٰ يَرُدُّوكُمْ عَن دِينِكُمْ إِنِ اسْتَطَاعُوا   ۚ   وَمَن   يَرْتَدِدْ   مِنكُمْ عَن دِينِهِ فَيَمُتْ وَهُوَ كَافِرٌ فَأُولَـٰئِكَ حَبِطَتْ أَعْمَالُهُمْ فِي الدُّنْيَا وَالْآخِرَةِ   ۖ   وَأُولَـٰئِكَ أَصْحَابُ النَّارِ   ۖ   هُمْ فِيهَا خَالِدُونَ   ﴿   ٢١٧
[18:64] Shakir
He said: This is what we sought for; so they returned retracing their footsteps  .
قَالَ ذَٰلِكَ مَا كُنَّا نَبْغِ   ۚ   فَ  ارْتَدَّا   عَلَىٰ آثَارِهِمَا قَصَصًا   ﴿   ٦٤   ﴾

dubur = back
back off

Then he looked, Then he frowned and scowled, Then he turned back and was big with pride,

Daar:[دَارَ      ] to go about in circles, to rotate
Taawfa: [طَافَ       ] to go around something, to revolve or to orbit a central point
Haara: [حَارَ   ] to go and come back to the same place, to spin around one's own axis, to whirl
Taqallaba/Inqalaba: [تقلب انقلب   ] to turn from one state to another

Insarafa:[  ]  to turn one's direction; a big or a small change of situation
Walla/Tawalla (a'an): [  ولَّي     ]  to be averse; to turn away
Irtadda: [اِرْتَدَّ       ]   to revert because of unfavorable conditions
Adbara: [اَدْبَرَ      ]  to turn around and flee

9. Adbara (dubur/adbaar) أَدْبَرَ

  1. dubur = back
  1. back off
  2. nullify
  3. retreat
  4. backtrack
  5. recede
  6. retire
  7. withdraw

 [74:21-23] Shakir

Then he looked, Then he frowned and scowled, Then he turned back and was big with pride, 

 ثُمَّ نَظَرَ ﴿٢١﴾ ثُمَّ عَبَسَ وَبَسَرَ ﴿٢٢﴾ ثُمَّ أَدْبَرَ وَاسْتَكْبَرَ ﴿٢٣﴾

Summary:

  1. Daar:[دَارَ  ] to go about in circles, to rotate
  2.  Taawfa: [طَافَ   ] to go around something, to revolve or to orbit a central point
  3. Haara: [حَارَ   ] to go and come back to the same place, to spin around one's own axis, to whirl
  4. Taqallaba/Inqalaba: [تقلب انقلب   ] to turn from one state to another
  5. Nakasaw ala aqebaihi: [ نَكَصَ علي عقبة  ] to turn away from good deeds to bad
  6.  Insarafa:[  ]  to turn one's direction; a big or a small change of situation
  7.  Walla/Tawalla (a'an): [  ولَّي ]  to be averse; to turn away
  8. Irtadda: [اِرْتَدَّ   ]   to revert because of unfavorable conditions
  9. Adbara: [اَدْبَرَ  ]  to turn around and flee

To turn someone/Something   (#35 Phairna) Page
Synonyms:
Aqlaba/Qallaba
Sawrafa
Walla
Radda
LAfat
Afaka
1. Aqlaba/Qallaba    تُقْلَبُونَ
to change someone from one state to another
to turn something or someone
[29:21] Shakir
He punishes whom He pleases and has mercy on whom He pleases, and to Him you shall be turned back.
يُعَذِّبُ مَن يَشَاءُ وَيَرْحَمُ مَن يَشَاءُ   ۖ   وَإِلَيْهِ   تُقْلَبُونَ     ﴿   ٢١   ﴾
[18:18] Shakir
And you might think them awake while they were asleep and We turned them about to the right and to the left, while their dog (lay) outstretching its paws at the entrance; if you looked at them you would certainly turn back from them in flight, and you would certainly be filled with awe because of them.
وَتَحْسَبُهُمْ أَيْقَاظًا وَهُمْ رُقُودٌ   ۚ   وَ  نُقَلِّبُهُمْ   ذَاتَ الْيَمِينِ وَذَاتَ الشِّمَالِ   ۖ   وَكَلْبُهُم بَاسِطٌ ذِرَاعَيْهِ بِالْوَصِيدِ   ۚ   لَوِ اطَّلَعْتَ عَلَيْهِمْ لَوَلَّيْتَ مِنْهُمْ فِرَارًا وَلَمُلِئْتَ مِنْهُمْ رُعْبًا   ﴿   ١٨   ﴾
2.   Saw  rafa   صُرِفَتْ
to roll something
to divert something
[7:47] Sahih International
And when their eyes are turned toward the companions of the Fire, they say, "Our Lord, do not place us with the wrongdoing people."
وَإِذَا   صُرِفَتْ   أَبْصَارُهُمْ تِلْقَاءَ أَصْحَابِ النَّارِ قَالُوا رَبَّنَا لَا تَجْعَلْنَا مَعَ الْقَوْمِ الظَّالِمِينَ   ﴿   ٤٧
3. Walla   وَلِّ
to shun
to stay away or keep away
to turn to
to turn away from
to face towards
[2:144] Sahih International
We have certainly seen the turning of your face, [O Muhammad], toward the heaven, and We will surely   turn you   to a qiblah with which you will be pleased. So turn your face toward al-Masjid al-Haram. And wherever you [believers] are, turn your faces toward it [in prayer]. Indeed, those who have been given the Scripture well know that it is the truth from their Lord. And Allah is not unaware of what they do.
قَدْ نَرَىٰ تَقَلُّبَ وَجْهِكَ فِي السَّمَاءِ   ۖ   فَلَنُ  وَلِّ  يَنَّكَ قِبْلَةً تَرْضَاهَا   ۚ   فَوَلِّ وَجْهَكَ شَطْرَ الْمَسْجِدِ الْحَرَامِ   ۚ   وَحَيْثُ مَا كُنتُمْ فَوَلُّوا وُجُوهَكُمْ شَطْرَهُ   ۗ   وَإِنَّ الَّذِينَ أُوتُوا الْكِتَابَ لَيَعْلَمُونَ أَنَّهُ الْحَقُّ مِن رَّبِّهِمْ   ۗ   وَمَا اللَّـهُ بِغَافِلٍ عَمَّا يَعْمَلُونَ   ﴿   ١٤٤
4. Radda   رُدَّ
to dump
to return a thing
to be sent back
[  12:65] Sahih International
And when they opened their baggage, they found their merchandise returned to them. They said, "O our father, what [more] could we desire? This is our merchandise returned to us. And we will obtain supplies for our family and protect our brother and obtain an increase of a camel's load; that is an easy measurement."
وَلَمَّا فَتَحُوا مَتَاعَهُمْ وَجَدُوا بِضَاعَتَهُمْ رُدَّتْ إِلَيْهِمْ   ۖ   قَالُوا يَا أَبَانَا مَا نَبْغِي   ۖ   هَـٰذِهِ بِضَاعَتُنَا   رُدَّتْ   إِلَيْنَا   ۖ   وَنَمِيرُ أَهْلَنَا وَنَحْفَظُ أَخَانَا وَنَزْدَادُ كَيْلَ بَعِيرٍ   ۖ   ذَٰلِكَ كَيْلٌ يَسِيرٌ   ﴿   ٦٥
5. Lafata    لْفِتَ
to turn something left or right
to turn one's attention
to turn around and face something
[10:78] Yusuf Ali
They said: "Hast thou come to us   to turn us away   from the ways we found our fathers following,- in order that thou and thy brother may have greatness in the land? But not we shall believe in you!"
قَالُوٓا۟ أَجِئْتَنَا   لِتَلْفِتَنَا   عَمَّا وَجَدْنَا عَلَيْهِ ءَابَآءَنَا وَتَكُونَ لَكُمَا ٱلْكِبْرِيَآءُ فِى ٱلْأَرْضِ وَمَا نَحْنُ لَكُمَا بِمُؤْمِنِينَ   ﴿   ٧٨
[11:81] Yusuf Ali
(The Messengers) said: "O Lut! We are Messengers from thy Lord! By no means shall they reach thee! now travel with thy family while yet a part of the night remains, and let not any of you look back: but thy wife (will remain behind): To her will happen what happens to the people. Morning is their time appointed: Is not the morning nigh?"
قَالُوا۟ يَـٰلُوطُ إِنَّا رُسُلُ رَبِّكَ لَن يَصِلُوٓا۟ إِلَيْكَ   ۖ   فَأَسْرِ بِأَهْلِكَ بِقِطْعٍ مِّنَ ٱلَّيْلِ وَلَا   يَلْتَفِتْ   مِنكُمْ أَحَدٌ إِلَّا ٱمْرَأَتَكَ   ۖ   إِنَّهُۥ مُصِيبُهَا مَآ أَصَابَهُمْ   ۚ   إِنَّ مَوْعِدَهُمُ ٱلصُّبْحُ  ۚ   أَلَيْسَ ٱلصُّبْحُ بِقَرِيبٍ   ﴿   ٨١
6. Afaka     لِتَأْفِكَنَا
false charges
spin a tale
white lies
mislead
fabricate
spin the truth around
[  46:22] Ahmed Ali
They said: "Have you come to turn us away from our gods? Then bring upon us what you predict for us, if you are a man of truth."
قَالُوٓا۟ أَجِئْتَنَا   لِتَأْفِكَنَا   عَنْ ءَالِهَتِنَا فَأْتِنَا بِمَا تَعِدُنَآ إِن كُنتَ مِنَ ٱلصَّـٰدِقِينَ   ﴿   ٢٢
Summary:
Taqallabu :[تَقَلَّبُ ] to change completely from the previous condition; to do exactly the opposite
Sawrafa: [ صَرَفَ  ] to turn one's direction
Walla:[ ولَّي  ]   to be averse, to turn away one's attention
Radda: [ رَدّ] to turn away something unwanted
Lafat:[لَفَتَ]  to turn right or left
Afaka:[اَفَكَ  ] to turn towards the wrong direction

To Slip or to make slip ( #36 Phisalna/Phislaana )
Synonyms:
Zalaqa/Azlaqa
Zalla/Azalla
Dahadaw/Adhadaw
Haala (heel)
Rawada
1. Zalaqa     زَلَقًا
opposite is Thabaata (being firm)
to slip, trip, and fall
to be on a slippery slope
[18:40] Yusuf Ali
"It may be that my Lord will give me something better than thy garden, and that He will send on thy garden thunderbolts (by way of reckoning) from heaven, making it (but) slippery sand!-
فَعَسَىٰ رَبِّىٓ أَن يُؤْتِيَنِ خَيْرًا مِّن جَنَّتِكَ وَيُرْسِلَ عَلَيْهَا حُسْبَانًا مِّنَ ٱلسَّمَآءِ فَتُصْبِحَ صَعِيدًا   زَلَقًا   ﴿   ٤٠
(68:51)
2. Zalla    فَأَزَلَّ
opposite is rasaqa
to fall on the face
to be uprooted
to be decieved
to fall in a trap
[2:36] Yusuf Ali
Then did Satan make them slip from the (garden), and get them out of the state (of felicity) in which they had been. We said: "Get ye down, all (ye people), with enmity between yourselves. On earth will be your dwelling-place and your means of livelihood - for a time
فَأَزَلَّ  هُمَا ٱلشَّيْطَـٰنُ عَنْهَا فَأَخْرَجَهُمَا مِمَّا كَانَا فِيهِ   ۖ   وَقُلْنَا ٱهْبِطُوا۟ بَعْضُكُمْ لِبَعْضٍ عَدُوٌّ   ۖ   وَلَكُمْ فِى ٱلْأَرْضِ مُسْتَقَرٌّ وَمَتَـٰعٌ إِلَىٰ حِينٍ   ﴿   ٣٦
3. Dahadaw/Adhadaw     لِيُدْحِضُو
to decline
to refute
to trip and fall
to stumble
not on a firm ground
'dahadawtil hujjah' is when a false argument is made to prove their case
[18:56] Yusuf Ali
We only send the messengers to give Glad Tidings and to give warnings: But the unbelievers dispute with vain argument, in order therewith to weaken the truth, and they treat My Signs as a jest, as also the fact that they are warned!
نُرْسِلُ ٱلْمُرْسَلِينَ إِلَّا مُبَشِّرِينَ وَمُنذِرِينَ   ۚ   وَيُجَـٰدِلُ ٱلَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا۟ بِٱلْبَـٰطِلِ   لِيُدْحِضُو  ا۟ بِهِ ٱلْحَقَّ   ۖ   وَٱتَّخَذُوٓا۟ ءَايَـٰتِى وَمَآ أُنذِرُوا۟ هُزُوًا   ﴿   ٥٦
4. Haal( hiil)    هِيلًا
Sand slipping off from the slope of a sand dune
to be in a unstable motion
[73:14] Yusuf Ali
One Day the earth and the mountains will be in violent commotion. And the mountains will be as a heap of sand poured out and flowing down
يَوْمَ تَرْجُفُ ٱلْأَرْضُ وَٱلْجِبَالُ وَكَانَتِ ٱلْجِبَالُ كَثِيبًا   مَّهِيلًا     ﴿   ١٤
5. Rawada    رَٰوَدتُّهُۥ
to lure
to seduce
[12:51] Yusuf Ali
(The king) said (to the ladies): "What was your affair when ye did seek to seduce Joseph from his (true) self?" The ladies said: "Allah preserve us! no evil know we against him!" Said the 'Aziz's wife: "Now is the truth manifest (to all): it was I who sought to seduce him from his (true) self: He is indeed of those who are (ever) true (and virtuous).
قَالَ مَا خَطْبُكُنَّ إِذْ   رَٰوَدتُّنَّ   يُوسُفَ عَن نَّفْسِهِۦ   ۚ   قُلْنَ حَـٰشَ لِلَّـهِ مَا عَلِمْنَا عَلَيْهِ مِن سُوٓءٍ   ۚ   قَالَتِ ٱمْرَأَتُ ٱلْعَزِيزِ ٱلْـَٔـٰنَ حَصْحَصَ ٱلْحَقُّ أَنَا۠   رَٰوَدتُّهُۥ   عَن نَّفْسِهِۦ وَإِنَّهُۥ لَمِنَ ٱلصَّـٰدِقِينَ   ﴿   ٥١

“  And indeed, those who disbelieve would almost make you slip with their eyes   when they hear the message, and they say, "Indeed, he is mad."   (meaning that they will stare at you with such persistence and attention that you would lose your balance out of fright and terror)

“  And do not take your oaths as [means of] deceit between you, lest a foot slip after it was [once] firm  , and you would taste evil [in this world] for what [people] you diverted from the way of Allah , and you would have [in the Hereafter] a great punishment.”
And   azalla     (اَزَلِّ)     means to loosen a person’s balance or make them slip off in such a way that they are fully uprooted from their original situation. Both terms   zalla     (زَلّ)   and     azalla   (اَزَلِّ)   are used in a literal and a metaphorical context.

(The king said to the women asking what is your truth and reality of that when you staggered and astrayed Joseph from the protection of his conscience and righteousness) – Usmani

(1)       Zalaq زَلَق : to trip or slip unintentionally.
(2)       Zalla   زَلّ   : to slip inadvertently and dislocate by means of uprooting or falling.
(3)       Dahz دَحَضَ     : to slip and lose steadiness hence getting weakened. To be removed.

37. Phal پھل     (Fruit)
Also commonly known as   thamar ثمر , fakeh فاكِه , janni جَنى , ukul اُكل
1.          Thamar ثمر :   means fruit. This is a commonly used word for a variation of fruits including fresh fruit, dry fruit and other type of fruit may also be encompassed in its meaning. The plural of this word is   athmaar اثمار   and   thamraat ثمرات  .
Allah Taa’la says:
Surah Al Baqarah (The Cow)   سُوۡرَةُ البَقَرَة
(2:22)
فَأَخۡرَجَ بِهِۦ مِنَ ٱلثَّمَرَٲتِ رِزۡقً۬ا لَّكُمۡ‌ۖ
“[He] who made for you the earth a bed [spread out] and the sky a ceiling and sent down from the sky, rain and brought forth   thereby fruits as provision for you.   So do not attribute to Allah equals while you know [that there is nothing similar to Him].”
2.          Fakeha فَاكِهَة :   All fruits with the exception of dates, grapes and pomegranate are called   fakeha فَاكِهَة .   And the plural for this is   fawaakeh فواكه   . However, to some scholars, the word   fakeh فاكه   stands for all fruits, including grapes, with the exception of dates and pomegranate. The following ayah of the Holy Quran validates the context of the aforementioned logic:
Surah Al Rahman (The Beneficent)   سُوۡرَةُ الرَّحمٰن
(55:68)
فِيہِمَا فَـٰكِهَةٌ۬ وَنَخۡلٌ۬ وَرُمَّانٌ۬
“  In both of them are fruit and palm trees and pomegranates.  ”
The above ayah verifies that the date-palm and pomegranate are a different category of fruits that do not include in the meaning of   fakeh فاكه   . In other contexts, however,   fawaakeh فواكه   is used for the meaning of dry fruits.   Fakeha فَاكِهَ   means to be lively, carrying a sprightly persona and the capability of amusement and joyfulness.   Fakkaha فَكَّهَ   means to provide or feed fruit to someone   and   it also means to bring joy and pleasure to someone by means of a delightful conversation or speech. It is because of this Ibn-e-Faris believes that   fakeha فكهة   is a fruit that brings relish and pleasure simultaneously.
3.          Janni جنى :   Fresh fruit: meaning such a fruit that has reached its fruition, is ripe and ready to be picked, whether it is still hanging from a tree or has already been picked.   Janni-ya جَنِىَ   means to pick and choose a fruit or to pick it from a tree.
Allah Taa’la says:
Surah Al Rahman (The Beneficent)   سُوۡرَةُ الرَّحمٰن
(55:54)
وَجَنَى ٱلۡجَنَّتَيۡنِ دَانٍ۬
“[They are] reclining on beds whose linings are of silk brocade,   and the fruit of the two gardens is hanging low.  ”
4.          Ukul اُكُل :   Signifies those particular parts of the plants and trees that could be included in the staple diet of a human being. In a contextual Arabic meaning, it signifies fruit, nutrition and bounteous sustenance.
As mentioned in the Holy Quran:
Surah Al Baqarah (The Cow)   سُوۡرَةُ البَقَرَة
(2:265)
كَمَثَلِ جَنَّةِۭ بِرَبۡوَةٍ أَصَابَهَا وَابِلٌ۬
“And the example of those who spend their wealth seeking means to the approval of Allah and assuring [reward for]   themselves is like a garden on high ground which is hit by a downpour - so it yields its fruits in double.   And [even] if it is not hit by a downpour, then a drizzle [is sufficient]. And Allah , of what you do, is Seeing.”
Conclusion:
(1)       Samar ثمر : A common word for fruit.
(2)       Fakeha فاكِه : All fruits withholding the exception of date palm and pomegranate; however in other contexts any delicious fruit or dry fruit.
(3)       Janni جَنى : The fresh and ripe lot of fruit that is either just picked or may still be hanging from a tree.
(4)       Ukul اُكل : The fruitful and feracious parts of a plant or a tree that would be used as nourishment for human beings.

“[He] who made for you the earth a bed [spread out] and the sky a ceiling and sent down from the sky, rain and brought forth thereby fruits as provision for you. So do not attribute to Allah equals while you know [that there is nothing similar to Him].”

 

2.      Fakeha فَاكِهَة : All fruits with the exception of dates, grapes and pomegranate are called fakeha فَاكِهَة . And the plural for this is fawaakeh فواكه . However, to some scholars, the word fakeh فاكه stands for all fruits, including grapes, with the exception of dates and pomegranate. The following ayah of the Holy Quran validates the context of the aforementioned logic:

Surah Al Rahman (The Beneficent) سُوۡرَةُ الرَّحمٰن

(55:68)

فِيہِمَا فَـٰكِهَةٌ۬ وَنَخۡلٌ۬ وَرُمَّانٌ۬

“In both of them are fruit and palm trees and pomegranates.”

The above ayah verifies that the date-palm and pomegranate are a different category of fruits that do not include in the meaning of fakeh فاكه . In other contexts, however, fawaakeh فواكه is used for the meaning of dry fruits. Fakeha فَاكِهَ means to be lively, carrying a sprightly persona and the capability of amusement and joyfulness. Fakkaha فَكَّهَ means to provide or feed fruit to someone and it also means to bring joy and pleasure to someone by means of a delightful conversation or speech. It is because of this Ibn-e-Faris believes that fakeha فكهة is a fruit that brings relish and pleasure simultaneously.

3.      Janni جنى : Fresh fruit: meaning such a fruit that has reached its fruition, is ripe and ready to be picked, whether it is still hanging from a tree or has already been picked. Janni-ya جَنِىَ means to pick and choose a fruit or to pick it from a tree.

Allah Taa’la says:

Surah Al Rahman (The Beneficent) سُوۡرَةُ الرَّحمٰن

(55:54)

وَجَنَى ٱلۡجَنَّتَيۡنِ دَانٍ۬

“[They are] reclining on beds whose linings are of silk brocade, and the fruit of the two gardens is hanging low.”

4.      Ukul اُكُل : Signifies those particular parts of the plants and trees that could be included in the staple diet of a human being. In a contextual Arabic meaning, it signifies fruit, nutrition and bounteous sustenance.

As mentioned in the Holy Quran:

Surah Al Baqarah (The Cow) سُوۡرَةُ البَقَرَة

(2:265)

كَمَثَلِ جَنَّةِۭ بِرَبۡوَةٍ أَصَابَهَا وَابِلٌ۬

“And the example of those who spend their wealth seeking means to the approval of Allah and assuring [reward for] themselves is like a garden on high ground which is hit by a downpour - so it yields its fruits in double. And [even] if it is not hit by a downpour, then a drizzle [is sufficient]. And Allah , of what you do, is Seeing.”

 

Conclusion:

(1)   Samar ثمر : A common word for fruit.

(2)   Fakeha فاكِه : All fruits withholding the exception of date palm and pomegranate; however in other contexts any delicious fruit or dry fruit.

(3)   Janni جَنى : The fresh and ripe lot of fruit that is either just picked or may still be hanging from a tree.

(4)   Ukul اُكل : The fruitful and feracious parts of a plant or a tree that would be used as nourishment for human beings.

38. Phal Pakna پھل پکنا (The ripening of fruits)
Also known as   yana’a يَنَعَ   and   janaa     جَنَى.
1.          Yana’a يَنَعَ :   implies the point at which the fruit has fully ripened and ready. And a ripened and mature fruit is called   yaane’a يَانِعَةٌ   or   mune’aa مُونِعَةٌ   .
Allah Taa’la says:
Surah Al Anaam (The Cattle)   سُوۡرَةُ الاٴنعَام
(6:99)
ٱنظُرُوٓاْ إِلَىٰ ثَمَرِهِۦۤ إِذَآ أَثۡمَرَ وَيَنۡعِهِۦۤ‌ۚ
“  And it is He who sends down rain from the sky, and We produce thereby the growth of all things. We produce from it greenery from which We produce grains arranged in layers. And from the palm trees - of its emerging fruit are clusters hanging low. And [We produce] gardens of grapevines and olives and pomegranates, similar yet varied.   Look at [each of] its fruit when it yields and [at] its ripening.   Indeed in that are signs for a people who believe.”
2.          Janaa جنى : janaa yajnee جنا يجنى :   The lexical or dictionary meaning implies the choosing and picking of ripened fruit. However in the Holy Quran, this word has been used twice signifying the fruit that is ripe and is ready to be picked from a tree.
Allah Taa’la says:
Surah Al Rahman (The Beneficent)   سُوۡرَةُ الرَّحمٰن
(55:54)
وَجَنَى ٱلۡجَنَّتَيۡنِ دَانٍ۬
“[They are] reclining on beds whose linings are of silk brocade,   and the fruit of the two gardens is hanging low.  ”
At another location in the Holy Quran,
Surah Al Maryam  (Mary)   سُوۡرَةُ مَریَم
(19:25)
وَهُزِّىٓ إِلَيۡكِ بِجِذۡعِ ٱلنَّخۡلَةِ تُسَـٰقِطۡ عَلَيۡكِ رُطَبً۬ا جَنِيًّ۬
“And shake toward you the trunk of the palm tree; it will drop upon you ripe, fresh dates.”
Conclusion:
(1)       Yana’a يَنَعَ : The ripening of the fruit.
(2)       Janaa جَنَى : The point of ripening at which if the fruit is not picked, it would fall from the tree by itself. The picking of a ripened fruit.
For   ‘Phootna’ پھوٹنا    (splitting out/leaking out), see   ‘chashma pootna’ چشمہ پھوٹنا    (spring or fountain leaking/splitting out)

39. Phoonkna – phoonk marna
پھونکنا - پھونک مارنا ( To blow/to blow out/breathe into)
Also known as   nafakha نفخ , naqara نقر , nafatha نفث , atfaa اطفَاَ (tafaa) طَفَاَء .
1.          Nafakha نفخ :   means the inflation of one’s stomach. A derivation   manfookh منفوخ    is used for a plump or fat person or a person with a large belly.   Nafakha نفخ    means to enter air into a body by means of blowing into or breathing into. And in context,   nafakha نفخ    stands for just the action of blowing air. However,   manfaakh منفاخ    is known to be the bellows that belongs to a blacksmith.
In the Holy Quran,
Surah Al-E-Imran (The Family of Imran)   سُوۡرَةُ آل عِمرَان
(3:49)
فَأَنفُخُ فِيهِ فَيَكُونُ طَيۡرَۢا بِإِذۡنِ ٱللَّهِ‌ۖ
“And [make him] a messenger to the Children of Israel, [who will say], 'Indeed I have come to you with a sign from your Lord in that I design for you from clay [that which is] like the form of a bird,   then I breathe into it and it becomes a bird by permission of Allah .   And I cure the blind and the leper, and I give life to the dead - by permission of Allah. And I inform you of what you eat and what you store in your houses. Indeed in that is a sign for you, if you are believers.  ”
2.          Naqara نقر :   means to run an instrument by breathing air into it; an instrument that creates vibration and sound.   Naqoor ناقور    stands for anything and everything that is hollow and coarse. For example, a clarion, bugle, a trumpet or any instrument as such.
In the Holy Quran,
Surah Al Muddaththir (The Cloaked One)   سُوۡرَةُ المدَّثِّر
(74:8)
فَإِذَا نُقِرَ فِى ٱلنَّاقُورِ
“And when the trumpet is blown,”
3.          Nafatha نَفَثَ :   means to spit out in form of exudation. It also means to blow a spell (such as witchcraft) or exude virulence and toxicity.   Nafth-ud-dam نَفثُ الدّم    is known for a disease in which there is excretion of blood with the saliva.
In the Holy Quran,
Surah Al Falaq (The Dawn)   سُوۡرَةُ الفَلَق
(113:4)
وَمِن شَرِّ ٱلنَّفَّـٰثَـٰتِ فِى ٱلۡعُقَ
“And from the evil of the blowers in knots”
(Oh Allah, we seek refuge with You)
4.          Atfaa اَطفَاَ : Tafa’at-in-naar طَفَئَتِ النَّار   means the extinguishing of a fire.   Atfa’a     اَطفَاَ   means to extinguish a fire by means of blowing air to it. The same term is used in expression of putting out a source of light such as a candle or a lamp.
Allah Taa’la says:
Surah As-Saff (The Ranks)   سُوۡرَةُ الصَّف
(61:8)
يُرِيدُونَ لِيُطۡفِـُٔواْ نُورَ ٱللَّهِ بِأَفۡوَٲهِهِمۡ
“  They want to extinguish the light of Allah with their mouths,   but Allah will perfect His light, although the disbelievers dislike it.  ”
Conclusion:
(1)       Nafakha نفخ : Commonly used to express the action of blowing out or breathing into. And in other places, it also suggests the breathing of air into a body.
(2)       Naqara نقر : To breathe into or blow into a hollow instrument that creates a sound or vibration.
(3)       Nafatha نفث : To exude. The action of blowing a spell by the one who performs witchcraft.
(4)       Atfaa اطفَاَ : To put out or extinguish a fire or a lamp by means of blowing air out.
For   “Phaelnaa” پھیلانا   (spreading out), see   “bikharnaa” بکھرنا    (scattering out)

4. Paana پانا (To get/ to find)
Also known as ‘Wajad’ وَجَد, ‘thaqaf’ ثَقَفَ, ‘alfaa’ اَلفَى and ‘Adrak’ اَدرَك
1.          Wajad وَجَد  : To find the presence of something. This is a commonly used word and can be used anywhere.
In the Holy Quran,
Surah Al-e-Imran (Family of Imran)   سُوۡرَةُ آل عِمرَان
(3:37)
كُلَّمَا دَخَلَ عَلَيۡهَا زَكَرِيَّا ٱلۡمِحۡرَابَ وَجَدَ عِندَهَا رِزۡقً۬ا‌ۖ
“So her Lord accepted her with good acceptance and caused her to grow in a good manner and put her in the care of Zechariah.   Every time Zechariah entered upon her in the prayer chamber, he found with her provision.   He said, "O Mary, from where is this [coming] to you?" She said, "It is from Allah. Indeed, Allah provides for whom He wills without account."
2.          Thaqaf   ثَقَفَ: It means for one to be meticulous and skillful while in the process of acquiring something. ‘Thaqaf fin’ ثقف فِن is known to be a skillful master of war and combat. ‘Thaqeef’ ثقِيف means wise and clever. ‘Thaqafat’ ثقَافت means wisdom and skillfulness. ‘Thaqaf’ ثَقَفَ means to get or find someone, dress down and rebuke and then conquer them.
Allah Taa’la says:
Surah Al Baqarah (The Cow)   سُوۡرَةُ البَقَرَة
(2:191)
وَٱقۡتُلُوهُمۡ حَيۡثُ ثَقِفۡتُمُوهُمۡ وَأَخۡرِجُوهُم مِّنۡ حَيۡثُ أَخۡرَجُوكُمۡ‌ۚ
“  And kill them wherever you overtake them and expel them from wherever they have expelled you  , and fitnah is worse than killing. And do not fight them at al-Masjid al- Haram until they fight you there. But if they fight you, then kill them. Such is the recompense of the disbelievers.”
In another location, for a similar situation the word ‘wajd’   وَجَد   has been used instead of ‘thaqaf’   ثَقَفَ  , which implies the generality of ‘wajd’   وَجَد  .
Allah Taa’la says:
Surah An Nisa (The Women)   سُوۡرَةُ النِّسَاء
(4:89)
فَخُذُوهُمۡ وَٱقۡتُلُوهُمۡ حَيۡثُ وَجَدتُّمُوهُمۡ‌ۖ
“They wish you would disbelieve as they disbelieved so you would be alike. So do not take from among them allies until they emigrate for the cause of Allah . But if they turn away, then seize them   and kill them wherever you find them   and take not from among them any ally or helper.”
3.          Alfaa   اَلفَى: ‘Lafu’ لفو  means for something to uncover by losing its veil/cover. ‘Alfaa’ اَلفَى means for something to disclose/come into knowledge or reveal itself.
In the Holy Quran:
Surah Al Yusuf (Joseph)   سُوۡرَةُ یُوسُف
(12:25)
وَٱسۡتَبَقَا ٱلۡبَابَ وَقَدَّتۡ قَمِيصَهُ ۥ مِن دُبُرٍ۬ وَأَلۡفَيَا سَيِّدَهَا لَدَا ٱلۡبَابِ‌ۚ
“  And they both raced to the door, and she tore his shirt from the back, and they found her husband at the door.   She said, "What is the recompense of one who intended evil for your wife but that he be imprisoned or a painful punishment?"
In another location in the Holy Quran,
Surah Al Baqarah (The Cow)   سُوۡرَةُ البَقَرَة
(2:170)
قَالُواْ بَلۡ نَتَّبِعُ مَآ أَلۡفَيۡنَا عَلَيۡهِ ءَابَآءَنَآ‌ۗ
“And when it is said to them, "Follow what Allah has revealed,"   they say, "Rather, we will follow that which we found our fathers doing."   Even though their fathers understood nothing, nor were they guided?”
In the above ayah, the use of the word ‘alfaa’ اَلفَى has been in a context that something has been handed down to them by their ancestors. In a different location, but a similar situation, the words ‘wajd’ وَجَد has been used instead of ‘alfaa’ اَلفَى proving the generality of the word ‘wajd’ وَجَد.
Allah Taa’la says:
Surah Al Maidah (The Table Spread)   سُوۡرَةُ المَائدة
(5:104)
قَالُواْ حَسۡبُنَا مَا وَجَدۡنَا عَلَيۡهِ ءَابَآءَنَآ‌ۚ
“And when it is said to them, "Come to what Allah has revealed and to the Messenger," they say, "  Sufficient for us is that upon which we found our fathers.  " Even though their fathers knew nothing, nor were they guided?”
4.          Adrak   اَدرَك: ‘Darak’ درَك and ‘Darj’ درج are two words meaning the same thing. While climbing up the stairs, it is called ‘darj’ درج or ‘darjah’ درجَة, and while climbing down the stairs it is called ‘darak’ درَك. It is because of this the phrases ‘darjat-ul-jannah’ درجَتُ الجَنَّة and ‘darkat-un-naar’ دركَاتُ النَار are used.
Allah Taa’la says:
Surah An Nisa (The Women)   سُوۡرَةُ النِّسَاء
(4:145)
إِنَّ ٱلۡمُنَـٰفِقِينَ فِى ٱلدَّرۡكِ ٱلۡأَسۡفَلِ مِنَ ٱلنَّارِ
“  Indeed, the hypocrites will be in the lowest depths of the Fire   - and never will you find for them a helper -”
‘Adrak’   اَدرَك   means for something to, step by step, reach its limit or extremity. ‘Adrak uth-thamar’ اَدرَكَ الثّمَرُ would mean a fruit that reaches its fruition and ‘adrak al-wald’ اَدرَكَ الوَلد would mean for a boy to reach maturity/puberty. According to Ibn-e-Faris, it means for one thing to grasp or merge with another. (to catch it, grab it or occupy or take over). For more details, see ‘Girana’ گرانا (to demolish, spill, bring down)
Allah Taa’la says:
Surah Al Anaam (The Cattle)   سُوۡرَةُ الاٴنعَام
(6:103)
لَّا تُدۡرِڪُهُ ٱلۡأَبۡصَـٰرُ وَهُوَ يُدۡرِكُ ٱلۡأَبۡصَـٰرَ‌ۖ
“  Vision perceives Him not, but He perceives [all] vision  ; and He is the Subtle, the Acquainted”
Conclusion:
(1)       Wajd وَجَد: To find the presence of something. It is used commonly.
(2)       Thaqaf ثَقَفَ: To be meticulous and skillful while achieving or acquiring something. To get hold of required individuals during a war.
(3)       Alfaa اَلفَى: To find something coincidentally or by chance. To discover something as it uncovers itself or loses its veil. For one to find out/discover something by themselves.
(4)       Adrak اَدرَك: To gain something by reaching to its limits.

كُلَّمَا دَخَلَ عَلَيۡهَا زَكَرِيَّا ٱلۡمِحۡرَابَ وَجَدَ عِندَهَا رِزۡقً۬ا‌ۖ

“So her Lord accepted her with good acceptance and caused her to grow in a good manner and put her in the care of Zechariah. Every time Zechariah entered upon her in the prayer chamber, he found with her provision. He said, "O Mary, from where is this [coming] to you?" She said, "It is from Allah. Indeed, Allah provides for whom He wills without account."

2.      Thaqaf ثَقَفَ: It means for one to be meticulous and skillful while in the process of acquiring something. ‘Thaqaf fin’ ثقف فِن is known to be a skillful master of war and combat. ‘Thaqeef’ ثقِيف means wise and clever. ‘Thaqafat’ ثقَافت means wisdom and skillfulness. ‘Thaqaf’ ثَقَفَ means to get or find someone, dress down and rebuke and then conquer them.

Allah Taa’la says:

Surah Al Baqarah (The Cow) سُوۡرَةُ البَقَرَة

(2:191)

وَٱقۡتُلُوهُمۡ حَيۡثُ ثَقِفۡتُمُوهُمۡ وَأَخۡرِجُوهُم مِّنۡ حَيۡثُ أَخۡرَجُوكُمۡ‌ۚ

“And kill them wherever you overtake them and expel them from wherever they have expelled you, and fitnah is worse than killing. And do not fight them at al-Masjid al- Haram until they fight you there. But if they fight you, then kill them. Such is the recompense of the disbelievers.”

In another location, for a similar situation the word ‘wajd’ وَجَد has been used instead of ‘thaqaf’ ثَقَفَ, which implies the generality of ‘wajd’ وَجَد.

Allah Taa’la says:

Surah An Nisa (The Women) سُوۡرَةُ النِّسَاء

(4:89)

فَخُذُوهُمۡ وَٱقۡتُلُوهُمۡ حَيۡثُ وَجَدتُّمُوهُمۡ‌ۖ

“They wish you would disbelieve as they disbelieved so you would be alike. So do not take from among them allies until they emigrate for the cause of Allah . But if they turn away, then seize them and kill them wherever you find them and take not from among them any ally or helper.”

3.      Alfaa اَلفَى: ‘Lafu’ لفو  means for something to uncover by losing its veil/cover. ‘Alfaa’ اَلفَى means for something to disclose/come into knowledge or reveal itself.

In the Holy Quran:

Surah Al Yusuf (Joseph) سُوۡرَةُ یُوسُف

(12:25)

وَٱسۡتَبَقَا ٱلۡبَابَ وَقَدَّتۡ قَمِيصَهُ ۥ مِن دُبُرٍ۬ وَأَلۡفَيَا سَيِّدَهَا لَدَا ٱلۡبَابِ‌ۚ

“And they both raced to the door, and she tore his shirt from the back, and they found her husband at the door. She said, "What is the recompense of one who intended evil for your wife but that he be imprisoned or a painful punishment?"

In another location in the Holy Quran,

Surah Al Baqarah (The Cow) سُوۡرَةُ البَقَرَة

(2:170)

قَالُواْ بَلۡ نَتَّبِعُ مَآ أَلۡفَيۡنَا عَلَيۡهِ ءَابَآءَنَآ‌ۗ

“And when it is said to them, "Follow what Allah has revealed," they say, "Rather, we will follow that which we found our fathers doing." Even though their fathers understood nothing, nor were they guided?”

In the above ayah, the use of the word ‘alfaa’ اَلفَى has been in a context that something has been handed down to them by their ancestors. In a different location, but a similar situation, the words ‘wajd’ وَجَد has been used instead of ‘alfaa’ اَلفَى proving the generality of the word ‘wajd’ وَجَد.

Allah Taa’la says:

Surah Al Maidah (The Table Spread) سُوۡرَةُ المَائدة

(5:104)

 قَالُواْ حَسۡبُنَا مَا وَجَدۡنَا عَلَيۡهِ ءَابَآءَنَآ‌ۚ

“And when it is said to them, "Come to what Allah has revealed and to the Messenger," they say, "Sufficient for us is that upon which we found our fathers." Even though their fathers knew nothing, nor were they guided?”

4.      Adrak اَدرَك: ‘Darak’ درَك and ‘Darj’ درج are two words meaning the same thing. While climbing up the stairs, it is called ‘darj’ درج or ‘darjah’ درجَة, and while climbing down the stairs it is called ‘darak’ درَك. It is because of this the phrases ‘darjat-ul-jannah’ درجَتُ الجَنَّة and ‘darkat-un-naar’ دركَاتُ النَار are used.

Allah Taa’la says:

Surah An Nisa (The Women) سُوۡرَةُ النِّسَاء

(4:145)

إِنَّ ٱلۡمُنَـٰفِقِينَ فِى ٱلدَّرۡكِ ٱلۡأَسۡفَلِ مِنَ ٱلنَّارِ

“Indeed, the hypocrites will be in the lowest depths of the Fire - and never will you find for them a helper -”

‘Adrak’ اَدرَك means for something to, step by step, reach its limit or extremity. ‘Adrak uth-thamar’ اَدرَكَ الثّمَرُ would mean a fruit that reaches its fruition and ‘adrak al-wald’ اَدرَكَ الوَلد would mean for a boy to reach maturity/puberty. According to Ibn-e-Faris, it means for one thing to grasp or merge with another. (to catch it, grab it or occupy or take over). For more details, see ‘Girana’ گرانا (to demolish, spill, bring down)

Allah Taa’la says:

Surah Al Anaam (The Cattle) سُوۡرَةُ الاٴنعَام

(6:103)

لَّا تُدۡرِڪُهُ ٱلۡأَبۡصَـٰرُ وَهُوَ يُدۡرِكُ ٱلۡأَبۡصَـٰرَ‌ۖ

“Vision perceives Him not, but He perceives [all] vision; and He is the Subtle, the Acquainted”

Conclusion:

(1)   Wajd وَجَد: To find the presence of something. It is used commonly.

(2)   Thaqaf ثَقَفَ: To be meticulous and skillful while achieving or acquiring something. To get hold of required individuals during a war.

(3)   Alfaa اَلفَى: To find something coincidentally or by chance. To discover something as it uncovers itself or loses its veil. For one to find out/discover something by themselves.

(4)   Adrak اَدرَك: To gain something by reaching to its limits.

40. Phaelnaa پھیلنا (To spread out)
Also known as   zara’aa زَرَاَ , mad’daa مَدَّ , dahaa دَحَى , tahaa طَحَى , nasharaa نَشَرَ , basataa بَسَطَ    and   baththaa بَثَّ .
1.          Zara’aa زَرَاَ :     Zar’aa زرءَ    is anything and everything that is sown and cultivated.   Zara’a al arz  زَرَاَ الاَرض   means to sow a seed in the ground and the Arabic scholars (صاحب منتہی الادب )consider its meaning as to create, grow and develop or to raise. The term   zurri-ya زُرِّيَّة    is driven from it, the meaning of which deals with the progeny of the mankind and the jinn. The Holy Quran, too, accentuates the connotation of the Arabic scholars (صاحب منتہی الادب ) . For example,
(a)        The meaning of ‘creating’ would be:
Surah Al A’raaf (The Heights)   سُوۡرَةُ الاٴعرَاف
(7:179)
وَلَقَدۡ ذَرَأۡنَا لِجَهَنَّمَ ڪَثِيرً۬ا مِّنَ ٱلۡجِنِّ وَٱلۡإِنسِ‌ۖ
“  And We have certainly created for Hell many of the jinn and mankind.   They have hearts with which they do not understand, they have eyes with which they do not see, and they have ears with which they do not hear. Those are like livestock; rather, they are more astray. It is they who are the heedless.  ”
(b)       The meaning of ‘spreading out’ or ‘growing’ would be:
Surah Al Mulk (The Sovereignty)     سُوۡرَةُ المُلک
(67:24)
قُلۡ هُوَ ٱلَّذِى ذَرَأَكُمۡ فِى ٱلۡأَرۡضِ وَإِلَيۡهِ تُحۡشَرُونَ
“Say, " It is He who has multiplied you throughout the earth, and to Him you will be gathered.”
2.          Mad’daa مَدَّ :    To stretch something in length thus spreading it out; in a way that   mad’daa مَدَّ     would mean to elongate and extend in length, and expand it in spread.
Allah Taa’la says:
Surah Al Furqan (The Criterion)   سُوۡرَةُ الفُرقان
(25:45)
أَلَمۡ تَرَ إِلَىٰ رَبِّكَ كَيۡفَ مَدَّ ٱلظِّلَّ
“  Have you not considered your Lord - how He extends the shadow,   and if He willed, He could have made it stationary? Then We made the sun for it an indication.”
3.          Dahaa دَحَى , Tahaaha طَحَى :   Realistically they are the same words. The only difference that lies at all is of the pronunciation, or the cultural intonation or accent that gives precedence. Having said that, meaning of this word is to spread something out far and wide. The detailed features and particularities have been illuminated previously in the term   “bichaana” بچھانا    (to lay something down)
4.             Nasharaa نَشَرَ :    This means to broadcast or propagate something, to spread news. The antonym of   nasharaa نَشَرَ    would be   tawaee طوى   , which means to enwrap or envelop something. When it is said that   nasharat-ul-kitaaba summa tawaeetuh’ نشرتُ الكتابَ ثم طويته    it would mean ‘I opened a book and then I closed it.’
Allah Taa’la says:
Surah Ash Shura (Consultation)   سُوۡرَةُ الشّوریٰ
(42:28)
وَهُوَ ٱلَّذِى يُنَزِّلُ ٱلۡغَيۡثَ مِنۢ بَعۡدِ مَا قَنَطُواْ وَيَنشُرُ رَحۡمَتَهُ ۥ‌ۚ
“  And it is He who sends down the rain after they had despaired and spreads His mercy.   And He is the Protector, the Praiseworthy.”
5.          Basataa بَسَطَ      :   means to open, spread and expand something.   Bisaat بساط    would also mean a land that is large and extended. Also known as   wusa’at وسعت   , the antonym of which is   qabz قبض    (2:245) and also,   qadr قدر    (13:26)
Allah Taa’la says:
Surah Al Room (The Romans)   سُوۡرَةُ الرُّوم
(30:48)
ٱللَّهُ ٱلَّذِى يُرۡسِلُ ٱلرِّيَـٰحَ فَتُثِيرُ سَحَابً۬ا فَيَبۡسُطُهُ ۥ فِى ٱلسَّمَآءِ كَيۡفَ يَشَآءُ
“  It is Allah who sends the winds, and they stir the clouds and spread them in the sky however He wills  , and He makes them fragments so you see the rain emerge from within them. And when He causes it to fall upon whom He wills of His servants, immediately they rejoice  ”
6.          Baththaa بَثَّ :   means to disperse, derange or disarrange.   Baththaa بَثَّ    also implies a feeling of extreme perplexity and great depression; as though   baththaa بَثَّ   would be used in a context of something whose constituents are dispersed or scattered. For example pollution in the air (56:6) or the moth around a fire (candle).
Allah Taa’la says:
Surah An Nisa (The Women)   سُوۡرَةُ النِّسَاء
(4:1)
يَـٰٓأَيُّہَا ٱلنَّاسُ ٱتَّقُواْ رَبَّكُمُ ٱلَّذِى خَلَقَكُم مِّن نَّفۡسٍ۬ وَٲحِدَةٍ۬ وَخَلَقَ مِنۡہَا زَوۡجَهَا وَبَثَّ مِنۡہُمَا رِجَالاً۬ كَثِيرً۬ا وَنِسَآءً۬‌ۚ
“  O mankind, fear your Lord, who created you from one soul and created from it its mate and dispersed from both of them many men and women  . And fear Allah , through whom you ask one another, and the wombs. Indeed Allah is ever, over you, an Observer.  ”
Conclusion:
(1)       Zara’aa زَرَاَ : means to create and spread.
(2)       Mad’daa مَدَّ : To stretch and extend something in length.
(3)       Dahaa دَحَى , Tahaa طَحَى : To spread something out far and wide.
(4)       Nasharaa نَشَرَ : To broadcast and propagate something.
(5)       Basataa بَسَطَ      : To open and spread something, and expand(widen) it.
(6)       Baththaa بَثَّ : To spread something in a way that the contents are scattered, dispersed and disordered.

41. Phaenknaa پھینکنا (To throw)
Also known as   nabaza نَبَزَ , tarahaa طَرَحَ , rajama رَجَمَ , ramaa رَمَى , qazafa قَضَفَ    and   jafa’a جَفَاَ .
1.          Nabaza نَبَزَ :   means to throw something away after considering it as a reasonably less important deal. To toss something behind in a carefree approach.
Allah Taa’la says:
Surah Al Baqarah (The Cow)   سُوۡرَةُ البَقَرَة
(2:100)
أَوَڪُلَّمَا عَـٰهَدُواْ عَهۡدً۬ا نَّبَذَهُ ۥ فَرِيقٌ۬ مِّنۡهُم‌ۚ
“  Is it not [true] that every time they took a covenant a party of them threw it away?   But, [in fact], most of them do not believe.  ”
2.          Tarahaa طَرَحَ :    To discard and throw something away with the understanding of it being futile and worthless; when something is casted away, carefully avoiding the attention of people. It is said   raa’aituhu min tarha رَاَئتُهُ مِن طَرح    meaning, ‘I saw him from a distance.’   Tarooh طروح    stands for a remote location.   Al-tarhaa الطرح    is any object that is valueless and therefore discarded and thrown away.
In the Holy Quran:
Surah Al Yusuf (Joseph)   سُوۡرَةُ یُوسُف
(12:9)
ٱقۡتُلُواْ يُوسُفَ أَوِ ٱطۡرَحُوهُ أَرۡضً۬ا يَخۡلُ لَكُمۡ وَجۡهُ أَبِيكُمۡ
“  Kill Joseph or cast him out to [another] land; the countenance of your father will [then] be only for you  , and you will be after that a righteous people."
3.          Rajama رَجَمَ :   To stone somebody to death; assassinate them by means of lapidation.
In the Holy Quran:
Surah Al Kahf (The Cave)   سُوۡرَةُ الکهف
(18:20)
إِنَّہُمۡ إِن يَظۡهَرُواْ عَلَيۡكُمۡ يَرۡجُمُوكُمۡ أَوۡ يُعِيدُوڪُمۡ فِى مِلَّتِهِمۡ
“  Indeed, if they come to know of you, they will stone you or return you to their religion.   And never would you succeed, then - ever."
4, 5. Ramaa رَمَى   , Qazafa قَضَفَ   :    Both of these words share a similar meaning, signifying stone. To throw a stone or a pebble at a distance or from a distance. The basic difference is that   ramaa رَمَى    is normally used to express the throwing of materialistic or concrete matter.
Allah Taa’la says:
Surah Al Anfal (The Spoils of War)   سُوۡرَةُ الاٴنفَال
(8:17)
وَمَا رَمَيۡتَ إِذۡ رَمَيۡتَ وَلَـٰكِنَّ ٱللَّهَ رَمَىٰ‌ۚ
“And you did not kill them, but it was Allah who killed them.   And you threw not, [O Muhammad], when you threw, but it was Allah who threw   that He might test the believers with a good test. Indeed, Allah is Hearing and Knowing.”
In the same way, the legitimate terminology of   rami-aljamaar رمى الجمار   is also covered under the same meaning implying that the Muslim pilgrims (Haaji) perform the stoning of Satan (Shaitaan) at the location of Mina. The meaning of   Qazafa  قَضَفَ   is linguistically used, as though   had-e-qazaf   حد قزف     (the limit of transgression) is a well known terminology implying the restriction and limit to accuse or charge a person of a crime or delinquency. Bearing this context in mind,
In the Holy Quran,
Surah Al – Ahzab (The Combined Forces)   سُوۡرَةُ الاٴحزَاب
(33:26)

“And He brought down those who supported them among the People of the Scripture from their fortresses   and cast terror into their hearts [so that] a party you killed, and you took captive a party  .”
However, later on, both these words   ramaa رَمَى    and   qazafa قَضَفَ           began to be used in the same context and meaning. Therefore, in the Holy Quran, the word   ramee رَمى    has been used semantically as well.

6. (6) Jafa’a جَفَاَ : The action of a river throwing out its foam on its banks or of a utensil throwing out its discarded boiled contents on the sides.

Also known as nabaza نَبَزَ , tarahaa طَرَحَ , rajama رَجَمَ , ramaa رَمَى , qazafa قَضَفَ  and jafa’a جَفَاَ .

1.      Nabaza نَبَزَ : means to throw something away after considering it as a reasonably less important deal. To toss something behind in a carefree approach.

“Is it not [true] that every time they took a covenant a party of them threw it away? But, [in fact], most of them do not believe.”

 

2.      Tarahaa طَرَحَ :  To discard and throw something away with the understanding of it being futile and worthless; when something is casted away, carefully avoiding the attention of people. It is said raa’aituhu min tarha رَاَئتُهُ مِن طَرح  meaning, ‘I saw him from a distance.’ Tarooh طروح  stands for a remote location. Al-tarhaa الطرح  is any object that is valueless and therefore discarded and thrown away.

In the Holy Quran:

Surah Al Yusuf (Joseph) سُوۡرَةُ یُوسُف

(12:9)

ٱقۡتُلُواْ يُوسُفَ أَوِ ٱطۡرَحُوهُ أَرۡضً۬ا يَخۡلُ لَكُمۡ وَجۡهُ أَبِيكُمۡ

“Kill Joseph or cast him out to [another] land; the countenance of your father will [then] be only for you, and you will be after that a righteous people."

 

3.      Rajama رَجَمَ : To stone somebody to death; assassinate them by means of lapidation.

In the Holy Quran:

Surah Al Kahf (The Cave) سُوۡرَةُ الکهف

(18:20)

إِنَّہُمۡ إِن يَظۡهَرُواْ عَلَيۡكُمۡ يَرۡجُمُوكُمۡ أَوۡ يُعِيدُوڪُمۡ فِى مِلَّتِهِمۡ

42. Pyasaa – Pyasaa Hona پیاسا - پیاسا ہونا (Thirsty – To be Thirsty)
Also known as   zam’aan ظَماَن , wird وِرد , heem هِيم   and   lahatha لَهَث .
1.          Zam’aan ظَماَن : zama’aa ظَمَاَ    means to be thirsty or athirst.   Zam’un ظَماٌ    means thirst. In addition, the word   zam’un ظَماٌ   is the superlative degree of the word   atshaa عَطشَ   which means thirst.   Zam’aan ظَماَن   is a constituent of the hyperbolic noun, i.e. a person losing patience due to thirst. Extreme thirst.
In the Holy Quran,
Surah Al Noor (The Light)   سُوۡرَةُ النُّور
(24:39)
وَٱلَّذِينَ ڪَفَرُوٓاْ أَعۡمَـٰلُهُمۡ كَسَرَابِۭ بِقِيعَةٍ۬ يَحۡسَبُهُ ٱلظَّمۡـَٔانُ مَآءً
“  But those who disbelieved - their deeds are like a mirage in a lowland which a thirsty one thinks is water   until, when he comes to it, he finds it is nothing but finds Allah before Him, and He will pay him in full his due; and Allah is swift in account.”
2.          Wird وِرد :   A thirsty person or a caravan that has set out in the quest of water.   Warada وَرَدَ   means to reach to a pier or a quay in order to drink water.   Wird وِرد    and   morood مَورُود   would mean a pier of water. The antonym of   warada وَرَدَ    is   sadaraa     صَدَرَ   which means to return after drinking the water.
Allah Taa’la says:
Surah Al Maryam (Mary)   سُوۡرَةُ مَریَم
(19:86)
وَنَسُوقُ ٱلۡمُجۡرِمِينَ إِلَىٰ جَهَنَّمَ وِرۡدً۬ا
“And will drive the criminals to Hell in thirst”
3.          Heem هِيم : (al-heyaam)     الهيام    an extreme thirst.   Haama هَامَ    means to be extremely thirsty.   Hayaam هَيَام ,   on the other hand, is an illness manifested in a camel in which the camel suffers from extreme thirst.   Heem هِيم   is an extremely thirsty camel that is suffering from an illness causing his thirst to be unquenchable.
Allah Taa’la says:
Surah Al Waqia (The Inevitable)   سُوۡرَةُ الواقِعَة
(56:54-55)
فَشَـٰرِبُونَ عَلَيۡهِ مِنَ ٱلۡحَمِيمِ (  ﻿  ٥٤  ﻿  ) فَشَـٰرِبُونَ شُرۡبَ ٱلۡهِيمِ
“And drinking on top of it from scalding water;   And will drink as the drinking of thirsty camels.”
4.          Lahatha لَهَث :   The action of one’s tongue sticking out and panting due to an extreme degree of thirst. However, in other connotations, this word is also used to describe both thirst and depression or helplessness.   Luhthaa-tun لُهثَةٌ    is extreme thirst and   lahaath لهاث    is a thirst that is caused by an inner cause of heat.
Allah Taa’la says:
Surah Al Araf (The Heights)   سُوۡرَةُ الاٴعرَاف
(7:176)
فَمَثَلُهُ ۥ كَمَثَلِ ٱلۡڪَلۡبِ إِن تَحۡمِلۡ عَلَيۡهِ يَلۡهَثۡ
“And if We had willed, we could have elevated him thereby, but he adhered [instead] to the earth and followed his own desire.   So his example is like that of the dog: if you chase him, he pants, or if you leave him, he [still] pants.   That is the example of the people who denied Our signs. So relate the stories that perhaps they will give thought.”
Conclusion:
(1)       Zam’aan  ظَماَن : Impatient due to thirst.
(2)       Wird وِرد : A thirsty person setting out in order to search for water.
(3)       Heem هِيم : An extremely thirsty person whose thirstiness is unquenchable.
(4)       Lahatha لَهَث : The sticking out of the tongue due to extreme thirst.

43. Pyaala پیالہ (Cup/ Vessel)
Also known as   akwaab اَكوَاب , kaas كَاس , saqaaya سَقَايَة    and   suwaa’a صُوَاع .
1.          Akwaab اَكوَاب :   is the plural of   koob كوُب.     Koob كوُب   is known to be a cup or a bowl without a handle (a drinking glass, for example). And if the cup has a handle, then it is called   kooz كوُز   . However, if the vessel has a handle and a spout, in that case it is called   ibreeq اِبريق   , the plural of which, is   abareeq اباريق   . For example a jug or a pitcher.
2.          Kaas كَاس :   A cup filled with a drink. A drinking cup or a glass overflowing with the drink. If, however, the cup is empty, then it is called   qadah قدح   .   Kaas كَاس    is normally used to describe a cup full of wine. In addition,   kaas كَاس    also means wine itself.
Allah Taa’la says:
Surah Al Waqia (The Inevitable)   سُوۡرَةُ الواقِعَة
(56:17-18)
يَطُوفُ عَلَيۡہِمۡ وِلۡدَٲنٌ۬ مُّخَلَّدُونَ (  ﻿  ١٧  ﻿  ) بِأَكۡوَابٍ۬ وَأَبَارِيقَ وَكَأۡسٍ۬ مِّن مَّعِينٍ۬
“There will circulate among them young boys made eternal;   With vessels, pitchers and a cup [of wine] from a flowing spring”
3.          Saqaaya سَقَايَة : Saqaa’     سَقَى   means the action to have someone to drink water or the action to serve any drink to someone.   Siqayaa سَقَايَة    also means to have someone drink water, and is also known to be the vessel or pot from which one drinks.
In the Holy Quran,
Surah Yusuf (Joseph)   سُوۡرَةُ یُوسُف
(16:70)
فَلَمَّا جَهَّزَهُم بِجَهَازِهِمۡ جَعَلَ ٱلسِّقَايَةَ فِى رَحۡلِ أَخِيهِ
“  So when he had furnished them with their supplies, he put the [gold measuring] bowl into the bag of his brother.   Then an announcer called out, "O caravan, indeed you are thieves."
4.          Suwaa’a صُوَاع :   Also   siwaa’ صِوَاع    mean a drinking cup or a drinking vessel that is made out of gold or silver. If, however, the vessel is made out of glass it is called   qadah قدح ;   if it is a wooden vessel, it is called   u’uss عُس ;   if it is made out of leather, then   a’albah عَلبَه ;   and in case it is made out of clay, then it is called   markan مركن   .(Al-Jamaal Wal-Kamaal- Salman Mansur Puri 174). It must be clarified that this word is not derived from the word   saa’ صاع   , meaning: a known measurement.
Allah Taa’la says:
Surah Yusuf (Joseph)     سُوۡرَةُ یُوسُف
(12:72)
قَالُواْ نَفۡقِدُ صُوَاعَ ٱلۡمَلِكِ
“They said, "We are missing the measure of the king.   And for he who produces it is [the reward of] a camel's load, and I am responsible for it."
Conclusion:
(1)       Akwaab  اَكوَاب: Plural of   koob  , meaning: a cup or a vessel without a handle.
(2)       Kaas كَاس : A cup overflowing with a drink (wine).
(3)       Siqaaya سَقَايَة      : A vessel or a cup used for the purpose of drinking water.
(4)       Suwaa’a صُوَاع : A vessel or a cup made for drinking water, made out of gold or silver.

يَطُوفُ عَلَيۡہِمۡ وِلۡدَٲنٌ۬ مُّخَلَّدُونَ (﻿١٧﻿) بِأَكۡوَابٍ۬ وَأَبَارِيقَ وَكَأۡسٍ۬ مِّن مَّعِينٍ۬

“There will circulate among them young boys made eternal; With vessels, pitchers and a cup [of wine] from a flowing spring”

3.      Saqaaya سَقَايَة : Saqaa’ سَقَى means the action to have someone to drink water or the action to serve any drink to someone. Siqayaa سَقَايَة  also means to have someone drink water, and is also known to be the vessel or pot from which one drinks.

In the Holy Quran,

Surah Yusuf (Joseph) سُوۡرَةُ یُوسُف

(16:70)

فَلَمَّا جَهَّزَهُم بِجَهَازِهِمۡ جَعَلَ ٱلسِّقَايَةَ فِى رَحۡلِ أَخِيهِ

“So when he had furnished them with their supplies, he put the [gold measuring] bowl into the bag of his brother. Then an announcer called out, "O caravan, indeed you are thieves."

4.      Suwaa’a صُوَاع : Also siwaa’ صِوَاع  mean a drinking cup or a drinking vessel that is made out of gold or silver. If, however, the vessel is made out of glass it is called qadah قدح ; if it is a wooden vessel, it is called u’uss عُس ; if it is made out of leather, then a’albah عَلبَه ; and in case it is made out of clay, then it is called markan مركن .(Al-Jamaal Wal-Kamaal- Salman Mansur Puri 174). It must be clarified that this word is not derived from the word saa’ صاع , meaning: a known measurement.

 

Allah Taa’la says:

 

Surah Yusuf (Joseph) سُوۡرَةُ یُوسُف

 

(12:72)

 

قَالُواْ نَفۡقِدُ صُوَاعَ ٱلۡمَلِكِ

 

“They said, "We are missing the measure of the king. And for he who produces it is [the reward of] a camel's load, and I am responsible for it."

 

Conclusion:

(1)   Akwaab  اَكوَاب: Plural of koob, meaning: a cup or a vessel without a handle.

(2)   Kaas كَاس : A cup overflowing with a drink (wine).

(3)   Siqaaya سَقَايَة  : A vessel or a cup used for the purpose of drinking water.

(4)   Suwaa’a صُوَاع : A vessel or a cup made for drinking water, made out of gold or silver.

44. Peep پیپ (Pus)
Also known as   ghis-leen غِسلِين , ghassaaq غَسَّاق    and   saddeed صَدِيد .
1.          Ghisleen غِسلِين : Gha-sa-la غَسَلَ   means to purify something with water and cleanse the filth and impurities.   Ghisl غِسل   means any and everything that is used to cleanse or wash something with.
Ghisleen غِسلِين   is the unclean and filthy water or hogwash. It also describes the discharge and purulence of the wounds and injuries, which would include pus, blood and other types of filth in it.
Allah Taa’la says:
Surah Al Haaqqa (The Reality)   سُوۡرَةُ الحَاقَّة
(69:36-37)
وَلَا طَعَامٌ إِلَّا مِنۡ غِسۡلِينٍ۬ (  ﻿  ٣٦  ﻿  ) لَّا يَأۡكُلُهُ ۥۤ إِلَّا ٱلۡخَـٰطِـُٔونَ
“So there is not for him here this Day any devoted friend,   Nor any food except from the discharge of wounds;”
2.          Ghassaaq غَسَّاق  : Ghasaaq  غَسَّاق    normally translates either into pus or flowing pus. Al Munjid, the sector of literary system and the Arabic scholars of literature (صاحب منتہی الادب ) unanimously agree on the translation of   ghasaaq غَسَّاق    to be cold water with a putrid and malodorous smell. In another literature (صاحب مقائیس اللغتہ ), it is described as   ma-taq-turu min julood-e ahl-in-naar (مَاتَقطُرُ مِن جُلُودِ اَهلِ النَّارِ )   meaning: ‘All that will drip from the skins of the ones in hellfire, drop by drop.’ It is written that in the Holy Quran, the meaning of   ghasaaq غَسَّاق    has been used twice in comparison with   hameem حميم   , which signifies that its meaning of cold and filthy water is the most appropriate. And Allah knows best. Following are the examples of the aforementioned terms:
(1)       Surah An Naba (The Tidings)     سُوۡرَةُ النّبَإِ
(78:25)
إِلَّا حَمِيمً۬ا وَغَسَّاقً۬ا
“Except boiling water and pus”   (Translation by Mufti Usmani)
“Except scalding water and [foul] purulence”   (Translation by Sahih)
(2)       Surah Sad (The Letter “Saad”)   سُوۡرَةُ صٓ
(38:25)
هَـٰذَا فَلۡيَذُوقُوهُ حَمِيمٌ۬ وَغَسَّاقٌ۬
“Let them taste this: hot water and pus.”   (Translation by Mufti Usmani)
“This - so let them taste it - is scalding water and [foul] purulence.”   (Translation by Sahih)
3.          Saddeed صَدِيد :   According to Imam Raghib, it means the pus that lies between the flesh and the skin. And it is probably defined by the meaning of   sad صَّد   . Al-Munjid writes its meaning as ‘pus with blood in it’ or ‘purulent discharge’, which makes most sense. The sector of literary system writes its meaning as ‘admixture of water and blood in the wound’.
Allah Taa’la says:
Surah Ibrahim (Abrahim)   سُوۡرَةُ إبراهیم
(14:16)
مِّن وَرَآٮِٕهِۦ جَهَنَّمُ وَيُسۡقَىٰ مِن مَّآءٍ۬ صَدِيدٍ۬
“Before him is Hell, and he will be given a drink of purulent water.”
Conclusion:
(1)       Ghis-leen   غِسلِين      : A combination of discharge of wounds, hogwash, purulence, blood and pus.
(2)       Ghassaaq   غَسَّاق      :  Cold water having a pungent smell, or flowing pus.
(3)       Saddeed   صَدِيد   : Admixture of pus, blood and water. Purulent water.

45. Peeth – Pusht پیٹھ - پشت (Back – Behind)
Also known as   zahr ظَهر , dubur دُبُر    and   suulb صُلب .
1.          Zahr ظَهر :   The entire external portion of the body from behind, starting from the rectum up till the neck. The plural of   zahr ظَهر   is   zuhoor ظُهور   .
In the Holy Quran,
Surah Al Inshiqaq (The Sundering)  سُوۡرَةُ الانشقاق
(84:10)
وَأَمَّا مَنۡ أُوتِىَ كِتَـٰبَهُ ۥ وَرَآءَ ظَهۡرِهِۦ
“  But as for he who is given his record behind his back,”
2.          Dubur دُبُر  :   This means the rectum and the back or behind of everything. The plural of   dubur دُبُر      is   adbaar ادبار    , and the antonym is   qubul قُبُل   . The meaning of   dubur دُبُر      and   adbaar ادبار    also define afterward or backward.   Dubur-as-salaat (دبرالصلوة )   and   adbaar-us-sujood (ادبارالسجود )   (50:40) mean ‘after the salaat(prayer)’.
Similarly,
Surah Al Hijr (The Rocky Tract)   سُوۡرَةُ الحِجر
(15:65)
وَٱتَّبِعۡ أَدۡبَـٰرَهُمۡ
“So set out with your family during a portion of the night   and follow behind them   and let not anyone among you look back and continue on to where you are commanded."
As though, the meaning of   dubur دُبُر      is vast and far more descriptive than   zahr ظَهر .
In the Holy Quran,
Surah Al Qamar (The Moon)   سُوۡرَةُ القَمَر
(54:45)
سَيُہۡزَمُ ٱلۡجَمۡعُ وَيُوَلُّونَ ٱلدُّبُرَ
“[Their] assembly will be defeated, and they will turn their backs [in retreat].”
3.          Suulb صُلب : salab-al-azm صَلَبَ العَظم    means to extract the fatty tissue from the bone.   Salab صلب    means the fats and the marrow of the backbone/vertebra. Now since the backbone lies in the middle of the back, therefore the translation of   salab صلب    is taken as back or behind.
Allah Taa’la says:
Surah At Tariq (The Nightcommer)   سُوۡرَةُ الطّارق
(86:7)
يَخۡرُجُ مِنۢ بَيۡنِ ٱلصُّلۡبِ وَٱلتَّرَآٮِٕبِ
“Emerging from between the backbone and the ribs.”
Conclusion:
(1)       Zahr ظَهر : The external back portion of any living being, starting from the rectum up till the neck.
(2)       Dubur دُبُر      : The rectum and the back or behind of everything.
(3)       Suulb صُلب : The backbone, including the fats and marrow. The behind.

46. Peechhaa Kerna پیچھا کرنا (To follow)
Also known as   ibti-ghaa اِبتِغَاء , qassaa قَصَّ    and   atba’aa اَتبَعَ .
1.          Ibti-ghaa اِبتِغَاء : Baghaa بَغَى    means to search, to look for, to crave.   Ibti-ghaa اِبتِغَاء    means to search for a required object and then pursue it.
Allah Taa’la says:
Surah An Nisa (The Women)   سُوۡرَةُ النِّسَاء
(4:104)
وَلَا تَهِنُواْ فِى ٱبۡتِغَآءِ ٱلۡقَوۡمِ‌ۖ
“  And do not weaken in pursuit of the enemy.   If you should be suffering - so are they suffering as you are suffering, but you expect from Allah that which they expect not. And Allah is ever Knowing and Wise.”
2.          Qassaa قَصَّ :   It     means to follow by foot, or to continuously follow a sign or a landmark.
In the Holy Quran,
Surah Al Qasas (The Stories)   سُوۡرَةُ القَصَص
(28:11)
وَقَالَتۡ لِأُخۡتِهِۦ قُصِّيهِ‌ۖ
“  And she said to his sister, "Follow him"  ; so she watched him from a distance while they perceived not.”
3.          Atba’aa اَتبَعَ :   It means to follow someone, pursue them and reach them.
In the Holy Quran,
Surah Al Shuara (The Poets)   سُوۡرَةُ الشُّعَرَاء
(26:60-61)
فَأَتۡبَعُوهُم مُّشۡرِقِينَ (  ﻿  ٦٠  ﻿  ) فَلَمَّا تَرَٲٓءَا ٱلۡجَمۡعَانِ قَالَ أَصۡحَـٰبُ مُوسَىٰٓ إِنَّا لَمُدۡرَكُونَ
“So they pursued them at sunrise.   And when the two companies saw one another, the companions of Moses said, "Indeed, we are to be overtaken!"
Conclusion:
(1)       Ibti-ghaa   اِبتِغَاء   : To search for a particular required object and then to pursue it.
(2)       Qassaa   قَصَّ      : To follow something with the guidance of a sign or a landmark.
(3)       Atba’aa   اَتبَعَ   : To follow someone and reach them.

47. Peechhay پیچھے (Behind/Back)
Also known as   ba’ad بعد , wara’aa ورا , khalf خلف    and    adbaar اَدبَار .
1.          Ba’ad بعد :   It means back, after, afterwards. The meaning of this lies within the context of time. And its antonym is   qabal قبل   which means before.
In the Holy Quran:
Surah Al Baqarah (The Cow)   سُوۡرَةُ البَقَرَة
(2:56)
ثُمَّ بَعَثۡنَـٰكُم مِّنۢ بَعۡدِ مَوۡتِكُمۡ لَعَلَّڪُمۡ تَشۡكُرُونَ
“  Then We revived you after your death that perhaps you would be grateful.”
2.          Adbaar اَدبَار :   The back or behind of anything is called   dubur دُبر   , the antonym of which, is   qubl     قُبل.   Its meaning is connected within the context of time; i.e. with the ending of something or right after it. With that in mind,   dubur-as-salaat دبرالصلوة    would mean ‘after salaat(prayer)’ The plural is   adbaar اَدبَار   .
Allah Taa’la says:
Surah Qaf (The Letter “Qaf”)   سُوۡرَةُ قٓ
(50:40)
وَمِنَ ٱلَّيۡلِ فَسَبِّحۡهُ وَأَدۡبَـٰرَ ٱلسُّجُودِ
“And [in part] of the night exalt Him and after prostration.”
Adbaar اَدبَار   means for something to back out and disappear. Therefore, in a different chapter in the Holy Quran,
Allah Taa’la says:
Surah At Tur (The Mount)   سُوۡرَةُ الطُّور
(52:49)
وَمِنَ ٱلَّيۡلِ فَسَبِّحۡهُ وَإِدۡبَـٰرَ ٱلنُّجُومِ
“And in a part of the night exalt Him and after [the setting of] the stars.”
The eloquence of this verse is evident with the fact that the meaning and concept of   adbaar اَدبَار   are well comprehended.

47. Peechhay پیچھے (Behind/Back)

Also known as ba’ad بعد , wara’aa ورا , khalf خلف  and  adbaar اَدبَار .

1.      Ba’ad بعد : It means back, after, afterwards. The meaning of this lies within the context of time. And its antonym is qabal قبل which means before.

In the Holy Quran:

Surah Al Baqarah (The Cow) سُوۡرَةُ البَقَرَة

(2:56)

ثُمَّ بَعَثۡنَـٰكُم مِّنۢ بَعۡدِ مَوۡتِكُمۡ لَعَلَّڪُمۡ تَشۡكُرُونَ

“Then We revived you after your death that perhaps you would be grateful.”

2.      Adbaar اَدبَار : The back or behind of anything is called dubur دُبر , the antonym of which, is qubl قُبل. Its meaning is connected within the context of time; i.e. with the ending of something or right after it. With that in mind, dubur-as-salaat دبرالصلوة  would mean ‘after salaat(prayer)’ The plural is adbaar اَدبَار .

Allah Taa’la says:

Surah Qaf (The Letter “Qaf”) سُوۡرَةُ قٓ

(50:40)

وَمِنَ ٱلَّيۡلِ فَسَبِّحۡهُ وَأَدۡبَـٰرَ ٱلسُّجُودِ

“And [in part] of the night exalt Him and after prostration.”

Adbaar اَدبَار means for something to back out and disappear. Therefore, in a different chapter in the Holy Quran,

Allah Taa’la says:

Surah At Tur (The Mount) سُوۡرَةُ الطُّور

(52:49)

وَمِنَ ٱلَّيۡلِ فَسَبِّحۡهُ وَإِدۡبَـٰرَ ٱلنُّجُومِ

“And in a part of the night exalt Him and after [the setting of] the stars.”

The eloquence of this verse is evident with the fact that the meaning and concept of adbaar اَدبَار are well comprehended.

Allah says in quran :
وَعَلَى الثَّلَاثَةِ الَّذِينَ خُلِّفُوا
9:118 (surah 9 at tawbah,verse 118)

akhraa only used as adverd of time and khalafaah can be adverb of time or location both at the same time

raw_text:
5.Paani aur uski Aqsaam پانی اور اسکی اقسام (Water and its Types)
A commonly used word for water is ‘Maa-un’ مَاءٌ, whether the described water is muddy or clean, sweet or has alkalinity. The following examples of water are discussed in the Holy Quran:
Hameem حَمِيم, Ghassaaq غَسَّاق, Aanin اَنٍ and Aaniyatin اَنِيَةٍ, Ghaor غَور, Ma’een مَعِين, Azb عَزب, Furaat فُرَات, Milh مِلحٌ, Ujaaj اُجَاج.
1.          Hameem   حَمِيم: ‘Hamma’ حَمَّ means to be hot. ‘Hammaa’ حَمَّى means temperature or fever. ‘Hameem’ حميم is known to be the water that becomes scalding and often times reeks due to its presence in the sun. The scholars of linguistics write its meaning as ‘scalding hot water’.
2.          Ghassaaq   غَسَّاق: It is normally translated as pus or oozing pus or purulence. However, the scholars of linguistics and scholars of Arabic literature unanimously state its meaning to be cold and smelly water. The Holy Quran has also verified the same meaning, since both words ‘Hameem’ حَمِيم and ‘Ghassaaq’ غَسَّاق have been used in the Holy Quran in contrast. For example:
(i)                     Surah An Naba (The Tidings)   سُوۡرَةُ النّبَإِ
(78:24-25)
لَّا يَذُوقُونَ فِيہَا بَرۡدً۬ا وَلَا شَرَابًا (  ﻿  ٢٤  ﻿  ) إِلَّا حَمِيمً۬ا وَغَسَّاقً۬ا
“They will not taste therein [any] coolness or drink - Except scalding water and [foul] purulence”
(ii)                   Surah As Sad (The Letter Saad)   سُوۡرَةُ صٓ
(38:56-57)
جَهَنَّمَ يَصۡلَوۡنَہَا فَبِئۡسَ ٱلۡمِهَادُ (  ﻿  ٥٦  ﻿  ) هَـٰذَا فَلۡيَذُوقُوهُ حَمِيمٌ۬ وَغَسَّاقٌ۬
“Hell, which they will [enter to] burn, and wretched is the resting place. This - so let them taste it - is scalding water and [foul] purulence.”
3.          Aanin   اَنٍ –  Aaniyatin   اَنِيَةٍ: ‘Anaa’ اَنَى means for the water to boil or its boiling time to be near. ‘Aanin’ اَنٍ means such hot water that it starts scorching and scalding.
Allah Taa’la says:
Surah Ar Rahman (The Beneficent)   سُوۡرَةُ الرَّحمٰن
(55:44)
يَطُوفُونَ بَيۡنَہَا وَبَيۡنَ حَمِيمٍ ءَانٍ۬
“They will go around between it and scalding water, heated [to the utmost degree].”
In another location, Allah Taa’la says:
Surah Al Ghashiyah (The Overwhelming)   سُوۡرَةُ الغَاشِیَة
(88:4-5)
تَصۡلَىٰ نَارًا حَامِيَةً۬ (  ﻿  ٤  ﻿  ) تُسۡقَىٰ مِنۡ عَيۡنٍ ءَانِيَةٍ۬
“They will [enter to] burn in an intensely hot Fire. They will be given drink from a boiling spring.”
4.          Ghaur     غَور  : Water that is underground; in a depth. The Arabic scholars state its meaning as water that tends to absorb in the ground.
5.          Ma’een     مَعِين  : ‘Ma’ana’ مَعَنَ means water that flows smoothly. ‘Ma’een’   مَعِين   is described as water that runs on the surface of the ground. Unlike a gushing flood, it is flowing rather smoothly, peacefully and serenely.
Therefore, Allah Taa’la says:
Surah Al Mulk (The Sovereignty)   سُوۡرَةُ المُلک
(67:30)
قُلۡ أَرَءَيۡتُمۡ إِنۡ أَصۡبَحَ مَآؤُكُمۡ غَوۡرً۬ا فَمَن يَأۡتِيكُم بِمَآءٍ۬ مَّعِينِۭ
“Say, "Have you considered: if your water was to become sunken [into the earth], then who could bring you flowing water?"
In terms of taste:
6.          Azb     عَزب  : Water that is sweet and freshly pleasing to taste; such water that one would desire to drink without a reason.
7.          Furaat   فُرَات: ‘Furaat’ فُرَات means sea. It is also the name of a great river that falls into the Persian Gulf. ‘Furataan’ فُرَاتَان is known to be ‘furaat’ فُرَات and the river Daljh دلجہ. ‘Furaat-il-maa’ فُرَاتِ المَاءِ means for the water to be pleasant and sweet in taste as though ‘furaat’ فُرَات carries the qualities of ‘azb’   عَزب  , yet be great in quantity.
8.          Milh   مِلحٌ: Alkaline/saltwater/brine.
End of page 268

إِنَّكُمْ رَضِيتُم بِالْقُعُودِ أَوَّلَ مَرَّةٍ فَاقْعُدُوا مَعَ الْخَالِفِينَ

title: content/p/p52.html
raw_text:
to make someone follow (peechay laagana) or to pursue – 52
Synonyms are:
1)   اَتْبَعَ
2)   قَفٰي (قَفَّي) and (قَفُّو)
3)   اَغْرٰ (غرَى)
1)Itbaa   اَتْبَعَ:   can be used in both ways as Transitive and intransitive verbs if it is intransitive verb then it means behind someone or to follow sum one for example:
فَأَتْبَعُوهُم مُّشْرِقِينَ
26:60 (surah 26 as shuaaraa,verse 60)
Translation: So they pursued them at sunrise.
and if it is transitive verb then it means to put something on follow.
Example :   وَأَتْبَعْنَاهُمْ فِي هَٰذِهِ الدُّنْيَا لَعْنَةً
28:42 (Surah 28 al qasas verse 42)
Transaltion: in this world we made a curse to follow them.
2)kafa and qaffa   قَفٰي (قَفَّي)  : al qafaa القفَاء means nape and qafa ,yakfoo قفا يَقفُوْا means to hit someone on nape and to follow sumone or behind sumone   Mufraddat - مفردات  by Imam Raghib - (Arabic to Urdu) =(مف).(to follow sumthing ,to purse in a way that is irritating,peechay paar jaanaa)
Allah says in quran :
وَلَا تَقْفُ مَا لَيْسَ لَكَ بِهِ عِلْمٌ
17:36 (surah 17 al israa,verse 36)
Transaltion: (O man), follow not that whereof thou hast no knowledge
And qaffaa   قَفَّي   means to put sumthing behind other thing continually from this word the word qafia   قافيه   originated. It means to follow consecutively.
Allah says
وَقَفَّيْنَا مِن بَعْدِهِ بِالرُّسُلِ
2:87 (surah 2 al baqarah verse 87)
Translation: and followed him up with a succession of messengers.
3)aghraa   اَغْرٰ   means to provoke dog or any other animal used for hunting behind its prey Allah says :
فَأَغْرَيْنَا بَيْنَهُمُ الْعَدَاوَةَ وَالْبَغْضَاءَ
5:14 (surah 5 al maiodah,verse 14)
Translation: so we estranged them, with enmity and hatred between the one and the other.
Summary
1) aatbaa: is usual word comes in both senses transitive and intransitive verb. it means to follow or to put someone/sumthing on following
2) qafaa: means to pursue someone and qaffaa means to put something behind other continually .
3)aghraa :to provoke and make one thing to purse the other.

Other derivatives of behind -53
Furthermore some derivatives of behind for which Quran uses only one word they are mentioned below:
For example :
1)to walk behind the word used is itbaa   اِتَّبَعَ
And to look behind the word is altafaat اِلْتَفَتَ:lafata   لَفَتَ   means to turn sumthing towards left or right   Maqaayeesul-lughat - مقائيس اللغة  (Arabic to Arabic) = (م-ل)
and altafat   التَفت   means to turn and watch. Giving attention and looking behind.altafaat   التَفات  is a common word.

فَأَسْرِ بِأَهْلِكَ بِقِطْعٍ مِّنَ اللَّيْلِ وَاتَّبِعْ أَدْبَارَهُمْ وَلَا يَلْتَفِتْ مِنكُمْ أَحَدٌ
15:65 (surah 15 al hijr verse no 65)
Translation: Then travel by night with thy household, when a portion of the night (yet remains), and do thou bring up the rear: let no one amongst you look back
