title: content/p/p54.html
raw_text:
Giving birth -54
Synonyms are:
1) بَرَاَ
2) بَدَع
3) فَطَرَ
4) خَلَقَ
5) اَنْشَأَ
6) ذَرَاَ
1)  baraa بَرَاَ  : it means to bring a thing from inexistence or nothingness into being   Munjid – منجد (Alfurooqul-lughwiyyah - الفروق اللغوية 113)  .to create something to invent something.
Allah says:
فَاقْتُلُوا أَنفُسَكُمْ ذَٰلِكُمْ خَيْرٌ لَّكُمْ عِندَ بَارِئِكُمْ
2:54 (Surah 2 al baqarah, verse 54 )
Translation: and slay yourselves (the wrong-doers); that will be better for you in the sight of your Maker.
2)   badaa بَدَع   : creating for the first time. To create without any sample or following anything   Munjid – منجد   and badia   بديع   means the one who creates something unique or extraordinary .
Allah says
بَدِيعُ السَّمَاوَاتِ وَالْأَرْضِ
2:117 (SURAH 2 AL BAQARAH , VERSE 117)
Translation : The Originator of the heavens and the earth.
3)   fatara فَطَرَ   : to give the cuts and curves beautifully ayat “  فِطْرَتَ اللَّهِ الَّتِي فَطَرَ النَّاسَ عَلَيْهَا”(  30:30 surah 30 ar room, verse 30) is translated by sir usmani “Allah´s handiwork according to the pattern on which He has made mankind.”
Allah says
الْحَمْدُ لِلَّهِ فَاطِرِ السَّمَاوَاتِ وَالْأَرْضِ
35:1 (surah 35 faatir, verse number 1)
Transaltion: Praise be to Allah, Who created (out of nothing) the heavens and the earth.
4)  khlaaqaa خَلَقَ   : this word can be taken in many ways
Such as
a)to make a diagram or to make a rough figure(appraise) before creating something   Mufraddat – مفردات   so creating something can be a job of brain and it can be attributed to someone other than ALLAH.
b)  khlaqa خَلَقَ   sumtime is also used in sense of ibdaa which means creating first time. In Quran
خَلْقَ السَّمَاوَاتِ وَالأَرْضِ   translated as”created the heavens and the earth “
And in the same way
“  بَدِيعُ السَّمَاوَاتِ وَالْأَرْضِ   “ translated as “Originator of the heavens and the earth.”
in both cases creator is none other than Allah.

raw_text:
Messenger-57
Synonyms are:
1)   نَبى
2)   رَسُول (مُرْسِلْ)
3)   مَلٰئِكة
1-2)  Nabii نَبى   , rasool and   mursaal رَسُول (مُرْسِلْ  ) :   PROPHET nabii نَبى   derivates from the root word   nabba نبا   which means news. And it means to receive the news of unknown/unseen from ALLAH through revelation. And prophet hood is attributed to the prophet.
The dictionary definition of   rasool رَسُول   is messenger and that can be anyone. but according to   Religious Terminology or Islamic Jurisprudence terminology   messenger is the one who through divine revelation and inspiration receive the news of unknown and receive orders and rulings and then deliver them to others.   Risallat رسالت   messengership is not attributed to messenger instead it is attributed to Allah . Only then a rasool is called a   mursail مُرسل   when he delivers the message to others. Whereas he is called a rasool ( messenger) at the time when the message is handed over to him   Alfurooqul-lughwiyyah - الفروق اللغوية 223.
Some people think there is no difference between nabii and rasool. They say it is two sides of the same coin. And their logic is, that the people Allah referred as in nabi in Quran, most of them are also called rasool as well. But in actual there is a difference between both
And prove/explanation of this is given in the verse below:
وَمَا أَرْسَلْنَا مِن قَبْلِكَ مِن رَّسُولٍ وَلَا نَبِيٍّ إِلَّا إِذَا تَمَنَّىٰ أَلْقَى الشَّيْطَانُ فِي أُمْنِيَّتِهِ
22:52 (surah 22 hajj, verse 52)
Transaltion: Never did We send a messenger or a prophet before thee, but, when he framed a desire, Satan threw some (vanity) into his desire.
From this verse it is clearly mentioned that these two are two separate terms and the root difference between both of them is as follow:
1) before arrival of a prophet the news of his arrival is delivered to the already present messengers and they announce it.but for a nabii(messenger) it is not important (he does not do like this).
2)every rasool /messenger brings new religious jurisprudence and built a new nation but nabii/prophet is sent upon to the nation of rasool prior to him so that he can do the corrections in the ruined up teachings of that rasool and to make corrections in the character of that nation.
3) from the evil of people rasools/messengers are protected by Allah but anbiaa prophets(   اَنبيَاء   plural of nabi) were killed in past unjustly.
3)  maliikaah مَلٰئِكة   : the root of this is   laak(لأك )” اَلاَكةُ الئٰ فلان   “ means deliver my massage to him/her.
“اَلكني الئٰ فلانٍ “ means give my message to him and   ملْاَك malaak or مَلَك malak
means angel who delivers messages   Munjid - منجد  .malik   مَلَك   means angel and its plural is   malika مَلٰئِكة   is also used a Islamic jurisprudence terminology. And it is not necessary that a all the malik   مَلَك   has to be a messenger. The angel who is assigned to deliver the message of Allah to messengers and prophets (nabi and rasool) is jabrail (a.s),ALLAH mentioned him with the title of Rooh (SPIRIT) and also as rooh al amen(the trustworthy spirit).however other angels also delivers the messages
as Allah says:
إِذْ قَالَتِ الْمَلَائِكَةُ يَا مَرْيَمُ إِنَّ اللَّهَ يُبَشِّرُكِ بِكَلِمَةٍ مِّنْهُ اسْمُهُ الْمَسِيحُ عِيسَى ابْنُ مَرْيَمَ
3:45 (surah 3 ali imran, verse number 45)
Translation: Behold! the angels said: "O Mary! Allah giveth thee glad tidings of a Word from Him: his name will be Christ Jesus, the son of Mary.
Summary:
1)Nabi: prophet is the one who receives the news of unknown/unseen (the hidden knowledge) by Allah through revelation and according to those revelation make correction in prior teachings and character of prior nations .
2)rasool:is the messenger who has been authorized with religious jurisprudence and formulate a new nation and convey Allah’s message to others.
3)malikaa: are the angels that also delivers messages.

Some people think there is no difference between nabii and rasool. They say it is two sides of the same coin. And their logic is, that the people Allah referred as in nabi in Quran, most of them are also called rasool as well. But in actual there is a difference between both

And prove/explanation of this is given in the verse below:

وَمَا أَرْسَلْنَا مِن قَبْلِكَ مِن رَّسُولٍ وَلَا نَبِيٍّ إِلَّا إِذَا تَمَنَّىٰ أَلْقَى الشَّيْطَانُ فِي أُمْنِيَّتِهِ

22:52 (surah 22 hajj, verse 52)

Transaltion: Never did We send a messenger or a prophet before thee, but, when he framed a desire, Satan threw some (vanity) into his desire.

From this verse it is clearly mentioned that these two are two separate terms and the root difference between both of them is as follow:

1) before arrival of a prophet the news of his arrival is delivered to the already present messengers and they announce it.but for a nabii(messenger) it is not important (he does not do like this).

2)every rasool /messenger brings new religious jurisprudence and built a new nation but nabii/prophet is sent upon to the nation of rasool prior to him so that he can do the corrections in the ruined up teachings of that rasool and to make corrections in the character of that nation.

3) from the evil of people rasools/messengers are protected by Allah but anbiaa prophets( اَنبيَاء plural of nabi) were killed in past unjustly.

3)maliikaah مَلٰئِكة : the root of this is laak(لأك )” اَلاَكةُ الئٰ فلان “ means deliver my massage to him/her.

“اَلكني الئٰ فلانٍ “ means give my message to him and ملْاَك malaak or مَلَك malak

means angel who delivers messages Munjid - منجد.malik مَلَك means angel and its plural is malika مَلٰئِكة is also used a Islamic jurisprudence terminology. And it is not necessary that a all the malik مَلَك has to be a messenger. The angel who is assigned to deliver the message of Allah to messengers and prophets (nabi and rasool) is jabrail (a.s),ALLAH mentioned him with the title of Rooh (SPIRIT) and also as rooh al amen(the trustworthy spirit).however other angels also delivers the messages

as Allah says:

إِذْ قَالَتِ الْمَلَائِكَةُ يَا مَرْيَمُ إِنَّ اللَّهَ يُبَشِّرُكِ بِكَلِمَةٍ مِّنْهُ اسْمُهُ الْمَسِيحُ عِيسَى ابْنُ مَرْيَمَ

3:45 (surah 3 ali imran, verse number 45)

Translation: Behold! the angels said: "O Mary! Allah giveth thee glad tidings of a Word from Him: his name will be Christ Jesus, the son of Mary.

Summary:

1)Nabi: prophet is the one who receives the news of unknown/unseen (the hidden knowledge) by Allah through revelation and according to those revelation make correction in prior teachings and character of prior nations .

2)rasool:is the messenger who has been authorized with religious jurisprudence and formulate a new nation and convey Allah’s message to others.

3)malikaa: are the angels that also delivers messages.

raw_text:
Rivals of messangers-58
The dictinory definition of hareef/ حَريف is confrere(A fellow member of a fraternity or profession).however this word can also be applied even if there is similarity between any one aspect. Whenever messengers presented invitation of deen( deen and oness of ALLAh) they were called as magician, soothsayer, poet and insane. We here want to see the main difference between the job of messengers and all these people.
1)  saher ساحر   means magician :prophets and messengers ,sometimes from their own wish ,sumtimes on demand of people and sometimes because of an urgent requirement were given miracles from Allah. after seeing the miracles the unbelievers used to call them magicians .
Allah says:
اقْتَرَبَتِ السَّاعَةُ وَانشَقَّ الْقَمَرُ وَإِن يَرَوْا آيَةً يُعْرِضُوا وَيَقُولُوا سِحْرٌ مُّسْتَمِرٌّ
54:1-2 (surah 54 al qamar verse 1-2)
Transaltion: The Hour has drawn near, and the moon has been cleft asunder, And if they see a sign, they turn away, and say: "This is continuous magic.
After the first verse in which the miracle of splitting of moon is told in the second verse it is mentioned that it is the job of unbelievers whenever they see a miracle they immediately call it magic. So it is important to understand the difference between magic and miracle.
The main difference between them is:
1) The substance/essence and reality of things does not change in magic. Magic works on the eyes of viewer and they see things what magicians want them to view. When competing with Mosa (a.s) the magicians turned their sticks and ropes into snakes ALLAH says for them.
فَلَمَّا أَلْقَوْا سَحَرُوا أَعْيُنَ النَّاسِ وَاسْتَرْهَبُوهُمْ وَجَاءُوا بِسِحْرٍ عَظِيمٍ
7:116 (surah 7 al al aaraaf verse 116)
Translation: “Throw you (first)” So when they threw, they bewitched the eyes of the people, and struck terror into them, and they displayed a great magic.
Whereas, in miracle the substance (essence) and reality of thing is changed.for example the stick of prophet mosa (a.s) used to become a snake when thrown and comes to its original state when held in hand.
2) the newly created things from miracles stays in the same states as it is created like zam zam and the 12 springs or it comes to its original state like splitting of moon, stick of mosa and the white hand of mosa (when mosa showed his hand it was shinning bright ). a miracle cannot be finished or destroyed but magic can be destroyed for example the snake of all the magicians were eaten by the stick(snake) of mosa.
In quran word miracle is not used instead   ayah اٰية   ayah bayyinah  اٰية بينة,,mubsarah مبصرة ,and burhan     برهان   are used.the way how quran is explained its way of speech and its context explain that the word is used in its original meaning or it means miracle. And sometime among all these words none is used only from the way of explanation from the speech it is understood that its talking about a miracle for example   سُبْحَانَ الَّذِي أَسْرَىٰ  17:1 (Surah 17 AL ISRAA ,verse 1)  ”in this subhan ALLAh is a word of interjection to explain that the journey of isra wal miraj was not a spiritual journey but was actually a physical journey and thus it was a miracle.
3) Magic is an art that can be acquired. But miracle cannot be acquired and gained. This was the reason that the magician who were on the heights of talent, when came to compete with mosa realized that what mosa has presented is unique then art and that’s why they accepted the true deen.
4) The nature and character of magician is disliked or offensive(detestable) and people wants to be saved from their evil and that’s why they scare from them. but the life of messengers are extremely pure and pious and for this reason they are respected and loved by people.
2) Kahiin soothsayer :messengers also tells the news of coming future and soothsayers also predicts the future. because of this messengers were blamed as soothsayers. The difference between both of them is the source of messenger prediction is from Allah swt and to prove it wrong is impossible. For example at the time of prophet the Romans got defeated and through revelation it was told that within 3 to 9 years they will again be conquerors .although there was no such hope for it. whereas the soothsayer gets news from ghosts and evil spirits who hear the news from the seventh sky and add some lies and truth in it and then give to the soothsayers, so sometimes their news are correct and sometimes their news are wrong.
another difference between messenger and soothsayer is that a women can be a soothsayer but not a prophtess.1 lakh and 24 thousand messengers came but none among them was a female even bibi maryum was not a prophetess. Soothsayer man/ women were given religious respect. And people asked them to take decision in their difficult matters and due to the respect given to them their decisions were accepted as the final decision. In the time of prophet ibn e siaad was one such soothsayer and he is mentioned in saheeh ahadees.instead of scarifying a human life a sacrifice of 100 camels was also a trend settled by soothsayers which was also continued even in Islam.
3)shayer poet: it’s the job of a poet that in an eloquent and justified language describes his thinking and point of view in such a way that his /her listeners are left out in trance. Although the verses in Quran are without prosodic rules ( behr and wazan).but rest all the qualities are present in Quran at its extreme which is not possible in a human speech. Due to this similarity prophet was also called poet. The difference between a poet and messenger is that the imagination of a poet is inspired by the good and bad aspects of life. Poet is influenced by Environment, and the majority of society is misguided so is the imagination of poet.
ALLAH SAYS:
وَالشُّعَرَاءُ يَتَّبِعُهُمُ الْغَاوُونَ أَلَمْ تَرَ أَنَّهُمْ فِي كُلِّ وَادٍ يَهِيمُونَ
26:224-225 (surah 26 as shuaara,verse 224-225)
Translation: As for the poets, the erring ones follow them, See you not that they speak about every subject (praising people - right or wrong) in their poetry?
Whereas, prophet imagination is according to the revelation of Allah and the second difference is, the point of view of a poet keeps on changing as per his/her age or mental level and experiences grows. But whatever a messenger says will always be in favor of his previous talks. The blames of unbelievers were rejected by Allah in Quran:
وَمَا هُوَ بِقَوْلِ شَاعِرٍ ۚ قَلِيلًا مَّا تُؤْمِنُونَ وَلَا بِقَوْلِ كَاهِنٍ ۚ قَلِيلًا مَّا تَذَكَّرُونَ
69:41-42 (surah 69 al haqqah,verses 41 and 42)
Transalation: It is not the word of a poet: little it is ye believe! Nor is it the word of a soothsayer: little admonition it is ye receive.
Because of these problems prophet (sal lal la ho alhi wa salim )was not taught poetry.even though prophet was the most eloquent/polite among all Arabs and non Arabs. Even after all these things it is wrong to say that all the poets and poetry is cursed. The imagination of poet can be on right direction. prophet (sal lal la ho alhi wa salim ) in times of iqnorance liked the poetry of Labeedah(may ALLAh be pleased with him) as this poetry was depicting the message of ALLAH.
اَلاَكُلُّ شَىْءٍمَا خلاَالّلٰهَ باطِلُ
وكُلُّ نَعيمٍ لَّامَحَلَةَ زاءلُ
Transaltion:
Know that other then Allah all things are invalid
And all the blessings without doubt will be vanished
4) insane: means unsound mind, a person who does not use mind (aqal pay pardah par janaa).and he/she talks insanely. People of Arab use to call insane (majnoon) because according to their mentality ghost enters into the body of the person and make him/her insane because of which they talk inordinately or talk insanely. The teachings of prophets are not suitable to unbelievers thts y they give them title of insane.
Allah says :
كَذَٰلِكَ مَا أَتَى الَّذِينَ مِن قَبْلِهِم مِّن رَّسُولٍ إِلَّا قَالُوا سَاحِرٌ أَوْ مَجْنُونٌ
51:52 (surah 51 ad dhariyaat, verse 52)
Transaltion: Similarly, no messenger came to the Peoples before them, but they said (of him) in like manner, "A sorcerer, or one possessed.
The root difference between a prophet and an insane person is that even though the teaching of prophet   is against the society and trends of society but the prophet stays on his path and act accordingly. And from his purity, good nature and character proves himself to be right.Where as an insane person does not possess any of the above qualities.

Drinking-59
Synonyums are:
1)   شَرِبَ
2)   جَرَّعَ
3)   سَاغَ (سوغ)
1)  sharaba شَرِبَ:   means to drink water or any other drink .this word is generally used for drinking. Sharaba means any drink .  shirab-shirbah شِرب or شِربة   means chance of drinking or drinking once. and   mashraba مَشرب   means place of drinking ”wharf”.ALLAH SAYS in Quran
فَمَن شَرِبَ مِنْهُ فَلَيْسَ مِنِّي
2:249 (SURAH 2 AL BAQARAH VERSE 249)
TRANSALTION: if any drinks of its water, He goes not with my army.
2  ) jaraa جَرَّعَ   :means to drink in sips   Munjid - منجد  (to swallow in draught)and juraah جُرعة means sip and   ijtraa اِجترع   means to drink in one go.example:
يَتَجَرَّعُهُ وَلَا يَكَادُ يُسِيغُهُ
14:17 (surah 14 Ibraheem, verse 17)
Transaltion: In gulps will he sip it, but never will he be near swallowing it down his throat.
3)   sagha سَاغَ   :means very easily to gulp down a drink from throat  Mufraddat – مفردات  ..or quaff(To drink with relish; to drink copiously of; to swallow in large draughts)and   sagia ساغيه   is refer to a drink or juice with good taste and its antonym is   ghasa غصَّ   means sumthing which is difficult to swallow down the throat and get stuck in throat.
Allah says
نُّسْقِيكُم مِّمَّا فِي بُطُونِهِ مِن بَيْنِ فَرْثٍ وَدَمٍ لَّبَنًا خَالِصًا سَائِغًا لِّلشَّارِبِينَ
16:66 (surah 16 an nahl, verse 66)
Translation: From what is within their bodies between excretions and blood, We produce, for your drink, milk, pure and agreeable to those who drink it.
Summary:
1)sharaba :the usual word used for drinking.
2)jaraa:to drink in sips.
3)sagha:to gulp down the drink quickly because of good taste.

Page 269:
Water avenues and reservoirs:
To demonstrate it six words have been used in Quran:
1.اودِية: its plural of وَادِي which means a vast field or ground which is found amidst mountains. And it has slope towards mountains where water flows. The word وَادِي is used sometimes for streams and canals and at times comes in context of valleys. Ref(13:19)
2.عين: if water oozes out of mountain or earth and gets amasses in any sloppy pit then we call it lake. And where these lakes merge in an ocean that place is called as خليج. Ref (18:86) and according to historical evidences this was the place where بحرايجين divides in to small خليجor lakes. And this word عين has been used here which slacks the meaning totally.
Page: 270
3.انهر: the plural of نهر means a bigger channel/canal for the course of water where small water channels fall. This word is particular to the streams which can easily be directed according to need. Ref (76:6),(2:25)

title: Mutaradifatul Qur'aan - preface
raw_text:
Mutaradifatul Qur'aan - preface      Author's Preface
My reasons for writing the book: Mutaraadifaatul Quraan
I vividly recall in my childhood when I was in the fourth/ fifth year of school, my late father used to teach me basic Arabic grammar and Quran in the night. In this way I finished the translation of the Quran once in my childhood. As I became older, I developed an enthusiasm for the close reading of the Quran.
I became aware that different words of the Quran had been erroneously translated into Urdu using only one word, for example the words خشية خوف حذر وجل وجس تقوى رهب   are all translated into ‘to fear’, which did not do justice to the subtle gradations of meaning. I had an inquisitive eagerness, to find out the underlying differences of these synonyms of the Quran, but found that most of the time, I was disappointed. Then I tried to turn to the scholars but was amazed that most of them had not looked into this matter, besides a few exceptions, such as Moulana Aziz Zubaidy, who was one of the first scholars I benefitted from.
The original problem was almost impossible to disentangle. Then I started looking closely at various books of transliterations. I found some books in which synonyms in Arabic had been collated; however the different underlying meanings were not distinguishable. However my first glimmer of hope came from Imam Raghib’s book, Mufradaat. The Imam had indicated in some places, information relating to this matter, however, the Imam’s focus was to discuss the individual subject matters of the Quran, not to show the differences in the underlying meanings of the lexis. Therefore most of the real problem was left unsolved, leaving my thirst for answers to this predicament, unquenched. Imam Raghib writes in the beginning of his preface:
“Allah willing, if I live, I wish to offer such a comprehensive book in which the investigation of synonyms of the Quran and its subtle differences will be clearly described. With this, the wisdom of using different synonyms in the same topic of the Quran will be made clear, for example, in one place the word   قلب   , another place   فؤاد   , and in another place   صدر   has been used. In the same formula/way we would show what the intricate subtle difference is to the ending of stories, such as in one place The Almighty says (16:79)   إِنَّ فِي ذَٰلِكَ لَآيَاتٍ لِّقَوْمٍ يُؤْمِنُونَ   and in another place   لِّقَوْمٍ يَتَفَكَّرُونَ   ,(30:21) another place (30:24)   لِّقَوْمٍ يَعْقِلُونَ   and in some places  لقوم يفقهون   .
Surely, there must be a clear reason behind these subtle, yet quite obvious, differences? Therefore words used in the Quran such as   لاولي الابصار  ,   لذي حجر  ,   لاولي النهي   led translators to sometimes select mere superficial meanings, thereby losing the essence of the message. They believe that they have done full justice to the Quran, by translating   الحمد الله   with the definition of   الشكر لله   and   لاريب   with the definition of   لا شك  .”
Only Allah knows if Imam Raghib completed this noble intention. Despite a lot of effort I was unable to locate any book which fulfilled this criteria. Even if I had done so, I am sure it would have only benefited Arabic Linguists or scholars. I was intent on producing a book which would focus on the subtle nuances of Arabic Linguistics, which would benefit both the scholar and the speaker of Urdu alike. So, therefore despite my ignorance I decided to write this book.
Where there is a will there is a way: I slowly found books which made this hard task, easy. Within my focus I came across, another book called ‘Fiqhul lughat’ by Abu Mansoor Abdul Malik ibn Mohammad Athaalaby in which I was able to find some basic indicators, for example he writes under the heading of ‘  في السقوط  ’ five sentences   ذراناب البعير   ,   هوي النجم  ,   انقض الجدار  ,   خرالسقف   and   طاح الفص   . However, looking at the five sentences you see that the first and last sentences have no connection with the Quran; and the second, third and fourth sentences you only learn that   هوي   is used for falling of the star,   انقض   for the falling of the wall, and   خر   for the falling of the roof. This was frustrating as there was no depth, no indication of connections between the words or detail in which the underlying differences were made apparent.
The third book which was beneficial in this matter was the book ‘Alfurooqul lughawiyah’   الفروق اللغوىة   by Abu Hilal Askari. He describes the underlying differences of synonyms but only two at a time, sometimes the most would be three at a time, for example he will show the difference between   خوف   and   خشية  ,   خوف   and   رهبة   separately ,   خشية   and   شفقة   separately , and   تخويف  and   انذار   separately. But when we put them together and try to understand all the differences we experience great difficulties and it is quite disturbing. Therefore I could not benefit from it fully, in addition this book was limited and did not encompass all the root words of the Quran and its meanings.
Basic meanings of root letters- old and modern inclination
The fourth book with which I took guidance from was the more modern text, Maqaayeesul-lughat مقائيس اللغة . The prominent speciality of this book is that it offers two or three base form root meanings/vocabulary depending on the situation, instead of just one.
Earlier scholars had a tendency of using just one basic pivotal meaning and then exploring the derivations, which resulted in making tenuous links. Although the reality is that some base forms when they are formed with the derived form of trilateral verb, the fundamental/root meaning disappears for example كلم (kalama) means to injure and كلم (kallama – with an emphasis on the second l) means to talk, ,جاب يجوب means to carve when اجاب means to answer and to accept, (azaba)عذب means the water to be sweet and pleasant and عذب   (azzaba – when emphasis on the second z) means to give hard punishment,  قنع   means to be content, to be content with less and   اقنع   means to raise your head in order to see what is ahead, and not to look down . Basically in the Arabic language and in the Quraan there are many base forms which when used with derived form of the trilateral verb, have no relevance with the actual meaning, and this principle is directly related to the characteristic features of some of the derived forms, for which there are many examples.
Imam Raghib was an early scholar therefore when he connects the fundamental meanings of derivations with the actual base form meanings, in the majority of cases, it is appropriate and the reader derives a good sense of understanding. However, when he starts to develop this further and goes on to explore further links which are quite tenuous, it does create conflict in the kind of the reader. For instance he translates   كلمته  (kalamtahoo), which means I injured him, then he connects,   كلم  and,   كلام,   which means to talk; and states that this is used because injury caused by the tongue is noless severe than the physical injuries. Nevertheless,   كلم   clearly means to injure and   كلام   clearly means to talk without reference to injury. Obviously all speech does not injure, the vast majority of times, it is pleasant and heals the wounds. In the same way, Imam Raghib takes   حرب   which means to take the property of another, and connects it to the mihrab in a mosque, resulting in him stating that the mihrab is the place of war against the devil and personal desires or a place where the worshipper should leave all worldly affairs and thoughts (as though these worldly affairs and thoughts are taken away from him). However it seems, as though this function is just specific to the mihraab of the masjid, intimating that there is no further need or connection outside of this place (the mihraab). This explanation is a clear example of the weakness of the links made by Imam Raghib.
On the contrary the author of   مقائيس اللغة   Maqaayeesul-lughat has a modern approach, he states two basic meanings of   قل   (qalla)1, to be less 2, to be lofty, whereas Imam Raghib only states one basic meaning ,to be less and when the word  اقل   comes , like in the Quraan   حتي اذا اقلت سحاباثقالا   (7:57) he indicates that this as, “”the winds elevates the heavy clouds thinking them as light and insignificant,” that’s why the word   اقل   has been used .” Now the question arises, if we take the meaning of   اقل   as insignificant and light, then how do we get the meaning of elevation?
مقائيس اللغة   Maqaayeesul-lughat, is particularly excellent becauseit states 2,3 basic meanings of the base form in such a way that the underlying differences is automatically determined, for example for (  ب ي ن  ) he writes 3 basic meanings, 1,separation 2, distance 3, clarification. Automatically you can understand that   بان   means something to be separated and distanced from another thing and to stand clear. Likewise the meaning of   طلع   1, to become visible 2, to appear in front. The meaning of   نظر   is 1,to inspect(to see something with your eyes) 2,   تامل الشئ   waiting for something, to give a reprieve, allow time. The meaning of   ظلم   1,to remove something from its original place to another by unlawful ways 2, darkness opposite of light and brightness. For this reason, it is quite obvious that there is no need to explore more tenuous links as the layers of meanings are made clear.
Anyhow all these texts are beneficial according to their topics and I found some parts of the text quite useful, whilst having to leave some aspects untouched. This is mainly because my focus was minute detail and more literary research, therefore I had to take advantage of many more dictionaries, translations and exegesis.
The references, sources and symbols
In the compilation of this book I have tried, to the best of my ability, that whenever a meaning is written, I state the reference of the dictionary used, except when the meaning of the word is so well known that a reference is not needed, for example   ذهب   means to go and   خرج   means to come out.
The abbreviations of the dictionaries which I have used, is given below in detail. I have tried not to present the translation of Quranic Aayaats myself , I have instead deferred to the translation of Moulana Fath Mohammad Jhaalandari Saheb because it is simple and idiomatic phrases are made clear. However, when the actual meaning was compromised due to urdu idiomatic phrases, then I have presented Moulana Shabbir Ahmed Uthmani’s translation and have written in brackets (  عثماني  ). In some rare instances, I have selected from the translation of Moulana Moududi’s translation Tafheemul-Quran. Although I used the above strategy in the main, there were some instances, when I had to make personal vocabulary selections in order to make the literal meaning clear. For the references of Quraan Ayaats, I employed the text of my Paternal Uncle Hafiz Abdul-Hayy ‘s   مراة القران   , in addition to this, I have, in some rare instances, also referenced his literal research.
The Details of the references, sources and symbols:
Reference Books and Dictionaries:
1.   Mufraddat -   مفردات  by Imam Raghib - (Arabic to Urdu) =(  مف  )
2.   Fiqhul lughat -   فقه اللغة   by Abdul Malik ibn Mohammad Athaalalaby ( Arabic to Arabic) =(  ف ل\فل  ) - the page number is included because it is not written in Alphabetical Order.
3.   Alfurooqul-lughwiyyah -   الفروق اللغوية   by AbuHilal Askari - (Arabic to Arabic)= (  فق-ل  )
4.   Maqaayeesul-lughat -   مقائيس اللغة  (Arabic to Arabic) = (  م-ل  )
5.   Munjid -   منجد   - Dictionary - (Arabic to Urdu)=(  منجد  )
6.   Mutahal arab -   منتهي الارب   - (Arabic to Persian)=(  م-ا  )
7.   Muheetul Muheet -   محيط المحيط   - (Arabic to Arabic) = (  محيط-يام-م  )
8.   Miraatul Quraan –   مراة القران   (Arabic to Urdu)=(  م-ق  )
9.   Alqamoosul-jadid  القاموس الجديد   -  (Urdu to Arabic)=(  ق-ج  )
10.   Alqamoosul Jaded Alasry   - القاموس الجديد العصري  (Arabic to English)=(  ق-ج  )
11.   Gareebul Quraan   - غريب القران  (Arabic) by Ibn Qutaibah=(  غ-ق  )
Quran, Translations and Exegesis:
12.   Gareebul Quraan Tafseer  غريب القران تفسير   (Arabic to Arabic)=(  غ-ق  )
13.   Tafheemul Quraan   تفهيم القران   (Arabic to Urdu)=(  ت-ق  )
14.   Fathul Hameed   فتح الحميد   د  (translation and footnotes), most of the ayaat’s translation is by Moulana Fath Mohammad Jhaalandari.
15.   Tafseer - Shabbir Ahmed Uthmani   تفسير شبير احمد عثماني   =(  عثماني  )
In modern Arabic Grammar, a useful symbol is used to represent the tenses Present/Future from the Past Tense derivation, eg   ضرب يضرب  . Would be represented as   ضرب -   and   نصر ينصر   by   نصر--)   with a kasra placed underneath the dash). This has been done for the sake of efficiency; therefore I have also done the same. The details of the symbols and the supplements of the numbers of the Ayats which have been used have been written in detail before the list no 2.
The Compilation and the Order of the book
Some things need to be mentioned relating to the compilation and order of this book.
1.   The order of the headings: The main focus of this book is to present the underlying differences in all the synonyms used in the Quraan, therefore the titles are in the order of the Urdu Alphabet. In the Arabic language if a verb is trilateral intransitive, when it is used in the derived trilateral form it becomes transitive. And if it is transitive in trilateral verb form, then it becomes double transitive or it holds specific qualities, except the derived form of the trilateral verb (infiaal )  انفعال   as it always stays intransitive. In the Arabic language under the base form, all the intransitive and transitive meanings are given but in the Urdu language, different words for intransitive and transitive forms are employed, such as from   پہرنا   to   پہیرنا پہسلنا   to   پہسلانا کٹنا   to   کاٹنا  . If I maintain the alphabetical order, then after   پہرنا   and   پہسلنا   it would be   پہل   and then   پہیرنا   and the demand of explanation required of the Arabic basic form meaning, is that they are all are put together   پہرناپہیرنا   put together, therefore to save time and repetition, I have chosen the latter. I have rejected the alphabetical order and put all the above mentioned words together. If the synonyms are more, then I have categorised them under two separate headings and if they are less then under just one heading such as   اترنا اتارنا  .
Likewise is the matter of joint verbs (afaal murakkaba) In which the first word is a noun and the next if it’s an intransitive verb then the murakkab becomes an intransitive and if it’s a transitive it becomes a transitive. Such as   آباد ہونا آباد کرنا   for the abovementioned reason I have again rejected the alphabetical order and mentioned   آباد ہونا  before   آباد کرنا  .
2.   The underlying differences of the Urdu headings: sometimes the urdu headings are so close in meaning it is hard to distinguish the underlying differences such as   بہاگنا دوڑنا  ,   ٹہیرنا رکنا  , and   ٹہیرنا آبادہونا   , in such place as well as clarification of the differences, I have indicated another heading which should be referred to.
3.   The repetition of the Arabic base forms: This is clear that some Arabic words are so ambiguous in meaning that it is not possible to translate into one or two urdu words, a lot of explanation is needed such as   و ع ي  means to put something in a bag and to tie the neck, now this word will come under the headings of, to be mean, to look after, to remember. Likewise   خ ذ ل  means the abandoning of an intimate friend, of a friend at the time of need and to betray him, therefore this word will come under both headings, friend and to betray. Likewise the word   زوج   will come under many headings; husband, wife, companion, couple. Such words have been explained in one place and then referred to the other places.
4.   The summary of synonyms: when there is only 2 or 3 synonyms to a word and is self-explanatory and the meaning of the underlying differences is made clear, then there is no need of a summary at the end. However, if there are more than 2 or 3 synonyms, then at the end of the heading, the summary of the words have been given. In a few places there were only 2 or 3 synonyms, but even after literal explanation, the underlying difference was not clear, therefore I have made it added a summary for further clarification.
Under some headings, there is a plethora of synonyms in the Quraan, for example:
Nineteen words have been used for: to fall or to make someone fall;
Fifteen words have been used for goods;
Thirteen have used for, to destroy;
Thirteen words for edge,
Twelve for, to make something strong,
Twenty one words for earth and others in this category
Twenty words, for noise and its type,
Thirteen words, for to become,
Fifteen words for, to fear,
Eleven words 11 for to run,
Twelve words for, to walk,
Twelve words for, to bend,
Fourteen words for, a group ,
Twelve words for, recompense,
Ten words have been used for, to be happy,
Ten words for, to collect,
Ten words for, to carry,
Ten words for, to give
Ten words for, friend.
Now you can understand how difficult it is to explain the underlying differences to all these synonyms and you can understand why there is a need of a summary at the end.
5.   The use of Antonyms: the use of the antonyms is useful in such a way that if you know the opposite meaning of one word then the meaning becomes immediately apparent, for this reason the linguistics usually mention the antonyms. Even in many places of the Quraan, antonyms have been mentioned. For example; (5:2)
وَتَعَاوَنُوا عَلَى الْبِرِّ وَالتَّقْوَىٰ ۖ وَلَا تَعَاوَنُوا عَلَى الْإِثْمِ وَالْعُدْوَانِ ۚ   And cooperate in righteousness and piety, but do not cooperate in sin and aggression. Now look in this ayat the word   اثم   has come contrary to   بر   and   عدوان   opposite of  تقوي  . So if someone knows the meaning of   بر   and   تقوي   then he can fully understand the connotations of the words   عدوان   and   اثم   and vice versa. Therefore besides mentioning the opposites in the main body of the text, I have added a chapter with the heading of Antonyms, in the appendix and I have further categorised this into three parts.
6.   The use of Quraanic Ayaats: I have only mentioned the specific Quraanic Ayaats, Ayaat or even part of an ayat according to the requirements for clarification purposes and to provide further examples.
7.   Arabic Base Forms: To search for base forms of certain words is a real challenge. Even famous Linguists differ in their conclusions regarding the base forms of these particular words. In order to address this concern, I have placed these particular difficult words in brackets and also given a list of these words in the appendix, number five, under the title Some Difficult Base Forms.
8.   Appendices: After mentioning the synonyms there were many words, such as Proper Nouns, which had no synonyms but required further explanation. Therefore to increase the benefit of this book, I have added a list of the following words in the appendix:
1.   All Proper Nouns under different headings (Prophets, Names of men and places and numbers)
2.   Common nouns
3.   Antonyms
4.   Past or Present/Future Tense – when the harkat (dhamma/kasra/fatha) of the second Radical (letter :  ع   ) changes, the meaning of the word also changes and this is made explicit.
5.   Miscellaneous

I have added these type of words in this table and stated its meaning, with the ayat and surah number in brackets, e.g.   بكي   to cry (12/16) , which means the numerator is the surah number, in which case here it means Surah Dahr, and the denominator is the ayat number , therefore this word is from the sixteenth ayah of Surah Dahr. It is important to highlight, when a base form is used in the Quraan under which derivative form it appears, all the forms have been enlisted in this table, therefore this table works as a comprehensive, albeit, abridged dictionary for the Quraan.

Author's Preface

My reasons for writing the book: Mutaraadifaatul Quraan

I vividly recall in my childhood when I was in the fourth/ fifth year of school, my late father used to teach me basic Arabic grammar and Quran in the night. In this way I finished the translation of the Quran once in my childhood. As I became older, I developed an enthusiasm for the close reading of the Quran.

I became aware that different words of the Quran had been erroneously translated into Urdu using only one word, for example the words خشية خوف حذر وجل وجس تقوى رهب are all translated into ‘to fear’, which did not do justice to the subtle gradations of meaning. I had an inquisitive eagerness, to find out the underlying differences of these synonyms of the Quran, but found that most of the time, I was disappointed. Then I tried to turn to the scholars but was amazed that most of them had not looked into this matter, besides a few exceptions, such as Moulana Aziz Zubaidy, who was one of the first scholars I benefitted from.

The original problem was almost impossible to disentangle. Then I started looking closely at various books of transliterations. I found some books in which synonyms in Arabic had been collated; however the different underlying meanings were not distinguishable. However my first glimmer of hope came from Imam Raghib’s book, Mufradaat. The Imam had indicated in some places, information relating to this matter, however, the Imam’s focus was to discuss the individual subject matters of the Quran, not to show the differences in the underlying meanings of the lexis. Therefore most of the real problem was left unsolved, leaving my thirst for answers to this predicament, unquenched. Imam Raghib writes in the beginning of his preface:

“Allah willing, if I live, I wish to offer such a comprehensive book in which the investigation of synonyms of the Quran and its subtle differences will be clearly described. With this, the wisdom of using different synonyms in the same topic of the Quran will be made clear, for example, in one place the word قلب , another place فؤاد , and in another place صدر has been used. In the same formula/way we would show what the intricate subtle difference is to the ending of stories, such as in one place The Almighty says (16:79) إِنَّ فِي ذَٰلِكَ لَآيَاتٍ لِّقَوْمٍ يُؤْمِنُونَ and in another place لِّقَوْمٍ يَتَفَكَّرُونَ ,(30:21) another place (30:24) لِّقَوْمٍ يَعْقِلُونَ and in some placesلقوم يفقهون .

Surely, there must be a clear reason behind these subtle, yet quite obvious, differences? Therefore words used in the Quran such as لاولي الابصار, لذي حجر, لاولي النهي led translators to sometimes select mere superficial meanings, thereby losing the essence of the message. They believe that they have done full justice to the Quran, by translating الحمد الله with the definition of الشكر لله and لاريب with the definition of لا شك.”

Only Allah knows if Imam Raghib completed this noble intention. Despite a lot of effort I was unable to locate any book which fulfilled this criteria. Even if I had done so, I am sure it would have only benefited Arabic Linguists or scholars. I was intent on producing a book which would focus on the subtle nuances of Arabic Linguistics, which would benefit both the scholar and the speaker of Urdu alike. So, therefore despite my ignorance I decided to write this book.

Where there is a will there is a way: I slowly found books which made this hard task, easy. Within my focus I came across, another book called ‘Fiqhul lughat’ by Abu Mansoor Abdul Malik ibn Mohammad Athaalaby in which I was able to find some basic indicators, for example he writes under the heading of ‘في السقوط’ five sentences ذراناب البعير , هوي النجم, انقض الجدار, خرالسقف and طاح الفص . However, looking at the five sentences you see that the first and last sentences have no connection with the Quran; and the second, third and fourth sentences you only learn that هوي is used for falling of the star, انقض for the falling of the wall, and خر for the falling of the roof. This was frustrating as there was no depth, no indication of connections between the words or detail in which the underlying differences were made apparent.

The third book which was beneficial in this matter was the book ‘Alfurooqul lughawiyah’ الفروق اللغوىة by Abu Hilal Askari. He describes the underlying differences of synonyms but only two at a time, sometimes the most would be three at a time, for example he will show the difference between خوف and خشية, خوف and رهبة separately , خشية and شفقة separately , and تخويفand انذار separately. But when we put them together and try to understand all the differences we experience great difficulties and it is quite disturbing. Therefore I could not benefit from it fully, in addition this book was limited and did not encompass all the root words of the Quran and its meanings.

Basic meanings of root letters- old and modern inclination

The fourth book with which I took guidance from was the more modern text, Maqaayeesul-lughat مقائيس اللغة . The prominent speciality of this book is that it offers two or three base form root meanings/vocabulary depending on the situation, instead of just one.

Earlier scholars had a tendency of using just one basic pivotal meaning and then exploring the derivations, which resulted in making tenuous links. Although the reality is that some base forms when they are formed with the derived form of trilateral verb, the fundamental/root meaning disappears for example كلم (kalama) means to injure and كلم (kallama – with an emphasis on the second l) means to talk, ,جاب يجوب means to carve when اجاب means to answer and to accept, (azaba)عذب means the water to be sweet and pleasant and عذب (azzaba – when emphasis on the second z) means to give hard punishment,قنع means to be content, to be content with less and اقنع means to raise your head in order to see what is ahead, and not to look down . Basically in the Arabic language and in the Quraan there are many base forms which when used with derived form of the trilateral verb, have no relevance with the actual meaning, and this principle is directly related to the characteristic features of some of the derived forms, for which there are many examples.

Imam Raghib was an early scholar therefore when he connects the fundamental meanings of derivations with the actual base form meanings, in the majority of cases, it is appropriate and the reader derives a good sense of understanding. However, when he starts to develop this further and goes on to explore further links which are quite tenuous, it does create conflict in the kind of the reader. For instance he translates كلمته(kalamtahoo), which means I injured him, then he connects, كلمand, كلام, which means to talk; and states that this is used because injury caused by the tongue is noless severe than the physical injuries. Nevertheless, كلم clearly means to injure and كلام clearly means to talk without reference to injury. Obviously all speech does not injure, the vast majority of times, it is pleasant and heals the wounds. In the same way, Imam Raghib takes حرب which means to take the property of another, and connects it to the mihrab in a mosque, resulting in him stating that the mihrab is the place of war against the devil and personal desires or a place where the worshipper should leave all worldly affairs and thoughts (as though these worldly affairs and thoughts are taken away from him). However it seems, as though this function is just specific to the mihraab of the masjid, intimating that there is no further need or connection outside of this place (the mihraab). This explanation is a clear example of the weakness of the links made by Imam Raghib.

On the contrary the author of مقائيس اللغة Maqaayeesul-lughat has a modern approach, he states two basic meanings of قل (qalla)1, to be less 2, to be lofty, whereas Imam Raghib only states one basic meaning ,to be less and when the wordاقل comes , like in the Quraan حتي اذا اقلت سحاباثقالا (7:57) he indicates that this as, “”the winds elevates the heavy clouds thinking them as light and insignificant,” that’s why the word اقل has been used .” Now the question arises, if we take the meaning of اقل as insignificant and light, then how do we get the meaning of elevation?

مقائيس اللغة Maqaayeesul-lughat, is particularly excellent becauseit states 2,3 basic meanings of the base form in such a way that the underlying differences is automatically determined, for example for (ب ي ن) he writes 3 basic meanings, 1,separation 2, distance 3, clarification. Automatically you can understand that بان means something to be separated and distanced from another thing and to stand clear. Likewise the meaning of طلع 1, to become visible 2, to appear in front. The meaning of نظر is 1,to inspect(to see something with your eyes) 2, تامل الشئ waiting for something, to give a reprieve, allow time. The meaning of ظلم 1,to remove something from its original place to another by unlawful ways 2, darkness opposite of light and brightness. For this reason, it is quite obvious that there is no need to explore more tenuous links as the layers of meanings are made clear.

Anyhow all these texts are beneficial according to their topics and I found some parts of the text quite useful, whilst having to leave some aspects untouched. This is mainly because my focus was minute detail and more literary research, therefore I had to take advantage of many more dictionaries, translations and exegesis.

The references, sources and symbols

In the compilation of this book I have tried, to the best of my ability, that whenever a meaning is written, I state the reference of the dictionary used, except when the meaning of the word is so well known that a reference is not needed, for example ذهب means to go and خرج means to come out.

The abbreviations of the dictionaries which I have used, is given below in detail. I have tried not to present the translation of Quranic Aayaats myself , I have instead deferred to the translation of Moulana Fath Mohammad Jhaalandari Saheb because it is simple and idiomatic phrases are made clear. However, when the actual meaning was compromised due to urdu idiomatic phrases, then I have presented Moulana Shabbir Ahmed Uthmani’s translation and have written in brackets (عثماني). In some rare instances, I have selected from the translation of Moulana Moududi’s translation Tafheemul-Quran. Although I used the above strategy in the main, there were some instances, when I had to make personal vocabulary selections in order to make the literal meaning clear. For the references of Quraan Ayaats, I employed the text of my Paternal Uncle Hafiz Abdul-Hayy ‘s مراة القران , in addition to this, I have, in some rare instances, also referenced his literal research.

The Details of the references, sources and symbols:

Reference Books and Dictionaries:

1. Mufraddat - مفرداتby Imam Raghib - (Arabic to Urdu) =(مف)

2. Fiqhul lughat - فقه اللغة by Abdul Malik ibn Mohammad Athaalalaby ( Arabic to Arabic) =(ف ل\فل) - the page number is included because it is not written in Alphabetical Order.

3. Alfurooqul-lughwiyyah - الفروق اللغوية by AbuHilal Askari - (Arabic to Arabic)= (فق-ل)

4. Maqaayeesul-lughat - مقائيس اللغة(Arabic to Arabic) = (م-ل)

5. Munjid - منجد - Dictionary - (Arabic to Urdu)=(منجد)

6. Mutahal arab - منتهي الارب - (Arabic to Persian)=(م-ا)

7. Muheetul Muheet - محيط المحيط - (Arabic to Arabic) = (محيط-يام-م)

8. Miraatul Quraan – مراة القران (Arabic to Urdu)=(م-ق)

9. Alqamoosul-jadidالقاموس الجديد -(Urdu to Arabic)=(ق-ج)

10. Alqamoosul Jaded Alasry - القاموس الجديد العصري(Arabic to English)=(ق-ج)

11. Gareebul Quraan - غريب القران(Arabic) by Ibn Qutaibah=(غ-ق)

Quran, Translations and Exegesis:

12. Gareebul Quraan Tafseerغريب القران تفسير (Arabic to Arabic)=(غ-ق)

13. Tafheemul Quraan تفهيم القران (Arabic to Urdu)=(ت-ق)

14. Fathul Hameed فتح الحميد د(translation and footnotes), most of the ayaat’s translation is by Moulana Fath Mohammad Jhaalandari.

15. Tafseer - Shabbir Ahmed Uthmani تفسير شبير احمد عثماني =(عثماني)

In modern Arabic Grammar, a useful symbol is used to represent the tenses Present/Future from the Past Tense derivation, eg ضرب يضرب. Would be represented as ضرب - and نصر ينصر by نصر--) with a kasra placed underneath the dash). This has been done for the sake of efficiency; therefore I have also done the same. The details of the symbols and the supplements of the numbers of the Ayats which have been used have been written in detail before the list no 2.

The Compilation and the Order of the book

Some things need to be mentioned relating to the compilation and order of this book.

1. The order of the headings: The main focus of this book is to present the underlying differences in all the synonyms used in the Quraan, therefore the titles are in the order of the Urdu Alphabet. In the Arabic language if a verb is trilateral intransitive, when it is used in the derived trilateral form it becomes transitive. And if it is transitive in trilateral verb form, then it becomes double transitive or it holds specific qualities, except the derived form of the trilateral verb (infiaal )انفعال as it always stays intransitive. In the Arabic language under the base form, all the intransitive and transitive meanings are given but in the Urdu language, different words for intransitive and transitive forms are employed, such as from پہرنا to پہیرنا پہسلنا to پہسلانا کٹنا to کاٹنا. If I maintain the alphabetical order, then after پہرنا and پہسلنا it would be پہل and then پہیرنا and the demand of explanation required of the Arabic basic form meaning, is that they are all are put together پہرناپہیرنا put together, therefore to save time and repetition, I have chosen the latter. I have rejected the alphabetical order and put all the above mentioned words together. If the synonyms are more, then I have categorised them under two separate headings and if they are less then under just one heading such as اترنا اتارنا.

Likewise is the matter of joint verbs (afaal murakkaba) In which the first word is a noun and the next if it’s an intransitive verb then the murakkab becomes an intransitive and if it’s a transitive it becomes a transitive. Such as آباد ہونا آباد کرنا for the abovementioned reason I have again rejected the alphabetical order and mentioned آباد ہوناbefore آباد کرنا.

2. The underlying differences of the Urdu headings: sometimes the urdu headings are so close in meaning it is hard to distinguish the underlying differences such as بہاگنا دوڑنا, ٹہیرنا رکنا, and ٹہیرنا آبادہونا , in such place as well as clarification of the differences, I have indicated another heading which should be referred to.

3. The repetition of the Arabic base forms: This is clear that some Arabic words are so ambiguous in meaning that it is not possible to translate into one or two urdu words, a lot of explanation is needed such as و ع يmeans to put something in a bag and to tie the neck, now this word will come under the headings of, to be mean, to look after, to remember. Likewise خ ذ لmeans the abandoning of an intimate friend, of a friend at the time of need and to betray him, therefore this word will come under both headings, friend and to betray. Likewise the word زوج will come under many headings; husband, wife, companion, couple. Such words have been explained in one place and then referred to the other places.

4. The summary of synonyms: when there is only 2 or 3 synonyms to a word and is self-explanatory and the meaning of the underlying differences is made clear, then there is no need of a summary at the end. However, if there are more than 2 or 3 synonyms, then at the end of the heading, the summary of the words have been given. In a few places there were only 2 or 3 synonyms, but even after literal explanation, the underlying difference was not clear, therefore I have made it added a summary for further clarification.

Under some headings, there is a plethora of synonyms in the Quraan, for example:

Nineteen words have been used for: to fall or to make someone fall;

Fifteen words have been used for goods;

Thirteen have used for, to destroy;

Thirteen words for edge,

Twelve for, to make something strong,

Twenty one words for earth and others in this category

Twenty words, for noise and its type,

Thirteen words, for to become,

Fifteen words for, to fear,

Eleven words 11 for to run,

Twelve words for, to walk,

Twelve words for, to bend,

Fourteen words for, a group ,

Twelve words for, recompense,

Ten words have been used for, to be happy,

Ten words for, to collect,

Ten words for, to carry,

Ten words for, to give

Ten words for, friend.

Now you can understand how difficult it is to explain the underlying differences to all these synonyms and you can understand why there is a need of a summary at the end.

5. The use of Antonyms: the use of the antonyms is useful in such a way that if you know the opposite meaning of one word then the meaning becomes immediately apparent, for this reason the linguistics usually mention the antonyms. Even in many places of the Quraan, antonyms have been mentioned. For example; (5:2)

وَتَعَاوَنُوا عَلَى الْبِرِّ وَالتَّقْوَىٰ ۖ وَلَا تَعَاوَنُوا عَلَى الْإِثْمِ وَالْعُدْوَانِ ۚ And cooperate in righteousness and piety, but do not cooperate in sin and aggression. Now look in this ayat the word اثم has come contrary to بر and عدوان opposite ofتقوي. So if someone knows the meaning of بر and تقوي then he can fully understand the connotations of the words عدوان and اثم and vice versa. Therefore besides mentioning the opposites in the main body of the text, I have added a chapter with the heading of Antonyms, in the appendix and I have further categorised this into three parts.

6. The use of Quraanic Ayaats: I have only mentioned the specific Quraanic Ayaats, Ayaat or even part of an ayat according to the requirements for clarification purposes and to provide further examples.

7. Arabic Base Forms: To search for base forms of certain words is a real challenge. Even famous Linguists differ in their conclusions regarding the base forms of these particular words. In order to address this concern, I have placed these particular difficult words in brackets and also given a list of these words in the appendix, number five, under the title Some Difficult Base Forms.

8. Appendices: After mentioning the synonyms there were many words, such as Proper Nouns, which had no synonyms but required further explanation. Therefore to increase the benefit of this book, I have added a list of the following words in the appendix:

Q = Kaboo Pana (to gain control over)
Urdu Pg. 671-678
Pdf pg. 689-696
1. قَدَرَ  (Qadara):  قَدَر،قَدِر   (  قدرَا،قُدرَةَ  )   قدر  (Qadr):   To have control over.
·   قَدَرَالرِزق  :   to distribute sustenance (rizq) which includes everything that a person needs to survive, (for example, food, clothing, house, money and career etc.) to the last degree with proper planning. Or to hold back this sustenance or rizq.
·   قَدَرَعَلَيألْشَّيْء  :   to have control over something or to gain control.
Allah SWT says in Surah Al-Anbiya (21:87):     وَذَاٱلنُّونِإِذذَّهَبَمُغَـٰضِبً۬افَظَنَّأَنلَّننَّقۡدِرَعَلَيۡهِ  “And (mention) Dhu'n-Nun (Younis AS) (who got caught in a fish) when he went off in anger and deemed that We had no   power (control)  over him.”
2. اَقرَنَ   (Aqraan) :   to merge two things into one. Having the ability to subdue an accomplice.
·   :  قَرَنَ  to combine one thing with another or to tie together.
· قَرْن  :   a rope through which two camels are tied together.
·   اَقْرَنَلِلاَمْر  :   to be able to do something and to have complete control over a matter.
· اَقْرَنَعَلَيْهِ  :   to get tired or fed up of something.
Allah SWT says in Surah Az-Zukhruf (43:13):   سُبۡحَـٰنَٱلَّذِىسَخَّرَلَنَاهَـٰذَاوَمَاڪُنَّالَهُۥمُقۡرِنِينَ  “Glory to Him Who has   subjected   this (vehicle) to us, and we could have never had it.”
3. اِستَحُوذَ   (Istahoodh’a):   to subdue someone or something and impel it hastily because of one’s superior strength.
·   حَاذَألدَّآبَّة  : to drive an animal quickly.
·   حُوذ  : to be vigorous while doing an activity, doing something with quick, calculated, planned movements.
·   حاذ  : to be driven because a person is in difficulty?
·   استحُوذ  : to be seated on someone for example, an animal and to drive it with harshness or to overpower someone and hasten them with harshness.
·   اِستَحُوذَأَلْعَيرُعَلَياْلاَتانِ  : For a male donkey to ride on a back of female donkey and subduing her from both ends.
Allah SWT says in Surah Al-Mujadila (58:19):   اسْتَحْوَذَعَلَيْهِمُالشَّيْطَـنُفَأَنسَـهُمْذِكْرَاللَّهِ  “The Shaytan has   overpowered   them. So he has made them forget the remembrance of Allah.”
4. اِحْتَنَكَ  (Ih’tina’ka):   to gain control over someone or something because of superior intellect and wisdom.
·   حُنْك  : palate of the mouth
·   اِحتَنَكَالْفَرْس  : to insert a rope in a horse’s mouth
·   اَلْحُنُك  : a man whom society has made experienced or a man who gains experience during a lifetime.
·   احتنك  : to gain an upper hand on someone through intellect and experience
Allah SWT says in Surah Bani-Isra’iil (17:62):     لَئِنْأَخَّرْتَنِإِلَىيَوْمِالْقِيَـمَةِلأَحْتَنِكَنَّذُرِّيَّتَهُإَلاَّقَلِيلاً   “if You give me respite to the Day of Resurrection, I will surely,   seize   and mislead his offspring, all but a few!.”
Summary:

· قَدَرَالرِزق: to distribute sustenance (rizq) which includes everything that a person needs to survive, (for example, food, clothing, house, money and career etc.) to the last degree with proper planning. Or to hold back this sustenance or rizq.

· قَدَرَعَلَيألْشَّيْء: to have control over something or to gain control.

Allah SWT says in Surah Al-Anbiya (21:87): وَذَاٱلنُّونِإِذذَّهَبَمُغَـٰضِبً۬افَظَنَّأَنلَّننَّقۡدِرَعَلَيۡهِ“And (mention) Dhu'n-Nun (Younis AS) (who got caught in a fish) when he went off in anger and deemed that We had no power (control)over him.”

2. اَقرَنَ (Aqraan) : to merge two things into one. Having the ability to subdue an accomplice.

· :قَرَنَto combine one thing with another or to tie together.

· قَرْن: a rope through which two camels are tied together.

· اَقْرَنَلِلاَمْر: to be able to do something and to have complete control over a matter.

· اَقْرَنَعَلَيْهِ: to get tired or fed up of something.

Allah SWT says in Surah Az-Zukhruf (43:13): سُبۡحَـٰنَٱلَّذِىسَخَّرَلَنَاهَـٰذَاوَمَاڪُنَّالَهُۥمُقۡرِنِينَ“Glory to Him Who has subjected this (vehicle) to us, and we could have never had it.”

3. اِستَحُوذَ (Istahoodh’a): to subdue someone or something and impel it hastily because of one’s superior strength.

· حَاذَألدَّآبَّة: to drive an animal quickly.

· حُوذ: to be vigorous while doing an activity, doing something with quick, calculated, planned movements.

· حاذ: to be driven because a person is in difficulty?

· استحُوذ: to be seated on someone for example, an animal and to drive it with harshness or to overpower someone and hasten them with harshness.

· اِستَحُوذَأَلْعَيرُعَلَياْلاَتانِ: For a male donkey to ride on a back of female donkey and subduing her from both ends.

Allah SWT says in Surah Al-Mujadila (58:19): اسْتَحْوَذَعَلَيْهِمُالشَّيْطَـنُفَأَنسَـهُمْذِكْرَاللَّهِ“The Shaytan has overpowered them. So he has made them forget the remembrance of Allah.”

· حُنْك: palate of the mouth

· اِحتَنَكَالْفَرْس: to insert a rope in a horse’s mouth

· اَلْحُنُك: a man whom society has made experienced or a man who gains experience during a lifetime.

· احتنك: to gain an upper hand on someone through intellect and experience

1. قَدَر: To plan for a situation. To have control over

2. اَقرَنَ: to merge two things into one. Having the ability to subdue an accomplice.

3. اِستَحُوذَ: to subdue someone or something and impel it hastily because of one’s superior strength.

4. اِحْتَنَكَ: to gain control over someone or something because of superior intellect and wisdom.

10- QURBANI KA JANWAR [The Animal for Sacrifice]
Quran-Kareem has used the words like BUDN (بدن), NUSUK (نسك), HADA (هدى), and QALAID (قلائد).
10.1     BUDAN (بدن):   Plural of BUDNAU (بدنه). BADAN (بدن) is called the body of every living being provided that its blood has not dried. BADANA (بدن) and BADAN (بدن) means to become fat. And BUDN (بدن) means camels for sacrifice that are taken at Makah to slaughter. And the sacrificial camels are called BUDN (بدن) due to the relevance of their huge fat bodies.  Allah says:
Page-680
Surat Al-Ĥaj (The Pilgrimage) - سورة الحج     22:36
وَالْبُدْنَ جَعَلْنٰهَا لَكُمْ مِّنْ شَعَاۗىِٕرِ اللّٰهِ
And the camels and cattle We have appointed for you as among the symbols of Allah.
10.2     NUSUK (نسك):   NASAK (نسك) advocates about pray and closeness to GOD. NASIK (ناسيك) means chaste and NASEEKA (نسیکه) is called that animal for sacrifice that is done for drawing closer to GOD. And NUSUK (نسك) is the plural of NASEEKA (نسیکه). Then this word has generally connected to HAJJ. MANASIK-E-HAJJ (مناسک حج) i.e. rules and regulations of HAJJ. And also those sites where these commands are performed. Similarly NUSUK (نسك) refers to those sacrificial animals that are slaughtered at the site of MANA (منى) during AYAAM-E-TASHREEQ (ایام تشریق). Allah says:
Surat Al-Baqarah (The Cow) - سورة البقرة     2:196
فَمَنْ كَانَ مِنْكُمْ مَّرِيْضًا اَوْ بِهٖٓ اَذًى مِّنْ رَّاْسِهٖ فَفِدْيَةٌ مِّنْ صِيَامٍ اَوْ صَدَقَةٍ اَوْ نُسُك
And whoever among you is ill or has an ailment of the head [making shaving necessary must offer] a ransom of fasting [three days] or charity or sacrifice.
10.3     HADA (هدى):   Plural of HADIATUN (هدية) that sacrificial animal that is sent to BAIT-ALLAH-SHARIF (بیت الله شریف) whether it is camel or cow or sheep and whether it is male or female. Allah says:
Surat Al-Baqarah (The Cow) - سورة البقرة     2:196
وَلَا تَحْلِقُوْا رُءُوْسَكُمْ حَتّٰى يَبْلُغَ الْهَدْيُ مَحِلَّه
And do not shave your heads until the sacrificial animal has reached its place of slaughter.
10.4     QALAID (قلائد):   Singular QALADATA (قلادة). QALADA (قلد) means to put necklace in neck and QALADATA (قلادة) means necklace. And QALADATA (قلادة) is also called that sacrificial animal whose neck is fitted with a necklace or strap as a mark. Whether it is related to HAJJ (حج) or fulfilling a vow.  Allah says:
Surat Al-Mā'idah (The Table Spread) - سورة المائدة     5:2
يٰٓاَيُّھَا الَّذِيْنَ اٰمَنُوْا لَا تُحِلُّوْا شَعَاۗىِٕرَ اللّٰهِ وَلَا الشَّهْرَ الْحَرَامَ وَلَا الْهَدْيَ وَلَا الْقَلَاۗىِٕدَ
O you who have believed, do not violate the rites of Allah or [the sanctity of] the sacred month or [neglect the marking of] the sacrificial animals and garlanding [them].
Summary:
10.1   BUDN:   The sacrificial camels that are slaughtered during HAJJ.
10.2 HUDA: Those sacrificial animals which are taken by HAJI for HAJJ.
10.3 NUSUK: All types of those animals that are sacrificed at MNA.
10.4 QALAID: Those sacrificial animals whose necks are fitted with strap.

11. QASAM UTHANA [to swear, oath]
The words WA (وَ), TA (تَ), and LA (لَ), are used to give the meaning of swearing in native Arabic language. These words are either used as a habit or a catch phrase or sometimes to emphasize on something. If these words are related to ALLAH, it means to provide a testimony for something one swears upon. For example, Allah says in the Quran
Surah Al Asr (The Time): سورۃ العصر 103:1
وَٱلۡعَصۡرِ إِنَّ ٱلۡإِنسَـٰنَ لَفِى خُسۡرٍ
By (the Token of) Time (through the ages), Verily Man is in loss,
TA (تَ) is specifically used to swear upon Allah, as said by Hazrat Ibraheem:
Surah Al-Anbiya (the prophets): سورۃ الانَبیاء 21:57
وَتَٱللَّهِ لَأَڪِيدَنَّ أَصۡنَـٰمَكُم
And by Allah, I have a plan for your idols -
LA (لَ) is not used in Quran for swearing.
Synonyms:  QASAMA, YAMEEN, HALF, ALAI’AH, EELAA’
11.1 QASAMA (قَسَمَ):   QASAMA (قَسَمَ) means to distribute or dispense and also to swear, QASM (قَسْم) means a suspicion in heart that later turns into certainty   (dictionary Al   Manjad  ).    QUSAAMAT (قَُسَامَت) are those oaths that were undertaken on blood by the suspicious tribes with the saints   (dictionary Al   Manjad  ).   Thus QASAM (قَسَمَ) word is used to remove the suspicion in something and mostly used in case of a conflict. Allah says in the Holy Quran
Surah Al-Waqiah (The Inevitable): سُوۡرَةُ الواقِعَة 56:76
وَإِنَّهُ ۥ لَقَسَمٌ۬ لَّوۡ تَعۡلَمُونَ عَظِيمٌ
It is an oath, if you only knew, that is tremendous.
Another reference from the Holy Quran
Surah Al-Araf (The heights): سورۃ الأعرَاف 7:21
وَقَاسَمَهُمَآ إِنِّى لَكُمَا لَمِنَ ٱلنَّـٰصِحِينَ
And he swore to them, “I am a sincere advisor to you.”
11.2 YAMEEN (یَمِیْن):   To exempt from blame. Prophet Muhammad (S.A.A.W) said
الْبَيِّنَةَ عَلَى الْمُدَّعِي وَالْيَمِينَ عَلَى الْمُدَّعٰی عَلَیْہ
The burden of proof is on the claimant, and the taking of an oath is an obligation upon him who denies the claim
And YAMEEN (یَمِیْن) also refers to the right hand. When Native Arabs used to strengthen an oath, then the pledger would put his right hand on the hand of the pledgee. Therefore the word YAMEEN (یَمِیْن) started to be used to give the meaning of taking an oath. Plural AEMAAN (اَیْمَان). The word YAMEEN (یَمِیْن) is borrowed from word oath.
PAGE 682
Sometimes in order to emphasize on something, Native Arabs used to swear upon, and pledge oath by placing hand which had no significance in reality. These oaths were called frivolous by Allah and could be forgiven. An oath that has significance in reality and importance are called YAMEEN-MUNAQIDAH (یَمِیْن مُنْعَقِدَۃ) and one can be held responsible for them. Allah says in the Holy Quran
Surah Al-Baqarah (The cow): سورۃ البَقَرَۃ  2:225
لَّا يُؤَاخِذُكُمُ ٱللَّهُ بِٱللَّغۡوِ فِىٓ أَيۡمَـٰنِكُمۡ وَلَـٰكِن يُؤَاخِذُكُم بِمَا كَسَبَتۡ قُلُوبُكُمۡ‌ۗ
God does not hold you responsible for your unintentional oaths, but He holds you responsible for your intentions.
11.3 HALF (حَلْف):   HALAFA (حَلَفَ) means to be steadfast on something. Oath of loyalty. To stand resolutely to a pledge. Haleef tribes were those tribes which would pledge to help each other in peace or war. Thus HALF (حَلْف) referred to dissolving previous hostility and differences and to establish peace and loyalty amongst each other. In the Quran
Surah Al Tawbah (The repentance): سورۃ التوبھ 9:42
وَسَيَحۡلِفُونَ بِٱللَّهِ لَوِ ٱسۡتَطَعۡنَا لَخَرَجۡنَا مَعَكُمۡ
Still they swear by God: “Had we been able, we would have marched out with you.
11.4 ALAI’AH (اَلِیَّۃ):   ALA (اَلَا) (YA’LU (یَاْلُوْا), ALUWWA (اَلْوَّا)) comprises of two meanings, 1. to delay or show delinquency in some matter. For instance
Surah Ale- Imran (The family of Imran): سورۃ آل عِمْرن 3:118
لَا يَأۡلُونَكُمۡ خَبَالاً۬
who never cease to wish you harm.
2. to swear or pledge and oath, ALAI’AHTAN (اَلِیَّۃً) means a swear or oath. An oath whose pledger has to face suffering and delinquency. According to Ibn-Al-Faris an oath to prevent or disrupt a righteous matter. Allah says in the Holy Quran
Surah Al-Noor (The light): سورۃ النور 24:22
وَلَا يَأۡتَلِ أُوْلُواْ ٱلۡفَضۡلِ مِنكُمۡ وَٱلسَّعَةِ أَن يُؤۡتُوٓاْ أُوْلِى ٱلۡقُرۡبَىٰ وَٱلۡمَسَـٰكِينَ
And let not those who possess dignity and ease among you swear not to give to the near of kin and to the needy,
11.5 EELAA’ (اِیْلَا):   (ALA (اٰلٰی), YU’LU (یُؤْلُوْا), EELA’AN (اِیْلَاءً)): to stay away from wife, to oath to refrain from intimacy and sexual activates. During the times of ignorance people used to upset and distress their wives due to such oaths. Shariah has proclaimed the maximum tenure for this oath to be four months in order to curb this absurdity.  Allah says in the Quran
Surah Al-Baqarah (The cow): سورۃ البَقَرَۃ  2:226
لِّلَّذِينَ يُؤۡلُونَ مِن نِّسَآٮِٕهِمۡ تَرَبُّصُ أَرۡبَعَةِ أَشۡہُرٍ۬‌ۖ
Those who vow abstinence from their wives must wait for four months
Summary:
11.1 QASAM: For removing suspicion
11.2 YAMEEN: Exempt from blame, strengthen an oath
11.3 HALAF: Oaths of peace and loyalty amongst each other
11.4 ALAI’AH: Oath to prevent or disrupt a righteous matter
11.5 EELAA’: Oath to refrain from intimacy with wife

11.4 ALAI’AH (اَلِیَّۃ): ALA (اَلَا) (YA’LU (یَاْلُوْا), ALUWWA (اَلْوَّا)) comprises of two meanings, 1. to delay or show delinquency in some matter. For instance

Surah Ale- Imran (The family of Imran): سورۃ آل عِمْرن 3:118

 لَا يَأۡلُونَكُمۡ خَبَالاً۬

who never cease to wish you harm.

 

2. to swear or pledge and oath, ALAI’AHTAN (اَلِیَّۃً) means a swear or oath. An oath whose pledger has to face suffering and delinquency. According to Ibn-Al-Faris an oath to prevent or disrupt a righteous matter. Allah says in the Holy Quran

Surah Al-Noor (The light): سورۃ النور 24:22

وَلَا يَأۡتَلِ أُوْلُواْ ٱلۡفَضۡلِ مِنكُمۡ وَٱلسَّعَةِ أَن يُؤۡتُوٓاْ أُوْلِى ٱلۡقُرۡبَىٰ وَٱلۡمَسَـٰكِينَ

 And let not those who possess dignity and ease among you swear not to give to the near of kin and to the needy,

11.5 EELAA’ (اِیْلَا): (ALA (اٰلٰی), YU’LU (یُؤْلُوْا), EELA’AN (اِیْلَاءً)): to stay away from wife, to oath to refrain from intimacy and sexual activates. During the times of ignorance people used to upset and distress their wives due to such oaths. Shariah has proclaimed the maximum tenure for this oath to be four months in order to curb this absurdity.  Allah says in the Quran

Surah Al-Baqarah (The cow): سورۃ البَقَرَۃ  2:226

 لِّلَّذِينَ يُؤۡلُونَ مِن نِّسَآٮِٕهِمۡ تَرَبُّصُ أَرۡبَعَةِ أَشۡہُرٍ۬‌ۖ

Those who vow abstinence from their wives must wait for four months

Summary:

11.1 QASAM: For removing suspicion

11.2 YAMEEN: Exempt from blame, strengthen an oath

11.3 HALAF: Oaths of peace and loyalty amongst each other

11.4 ALAI’AH: Oath to prevent or disrupt a righteous matter

11.5 EELAA’: Oath to refrain from intimacy with wife

raw_text:
12. QASAM TORNA [to break an oath]
Synonyms: NAQATHA, NAQADA, HANITHA
PAGE 683
12.1 NAQATHA (نَکَثَ):   popular word for breaking an oath. To break an oath of commitment, allegiance, to break a promise   (dictionary Al   Manjad  ).    Allah says in the Quran
Surah Al Tawbah (The repentance): سورۃ التوبھ 9:13
أَلَا تُقَـٰتِلُونَ قَوۡمً۬ا نَّكَثُوٓاْ أَيۡمَـٰنَهُمۡ
Will you not fight a people who violated their oaths?
12.2 NAQADA (نَقَضَ):   NAQADA (نَقَضَ) means destruction. NAQDA-AL-BANA’ (نَقْضَ الْبَنَاء) means to demolish a building. NAQAD-AL-JABL (نَقَضَ الجَبْل) means to untie the knots of a rope. NAQAD-AL-AHD-WAL-AMR (نقض العھد والامر) means to ruin an oath after solidity, with lame excuses. NAQAD-AMAN means to disrupt peace and to spread mayhem   (dictionary Al   Manjad  ).    The word NAQADA (نَقَضَ) relates to wider meanings than NAQATHA (نَکَثَ). (Also see TORNA (to break)). Allah says in the Quran
Surat An-Nahl (The Bee): سورۃ النّحل16:91
وَلَا تَنقُضُواْ ٱلۡأَيۡمَـٰنَ بَعۡدَ تَوۡڪِيدِهَا
and do not break your oaths after ratifying them
12.3 HANITHA (حَنِثَ):   HINTH (حَنْث) means a false or fake oath, sin or disobey. HINTHA-FIL-YAMEEN (حَنِثَ فِی الْیَمِیْن) means to break a pledge or vow. To vow to do something and break it. Allah Says in the Holy Quran
Surah Saad (Saad): سورۃ ص 38:44
وَخُذۡ بِيَدِكَ ضِغۡثً۬ا فَٱضۡرِب بِّهِۦ وَلَا تَحۡنَثۡ‌ۗ
“Take with your hand a bundle, and strike with it, and do not break your oath.”
Summary:
12.1 NAQATHA: common word for breaking a vow.
12.2 NAQADA: ruin and oath after solidity, with lame excuses.
12.3 HANITHA: falsify an oath, to vow to do something and break the vow.

raw_text:
13 QALA’ [castle, stronghold]
Synonyms: HUSOON, SAYASEE, BUROOJ, MAHAREEB
13.1 HUSOON (حُصُوْن):   (singular HISN (حِصْن)) HISN (حِصْن) refers to any place that can give protection, it can be surrounded and where one can take refuge. Castle with barricade so one can take refuge, protect oneself and face the enemy. In the Quran
Surah Al Hashr (The Exile): سورۃ الحَشر 59:2
وَظَنُّوٓاْ أَنَّهُم مَّانِعَتُهُمۡ حُصُونُہُم مِّنَ ٱللَّهِ
while they deemed that their strongholds would protect them from Allah.
13.2 SAYASEE (صَیَاصِی):   (singular SISIYAH (صَیْصِیَہ)) Anything that is used for protection. The horns of a bull are also called SISIYAH (صَیْصِیَہ) because it is used by the bull to protect itself. Protective place or a castle, anything resembling a castle, the battle strongholds of Jews. Allah says in the Quran
Suran Al-Ahzaab (The Clans): سورۃ الأحزَاب 33:26
وَأَنزَلَ ٱلَّذِينَ ظَـٰهَرُوهُم مِّنۡ أَهۡلِ ٱلۡكِتَـٰبِ مِن صَيَاصِيهِمۡ وَقَذَفَ فِى قُلُوبِهِمُ ٱلرُّعۡبَ
And He brought down from their strongholds those of the People of the Book who backed them, and He threw terror into their hearts.
PAGE 684
13.3 BUROOJ (بُرُوْج):   (singular BURJ (بُرْج)) BARAJA (بَرَجَ) means to appear, to emerge. BARRAJ (بَرَّج) mean to construct a BURJ (بُرْج), and BURJ (بُرْج)means any dome shaped tall building, a castle or a palace. Allah says in the Quran
Surah An-Nisa (The women): سورۃ النِّسا 4:78
أَيۡنَمَا تَكُونُواْ يُدۡرِككُّمُ ٱلۡمَوۡتُ وَلَوۡ كُنتُمۡ فِى بُرُوجٍ۬ مُّشَيَّدَةٍ۬‌ۗ
"Wherever you are, death will find you out, even if you are in towers built up strong and high!"
13.4 MAHAREEB (مَحَارِیْب):   (singular MEHRAAB (مَحْرَاب)) MEHRAAB (مَحْرَاب) means the area of entry of a house, an arch, a place for people to gather. Also it means contentious, litigious or brave   (dictionary Al   Manjad  ), and place where a battle is planned or battle equipment is made. Therefore can be used to refer to a stronghold. In the Quran
Surah Saba (Sheba): سورۃ سَبَإ 34:13
يَعۡمَلُونَ لَهُ ۥ مَا يَشَآءُ مِن مَّحَـٰرِيبَ وَتَمَـٰثِيلَ
They worked for him as he desired, (making) arches, images,
Summary:
13.1 HUSOON: A castle that can be surrounded can be used for protection and refuge.
13.2 SAYASEE: Protective place or a castle, anything resembling a castle, the battle strongholds of Jews.
13.3 BUROOJ: Dome shaped tall building, a castle or a palace
13.4 MAHAREEB: P  lace where a battle is planned and is safe.
For QUWWAT see TAAQAT

14. QAMEES [Shirt]
Synonyms: QAMEES, SARABEEL
14.1 QAMEES (قَمِیْص):   A famous type of garment, a shirt or a kurta (long shirt). In the Quran
Surah Yusuf (Joseph): سورۃ یُوسُف 12:27
وَإِن كَانَ قَمِيصُهُ ۥ قُدَّ مِن دُبُرٍ۬ فَكَذَبَتۡ
But if his shirt is torn from the back: then she has lied
14.2 SARABEEL (سَرَابِیْل):   (singular SARBAL (سربال)) The word is used for both shirt and trouser. Shirt or anything that can be worn (dictionary Al   Manjad  ).
Surat An-Nahl (The Bee): سورۃ النّحل16:81
وَجَعَلَ لَكُمۡ سَرَٲبِيلَ تَقِيڪُمُ ٱلۡحَرَّ
Has given you garments to protect you from the heat,
