title: content/q/q15.html
raw_text:
PAGE 685
15 QUWWAT DAINA [to empower, strengthen]
Synonyms: AYYAD, AAZARA, AZZAZA
15.1 AYYAD (اَیَّدَ):   AL-AID (الاید) means intense power. And AYYAD (اَیَّدَ) means to help someone tremendously, to strengthen, to aid. Allah says in the Quran
Surah Al Tawbah (The repentance): سورۃ التوبھ 9:40
فَأَنزَلَ ٱللَّهُ سَڪِينَتَهُ ۥ عَلَيۡهِ وَأَيَّدَهُ ۥ بِجُنُودٍ۬ لَّمۡ تَرَوۡهَا
God made His tranquility descend upon him, and supported him with forces you did not see
15.2 AAZARA (اٰزَرَ):   AL-IZR (اَلْاِزْر) means root or TEHBAND (تہبند)   (a cloth wrapped around the bottom half). AL-IZAAR   (اَلْاِزَار)   means a shawl, tehband, a drape or quay. AAZAR-AL-BANAAT   (اٰزَرَالْبَنَات)   means intertwining of plants. AZZARA   (اَزَّرَ)   means to strengthen, or to give power   (dictionary Al   Manjad  ). Thus AAZARA (اٰزَرَ) means  something giving itself power. Allah says in the Quran
Surah Al-Fath (The victory): سورۃ الفَتْح  48:29
كَزَرۡعٍ أَخۡرَجَ شَطۡـَٔهُ ۥ فَـَٔازَرَهُ ۥ فَٱسۡتَغۡلَظَ فَٱسۡتَوَىٰ عَلَىٰ سُوقِهِ
Like a plant that sprouts, becomes strong, grows thick, and rests on its stem,
15.3 AZZAZA (عَزَّزَ):   the opposite of AZZA (عَزَّ) is DALLA (ذَلَّ). AZZ (عَزَّ) means to be superior, AAZZA (اَعَزَّ) means to honor and AZZAZA (عَزَّزَ) means to empower or strengthen an inferior so much so that he becomes a noble and dignified person. Dignity means a state which saves a man from humiliation and inferiority (dictionary Al   Manjad  ). Allah says in the Quran
Surah Yaseen (Yaseen): سورۃ ٰیٰس 36:14
إِذۡ أَرۡسَلۡنَآ إِلَيۡہِمُ ٱثۡنَيۡنِ فَكَذَّبُوهُمَا فَعَزَّزۡنَا بِثَالِثٍ۬
When We (first) sent to them two messengers, they rejected them: But We strengthened them with a third
Summary:
15.1 AYYADA: help someone tremendously, to strengthen
15.2 AAZARA: Giving power to itself and strengthen
15.3 AZZAZA: Empower or strengthen an inferior so he no longer remains inferior.
Also see MADAD KERNA [to help], and MAZBOOT KARNA [to fortify]

title: content/q/q16.html
raw_text:
16 QAYAMAT [QAYAMAH (Day of resurrection) and its Synonyms]
Synonyms: QIYAMAH, ASSA’ATA, YAWM-AD-DEEN, YAWM-AL-KHUROOJ, YAWM-AL-HISAAB, YAWM-AL-FASAL, GHASHIA, WAQIAH, AL-HAQQAH, SAKH-KHATA, AZIFAH, QARIAH, TA’AMMA-TIL-KUBRA
16.1 QIYAMAH (قِیَامَۃ):   something that will be certainly established. A day or time that will be established for the implementation of truth and justice. The different names of this day in the Quran are due to the different aspects and conditions of this day. Allah says in the Quran
Surah Ale- Imran (The family of Imran): سورۃ آل عِمْرن 3:185
كُلُّ نَفۡسٍ۬ ذَآٮِٕقَةُ ٱلۡمَوۡتِ‌ۗ وَإِنَّمَا تُوَفَّوۡنَ أُجُورَڪُمۡ يَوۡمَ ٱلۡقِيَـٰمَةِ‌ۖ
Every soul will have a taste of death, and you will receive your recompense on the Day of Resurrection.
PAGE 686
16.2 ASSA’ATA (السَّاعَۃ):   SA’ATA (سَاعَۃ) means time. And ASSA’ATA  (السَّاعَۃ) means a specific time. In Quran ASSA’ATA (السَّاعَۃ) refers to the time when the trumpets will be blown for the first time. Allah says in the Quran
Surah Al-Ana’am (The Cattle): سورۃ الانعام 6:31
إِذَا جَآءَتۡہُمُ ٱلسَّاعَةُ بَغۡتَةً۬ قَالُواْ يَـٰحَسۡرَتَنَا عَلَىٰ مَا فَرَّطۡنَا فِيہَا
Then, when the Hour comes upon them suddenly, they will say, “Alas for us, how we have neglected it.”

17. QAID KHANA [Prison, Jail]
Synonyms: SIJN, HASEER
17.1 SIJN (سِجْن): A famous word for prison or jail. An institution where persons are confined for punishment by the order of court. In the Quran
Surah Yusuf (Joseph): سورۃ یُوسُف 12:42
فَلَبِثَ فِى ٱلسِّجۡنِ بِضۡعَ سِنِينَ
So he remained in prison for several years.
17.2 HASEER (حَصِیْر):   HASARA (حَصَرَ) means to surround from all the sides, to besiege or circumvent. HASEER (حَصِیْر) is a place to detain or confine a prison. In the Quran
Surah Al-Israa (The Night Journey): سورۃ الٕاسرَاء  17:8
وَجَعَلۡنَا جَهَنَّمَ لِلۡكَـٰفِرِينَ حَصِيرًا
We have made Hell a prison for the disbelievers

18. QAID KARNA – QAIDI BANANA [to imprison, to hold captive]
Synonyms: HABASA, ATHBATA, ASARA, SAJANA
18.1 HABASA (حَبَسَ):   To stop someone from getting up. HABAS-ASH-SHAI (حَبَسَ الشَّیْ) means to guard something. MAHBASA (مَحْبَسَۃ) means a prison. Also the place of meditation or reclusion of saints. HABASA (حَبَسَ) means to detain someone, or keep in custody   (dictionary Al   Manjad  )  . And HABASA (حَبَسَ) also means MANA’-AT-TASARAF (منع عن التصرّف) means to stop someone to use his/her property. MAHBAS (مَحْبَسَ) means jail or prison where criminals are kept during interrogation. Allah says in the Holy Quran
Surah Al-Maeda (The table spread): سورۃ المَائدہ 5:106
تَحۡبِسُونَهُمَا مِنۢ بَعۡدِ ٱلصَّلَوٰةِ فَيُقۡسِمَانِ بِٱللَّهِ
Detain them both after prayer, and let them both swear by Allah:
18.2 ATHBATA (اَثْبَتَ):   To tie someone up with lace or rope   (dictionary Al   Manjad  )  , to lash someone up and stop his/her movement and keep him in ones custody. In the Quran
Surah Al-Anfal (The Spoils of War): سُوۡرَةُ الاٴنفَال 8:30
وَإِذۡ يَمۡكُرُ بِكَ ٱلَّذِينَ كَفَرُواْ لِيُثۡبِتُوكَ أَوۡ يَقۡتُلُوكَ أَوۡ يُخۡرِجُوكَ‌ۚ
When the disbelievers plotted against you, to imprison you, or kill you, or expel you.
18.3 ASARA (اَسَرَ):   Also means to tie someone up with a rope. The difference between ASARA (اَسَرَ) and ATHBATA (اَثْبَتَ) is that ASARA (اَسَرَ) means to capture during a battle. ASEER means war prisoner (plural ASRAA (اَسْرٰی), USARAA (اُسَارٰی)). Allah says in the Quran
Surah Al-Baqarah (The cow): سورۃ البَقَرَۃ  2:85
وَإِن يَأۡتُوكُمۡ أُسَـٰرَىٰ تُفَـٰدُوهُمۡ وَهُوَ مُحَرَّمٌ عَلَيۡڪُمۡ إِخۡرَاجُهُمۡ‌ۚ
And if they come to you as captives, you ransom them, although it was forbidden to you.
In Another Reference in Holy Quran
Suran Al-Ahzaab (The clans): سورۃ الأحزَاب 33:26
فَرِيقً۬ا تَقۡتُلُونَ وَتَأۡسِرُونَ فَرِيقً۬ا
Some of them you killed, and others you took captive.
18.4 SAJANA (سَجَنَ):   To imprison someone after finding him guilty of charges against him by the court. To send to prison, prison someone for some crime by the leader. In the Quran
Surah Yusuf (Joseph): سورۃ یُوسُف 12:25
قَالَتۡ مَا جَزَآءُ مَنۡ أَرَادَ بِأَهۡلِكَ سُوٓءًا إِلَّآ أَن يُسۡجَنَ أَوۡ عَذَابٌ أَلِيمٌ۬
She said, “What is the penalty for him who desired to dishonor your wife, except imprisonment or a painful punishment?”
Summary:
18.1 HABASA: Stop someone to use his/her property.
18.2 ATHBATA: To lash someone up and stop his/her movement
18.3 ASARA: Capture during a battle
18.4 SAJANA: Imprison someone after finding him guilty of charges against him by the court

 فَرِيقً۬ا تَقۡتُلُونَ وَتَأۡسِرُونَ فَرِيقً۬ا

 Some of them you killed, and others you took captive.

18.4 SAJANA (سَجَنَ): To imprison someone after finding him guilty of charges against him by the court. To send to prison, prison someone for some crime by the leader. In the Quran

Surah Yusuf (Joseph): سورۃ یُوسُف 12:25

قَالَتۡ مَا جَزَآءُ مَنۡ أَرَادَ بِأَهۡلِكَ سُوٓءًا إِلَّآ أَن يُسۡجَنَ أَوۡ عَذَابٌ أَلِيمٌ۬

She said, “What is the penalty for him who desired to dishonor your wife, except imprisonment or a painful punishment?”

Summary:

18.1 HABASA: Stop someone to use his/her property.

18.2 ATHBATA: To lash someone up and stop his/her movement

18.3 ASARA: Capture during a battle

18.4 SAJANA: Imprison someone after finding him guilty of charges against him by the court

title: content/q/q2.html
raw_text:
Qaafla (caravan)
1.   سَيَّارَة   (siyaara’ta):   Anyone or anything that continuously stays in motion. This motion can be rotational for example, in the case of planets, or translational for example, a car. In common language, this means a group of people or a convoy that are travelling together.
· سَارَ  :   to walk or move around.
· سَيَّارَات  :   the planets of the universe.
Allah SWT says in Surah Yusuf (Jacob) (12:19):   وَجَاءَتْسَيَّارَةٌفَأَرْسَلُواْوَارِدَهُمْفَأَدْلَىدَلْوَهُ  “And there came a   caravan   of travelers and they sent their water-drawer, and he let down his bucket (into the well).”
2.   عِيْر  :   A caravan that carries food. People and animals are all included in the caravan. Among linguists it doesn’t matter if this caravan has camels, horses or donkeys, they are all part of it.   Hence, the Humeri tribe is also described by this term.
Allah SWT says in the Surah Yusuf (12:70):   ثُمَّأَذَّنَمُؤَذِّنٌأَيَّتُهَاالْعِيرُإِنَّكُمْلَسَارِقُونَ   “Then a crier cried: "O you (in) the   caravan  ! Surely, you are thieves!”
3.   رَكْب  :   A caravan riding on horses or ostriches.
·   رَكَبَ  : to ride on
·   رِكَاب  : the vehicle on which a rider rides. It can be an animal or modern day cars.
·   رَاكِب  : rider. In common usage this word has been designated for someone who is riding a high tide. In other words who thinks highly of him or herself and is probably in a seventh sky. Literally, a caravan riding on ostriches.
·   رُكْبَان  ,   رَكْب  ,  رُكُوْب  :   These are all plural of   رَاكِب   or rider.
·   ركْبُ  : a convoy that is riding on horses or camels.
Allah SWT says in Surah Anfaal (8:42):   إِذْأَنتُمبِالْعُدْوَةِالدُّنْيَاوَهُمبِالْعُدْوَةِالْقُصْوَىوَالرَّكْبُأَسْفَلَمِنكُمْ  “(And remember) when you (the Muslim army) were on the near side of the valley (Medina), and they on the farther side, and the   caravan   on the ground lower than you.”
Summary:
1.   سَيَّارَة  :   people travelling together either on foot or riding on animals/vehicles. This is common usage.
2.   عِيْر  :   A convoy that carries food or crops.
3.   رَكْب  :   A caravan riding on horses or ostriches.

title: content/q/q3.html
raw_text:
Qabar (grave)
1.   قَبْر   (Qabar):   grave
·   قبُور  :   Plural i.e. graves
·   مقبره  :   A tomb. Grave of a famous person
· مقابر  :   Plural of tombs
Allah SWT says in Surah Tawbah (9:84):   وَلاَتُصَلِّعَلَىأَحَدٍمِّنْهُممَّاتَأَبَداًوَلاَتَقُمْعَلَىقَبْرِهِ   “  And never (O Muhammad) pray (funeral prayer) for any of them (hypocrites) who dies, nor stand at his   grave  .”
2.   مَرقْد   (Marqad):   Bedroom or wherever one sleeps. In the Qur’an this word is used metaphorically because disbelievers will compare the hardships of graveto those of the Day of Judgment and associate the former as easier compared to the latter.
· رَقَدَ  :   To sleep lightly for a long time. Slumber.
Allah SWT says in Surah Ya’seen (36:52):   قَالُواْيوَيْلَنَامَنبَعَثَنَامِنمَّرْقَدِنَا  “They (disbelievers) will say: "Woe to us! Who has raised us up from our   place of sleep  ?”
3.   جَدَث   (Jada’as):   A body which has no remains left or are not identifiable.
·   جدث   :Linguists have not distinguished this word from qabar. But, in the Quran even though qabar is used more commonly,   جدث   refers to a grave that cannot be identified as it has no remnants. Besides, many a times, somebody is devoured by an animal or a human is drowned in the ocean where sea animals eat the body. In Hindu and other cultures, the bodies are cremated so there is no chance that it can be identified and are just part of the larger system. So, for those cases   جدث   is used. In the Quran, this word is used twice and both the times it is used when there have been nothing left of the graves and thus, they cannot be identified.
· اجداث  :   plural of   جدث
Allah SWT says in Surah Ma’aarij (70:43):   يَوْمَيَخْرُجُونَمِنَالاٌّجْدَاثِسِرَاعاًكَأَنَّهُمْإِلَىنُصُبٍيُوفِضُونَ  “The Day when they will come out of the   graves   quickly as a (hunter) runs towards the caged hunted game.”
This Ayah (verse) mentions Day of Judgment, when there would be no remnants of the graves would be left around. This second verse paints a similar picture:
Allah SWT says in Surah Ya’seen (36:51):   وَنُفِخَفِىالصُّورِفَإِذَاهُممِّنَالاٌّجْدَاثِإِلَىرَبِّهِمْيَنسِلُونَ  “And the Trumpet will be blown (second time) and behold from the   graves   they will come out quickly to their Lord.”
Summary:
1.   قَبْر  :   this is common usage. Used for a body of which may or may not have any remains left.
2.   مَرقْد  :   used for the grave as a metaphor.
3.   جَدَث  :   a body which has no remains left or are not identifiable.

title: content/q/q4.html
raw_text:
Qabool kerna (to accept)
1.   قَبِلَ   (Qabila):   To happily accept something. Used only for actions.
·   قَبُوْلاً  :   To be accepting of how one acts or behaves.
Allah SWT says in Surah Nuur (24:4):   وَلاَتَقْبَلُواْلَهُمْشَهَادَةًأَبَداً   “  and never   accept   their testimony.”
2.   قَبِلَ  ,   تَقَبَّل   (Taqabul and Qabila):   both have similar meanings.
· تَقَبَّل  :   to accept payment for something.
· قَبِل  :   this is used more commonly.
Allah SWT says in Surah Al-Imraan (3:35):   إِذْقَالَتِامْرَأَتُعِمْرَنَرَبِّإِنِّينَذَرْتُلَكَمَافِيبَطْنِيمُحَرَّرًافَتَقَبَّلْمِنِّي  “(Remember) when the wife of `Imran said: "O my Lord! I have vowed to You what is in my womb to be dedicated for Your services, so   accept   this from me.”
3.   اَجَاب  ,   اِسْتِجَاب   (Ajaab and Istijaab):   both are used for acceptance of prayer. Means to not only accept the prayer, but to console the person as well.
Allah SWT says in Surah Naml (27:62):   أَمَّنيُجِيبُالْمُضْطَرَّإِذَادَعَاهُ  “Is not He Who   responds   to the distressed one, when he calls on Him.”
Also in Surah Mu’min He says (40:60):   وَقَالَرَبُّكُـمْادْعُونِىأَسْتَجِبْلَكُمْ   “  And your Lord said: "Call upon Me, I will   answer   you.”
Summary:
1.   قَبِلَ  :   to happily accept something. Used only for actions.
2.   تَقَبَّل  :   It is derived from   قَبِلَ   . Means to accept payment for something.
3.   اِسْتِجَاب  :   to not only accept the prayer, but to console the person as well.

title: content/q/q5.html
raw_text:
Qabeela and Khandaan (Tribe and Family)
1.   شُعُوْب   (Shaboob):   a person with an offspring and from that, the continuation of generations which later on becomes a whole new sect or race. Caste.
·   شعب  :   a generation or sect. It is also used for a branch. Basically, two elements are necessarily implied by the meaning of   شعب  . It has to have 1) a common origin and 2) it must be divided. For instance, it is used when something emerges from a common ancestor but, divides into several different fragments while still maintaining contact with the original. It can be a tree with the same roots and many branches. Or a family.
2.   قَبَائِل   (Qabaa’el):   tribes.
·   قبيله  :   singular i.e. A tribe. So, a   شعب   which has the same origins gets divided into many tribes   قَبَائِل  .
· قبائلالرأس  :   For example, the bones of the skull which are interconnected to each other.
Allah SWT says in Surah Hujuraat (49:13):   وَجَعَلْنَـكُمْشُعُوباًوَقَبَآئِلَلِتَعَـرَفُواْإِنَّأَكْرَمَكُمْعَندَاللَّهِأَتْقَـكُمْ  “and We made you into nations and   tribes   that you may know one another. Verily, the most honorable of you with Allah is that (believer) who has At-Taqwa.”
3.   فَصِيْلَة   (Faseela’tah):   a family or a household. In today’s terminology, a nuclear family.
Allah SWT says in Surah Ma’aarij (70:11-13):   يَوَدُّالْمُجْرِمُلَوْيَفْتَدِيمِنْعَذَابِيَوْمِئِذٍبِبَنِيهِ   -   وَصَـحِبَتِهِوَأَخِيهِ   -   وَفَصِيلَتِهِالَّتِىتُـْوِيهِ  “The guilty man will long to be able to ransom himself from the punishment of that day at the price of his children. And his spouse and his brother. And his   kin   that harbored him.”
4.   رَهط   (Rahat):   a tribe with only three to nine young male members, excluding the women is labeled as   رَهط  .   This word is also used for the leader of such a tribe. Adding numerical or numbers after the word would imply number of people. For example,   خَمْسَةُرَهطٍ   means five men.
Allah SWT says in Surah Hud (11:92):   قَالَيقَوْمِأَرَهْطِىأَعَزُّعَلَيْكُممِّنَاللَّهِ  “He (Shu’aib AS) said: "O my people! Is then my   brothers   are of more weight with you than Allah?”
5.   عَشِيْرة   (Asheer’at):   A small tribe which only comprises of the male’s relatives.
· عَشَر  :   to live together
·   عشيرة  :   A small tribe which only comprises of the male’s relatives. For example, sons, daughters, paternal grandparents, paternal uncles and aunts.
Allah SWT says in Surah Shu’araa (26:214):   وَأَنذِرْعَشِيرَتَكَالاٌّقْرَبِينَ  “And warn your   tribe of near kindred  .”
6.   اَسْبَاط   (Asbaat):   daughter’s children or tribes of Jews (Israelites).
·   سِبْط  :   used for grandchildren. For example, grandsons but, the word is mainly specific for any grandchildren from one’s daughter just like   حفيد   is specific for son’s children.
In normal lexicon if this word is used in association with Jews, then it means tribe. In classical Arabic, the word   اَسْبَاط   is used for the children of Ishaac (Isaac AS) just like the word   قبيله   is used for the children of Ismaael (Ishmael AS).
Allah SWT says in Surah Al-Araf (7:160):   وَقَطَّعْنَاهُمُاثْنَتَيْعَشْرَةَأَسْبَاطًاأُمَمًا  “And We divided them into twelve   tribes   (as distinct) nations.”
Summary:
1. شُعُوْب  :   castes
2. قَبَائِل  :   tribes
3. فَصِيْلَة  :   a family or a household
4. رَهط  :   a tribe with up to nine young male members and their leader or chief
5. عَشِيْرة  :   a small tribe which only comprises of the male’s relatives
6. اَسْبَاط  :   daughter’s children or tribes of Jews (Israelites)

Allah SWT says in Surah Shu’araa (26:214): وَأَنذِرْعَشِيرَتَكَالاٌّقْرَبِينَ“And warn your tribe of near kindred.”

6. اَسْبَاط (Asbaat): daughter’s children or tribes of Jews (Israelites).

· سِبْط: used for grandchildren. For example, grandsons but, the word is mainly specific for any grandchildren from one’s daughter just like حفيد is specific for son’s children.

In normal lexicon if this word is used in association with Jews, then it means tribe. In classical Arabic, the word اَسْبَاط is used for the children of Ishaac (Isaac AS) just like the word قبيله is used for the children of Ismaael (Ishmael AS).

Allah SWT says in Surah Al-Araf (7:160): وَقَطَّعْنَاهُمُاثْنَتَيْعَشْرَةَأَسْبَاطًاأُمَمًا“And We divided them into twelve tribes (as distinct) nations.”

Summary:

1. شُعُوْب: castes

2. قَبَائِل: tribes

3. فَصِيْلَة: a family or a household

4. رَهط: a tribe with up to nine young male members and their leader or chief

5. عَشِيْرة: a small tribe which only comprises of the male’s relatives

6. اَسْبَاط: daughter’s children or tribes of Jews (Israelites)

title: content/q/q6.html
raw_text:
Qatal kerna (to murder someone)
1.   قَتَلَ   (Qatala):   This is used commonly. To kill. To separate the soul from the body either through execution or by other means.
Allah SWT says in Surah Nisaa (4:89):   فَإِنلَّمْيَعْتَزِلُوكُمْوَيُلْقُواْإِلَيْكُمُالسَّلَمَوَيَكُفُّواْأَيْدِيَهُمْفَخُذُوهُمْوَاقْتُلُوهُمْحَيْثُثِقِفْتُمُوهُمْ  “If they withdraw not and do not restraint themselves then take (hold of) them and   kill them   wherever you find them.”
2.   سَفَكَ   (Safa’ka): to spill water or innocent blood
· سَفُوْك  :   a liar
·   سَفَّاك  :   a tyrant. Someone who murders innocent people and sheds their blood
Allah SWT says in Surah Al-Baqarah (2:30):   قَالُواْأَتَجْعَلُفِيهَامَنيُفْسِدُفِيهَاوَيَسْفِكُالدِّمَآءَ  “Angels said: "Will You place therein those who will make mischief therein and   shed blood  .”
3.   حَسَّ   (Hasaa):   to pull something from its roots. In dictionary terms it means how severely somebody is killed. Therefore, it means to kill somebody so brutally or kill so precisely that enemy gets completely annihilated and rooted out.
Allah SWT says in Surah Al-Imran (3:152):   وَلَقَدْصَدَقَكُمُاللَّهُوَعْدَهُإِذْتَحُسُّونَهُمبِإِذْنِهِ   “And Allah did indeed fulfill His promise to you when you were   killing them  (your enemy) with His permission.”
4.   اَثْخَنَ   (Askha’an):   to be harsh while killing or murdering someone, mass murder or genocide.
· ثَخَنَ  :   to weigh something while carrying
·   ثَخُنَ  :   thick and sturdy
·   اثخنفياَلارض  :   transgressing the limits in shedding blood
Allah SWT says in Surah Muhammad (47:4)   فَإِذَالَقِيتُمُالَّذِينَكَفَرُواْفَضَرْبَالرِّقَابِحَتَّىإِذَآأَثْخَنتُمُوهُمْفَشُدُّواْالْوَثَاقَ   “  So, when you meet those who disbelieve (in battle),   smite (their) necks  until you have fully defeated them, then tighten their bonds.”
Summary:
1.   قَتَلَ  :   This is used commonly. Murder
2.   سَفَكَ  : to spill innocent blood
3.   حَسَّ  : to root out the enemy
4.   اَثْخَنَ  : to be harsh while killing or murdering someone, mass murder or genocide.

title: content/q/q7.html
raw_text:
Qadam (feet)
1.   قَدَم   (Qadam):   foot or to step forward. Therefore, it is not only foot but the whole shin and the feet, famous body parts.
·   اقدام  :   plural i.e. feet
Allah SWT says in Surah Nahl (16:94):   فَتَزِلَّقَدَمٌبَعْدَثُبُوتِهَا   “resulting in the slip of a   foot   after it was firmly planted.”
2.   خُطُوَة   (Khoot’wata):   distance between the two feet. It means to cross the limits. To move forward.
·   خُطُوَات  :   plural i.e. Steps, moving forward or progressing or the complete way.
·   خُطُوَاتلَازِمَه  :   necessary steps
Allah SWT says in Surah Al-Baqarah (2:168):   وَلاَتَتَّبِعُواْخُطُوَتِالشَّيْطَـنِ   “and follow not the   footsteps   of Shaytan (Satan).”
3.   اَثَر   (Asaar):   landmarks, signs, remnants for example, from a historical site.
·   اثار  :   impressions left by footsteps.
Allah SWT says in Surah Kahf (18:64):   قَالَذَلِكَمَاكُنَّانَبْغِفَارْتَدَّاعَلَىءَاثَارِهِمَاقَصَصًا  “Musa AS said (to his companion Yusha AS): "That is what we have been seeking.'' So they went back retracing their   footsteps  .”
Summary:
1.   قَدَم  :   distance between two feet, famous body parts or limbs and to step forward, to walk
2.   خُطُوَة  :   distance between the two feet
3.   اَثَر  :   impression of a footstep or foot

title: content/q/q8.html
raw_text:
Qarar Pakarna (to hold firmly, to settle)
1.   قَرَّ   (Qar’ra):  to stay, stagnant, motionless or still and to be cold. The connection between the two is that there is a loss of energy or motion when something gets cold while movement requires energy or heat.
Allah SWT said in Surah Al-Ahzaab (33:33):   وَقَرْنَفِىبُيُوتِكُنَّوَلاَتَبَرَّجْنَتَبَرُّجَالْجَـهِلِيَّةِالاٍّولَى   “And   stay   in your houses, and do not display yourselves like (women used to in) the times of ignorance.”
2.   اِسْتَويعَلي   (Istawa Ala):   to ride on an animal or vehicle and plant oneself firmly and confidently. The difference between   قَرَّ   and   اِسْتَويعَلي   is that later is used to indicate stillness when thing transforms from one state to another.
Allah SWT says in Surah Hud (11:44):   وَاسْتَوَتْعَلَىالْجُودِىِّ   “And the water was made to subside and the decree was fulfilled. And it (the boat of Noah AS which was sailing on the water)   rested   on (Mount) Judi.”
And then again in Surah Al-Muminoon (23:28):   فَإِذَااسْتَوَيْتَأَنتَوَمَنمَّعَكَعَلَىالْفُلْكِ   “(Noah AS) And when you have   embarked   on the ship, you and whoever is with you.”
Similarly He said in Surah Al-Araf (7:54):   ثُمَّاسْتَوَىٰعَلَىالْعَرْشِ   “then He   settled   (rose over) on the Throne.”
Summary:
1.   قَرَّ  :   To be motionlessness in the first state
2.   اِسْتَويعَلي  :   to be motionless or firm in the second state after transformation from the first.

raw_text:
9- QURAN KE MUKHTALIF NAAM [Different Names of Quran]
The words are used like QURAN (قران ), FURQAN (فرقان), ZIKR (ذكر), TAZKIRA (تذكرة), KITABUN-MUBIN (كتاب مبين) and HADEES (حديث ) which describe its different aspects.
9.1     QURAN (قران ):   QARA (قر) means from read to exaggerate means repeatedly, frequently and the book that is always recited. Allah says:
Surat Qāf (The Letter "Qaf") - سورة ق     50:1
قۗ ڗوَالْقُرْاٰنِ الْمَجِيْدِ
Qaf. By the honored Qur'an.
9.2     FURQAN (فرقان):   FARAQA (فرق) means to separate, to disjoint from exaggerate means such book which distinguishes and discriminates between each and every aspect of right and wrong. Allah says:
Surat Al-Furqān (The Criterian) - سورة الفرقان     25:1
تَبٰرَكَ الَّذِيْ نَزَّلَ الْفُرْقَانَ عَلٰي عَبْدِهٖ
Blessed is He who sent down the Criterion upon His Servant.
9.3     ZIKR (ذكر) and TAZKIRA (تذكرة):   The antonym of ZIKR (ذكر) is NASSIA (نسي). ZAKAR (ذكر) means to remember and to be remembered which is opposite of forgetting.
Page-679
And Quran is called ZIKR (ذكر) for the reason that it recalls the natural offering of mans goodness also of AHED-E-ALSAT (عہد الست). Hence it is also an advice. And similarly the meaning of TAZKIRA (تذكرة) is also advice and remembering as well. And the ticket of some ride such as rail, airplane  is called TAZKIRA (تذكرة) and also to certificate and passport. Allah says:
Surat Şād (The Letter "Saad") - سورة ص     38:8
ءَاُنْزِلَ عَلَيْهِ الذِّكْرُ مِنْۢ بَيْنِنَا
Has the message been revealed to him out of [all of] us? And said:
Surat Al-Muzzammil (The Enshrouded One) - سورة المزمل     73:19
اِنَّ هٰذِهٖ تَذْكِرَةٌ
Indeed, this is a reminder.
9.4     KITABUN-MUBIN (كتاب مبين):   BANA (بان) means to get away or to separate. Three things are found in BRAIN (بين)  (1) IFTRAAQ (افتراق), (2) BUAD (بعد), (3) WUJUU (وضو ح) and BAYANA (بين) means to openly describe something. And KITABUN-MUBIN (كتاب مبين) means such book in which everything about the guidance is explained with complete explanation and interpretation. Clear and shinning book i.e. QURAN-KAREEM.  Allah says:
Surat Al-Mā'idah (The Table Spread) - سورة المائدة     5:15
قَدْ جَاۗءَكُمْ مِّنَ اللّٰهِ نُوْرٌ وَّكِتٰبٌ مُّبِيْنٌ
There has come to you from Allah a light and a clear Book.
9.5     HADEES (حديث ):   The antonym of HADAS (حدث) is ADAM (عدم). And HADASA (حدث) means the emergence of a new thing. And HADEES (حديث) means everything that was not before and emerges entirely new. New thing. Like said:
Surat Aţ-Ţalāq (The Divorce) - سورة الطلاق     65:1
لَعَلَّ اللّٰهَ يُحْدِثُ بَعْدَ ذٰلِكَ اَمْرًا
Perhaps Allah will bring about after that a [different] matter.
And HADEES (حديث) also applies to everything that was present before but have been erased from peoples mind due to the passing of time. if it becomes alive again then HADEES (حديث) will also be applicable on it. New thing. Quran is called HADEES (حديث) in the same sense. Allah says:
Surat Az-Zumar (The Troops) - سورة الزمر     39:23
اَللّٰهُ نَزَّلَ اَحْسَنَ الْحَدِيْثِ
Allah has sent down the best statement.

Page-533
1- RAAT [Night]
Qur’an has referred them by the words     LAIL (ليل ) and BAYAAT (بيات ).
1.1         LAIL  (لیل ):     night “opposite of Day” is a known word. The time from sunset till sunrise. And in Qur’an, there are many occasions where LAIL AND NIHAAR (ليل و نهار ) are used together. The night is divided into 12 times or 12 hours. These names of these times are written in order as: SHAFAQ (شفق ) GHASAK (غسق ) DUQA (دقة ) FAHMA (فحمة ) ZULFA (زلفة ) ZALUQA (زلقة ) BEHRA (بحرة ) SAHER (سحر ) FAJAR (فجر ) SUBAH (صبح ) SABAH (صباح ).
1.2         BAYATUN  (بیاتا ):     BAAT(بات )  means to spend night, spending of night-time.  It is in Qur’an
Surat Al-Furqān (The Criterian) -     سورة الفرقان     25:64
فوَالَّذِيْنَ يَبِيْتُوْنَ لِرَبِّهِمْ سُجَّدًا وَّقِيَامًا
And those who spend [part of] the night to their Lord prostrating and standing [in prayer].
And     BAYATUN  (بیاتا )     means any time during the night, when sleeping, when dreaming. It is in Qur’an
Surat Yūnus (Jonah) -     سورة يونس   10:50

1- RAAT [Night]

 

Qur’an has referred them by the words LAIL (ليل ) and BAYAAT (بيات ).

 

 

1.1   LAIL  (لیل ): night “opposite of Day” is a known word. The time from sunset till sunrise. And in Qur’an, there are many occasions where LAIL AND NIHAAR (ليل و نهار ) are used together. The night is divided into 12 times or 12 hours. These names of these times are written in order as: SHAFAQ (شفق ) GHASAK (غسق ) DUQA (دقة ) FAHMA (فحمة ) ZULFA (زلفة ) ZALUQA (زلقة ) BEHRA (بحرة ) SAHER (سحر ) FAJAR (فجر ) SUBAH (صبح ) SABAH (صباح ).

1.2   BAYATUN  (بیاتا ): BAAT(بات )  means to spend night, spending of night-time.  It is in Qur’an

10 – Relatives
The words اَقرَبُونَ, نَسَبَ. صِهر, الاَرحَام اُولُو and اِلّ have been used in the holy Quran
10.1 AQRABUN (اَقرَبُونَ): قَرُبَ means to be near, to be close; this word can be used with reference to time, distance, status, relations and in any other context.  اَقرَبَ refers to being more close, more near.  The words اَقرَبُونَ, اَقرَبِين, ذَاقُربىٰ and القُربىٰ ذَوِي are used especially in the context of close relatives.  Close relatives are those for whom Allah has fixed a share in inheritance, such as children, parents, spouses and siblings.
Surat An-Nisā' (The Women) - النساء سورة
4:7
لِّلرِّجَالِ نَصِيبٌ۬ مِّمَّا تَرَكَ ٱلۡوَٲلِدَانِ وَٱلۡأَقۡرَبُونَ (﻿٧﻿)
For men is a share of what the parents and close relatives leave (7)
10.2 NASAB (نَسَب):  يَنسُبُ نَسَبَ means to relate lineage or to get information about it.  اِستَنسَبَ is to relate lineage, to inquire about it.  نَسَب and اِنسَاب are in the meaning of relationship, relatedness. نَسَب can be used to refer only to relatives from the father’s side because of patrilineal descent rules.  According to Imam Ragib, نَسَب can be refer to any one side of a person’s relatives, for example, either the mother’s side (including maternal grandparents, aunts and uncles) or the father’s side (including paternal grandparents, aunts and uncles).
Surat Al-Mu'minūn (The Believers) - المؤمنون سورة
23:101
فَإِذَا نُفِخَ فِى ٱلصُّورِ فَلَآ أَنسَابَ بَيۡنَهُمۡ يَوۡمَٮِٕذٍ۬ َ (﻿١٠١﻿)
So when the Horn is blown, no relationship will there be among them that Day (101)
10.3 SIHR (صِهر): refers to in-laws or relatedness which arises because of marriage.  For the wife, the lineal relatives of the husband and for the husband the lineal relatives of the wife are in-laws.
Surat Al-Furqān (The Criterian) - الفرقان سورة
25:54
وَهُوَ ٱلَّذِى خَلَقَ مِنَ ٱلۡمَآءِ بَشَرً۬ا فَجَعَلَهُ ۥ نَسَبً۬ا وَصِهۡرً۬ا‌ (﻿٥٤﻿)
And it is He who has created from water a human being and made him [a relative by] lineage and marriage (54)
10.4 ULUL ARHAAM (الاَرحَام اُولُو): literally it means relatives because of the womb; this encompasses all of the blood relatives from both the mother and father’s side.
Surat Al-'Anfāl (The Spoils of War) - الأنفال سورة
8:75
وَأُوْلُواْ ٱلۡأَرۡحَامِ بَعۡضُہُمۡ أَوۡلَىٰ بِبَعۡضٍ۬ فِى كِتَـٰبِ ٱللَّهِ  (﻿٧٥﻿)
But those of [blood] relationship are more entitled [to inheritance] in the decree of Allah (75)
10.5 ILLA (اِلّ): often translated as nearness or relatedness but linguistically it refers to promises or contracts made to relatives.  اِلّ refers to an oath.  The phrase الرَّجُل اِلَّ means جَارَبِهِ - ‘he became his neighbor.
Surat At-Tawbah (The Repentance) - التوبة سورة
9:10
لَا يَرۡقُبُونَ فِى مُؤۡمِنٍ إِلاًّ۬ وَلَا ذِمَّةً۬‌ (﻿١٠﻿)
They do not observe toward a believer any pact of kinship or covenant of protection (10)
Summary:
1.          اَقرَبُونَ: close relatives which have a share in inheritance
2.          نَسَب: relatives from the father’s side
3.          صِهر: in-laws
4.          الاَرحَام : relatives related to the womb, encompasses most relatives
5.          اِلّ: contracts made to relatives or neighbors

11 – Approval; Satisfaction
The words رِضوَان, مَرضَاة and وَجه have been used in the holy Quran
11.1 RIDWAAN (رِضوَان); MARDAAH ( مَرضَاة):  رَضِيَ is commonly used for happiness or pleasure, from it the words رِضوَان, رَضوَان and  مَرضَاة are derived.  These terms are infinitive nouns used in the meaning of approval, satisfaction and liking.
Surat Al-Mā'idah (The Table Spread) - المائدة سورة
5:2
يَبۡتَغُونَ فَضۡلاً۬ مِّن رَّبِّہِمۡ وَرِضۡوَٲنً۬ا‌ۚ (﻿٢﻿)
[violate the safety of] those coming to the Sacred House seeking bounty from their Lord and [His] approval (2)
And in another place the Almighty says:
Surat At-Taĥrīm (The Prohibtiion) - التحريم سورة
66:1
يَـٰٓأَيُّہَا ٱلنَّبِىُّ لِمَ تُحَرِّمُ مَآ أَحَلَّ ٱللَّهُ لَكَ‌ۖ تَبۡتَغِى مَرۡضَاتَ أَزۡوَٲجِكَ‌ۚ (﻿١﻿)
O Prophet, why do you prohibit [yourself from] what Allah has made lawful for you, seeking the approval of your wives? (1)
11.2 WAJH (وَجه):  literally the face/countenance, direction or front side or the side that comes first, used for approval.  The phrase النَّهَار وَجهُ refers to the first part of the day.  Turning the face away from another is a sign of disapproval while turning one’s face towards another is a sign of satisfaction and attentiveness.  To seek approval is to seek ‘the face’; this can be done by doing what leads to satisfaction and avoiding what leads to dissatisfaction.
Surat Al-Baqarah (The Cow) - البقرة سورة
2: 272
وَمَا تُنفِقُونَ إِلَّا ٱبۡتِغَآءَ وَجۡهِ ٱللَّهِ‌ۚ (﻿٢٧٢﻿)
And you do not spend except seeking the countenance of Allah (272)
Summary:
رِضوَان and مَرضَاة are used only for approval while وَجه also includes attention along with approval.

title: content/r/r12.html
raw_text:
12 – To Incline
The words رَغِبَ and تَنَافَسَ have been used in the holy Quran
12.1 RAGIBA (رَغِبَ): to incline/slant or to be inclined; to have the desire to attain something in one’s heart and to endeavor to attain it.
Surat Ash-Sharĥ (The Relief) - الشرح سورة
94:7-8
فَإِذَا فَرَغۡتَ فَٱنصَبۡ (﻿٧﻿) وَإِلَىٰ رَبِّكَ فَٱرۡغَب (﻿٨﻿)
So when you have finished [your duties], then stand up [for worship] (7).  And to your Lord direct [your] longing (8).
12.2 TANAFUS (تَنَافَسَ): نَفِسَ means to envy while نَفَّسَ means to recommend something.  تنافس means to be proud mutually, to incline in competition.  To compete with esteem in inclining towards virtuous deeds.
Surat Al-Muţaffifīn (The Defrauding) - المطففين سورة
83: 25-6
يُسۡقَوۡنَ مِن رَّحِيقٍ۬ مَّخۡتُومٍ (﻿٢٥﻿) خِتَـٰمُهُ ۥ مِسۡكٌ۬‌ۚ وَفِى ذَٲلِكَ فَلۡيَتَنَافَسِ ٱلۡمُتَنَـٰفِسُونَ (﻿٢٦﻿)
They will be given to drink [pure] wine [which was] sealed (25).  The last of it is musk. So for this let the competitors compete (26).
Summary:
رَغِبَ is commonly used for inclination/desire while تَنَافَسَ is used for competing in going towards virtuous deeds because of desire for them.

title: content/r/r13.html
raw_text:
13 – To Place, Put
The words وَضَعَ and القىٰ have been used in the holy Quran
13.1 WADA’A (وَضَعَ):  its opposite is رَفَعَ – to pick up or raise up.  Means to carefully put something down.   رفيع is the opposite of وضيع which refers to a person who has no place in society.  حمل وضع refers to unload a burden, whether apparent or hidden.
Surat Ash-Sharĥ (The Relief) - الشرح سورة
94:2-3
وَوَضَعۡنَا عَنكَ وِزۡرَكَ (﻿٢﻿) ٱلَّذِىٓ أَنقَضَ ظَهۡرَكَ (﻿٣﻿)
And We removed from you your burden (2). Which had weighed upon your back (3).
13: 2 ALQAA (القىٰ): means to put something, in the meaning of carefully and slowly placing something; does not include throwing.  Also includes the notion of placing something which is visible for others to see.
Surat An-Naĥl (The Bee) - النحل سورة
16:15
وَأَلۡقَىٰ فِى ٱلۡأَرۡضِ رَوَٲسِىَ (﻿١٥﻿)
And He has cast into the earth firmly set mountains (15)
Summary:
1.          وَضَعَ: to place something whether visible or not
2.          القىٰ: to place something that is visible to others

for light following words are used :
انار (light) , اضاء (lighting), نار (flame , light), جلى ,تجلى (glorification) , وهج (flame, blaze , heat , glare ) اشرق (sunrise, rdiate ,shine) اسفر (brighten, uncover) ,ابصر(sight, vision, eyes)
1  انار   :   نور   in sense of light which irradiate the things ,diffusing light which help in seeing things .
نور     light is used in both corporeal and incorporeal meanings
as Allah says in quran (sorah az-zummar # 22)
what is he whose heart Allah has open for islam so that he is in light from his lord.
(in this verse noor means both righteous path and enlightened heart)

16. ROZA DAAR [one who observes a fast]
Synonyms: SAA’IM, SAA-IH
16.1 SAA’IM (صَاٰئم):   SAWM (صَوْم) (plural SIYAAM صیام) means fasting and SAAMA (صَامَ) means to fast. To abstain from eating and some other activities from saahr (before dawn) to aftaar (dusk). And SAA’IM (صَاٰئم) means the one who fasts. In the Quran
Suran Al-Ahzaab (The clans): سورۃ الأحزَاب 33:35
وَٱلصَّـٰٓٮِٕمِينَ وَٱلصَّـٰٓٮِٕمَـٰتِ
Fasting men and fasting women
16.2 SAA’IH (سَائِح):   SAYH (سیح) ASAAHATA (السّاحَۃ) means an open place or a patio. And SAHA (سَاحَ) means to make a trip for pleasure, to undertake a journey or move across an open area.
SAHA (سَاحَ) also means to fast and to abide by all its rules and restrictions like abstention from not only eating, drinking but also refraining your eyes, ears and tongue from transgressing. It also means a person who stays in a Mosque during his fast.   (dictionary Al   Manjad  ). In the Holy Quran:
Surah Al Tawbah (The repentance): سورۃ التوبھ 9:112
ٱلتَّـٰٓٮِٕبُونَ ٱلۡعَـٰبِدُونَ ٱلۡحَـٰمِدُونَ ٱلسَّـٰٓٮِٕحُونَ
(Triumphant) are those who turn repentant (to Allah), those who serve (Him), those who praise (Him), those who fast
Summary:
16.1 SAA’IM referring to anyone observing fast.
16.2 SAA-IH who observes fast and also abides by other restrictions.

WORDS صايم سايح  are used for fasting

FASTING means frommorning prayer to evening prayer according to legality of islamic law avoiding eating drinking and some other things
and  صايم means one who fast
in quran (sorah ahzab # 33)
and the fasting men and the fasting women
2  سايح  : سيح الساحة in terms of wide spacious place  ,or patio ,lanai ,courtyard of house place  and ساح means strolling ,recruitting , moving in open place , far fetched journey , long distance trip
ساح means fasting and following all the bindingness an obligations  of fast not only refraining from food but also self restain of eyes ,ears ,tongue from ill doings
according to scholors سايح means some one who stay inside the mosque while fasting
ALQURAN (SORAH TOBA # 113)
they who turn of allah , who serve him who praise him  who fast
OUT TURN :
سايح  WHO FAST AND FOLLOW ALL THE OBLIGATIONS AND BINDINGMESS OF FAST  ALONG WITH REFRAAINING FROM FOOD
صايم  : IS USE FOR EVERY ONE WHO FAST

17 ROKNA [to stop, to forbid]
Synonyms: MANA, NAHA, AWWAQA, ADAL, AMSAKA, SADDA, AHSARA, HADARA, AKAFA, SABBATA, KAFFA, ZAADA, WAZ’A, HABASA, HAJARA
17.1 MANA’A (مَنَعَ): basically has two meanings,
1. To be ungenerous (and withhold) (opposite of ATTA’ عطا ). MANNAA’ (مَنَّاع) means a miser.
2. To forbid someone (either verbally or physically) to do something. Become a hindrance in some work. To deprive of. or to stop (dictionary Al   Manjad  ) .In the Quran:
Surah Al-Baqarah (The cow): سورۃ البَقَرَۃ 2:114
وَمَنۡ أَظۡلَمُ مِمَّن مَّنَعَ مَسَـٰجِدَ ٱللَّهِ أَن يُذۡكَرَ فِيہَا ٱسۡمُهُ
Who is more unjust than him who forbids the remembrance of God’s name in places of worship
Page – 550
17.2 NAHA (نَھٰی):   mostly means to restrain from doing sinful activities. Allahﷻ says in the Quran
Surah An-Nazi'at (Those who drag forth): سورۃ النَّازعَات 79:40

18 RUKNA [to refrain, to abstain]
Synonyms: INTAHA, AKDA, ISHMAZZA, QALA’
18.1 INTAHA (اِنْتَھٰی):   abstain or refrain. To refrain from sinful activities and dispose of them. In the Quran
Surah Al-Maeda (The table spread): سورۃ المَائدہ 5:91
وَيَصُدَّكُمۡ عَن ذِكۡرِ ٱللَّهِ وَعَنِ ٱلصَّلَوٰةِ*ۖ فَهَلۡ أَنتُم مُّنتَہُونَ
and hinder you from the remembrance of Allah, and from prayer: will you not then abstain?
18.2 AKDA (اَکْدٰی):   ALKUDIAH (اَلْکُدْیَھ) means hardened and solid ground or mountain. HAFARA FA-AKDA ( حَفَرَفَاَکْدٰی) means he dug till he reached hardened ground. KADDA is to question or ask forgiveness SA-ALAHU-FA-AKDA (سََاَلَہُ فَاَکْدٰی) means on his inquiry he found him to be a stiff (rigid) person and thus gave him nothing. In other words - after spending a little, he then held back. Allah says in the Quran:
Surah An-Najm (the star): سورۃ النَّجم 53:34
وَأَعۡطَىٰ قَلِيلاً۬ وَأَكۡدَىٰٓ
And gave a little, and held back?
Page 553
18.3 ISHMAAZA (اِشْمَاَزّ):   SHAMAAZA(شَمَاَزَ) means to despise something that is condemned and ISHAMAAZA (اِشْمَاَزّ) means mournful and distressed, resentment (dictionary Al   Manjad  ). In the Quran
Surah Az-Zumar (The groups): سورۃ الزُّمَر 39:45
وَإِذَا ذُكِرَ ٱللَّهُ وَحۡدَهُ ٱشۡمَأَزَّتۡ قُلُوبُ ٱلَّذِينَ لَا يُؤۡمِنُونَ بِٱلۡأَخِرَةِ*ۖ
When God alone is mentioned, the hearts of those who do not believe in the Hereafter shrink with resentment. But when those other than Him are mentioned, they become filled with joy.
18.4 QALA’ (قَلَعَ):   means to give up something and refrain from something (dictionary Al   Manjad  ). To refrain from something that is in progress, right away. Allah says in Quran
Surah Hud (Hud): سورۃ ھود 11:44
وَقِيلَ يَـٰٓأَرۡضُ ٱبۡلَعِى مَآءَكِ وَيَـٰسَمَآءُ أَقۡلِعِى وَغِيضَ ٱلۡمَآءُ
And it was said, “O earth, swallow your waters,” and “O heaven, clear up.” And the waters receded
Summary:
18.1 INTAHA: refrain from sinful activities.
18.2 AKDA: to refrain from spending.
18.3 ISHMAAZA: refrain from something due to loss of interest.
18.4 QALA’: refrain from something straight away, which is in progress

19 RONDNA [to trample]
Synonyms: HATAMA, WATA’A
19.1 HATAMA (حَطَمَ):   means to break or twist. HATOOM (حَطْوْم) refers to a very strong wind that can destroy everything in its path. HUTAAM (حُطَام) means a broken or battered thing (dictionary Al   Manjad  ). The word is used to refer to break or batter a thing into pieces. To crush, to trample or to grind. In the Quran
Surah An-Naml (The ant): سورۃ النَّمل 27:18
قَالَتۡ نَمۡلَةٌ۬ يَـٰٓأَيُّهَا ٱلنَّمۡلُ ٱدۡخُلُواْ مَسَـٰكِنَڪُمۡ لَا يَحۡطِمَنَّكُمۡ سُلَيۡمَـٰنُ وَجُنُودُهُ ۥ وَهُمۡ لَا يَشۡعُرُونَ
An ant said, “O ants! Go into your nests, lest Solomon and his troops crush you without noticing.”
19.2 WATA-A (وَطَاَ):
1. To wear out something, or to crush under ones’ feet. The word WATI (وطی) also means to meet or get intimate, but in the Quran this word is not used with this meaning. In the Quran
Surah Al-Fath (The victory): سورۃ الفَتْح 48:25
وَلَوۡلَا رِجَالٌ۬ مُّؤۡمِنُونَ وَنِسَآءٌ۬ مُّؤۡمِنَـٰتٌ۬ لَّمۡ تَعۡلَمُوهُمۡ أَن تَطَـُٔوهُمۡ فَتُصِيبَكُم مِّنۡهُم مَّعَرَّةُۢ بِغَيۡرِ عِلۡمٍ۬*ۖ
Had there not been believing men and believing women whom you did not know that you were trampling down and on whose account a crime would have accrued to you without (your) knowledge,
2. To endure extreme hardship, extreme pain (dictionary Al   Manjad  ). In the Quran
Surah Al-Muzammil (The enshrouded one): سورۃ المُزمّل 73:6
إِنَّ نَاشِئَةَ ٱلَّيۡلِ هِىَ أَشَدُّ وَطۡـًٔ۬ا وَأَقۡوَمُ قِيلاً
Truly the rising by night is most potent for governing (the soul), and most suitable for (framing) the Word (of Prayer and Praise).
Summary:
19.1 HATAMA: To crush, to trample or to grind.
19.2 WATA-A: Wear out something, or to crush under ones’ feet.

2- RAAT KE KAAM [Night Work]
Qur’an has referred them by the words BAAT (بات ) BAYATA (بيت ) ASRAA (أسرى ) TARAQA (طرق ) NAQASHA (نفش ) AND TAHAJADA (تھجدا).
2.1      BAAT   (بات ):     means to spend night, to spend night time and the place where the night is spend: that is BAYATA (بيت ) or Home. Allah says
Surat Al-Furqān (The Criterian) -     سورة الفرقان     25:64
فوَالَّذِيْنَ يَبِيْتُوْنَ لِرَبِّهِمْ سُجَّدًا وَّقِيَامًا
And those who spend [part of] the night to their Lord prostrating and standing [in prayer].
2.2         BAYAT  (بيت):     After a portion of night is gone, to unite at home for mutual consultation about some matter. It is in Qur’an
Surat An-Nisā' (The Women) -     سورة النساء     4:108
اِذْ يُبَيِّتُوْنَ مَا لَا يَرْضٰى مِنَ الْقَوْلِ
When they spend the night in such as He does not accept of speech.
Page-534
And to suddenly attack the enemy at night time. To attack at night time without alerting. Allah says:
Surat An-Naml (The Ant) -     سورة النمل     27:49
قَالُوْا تَقَاسَمُوْا بِاللّٰهِ لَـنُبَيِّتَـنَّهٗ وَاَهْلَهٗ ثُمَّ لَـنَقُوْلَنَّ لِوَلِيِّهٖ مَا شَهِدْنَا مَهْلِكَ اَهْلِهٖ
They said, "Take a mutual oath by Allah that we will kill him by night, he and his family. Then we will say to his executor, 'We did not witness the destruction of his family.
2.3         ASRA   (أسرى ):     to give a ride at night time. Take out. It is in Qur’an:
(Surat-BaniIsrael) (Bani Israel)     سورة بنی اسراءیل 17:1
سُبْحٰنَ الَّذِيْٓ اَسْرٰى بِعَبْدِهٖ لَيْلًا مِّنَ الْمَسْجِدِ الْحَرَامِ اِلَى الْمَسْجِدِ الْاَقْصَا
Exalted is He who took His Servant by night from al-Masjid al-Haram to al-Masjid al- Aqsa.
2.4         TARAQA  (طرق ):     TAREEQ (طريق ) means path and TAARIQ (طارق ) means traveller on the path. But in general terms, it denotes that traveller who comes at night. And star is called as TARAQ (طارق ) because it appears at night. Allah says
Surat Aţ-Ţāriq (The Nightcommer) -     سورة الطارق     86:1
وَالسَّمَاۗءِ وَالطَّارِقِ
By the sky and the night comer.
In this verse, Tariq may represent stars and the guest who comes at night as well.
2.5         NAFASHA  (نفش ):     NAFSHU NAAM (نفش الغنم ) means the scattering of goats at night time for grazing without shepherd. And ANNAFSH (النفش) denotes those goats who have been dispersed at night time to graze without shepherd. Allah says
Surat Al-'Anbyā' (The Prophets)   -   سورة الأنبياء     21:78
وَدَاوٗدَ وَسُلَيْمٰنَ اِذْ يَحْكُمٰنِ فِي الْحَرْثِ اِذْ نَفَشَتْ فِيْهِ غَنَمُ الْقَوْمِ
And [mention] David and Solomon, when they judged concerning the field - when the sheep of a people overran it [at night].
2.6         TAHAJADA  ( تهجد ):     HAJADA (ھجد) means to sleep and wakeup at night time and HAJADA TAHAJADA  ( تهجد ھجد) means to make sleep and wakeup as well. To wake up from sleep. To sleep at night. To offer prayer after waking up at night. Allah says
(Surat-BaniIsrael) (Bani Israel)     سورة بنی اسراءیل     17:79
وَمِنَ الَّيْلِ فَتَهَجَّدْ بِهٖ نَافِلَةً لَّكَ
And from [part of] the night, pray with it as additional [worship] for you.

20 RONAQ (dazzle, lustrous)
Synonym: ZAHRAH, NADRAH, BAHJAH
20.1 ZAHRAH (زَھْرَۃ):   lustrous glistening or something in tip-top shape. And ZAHRA-TUD-DUNIYA (زَھْرَۃُ الدُنْیَا) means worldly radiance (dictionary Al   Manjad  ). Word is commonly used to denote splendour and fancies of the ephemeral world. Allah says in Quran
Surah Ta-Ha (Ta-ha): سورۃ طٰھٰ 20:131
وَلَا تَمُدَّنَّ عَيۡنَيۡكَ إِلَىٰ مَا مَتَّعۡنَا بِهِۦۤ أَزۡوَٲجً۬ا مِّنۡہُمۡ زَهۡرَةَ ٱلۡحَيَوٰةِ ٱلدُّنۡيَا
And do not extend your glance towards what We have given some classes of them to enjoy—the splendour of the life of this world
20.2 NADRAH (نَضْرَۃً):   means facial radiance, freshness, vivaciousness and beauty (dictionary Al   Manjad  ). It can be used both for face or plant, but in Quran where ever the word is used, its refers to facial radiance. Allah says in Quran
Surah Al-Qiyammah (the resurrection): سورۃ القِیَِامَھ75:22
ٌ وُجُوهٌ۬ يَوۡمَٮِٕذٍ۬ نَّاضِرَة إِلَىٰ رَبِّہَا نَاظِرَةٌ۬
Faces on that Day will be radiant. Looking towards their Lord.
20.3 BAHJAH (  بَھْجَھ):   something that is pleasing and delightful. According to Khalil it refers to freshness and radiance of something. It can be used for humans but mostly it is used to portray the spring season and freshness of plants. In the Quran
Surah An-Naml (The ant): سورۃ النَّمل 27:60
وَأَنزَلَ لَڪُم مِّنَ ٱلسَّمَآءِ مَآءً۬ فَأَنۢبَتۡنَا بِهِۦ حَدَآٮِٕقَ ذَاتَ بَهۡجَةٍ۬
Or, who created the heavens and the earth, and rains down water from the sky for you? With it we produce gardens full of beauty,
Summary:
20.1 ZAHRAH: beauty and fancies of the ephemeral world and plant radiance.
20.2 NADRAH: facial radiance.
20.3 BAHJAH: freshness of plants.
*REHNA see AABAD HONA, TEHERNA

raw_text:
21 RAIT [sand]
Synonyms: SARAAB, KATHEEB, AHQAAF, by Arabic dictionary the word used is RAML but this word is not used in Quran
21.1 SARAAB (سَرَاب):   Every beverage is known as SHARAAB (شراب). Anything that seems like potable but is actually not a beverage is known as SARAAB (سَرَاب). Figuratively this word is used to describe anything that does not exist and is mostly used to describe a mirage (i.e. when the heat and light of sun makes sand appear like water to a distant observer). In the Quran
Surah Al-Noor (The light): سورۃ النور 24:39
كَسَرَابِۭ بِقِيعَةٍ۬ يَحۡسَبُهُ ٱلظَّمۡـَٔانُ مَآءً
their works are like a mirage in a desert. The thirsty assumes it is to be water.
21.2 KATHEEB (کَثِیِْب):   means a sand dune. Allah says in Quran
Surah Al-Muzammil (The enshrouded one): سورۃ المُزمّل 73:14
كَانَتِ ٱلۡجِبَالُ كَثِيبً۬ا مَّهِيلاً
On the Day when the earth and the mountains tremble, and the mountains become heaps of sand.
21.3 AHQAAF (اَحْقَاف):   (singular HAQF (حقف) which means a field of sand dunes) AHQAAF(اَحْقَاف) means a wide terrain consisting of thousands of sand dunes (  Manjad  ). According to Ruba-e-Maskoon it refers to an area in Yemen that was the centre of the people of ‘Aad. In the Quran
Surah Al-Ahqaaf (The Dunes): سورۃ الاَحْقَاف 46:21
وَٱذۡكُرۡ أَخَا عَادٍ إِذۡ أَنذَرَ قَوۡمَهُ ۥ بِٱلۡأَحۡقَافِ
And mention the brother of Aad, as he warned his people at the dunes.
Summary:
21.1: SARAAB: a mirage i.e. field of sand appearing like water to a distant viewer.
21.2: KATHEEB: sand dune.
21.3: AHQAAF: wide terrain consisting of thousands of sand dunes.

raw_text:
3- RAH-RAASTA [Way Path]
Qur’an has referred them by the words     SIRAAT   (صراط )  TAREEQ   (طريق )  SABEEL (سبيل ) FAJH  (  فج ) IMAAM  (امام ) HUDA  (هدى ) NAJD  ( نجد ) AND SABAB   (سبب ).
Page-535
3.1         TAREEQ   (طريق ) :   This word is used for all types of paths. This word is also used in both physical and spiritual terms. A physical example is this.
Surat Ţāhā (Ta-Ha) - سورة طه      20:77
فَاضْرِبْ لَهُمْ طَرِيْقًا فِي الْبَحْرِ يَبَسًا
And strike for them a dry path through the sea.
And Spiritual example is this.
Surat An-Nisā' (The Women) -     سورة النساء 4:168:169
اِلَّا طَرِيْقَ جَهَنَّمَ وَلَا لِيَهْدِيَهُمْ طَرِيْقًا
Nor will He guide them to a path Except the path of Hell.
3.2         SIRAAT   (صراط ):     SIRAAT   (صراط ) is called as long and sharp sword and the path that will be made to cross the Jahanam, which is normally called as PULLSIRAAT (پلصراط) It is described with same attribute that it will be sharper than sword and thinner than hair. Hence SIRAAT   (صراط ) is the path that is to be passed with extreme care and around which are many dangers. The way of crossing this path with extreme care is named as TAQWA: This word of SIRAAT   (صراط ) is used in both physical and spiritual terms. Its concept in literal terms is generally the path of guidance. And according to Abu-Hilaal, SIRAAT   (صراط ) is called as an easy path. Allah says:
Surat Al-Fātiĥah (The Opener) - سورة الفاتحة     1:4
اِھْدِنَا الصِّرَاطَ الْمُسْتَـقِيْمَ
Guide us to the straight path.
And an example of its usage in physical terms is this:
Surat Al-'A`rāf (The Heights) -     سورة الأعراف     7:86
وَلَا تَقْعُدُوْا بِكُلِّ صِرَاطٍ تُوْعِدُوْنَ وَتَصُدُّوْنَ عَنْ سَبِيْلِ اللّٰهِ
And do not sit on every path, threatening and averting from the way of Allah those who believe in Him.
3.3         SABEEL (سبيل ):     Every path on which one can walk easily. IBNESABEEL (ابن اسبیل) means traveller and ABARISABEEL (عابری سبیل) means passer and SABEEL (سبيل ) means wide road. ASBALATAREEQ (اسبل اطریق) means the route that has great traffic and ASBALADAMAAWALMATR (اسبل ادمع و المطر) means continuous flow of tears or continuous rain shower. Hence SABEEL (سبيل ) is called as the path that has the most traffic. Allah says to honey bee:
Surat An-Naĥl (The Bee) -     سورة النحل     16:69
فَاسْلُكِيْ سُبُلَ رَبِّكِ ذُلُلًا
And follow the ways of your Lord laid down [for you].
Here Subul (سبل)     denotes that natural guidance which Allah has installed in everything. And on which one can move easily and all move equally. This word is also used in both physical and spiritual terms. The above example is the spiritual form and an example of physical form is this: Allah says:
Surat Al-Ĥijr (The Rocky Tract) -     سورة الحجر     15:76
وَاِنَّهَا لَبِسَبِيْلٍ مُّقِيْمٍ
And indeed, those cities are [situated] on an established road.
Page-536
Now see that Allah has used 3 words     TAREEQ   (طريق ) SABEEL (سبيل ) and SABEEL (سبيل )     in Qur’an for this “path of guidance”.     TAREEQ   (طريق ) is in the sense that TAREEQ   (طريق )     is a common word that is used for any route.     SIRAAT   (صراط ) is in the sense that it is encircled in the limits and restrictions of commands & prohibitions. And SABEEL (سبيل )     is in the sense that when a person starts walking on this path with determination then Shariat has taken account of all conveniences. And the number of people walking on it is also enough.
3.4         FAJH  (  فج ):     FAJATUN (فجة ) is the opening between two mountains and FAJWA (فجوة ) is the field between two mountains and FAJAH (فج ) is that open path who connects two mountains after passing through this field. It is in Qur’an:
Surat Al-Ĥaj (The Pilgrimage) -     سورة الحج     22:27
وَاَذِّنْ فِي النَّاسِ بِالْحَجِّ يَاْتُوْكَ رِجَالًا وَّعَلٰي كُلِّ ضَامِرٍ يَّاْتِيْنَ مِنْ كُلِّ فَجٍّ عَمِيْقٍ
And proclaim to the people the Hajj [pilgrimage]; they will come to you on foot and on every lean camel; they will come from every distant pass.
3.5         IMAAM  (امام ):     means leader and means highway, a wide and long road. It is in Qur’an
Surat Al-Ĥijr (The Rocky Tract) -     سورة الحجر     15:79
فَانْتَقَمْنَا مِنْهُمْ ۘ وَاِنَّهُمَا لَبِاِمَامٍ مُّبِيْنٍ
So We took retribution from them, and indeed, both [cities] are on a clear highway.
3.6         NAJD  ( نجد ):     means difficult pass and the path that climbs to the top altitude or comes down from the top. Allah says
Surat Al-Balad (The City) -     سورة البلد     90:10:11
فَلَا اقْتَحَمَ الْعَقَبَةَ وَهَدَيْنٰهُ النَّجْدَيْنِ
And have shown him the two ways But he has not broken through the difficult pass.
3.7         HUDA  (هدى ):     means Guidance and Path. If a forgotten or lost person finds the right path then it will be called Huda:  It is in Qur’an
Surat Ţāhā (Ta-Ha) - سورة طه     20:10
اِنِّىْٓ اٰنَسْتُ نَارًا لَّعَلِّيْٓ اٰتِيْكُمْ مِّنْهَا بِقَبَسٍ اَوْ اَجِدُ عَلَي  النَّارِ هُدًى
I have perceived a fire; perhaps I can bring you a torch or find at the fire some guidance.
3.8         SABAB   (سبب ):     means Source, rope, path. The path and the resources to pass it. Travel supplies  It is in Qur’an
Surat Al-Kahf     (The Cave) - سورة الكهف     18:89
ثُمَّ اَتْـبَـعَ سَبَبًا
Then he followed a way.
(Surat-Momin) (True Believer) -      سورة مومن     40:36
وَقَالَ فِرْعَوْنُ يٰهَامٰنُ ابْنِ لِيْ صَرْحًا لَّعَلِّيْٓ اَبْلُغُ الْاَسْبَابَ
And Pharaoh said, "O Haman, construct for me a tower that I might reach the ways.
Page-537
Summary:
3.1              TAREEQ:     Common word for path.
3.2              SIRAAT:      The path where one has to walk carefully.
3.3              SABEEL:     The path where one can walk easily and there is high traffic  .
3.4              FAJH:     Wide path between two mountains  .
3.5                IMAAM:     highway, wide road.
3.6              NAJD:     The path to climb and descend from a difficult pass  .
3.7              HUDAA:     If a lost forgotten person finds the right path.
3.8              SABAB:     Path with supplies and resources  .

  وَقَالَ فِرْعَوْنُ يٰهَامٰنُ ابْنِ لِيْ صَرْحًا لَّعَلِّيْٓ اَبْلُغُ الْاَسْبَابَ         

And Pharaoh said, "O Haman, construct for me a tower that I might reach the ways.

Page-537

 

Summary:

3.1          TAREEQ: Common word for path.

3.2          SIRAAT:  The path where one has to walk carefully.

3.3          SABEEL: The path where one can walk easily and there is high traffic.

3.4          FAJH: Wide path between two mountains.

3.5            IMAAM: highway, wide road.

3.6          NAJD: The path to climb and descend from a difficult pass.

3.7          HUDAA: If a lost forgotten person finds the right path.

3.8          SABAB: Path with supplies and resources.

4- RAAH DALNA RAAIJ KERNA [Put to Way, Put Into Practice]
Qur’an has referred them by the words     SANAH (سن ) SHARAA (شرع  ) AND IBTADAAA (ابتدع ).
4.1         SANAH  (سنة ):     San: means if something is issued or put in practice and if it runs properly. It is used as both essential and plural such as the prophet (P.B.U.H) says MUN SANAH SANATUN (من سن سنة ) anybody who puts a way into practice. it is used for both good and bad meanings and when it is related to Allah then it is called Divine Rule or Allah’s Practice. Allah says
Surat Fāţir (Originator) -     سورة فاطر     35:43
فَهَلْ يَنْظُرُوْنَ اِلَّا سُنَّتَ الْاَوَّلِيْنَ ۚ فَلَنْ تَجِدَ لِسُنَّتِ اللّٰهِ تَبْدِيْلًا
Then do they await except the way of the former peoples? But you will never find in the way of Allah any change.
4.2       SHARAA  (شرع ):     means clear and set path but it is only applied on Allah’s Commands. And SHARAALILQOME (شرع للقوم) means to make law for the nation and in Shariat, it means Islamic law, Divine commands, code. SHARAA (شرع  ) are in fact those laws that are changed by Allah according to the requirement of that period. For more information, refer to TAREEQA AUR DEEN (طريقة اور دين ) . Allah says:
(Surat-Shuraa) سورة الشورى   42:13
شَرَعَ لَكُمْ مِّنَ الدِّيْنِ مَا وَصّٰى بِهٖ نُوْحًا
He has ordained for you of religion what He enjoined upon Noah.
However according to dictionary, this word can be related to other than Allah or false gods: such as Allah says
Surat Ash-Shūraá (The Consultation) - سورة الشورى     42:21
اَمْ لَهُمْ شُرَكٰۗؤُا شَرَعُوْا لَهُمْ مِّنَ الدِّيْنِ مَا لَمْ يَاْذَنْۢ بِهِ اللّٰهُ
Or have they other deities who have ordained for them a religion to which Allah has not consented?
4.3         IBTADAA  (ابتدع ):     ILABADAA (الابداع) means invent something without following anyone. And BIDAAT (بدعت) is every that new tradition which is included in religion after considering it as of religion and there is no evidence of it in Shariat. And IBTADAAA (ابتدع ) means to include a new thing in Shariat and call it as a part of it. And prophet (P.B.U.H) said every BIDAAT (بدعت) no matter how good it may seemed is a sheer misguidance. Allah Says
Page-538
Surat Al-Ĥadīd (The Iron) -     سورة الحديد     57:27
وَرَهْبَانِيَّةَۨ ابْتَدَعُوْهَا مَا كَتَبْنٰهَا عَلَيْهِمْ
We did not prescribe it for them except [that they did so] seeking the approval of Allah.
Summary:
4.1              SANNA: is used to put every good and bad thing in practice. however, according to Sharia, Sanna: means only the actions and talks of messenger (P.B.U.H) of Allah.
4.2              SHARAA: The establishment of a clear and set path for the people by Allah via messenger. It was being changed from Adam (A.S) till Hazrat Muhammad (P.B.U.H) but now, this part of religion is also non-changeable because He was the last prophet of Allah and deen was completed on him.
4.3              IBTADAA:     To include a tradition or method in religion after considering it a part of Shariat and there is no evidence about it in Shariat.

raw_text:
5- RAAZI KERNA- RAAZI HONA [Make Please- Be Pleased]
Qur’an has referred them by the words     RAZIA (رضی ) TOOAA  (طوع ) AND AATABA  (اعتب ).
5.1         RAZIA (رضی   ): is a famous word means to be pleased with somebody, to be happy, likeness or to express it. Allah says
Surat Al-Mā'idah (The Table Spread) - سورة المائدة, Surat Al-Bayyinah (The Clear Proof) - سورة البينة      98,5:8:119
رَضِيَ اللّٰهُ عَنْهُمْ وَرَضُوْا عَنْهُ
Allah being pleased with them and they with Him.
5.2         TOOAA  (طوع ):     ATAAA (اطاع) means to follow the order with heartily happiness and TOOAA  (طوع ) means to agree your heart for an abominable job. Allah says:
Surat Al-Mā'idah (The Table Spread) - سورة المائدة     5:30
فَطَوَّعَتْ لَهٗ نَفْسُهٗ قَتْلَ اَخِيْهِ
And his soul permitted to him the murder of his brother.
5.3          AATABA  (اعتب ):     means to blame someone or to be annoyed. And AATABA  (اعتب ) means to dispel the cause of resentment. To placate the resented person. And ETAAB (عتاب) means to show resentment due to the loss of friendship and compassion relations. Allah says:
(Surat-Ham-m-Sajda) (H-m Sajda)     سورة حم السجدہ     41:24
وَاِنْ يَّسْـتَعْتِبُوْا فَمَا هُمْ مِّنَ الْمُعْتَـبِيْنَ
They will not be of those who are allowed to appease.
Summary:
5.1              RAZIA:     to be pleased with somebody, to be happy, a common word.
5.2              TOWAAA: to agree your heart for an abominable job.
5.3              AATABA:     To post complaints and grievances to placate the resented one.

Page-539
6- RUTBA- RUTBA PANA [Status-To Achieve Status]
Qur’an has referred them by the words DARAJA  (درجة ) ZULFA  (  زلفى ) QARABA  (قرب ) AND MAKANA (  مکن ).
6.1         DARAJA  (درجة ) :     means edge, superiority, status, rank. The antonym of DARAJ (درج) is DARAK (درك ) And both of these words are the two dimensions of one thing. If someone ascends to the ceiling above via stairs then the same stairs or sticks are called DARAJAAT (درجات ) and in terms of descending, the same stairs are called DARAKAAT (دركات ) for the same reason, the idiom of DARAJAAT-UL-JANNAH (درجات الجنة ) and DARAKAAT-UN-NAAR (دركات النار ) is used. And status means such an excellence or dominance which is from one terminal to the second. Allah says:
Surat Al-Baqarah (The Cow) -     سورة البقرة      2:228
وَلَهُنَّ مِثْلُ الَّذِيْ عَلَيْهِنَّ بِالْمَعْرُوْفِ ۠ وَلِلرِّجَالِ عَلَيْهِنَّ دَرَجَةٌ
And due to the wives is similar to what is expected of them, according to what is reasonable. But the men have a degree over them [in responsibility and authority].
6.2         ZULFA  (  زلفى ):     means value and attachment, and the proximity in status. Allah says:
Surat Şād (The Letter "Saad") -     سورة ص     38:40
وَاِنَّ لَهٗ عِنْدَنَا لَزُلْفٰى وَحُسْنَ مَاٰبٍ
And indeed, for him is nearness to Us and a good place of return.
But when this matter goes in Ifaal-e-baab, it gives the meaning of proximity in the distance. Allah says:
Surat Ash-Shu`arā' (The Poets) -     سورة الشعراء     26:64
وَاَزْلَفْنَا ثَمَّ الْاٰخَرِيْنَ
And We advanced thereto the pursuers.
6.3          QARABA  (قرب ):     QAROBA  (قرب ) means to get closer and the action which becomes source to get closer in status. And QURBAAN (قربان ) is that scarification by which one needs to achieve the status and rank.  Allah says:
Surat Al-Mā'idah (The Table Spread) - سورة المائدة 5:27
وَاتْلُ عَلَيْهِمْ نَبَاَ ابْنَيْ اٰدَمَ بِالْحَقِّ  ۘاِذْ قَرَّبَا قُرْبَانًا
And recite to them the story of Adam's two sons, in truth, when they both offered a sacrifice [to Allah ].
At another occasion:
Surat Al-Wāqi`ah (The Inevitable) -     سورة الواقعة   56:10,11
ڌاُولٰۗىِٕكَ الْمُقَرَّبُوْنَوَالسّٰبِقُوْنَ السّٰبِقُوْنَ
And the forerunners, the forerunners. Those are the ones brought near [to Allah ].
6.4          MAKANA (  مکن ):     means having a high-rise status. And MAKAAN (مكان ) means place, location, residence. A place that has a body. And MAKANA (  مکن ) means to endow power to someone, to grant government and MAKEEN (مكين ) means both i.e. one who lives in a house and person who has a status.  Allah says:

raw_text:
7- To Face
The words   اَقبَلَ   and   تَوَجَّهَ   have been used in the holy Quran
7.1 AQBALA (  اَقبَلَ  ): the phrase   المَكَان     قَبَلَ   means to face some place.    قَابَل   means to be face to face, to be opposite; for two things to be placed facing each other, opposing.    قَبَّل   means to give a kiss.    اَقبَل   means to turn towards something or someone who is in front of you.
Surat Al-Qalam (The Pen) -   القلم     سورة
68:30
فَأَقۡبَلَ بَعۡضُہُمۡ عَلَىٰ بَعۡضٍ۬ يَتَلَـٰوَمُونَ (﻿٣٠﻿)
Then they approached one another, blaming each other (30)
7.2 TAWAJJAH (  تَوَجَّهَ  ):   وَجه   means face or countenance.   وَجَّهَ   means to send towards someone and
تَوَجَّهَ     اِلَيهِ   refers to be attentive, to turn your face towards someone.
Surat Al-Qaşaş (The Stories) -   القصص     سورة
28:22
وَلَمَّا تَوَجَّهَ تِلۡقَآءَ مَدۡيَنَ (﻿٢٢﻿)
And when he directed himself toward Madyan (22)
Summary:
اَقبَل   is used when facing something directly in front while   تَوَجَّهَ   is used for when facing anything, whether something is directly in front of you or at a distance.

raw_text:
8 – Rubbish, Trash
The words نَكِدَ, خَمطَ, دَاحِضَة, نَاقص, بَخس, خَبِيث, اَدنىٰ and مَزجٰة have been used in the holy Quran
8.1 NAKIDA (نَكِدَ):   refers to something that lacks goodness or good qualities - الخير قليل.   According to Imam Ragib, it refers to anything that is attained by a seeker after great difficulty.  The phrase نكداء ناقة refers to a she-camel that gives very little milk and is also difficult to milk.  نَكِدَ means to prevent someone from attaining their needs, to deprive or to give less. الرجل نكد refers to a person who asks much and lacks goodness.  نَكِدَ is something which is attained after difficulty, is very little in quantity, and lacks goodness; something that is little and is rubbish.
Surat Al-'A`rāf (The Heights) -  الأعراف سورة
7:58
وَٱلَّذِى خَبُثَ لَا يَخۡرُجُ إِلَّا نَكِدً۬ا‌ۚ (﻿٥٨﻿)
But that which is bad - nothing emerges except sparsely, with difficulty (58)
8.2 KHAMTA (خَمطَ):   every sour or bitter thing; trees which bear little fruit; a tree which has long thorns.
Surat Saba' (Sheba) - سبإ سورة
34:16

And do not substitute the defective [of your own] for the good [of theirs] (2)

قَالَ أَتَسۡتَبۡدِلُونَ ٱلَّذِى هُوَ أَدۡنَىٰ بِٱلَّذِى هُوَ خَيۡرٌ‌ (﻿٦١﻿)
[Moses] said, "Would you exchange what is better for what is less? (61)

12:88
قَالُواْ يَـٰٓأَيُّہَا ٱلۡعَزِيزُ مَسَّنَا وَأَهۡلَنَا ٱلضُّرُّ وَجِئۡنَا بِبِضَـٰعَةٍ۬ مُّزۡجَٮٰةٍ۬ فَأَوۡفِ لَنَا ٱلۡكَيۡلَ (﻿٨٨﻿)
So when they entered upon Joseph, they said, "O 'Azeez, adversity has touched us and our family, and we have come with goods poor in quality, but give us full measure (88)
Summary:
1.          نَكِدَ: something that is little in quantity, is difficult to attain and is discarded
2.          خَمطَ: something bitter, repugnant and distasteful
3.          دَاحِضَة: futile, indecent and false
4.          نَاقص: incomplete and defective
5.          بَخس:  of poor quality and is junk
6.          خَبِيث: dirty, impure or something impermissible
7.          اَدنىٰ: something that is deficient in comparison to something else
8.          مَزجٰة:  something so rejected that no one is willing to accept it

9 – Rope
The words حَبل and سَبَب have been used in the holy book.
9.1 HABL (حَبل): [plural – حبال] means a rope or something that resembles it.  The phrase
الوريد حبل refers to the jugular vein.  الصيّاد حبالة refers to the rope used by a hunter.  This word is used commonly.
Surat Al-Masad (The Palm Fiber, Flame) - المسد سورة
111:5
فِى جِيدِهَا حَبۡلٌ۬ مِّن مَّسَدِۭ (﻿٥﻿)
Around her neck is a rope of [twisted] fiber (5)
9.2 SABAB (سَبَب): a rope which is used to climb a tree, a rope which is used in travel, as a travel essential or as a tool to tie travel luggage.
Surat Al-Ĥaj (The Pilgrimage) - الحج سورة
22:15
فَلۡيَمۡدُدۡ بِسَبَبٍ إِلَى ٱلسَّمَآءِ ثُمَّ لۡيَقۡطَعۡ فَلۡيَنظُرۡ هَلۡ يُذۡهِبَنَّ كَيۡدُهُ ۥ مَا يَغِيظُ (﻿١٥﻿)
Let him extend a rope to the ceiling, then cut off [his breath], and let him see: will his effort remove that which enrages [him]? (15)
Summary:
HABL (حَبل) is used for any kind of rope while SABAB (سَبَب) is used to describe a rope which is used for climbing or for a rope used in travel.

1.            Along with (saath):
Maa’a    مَعَ   & bee   بِ    are the words used.
The difference between both the words is that maa’a    مَعَ   is used for companionship & for rest of the cases, bee   بِ    is used. The example of maa’a   مَعَ    in Quran is :
12:13: Surah Yūsuf (Joseph) -   سورة يوسف
أَرْسِلْهُ مَعَنَا غَدًا يَرْتَعْ وَيَلْعَبْ وَإِنَّا لَهُ لَحَافِظُونَ
Send him with us tomorrow that he may eat well and play. And indeed, we will be his guardians  .
The example of bee   بِ    would be:
2:45 : Surah Al-Baqarah (The Cow) -   سورة البقرة
وَاسْتَعِينُوا بِالصَّبْرِ وَالصَّلَاةِ ۚ وَإِنَّهَا لَكَبِيرَةٌ إِلَّا عَلَى الْخَاشِعِينَ
And seek help through patience and prayer, and indeed, it is difficult except for the humbly submissive [to Allah ]
Another example would be:
2:60:   Surah Al-Baqarah (The Cow) -   سورة البقرة
وَإِذِ اسْتَسْقَىٰ مُوسَىٰ لِقَوْمِهِ فَقُلْنَا اضْرِب بِّعَصَاكَ الْحَجَرَ ۖ فَانفَجَرَتْ مِنْهُ اثْنَتَا عَشْرَةَ عَيْنًا ۖ قَدْ عَلِمَ كُلُّ أُنَاسٍ مَّشْرَبَهُمْ ۖ كُلُوا وَاشْرَبُوا مِن رِّزْقِ اللَّهِ وَلَا تَعْثَوْا فِي الْأَرْضِ مُفْسِدِينَ
And [recall] when Moses prayed for water for his people, so We said, "Strike with your staff the stone." And there gushed forth from it twelve springs, and every people knew its watering place. "Eat and drink from the provision of Allah , and do not commit abuse on the earth, spreading corruption."

10 SAKHT [difficult, tough]
Synonyms: ASHAQQ, ASHADD, ADHA, RABIYAH (RABU), ASEEB, QAMTAREER (QAMTR), QAASIYAH (QASW), GHALEEZ, ARIMA
10.1 ASHAQQ (اَشَقّ):   SHAQQ-AL-AMR (شَقَّ الْاَمْر) means a difficult work. SHAQQ-ALA-FULAN (شَقَّ علٰی فُلَانٍ) means to put someone into some difficulty   (dictionary Al   Manjad  )  . The word ASHAQQ (اَشَقّ) usually refers to a difficulty that is unbearable or harsh. Allah says in the Holy Quran
Surah Ar-Ra’d (The Thunder): سورۃ الرّعد 13:34

DAWAHI-AD-DAHR (دَوَاھِیَ اَلدَّھْر) means the adversities of time. And ADHA (اَدْھٰی) means rough in respect of problems and tribulations. Allah says in Holy Quran
Surah Al-Qamar (The moon): سورۃ القَمَر 54:46
وَٱلسَّاعَةُ أَدۡهَىٰ وَأَمَرُّ
The Hour is more disastrous, and most bitter.
10.4 RABIYAH (رَابِیَۃ):   (RABUربو ) RABA (رَبَا) means to grow, flourish or increase, and RABIYAH (رَابِیَۃ) means to keep on increasing with time.

But they disobeyed the messenger of their Lord, so He seized them with an overpowering grip.
10.5 ASEEB (عَصِیْب):   ASABA (عَصَبَ) comprises of two parts, one is the connection and association between two things and the other is difficulty. ASBAH (عصبۃ) (plural AASAABاعصاب ) means muscles. And USBAH (عُصْبَۃ) refers to that powerful group which comprises of ten or more in quantity and they have strong association with each other making the whole group compelling. Like the brother of Prophet Joseph (Yusuf) said to their father WA-NAHNU-USBATAN  وَنَحۡنُ عُصۡبَةٌ (we are a powerful team)12:14, TA’SSUB (تعصّب) refers to strictness in ideology or belief that a person after even knowing the truth, rejects it. ASEEB (عَصِیْب) means something that is dreadful and also void of goodness and well-being. Allah says in the Holy Quran

And when Our envoys came to Lot, he was anxious for them, and concerned for them. He said, “This is a dreadful day.”
10.6 QAMTAREER (قَمْطَرِیْر):   someone who consternates others. QIMTAR (قِمْطَرِ) is a wood that is used in punishing the criminals. QAMTAREER (قَمْطَرِیْر) means extreme evil or difficult or grim times   (dictionary Al   Manjad  )  . In the Quran
Surah Al-Insan (The Man): سورۃ الانْسان 76:10
إِنَّا نَخَافُ مِن رَّبِّنَا يَوۡمًا عَبُوسً۬ا قَمۡطَرِيرً۬ا
We dread from our Lord a frowning grim Day.
10.7 QAASIAH (قَاسِیَۃ):   The word QASW (قاسو) indicates extremity and stiffness. QASA (قَاسَا) means though and solid   (dictionary Al   Manjad  )  . HIJARUN-QAS (حِجَرٌقَاسٍ) means a hard stone. فَوَيۡلٌ۬ لِّلۡقَـٰسِيَةِ قُلُوبُہُم مِّن ذِكۡرِ ٱللَّهِ‌ۚ
Woe to those whose hearts are hardened against the mention of God
10.8 GHALEEZ (غَلِیْظ):   GHALAZA (غَلَظَ) means to thicken, inspissate, become tough or harsh, rough. GHALAZA-AR-RUJL (غَلَظَ الْرَّجُل) refers to a man being vicious and scurrilous. (Plural GHILAAZغِلَاظُ) Allah says in the Quran

We unleashed against them the flood of the dam

11. SAKHTI [Stiffness, obduracy]
Synonyms: GHILZA, QASWA, BA’SA (BU’AS, BI’AS), KABDA
11.1 QASWA (قَسْوَۃ):   QASWA (قَسْوَۃ) and GHILZA (غِلْظَ) have been discussed earlier. QASWA means being remorseless and ruthless from heart. Allah says in the Holy Quran
Surah Al-Baqarah (The cow): سورۃ البَقَرَۃ 2:74
ثُمَّ قَسَتۡ قُلُوبُكُم مِّنۢ بَعۡدِ ذَٲلِكَ فَهِىَ كَٱلۡحِجَارَةِ أَوۡ أَشَدُّ قَسۡوَةً۬‌ۚ
Then after that your hearts hardened. They were as rocks, or even harder.
11.2 GHILZA (غِلْظَ):   combination remorseless and severe. Refers to nature. Allah says in the Quran.
Surah Al Tawbah (The repentance): سورۃ التوبھ 9:123
يَـٰٓأَيُّہَا ٱلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُواْ قَـٰتِلُواْ ٱلَّذِينَ يَلُونَكُم مِّنَ ٱلۡڪُفَّارِ وَلۡيَجِدُواْ فِيكُمۡ غِلۡظَةً۬‌ۚ
O you who believe! Fight those of the disbelievers who attack you, and let them find severity in you
11.3 BA’SA (باَْسَاء):   BU’AS (بؤس) refers stiffness and rigor which may come from disputes or hunger. BA’S (بَاَْس) word is used in Quran for battles   وَحِينَ ٱلۡبَأۡسِ  ‌ۗ   (hardship, and in the time of conflict) (2:177), for punishment      إِذۡ جَآءَهُم بَأۡسُنَا   (when Our calamity came upon them) (6:43), for calamity      بَأۡسً۬ا شَدِيدً۬ا     (severe punishment) (18:2) all of them giving the meaning of grimness and hardship. BA’SAA (باَْسَاء) means a hardships or difficulties that can be financial or conflict related. Allah says in the Holy Quran
Surah Al-Ana’am (The cattle): سورۃ الانعام 6:42
وَلَقَدۡ أَرۡسَلۡنَآ إِلَىٰٓ أُمَمٍ۬ مِّن قَبۡلِكَ فَأَخَذۡنَـٰهُم بِٱلۡبَأۡسَآءِ وَٱلضَّرَّآءِ لَعَلَّهُمۡ يَتَضَرَّعُونَ
We sent messengers to communities before you, and We afflicted them with suffering and hardship, that they may humble themselves.
11.4 KABADA (کَبَد):   means liver. The meaning of word KABAD (کَبَد) consists of toughness and power. TAKABBAD (تَکَبَّد) and KAABAD (کَابد) means to bear hardship   (dictionary Al   Manjad  ). FI-KABAD   (فِیْ کَبَد)   is used as an idiom and represents human nature that when a man wishes for something, to fulfill the wish he endures pain, suffering and struggles for it, before it is rewarded some more wishes come through. Then to fulfill the other wishes he agrees to tolerate more pain and agony, and his whole life comes to end following the same pattern of struggle. Allah has described this fact in Quran as
Surah Al-Balad (The city): سورۃ البَلد         90:4
لَقَدۡ خَلَقۡنَا ٱلۡإِنسَـٰنَ فِى كَبَدٍ
We have created man into toil and struggle.
Summary:
11.1 QASWA:   Ruthless from heart
11.2 GHILZA:   Remorseless and vicious nature.
11.3 BA’SAA: Tenure of hardship.
11.4 KABAD: The nature of man to endure pain and struggle for life.

12 SAR UTHANA [raise head]
Synonyms: AQMAH, AQNAH, A’LA
12.1 AQMAH (اَقْمَحَ):   when a camel lifts his head after finishing his drink looking down this condition is known as AQMAH-AL-BAEER (اَقْمَحَ البَعِیْر). And when a human is forced to lift his head and can only lower eyes to look down that is also known as AQMAH-AR-RUJULU-WAGHADDA-BASRUH (اَقْمَحَ الرَّجُلُ وَغَضَّ بَصَرُہُ) . Allah says in the Holy Quran
Surah Yaseen (Yaseen): سورۃ ٰیٰس 36:8
إِنَّا جَعَلۡنَا فِىٓ أَعۡنَـٰقِهِمۡ أَغۡلَـٰلاً۬ فَهِىَ إِلَى ٱلۡأَذۡقَانِ فَهُم مُّقۡمَحُونَ
We have put yokes round their necks right up to their chins, so that their heads are forced up
12.2 AQNA’ (اَقْنَعَ):   means to raise your hear or voice, to lift up. MUQNAE’ (مُقْنِع) means one who raises head to look. Allah says in the Quran.
Surah Ibraheem (Abraham): سورۃ ابراھیم 14:43
مُهۡطِعِينَ مُقۡنِعِى رُءُوسِہِمۡ لَا يَرۡتَدُّ إِلَيۡہِمۡ طَرۡفُهُمۡ‌ۖ وَأَفۡـِٔدَتُہُمۡ هَوَآءٌ۬
Their necks outstretched, their heads upraised, their gaze unblinking, their hearts void.

13 SARDAR [Leader, Chief]
Synonyms: SAYYED, MALA’, RAHT, AI’MMA, NAQEEB
13.1 SAYYED (سَیِّد):   SAAD (سَادَ) means honorable, wise, elder, head of a nation, to dominate due to grandeur and dignity (dictionary Al   Manjad  ). SAWADA (سَوَادَ) means a large group, and SAYYED (سَیِّد) means the leader of a big group. A leader should be civilized therefore a noble person can also be called SAYYED (سَیِّد) and in the same manner master/lord or a husband can also be referred to as SAYYED (سَیِّد) (plural SAADAT (سَادَت) (33:67), SAADAAT (سَادَات)). Used in a positive sense. In the Quran
Suran Al-Ahzaab (The clans): سورۃ الأحزَاب 33:67
وَقَالُواْ رَبَّنَآ إِنَّآ أَطَعۡنَا سَادَتَنَا وَكُبَرَآءَنَا فَأَضَلُّونَا ٱلسَّبِيلَا۟
And they would say: "Our Lord! We obeyed our chiefs and our great ones, and they misled us as to the (right) Path
13.2 MALA’ (مَلَأ):   MALA (مَلَا) means to fill, MALA’ (مَلَأ) means a group have a congregation for inviolability. Who fill the sight with apparent beauty and souls with horror. And their leaders gaze with pride move around causing terror. In commonly parlance MALA (ملا) means those government officials who due regal influence are imposed on people. Allah says in the Holy Quran
Surah Al-Araf (The heights): سورۃ الأعرَاف 7:88
قَالَ ٱلۡمَلَأُ ٱلَّذِينَ ٱسۡتَكۡبَرُواْ مِن قَوۡمِهِۦ لَنُخۡرِجَنَّكَ يَـٰشُعَيۡبُ وَٱلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُواْ مَعَكَ مِن قَرۡيَتِنَآ
The leaders, the arrogant party among his people, said: "O Shu´aib! we shall certainly drive you out of our city
13.3 RAHT (رَھْط):   Clan, group of people belonging to a tribe, who are less than 10 in number and have no women amongst them. The leader of this group is also called RAHT(رَھْط). Used in a negative sense. The shred of cloth which women place under their private parts during   menstruation is also called   RAHT (رَھْط) and hence the idiom “(ھُوَ اَذَلُّ مِنَ الَرَّھْط)” translation “more wretched then shred of menstruation”. When the word RAHT (رَھْط) refers to some number then its meaning is taken a people or individuals. Like ISHROON-A-RAHTAN (عِشْرُوْنَ رَھْطاً) means twenty people (dictionary Al   Manjad  ). Allah says in the Holy Quran
Surah An-Naml (The ant): سورۃ النَّمل 27:48
وَكَانَ فِى ٱلۡمَدِينَةِ تِسۡعَةُ رَهۡطٍ۬ يُفۡسِدُونَ فِى ٱلۡأَرۡضِ وَلَا يُصۡلِحُونَ
There were in the city nine men of a family, who made mischief in the land, and would not reform
13.4 AI’MMAH (اَئِمَّۃ):   plural of IMAM (اِمَام), a person, book or saying that is obeyed. Can be a human, a book or a quote can be righteous or wicked. In case of human mostly it’s a religious leader, or the one who leads the prayer. For instance
Surah Yaseen (Yaseen): سورۃ ٰیٰس 36:12
وَكُلَّ شَىۡءٍ أَحۡصَيۡنَـٰهُ فِىٓ إِمَامٍ۬ مُّبِينٍ۬
We have tallied all things in a Clear Record.
For leaders of guidance
Surah As-Sajdah (The Prostration): سورۃ السَّجدَہ 32:24
وَجَعَلۡنَا مِنۡہُمۡ أَٮِٕمَّةً۬ يَہۡدُونَ بِأَمۡرِنَا لَمَّا صَبَرُواْ‌ۖ
And We appointed leaders from among them, guiding by Our command
Leader of infidels
Surah Al Tawbah (The repentance): سورۃ التوبھ 9:12
فَقَـٰتِلُوٓاْ أَٮِٕمَّةَ ٱلۡڪُفۡرِ‌ۙ إِنَّهُمۡ لَآ أَيۡمَـٰنَ لَهُمۡ
Then fight the leaders of disbelief—they have no faith
13.5 NAQEEB (نقیب):   NAQABA(نَقَبَ) means to drill through a wall, a subterraneous excavation, NAQABA-ANIL-AKHBAAR (نَقَبَ عَنِ الاَخْبَار) means to investigate the news, NA’QABA (نَاقَبَ) means to take pride in your actions, NA’QIB (نَاقِبْ) means someone who is aware of the condition of a nation, MUNQABAT (مُنْقَبَتْ) means a noble act. NAQEEB (نقیب) someone who is aware of the condition of a nation, a leader of a nation, chief, one whose accountable for a nation (dictionary Al   Manjad  ). Used in a positive sense. Allah says in the Holy Quran.
Surah Al-Maeda (The table spread): سورۃ المَائدہ 5:12
وَلَقَدۡ أَخَذَ ٱللَّهُ مِيثَـٰقَ بَنِىٓ إِسۡرَٲٓءِيلَ وَبَعَثۡنَا مِنۡهُمُ ٱثۡنَىۡ عَشَرَ نَقِيبً۬ا‌ۖ
God received a pledge from the Children of Israel, and we raised among them twelve chiefs.
Summary:
13.1 SAYYED: Leader of a big nation (positive sense)
13.2 MALA’: Officials imposed on people (negative sense)
13.3 RAHT: Small group of people from a tribe, mischievous group and its leader.
13.4 IMAM: Leader, one who is obeyed irrespective of him being good or bad.
13.5 NAQEEB: Guarantor, leader or guardian.
