14 SARD,SARDI [winter, cold]
Synonyms: SHITAA’, SIRR, SARSAR, NAFHAH, ZAMHAREER
14.1 SHITAA’ (شِتَآء):   means winter season (opposite SAIF (صَیْف) summer season), SHATWII (شَتْوِیّ) means rain in winter season   (dictionary Al   Manjad  )  . Allah says in the Quran
Surah Quraish (Quraish): سورۃ قُرَیْش 106:1-2
لِإِيلَـٰفِ قُرَيۡشٍ إِیلَـٰفِهِمۡ رِحۡلَةَ ٱلشِّتَآءِ وَٱلصَّيۡفِ
For the security of Quraish. Their security during winter and summer journeys.
14.2 SIRR (صِرّ):   SURR-AL-BANAT (صُرَّالْبَنَات) means vegetation destroyed due to cold winds   (dictionary Al   Manjad  )  . SIRR (صِرّ) means severe cold, frost or haze. Allah says in the Holy Quran.
Surah Ale- Imran (The family of Imran): سورۃ آل عِمْرن 3:117
ڪَمَثَلِ رِيحٍ۬ فِيہَا صِرٌّ أَصَابَتۡ حَرۡثَ قَوۡمٍ۬ ظَلَمُوٓاْ أَنفُسَهُمۡ فَأَهۡلَڪَتۡهُ‌ۚ
May be likened to a wind which brings a nipping frost: It strikes and destroys the harvest of men who have wronged their own souls:
14.3 SARSAR (صَرْصَر):   means swift cold wind. Wind that is cold and creates sound. Whistling cold wind. Allah says in the Holy Quran
Surah Al-Haqqah (The reality): سورۃ الحَاقَّۃ 69:6
وَأَمَّا عَادٌ۬ فَأُهۡلِڪُواْ بِرِيحٍ۬ صَرۡصَرٍ عَاتِيَةٍ۬
And as for Aad; they were annihilated by a furious, roaring wind.
14.4 NAFHA (نَفْحَۃ):   NAFAHA (نَفَحَ) means blowing of wind in winter, blowing of chilly wind, NAFHA (نَفْحَۃ) is an instant noun. Like a rush of cold wind. (Opposite LAFHA (لَفْحَۃ) means a rush of warm wind).Allah says in the Holy Quran
Surah Al-Anbiya (the prophets): سورۃ الانَبیاء 21:46
وَلَٮِٕن مَّسَّتۡهُمۡ نَفۡحَةٌ۬ مِّنۡ عَذَابِ رَبِّكَ
And when a breath of your Lord’s punishment touches them, they say
14.5 ZAMHAREER (زَمْھَرِیْر):   IZMAHARR-AL-YAUM (اِزْمَھَرَّالیوم) means a very cold day. ZAMHAREER (زَمْھَرِیْر) means severe cold and also a place where there is severe cold   (dictionary Al   Manjad  )  . Allah says in the Holy Quran.
Surah Al-Insan (The Man): سورۃ الانْسان 76:13
لَا يَرَوۡنَ فِيہَا شَمۡسً۬ا وَلَا زَمۡهَرِيرً۬ا
They will see there neither the sun´s (excessive heat) nor (the moon´s) excessive cold.
SUMMARY:
14.1 SHITAA’ : Winter
14.2 SIRR: Haze or frost
14.3 SARSAR: Clattering swift cold wind.
14.4 NAFHA: A single rush of cold wind
14.5 ZAMHAREER: Severe cold, or area which is cold.

title: content/s/s15.html
raw_text:
15 SARKASHI KARNA [rebellious, insubordinate]
Synonyms: TAGHA, A’TA, A’LA, MARADA
15.1 TAGHA (طَغٰی):   means to surpass all the limits in disobedience, extremely rebellious, TAGH-AL-MAA’ (طَغَاالْمَاء) means flooding of water, inundation   (dictionary Al   Manjad  )  . TAGHIYAH (طَاغِیَۃ) means a violent storm. A huge thunderstorm. And TAGHOOT (طَاغُوْت) means something you offer the service to, except Allah, that can be a person or system. Therefore TUGHYANI (طُغیانی) refers to both surpassing limits and wrath, predominance. Allah says in the Holy Quran.
Surah Al-Alaq (The Clot): سورۃ العَلق 96:6
كَلَّآ إِنَّ ٱلۡإِنسَـٰنَ لَيَطۡغَىٰٓ  أَن رَّءَاهُ ٱسۡتَغۡنَىٰٓ
In fact, man oversteps all bounds. When he considers himself exempt.
15.2 A’TA (عَتَا):   ATAWIDAL-ALA-ASTAKBRAM (عتویدل علی استکبارام) means defiance due to pride. A person considering himself powerful and disobeys Allah’s orders. In the Quran
Surah Al-Mulk (The sovereignty): سُوۡرَةُ المُلک 67:21
بَل لَّجُّواْ فِى عُتُوٍّ۬ وَنُفُورٍ
Yet they persist in defiance and aversion.
15.3 A’LA (عَلَا):   To rise, to dominate, to be arrogant   (dictionary Al   Manjad  )  . To insubordinate and unruly after gaining power and authority. In the Quran
Surah Al-Israa (The Night Journey): سورۃ الٕاسرَاء  17:4
لَتُفۡسِدُنَّ فِى ٱلۡأَرۡضِ مَرَّتَيۡنِ وَلَتَعۡلُنَّ عُلُوًّ۬ا ڪَبِيرً۬ا
That twice would they do mischief on the earth and be elated with mighty arrogance (and twice would they be punished)!
15.4 MARADA (مَرَدَ):   means to be disobedient and unruly, to surpass your peers   (dictionary Al   Manjad  )  . Thus MARADA (مَرَدَ) means to surpass everyone in disobedience and insubordination. Allah says in the Holy Quran.

وَإِن يَدۡعُونَ إِلَّا شَيۡطَـٰنً۬ا مَّرِيدً۬ا
In fact, they invoke none but a rebellious devil.
Summary:
15.1 TAGHA: Encroach with dominance and wrath
15.2 A’TA: Disobedience due to arrogance
15.3 A’LA: Unruly after gain power and authority
15.4 MARADA: To surpass in being rebellious
For SARGARDAN PHIRNA see AWARA PHIRNA

16 SARGOSHI KERNA [to whisper]
Synonyms: TAKHAFAT, TANAJA-NAJWA
16.1 TAKHAFAT (تَخَافَتَ):   KHAFAT (خَفَتَ) means muffled voice, to murmur; TAKHAFAT (تَخَافَتَ) means to talk in a low voice   (dictionary Al   Manjad  )  . To whisper to others even if others can hear it. In the Quran
Surah Ta-Ha (Ta-ha): سورۃ طٰھٰ  20:103
يَتَخَـٰفَتُونَ بَيۡنَہُمۡ إِن لَّبِثۡتُمۡ إِلَّا عَشۡرً۬ا
Murmuring among themselves: “You have lingered only for ten.”
16.2 TANAJA – NAJWA (تَنَاجٰی نَجْوٰی):   NAJA’A (نَجَاَ) means to whisper, to talk about secrecy, TANAJA (تَنَاجٰی) means to make a confidant   (dictionary Al   Manjad  ). To hold a secret meeting, to talk about secrets separately. Allah says in the Holy Quran
Surah Al-Mujadila (The pleading Women): سُوۡرَةُ المجَادلة 58:10
إِنَّمَا ٱلنَّجۡوَىٰ مِنَ ٱلشَّيۡطَـٰنِ لِيَحۡزُنَ ٱلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُواْ
Secret counsels are only (inspired) by the Evil One, in order that he may cause grief to the Believers
In Another Place:
يَـٰٓأَيُّہَا ٱلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُوٓاْ إِذَا تَنَـٰجَيۡتُمۡ فَلَا تَتَنَـٰجَوۡاْ بِٱلۡإِثۡمِ وَٱلۡعُدۡوَٲنِ وَمَعۡصِيَتِ ٱلرَّسُولِ وَتَنَـٰجَوۡاْ بِٱلۡبِرِّ وَٱلتَّقۡوَىٰ‌ۖ
O you who believe! When you converse secretly, do not converse in sin, and aggression, and disobedience of the Messenger; but converse in virtue and piety
Summary:
16.1 TAKHAFAT: To converse in a low voice.
16.2 NAJWA: To converse about secrets in privacy

title: content/s/s17.html
raw_text:
17 SURANG [tunnel]
Synonyms: NAFAQ, SARAB
17.1 NAFAQ (نَفَق):   a tunnel that opens at both ends. a subterraneous passage that opens at both ends. Like a tunnel dug through mountain for traffic or trains. NAFEEQ-US-SARAWEEL (نَیْفَقُ السَّرَاوِیْل) means belt of a pajama, NAFIQA’-AL-YARBU’ (نَافِقاء الیَرْبُوْع) means the hole of a wild rat having two openings. NAFAQAL-YARBU’U-WA-NAFAQ (نَافَقَ الیَرْبُوْعُ وَنَفَقَ) means the mouse entered from one end and left from other. Allah says in the Holy Quran
Surah Al-Ana’am (The cattle): سورۃ الانعام 6:35
فَإِنِ ٱسۡتَطَعۡتَ أَن تَبۡتَغِىَ نَفَقً۬ا فِى ٱلۡأَرۡضِ أَوۡ سُلَّمً۬ا فِى ٱلسَّمَآءِ
If you find their rejection hard to bear, then if you can, seek a tunnel into the earth, or a stairway into the heaven
17.2 SARAB (سَرَب):   a tunnel with only one opening. SARABA (سَرَبَ) means to keep on advancing in, and WA-INSARBAT-AL-HAYYAHTU-ILA-HUJARIHA (انسَرَبتِ الْحَیَّۃُ اِلٰی جُحْرِھَا) refers a snake slipping into his hole or burrow. Allah says in the Holy Quran
Surah Al-Kahf (The Cave): سورۃ الکھف 18:61
فَلَمَّا بَلَغَا مَجۡمَعَ بَيۡنِهِمَا نَسِيَا حُوتَهُمَا فَٱتَّخَذَ سَبِيلَهُ ۥ فِى ٱلۡبَحۡرِ سَرَبً۬ا
But when they reached the Junction, they forgot (about) their Fish, which took its course through the sea (straight) as in a tunnel.
Summary:
17.1 NAFAQ: A tunnel with two openings
17.2 SARAB: A tunnel with a single opening
For SAZA see AZAAB
For SAZAWAAR see LAIQ HONA

title: content/s/s18.html
raw_text:
18 SUSTI KARNA, SUST HONA [ to be lazy]
Synonyms: KASAL, WAHAN, WANAA, ISTAHSARA, BATTA’A
18.1 KASAL (کَسَلَ):   To be grievous due to lack of interest and heart. To be lazy and slow. Allah says in the Holy Quran
Surah An-Nisa (The women): سورۃ النِّسا 4:142
وَإِذَا قَامُوٓاْ إِلَى ٱلصَّلَوٰةِ قَامُواْ كُسَالَىٰ
And when they stand for prayer, they stand lazily,
18.2 WAHANA (وَھَنَ):   To be lazy due to physical weakness. Allah says in the Holy Quran
Surah An-Nisa (The women): سورۃ النِّسا 4:104
وَلَا تَهِنُواْ فِى ٱبۡتِغَآءِ ٱلۡقَوۡمِ‌ۖ
And slacken not in following up the enemy:
18.3 WANAA (وَنٰی):   to neglect, to be lazy, to be sloppy   (dictionary Al   Manjad  ). To make no efforts. Allah says in the Holy Quran
Surah Ta-Ha (Ta-ha): سورۃ طٰھٰ  20:42
ٱذۡهَبۡ أَنتَ وَأَخُوكَ بِـَٔايَـٰتِى وَلَا تَنِيَا فِى ذِكۡرِى
Go, you and your brother, with My signs, and do not neglect My remembrance.
18.4 ISTAHSAR (اِسْتَحْسَرَ):   HASARA (حَسَرَ) means to get tired, weary, HASAR-AL-BASAR (حَسَرَالْبَصَرَ) means a weary sight, weak eyesight. HASEER (حَسِیْر) means tired and weak (dictionary Al   Manjad  ). HASAR (حسر) is to be lazy due to fatigue, tedium. Allah says in the Quran
Surah Al-Anbiya (the prophets): سورۃ الانَبیاء 21:19
وَمَنۡ عِندَهُ ۥ لَا يَسۡتَكۡبِرُونَ عَنۡ عِبَادَتِهِۦ وَلَا يَسۡتَحۡسِرُونَ
Even those who are in His (very) Presence are not too proud to serve Him, nor are they (ever) weary (of His service):
18.5 BATTA’A (بَطَّاَ):   AL-BATU’U (اَلبَطْؤُ) to be lazy, to delay while walking, IBTA’UN(اِبْطَاءٌ) means to walk lazily. And BATTA’A (بَطَّاَ) means utmost laziness, and delay, to lag. In the Quran
Surah An-Nisa (The women): سورۃ النِّسا 4:72
وَإِنَّ مِنكُمۡ لَمَن لَّيُبَطِّئَنَّ
Among you is he who lags behind
18.1 KASAL: Laziness due to lack of interest
18.2 WAHANA: Laziness due to physical weakness
18.3 WANAA: Laziness due to carelessness
18.4 ISTAHSARA: Laziness due to fatigue
18.5 BATTA’A: Be lazy and cause delay, laziness

title: content/s/s19.html
raw_text:
19 SAFAR KERNA [to travel]
Synonyms: SAFARA, SAHA, ZA’ANA, NAFARA, DARABA
19.1 SAFARA (سَفَرَ):   to go far away from residence. To travel, a very common word. Used for travelling regardless of its purpose. In the Quran
Surah An-Nisa (The women): سورۃ النِّسا 4:43
وَإِن كُنتُم مَّرۡضَىٰٓ أَوۡ عَلَىٰ سَفَرٍ
If you are sick, or traveling
19.2 SAHA (سَاحَ):   SAHA-AL-MAA’ (سَاحَ الْمَاَء) means the random flow of water, SAHAH (سَاحَۃ) means an open area, SAHAH-TUD-DAAR (سَاحَۃُالدَّار) means the courtyard of a house, an open place next to or near a house, SAHA (سَاحَ) means to walk around in an open place, to travel or move for the sake of fun or some other purpose. In the Quran
Surah Al Tawbah (The repentance): سورۃ التوبھ 9:2
فَسِيحُواْ فِى ٱلۡأَرۡضِ أَرۡبَعَةَ أَشۡہُرٍ۬
So travel the land for four months,
19.3 ZA’ANA (ظَعَنَ):   means to depart, to journey from one place to other, to shift residence. ZA’HAN(ظَعَانَ) means a rope to tie a HOWDAH (ھووج) ( a seat for two or more, with a canopy, for riding on the back of an elephant or camel ), ZUGHUN(ظَعُوْن)  means a camel for freight, ZAEENA (ظعینہ) means a HOWDAH(ھووج) or a woman who travels a lot in a HOWDAH(ھووج)
Surat An-Nahl (The Bee): سورۃ النّحل16:80
وَجَعَلَ لَكُم مِّن جُلُودِ ٱلۡأَنۡعَـٰمِ بُيُوتً۬ا تَسۡتَخِفُّونَهَا يَوۡمَ ظَعۡنِكُمۡ وَيَوۡمَ إِقَامَتِڪُمۡ‌ۙ
And has provided for you out of the hides of livestock portable homes for you, so you can use them when you travel, and when you camp
19.4 NAFARA (نَفَرَ):   AN-NAFEER (النَّفِیْر) a group of less than ten men, mobilizing for a fight, AN-NAFEER-UL-AAM (النَّفْیِرُ الْعَام) means standing of public against an enemy, NAFARA (نَفَرَ) means to go a war or mission to face an enemy. Allah Says in the Quran.
Surah An-Nisa (The women): سورۃ النِّسا 4:71
فَٱنفِرُواْ ثُبَاتٍ أَوِ ٱنفِرُواْ جَمِيعً۬ا
And mobilize in groups, or mobilize altogether.
<<partial entry>>
Journey – To Travel
The glorious Quran uses the words ضَرَبَ فِي الاَرض, نَفَرَ, ظَعَنَ, سََاحَ(سِيح), سَفَرَ, رَحَلَfor this.
1- سَفَرَ
means to leave your place of residence to go somewhere far and is used in the meaning of travelling. Its a common used word.
وَإِن كُنتُم مَّرۡضَىٰٓ أَوۡ عَلَىٰ سَفَرٍ
“And if ye be ill, or on a journey”     4/43
2- سََاحَ
سَاحَ     المَاءmeans water running freely and سَاحَةmeans a wide place. سَاحَةُالدَّارmeans a yard in a house , a wide space adjacent to the house and سََاحَmeans to walk about in a wide place, whether it is leisurely or for some other reason.
فَسِيحُواْ فِى ٱلۡأَرۡضِ أَرۡبَعَةَ أَشۡہُرٍ۬
“Travel freely in the land four months”     9/2
3- ظَعَنَ
Means to depart, to leave for a a destination or to emigrate. ظَعَانmeans a rope for tying a saddle on an animal and ظَعنةis a woman who often travels.
وَجَعَلَ لَكُم مِّن جُلُودِ ٱلۡأَنۡعَـٰمِ بُيُوتً۬ا تَسۡتَخِفُّونَهَا يَوۡمَ ظَعۡنِكُمۡ وَيَوۡمَ إِقَامَتِڪُمۡ*ۙ
“And hath given you (also), of the hides of cattle, tent-houses which ye find light (to carry) on the day of migration and on the day of pitching camp”     16/80
4- نَفَرَ
النَّفِير     is a group of less than 10 men, a battle party that is departing and النَّفِيرالعَامmeans when people rise against the enemy and نَفَرَ means to go on a venture or a war against the enemy.
فَٱنفِرُواْ ثُبَاتٍ أَوِ ٱنفِرُواْ جَمِيعً۬ا
“Then advance the proven ones, or advance all together” 4/71
5- ضَرَبَ فِي الاَرض
Means to strike feet on the ground and is used proverbially for a journey and usually for a long and purposeful journey.
وَءَاخَرُونَ يَضۡرِبُونَ فِى ٱلۡأَرۡضِ يَبۡتَغُونَ مِن فَضۡلِ ٱللَّهِ*ۙ
“There are sick folk among you, while others travel in the land in search of Allah's bounty”     73:20
6- رَحَلَ
اَلرَّحَل     means destiny, place of rest, saddle of a camel, a cushion used between the saddle and the body of a beast of burden, luggage that stays with the traveller. رَحَلَis to saddle a beast for riding, to climb on an animal, to march, to set off on a journey.
إِیلَـٰفِهِمۡ رِحۡلَةَ ٱلشِّتَآءِ وَٱلصَّيۡفِ
“For their taming (We cause) the caravans to set forth in winter and summer”     106:2
Inference
1- سَفَرَ: Common word for a journey
2- سََاحَ: A journey in numerous directions in the opens, also means tourism
3- ظَعَنَ: To emigrate
4- نَفَرَ: To set off for a venture
5- ضَرَبَفِيالاَرض: To make a purposeful, long journey
6- رَحَلَ: Marching off and everything related to it, including preparations

2  .            Companion (saathi):
Saahib   صَاحِب   ,Asheer   عَشير   ,Qareen   قَرين   , & azwaaj    ازواج   are the words used.
1.            Saahib   صَاحِب   : Meaning a companion for a long time. Someone who has been living with someone for a long time. This companionship could be with an animal or human, or time or place. According to Ibne Faaris, Sahab    صَحَبَ    has two things in it.  A) Makarna   مقارنة   & b)Maqarba   مقاربة   meaning one who is not only a company but also lives in close vicinity./closeby. ( plural is ashaab   اصحاب   & feminine is sahiba   صاحبة   ) & according to the people of dictionary, this word is associated with men.
Allah says in the Quran: 9:40 : Surah At-Tawbah (The Repentance) -   سورة التوبة
إِلَّا تَنصُرُوهُ فَقَدْ نَصَرَهُ اللَّهُ إِذْ أَخْرَجَهُ الَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا ثَانِيَ اثْنَيْنِ إِذْ هُمَا فِي الْغَارِ إِذْ يَقُولُ لِصَاحِبِهِ لَا تَحْزَنْ إِنَّ اللَّهَ مَعَنَا ۖ فَأَنزَلَ اللَّهُ سَكِينَتَهُ عَلَيْهِ وَأَيَّدَهُ بِجُنُودٍ لَّمْ تَرَوْهَا وَجَعَلَ كَلِمَةَ الَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا السُّفْلَىٰ ۗ وَكَلِمَةُ اللَّهِ هِيَ الْعُلْيَا ۗ وَاللَّهُ عَزِيزٌ حَكِيمٌ
If you do not aid the Prophet - Allah has already aided him when those who disbelieved had driven him out [of Makkah] as one of two, when they were in the cave and he said to his companion, "Do not grieve; indeed Allah is with us." And Allah sent down his tranquillity upon him and supported him with angels you did not see and made the word of those who disbelieved the lowest, while the word of Allah - that is the highest. And Allah is Exalted in Might and Wise.
2.            Asheera   عَشير   : This word is used for group of  paternal relatives. Meaning family of a person from his fathers side.  Aashar   عاشِر   to live together as a family would do. Asheer    عَشير   are all those people who live together, may it be family or strangers living together.
Allah says in the Quran: 22:13: Surah Al-Ĥaj (The Pilgrimage) -   سورة الحج
يَدْعُو لَمَن ضَرُّهُ أَقْرَبُ مِن نَّفْعِهِ ۚ لَبِئْسَ الْمَوْلَىٰ وَلَبِئْسَ الْعَشِيرُ
He invokes one whose harm is closer than his benefit - how wretched the protector and how wretched the associate.
3.            Qareen    قَرين  : means of the same age group & it also means all those people belonging to same age group or having the same expertise or equal in bravery,power etc. Its usage is objective.(look at ‘friends’ for details)
4.            Azwaaj    ازواج  : Zauj   زوج   means partner, spouse(husband or wife) . Both are zauj    زوج   for each other & are called zauj    زوج   collectively as well. This word is used in the Quran for the meaning of partner or people of the same gender. Meaning having same nature,qualities like each other. (look at ‘different’ for details).
Allah says in the Quran: 37:22: Surah Aş-Şāffāt (Those who set the Ranks) -   سورة الصافات
احْشُرُوا الَّذِينَ ظَلَمُوا وَأَزْوَاجَهُمْ وَمَا كَانُوا يَعْبُدُونَ
[The angels will be ordered], "Gather those who committed wrong, their kinds, and what they used to worship
Summary:
1.          Saahib    صَاحِب     :   companion for a very long time.
2.         Asheer   عَشير    : those people living together as family
3.         Qareen    قَرين   : people of the same age,same status,power etc.
4.         Azwaaj   ازواج    : means same gender , or people having same nature,qualities,characteristics.

To Understand – To Enlighten – To Elucidate
In the Quran, the words عَقَلَ, فَهَمَ, فَقَهَand شَعَرَhave been used.
1- شَعَرَ
اَشَّعَر     means hair and شَعَرَmeans to gain comprehensive knowledge like a fine hair, to comprehend the soul and true meaning of a matter.
وَمَا يَخۡدَعُونَ إِلَّآ أَنفُسَهُمۡ وَمَا يَشۡعُرُونَ
“And they beguile none save themselves; but they perceive not” 2:9
2- فَهَمَ
اَلفَهم     is the capability of a human being by which he comprehends and understands the gist and the meanings and فَهَمَmeans to fully understand something and also in the meaning of understanding immediately as soon as one hears something. سَرِيعُالفَهمis to understand quickly and سئالفهمmeans a dull mind and فَهَّمَmeans to elucidate the reality to someone else.
وَڪُنَّا لِحُكۡمِهِمۡ شَـٰهِدِينَ (﻿٧٨﻿) فَفَهَّمۡنَـٰهَا سُلَيۡمَـٰنَ*ۚ
“And We were witnesses to their judgement. (78) And We made Solomon to understand” 21:78
3- فَقَهَ
اَلفِقَه     is the knowledge or the study of deriving inferences or arriving at decisions while taking into consideration numerous other verdicts surrounding that particular matter.
ٱنظُرۡ كَيۡفَ نُصَرِّفُ ٱلۡأَيَـٰتِ لَعَلَّهُمۡ يَفۡقَهُونَ
“See how We display the revelations so that they may understand”     6:65
Also, تَفَقَّهَmeans to find the deeper and true meaning of a matter.
فَلَوۡلَا نَفَرَ مِن كُلِّ فِرۡقَةٍ۬ مِّنۡہُمۡ طَآٮِٕفَةٌ۬ لِّيَتَفَقَّهُواْ فِى ٱلدِّينِ
“A party only should go forth, that they (who are left behind) may gain sound knowledge in religion” 9:122
4- عَقَلَ
Means to be wise and judicious. A person who can comprehend mistakes and errors and عَقَلَmeans to stop, to halt. عِقَالis that which is used to arrest the foot of a camel. اَلمعقلis a refuge, hills or a citadel for taking refuge. Hence, wisdom helps a person to discern between loss and gain and to discover ways to desist from doing harm and to be receptive and centripetal to gaining knowledge. Also, means to reflect and ponder.
أَتَأۡمُرُونَ ٱلنَّاسَ بِٱلۡبِرِّ وَتَنسَوۡنَ أَنفُسَكُمۡ وَأَنتُمۡ تَتۡلُونَ ٱلۡكِتَـٰبَ*ۚ أَفَلَا تَعۡقِلُونَ
“Enjoin ye righteousness upon mankind while ye yourselves forget (to practise it)? And ye are readers of the Scripture! Have ye then no sense? “     2:44
Inference
1- شَعَرَ: To comprehend the true meaning
2- فَهَمَ: To grasp the meaning of, to understand
3- فَقَهَ: To derive decisions from similar examples of the past
4- عَقَلَ: To understand about one's gains and losses and to find ways of preventing loss.

title: content/s/s21.html
raw_text:
To Listen – To Declare or Denote
For this the Quran has used the words اَذَنَ, اَذِنَ,إِستَمِع, إِسمَعَ, سَمَّاعَ, سَمِعَ
1- سَمِعَ
To hear something with your ears and اَلسَّمعَis the ability to hear and also the ears.
قَدۡ سَمِعَ ٱللَّهُ قَوۡلَ ٱلَّتِى تُجَـٰدِلُكَ فِى زَوۡجِهَا
“Allah hath heard the saying of her that disputeth with thee (Muhammad) concerning her husband”     58:1
2- سَمَّاعَ
سَامِع     means the one who listens and سَمَّاعَis used for a spy, in other words one who eavesdrops on a conversation.
سَمَّـٰعُونَ لِلۡڪَذِبِ سَمَّـٰعُونَ لِقَوۡمٍ ءَاخَرِينَ لَمۡ يَأۡتُوكَ*ۖ
“Listeners for the sake of falsehood, listeners on behalf of other folk who come not unto thee”     5:41
3- إِسمَعَ
Means to make someone listen
إِنَّكَ لَا تُسۡمِعُ ٱلۡمَوۡتَىٰ وَلَا تُسۡمِعُ ٱلصُّمَّ ٱلدُّعَآءَ إِذَا وَلَّوۡاْ مُدۡبِرِينَ
“Lo! thou canst not make the dead to hear, nor canst thou make the deaf to hear the call when they have turned to flee”     27:80
4- إِستَمِع
It is to try hard to listen to something when its hard to hear.
قُلۡ أُوحِىَ إِلَىَّ أَنَّهُ ٱسۡتَمَعَ نَفَرٌ۬ مِّنَ ٱلۡجِنِّ فَقَالُوٓاْ إِنَّا سَمِعۡنَا قُرۡءَانًا عَجَبً۬ا
“Say (O Muhammad): It is revealed unto me that a company of the Jinn gave ear, and they said: Lo! we have heard a marvellous Qur'an”     72:1
5- اَذِنَ
To listen carefully and attentively
6- اَذَنَ
Means to tell off, to warn
وَيَوۡمَ يُنَادِيہِمۡ أَيۡنَ شُرَڪَآءِى قَالُوٓاْ ءَاذَنَّـٰكَ مَا مِنَّا مِن شَہِيدٍ۬
“And on the day when He calleth unto them: Where are now My partners? they will say: We confess unto Thee, not one of us is a witness (for them)”     41:47
Inference
1- سَمِعَ: To hear, used commonly
2- سَمَّاعَ: To eavesdrop
3- إِسمَعَ: To declare, to make someone listen
4- إِستَمِع: To try and hear
5- اَذِنَ: To listen attentively
6- اَذَنَ: To warn

“And on the day when He calleth unto them: Where are now My partners? they will say: We confess unto Thee, not one of us is a witness (for them)” 41:47

Inference 

1- سَمِعَ: To hear, used commonly

2- سَمَّاعَ: To eavesdrop

3- إِسمَعَ: To declare, to make someone listen

4- إِستَمِع: To try and hear

5- اَذِنَ: To listen attentively

6- اَذَنَ: To warn

title: content/s/s22.html
raw_text:
To Improve – To Better
For this the Quran uses, اَصلَحَ، زَكَّي
1- اَصلَحَ(Ant: اَفسَدَ)
To correct faults and flaws. It is commonly used in both material and non-physical meaning.
كَفَّرَ عَنۡہُمۡ سَيِّـَٔاتِہِمۡ وَأَصۡلَحَ بَالَهُمۡ
“He riddeth them of their ill-deeds and improveth their state”     47:2
And
وَلَا تُفۡسِدُواْ فِى ٱلۡأَرۡضِ بَعۡدَ إِصۡلَـٰحِهَا
“Work not confusion in the earth after the fair ordering” 7:56
2- زَكَّي(from زكو)
زكَي     andزَكَّيmean the thriving of crops and زَكِيمَالَهُmeans to pay زَكَوَةand زَكَّينَفسَهُmeans to blow ones one trumpet or to brag. But in jurisprudence, the word تَزكِيةhas been used in the meaning of facilitating improvement and تَزكِيةنَفسmeans to clean one's self from bad morals and to thrive in good character.
قَدۡ أَفۡلَحَ مَن زَكَّٮٰهَا (﻿٩﻿) وَقَدۡ خَابَ مَن دَسَّٮٰهَا
“He is indeed successful who causeth it to grow, And he is indeed a failure who stunteth it.”     91:9-10
Inference
إِصلاَح     is used for correcting any kind of faults or errors but زَكَّيis used specifically for improvements in one's character and excelling in it.

title: content/s/s23.html
raw_text:
To Climb on
The Quran uses the words, رَكِبَ, إِستَوَي (سوِي) حَمَلَ
1- رَكِبَ
To climb on a ride, to embark on a boa and رِكَابmeans the ride itself, a camel for riding and رَاكِبis the rider, especially the camel rider and رَكبmeans a caravan of camel riders.
حَتَّىٰٓ إِذَا رَكِبَا فِى ٱلسَّفِينَةِ خَرَقَهَا*ۖ
“Till, when they were in the ship, he made a hole therein”     18:71
2- إِستَوَي
Means to climb on and become steady on the ride.
لِتَسۡتَوُۥاْ عَلَىٰ ظُهُورِهِۦ ثُمَّ تَذۡكُرُواْ نِعۡمَةَ رَبِّكُمۡ إِذَا ٱسۡتَوَيۡتُمۡ عَلَيۡهِ
“That ye may mount upon their backs, and may remember your Lord's favour when ye mount thereon”     43:12
3- حَمَلَ
Means to carry the load and اَحمَلَmeans to help in lifting the burden and if this burden is a person and he has to be loaded on a ride then حَمَلَis used.
وَلَا عَلَى ٱلَّذِينَ إِذَا مَآ أَتَوۡكَ لِتَحۡمِلَهُمۡ قُلۡتَ لَآ أَجِدُ مَآ أَحۡمِلُڪُمۡ عَلَيۡهِ
“Nor unto those whom, when they came to thee (asking) that thou shouldst mount them, thou didst tell: I cannot find whereon to mount you”     51:91
Inference
1- رَكِبَ: To climb on any sort of ride
2- إِستَوَيعَلَي: To become steady on a ride
3- حَمَلَ: Means to carry the burden and حَمَلَعَلَيmeans to load someone

title: content/s/s24.html
raw_text:
Except – Exclude
For this term, the words إِ     لاَّ, دُون, غَيرَ, وَرَاءand إستِثنَاhave been used in the Quran.
1- إِلاَّ
Means but, except and in this form it can be used in a universal scope as the ayah below will make it clear.
لَّآ إِلَـٰهَ إِلَّا هُوَ ٱلرَّحۡمَـٰنُ ٱلرَّحِيمُ
“There is no God save Him, the Beneficent, the Merciful”     2:163
Furthermore, this word also gives the meaning of حَصَرَ
وَمَا يَخۡدَعُونَ إِلَّآ أَنفُسَهُمۡ
“And they beguile none save themselves” 2:9
2- غَيرَ
It is sometimes used simply for negation, just like 'not' in English as in
وَهُوَ فِى ٱلۡخِصَامِ غَيۡرُ مُبِينٍ۬
“And in dispute cannot make itself plain?”     43:18
On another occasion, it is used in the context of drawing an exception, in which case its scope becomes universal or absolute.
هَلۡ مِنۡ خَـٰلِقٍ غَيۡرُ ٱللَّهِ
“Is there any creator other than Allah”     35:3
3- دُون
دَان     means low, cheap, flim  sy and شَيٌدُونٌmeans a cheap item and دُونalso means something devoid of or lacking and when دُونgives   the meaning of exclusion, than it is used in the context of cheapness and weakness.
يَـٰٓأَيُّہَا ٱلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُواْ لَا تَتَّخِذُواْ بِطَانَةً۬ مِّن دُونِكُمۡ
“O ye who believe! Take not for intimates others than your own folk” 3:118
In this context, deficiency in other religions, except Islam is denoted.
On another occasion,
إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ لَا يَغۡفِرُ أَن يُشۡرَكَ بِهِۦ وَيَغۡفِرُ مَا دُونَ ذَٲلِكَ لِمَن يَشَآءُ*ۚ
“Lo! Allah forgiveth not that a partner should be ascribed unto Him. He forgiveth (all) save that to whom He will     “ 4:48
and in this ayah, other sins apart from shirk are intended. Similarly 2:108
4- وَرَاء
Means that whenever its used, situation on either side, that surround it are meant to be opposed or negated. This word means literally, on either side. In such situations, it also gives the meaning of exclusion.
فَمَنِ ٱبۡتَغَىٰ وَرَآءَ ذَٲلِكَ فَأُوْلَـٰٓٮِٕكَ هُمُ ٱلۡعَادُونَ
“But whoso craveth beyond that, such are transgressors “ 38:7
which actually means that whoever tries to find any other way, apart from the commandment of Allah is a sinner.
5- إستِثنَا
ثَنِي     means to exclude something from a common decree, for this usually إِلاَّis used but for excluding something according to he commandment of Allah.
وَلَا تَقُولَنَّ لِشَاْىۡءٍ إِنِّى فَاعِلٌ۬ ذَٲلِكَ غَدًا (﻿٢٣﻿) إِلَّآ أَن يَشَآءَ ٱللَّهُ*ۚ
“And say not of anything: Lo! I shall do that tomorrow, (23) Except if Allah will     “ 18:24
And إستِثنَاis used in place of saying إِنشَاالله.
إِذۡ أَقۡسَمُواْ لَيَصۡرِمُنَّہَا مُصۡبِحِينَ (﻿١٧﻿) وَلَا يَسۡتَثۡنُونَ
“When they vowed they would pluck its fruit next morning, (17) And made no exception”     68:17-18
Inference
1- إِلاَّ: Exclusion, also in the meaning of حَصَرَ
2- غَيرَ: Used for negation
3- دُون: Exclusion in the meaning of lacking
4- وَرَاء: Absolute exclusion
5- إستِثنَا: To exclude something from a common decree by saying إِنشَا الله.

title: content/s/s25.html
raw_text:
To Sleep
In the Quran, the words نََامَ, هَجَعَ, رَقَدَ,قَالَ (قِيل), ضَجَعَand تَهَجَّدَhave been used.
1- نََامَ
This is a commonly used word meaning to sleep. Sleep is a kind of death in which the soul leaves the body and the sensitivity of the 5 sensory perceptions is dramatically reduced. Also, one gets fresh and derives comfort because of physical and mental tranquillity. نَومmeans sleep and مَنَامmeans to dream in sleep.
أَفَأَمِنَ أَهۡلُ ٱلۡقُرَىٰٓ أَن يَأۡتِيَہُم بَأۡسُنَا بَيَـٰتً۬ا وَهُمۡ نَآٮِٕمُونَ
“Are the people of the townships then secure from the coming of Our wrath upon them as a night-raid while they sleep?”     7:97
2- هَجَعَ
It means very deep sleep, to sleep like there isn't a worry in the world and in the dictionary, ااَلهُجَعَةis said to be light sleep in the first part of the night abut it doesn’t sit right because in the same dictionary,اَلهُجَعُmeans stupid and someone who sleeps for long hours and also the former meaning is not endorsed by the usage in the Quran. So, the former meaning holds a stronger stance but هجوعis exclusive for sleeping at night as قيلولهis for the afternoon nap.
كَانُواْ قَلِيلاً۬ مِّنَ ٱلَّيۡلِ مَا يَہۡجَعُونَ (﻿١٧﻿) وَبِٱلۡأَسۡحَارِ هُمۡ يَسۡتَغۡفِرُونَ
“They used to sleep but little of the night, (17) And ere the dawning of each day would seek forgiveness”
51:17
3- رَقَدَ
It means to sleep for long hours and اَلرَّقَادmeans light and comforting sleep. الرقدةand اليرقودmeans one who sleeps long hours and الرقودis one who is always sleeping. All of the above converge to a conclusion thatرَقدis a kind of sleep which is long, light, comforting, hence, a person could easily wake up from it.
وَتَحۡسَبُہُمۡ أَيۡقَاظً۬ا وَهُمۡ رُقُودٌ۬*ۚ
“And thou wouldst have deemed them waking though they were asleep”     18:18
4- يَقِيلُوقَيلاً وَ قَيلُوله – قَالَ
It means the afternoon nap and to have a kip in the daytime.
وَكَم مِّن قَرۡيَةٍ أَهۡلَكۡنَـٰهَا فَجَآءَهَا بَأۡسُنَا بَيَـٰتًا أَوۡ هُمۡ قَآٮِٕلُونَ
“How many a township have We destroyed! As a raid by night, or while they slept at noon, Our terror came unto them”     7:4
5- ضَجَعَ
To lie down on the side, to nap, to slumber and مَضَاجِعmeans bed or bedding and اَضجَعَهَmeans to put to bed.
تَتَجَافَىٰ جُنُوبُهُمۡ عَنِ ٱلۡمَضَاجِعِ يَدۡعُونَ رَبَّہُمۡ خَوۡفً۬ا وَطَمَعً۬ا
“Who forsake their beds to cry unto their Lord in fear and hope”     32:16
6- تَهَجَّدَ
هجود     means to sleep and to wake up at night, to sleep part and to wake up at some part and spend the night in these 2 states and هَجَّدَmeans to offer salat after waking up at night.
وَمِنَ ٱلَّيۡلِ فَتَهَجَّدۡ بِهِۦ نَافِلَةً۬ لَّكَ
“And some part of the night awake for it     “ 17:79
Inference
1- نََامَ: Common word for sleeping
2- هَجَعَ: Deep and in-cognisant sleep
3- رَقَدَ: Long and light sleep
4- قَالَ: Afternoon nap
5- ضَجَعَ: To lie down on the side for a kip, whether it is for sleeping or not
6- تَهَجَّدَ: To sleep and wake at night

تَتَجَافَىٰ جُنُوبُهُمۡ عَنِ ٱلۡمَضَاجِعِ يَدۡعُونَ رَبَّہُمۡ خَوۡفً۬ا وَطَمَعً۬ا 

“Who forsake their beds to cry unto their Lord in fear and hope” 32:16

6- تَهَجَّدَ

هجود means to sleep and to wake up at night, to sleep part and to wake up at some part and spend the night in these 2 states and هَجَّدَmeans to offer salat after waking up at night.

وَمِنَ ٱلَّيۡلِ فَتَهَجَّدۡ بِهِۦ نَافِلَةً۬ لَّكَ 

“And some part of the night awake for it “ 17:79

Inference 

1- نََامَ: Common word for sleeping

2- هَجَعَ: Deep and in-cognisant sleep

3- رَقَدَ: Long and light sleep

4- قَالَ: Afternoon nap

5- ضَجَعَ: To lie down on the side for a kip, whether it is for sleeping or not

6- تَهَجَّدَ: To sleep and wake at night

Black – Blackness
For this, the Quran uses the words اَسوَدَ, غَرَابِيب, اَحوِي, مُد هَامَّتََاند هم (دَهم), قَتَرَةَ,مِدَاد
1- اَسوَدَ
It is the black colour (Ant:     اَبيَض) and is a common use word. (Pl:سُود) (Fem:سَودََأ)
وَكُلُواْ وَٱشۡرَبُواْ حَتَّىٰ يَتَبَيَّنَ لَكُمُ ٱلۡخَيۡطُ ٱلۡأَبۡيَضُ مِنَ ٱلۡخَيۡطِ ٱلۡأَسۡوَدِ مِنَ ٱلۡفَجۡرِ*ۖ
“And eat and drink until the white thread becometh distinct to you from the black thread of the dawn     “ 2:187
2- غَرَابِيب
غُرَاب     is the crow and غِربِيبis as black as the crow and غُربِيبis a person who dies his hair black. (Pl:غَرَابِيب)
وَمِنَ ٱلۡجِبَالِ جُدَدُۢ بِيضٌ۬ وَحُمۡرٌ۬ مُّخۡتَلِفٌ أَلۡوَٲنُہَا وَغَرَابِيبُ سُودٌ۬
“And among the hills are streaks white and red, of divers hues, and (others) raven-black”     35:27
3- اَحوِي
A blackish dark green or a blackish red colour. Quran usesغُثَآءً أَحۡوَىٰ
غُثَا     is the rubbish made up of twigs and leaves that forms in the foam of river water and and lands on the bank and when rubbish is trampled upon and the colour becomes blackish then that colour is called اَحوِي
فَجَعَلَهُۥ غُثَآءً أَحۡوَىٰ
“Then turneth it to russet stubble”     87:5
4- اَدهَم
دَهَمَ     is to drown in darkness and اَلدَّهمَةmeans blackness and دَهَّمَتِ النَّارََُالقِدرmeans that the fire has blackened the cooking pot.
مُدۡهَآمَّتَانِ
“Dark green with foliage     “ 55:64
5- قَتَرَةَ
قَتَرَالنََّار     means a sooty fire and قَتَرَةَmeans black like smoke, dark and dusty.
وَوُجُوهٌ۬ يَوۡمَٮِٕذٍ عَلَيۡہَا غَبَرَةٌ۬ (﻿٤٠﻿) تَرۡهَقُهَا قَتَرَةٌ
“And other faces, on that day, with dust upon them, (40) Veiled in darkness” 80:40-41
6- مِدَاد
مَدَدتُ     الدَّوَاةmeans to pour ink into the ink pot and مِدَادis the ink which is used in writing.
قُل لَّوۡ كَانَ ٱلۡبَحۡرُ مِدَادً۬ا لِّكَلِمَـٰتِ رَبِّى لَنَفِدَ ٱلۡبَحۡرُ قَبۡلَ أَن تَنفَدَ كَلِمَـٰتُ رَبِّى وَلَوۡ جِئۡنَا بِمِثۡلِهِۦ مَدَدً۬ا
“Say: Though the sea became ink for the Words of my Lord, verily the sea would be used up before the words of my Lord were exhausted, even though We brought the like thereof to help”     18:109
Inference
1- اَسوَدَ: Black colour, opposite of white
2- غَرَابِيب: Deep black colour
3- اَحوِي: Greenish black
4- اَدهَم: Blackish green
5- قَتَرَةَ: Smoky colour
6- مِدَاد: Ink

raw_text:
سیدھا سیدھی   - Straight
These words مستقيم سواء (سوى) قصد سديد  have been used in the Quran
1.             مستقيم –   قام على الامر  means to stay firm and to continue as before, and اقام الشئ means to stand something up and to straighten it and   مستقيم   is something which is straight and moderate, even.
In Surah Israa: (17:35):
وَزِنُوا بِالْقِسْطَاسِ الْمُسْتَقِيمِ ۚ
and weigh with an even balance
This is because the beam of the scale is always straight.  If this beam is not straight then the weighing will not be balanced correctly.  The beam of the scale is always straight even if one side of the scale is lower down;  therefore here “to be straight” means as well as horizontal, it can also be like the different positions of the beam, regardless of the balance on either side. According to geometry the minimal difference between two points, two places is called خط مستقیم, so to say صراط مستقیم  is that straight path which has no crease and  bend, free from excessiveness and lower extremity. In the Quran we have been taught this prayer:
In Surah Faatiha: (1:4):
اهْدِنَا الصِّرَاطَ الْمُسْتَقِيمَ
Guide us to the straight path.
2.          سواء (سوى)   – (sawaa & Saweeyya) – سوى يسوى (saweya yaswee)-  be corrected and   سوى   (sawwaa) to correct, straighten something and   سوى   (Saweeyya) means  straight, correct , healthy.
In Surah Maryam: (19:17):
فَتَمَثَّلَ لَهَا بَشَرًا سَوِيًّا
and he represented himself to her as a well-proportioned man.
And صراطا سويا means a path, which is straight, balanced and even. No inequality, highs or lows, no bends.
In Surah Maryam: (19:43):
فَاتَّبِعْنِي أَهْدِكَ صِرَاطًا سَوِيًّا
so follow me; I will guide you to an even path.
The word   سواء   is used for equal and even. If this evenness from both sides is according to the distance or number then the word وسط is used, but if the evenness is according to all things and sides then the word   سواء   is used, therefore it means centre point, middle point.
In Surah Dukhaan:  (44:47):
خُذُوهُ فَاعْتِلُوهُ إِلَىٰ سَوَاءِ الْجَحِيمِ
[It will be commanded], "Seize him and drag him into the midst of the Hellfire,
And سواء السبيل  means a straight path which comes out leaving behind all base acts, all misguidance and paganism.
In Surah Qasas: (28:22):
وَلَمَّا تَوَجَّهَ تِلْقَاءَ مَدْيَنَ قَالَ عَسَىٰ رَبِّي أَن يَهْدِيَنِي سَوَاءَ السَّبِيلِ
And when he directed himself toward Madyan, he said, "Perhaps my Lord will guide me to the sound way."
3.              قصد-   to use something in a permissible manner ie      If a man can have a bath in one bucket of water, then to use one bucket of water for a bath is   قصد.  T  o use more than one bucket is   اسراف – excessive,  and to use less than a bucket is بخل - miser. To consider this in each situation and to make it in to a habit is called اقتصاد.
Now looking at the meaning not all things and matters are the same, sometimes you have to be harsh, sometimes soft, to attain or reach a certain goal, aim and destination and to elaborate on this, is the function of Islamic jurisprudence.
In Surah An-Nahl: (16:9):
وَعَلَى اللَّهِ قَصْدُ السَّبِيلِ وَمِنْهَا جَائِرٌ
And upon Allah is the direction of the [right] way, and among the various paths are those deviating.
When the word   قصد   is translated with ‘central or even’ the connotation is not correct. That is why it is translated with ‘straight’.
4.              سديد  - سد   (sadd)   means barrier, or wall which is made between two objects and    سد   (sadda)   means to fill the crack with stones and سداد means the mixture which you put on cracks and holes ie cement. قول سديد  - speech which has no faults, defects or mistakes:  sound and truthful speech, that has integrity, the opposite is قول الزور which means much more than just  a lie.
In Surah Nisaa: (4:9):
فَلْيَتَّقُوا اللَّهَ وَلْيَقُولُوا قَوْلًا سَدِيدًا
So let them fear Allah and speak words of appropriate justice.
Summary:
1.          مستقيم    - even ,equal and straight
2.            (سوى)   level, straight and correct and   سواء   – something that passes in the middle and straight
3.          قصد  - someone who correctly defines the values and it is free from excessive and lower extremity.
4.          سديد  -  an object which has no cracks faults , strong, clean and straight.

28: Cause Travel:
Sayyara   سيَّر   & Asraa   اسرى    are the words used.   They have a prominent difference in them. If this travel/outing is at night time, then asraa   اسرى    is used. Asraa   اسرى    means to travel during night.
In the Quran: 17:1 : Surat Al-'Isrā' (The Night Journey) -   سورة الإسراء
سُبْحَانَ الَّذِي أَسْرَىٰ بِعَبْدِهِ لَيْلًا مِّنَ الْمَسْجِدِ الْحَرَامِ إِلَى الْمَسْجِدِ الْأَقْصَى الَّذِي بَارَكْنَا حَوْلَهُ لِنُرِيَهُ مِنْ آيَاتِنَا   ۚ   إِنَّهُ هُوَ السَّمِيعُ الْبَصِيرُ
Exalted is He who took His Servant by night from al-Masjid al-Haram to al-Masjid al- Aqsa, whose surroundings We have blessed, to show him of Our signs. Indeed, He is the Hearing, the Seeing.
& if this travel/outing is at day time, then sayyar    سيَّر   is used. So sayyar   سيَّر   is a common word & asraa   اسرى    is a special word.
As in Quran: 10:22: Surat Yūnus (Jonah) -   سورة يونس
هُوَ الَّذِي يُسَيِّرُكُمْ فِي الْبَرِّ وَالْبَحْرِ ۖ حَتَّىٰ إِذَا كُنتُمْ فِي الْفُلْكِ وَجَرَيْنَ بِهِم بِرِيحٍ طَيِّبَةٍ وَفَرِحُوا بِهَا جَاءَتْهَا رِيحٌ عَاصِفٌ وَجَاءَهُمُ الْمَوْجُ مِن كُلِّ مَكَانٍ وَظَنُّوا أَنَّهُمْ أُحِيطَ بِهِمْ ۙ دَعَوُا اللَّهَ مُخْلِصِينَ لَهُ الدِّينَ لَئِنْ أَنجَيْتَنَا مِنْ هَٰذِهِ لَنَكُونَنَّ مِنَ الشَّاكِرِينَ
It is He who enables you to travel on land and sea until, when you are in ships and they sail with them by a good wind and they rejoice therein, there comes a storm wind and the waves come upon them from everywhere and they assume that they are surrounded, supplicating Allah , sincere to Him in religion, "If You should save us from this, we will surely be among the thankful."

هُوَ الَّذِي يُسَيِّرُكُمْ فِي الْبَرِّ وَالْبَحْرِ ۖ حَتَّىٰ إِذَا كُنتُمْ فِي الْفُلْكِ وَجَرَيْنَ بِهِم بِرِيحٍ طَيِّبَةٍ وَفَرِحُوا بِهَا جَاءَتْهَا رِيحٌ عَاصِفٌ وَجَاءَهُمُ الْمَوْجُ مِن كُلِّ مَكَانٍ وَظَنُّوا أَنَّهُمْ أُحِيطَ بِهِمْ ۙ دَعَوُا اللَّهَ مُخْلِصِينَ لَهُ الدِّينَ لَئِنْ أَنجَيْتَنَا مِنْ هَٰذِهِ لَنَكُونَنَّ مِنَ الشَّاكِرِينَ

It is He who enables you to travel on land and sea until, when you are in ships and they sail with them by a good wind and they rejoice therein, there comes a storm wind and the waves come upon them from everywhere and they assume that they are surrounded, supplicating Allah , sincere to Him in religion, "If You should save us from this, we will surely be among the thankful."

29. Ladder:
Sullam     سُلَّم  , & Maa’arij    معارج   are the words used.
1.            Sullam    سُلَّم   :  This word is used as a replacement for maa’arij   معارج   or meiraaj    معراج  . So Sullam    سُلَّم   is used for both a stairway made of bricks & cement in the house or the wooden ladder . Sallam    سُلَّم   is a word used for anything that helps in reaching the top of something. ( plural is salalam    سلالم   or salaleem   سلاليم   ) Adraajus sullam     ادراجُ السُّلم   means the wooden planks of the ladder.
As per the Quran: 6:35 : Surat Al-'An`ām (The Cattle) -   سورة الأنعام
وَإِن كَانَ كَبُرَ عَلَيْكَ إِعْرَاضُهُمْ فَإِنِ اسْتَطَعْتَ أَن تَبْتَغِيَ نَفَقًا فِي الْأَرْضِ أَوْ سُلَّمًا فِي السَّمَاءِ فَتَأْتِيَهُم بِآيَةٍ ۚ وَلَوْ شَاءَ اللَّهُ لَجَمَعَهُمْ عَلَى الْهُدَىٰ ۚ فَلَا تَكُونَنَّ مِنَ الْجَاهِلِينَ
And if their evasion is difficult for you, then if you are able to seek a tunnel into the earth or a stairway into the sky to bring them a sign, [then do so]. But if Allah had willed, He would have united them upon guidance. So never be of the ignorant.
2.            Maa’arij    معارج   : This is the plural of mairaaj    معراج  . Araja   عَرَجَ   means to limp. & aaraj   اَعرَج   means disabled( without leg/legs). Araja fes sulm   عَرَجَ فى السُلَّم    means to step on the ladder/climb. Mairaaj   معراج     means ladder/stairway or a place to climb.So mairaaj    معراج    is derived from sullam    سُلَّم   . & it has the idea of reaching some high place or top with the help of a ladder/stairway. Whereas sullam     سُلَّم   is only used for ladder/stairway.
As per the Quran:43:32: Surat Az-Zukhruf (The Ornaments of Gold) -   سورة الزخرف
وَلَوْلَا أَن يَكُونَ النَّاسُ أُمَّةً وَاحِدَةً لَّجَعَلْنَا لِمَن يَكْفُرُ بِالرَّحْمَٰنِ لِبُيُوتِهِمْ سُقُفًا مِّن فِضَّةٍ وَمَعَارِجَ عَلَيْهَا يَظْهَرُونَ
And if it were not that the people would become one community [of disbelievers], We would have made for those who disbelieve in the Most Merciful - for their houses - ceilings and stairways of silver upon which to mount

3 SAAL
[Year]
Synonyms: AAM, SINEEN, HAUL, HIJJAJ
3.1 aam(  عَامٌ۬  )  : (pl: awaam (  عوام  )) the year that has amplitude and abundance meaning the year of peace and prosperity. It is stated in the Quran:
________________
Surat Yousuf (Joseph) -   سُوۡرَةُ یُوسُف
12:49
ثُمَّ     يَأۡتِى     مِنۢ     بَعۡدِ     ذَٲلِكَ     عَامٌ۬     فِيهِ     يُغَاثُ     ٱلنَّاسُ     وَفِيهِ     يَعۡصِرُونَ
Then, after that, will come a year when the people will have plenteous crops and when they will press (wine and oil)
________________
Similarly, the word aam is also used as a prayer. On occasions of Eid, instead of saying Eid Mubarak, people of Arab greet each other by saying
أنتم و كل عام
Meaning we wish and pray that your year ahead passes with peace and prosperity.
3.2 sanata (  سَنَةٍ  ) (pl. sineen) (  سِّنِينَ  ):   the year of hardships. This word has been used for depicting difficulty, drought and starvation. Allah states that:
________________
Surat al-A’raf (The Heights) -   سُوۡرَةُ     الاٴعرَاف
7:130
وَلَقَدۡ أَخَذۡنَآ ءَالَ فِرۡعَوۡنَ بِٱلسِّنِينَ وَنَقۡصٍ۬ مِّنَ ٱلثَّمَرَٲتِ لَعَلَّهُمۡ يَذَّڪَّرُونَ
And we straitened Pharaoh's folk with famine and dearth of fruits, that peradventure they might heed.
________________
And in the following ayah:
________________
Surat al-Ankaboot (The Spider) -   سُوۡرَةُ العَنکبوت
29:14
فَلَبِثَ فِيهِمۡ أَلۡفَ سَنَةٍ إِلَّا خَمۡسِينَ عَامً۬ا
And verily we sent Noah (as Our messenger) unto his folk,   and he continued with them for a thousand years save fifty years  ; and the flood engulfed them, for they were wrong-doers.
________________
the nine hundred and fifty years that Hazrat Noah passed in hardships against his nation, they have been described by the word sineen. And the fifty years prior to nabuwwat, when there weren’t any hardships or fights, have been described by the word aam. And to keep track of chronology or time and era, the word sanata has been used which also shows that days of prosperity are usually less than days of difficulty and distress. It is stated in the Quran:
________________
Surat Yunus (Jonah) -   سُوۡرَةُ یُونس
10:5
هُوَ ٱلَّذِى جَعَلَ ٱلشَّمۡسَ ضِيَآءً۬ وَٱلۡقَمَرَ نُورً۬ا وَقَدَّرَهُ ۥ مَنَازِلَ لِتَعۡلَمُواْ عَدَدَ ٱلسِّنِينَ وَٱلۡحِسَابَ‌ۚ
He it is Who appointed the sun a splendour and the moon a light, and measured for her stages, that ye might know the number of the years, and the reckoning.   Allah created not (all) that save in truth. He detaileth the revelations for people who have knowledge.
________________
3.3 haul(haal)(  حَوۡلِ  )  : meaning change from one state to another (haal pl halaat) Halaat-u-dahar(  حالات الدهر  ) meaning passing of day and night, revolutions of time and haal-ul-haul(  حال الحول  ) meaning passing of a period of one year and haul meaning the complete cycle of a year i.e. the period of time from a specific date of a year till the same date of next year is called haul. Zakat Is also given according to haul. The matters of breastfeeding and divorce are also in accordance with haul. It is stated in the Quran:
________________
Surat Al-Baqarah (The Cow) -   سورة البقرة
2:240
وَصِيَّةً۬ لِّأَزۡوَٲجِهِم مَّتَـٰعًا إِلَى ٱلۡحَوۡلِ غَيۡرَ إِخۡرَاجٍ۬‌ۚ
(In the case of) those of you who are about to die and leave behind them wives,   they should bequeath unto their wives a provision for the year without turning them out  , but if they go out (of their own accord) there is no sin for you in that which they do of themselves within their rights. Allah is Mighty, Wise.
________________
3.4 hijaj(sg: hajjah)(  حِجَج  )  : meaning to come and go repeatedly, to travel frequently. Hajjah(  حجة  ) is derived from the word hajj(  حج  ); and because hajj occurs once each year, a year is sometimes referred to as hajj. In earlier times when there were no calendars and no proper way of keeping track of days, months and years, people usually counted years on the basis of hajj. It is stated in the Quran:
________________
Surat Al-Qasas (The Story) -   سُوۡرَةُ القَصَص
28:27
إِنِّىٓ أُرِيدُ أَنۡ أُنكِحَكَ إِحۡدَى ٱبۡنَتَىَّ هَـٰتَيۡنِ عَلَىٰٓ أَن تَأۡجُرَنِى ثَمَـٰنِىَ حِجَجٍ۬‌ۖ
He said  : Lo! I fain would marry thee to one of these two daughters of mine on condition that thou hirest thyself to me for (the term of) eight pilgrimages  . Then if thou completest ten it will be of thine own accord, for I would not make it hard for thee. Allah willing, thou wilt find me of the righteous.
________________
Summary:
1. AAM: the year of peace and prosperity
2. SANAH: the year of drought and starvation
3. HAUL: A complete cycle of year from a specific date, according to lunar calculations.
4. HIJJAJ: The rough way of counting years.
Year
The words عم )عام , ( سنو) سِنِين, حول, حج) have been used.
1- عَام
عَامis considered a year of prosperity and thriving. It says in the Quran:
ثُمَّ يَأۡتِى مِنۢ بَعۡدِ ذَٲلِكَ عَامٌ۬ فِيهِ يُغَاثُ ٱلنَّاسُ وَفِيهِ يَعۡصِرُونَ
“Then, after that, will come a year when the people will have plenteous crops and when they will press (wine and oil)” 12/49
In a similar context, the word عَام has been used as a word of دعَا or prayer. The Arabs used to greet each other on Eid with a prayer saying:
اَنتُم وَّ كُلَّ عََامٍ بِخَير
“May this year bring you peace and tranquillity”
2- سَنَة(Pl: سِنِين)
It means a year of adversity. Also, the same word has been used for drought and famine.
وَلَقَدۡ أَخَذۡنَآ ءَالَ فِرۡعَوۡنَ بِٱلسِّنِينَ
“And we straitened Pharaoh's folk with famine and dearth“ 7/130
فَلَبِثَ فِيهِمۡ أَلۡفَ سَنَةٍ إِلَّا خَمۡسِينَ عَامً۬ا
“He continued with them for a thousand years save fifty years“ 29/14
In this ayah, the 950 years that Nooh (Noah) spent amongst his people in extreme hardship and opposition have been denoted by the word سِنِينand the 50 years before prophet hood, where there was no opposition from his people are denoted by عَام.
The word سنةis normally used to keep and account of time or a period which also points towards the fact that the periods of prosperity are normally a lot less than the periods of adversity.
هُوَ ٱلَّذِى جَعَلَ ٱلشَّمۡسَ ضِيَآءً۬ وَٱلۡقَمَرَ نُورً۬ا وَقَدَّرَهُ ۥ مَنَازِلَ لِتَعۡلَمُواْ عَدَدَ ٱلسِّنِينَ وَٱلۡحِسَابَ*ۚ
“He it is Who appointed the sun a splendour and the moon a light, and measured for her stages, that ye might know the number of the years” 10/5
3- حول
حَالَmeans the transition of times from one state to another. (حَال Pl: حَالاَت).
حََالاَت الدَّهَرmeans the passing of days or transition from day to day. حال الحولmeans the passing of a year and حولmeans one complete rotation of the year from one particular date in a year to the next time or date after one full year. زكوةis calculated and paid by حولand divorce and the period of suckling are also determined by it.
وَصِيَّةً۬ لِّأَزۡوَٲجِهِم مَّتَـٰعًا إِلَى ٱلۡحَوۡلِ غَيۡرَ إِخۡرَاجٍ۬*ۚ
“They should bequeath unto their wives a provision for the year without turning them out” 2/240
4- حِجّج(sing: حَجَّة)
It means something that comes again and again, some even that repeats, that comes a lot and because Hajj comes once a year, every year, hence the year is called Hajj. In old times there were no calendars to account for days, months or even years so people, would commonly count years with reference to the number of Hajjs.
قَالَ إِنِّىٓ أُرِيدُ أَنۡ أُنكِحَكَ إِحۡدَى ٱبۡنَتَىَّ هَـٰتَيۡنِ عَلَىٰٓ أَن تَأۡجُرَنِى ثَمَـٰنِىَ حِجَجٍ۬*ۖ
“He said: Lo! I fain would marry thee to one of these two daughters of mine on condition that thou hirest thyself to me for (the term of) eight pilgrimages” 28/27
Inference
1- عَام  : The year of prosperity
2- حول  : A whole rotation of the year, starting from a particular date (lunar)
3- سَنَةَ  : The year of drought
4- حِجَج  : A common way of counting years

“May this year bring you peace and tranquillity”

2- سَنَة(Pl: سِنِين)

It means a year of adversity. Also, the same word has been used for drought and famine.

وَلَقَدۡ أَخَذۡنَآ ءَالَ فِرۡعَوۡنَ بِٱلسِّنِينَ

“And we straitened Pharaoh's folk with famine and dearth“ 7/130

فَلَبِثَ فِيهِمۡ أَلۡفَ سَنَةٍ إِلَّا خَمۡسِينَ عَامً۬ا

“He continued with them for a thousand years save fifty years“ 29/14

In this ayah, the 950 years that Nooh (Noah) spent amongst his people in extreme hardship and opposition have been denoted by the word سِنِينand the 50 years before prophet hood, where there was no opposition from his people are denoted by عَام.

The word سنةis normally used to keep and account of time or a period which also points towards the fact that the periods of prosperity are normally a lot less than the periods of adversity.

هُوَ ٱلَّذِى جَعَلَ ٱلشَّمۡسَ ضِيَآءً۬ وَٱلۡقَمَرَ نُورً۬ا وَقَدَّرَهُ ۥ مَنَازِلَ لِتَعۡلَمُواْ عَدَدَ ٱلسِّنِينَ وَٱلۡحِسَابَ*ۚ

“He it is Who appointed the sun a splendour and the moon a light, and measured for her stages, that ye might know the number of the years” 10/5

3- حول

حَالَmeans the transition of times from one state to another. (حَال Pl: حَالاَت).

حََالاَت الدَّهَرmeans the passing of days or transition from day to day. حال الحولmeans the passing of a year and حولmeans one complete rotation of the year from one particular date in a year to the next time or date after one full year. زكوةis calculated and paid by حولand divorce and the period of suckling are also determined by it.

وَصِيَّةً۬ لِّأَزۡوَٲجِهِم مَّتَـٰعًا إِلَى ٱلۡحَوۡلِ غَيۡرَ إِخۡرَاجٍ۬*ۚ

“They should bequeath unto their wives a provision for the year without turning them out” 2/240

4- حِجّج(sing: حَجَّة)

It means something that comes again and again, some even that repeats, that comes a lot and because Hajj comes once a year, every year, hence the year is called Hajj. In old times there were no calendars to account for days, months or even years so people, would commonly count years with reference to the number of Hajjs.

قَالَ إِنِّىٓ أُرِيدُ أَنۡ أُنكِحَكَ إِحۡدَى ٱبۡنَتَىَّ هَـٰتَيۡنِ عَلَىٰٓ أَن تَأۡجُرَنِى ثَمَـٰنِىَ حِجَجٍ۬*ۖ

“He said: Lo! I fain would marry thee to one of these two daughters of mine on condition that thou hirest thyself to me for (the term of) eight pilgrimages” 28/27

Inference

1- عَام: The year of prosperity

2- حول: A whole rotation of the year, starting from a particular date (lunar)

3- سَنَةَ: The year of drought

4- حِجَج: A common way of counting years

30. To learn/teach:
Taa’allam   تعَلَّم   ,allam   عَلَّم   ,talaqqa    تَلَقَّى  , kallab   كَلَّب   are the words used.
1.            Ta’allam   تعَلَّم   : alima means to find out /learn about something & find the truth about something. Allama   عَلَّم  means to repeatedly tell something to someone,teach them. & taa’allam    تعَلَّم   means to gradually absorb the teachings or gradually learn.
As per the Quran: 2:31 : Surat Al-Baqarah (The Cow) -   سورة البقرة
وَعَلَّمَ آدَمَ الْأَسْمَاءَ كُلَّهَا ثُمَّ عَرَضَهُمْ عَلَى الْمَلَائِكَةِ فَقَالَ أَنبِئُونِي بِأَسْمَاءِ هَٰؤُلَاءِ إِن كُنتُمْ صَادِقِينَ
And He taught Adam the names - all of them. Then He showed them to the angels and said, "Inform Me of the names of these, if you are truthful."
In another verse: 2:102: Surat Al-Baqarah (The Cow) -   سورة البقرة
وَاتَّبَعُوا مَا تَتْلُو الشَّيَاطِينُ عَلَىٰ مُلْكِ سُلَيْمَانَ ۖ وَمَا كَفَرَ سُلَيْمَانُ وَلَٰكِنَّ الشَّيَاطِينَ كَفَرُوا يُعَلِّمُونَ النَّاسَ السِّحْرَ وَمَا أُنزِلَ عَلَى الْمَلَكَيْنِ بِبَابِلَ هَارُوتَ وَمَارُوتَ ۚ وَمَا يُعَلِّمَانِ مِنْ أَحَدٍ حَتَّىٰ يَقُولَا إِنَّمَا نَحْنُ فِتْنَةٌ فَلَا تَكْفُرْ ۖ فَيَتَعَلَّمُونَ مِنْهُمَا مَا يُفَرِّقُونَ بِهِ بَيْنَ الْمَرْءِ وَزَوْجِهِ ۚ وَمَا هُم بِضَارِّينَ بِهِ مِنْ أَحَدٍ إِلَّا بِإِذْنِ اللَّهِ ۚ وَيَتَعَلَّمُونَ مَا يَضُرُّهُمْ وَلَا يَنفَعُهُمْ ۚ وَلَقَدْ عَلِمُوا لَمَنِ اشْتَرَاهُ مَا لَهُ فِي الْآخِرَةِ مِنْ خَلَاقٍ ۚ وَلَبِئْسَ مَا شَرَوْا بِهِ أَنفُسَهُمْ ۚ لَوْ كَانُوا يَعْلَمُونَ
And they followed [instead] what the devils had recited during the reign of Solomon. It was not Solomon who disbelieved, but the devils disbelieved, teaching people magic and that which was revealed to the two angels at Babylon, Harut and Marut. But the two angels do not teach anyone unless they say, "We are a trial, so do not disbelieve [by practicing magic]." And [yet] they learn from them that by which they cause separation between a man and his wife. But they do not harm anyone through it except by permission of Allah . And the people learn what harms them and does not benefit them. But the Children of Israel certainly knew that whoever purchased the magic would not have in the Hereafter any share. And wretched is that for which they sold themselves, if they only knew.
2.            Tallaqa   تَلَقَّى   : laqee means to meet, to see, to get. Tallaqqa    تَلَقَّى  means to welcome someone. Talaqqash shaee minhu    تَلَقَّى الشَّىىء مِنهُ   means to learn something from someone. Talaqqa   تَلَقَّى  /alqaa   القاء   means to learn when something gets in the heart.
As per the Quran: 2:37: Surat Al-Baqarah (The Cow) -   سورة البقرة
فَتَلَقَّىٰ آدَمُ مِن رَّبِّهِ كَلِمَاتٍ فَتَابَ عَلَيْهِ ۚ إِنَّهُ هُوَ التَّوَّابُ الرَّحِيمُ
Then Adam received from his Lord [some] words, and He accepted his repentance. Indeed, it is He who is the Accepting of repentance, the Merciful.
3.            Kallaba   كَلَّب  : kalb means dog.  & kallabal kalb     كَلَّبَ الكَلب   means to teach a dog to hunt & train him. Muqallib   مُكلِّب   & kallab   كلَّاب   refers to that person who trains to hunt. & kallab  كَلَّب    not only means teaching dogs but also other hunting animals or birds etc.
Allah says in the Quran:5:4 : Surat Al-Mā'idah (The Table Spread) -   سورة المائدة
يَسْأَلُونَكَ مَاذَا أُحِلَّ لَهُمْ ۖ قُلْ أُحِلَّ لَكُمُ الطَّيِّبَاتُ ۙ وَمَا عَلَّمْتُم مِّنَ الْجَوَارِحِ مُكَلِّبِينَ تُعَلِّمُونَهُنَّ مِمَّا عَلَّمَكُمُ اللَّهُ ۖ فَكُلُوا مِمَّا أَمْسَكْنَ عَلَيْكُمْ وَاذْكُرُوا اسْمَ اللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ ۖ وَاتَّقُوا اللَّهَ ۚ إِنَّ اللَّهَ سَرِيعُ الْحِسَابِ
They ask you, [O Muhammad], what has been made lawful for them. Say, "Lawful for you are [all] good foods and [game caught by] what you have trained of hunting animals which you train as Allah has taught you. So eat of what they catch for you, and mention the name of Allah upon it, and fear Allah ." Indeed, Allah is swift in account.
Summary  :
1. Allama   عَلَّم  : to teach someone & taa’allam   تعَلَّم   means to learn
2.Tallaqqa    تَلَقَّى  . To learn something via alqaa ( when something gets in the heart)
3. Kallab   كَلَّب   : to teach /train hunting animals & bird etc.

title: content/s/s4.html
raw_text:
4 SAMAAN
[Luggage, belongings, provision]
Synonyms: ARZ, MATAA’, ASAAS, RAHAL, WIA’A, JAHAZ, ZAAD(ZOD), ASLIHAAH, UDDAH, NA’AMA, REESH, BIDA’A, MA’OON(MA’AN), HIZR, MA’AISH,
4.1 arz(  عَرَضَ  )  : all those things which are not eternal. Meaning that everything from this world’s belongings are arz. When one wants to shed light on the non-permanence and fragility of this world and its belongings, then the word arz will be used, the material gains of this world and its belongings. Allah states that:
________________
Surat An-Nisa (Women) -   سُوۡرَةُ النِّسَاء
4:94
وَلَا تَقُولُواْ لِمَنۡ أَلۡقَىٰٓ إِلَيۡڪُمُ ٱلسَّلَـٰمَ لَسۡتَ مُؤۡمِنً۬ا تَبۡتَغُونَ عَرَضَ ٱلۡحَيَوٰةِ ٱلدُّنۡيَا فَعِندَ ٱللَّهِ مَغَانِمُ ڪَثِيرَةٌ۬‌ۚ
O ye who believe! When ye go forth (to fight) in the way of Allah, be careful to discriminate,   and say not unto one who offereth you peace: "Thou art not a believer," seeking the chance profits of this life (so that ye may despoil him). With Allah are plenteous spoils.   Even thus (as he now is) were ye before; but Allah hath since then been gracious unto you. Therefore take care to discriminate. Allah is ever Informed of what ye do.
________________
4.2 mataa’ (  مَتَـٰعٌ  )(pl: amtia’a(  أمتعة  ))  : mata’a(  متع  ) meaning to gain benefit till a long time and mataa’(  متاع  ) means every beneficial thing or that part of a thing which can be of benefit, advantage, to take advantage of the belongings of this world. To shed light on this world’s belongings and benefitting from them, then this word is used. Allah states that:
________________
Surat Al-Baqarah (The Cow) -   سُوۡرَةُ البَقَرَة
2:36
وَلَكُمۡ فِى ٱلۡأَرۡضِ مُسۡتَقَرٌّ۬ وَمَتَـٰعٌ إِلَىٰ حِينٍ۬
But Satan caused them to deflect therefrom and expelled them from the (happy) state in which they were; and We said: Fall down, one of you a foe unto the other!   There shall be for you on earth a habitation and provision for a time.
________________
4.3 asaas(  أَثَـٰثً۬ا  )  : asaas is the plural of asaasa but it is usually used as a plural such as the noted word asaas-ul-bait(  أثاث البيت  ) meaning domestic equipment that is being used. Household equipment such as crockery, bed, clothes, furniture etc all these are included in asaas-ul-bait. Then this word got started to be used for useless and extra merchandise. And also used for shops and junkyards. Moreover, that animal or slave who is under the authority or personal use of someone is also included in asaas-ul-bait such as horse, cow, camel etc. Allah states that:
________________
Surat Maryam (Mary) -   سُوۡرَةُ مَریَم
19:74
وَكَمۡ أَهۡلَكۡنَا قَبۡلَهُم مِّن قَرۡنٍ هُمۡ أَحۡسَنُ أَثَـٰثً۬ا وَرِءۡيً۬ا
How many a generation have We destroyed before them, who were more imposing in respect of gear and outward seeming!
________________
4.4 rahal(  رَحۡلِ  )  : rahala means to saddle a camel, to travel, to ride and rahal means the luggage during a journey. The word rahala is used to describe taking off on a journey. Prophet Muhammad (PBUH) stated that:
لا تشدد الرجال إلا لثلاثة
meaning that apart from the three mosques (Bait-ullah, Prophet PBUH’s mosque and Aqsa mosque), do not saddle your camels for any other place (for pilgrimage and reward). It is stated in the Quran:
________________
Surat Yusuf (Joseph) -   سُوۡرَةُ یُوسُف
12:70
جَعَلَ ٱلسِّقَايَةَ فِى رَحۡلِ أَخِيهِ
And when he provided them with their provision,   he put the drinking-cup in his brother's saddlebag  , and then a crier cried: O camel-riders! Lo! ye are surely thieves!
________________
4.5 wia’a(  وِعَا  )(sg: auiya(  اوعيه  )):   wa’a(  وى  ) meaning to protect something by placing in a bag and tying its top part and auiyah(  اوعيه  ) is that thing which is placed in a safe and locked shut. It is stated in the Quran:
________________
Surat Yusuf (Joseph) -   سُوۡرَةُ یُوسُف
12:76
ثُمَّ ٱسۡتَخۡرَجَهَا مِن وِعَآءِ أَخِيهِ‌ۚ
Then he (Joseph) began the search with their bags before his brother's bag,   then he produced it from his brother's bag  . Thus did We contrive for Joseph. He could not have taken his brother according to the king's law unless Allah willed. We raise by grades (of mercy) whom We will, and over every lord of knowledge there is one more knowing.
________________
4.6 jahaz(  جَهَاز  )  : jahhaza(  جهز     ) meaning to prepare luggage, board and send it. Jahaz(  جهاز  ) is that luggage that a traveler prepares when he is about to travel. And tajheez(  تجهيز  ) is that luggage which is prepared before burying a coffin. And jahaiz(  جهييز  ) is that luggage which parents give to their daughter when they marry her. It is stated in the Quran:
________________
Surat Al-Yusuf (Joseph) -   سُوۡرَةُ یُوسُف
12:70
فَلَمَّا جَهَّزَهُم بِجَهَازِهِمۡ
And when he provided them with their provision  , he put the drinking-cup in his brother's saddlebag, and then a crier cried: O camel-riders! Lo! ye are surely thieves!
________________
4.7 zaad(  زَّادِ  )  : zaada meaning additional, extra, more than needs and the word zaad is typically used in relevance to travel. Travelling luggage meaning the money and food to be used during travel. And almazada(  المزادة  ) meaning the container of water that will be of use during a journey. And almizwad(  المزود  ) meaning store cupboard, and tazawwad(  تزود  ) also means to keep necessary luggage for journey. Allah states that:
________________
Surat Al-Baqarah (The Cow) -   سُوۡرَةُ البَقَرَة
2:197
وَتَزَوَّدُواْ فَإِنَّ خَيۡرَ ٱلزَّادِ ٱلتَّقۡوَىٰ‌ۚ
The pilgrimage is (in) the well-known months, and whoever is minded to perform the pilgrimage therein (let him remember that) there is (to be) no lewdness nor abuse nor angry conversation on the pilgrimage. And whatsoever good ye do Allah knoweth it.   So make provision for yourselves (Hereafter); for the best provision is to ward off evil.   Therefore keep your duty unto Me, O men of understanding.
________________
4.8 aslihah(  أَسۡلِحَ  ) (sg: salaah)  : this word is associated with war or fight which means equipment of war and destruction, weapons of fighting and everything that is used for fighting or for defense.  Allah states that:
________________

Luggage, Belongings
For this the words عَرَضَ, مَتَاع, اَثَاث, رَحَلَ, وِعَأ(وعِي), جَهَاز, زَاد (زود), اَسلِحة, عُدَّة , نَعمَة, رِيش, مَاعوُن (معن), مَعَا يشhave been used.
1- عَرَضَ
عَرَضَis everything which is not constant and everything in this world, with reference to this is عَرَضَ. When it is necessary to highlight inconstancy and fickleness of worldly things or possessions then عَرَضَis used. It also means that worldly gains and possession are flimsy and short lived.
وَلَا تَقُولُواْ لِمَنۡ أَلۡقَىٰٓ إِلَيۡڪُمُ ٱلسَّلَـٰمَ لَسۡتَ مُؤۡمِنً۬ا تَبۡتَغُونَ عَرَضَ ٱلۡحَيَوٰةِ ٱلدُّنۡيَا فَعِندَ ٱللَّهِ مَغَانِمُ ڪَثِيرَةٌ۬*ۚ
“Say not unto one who offereth you peace: "Thou art not a believer," seeking the chance profits of this life. With Allah are plenteous spoils” 4/94
2- مَتَاع(Pl: اَمتِعَة)
مَتَعَmeans to benefit from something in the long run. Any useful commodity or any part of it which is useful and to enjoy worldly gains a possessions. When its necessary to highlight worldly possessions and gains they bring, this word is used.
وَلَكُمۡ فِى ٱلۡأَرۡضِ مُسۡتَقَرٌّ۬ وَمَتَـٰعٌ إِلَىٰ حِينٍ۬
“There shall be for you on earth a habitation and provision for a time” 2/36
3- اَثَاث
اَثَاثةis the plural and is most commonly used. اثَاث البَيتis a famous phrase meaning household items or property. Household essentials like clothing, furniture, culinary items, beds etc. are all classed as اثَاث البَيت. This phrase, afterwards, was also used for all kinds of other things which were not so useful and has also been used for scrapyards and shops which sell this kind of items. Also, a slave or an animal that belongs to someone and is in direct use of that person is also referred to as اثَاث البَيت. For example, horse, cow, camel etc.
وَكَمۡ أَهۡلَكۡنَا قَبۡلَهُم مِّن قَرۡنٍ هُمۡ أَحۡسَنُ أَثَـٰثً۬ا وَرِءۡيً۬ا
“How many a generation have We destroyed before them, who were more imposing in respect of gear and outward seeming” 19/74
4- رَحل
رَحَلَmeans to put a saddle on a camel, to set off, to ride and the personal luggage that one takes on a journey is also رَحَلَ. In a Hadith, the Prophet Muhammad (saw) says:
لاَ تَشَدَّ و ا اَلَرِّحََالَ إِلاَّ لِثَلاَثة
which can be roughly translated as, 'don't put a saddle on your camel for pilgrimage of anywhere apart from 3 mosques(Masjid Al-Haraam, Masjid An-Nabawi, Masjid Al-Aqsa)'
In the Quran it says:
جَعَلَ ٱلسِّقَايَةَ فِى رَحۡلِ أَخِيهِ
“He put the drinking-cup in his brother's saddlebag” 12/70
5- وِعَأ(sing: اوعِيَة)
وَعَيmeans to put something a bag and tie a knot on it for safe keeping. اَوعِيَةis that item which is put inside a container and locked.
ثُمَّ ٱسۡتَخۡرَجَهَا مِن وِعَآءِ أَخِيهِ*ۚ
“Then he produced it from his brother's bag ” 12/76
6- جَهَاز
جَهَّزَmeans to make ready, to load and to send. جَهَازis that luggage which a passenger makes ready before setting off. تَجهِيزis that which is prepared before burying a person and جَهِيزis that which parents give to their daughter, at the time of her wedding, to take with.
فَلَمَّا جَهَّزَهُم بِجَهَازِهِمۡ
“And when he provided them with their provision” 12/70
7- زََاد
It means extra, something spare and زََادis normally used in text to journeys. زَادرَاهmeans 'spending money' and food for the journey andالمزاد هmeaning a water skin which is used during travelling and المِزوَدmeans a food container and تَزَوَّدَmeans to take provisions for a journey.
وَتَزَوَّدُواْ فَإِنَّ خَيۡرَ ٱلزَّادِ ٱلتَّقۡوَىٰ*ۚ
“So make provision for yourselves (Hereafter); for the best provision is to ward off evil“ 2/197
8- اَسلِحَة(sing: سَلاَح)
This word is commonly associated with war and fighting and gives the meaning of arms, weapons and everything else that is used to fight with or to resist with.
فَلۡتَقُمۡ طَآٮِٕفَةٌ۬ مِّنۡہُم مَّعَكَ وَلۡيَأۡخُذُوٓاْ أَسۡلِحَتَہُمۡ
“Let only a party of them stand with thee (to worship) and let them take their arms” 4/102
9- عُدَّة(sing: عُدَد)
عَدَّmeans to make preparations or to make ready.اَعَدَّand اَعتَدَmean to keep ready for actions and عُدَّةmeans equipment with regards to readiness. In Quran this word has been used in context of readiness and preparedness for war. Hence, the meaning more broadly encompasses any sort of preparation and equipment.
وَلَوۡ أَرَادُواْ ٱلۡخُرُوجَ لَأَعَدُّواْ لَهُۥ عُدَّةً۬
“And if they had wished to go forth they would assuredly have made ready some equipment” 9/46
10- نَعمَة
نَعَمmeans prosperity and good fortune. نَعمَةmeans items that constitute luxury.
وَنَعۡمَةٍ۬ كَانُواْ فِيہَا فَـٰكِهِينَ
“And pleasant things wherein they took delight!“ 44/27
11- رِيشاً
رِيش الطَّأرmeans the wings and feathers of a bird. رَيََّاشis a person who puts bird feathers on arrows. Because bird feathers are like regalia so similarly the word رِيشاًis used for raiment worn by people.
يَـٰبَنِىٓ ءَادَمَ قَدۡ أَنزَلۡنَا عَلَيۡكُمۡ لِبَاسً۬ا يُوَٲرِى سَوۡءَٲتِكُمۡ وَرِيشً۬ا*ۖ
“Children of Adam! We have revealed unto you raiment to conceal your shame, and splendid vesture” 7/26
It is also used in the meaning of decoration and ornamentation.
12- بِضَاعَةً
Means a generous part of wealth that is put aside for business or commodities that are for sale. It is also used for the capitol that is set aside for trade.
قَالَ يَـٰبُشۡرَىٰ هَـٰذَا غُلَـٰمٌ۬*ۚ وَأَسَرُّوهُ بِضَـٰعَةً۬*ۚ
“He said: Good luck! Here is a youth. And they hid him as a treasure” 12/19
13- مَاعُون
اَلمَعَنَmeans useful belongings. مَاعُونis everything of use that is commonly used by everyone. For example, everyday used things like axe, pots, household items etc.
وَيَمۡنَعُونَ ٱلۡمَاعُونَ
“Yet refuse small kindnesses” 107/7
14- حِذر
حَذَرَmeans to stay vigilant and sharp and حِذرis all the equipment that is used for defence. So, every instrument used in defence during a war is حِذر.
وَلَا جُنَاحَ عَلَيۡڪُمۡ إِن كَانَ بِكُمۡ أَذً۬ى مِّن مَّطَرٍ أَوۡ كُنتُم مَّرۡضَىٰٓ أَن تَضَعُوٓاْ أَسۡلِحَتَكُمۡ*ۖ وَخُذُواْ حِذۡرَكُمۡ*ۗ
“It is no sin for you to lay aside your arms, if rain impedeth you or ye are sick. But take your precaution” 4/102
15- مَعَائِش(sing: مَعِيشَة)
عَاشmeans to stay alive and everything that is needed to stay alive for example, good, water etc. isمَعَائِش.
وَلَقَدۡ مَكَّنَّـٰڪُمۡ فِى ٱلۡأَرۡضِ وَجَعَلۡنَا لَكُمۡ فِيہَا مَعَـٰيِشَ*ۗ
“And We have given you (mankind) power in the earth, and appointed for you therein livelihood” 7/10
Inference
1- عَرض  : Points towards fickleness of the world and the worldly wealth
2- مَتَاع  : Everything that is useful in some way
3- اَثَاث  : Household items and property
4- رَحل  : Luggage that stays with the traveller throughout the journey
5- وِعَأ  : Everything that is kept locked
6- جَهَاز  : Whatever is prepared for the journey and it can be زَادand/or رَحل
7- زَاد  : Food material for the journey
8- اَسلِحَة  : Arms and weapons
9- عُدَّةَ  : Preparation for war and fighting equipment
10- نَعمَة  : Items that constitute luxury
11- رِِيش  : Raiment and adornments
12- بِضَاعَة  : Commodities or wealth for investment
13- مَاعُون  : Everyday use household items
14- حِذر  : Defensive equipment or gear
15- مَعَائِش  : Necessities of life

And whatsoever good ye do Allah knoweth it. So make provision for yourselves (Hereafter); for the best provision is to ward off evil. Therefore keep your duty unto Me, O men of understanding.
